9032: A farmer kicks a cat sitting in front of the door of a house where a witch is said to live, whereupon the cat clings to the farmer's leg.
9033: A man who committed suicide is buried in unconsecrated ground. At a pond near a convent it begins to haunt in the evenings, so armed field guards keep watch. It is believed that the souls of the dead hover there. Later a water rat was found at that spot.
9375: At a place where someone committed suicide, there is haunting. After a dead rat was removed, the haunting stopped.
9505: A farmhand tells his girl that he has an errand to run, and that if she meets a vicious dog she must give it her handkerchief. She does indeed meet a dog, throws the handkerchief at it and flees. During the meal it is seen that he has pieces of a handkerchief between his teeth. When his room is searched, the belt that turns someone into a werewolf is found. As soon as the belt is thrown into the fire, the farmhand, who was working far away, is standing by the oven trying to jump into the fire. After the belt has burned, the farmhand is released.
9516:
A farmhand goes round all the inns every Sunday to drink himself full. Every Sunday night the farmer has to get out of bed to let the farmhand in. The farmer warns the farmhand and tells him he must be home before eleven. His mates, however, set the clock back an hour. The clock says five to eleven when the farmhand leaves. On the way home he meets the hellhound, which carries him home on its back. The farmer won't let him in; after all, he is an hour late. The farmhand becomes furious and throws his cap against the front of the house. A big hole appears, through which the dog and the farmhand disappear. The next morning the farmer finds the farmhand on the kitchen floor with a purple head. He has suffocated.
No one can explain the hole in the wall, and no one manages to close it.
12424: A man teases two sisters, who bewitch him as punishment. Things go rapidly downhill for the man and he suffers from hallucinations. The friars cannot help him. The man soon dies.
12425: Someone accepts sweets from a witch and then has hallucinations: he keeps seeing coals falling from the ceiling. The police find that nothing is wrong. This person is cured by the friars.
12428: A brewer notices that his beer keeps going wrong. One day he sees a cat walking across the kettle. He tries to chase the cat away, but the animal falls into the boiling brew. The cat climbs out of the kettle in a flash and flees. At home the brewer finds his wife covered in burns. She is a witch who can change herself into a cat and who spoils the brew every time.
12430: A house is haunted: the chaff mill turns at night and livestock keep dying. The fathers give the man medals to bury under the threshold to keep ghosts and witches away. Since then it has been quiet. Later it was found out that the two women who owned the house had tormented him with their witchcraft.
12431: A man is loading his cart with wood. A gentleman comes by and claims he should not load any more, because then the horse will not be able to pull the cart. The man pays no attention and puts more wood on the cart. But the horse indeed cannot pull the cart, and the man has to take off exactly as much wood as the gentleman had predicted.
12433: Two men are drinking a beer in a café near the seminary. Two seminary students, known for their magic, also offer them a beer. Once outside again, they lose their way and get lost. Only towards morning do they see where they are and return home.
12435: At a certain spot the witches, in the shape of cats, dance the cat dance and sing a song to it.
12437: Two farmers travel to town to sell their vegetables and fruit. There is a premonition that something will go wrong, so on the way they decide to have a drink at an inn. When they see another farmer go by, they actually want to catch up with him, but the landlady has the gift of foresight and says there is no need. When the farmers leave later, they catch up with the farmer after all: a wheel has come off his cart.
12438: A girl is offered something by a witch and from then on suffers from the 'fieteldans' or St Vitus' dance. She is cured of her madness by the friars. A clergyman warns the father not to look back on the way home. On the way back the dog cart has to battle an extreme headwind, but everyone keeps the command. The wind dies down when a bridge is reached. The girl is cured, but did not live very long after that.
12439: A farmhand wants to go to the market, but may only go once he has manured the field. He spreads four small heaps of manure at the corners of the field and by magic makes the rest of the manure spread itself over the land. Now the farmhand may go to the market. But when the farmer wants to plough the next morning, the manure is lying in heaps again and the farmhand is dismissed.
12440: A man breaks off his relationship with his girlfriend. On the way back he is harassed by a cat. The man throws his handkerchief at the cat. Later he meets his girlfriend with shreds of his handkerchief on her face. So his ex-girlfriend is a witch who can turn herself into a cat.
12442: A boy gets an apple from a witch. His father does not trust it and persuades his son to keep the apple until the next day. Then the apple turns out to have changed into excrement.
13117: You can get a wisseldaalder (a coin that always returns) on St John's Day at a crossing of cart tracks. You must stand in it and not step out or speak. An old woman will then put down a wisseldaalder for you. With this coin you will always have money in your pocket, because it always returns to your pocket.
13126: The glowing one is a man who wrongfully moved a boundary stone. After his death he must wander the heath, calling: "Where shall I put it?" Everyone is terrified of him. But a drunkard calls back: "Well, where you took it from." Now the glowing one has found rest and has never appeared to anyone again.
13127: A young man is a werewolf. When he is walking with his girl, he feels that he is about to change. He sends her on ahead and warns her about a big dog. She must throw her handkerchief to it, and then the girl can flee. Later, however, she and her family see the pieces of handkerchief between the young man's teeth. Werewolves always wear a band around their waist. The farmer the young man works for burns the band. The werewolf still tries to get into the fire, but he is held back. When the band has burned, the young man is an ordinary person again.
13220: One day a hunter shoots dead an unsuspecting aardmannetje (earth mannikin). Before it dies, the aardmannetje manages to drag itself to its hole. All the aardmannen (earth men) are in mourning. The news that the aardmannetje is dead buzzes through every village and town. At midnight all the aardmannen vanish from the towns and villages. Because a single cowardly hunter shot the aardman, all the aardmannen have left, and people can no longer expect help with their work.
13221: Witte wieven (white women) get up to all sorts of tricks. For instance, they go to a farmer's wife and conjure the bacon she is frying out of the pan. Witte wieven also swap children who are still in the cradle. They put a fake baby in the cradle and take the real baby with them. The fake baby eats and drinks a great deal, but cannot learn to talk. When a mother who also has a fake baby in her cradle decides to take the child to the nuns so it can learn to talk, she meets a wit wief (white woman) on the way. The white woman asks the child whether it is going to be baptised. Suddenly the child can talk and tells the white woman it is going to the nuns. The mother then knows she is holding a fake child and drops it on the ground. A farmer who wants to see the tricks of the witte wieven up close hits one of them on the shoulder with a heavy stick. The witte wieven then decide to return to Germany. On their journey to Germany one of them can walk no further. The others bury her alive, with the promise that she will rise again.
13222: Every night at exactly twelve o'clock a farmhand takes a small hoop out of the lime tree. He hangs the hoop around his neck and turns into a werewolf. He roams about for a while and tears apart everything that comes near him. After that he becomes an ordinary person again. The farmer finds his behaviour strange and asks the priest for advice. The priest realises that the farmhand is a werewolf and advises the farmer to send the farmhand on an errand from which he can never be back home by midnight. On the agreed night the priest takes the hoop out of the tree at midnight. The farmhand is standing under that tree and sees everything. He flees and never comes back.
13223: A couple go for a walk in the evening. The boy has to relieve himself, but before he disappears into the bushes he advises the girl that if a beast attacks her, she should throw her handkerchief in front of its mouth. A dangerous beast does indeed come at the girl. She throws her handkerchief in front of its jaws and the beast tears it apart. When the boy comes back, the girl sees that he has remnants of her handkerchief between his teeth. She now knows he is a werewolf and tells him so. The boy disappears and never came back.
13234: A clergyman who moved boundary stones calls out after his death asking where he should put them. After being told he must take them back to where they belong, the man finds rest.
13236: In the evening a man is chased by a dog that keeps growing larger, and it vanishes when the man calls on God.
13237: A black cat that keeps growing larger blocks the road, and vanishes after three Hail Marys are prayed.
13243: As punishment, a murderer turns into a fire spirit. A farmhand driving in the dark asks the fire spirit for help. The fire spirit rides along on the cart and gives light.
13268: Will-o'-the-wisps lure carters and walkers into the marsh and let them perish there.
13300: A woman regarded as a witch is given white mice by men, who expect them to multiply so much that she cannot magic them away. The woman trains the mice to come out when she whistles, and slips her wedding ring over the head of one of them. She fools the men by asking them, when they visit, to pray with her to find her lost wedding ring, after which, at her whistle, the mice appear, including the mouse with the ring around its neck.
13424: A white hare can only be shot with shot that has been dipped in holy water. The hare is really a witch.
13425: A farmhand is going home in the evening. On the Kattenberg he sees witches disguised as cats dancing. They take turns drinking from a cup. The witches also offer the farmhand the cup. Before he drinks, he says: "In God's name." At once the cats have vanished. He still has the cup. Later the Kattenberg was investigated. It turned out to be a burial mound.
13426: A man is riding home and on the way sees cats dancing. He flees, but a cat pursues him. He throws a knife at her. In the next village he knocks at someone's door. A woman with a cloth around her head opens it. She tells him where he can find his knife. She turns out to be the witch he threw his knife at.
13427: A cat is sitting in a tree. A farmer shouts that the cat must go away. When the farmer comes back, the cat is still there. The cat can talk and says: "I thought you would go easy on me." The farmer is very afraid of this talking cat. The meadow where the cat sat is now called the Kattendonke.
13429: A couple in love are walking in the evening. Suddenly the boy has to go away for a moment. He advises the girl that if she meets anything strange, she must throw away her handkerchief. The girl walks on and meets a werewolf. She throws away her handkerchief and flees. The werewolf tears the handkerchief apart. A little later she meets the boy again. There are still bits of her handkerchief between his teeth. She broke off the engagement.
13431: In the past there was much superstition about cats. Of the "cat dance" it is said that a walker at night was surrounded by hundreds of cats, which danced in a ring around that person. A boy on his way to his girlfriend met a cat on the road that would not get out of the way. So he kicked the cat. When he came home that night, he saw his mother lying in bed with a black eye. So she was a witch who could change herself into a cat. In Uden there is the "Kattenhol". Where this name comes from is not entirely clear. Some say the name derives from the tribe of "the Chatti", who were driven out of Germany. Others think the name comes from the Germanic spirit world.
13432: A man illegally poaching polecats in the evening hears a dog with a rattling chain go through a hedge. This frightens him badly, because there is no inhabited house anywhere for miles around.
13433: When a ghost cat sits on a gatepost, there is no way to knock it off. If you try, you strike right through it as if it were a spirit. A man is incurably ill. The doctor does not know what else to do. One evening a tramp comes in and warns that the neighbour's cat is causing the illness. When the cat comes in, everyone present begins to pray a rosary. At this the cat vanishes screeching into the fire and burns. The man's illness melts away like snow in the sun. A group of eight friends tease an old woman who sells herring. In the end they do buy some herring from her. On the way back six of the men get a thirst that cannot be quenched. The other two only notice in the evening that the woman has bewitched them; as they lie in bed a figure hovers above them and throws itself on them. When they switch on the light, the figure is gone.
13434: A farmer lying in bed hears rabbits screaming. When he switches on the light, he sees the rabbits, trembling, being pulled upward as if forced by an invisible hand. His brother, a priest, cannot explain it either. Although the cows in the stable are always tied with an iron band, they are sometimes found at the back of the stable while the iron bands are still closed. Holy water can undo this bewitchment. In the past glowing coals fell down through the ceiling while the alarm clock danced. Although the police investigated everything, they found nothing. A boy who seemed not quite right in the mind was suspected. When he was taken to the monks, his magic was broken. A boy in a café is bewitched by a glass of beer he accepted from a stranger. He sees mice and rats everywhere and foams at the mouth. When they try to take him to the fathers, the horse cannot cross the bridge. The boy claims there are rats and mice on the bridge too, but he is the only one who sees them. An old woman has a son who falls seriously ill and dies. The woman claims this is due to a curse spoken by a beggar woman when she refused to give her alms.
13435: A boy is courting his girlfriend by the fireside. Because of the heat they fall asleep. The boy wakes up but the girl sleeps on peacefully. He sees something strange come out of her that floats out through the chimney. After half an hour the strange figure comes back in and floats back to the girl. Because her spirit has returned, she wakes up. The boy tells her what he has seen, and the girl asks him to free her from the spell. At midnight the boy must go to the churchyard, where a cat dance is taking place. He must pick up a three-coloured cat and walk three times around the churchyard. He follows the instructions, and the three-coloured cat turns into his girlfriend. The spell is broken.
13451: Two men are playing cards. One of the men is cursing terribly and even says: "May the devil take me." The next day that man is found in a ditch with a broken neck. People say the devil jumped on his back on his way home and broke his neck.
13452: A witch causes a lot of trouble merely by being present somewhere. Her husband persuades her to use her magic power on trees instead. She does so, but as a result many trees around her die.
13453: Three people tell that late one evening they met a big dog with fiery eyes that jumped on their backs. Only at the edge of the field did it jump off and vanish. The dog vanished near a farm already known as uncanny, because the farmhand there said that the cows several times jumped up at the stroke of midnight while the stable doors flew open by themselves.
13454: In the dark people were frightened by a cow or horse in the meadow, which in the stories became phantom animals.
13455: Every time a farmer goes to buy or sell cattle, he hears strange noises of cats or owls in the wood. He never manages to chase the animals away. When he walks on, he ends up back on the same path where he started, and sometimes he arrives at the wrong place. A farm seems to be haunted because at night the cows, although well tied up, turn out to be walking loose in the cowshed. People do not know whether the farm is haunted, but they do believe they see the ghosts of old women who have died.
13456: Every time a poacher tries to shoot hares, his gun misfires. After having his bullets and powder blessed, he hits, hears a scream, and the hares disappear. A few days later he sees the woman known as a witch walking with a limp.
13458: Some men are sitting together chatting around the fire. Suddenly a cat comes in and also sits by the fire. Soon eight more cats follow, warming themselves in a circle by the fire. The men chase them away by throwing fire at them. The cats flee, howling. The next day nine women are lying in bed with burnt buttocks.
13461: A hare cannot be hit, however often the hunters shoot. When they put a sprig of palm in front of the gun, the hare turns into an old woman.
13466: A place where a few pollard willows stand is haunted. One evening a young man hears a pollard willow neigh there.
13497: A hunter shoots at a little gnome, which, mortally wounded, manages to drag itself to a hill. The hunter goes to that hill and hears the other gnomes saying sadly that their leader is dead. Since that day no gnomes have ever been seen in that town again.
13499: A werewolf is someone who as punishment must roam every night in the form of a wolf, or a sorcerer who can change into a wolf with the help of a wolfskin or a wolf belt. If the wolfskin is destroyed, the spell is broken.
13500: Someone who is bewitched and turns into a werewolf every night at twelve o'clock is freed from the spell. While the unfortunate man is playing cards, everyone stays seated until it strikes twelve. The bewitched man grows more and more nervous, but everyone simply stays put. On the stroke of twelve the werewolf's skin rolls in down the chimney and is burnt in the fireplace amid loud cheering. The man is released from the spell.
13501: A young man advises his fiancée that if she ever meets a werewolf, she should throw the beast a handkerchief so that nothing will happen to her. One evening, as the girl walks to her fiancé's house, a werewolf comes running towards her. She throws her handkerchief to it. The animal tears the handkerchief apart and disappears back into the wood. When the girl arrives at her fiancé's, she sees the shreds of her handkerchief between his teeth. The girl now knows that her bridegroom is a werewolf. The wedding is called off.
13522: Three giants dug the Maas. Because they were still fresh in the morning, they threw the sand very far, which is why the dykes are sometimes far apart. In the evening they were tired and threw the sand less far. When two of the giants speak two sentences to each other over a period of 200 years, the third giant thinks they talk far too much. He packs his things and leaves. As he knocks the sand out of his clog, a hill is formed. The two other giants keep digging and throw up a few hills.
14598: A cat always sits on a piece of wall.
14744: When someone looks under the table to see whether the cheat is hiding cards there, it is discovered that the stranger has horse's legs; the lamp goes out and the stranger disappears.
14747: A man who says he is not afraid of the devil is joined on his way back by a black dog. Once home, he manages to get rid of the dog by suddenly shutting the door.
14750:
A farm is haunted at night, and in addition a poacher cannot hit a certain hare. With a blessed medal chopped into pieces, on a priest's advice, the hare is hit in one eye. The woman who goes about the next day with a cloth over her eye is thought to have haunted the farm in the form of a hare, and the hare is believed to have been hit through the power of the blessed medal.
Blessed medal under the threshold as protection against the devil and ghosts.
14753: A maidservant does things backwards, whereupon the lady of the house asks the priest for help. He comes on Sunday after Mass, but, praying, can only get in through the front door after three attempts, for the devil disappears through the back door.
14755: One of a farmer's three daughters dies after eating an apple she was given by a woman possessed by the devil. After a journey full of obstacles he comes to a priest who has him look into a mirror in which the woman's likeness can be seen. The priest's prediction that the second child will also die and the third will become a nun comes true.
14760: On the priest's advice, a man strikes once with his flail at the black cat that will not get out of his way. The cat tells him to strike again if he dares. The man does not, and after that the cat stays away.
14761: A man is frightened by the cat dance he went to watch out of curiosity.
14762: A group of not very pious card players regularly has the devil fetch them a bottle of liquor.
14763: A man who declares that he would even court the devil meets a tall woman on his way home in the evening. He runs away from her and notices he is being chased by a big dog. At home the dog comes inside with him and a little later disappears again through the open door.
14764: One evening a man takes a kitten home. After he has gone to bed the house becomes restless, and the kitten appears before his bed despite the closed doors. The kitten says it wants to be taken back to the place it was taken from. Once this is done the house is quiet again.
14765: In the evenings a farmhand regularly sees a flame come out of the ground at the same spot in the meadow, from which a large dog leaps.
14766: To stop haunting in a house, a pan of fire is thrown inside, after which the screaming stops. The next day a woman in the neighbourhood has a burnt face.
14768: A woman comes back after her death because she was unable to carry out her intention to pray the Stations of the Cross. After the village has prayed the Stations of the Cross for her, she no longer returns.
14769: A man who has to burn the possessions of a woman declared a witch sees a one-winged chicken fly out of the fire.
14770: In the evening a large foal often lays its head on the back of passing horses and carts, and disappears when the carter stops.
14773: Two women who claim that shooting stars are devils' souls beckon them to come. At the thunderclap that follows they go inside, and two more bangs on the door follow.
14774: When the man strikes a dog, it feels as if he is hitting glass, and the dog has vanished.
14797: A criminal is visited in his cell by the devil, who leaves behind a sulphurous smell.
15179: Asking a witch to work magic for a reward; keeping her away from children; a slaughtered pig bewitched by a witch.
15572: A witch can bewitch a churn so that making butter fails.
16260: At the IVKO MAVO school in Tilburg the ghost of a priest wanders about. The priest had committed suicide in the physics classroom. The history teacher has seen it.
16261: A woman foresees that her father will die within a year. A week before her father dies, she sees him in a dream floating around and turning to ash. On her way to her father, she knows it is already too late and that he has already died. This turns out to be the case.
16262: A ghost wanders around the library of Mill Hill, a college run by priests in Goirle.
26425: General account of witches. A witch made a witches' brew and drank some before going to sleep. Hardly had such a woman fallen asleep than between twelve and two at night she woke up tossing and groaning. She then had no more rest in her witch's hole, jumped out of bed and flew from one corner of the hearth to the other. It also happened that she flew out through the chimney astride a broomstick, or sitting on a billy goat or a pig. With flapping hair and a sharp chin she then flew from one end of Liempde to the other hamlet, where she frightened or bewitched some people. She could also take on all kinds of shapes.
26426: Peerke thought: "Little cat, little cat, I'll hit you, I'll hit you; with my pickaxe I'll hit you, hit you off the turnstile," but before he got that far, the cat said: "Peerke, little man, go on and hit, go on and hit, if you dare, if you dare, if you... if you... if you..."
26427: When Bertha said "Gee up, horse," the animal could no longer move forward. Her cat jumps onto someone's neck and cannot be got off. Also the song of the convent of St. Arjaan, where two pairs of shoes stand by the little bed.
26428: When Januske van Drunen blew out the lanterns in the evening and the clock struck ten, cats from all around came through the Kattestraatje to the pit in the Lummelenkooi, where they danced around it paw in paw and sang: "How well this cap suits me, it is just as if I have a bonnet on." Unsuspecting passers-by were tricked, had the clothes torn off their backs or their faces scratched to pieces.
26429: One evening Jan Paulussen comes out of the pub, singing loudly about a pretty little finch he has, past the Lummelenkooi, where the cats screech at him: "How well this cap suits me! How well this cap suits me!" Jan, quick-witted, gives the cats a taste of their own medicine and answers: "It's just as if you have a turd on your head, it's just as if you have a turd on your head." At once the cats leap at him, tear the clothes off his back and rip his face open (and he runs home).
26435: Jaonte Aorte, who lives at the Kerkeind, can do more than others, but does not go to church on Sundays. Jaoneke means to cure her of that and goes to her with a bucket of holy water and throws it over her. And indeed she comes to the ten o'clock mass that Sunday. But the parish priest sees that she has a beehive on her head, and she thinks: "I'll get him." That afternoon the chaplain meets Jaonte and can no longer move forward. She gives him spurrey seed, which he is to shake out in the priest's stack of brushwood. The priest turns out to be in bed with a splitting headache and tells him to do it quickly. (If a medal of the Holy Childhood lay under her chair, she could not get up, and if her husband put his clogs crossed in front of the bed, she could not get into it.)
26440:
Bertus from Kasteren felt an urge at night to go to the bakehouse, and went there whether he wanted to or not. Once he lost his bearings and heard Nelia calling:
"Further, Bertus, further
Apparently, Bertus, apparently,
A bit more, Bertus, a bit more".
After hours of wandering he finally got home. Kulhannes advised him to go to Boxtel, where a clergyman freed him from Nelia's torment, though only for a short time. Then Bertus moved with his wife and children to St. Oedenrode. Then one day he dreams of a funeral, hears that Nelia has died and from then on sleeps peacefully.
26442: Govert was coming from Eindhoven to Liempde, and near Best he sees a black-spotted dog as big as a calf, with a chain around its neck and a red handkerchief hanging from its mouth. At first it walks beside him, but then the beast jumps on his back and Govert calls on all the saints in heaven, but they do nothing and shaking it off is useless. But then the Angelus bell rings in the distance and Govert crosses himself, prays the Our Father and cries "Amen, Amen"; only then does the dog let go. When Govert passes Knillis's farm some time later, Knillis is busy in front of his house and calls: "Hi, Govert!" And Govert sees shreds of the red handkerchief between his teeth.
29881: At the caravan camp ghosts rattle chains and chase people.
34717: A priest hangs two unconsecrated bells in the tower, and at night the devil steals and buries them; they can still be heard on Christmas Eve.
34719: You can recognise a witch by placing your foot crosswise in her footprint; then she has to turn around.
34755: In the old days people believed in witches, who danced in meadows at night or flew through the air. If a feather wreath was found in a sick person's pillow, that person was bewitched.
35060: A young man is a werewolf. When he is walking with his girl, he feels that he is about to change. He sends her on ahead and warns her about a big dog. She must throw her handkerchief to it, and then the girl can flee. Later, however, she and her family see the pieces of handkerchief between the young man's teeth. Werewolves always wear a band around their waist. The farmer the young man works for burns the band. The werewolf still tries to get into the fire, but he is held back. When the band has burned, the young man is an ordinary person again.
35072: You can get a wisseldaalder (a coin that always returns) on St John's Day at a crossing of cart tracks. You must stand in it and not step out or speak. An old woman will then put down a wisseldaalder for you. With this coin you will always have money in your pocket, because it always returns to your pocket.
39652: In the old days stories were told around the fire. Some would then say they had seen a ghost in the dark, but it could just as well have been a white horse.
40936: After a coach has crashed, it still haunts once a year.
41045: The cousins Folpert van Leerdam and Jan van Arkel live in constant rivalry. Once the parish priest is bribed so that Van Arkel and his retinue can be burned in the church. Since Van Arkel himself is ill, he escapes the attack and has the priest quartered. Folpert flees, but later returns and breaches the dikes. One day Folpert is inexplicably taken from this earth. He begins to haunt his castle, but that stops when his son tears the castle down.
41054: Kobus van der Schlossen is the leader of the Zwarte Bende (Black Gang), a gang of robbers who always blacken their faces with soot. Kobus had made a pact with the devil. One day he is chased by the police, jumps into a fen and turns into a clump of rushes. Because it still bubbles up, the spot is called Brobbelbies.
41069: Winus Monkels was a robber with magical powers who murdered and robbed many people. Once he wanted to rob a nobleman, but the nobleman got help from two archangels, who threw the robber into the marsh, where he drowned. Out of gratitude the nobleman had a chapel to Mary built above it. Only after the building was given another use did Winus Monkels dare to haunt. In the French period it became a chapel again, and Monkels no longer dared to haunt.
41387: Winus Monkels is a man who murders and robs people. One day he wants to rob a nobleman, but because the man is protected by two archangels sent by Our Lady, he fails. Winus Monkels flees and drowns in the marsh. Out of gratitude the nobleman has the marsh filled in and a chapel built over Winus Monkels' grave. Winus tells the devil he must not allow it, but instead the devil has the chapel converted into a weaver's house. Because Lauw Jonckers cannot weave anything there, he leaves. The Calvinists later turn it into a tavern, but this does not last long either, because Winus Monkels haunts it. In the time of the French the chapel is restored again, and Winus Monkels' skeleton is bent more crooked than ever before.
41489: After the grain is sieved, the rye looks like worms.
41491: A horse is held fast by magic. When the carter asks for the third time for the spell to be lifted, he strikes the table with wood from the cart, after which two men fall down dead.
41497: At a certain time the sound of a horse and cart is heard, but nothing is to be seen.
41505: After a father refuses to let his son in, the devil makes him go to hell and the castle sinks. In the same area a horse and cart loaded with stones ride into the water.
41510: A witch gets dung in her churn after someone has defecated in the churn of a woman whose butter-making fails.
41512: Twiddling the thumbs as protection against a witch. After a black cat is kicked, the witch is lame the next day.
41513: Poachers shoot two hares, and they hit the third as well. When they grab that hare, the hare asks whether the others have already gone. The poachers flee, but close to home they stop.
41516: In a pool where a chapel is said to have sunk, the ringing of bells is heard.
41519: At the site of a sunken chapel, the ringing of bells is said to be heard on Christmas night.
41529: Near a witches' ring, singing is heard from cats that are witches in disguise.
41530: Haunting; a witch changed into a cat punishes a carter by bewitching the spokes of his wagon so they break.
41531: Haunted house where crockery came out through the walls.
41534: Haunted house where stones fall down without there being a hole in the roof.
41540: A calf found dead under the table in the house, having passed through the closed stable door and with a trough that could not have gone through the door, was said to be the devil's work. A clergyman blesses the house to drive out the devil.
41541: A witch makes a man who says he will be home earlier lose his way.
41543: A plot of land called Kattendonk is the place where cats danced. Chasing them away did not work; there is a story that the cats were beaten off the bridge.
41547: Place where a murder was committed and which is haunted.
41550: Will-o'-the-wisps are unbaptised children; they are also called vuurwormen (fire worms).
41551: A man goes to a haunted place, hears the rattling of chains and finds a hermit who was imprisoned after a murder.
41564: At Kortome they tried to make butter, but it would not work. No one was strong enough to churn the butter. A clergyman told them to throw a guilder into it. She threw in a guilder and it turned into butter. The guilder was stronger than the people.
41566: Biesthoutakker used to be haunted. On a farm a few men were talking when suddenly all the cows were loose at the same time. The men went to tie the cows up again. When they had finished and sat down, exactly the same thing happened. The farm and the people who worked there were bewitched.
41567: When you came back with a basket from the egg market in Oisterwijk, you passed a house that used to be haunted. When you reached that house there was a woman who carried the basket for a hundred metres and then could carry it no further. Then she came back again. She always did this with one basket, not with the others. Once she had done her duty she could walk on, after handing out sweets there.
41574: Freeing a ghost locked up in chains in a house where a murder was committed.
41579: A parish priest puts an end to the haunting in the churchyard.
41584: People thought there were ghosts at Strijdhoef castle. The people who lived there were very poor and cleaned the house themselves. The daughters tucked their skirts into trousers and wore a cloth around their hair. People saw white women around the castle and thought they were ghosts. But they were probably the lady of the castle and her daughters.
41585: In Udenhout, Bet went from door to door telling fortunes. She predicted how long you would live and whether you would become poor or rich. None of it ever came true, however.
41587: A treasure was said to be buried among the hills in Udenhout. It had belonged to the former lord of the castle. People often searched for it, but the treasure was never found.
41591: At night a ghost jumps on people's backs and makes them carry it.
41602: Hearing chains rattle in the evening.
41603: Finding blocks of wood in bed is said to be witchcraft.
41605: When there is rattling, people think the devil is coming.
41609: Finding blocks of wood in bed is said to be the work of a witch.
41610: Haunted barn where chains are rattled at night.
41616: A pack of black cats that suddenly disappear must be witches.
41618: The faster someone cycles, the faster another pursues him; when a man walks he hears water sloshing, when he stands still the water is still.
41622: A bewitched horse is held fast; at night the horse stands with curled mane.
41623: Haunting around the crucifixes in the churchyard after the church bells ring at midnight.
41625: Children who witnessed other children drowning see the hands of the drowned children sticking out of the water at that spot every time.
41650: After a cat is beaten, a woman is injured.
41651: At midnight passers-by see a headless woman.
41654: Haunted house; ghostly goings-on at the haunted house.
41655: In the evening a man turns into a dog that leaps on people.
41656: At midnight the mist takes the shape of a creature.
41673: A ghost at the castle is said to have caused a farmhouse to burn down.
41720: A murdered noblewoman haunts the area around the castle.
41721: A passer-by who sees cats dancing is spoken to.
41723: A horse is bewitched by a witch who flies in on a sieve at night and then rides the horse. She comes to the man who took the sieve away; the silk ties from Amsterdam she promised are hanging on the door in the morning.
41724: Farmhand is helped by the devil while spreading manure.
41725: A bewitched man cannot finish his glass of beer.
41726: A card player can no longer play cards after they see a horse flying. The fathers can still help him because he has not touched the money won at cards.
41729: A stranger who joins as the fourth card player disappears when, after horse's hooves are seen on his legs, Jesus, Mary and Joseph are called upon.
41730: After being kicked twice, a cat tells a man to kick it a third time.
41733: Missing tethers in the cowshed, letting the cows roam loose, mean the devil has been in the cowshed.
41734: Undoing work is the devil's doing.
41738: Encounter with a talking cat, a witch changed into a cat.
42228: A story about a haunted spot at the 'Kraaienest'; also stories about UFOs and freemasonry, as well as folk beliefs about, among other things, kung fu and the Indonesian kris.
42673: Around midnight the sound of bells can be heard at the Kerkenakker in Kaatsheuvel and a funeral procession can be seen. The horse of Jan B. and Just once bolted when singing could be heard. Whoever digs a hole in the ground and puts his ear in it hears the singing.
42802: According to the Efteling attraction 'Villa Volta', bokkenrijders (goat riders, a gang of robbers) leader Hugo van de Loonse Duinen robbed the Abbey of Postel. Hugo will find no rest until 'a noble person with the pure conscience of a newborn child shall enter your dwelling.'
43005: In the old days you could encounter ghost animals near Kattenhol, such as cats that were really witches. You had to be very much on your guard. By kicking a cat, a man once injured his own wife.
43244: A cat that cannot be caught is a witch.
43808: A bewitched cat can be shot by placing silver on the cartridge.
43895: Digging of a river and creation of hills by giants.
43901: Having the jack of spades fetch gin.
43931: A witch makes a man wander until the moon has set.
43953: A wild boar that is shot at cannot be hit.
43956: A witch who often sits on a bridge works magic at someone's request. The next day that person is covered in lice.
44016: Prediction of telephoning and of a change of climate in summer and winter.
44038: A cat that walks along with you is a witch, but it can also be a stray cat.
44110: Women who put on a white shirt to go haunting. Places where ghosts and witches gather. Ghosts to frighten people; sometimes they were possessed by the devil.
44113: A witch in the shape of a white cat holds a horse and cart fast. Women who frighten passers-by with a white sheet and a black cloth.
44179: A girl reluctantly goes to work for a woman, because she is known as a witch. While she is working on the bleaching field with someone else, a cat comes along, and a little later the woman is standing behind the hedge and says she has heard everything.
44180: A girl works as a servant for a lady who is regarded as a witch. When they have been shopping together, the lady regularly disappears and then cats appeared. When the girl reaches a church, the cats disappear.
44181: A minister forbids a girl to believe in women who turn into cats. After the minister and his wife are set upon one evening by a swarm of cats that only leave when they pray the Lord's Prayer, he admits there is something beyond human understanding.
44182: Children on their way with empty herring barrels are attacked by cats that cannot be touched. Once they are home, a woman said to be a witch comes asking for herring, because she had noticed the barrels were empty.
44185: A cat will not be chased away; only with a hammered-up dime in the barrel does he manage to hit the cat. The next day the doctor comes for a woman who has been shot in the leg.
44321: A man, woman and child fall ill from the neighbour's sugar. They go to an exorcist, where in the reflection of a tub of water they see women, among them the neighbour: the exorcist points out the neighbour as the guilty witch. The next day they find in the mattress, for each of them, a (witch's) wreath of feathers that is not yet closed. On the exorcist's advice they stick the wreaths full of darning needles and boil them in a pan of oil. The neighbour comes and asks them to stop boiling the wreaths, because she has terrible stomach pains. The witch is sent away and the spell is broken: the sick people recover.
44323: A woman sees white rabbits come out of an ice cellar and dance on a burial vault. Women under fifty do not see the rabbits, but older women do.
44332: A girl who has been made ill is freed from witchcraft by priests. She is given relics to throw under the neighbour woman's chair, so that the neighbour cannot get up.
44336: Farmers are attacked at night by meowing black cats that jump onto the wagons and the horses' backs. When the narrator's father goes along, the cats do not come.
44341: Giving thanks for a loan with a bag of biscuits instead of money causes a woman to fall into the power of a witch. Her child is pulled through the cradle, a light that has fallen over keeps burning, a glass of drink that has tipped over does not spill, and in the evening a black cat sits outside. The priest called in to help puts a relic in trenches he dug at night around the house and through the garden, so the witch could no longer enter the yard.
44343: Around midnight it seems as if a storm is raging in a wood, and the rattling of chains can be heard from an uninhabited farmhouse, but when people go to look all is quiet.
44344: An old woman who thinks a married couple sleeps too long makes them fall out of bed. After the wife has given birth, the chaplain comes by. The midwife asks him to help. The chaplain had already seen from the smoke of the chimney that something was wrong. He takes his book and begins to read, and when he is finished, his face is covered in sweat.
44346: In the morning a horse stands sweating in the stable though no one has taken it out. In the evening the farmer and his farmhand keep watch in the barn. At midnight a woman comes in and tries to take the harness, but the farmer beats her and throws her onto the dung heap. When she later says that the harness has been moved, the farmer has power over her.
44347: A man knocks a cat off a gate several times, and each time the cat jumps back on. Even after the cat has said he should try it once more, he keeps going, whereupon a number of cats scratch at his leather boots and his face.
44348: A man who insulted a woman has to walk through ditches.
44349: A man waiting for hares at one point sees seven hares there, one of which puts its paw on his shoulder and says there sure are a lot of hares. The man never hunted again.
44350: On Christmas night a man tries to shoot hares, but the gun will not fire. With a silver dime in the barrel the gun does fire, but no wounded hares are to be seen.
44351: A man goes hare hunting against his wife's wishes. His gun keeps misfiring until he puts a silver dime in the barrel. The hare he shoots manages to escape, however. When he gets home, his wife is lying in bed with a cloth over her eye.
44442: Men bet that no one can send a jack of spades out for a bottle of gin. Someone known as a wizard makes the jack of spades go outside, and a little later it comes back with a rolling bottle of gin. The man to whom the wizard gives the bottle cannot get the cap off.
44444: A man asks a woman with a bunch of clover to keep walking, or else misfortune will befall him. She stays where she is, and the man breaks his neck. The cause is that the bunch of clover contained a three-leaf clover, which gives power over someone.
44450: After mocking the friars, a man on his way home gets a thing on his back that he cannot shake off. Someone accompanying him sees nothing. At his house the thing is gone, and the man promises never to laugh at the friars again.
44451: Every morning bacon has disappeared, so men keep watch. They see a large dog come in, jump on the table, take the bacon and go outside. The men do not see the dog walking away.
44457: In a family with sick children, neighbour women see a toad come out of the sink. One of the neighbours reads from a book, grabs the toad with tongs and throws it into the fire. The toad manages to get out of the fire and cannot be found. The next day the neighbour turns out to be burnt.
44530: Fear of a werewolf that jumps on people's backs.
44624: By making a cross on the road, a witch looks back and can do nothing.
44953: Witte wijven (white women) wash little children and look after them.
44955: Will-o'-the-wisps are the souls of unbaptised children.
44956: Glowing men are returned dead who let cattle graze on someone else's land, or surveyors who marked a boundary wrongly.
44962: List of haunted places in Someren.
44969: Appearance of a witch, examples of witchcraft.
45131: Witches can make people lose their way and hold them fast.
45141: Places in the Peel where sunken church bells lie.
45254: Ghostly phenomena such as being pushed aside by a funeral procession, being attacked by white dogs, and women flying through the air.
45285: Bewitching of a churn, making butter-making impossible.
45290: Spinvrouwtjes (little spinning women) in spiderwebs look inside and disappear once they know everything.
45782: People believed in ghosts. You were also frightened with werewolves. As a child the narrator was not allowed to accept an apple from Ann Potters. She was said to bewitch the apples.
45902: A parish priest's prediction that no priests will come from Heeze for a long time comes true.
45949: The narrator's ancestors believed in ghosts and witchcraft. Ante Ponny was the most powerful at magic; she was the greatest witch in Werkendam.
45990: Lange Jet is said to haunt 'De Kraaienest' on the Island of Dordrecht.
46021: Church bells lie sunk in a marsh.
46023: On demolition it turns out that rye or buckwheat flour was used in the mortar.
46143: A witch can conjure lice and can bewitch children.
46146: Werewolves jump on people's backs in the evening.
46148: A sunken bell rings at midnight at Christmas.
46167: For sickness among cows, people went to the fathers of Tongeren, who gave medals.
46176: Black cats that walk along with people prevent them from reaching the destination of their journey.
46178: A bewitched churn makes churning impossible.
46322: Having gin fetched by the jack of spades.
46335: A poacher hits a hare, whereupon the hare warns him to clear off, or else it will shoot the poacher.
46336: Breaking a spell that holds someone fast by making crosses and praying.
46353: No butter can be made with a bewitched churn.
46473: Bricklaying with rye flour or buckwheat flour.
46524: It is said that near Eersel there are ghostly apparitions, a kind of gnomes, of which people are afraid.
46557: It is told that in Riethoven there was a hunter who had shot dead Kyrië, the leader of the gnomes on the Duivelsberg. After Kyrië's death all the gnomes left the Duivelsberg.
46559: In Hoogeloon it is told that gnomes once lived there, who disappeared decades after the death of their king Kyrië.
46563: It is told that in Meerveldhoven the news of Kyrië's death hit the gnomes hard. People heard them running back and forth in their underground dwelling, talking busily. They were said to be leaving all together at night. A man from Veldhoven wanted to see this and stayed up all night. After thousands of gnomes had passed, there was so much dust that the man had to take another road home.
46565: It is told that in Aalst the gnomes left after the death of the gnome Kyria. A farmer had given some gnomes very bad porridge, and Kyria died of it.
46588: It is told that elves live in small hills and do not want anyone on the meadow after sunset, as that is their territory. The elves are mainly concerned with the plants and herbs they need.
46590: It is told that in Strijp 'witjes' (little white ones) often came by and slammed the stable doors open and shut. Then they sang a song in a circle.
46610: It is told that at a crossroads in Deurne you may meet a black dog. There is also a cartwheel around which Steilkerskens [will-o'-the-wisps] float. People are warned about this, because at this spot Satan's Sheepdog is said to guard the souls of unbaptised children. These little souls also often wander over the low land, but you must not follow them, for you will surely get lost in the night.
46614: It is told that in Den Bosch stalkaarsen [will-o'-the-wisps] were seen in winter.
46615: It is told that stallichten [will-o'-the-wisps] have been seen in Zundert.
46617: It is told that many stalkaarsen (will-o'-the-wisps) floated over the Zwart Ven near Rijsbergen. One night a farmer had to baptise a whole group of them. Since the marshy heath was turned into pasture, no stalkaarsen have been seen there.
46620: A treasure is buried by blue little fires on a plot of land.
46623: It is said that a man from Zeelst, as punishment for moving the boundary post, had to roam after his death in glowing form along the boundaries he had changed. A number of people have seen this figure and are afraid of it. They say it looks like an elongated, dark cone with a little light above it.
46625: It is said that an alderman from Woensel had to indicate the boundary between Woensel and Strijp. First he put sand from Woensel in his shoes and placed a lead spoon under his cap. Very close to Strijp he said he was still standing on Woensel ground, and he swore it by the Creator above. For this lie he was punished after his death: he had to keep wandering about as a fiery figure.
46631: It is said that the glowing figure seen every night on the heath at Eersel is an Englishman who was buried there while quartered in the area.
46632: It is said that a weaver from Steensel was murdered on the heath by an English or Spanish soldier. Since then the murderer has wandered the heath in glowing form.
46633: It is said that in Rijsbergen a shepherd burst into flames after he had lied. The shepherd had seen a chest of money fall from a carriage and had grabbed it at once. When the driver came back to ask whether he had found the chest, the shepherd answered that he would have to wander about burning forever if he had the money. And so it happened.
46634: The burning shepherd is also said to wander in the Kempen.
46635: The burning shepherd has also been seen on the heath between Tilburg and Breda.
46636: The glowing shepherd is also known in the area around Baarle.
46637: The burning shepherd of Hoogeloon is also known in Zeelst.
46638: The burning shepherd is also known in Luiksgestel.
46688: Ghost horses at Tiel announce coming floods, and show the inhabitants that they must close the gaps in the dike with horse manure. Before the ghost horses came, the inhabitants used all sorts of things to close the passage, but at high water it washed away every time and the town flooded. One night in heavy weather the dike watchmen are at work and suddenly see foaming hooves rising from the water. Gradually a gigantic horse of foam emerges and gallops off over the dike, followed by more and more horses. At the end of the night the dike watchmen returned to the town, assuming it would have flooded, but that turns out not to be so. The filling of the passage has stayed in place, and the watchmen smell horse manure, and so they realise that the ghost horses filled the passage with their manure and thereby saved the town. That is why it is now said that if you hear horses' hooves on the dike at night, you had better close the gaps quickly, because heavy weather is on its way.
46707: The stampvoet (stamping foot, a ghost) always appeared unexpectedly near Veldhoven and ran past with heavy hoofbeats, throwing people to the ground.
46708: A man was careless enough to follow the "hengstespoor" (stallion track). As punishment an invisible hand pulled his fine hat off his head and destroyed it.
46712: The glowing wagon was sighted in Aalst by a shepherd who was walking on the heath with his flock when the carriage approached him. The coachman and the horses were pitch black and the carriage was entirely on fire. The coachman drove straight through the flock and into the woods. The shepherd, the sheep and the dog were all terribly frightened.
46713: In Aalst, a farmer's wife's daughter saw a spirit while she was milking the cow. She was very frightened and the next day the farmhand went with her. He saw the spirit too. The spirit came closer every evening, and the priest said they should ask the spirit what it desired. The farmer's wife, the farmhand and the daughter asked the spirit what it desired, and it told them it had vowed to make a pilgrimage to Kevelaar but had never fulfilled it. They decided to make the pilgrimage all together. After the journey the spirit was released and could go to heaven.
46714: A young girl from Eersel met a spirit every evening. Finally she asked him who he was and what he wanted. The spirit answered that he was her father and that three more Masses had to be said for him. This was done, and then the spirit disappeared.
46715: A poor broom-maker saw the spirit of his father, who had recently died, sitting on the wheelbarrow. His father told him he had to make a pilgrimage and give bread to the poor, because his father had made a vow that he had not kept. After these words his father disappeared.
46716: The spirit of the priest asks a pious person whether she will do a good work for him, so that he can enter heaven.
46719: On the priest's advice, a girl asks the spirit that regularly appears to her what it wishes. After she promises to fulfil the request of the spirit, who turns out to be her mother, to have a Mass said, she receives a handshake that is visible in the cloth around her arm.
46720: The spirit of Havens appeared to his sister's maidservant in 's-Hertogenbosch. He asked her to have three Masses said for him and to bring an offering to the altar of the Holy Cross. He had promised this during his life, but it had never been done.
46723: In Eersel, too, the ghost of the boundary-post mover is known.
46737: One night a resident of Netersel saw a funeral procession pass by. Five days later his neighbour was buried, followed by as many men and women as he had seen that night.
46738: Adriaan Kr. from Rijsbergen once saw a funeral procession pass. This turned out to be a bad omen, for less than a month later his mother was buried.
46740: It is advisable to avoid a nighttime funeral procession, otherwise you risk getting a box on the ear.
46743: There used to be a castle near the watermill at Keersop. By a small dyke nearby, people often meet the white castle maiden.
46744: In Bergeik a woman sat spinning at night, leaning against the hedge.
46746: In Duizel a street is called the 'Haspelstraatje' (Reel Lane); it was named after an old woman who used to sit there in the evenings reeling yarn.
46747: Near Oerle there is a headless maiden, dressed all in white. When someone passes by, she accompanies them to their home without speaking.
46749: Around Bergeik the inhabitants often sighted a phantom dog. It was said to be a grey dog without legs that floated above the ground. This dog often accompanied walkers as far as their homes.
46750: The black ghost dog has been sighted in various places on the heath. Sometimes with a glowing key in its mouth and other times with a rattling chain.
46751: In Oerle the black dog is often seen by walkers, whom it then accompanies. The dog gradually grew larger, until in the end it was as big as a foal.
46752: After crossing the bridge between Borkel and Schaft, people saw a headless dog. It followed people without ever harming anyone.
46758: The 'white horse' could be seen every evening in Veldhoven. The plague broke out in the village and every appearance of the horse foretold new deaths.
46793: A poacher in Zand-Oerle once went hunting hares. He had one in his sights, but his gun misfired. The poacher took aim again, but a good twenty hares appeared, and more and more kept coming.
46794: A poacher in Zeelst was sitting in his hide when an enormous hare came hopping up. He took aim but missed. Suddenly hundreds of hares appeared and put him to flight.
46796: A centuries-old oak in Tilburg is said to be haunted.
46798: Jan Hurkmans from Bergeik met a ghost one night. It had the form of a horrible monster and was as big as a horse, but without head or legs. Jan was terribly frightened and did not dare to walk past that spot for seven years.
46802: A number of men poaching on the Bestsche hei suddenly saw a few riders race past at full speed. The riders changed into a carriage drawn by two horses, and when the poachers came closer it changed into a dog cart, and then suddenly disappeared.
46804: Francis Daris once saw a terrible ghost standing before him in an oak wood. For the rest of his life he did not dare to pass that place again.
46808: A group of companions were walking home at night, laughing, after drinking some beer. Suddenly they realised they were standing in a churchyard. They had to climb over the stone rampart to get away. Two men said they would rather go to the inn and wait there until it was light, but the other thought them cowards and said: "Even if the devil himself came, I would still go on." So he walked onto the heath, but at once saw a dog lying on the road. The dog had glowing eyes and a red tongue. The man ran off, but the dog kept following him until he reached the village of Heeze.
46815: In Heeze a young man was thrown into the ditch by an invisible hand.
46817: A tailor from Bergeik stayed past midnight in a house on the Loo. They asked him to stay the night, but the tailor would not hear of it. But when he set off, he met a ghost. He took to his heels and heard clear whistling and human voices above his head, without seeing anyone.
46818: One evening a pale, thin ghost came into a house. The ghost forced the occupant to sit down on a chair. It began to shave off the occupant's beard. The occupant was very frightened, and after the ghost had left his beard never grew again; even the hair on his head would no longer grow.
46819: In Vught a tailor who was also a barber once had to shave a ghost.
46820: An old house on the de Laec estate was haunted.
46821: The Wijnand van Steinstichting in Breda was a notorious haunted house. The Falison ladies, who had died there, were said to still haunt it.
46830: Near Westerhoven lies a large stretch of barren heath. The only plant that grows on it is the "heksendans" (witches' dance). The ground is so bare and dry because cat dances were always held there at night. That is why the place is called "Kattendans".
46831: Almost every village has its own 'cat dance'.
46832: A labourer from Westerhoven met a cat at night. He threw his spade at it, but suddenly he was swarming with cats all around him. They only left when he muttered a prayer; his spade was never found again.
46833: A cat tells people who throw a stick at her to try it again if they dare. Whoever dares is badly mauled by about ten cats.
46834: At Nederwetten the Dworussen lane was said to be haunted. A man once went through that lane with his horse and cart and at once saw two black cats. He knocked them off the horse, but at once thousands of cats came. They took hold of each other's front paws and danced in a ring on their hind legs.
46836: One evening Jan Prinsen was walking across the Bergerhei and saw four cats there, dancing paw in paw and singing. After the dance and the song they passed round a silver goblet, from which they drank in turn. Then they asked whether Jan would like to drink too; he did not, and with a blessing he managed to chase the cats away. He then took the cup back to the lady it belonged to, but he was not allowed to say anything about it.
46837: Witches often gather at the crossroads in Eersel to hold meetings. A sceptical student mocked an old woman there. Immediately an army of cats came and attacked him.
46838: Countless cats, actually witches, were said to gather regularly in an old linden tree in Westerhoven to deliberate about the secret arts they practised.
46839: In Rijsbergen there is the 'Kattekuil'. At night a number of cats were said to do the cats' dance there, and if you walked past you were obliged to join in. The cats could not be wounded or killed; if you tried, they came after you.
46841: A pedlar who had to pass the Krochten in Zundert at the witching hour was swept along in a wild waltz by a black cat and finally left unconscious on the road.
46842: An accordion player coming from the fair in Etten was playing his accordion. Suddenly a few cats leapt out and began to dance around him, paw in paw.
46852: To find out whether a woman is a witch, you must follow her and place your foot crosswise in her footprint; if she then looks back, she is a witch.
46853: When the missal stays open, no witch can leave the church.
46855: If you put an Easter nail under the threshold, no witch can cross that threshold.
46873: A woman in Bergeyk was much plagued by a witch. Someone advised her to chase a strange cat out of her house. From then on she never saw the witch again.
46876: At the Brouwers family in Bergeik, young calves regularly died. This was said to be because a witch's cat visited the stable at night.
46877: A young farmer's calves always died. His aunt warned him that the evil hand might be in the stable. He did indeed see a strange black cat walking about, and then he went to a man who could help him get rid of the evil hand. Since then he has never had dead calves again.
46880: A brewer sees a number of cats sitting on the rim of his brewing kettle. Furious, he throws a bucket full of boiling water over the cats. The next day he finds his wife lying dead in bed, covered in burns.
46892: Unhittable hares that have been hit turn around at the next shot and disappear.
46897: A black cat is said to be a witch; a witch makes cats; men experience all sorts of things in the evening.
46902: Jan Verhuyzen from Heeze asks a little black cat where she comes from. The cat answers him. Jan is scared out of his wits but reaches the farm. The cat also comes into the farm and sings that Jan has spoken to her.
46904: A cat is thrown off the railing of a bridge twice. When the man wants to do it a third time, she says: "Do that again if you dare."
46905: Some boys threw a cat into the brook. For the rest of the day the cat kept following them and looked at them with fiery eyes.
46906: In the hamlet of Dalem there was often a hare. If you shot at it and hit it, the hare was not bothered at all. Some thought it was a witch.
46907: In Bergeik a man met a dancing and leaping hare that he could not chase away with a stick.
46908: Adriaan Kr. from Rijsbergen once wanted to shoot a hare, but he could not hit the animal. It turned out to be old Bet from the village.
46909: A farmer had shot at a hare twice, but missed both times. Then he had his shot blessed by the priest, and this time the hare was hit.
46910: Near the village of Empel a large hare always ran about at night that could not be hit. It was said to be a witch. Only after a mission by a priest did the hare disappear.
46911: In Valkenswaard a crowd was chasing a hare. At the spot where it disappeared they saw a woman sitting, who said she had not seen the hare. People were convinced this woman was a witch who had turned herself into a hare.
46912: Witches can quickly change into cats and back again. Even so, they get caught doing it.
46913: A boy from Heeze met a black kitten on the way. He took it home, but it turned out not to be an ordinary cat. They locked the cat up, but the next day it had vanished without a trace.
46914: Some lads from Vught went to steal apples. They saw a cat with glowing eyes sitting in the apple tree and ran off. When they got home, the sack of apples turned out to have changed into a sack of horse droppings.
46915: A man heard from an unknown little woman that his wife had given birth to a daughter. Later he was told that during the birth celebration a black cat had come in. So this must have been a witch.
46918: At an inn in Oerle horses always get stuck and cannot go any further. The witch of that inn does this because she does not want people to drive past the inn without having something.
46920: A parish priest was suddenly put on the ground and held there by invisible beings. Only after he had read a passage from his breviary could he continue on his way.
46929: In Vught, during the Belgian Revolution, a sergeant is said to have 'fixed in place' an inn full of unwilling soldiers.
46931: Whoever wants a wisseldaalder (a coin that always returns to its owner) must make sure to be at a crossroads at twelve o'clock on St John's Eve.
46940: A young man is a werewolf. When he is walking with his girl, he feels that he is about to change. He sends her on ahead and warns her about a big dog. She must throw her handkerchief to it, and then the girl can flee. Later, however, she and her family see the pieces of handkerchief between the young man's teeth. This is how they know he is a werewolf.
46941: A farmhand in Bladel was a werewolf. He had a band with which he could transform himself. The farmer found this band and burnt it in the oven. Then the farmhand was released from being a werewolf.
46943: A farmer from Vught was released from his existence as a werewolf when friends burnt his wolfskin in the hearth fire.
46950: On Christmas Eve three men sat in the inn waiting for a fourth hand so they could play a game of cards. They had to wait a very long time and started cursing. Suddenly there was a traveller in the inn who was willing to join in. He later turned out to be the devil himself. The three not only missed Christmas Mass but had also become very frightened and never again dared play cards on Christmas Eve.
46953: Thijs van der Bruggen is in a very bad mood during carnival, because his girlfriend has broken up with him. When, dead drunk, he walks past some thorn bushes with a friend, he is fed up with always being teased. Thijs cries out, cursing: "If no girl will dance with me any more, then I'll dance with the devil". The next day, at midnight, he walks past the same thorn bush again and is suddenly seized by the devil, who starts dancing with him. Had he not called on Jesus for help and made a cross, it would have ended badly for him.
46954: In Ulvenhout lived a farmhand, Peer, who did not behave very well. He spent whole days in the pub playing cards with his mates and drank a great deal of beer. One day the farmer had had enough and told Peer he had to be home before 10 o'clock that evening, or he would not be let in any more. Peer was far too late and shouted, cursing: "Even if the devil has to bring me, I'll be home at ten". At that very moment a black dog came along and took Peer on its back. It ran a few times round the house, but the farmer did not open up. Peer threw his cap against the wall and a hole appeared there that could never be closed again. There was a hellish racket in the farmhouse, and the next morning the farmer found Peer lying dead on his bed. The devil had wrung his neck.
46955: A charcoal burner from Ginneken had murdered seven strangers. He was sentenced to hang, but kept denying it. He said that if he had done it, the dead might testify against him and the devil might carry him off to eternity. This is what happened. The seven dead stuck their fists out of the ground, and so the Zeven Heuveltjes (Seven Little Hills) came into being.
46962: The Klokkenkuil in Veldhoven always sounds a single stroke at twelve o'clock on Christmas night.
46963: The lord of Bloemendaal castle once hung a bell in the tower without having it consecrated first. The devil now had power over it, tore the bell out of the tower and threw it into a pool.
46964: In Ruimel there is a drained fen where the stroke of a bell can be heard on Christmas night. Long ago a bell was thrown into it.
46965: Near the Kapelberg at Ruiniel, a bell lies in a fen and rings on Christmas night. But if you go and listen to it, the devil will break your neck.
46967: The Klokkuil at Zitterd is a pit into which the bell of Steensel is said to have sunk long ago. On Christmas night, at twelve o'clock, you can still hear the bell ringing in the pit.
46968: In a fen at Bergeik lies a tower bell that rings on Christmas night.
46969: At the Duivelsbrug at Ginneken, on Christmas night the devil rings the bell he threw into the water.
46970: In a marsh at Riel lies the Duivelsput, where a bell rings at 12 o'clock on Christmas night.
46971: There is a Klokkenkuil close to Baarle. This bell rings on Christmas night.
46972: At various places in Noord-Brabant, bells lie sunk in pits, pools and small fens.
46973: A priest from Sambeek did many good works. Among other things he had a church built. He had a bell placed in this church, but forgot to have it consecrated. On Christmas night the devil came to ring the bell and then took it away. The devil threw the bell into the Sambeek marsh, where the devil can still be heard ringing the bell on Christmas night.
46975: At night the devils gather on the Duivelsberg in Riethoven. They dance, sing and drink together.
46977: For some years a ramshackle hut had stood on the heath at Zundert. The devil and his witches held their revels there. One night six brave men went to look at the devil's barn. One of the men said "God bless you" after a comrade sneezed. Then there was a bang and the revels stopped. A hole could be seen in the wall, through which the devil had fled.
46992: Bewitchment of a stable after the cows ate a witch's sandwiches.
47054: Three lads walk from Gilze to Princenhage to go to church for Midnight Mass on Christmas Eve. They stop on the way in 't Ginneken and go into an inn to play some cards and drink. They only lack a fourth man to play with. A rather strange gentleman comes in and is willing to play cards with them. It is very pleasant, but suddenly they hear the bells ringing and they are too late for Mass. In fright one of the lads drops his cards, and when he picks them up he sees that the gentleman has devil's feet. They have played cards with the devil himself. From then on they never missed Mass again.
47070: A cow sometimes comes out of a haunted fen.
47074: A witch makes cats. Warded off by the sign of the cross.
47085: Sometimes the cows had already been milked in the morning.
47088: Near the monastery barracks in Breda it is haunted. The damned souls of prostitutes who in former times offered their services to the soldiers haunt the place.
47107: The oak still has its leaves on the tree in winter and the leaves are notched; this is because of the devil.
47111: Sometimes people get lost at night and only get home in the morning.
47151: An evening encounter with a black cat that keeps growing larger; calling on God; cats on a turnstile; haunted place.
47162: Friars break the spell on a bewitched horse.
47164: Chaplain wards off disaster by praying.
47178: On Christmas night, sounds at the place where a castle sank as punishment.
47180: A light is the soul of a buyer of black goods.
47181: A cat that is struck off a turnpike barrier speaks to a man.
47182: Thirteen hares shot at on Christmas night cannot be hit.
47183: For bewitched livestock, people went to the fathers for blessed bread.
47185: Shortly after someone sees soldiers marching through the sky, war breaks out.
47188: Wizard takes a watch despite it being guarded; has the jack of spades fetch gin.
47196: Wandering for a long time without being able to get home.
47206: A churn is bewitched when churning fails. A cart axle is bewitched when it will not fit together.
47208: A man cannot leave; shortly afterwards a storm damages the house.
47223: A talking cat dares men to throw her into the water again.
47279: Grandpa Bertje is making deliveries when suddenly a huge fog comes up; he prays to Mary and the fog disappears. In her youth Mother heard a story about a woman in the neighbourhood who could supposedly turn into a cat and then attacked a man. The man defended himself, so that the cat had a wound on her front paw; the next day the woman had a bandage around her hand.
47302: Bewitched churn when the butter will not come.
47306: Holding a witch fast by placing your foot crosswise on her footprints.
47309: Gun goes off and the powder explodes, but the shot stays in the gun.
47312: Return of a dead person at midnight at a crossroads when he passes a crossroads.
47313: A passer-by who calls a witch names is held fast.
47327: Warding off a witch with a medal from the fathers.
47329: Chaplain's praying drives away the devil.
47450: Struck by the evil hand; a witch cannot come in over a sign of the cross; a witch looks back when you stand crosswise in her footprints.
47472: A proposal to shoot a witch's dog is prevented out of fear that the dog is the witch.
47501: Bricklaying with mortar mixed with rye flour.
47529: Bells ring in the klokkenkuil (bell pit) on Christmas night.
47535: Witch is blamed for the collapse of a house wall.
47538: Church and tower were built with rye flour.
47544: Witch must walk the same road in the same direction.
47568: How Bakel lost territory to Venray; as punishment, councillors wander about as glowing men.
47574: A boy with threads from a dress between his teeth turns out to be the black dog that bit a girl.
47579: A witch looks back when a foot is placed in her footprint.
47595: If you place your foot crosswise on a witch's footprints, she looks back.
47614: Seeing a comet and a fireball.
47639: A witch looks back when a foot is placed crosswise on her footprint.
47657: Bewitchment when setting one's foot crosswise on a witch's footprints. The witch makes anyone who does so lose their way.
47713: Haunted house with bewitched cattle and people.
47716: A group of cats keeps growing so that a passer-by cannot go on.
48122: It haunts at a gardener's in Den Bosch; every night a blue flame is seen in the shed. When one day the gardener breaks up his shed, he finds a treasure under the floorboards. From then on it no longer haunts there.
49065: Description of the cats' dance: green patches in the shape of a circle on the heath.
49066: The parish priest of Bergeijk witnesses a witches' sabbath. He sprinkles the witches with holy water, turning them into stones. These stones lie on the burial mound in Bergeijk to this day.
49067: Fear of darkness and of the churchyard. The miller's wife turns out to be a witch.
49539: Of four men who want to sell their souls to the devil, three stand in the middle of a witches' circle at midnight and call up the devil, who comes at once. The three are terrified and stay where they are; the fourth fetches the priest to free them. The priest and the devil agree that the devil will be satisfied with the last man in the circle. When the devil notices that the last one is not the third man but the crucifix that has fallen to the ground, he leaves in a rage.
49585: Three men staying up on Christmas Eve so as not to miss Midnight Mass curse when a fourth man does not come to play cards. In the end a traveller plays along, they forget the time, the stranger says the Mass is over anyway, and when one card player wants to pick a card up from the floor he notices the man has a goat's leg. The stranger flees, leaving a smell of sulphur behind.
49599: A black dog disappears when a formula is spoken.
50000: Three men stay up in an inn to be on time for Christmas Mass and play cards with a stranger. Although they know they are doing wrong by not going to Mass, they keep playing. When one wants to pick up a card that fell on the floor, he sees the stranger has a horse's leg and falls unconscious. The others are frightened; the stranger has vanished without a trace but leaves a smell of sulphur behind.
50001: The punishment of a man who falsely swears that he is indicating the boundary between two places is that after his death he must wander with a glowing head at the place where he dared to swear the oath.
50002: A bell stolen from a church tower sinks deeper and deeper with every attempt to dig it out. On Christmas night at midnight the ringing of bells can be heard.
50003: An invisible hand knocks off the hat of a man walking in the cart track. In Limburg there is a fear that if you walk in a cart track you can be pushed aside by a black horse.
50004: A headless lady can be seen in several places. She waits leaning against a birch tree, walks along silently, but does no harm and vanishes when houses come near.
50005: The stampvoet (stamp-foot), a phantom horse, knocks people to the ground at a wild pace and runs on.
50006: In times of plague, the appearance of a white horse in the evening means a new death. After a pilgrimage the horse can be used to bury the dead. As soon as the disease has gone, the horse stays away. A farmer driving his horse and cart one evening past a crossroads near the spot where the horse was last seen notices that his horse refuses to go on. When he takes his horse by the head, he sees the white horse rear up and run away.
50007: A poacher gets a hare in his sights, but his gun fails while more and more hares appear. The next day his gun goes off at once, without him having had to add a silver dime to the charge. Another poacher is asked by a hare whether the others have already gone by.
50008: A big black dog that keeps growing larger walks some way alongside a man.
50009: After a man strikes at a black cat with a stick, a crowd of cats blocks the road.
50010: Seeing a funeral procession between twelve and one at night; a few days later the neighbour is buried in the same way.
50011: After a man has said he is not afraid of meeting the glowing light, a light comes along, settles on the horse's hame and sends the cart off at a furious speed.
50012: A carter whose cart gets stuck calls out that the gloeiige (the glowing one) should harness up, whereupon it sits on the horse and drives off at great speed.
50013: A black object lying on the ground turns out, when approached, to be the gloeiige (the glowing one), which knocks the man over and disappears.
50014: A shepherd sees a fiery wagon with two black horses and a coachman with glittering eyes coming towards him, and it disappears through a pine wood.
50015: Explanation of will-o'-the-wisps, seen as the souls of unbaptised children who must wander about.
