132054: Knight Jan van Vliet is killed because he is said to have had Duke Jan van Bergen poisoned by a witch. The witch is said to have put the poison in his food in the shape of a cat.
132057: Two lovers are murdered in an underground passage in Valkenburg.
132064: After a coin is thrown into a bewitched churn, butter can be made again.
132065: Fear of a house with squeaking inside; later it was thought the sound had come from an experimental radio set.
156150: During the Second World War the Germans often stayed in a woman's house. The soldiers always played with F., the youngest of the woman's nine children. One day the Germans had to flee. After that the woman often dreamed of one of those German soldiers. So she suspected that the young man had died and that he came in her dream to ask her to have masses said. After the woman had a mass said, she no longer dreamed of the German.
156152: In Linden there lived so many witches that they could dance hand in hand around the church with a beehive on their heads. A bewitched girl who lay dying was exorcised by the brown friars of Leuven. A man who saw a witch standing at the girl's door threatened her, and so the girl was saved. From his pulpit the priest had said: "There are twenty-nine of you now, and you are working on the thirtieth. That is a young girl. If you carry on with it, I will name you by name."
156166: A man from Neerwinden said that a werewolf roamed the village. In reality werewolves were pranksters who had disguised themselves with a sheet over their heads to frighten others. A girl who went about as a werewolf left her boyfriend at twelve o'clock and attacked him a little later in werewolf form. The boy wore a red handkerchief around his neck. Later he unmasked his girlfriend as the werewolf when he saw that she had the red fibres of the handkerchief between her teeth.
156188: A girl of sixteen or seventeen who had been visiting her parents and was returning to Leefdaal in the evening saw, when she was halfway, a burning sheaf of straw flying through the air. The girl ran home across the fields as fast as she could. When she got home, the girl told her uncle what she had seen. The man then said: "Then something will happen." Shortly afterwards the war of 1870 broke out.
156193: At the crossroads by the tombeveld, which was also called 't Tommeke, there always sat a ghost in the shape of a black hen. One day the hen began to cackle and flap its wings, and a moment later it vanished again. That black hen sat there to make people have accidents.
156197: Two sorceresses lived in Schepdaal. Pregnant women did not dare walk past their house. The sorceresses had agreed that whoever died first would come back to tell the other what things were like in the afterlife. The dead sorceress came back to say: "Strictly reckoned and little forgiven."
156206: A man went past a bridge over the Gete to the village. When the man came back, he saw a dance tent there, where people called out: "Come on in, my boy!" In the dance tent there was much drinking and merrymaking. When the man said: "God, what is happening to me now!" everything had vanished. The man only had his glass still in his hand.
156212: When many children or animals died on a farm, people often believed they had been bewitched.
156221: Because the weather was bad, the procession was cancelled. The next day the statue of the Holy Trinity was found in the church completely covered in mud. Since that incident the procession has always been held, and the statue is always carried along.
156223: A midwife who was on good terms with her neighbours was often called on when a woman somewhere was giving birth. Later it was discovered that this woman was a witch. When the children she had delivered were a few months old, they wasted away. The children at whose birth that midwife was not called stayed alive.
156230: In the old days it sometimes happened that old people put something in the children's cradles, so that the children did not grow and people had to go to the priest.
156248: In Goetsenhoven there was an old haunted farm. In Napoleon's time an officer wanted to spend the night in the farm with his soldiers. At night four men suddenly appeared, walking around with a coffin. The officer drew his gun, but he could not hit the strange apparitions. The officer dropped dead of fright.
156270: A woman suspected of being a sorceress had a farmhand. One day the sorceress told her farmhand to fetch cow manure from another farm. The farmhand was too lazy to go that far and took manure from the farm's own dung heap. The next day a cow lay dead in the stable. The farmer's wife said: "You did not do what I asked."
156284:
In Bogaarden lived a woman suspected of being a sorceress. At midnight that woman came into a room where a baby lay in the cradle and said: "Keep away, keep away! They are there!"
When the woman found a turnip in the street, she took it to a stable and put it in the cows' manger.
156285: One evening a boy saw a light rising above the woods of Rillaar that looked like the moon. The light rose high into the sky, hung there for a while and then disappeared. A young woman who had murdered her child lived at that spot. The spirit of that child came back in the form of a will-o'-the-wisp.
156305: In Beert lived an old woman who could work magic. One woman had already lost three children through that sorceress's torments. When one of the boys was bewitched, he had himself exorcised by the friars of Lembeek. On the day the father went on pilgrimage to Elingen for his bewitched children, the sorceress stood listening at the door. Strangely enough, one of the little daughters was not susceptible to the sorceress's tricks.
156329: A man still had to plough a small piece of the field with his horse. However hard the man tried, he could not get the plough in the right place. Then the man said to a woman standing watching a little way off, who was suspected of being a sorceress: "You filthy, dirty sorceress!"
156332: An old woman always brought the children mints when their parents were working in the fields. A ten-year-old girl who had eaten one of those mints could not take another step. The friars of Leuven had to come and exorcise the child. That woman read evil books.
156333: Next to a farm was a pond with swans on it. Because those animals had their necks wrung, the farmer sent for the fathers of Affligem. After the clergymen had blessed the farm, the haunting stopped at once. The farmer had to make a novena to a saint.
156349: If an owl sat somewhere in the evening, people believed that someone in that place would die. Such things were easy to explain. A house where someone lay dying was usually the only one with a light burning. Owls came to lit places because there were small flies there.
156357: A woman from Hever who was suspected of being a sorceress was said to have brought the evil hand into the stable on a farm.
156382: A child was always ill after it had been given an apple by a woman. The mother went to have her child exorcised by the priest, who dismissed her suspicions of witchcraft as nonsense. But it was true all the same.
156387: People who were ridden by the mare were really having a nightmare.
156398: If people saw a black cat, they believed they would have bad luck. The same applied when Friday fell on the thirteenth or when someone had walked under a ladder.
156412: People who were ridden by the mare in their dreams could not move for a while.
156419: In Haacht there lived a boy who did not grow. People claimed that this misfortune had been caused by a witch who had swung her leg over the boy's head while saying: "You will grow no more".
156421: A boy had nearly died because he was bewitched. Later that boy still always went on pilgrimage to Tongerlo.
156439: A boy coming back from church with his girlfriend said: "I have to go and relieve myself. Here is a handkerchief. If you see anything, throw the handkerchief at the apparition, and then you need not be afraid." About five minutes later the girl saw a dog and threw the handkerchief at the animal's jaws. When the girl saw her boyfriend reappear a little later, she noticed that he had the fibres of the handkerchief between his teeth.
156455: In Huizingen there lived a woman who went to church every day and often attended masses for sick people. One day she brought a prayer card for a young mother who worked for her and whose little daughter was bewitched. The mother had to say the prayer every day. Half a year later the little daughter was cured.
156466: A man had struck a black cat. The next day he saw that a witch from the village was wearing a bandage around her head.
156472: A girl could make mice during catechism class. Suddenly the girl could no longer make mice because the priest had taken away her magic power.
156479: People who owned books could cover passers-by with fleas.
156494: When the people of Leerbeek walked past the house of a certain woman, their basket suddenly became as heavy as lead and they had to go to the toilet. When they went to the toilet at that woman's house, they were struck by an invisible hand. That was witchcraft.
156499: A woman who had gone to fetch milk at a farm went the wrong way and got lost. That woman had been ridden by the mare.
156510: A man had been to Halle with his mother. All the people who had delivered goods there went to a confectioner's to drink a cup of coffee and eat a roll or a cake. A woman from Elingen or Bellingen, who was said to be a witch, also often came to that baker. So the baker had once gone to the dean of Halle, who advised him to put a relic under the step in front of the door. One day the witch was in the shop with her daughter. The girl said to her mother: "Come, mother". However hard the woman tried, she could not get onto the step.
156524: One evening a girl from Bever had to fetch bread from the back room. When she opened the door, a cat jumped out. The girl was menstruating that day and was badly frightened at the sight of the cat. That evening she could no longer eat or sleep. After that the girl lay in her bed for eighteen years. The girl's mother always went on pilgrimage to the chapel of Zullik. When her mother died, the girl recovered and began to earn her own living. People believed that the girl had been bewitched by her mother and could only lead a normal life again after her mother had died.
156528: A man went to mass every day in the hope that his sister, who practised witchcraft, would mend her ways. But his sister laughed at him and bewitched him. Because of this the man always had bad luck whenever his sister had visited him. One time a child fell ill, another time a pig or a goat.
156532: People who had misfortune in their stable believed they had been ridden by the mare.
156542: A man coming back from the inn was startled at a crossroads by 'the white goat'. That was a joker who had disguised himself with a sheet over his head. On Monday the white goat appeared with a chain and bells. When the drunkard saw the white goat, he ran away in fear.
156543: On the Leuvense Steenweg a girl had been bewitched. She had fallen victim to a strange woman who always put her hand on people's shoulders when she talked to them. At midnight the girl always began to scream, and in the morning she came downstairs exhausted and worn out. The girl did not eat and became completely emaciated. Because the doctor could not help, people sought advice from the fathers of Hasselt. After the clergymen had said prayers over the girl, she confessed that she had been given chocolate by a woman. The priest then said prayers over that witch too. After that there were never any more problems.
156544: A man drove his horse and cart to his field. In the field the horses suddenly stopped, although there was only a little manure on the cart. The man began to curse and did not know why the horses would not go on. A little further on he saw a woman cutting fodder in the field. The man went to her with his dung fork and said: "If you don't get off my field quickly, I'll stab you dead right here with my dung fork." The woman left and the man's horse and cart started moving again.
156545: If you were bewitched, you had to urinate in a little bottle and then seal it tightly. If a woman nearby could no longer urinate, you knew she was the witch. A man from Dilbeek found out in this way who had bewitched him.
156550: A man who went poaching by moonlight saw a figure coming towards him. The two poachers with him did not see the figure, but his dog did see the ghost. A little later the ghost went into the castle of Horst.
156554: In catechism class there was a girl who could conjure mice. After the priest had taken the girl to the sacristy, she could no longer make mice.
156573: On a farm in Sint-Pieters-Leeuw cows often died. People believed that an old woman was responsible for this misfortune. The witch had first also tried to bewitch the farmhand, but he had defended himself and said: "If you try that one more time, you're done for!"
156576: A man coming back from visiting his girlfriend met a dog. He struck at the animal, which then backed away. The man took a detour, but on that road he met the dog again. When he got home he said he had met a dog that would not leave him alone and that could not be hit.
156588: A woman from Haaltert was visiting the parish priest of Aaigem. Since it was already evening when she wanted to leave, the priest said: "Stay here and sleep. There is a bed ready. You will be afraid on the way." But the woman stood her ground and left. When she was about halfway, a fierce wind rose and the leaves flew around her legs. The woman was terrified. She took her rosary and began to pray. Then the wind died down. A little further on, the woman experienced the same thing again.
156609: A soldier was engaged to a girl. When the girl became pregnant, the soldier's father did not want his son to marry her. Some time later the newborn child died while the soldier was in the army. On returning home, the soldier learned that his father had refused to make a coffin for the baby. In his rage the soldier beat his father to death. The soldier's mother laid her husband's body on the railway tracks. For a whole year that house was haunted; the doors flew open and shut by themselves while a voice cried: "Son, you have struck a sorrowful blow!"
156627: A witch could turn herself into an animal, for example a cat.
156631: People who were ridden by the mare fell onto their beds. They wanted to do something, but could not.
156639: In Mijlbeek there lived a woman who was suspected of being a witch. At night she often walked along the lane. The witch drove the wife of the deputy police commissioner so mad that she had to go to a psychiatric institution.
156660: In Willebringen lived a brave man called Sterke Jan. One evening, as Jan was baking cakes, someone called: "I'm falling," to which Jan replied: "Fall then! As long as you don't fall in my cake!" Sterke Jan threw all the bones that fell down the chimney into a corner and went on baking. A little later a ghost stood in the corner and asked if it could eat with him. At the window a second ghost appeared that also wanted to eat a cake. But Jan had baked a wire into the ghosts' cakes, so the ghosts could not eat them. "Wait," said Sterke Jan, "I'll file your teeth for you." Jan hurt the ghosts' lips so badly that the ghosts ran away and never came back.
156671: A farmer's wife who let her cow graze along the ditch saw a woman pass by, who stroked the cow's back and said: "That's a fine animal. That cow surely gives a lot of milk". The farmer's wife said yes. But afterwards she had misfortune in her byre. Her pig died and her cow fell ill, so she had to go to the fathers. The clergymen foretold that the witch would come to her byre at midnight. And so it happened.
156678: In the horse stable a witch appeared in the form of a spider. Once, when someone had struck at the spider, a woman was standing there the next moment.
156683: A man who worked for the priest had quarrelled with him and left. At that moment the priest had said: "I'll make sure you won't have so much as a wooden spoon left in your house!" After that the man had nothing but bad luck. His animals died and the milk of his cows was spoiled. The farmer went to a white canon (Norbertine priest), who told him: "The hand is too heavy. You will notice it when the person who is doing this to you dies". When the priest had to leave his parish because he had grown too old, the farmer had no more bad luck.
156711: In Kessel-Lo there used to be many lodders (werewolves) roaming about. A man who had to roam at night as a lodder would sometimes just walk away from the card game to fetch his skin and his chain from a hollow tree stump. Then lodder set off on his round. One day the man was spied on by his friends. Later the friends secretly took the skin out of the hollow tree stump. Because of this, however, they fell into the power of the Black One and were forced to put the skin back. Many years later people managed to burn lodder's skin in an oven. Lodder stood by crying and wailing, but he was released all the same.
156714: A farmer who could not make butter saw a fat slug sitting on a tub of cream in the cellar. The man grew angry and threw the slug into the stove. Then he heard a loud scream. The next moment a neighbour woman jumped out of the stove and ran outside as fast as she could.
156715: When people had misfortune in their byre, they believed they were bewitched. In Oudenaken people believed a girl had been bewitched. The child cried all the time, grew very thin and no longer wanted to play with the other children. At night the child had to sleep in her parents' bed, or else she would have screamed herself to death. The fathers of Affligem came to say prayers over the child. While they did so, they sweated terribly. The plates and the statue of Saint Roch on the mantelpiece were thrown to the floor. The fathers could have made the witch appear, but they did not want to. Shortly afterwards the child was cured.
156720: A farmhand hardly dared to walk past a certain lime tree, because he was always beaten there.
156730: In Sint-Joris-Winge there lived a seamstress who had not a single customer, because people did not dare come to her for fittings. They believed the seamstress was a witch. When she was in a café, nobody there dared to drink anything for fear that the drink would be bewitched.
156735: In Haacht there lived a woman with a bad reputation. A man noticed that she always looked at him strangely. When it happened once again, the man caught his foot on a post. He fell on his knee and broke his kneecap. The man saw the witch laughing at him.
156736: A man lying in his bed saw the moon come in through the window. The man lay with his mouth open. His wife tried to close his mouth, but could not.
156739: Sometimes old people came back after their death and said: "You must offer a sheaf of grain in Linter or in Miskom". For the dead found no rest when there was a vow they had not kept. Then noises or footsteps were heard in the attic, while nobody could be seen.
156762: In the evenings a man always saw cats coming into his house through the water drain hole. The next day everyone knew what had been said in that house that evening. One day someone hit the cat on the head. The next day a woman from the neighbourhood had a bruised nose.
156767: On a farm in Herne there was much misfortune with the cows and horses. The people who lived there were liberals who usually did not go to church. But because the misfortune did not end, they decided after all to go to Zarlardinge or Affligem. A father came to say prayers over the stables until he was drenched in sweat. At a certain spot the father stopped because he could go no further. At that spot there was a ventilation hole with a ball of horsehair stuck in it. The father took out the ball and burned it. The fire in which it was burned could hardly be kept under control. After that there was no more misfortune in the stables. But the people were ruined and did not dare buy any more animals. The farmer's son who lived there was somewhat infirm. People believed that he too was under the influence of witchcraft.
156778: On a bewitched farm where only one goat remained alive, the priest came to read prayers over the animal. Then he said to the farmer: "If you have some money left, buy another animal. The troubles will end, but you must be careful. Tomorrow something will appear here, but you must not say anything." The next day the farmer and his wife saw an old woman walk three times around a field of sprouts. Then the woman sat down in the middle of the field. A little later she turned into a large dog, which ran off along the Steenstraat.
156789: A child bewitched by a witch was prayed over by the fathers. The fathers said: "If the witch comes in, it will get better. If she does not come in, it will stay this way". The witch came in and the child was cured.
156799: If the priest forgot to close his missal, the witches could not leave the church.
156801: A woman who kept a café and had special powers made sure the horses would not take another step unless the carter first went for a drink in the café. That woman had read evil books.
156804: A man who was ridden by the mare saw a cat approach, which came and lay on him. The man would then start to sweat. When the cat left after a while, its tail dragged across the man's face. The man was always afraid when he had to go to sleep. He would then say: If only little Meike doesn't come again.
156842: In a bewitched house everything flew around. The occupants of a bewitched house in Elingen went to the fathers of Affligem. Through this it turned out that the old mother who lived there was herself responsible for the witchcraft.
156850: A woman coming home from work along the Schoonaarde saw a ghost beside her on the road the whole time. When the woman reached the door of her house, she heard a sigh and the ghost was gone.
156865: A mother had been given a red cabbage by a woman to cook that evening. But when she came home with it, her husband said: "Throw that red cabbage away!" The mother did as she was told. That evening, however, the woman came to visit and said: "You didn't eat my red cabbage! You threw it away!"
156874: Strange things happened in a house in Keerbergen. When a horse had died there, the bones were taken out of the flesh and set against the wall. At a certain moment the bones began to dance by themselves.
156886: In Nieuwrode a child had died. At night that child always came haunting with a little light in its hand. One night the child touched its parents and said: "You have forgotten me, that is not nice!"
156928: The house of an old woman in the Diestsestraat was haunted. Around midnight there was always noise in that house. One day police officers came and said: "If this goes on, we will get involved!" After that the house was no longer haunted.
156934: Someone who was ridden by the mare one night could not call out and had a tight feeling around the heart.
156942: On a farm in Halle the cows were all found untied in the morning. Although the farmer had never told anyone about this, one evening a man said to him: "So, is your place haunted?" The farmer had his stable exorcised, but it did not help. Then that man said: "I will buy a gun." One day the man was seen walking through the village in his best clothes. He wanted to give the impression that he had been to Sint-Truiden to buy a gun. After that day the farmer's cows were no longer untied.
156978: A newly married man saw a white cat walking ahead of him. The man kicked at the animal, but the cat would not be chased off and walked along with him as far as Scherremanskerk.
156989:
A man had a thief arrested who had stolen money from his shop. The thief had to go to prison. A while later the man was elected in the municipal elections. A friend of the thief had also stood as a candidate but was not elected. For revenge, the thief and his friend shot a hare out of hunting season and hung it on the man's property. The man was visited by the police of Wolvertem, who came to search the house. The police found nothing.
During a wedding party there was an accident in which the thief was shot dead when someone's gun suddenly went off. Afterwards the unfortunate culprit claimed he was being pursued by the ghost of the dead young man.
157002: A boy from Booienhoven could make mice by urinating in the dust. After the boy had been prayed over by the priest, to his great regret he could no longer make mice.
157004: If you saw a black cat, you could expect bad luck.
157021: A woman from Hoegaarden was always visited by a man from Kumtich. When that man wanted to leave at nightfall, he began to cry and pray and said: "Please pray with me, because I'm so afraid I'll meet that werewolf again and have to carry it on my back. If that happens, I'm completely worn out by the time I get home."
157038: In the past people often put hollowed-out beets with candles in the hedges, so that passers-by would think they were seeing a stallicht (will-o'-the-wisp). People believed that stallichten were the souls of unbaptised children.
157051: People who had been ridden by the mare had had a bad dream.
157072: People who were drenched in sweat because they were ridden by the mare were actually the victims of a witch, who paralysed them.
157083: Some people from Neerwinden coming back from Landen in the evening met a cat on the way that kept walking between their legs the whole time.
157132: On a farm in Kester a butcher came one evening to slaughter and salt a pig. On his way home the butcher had to pass a café whose landlady was a witch. At that café the butcher saw a black cat walking ahead of him. The butcher struck at the cat with his axe. The next day the café landlady had only one ear left.
157139: A man from Houwaart believed that a black cat could be a witch in animal form.
157152: An old woman from Elingen who was very fond of little children was suspected of being a witch. To amuse the children, she always caught small insects and let them crawl around on her palm. The children would then wonder why the little creatures stayed on the woman's hand.
157154: A man was walking with his friend through the Molenstraatje. The man, who was walking some twenty metres ahead, suddenly saw a fat hare. The hare said to him: "Catch me then." But the man did not trust it and let the hare go. A little later his friend said to him: "Why didn't you catch that hare?" The man replied: "There was something wrong with that hare." The friend replied: "If I had seen the hare first, I would have caught it!"
157201: One evening a man was dared to go and catch one of the mysterious little rabbits on the Keyberg in Bever. The man took the rabbit home and put it in a hutch. The next morning the rabbit had turned into a skull. The frightened people put the skull on a cooking pot outside on the windowsill and tried to shoot at it. The priest forbade them, however, and advised the man to take the skull back to the churchyard that evening and to bring a young child along. When the man arrived at the churchyard that evening with the child and the skull, he heard an invisible figure say: "Lucky for you that you have a child with you, or I would have wrung your neck!"
157249: A man was picking apples in the tree at the corner of his farm. At a certain moment a witch walked by. That night the man could not get to sleep and got up several times. The man was convinced that the witch had bewitched him.
157252: At five in the morning a female worker who was said to be a witch came knocking at a farm in Erembodegem. The woman came to say that the church of Haaltert had burned down at midnight.
157266: Werewolves were pranksters who attacked passers-by. A man who was attacked by a werewolf in Ezemaal wounded the animal. A few days later the man saw someone walking around with a wound on his head. You could unmask a werewolf by injuring it.
157317: At a café in Landen stood a horse and cart with a farmhand sitting on it. Because the horses would not go on, the farmhand fetched a suspect woman and said threateningly: "You'll make my horses go on, or else..." The witch turned round and went home. After that the horses went on again.
157324: A man coming back from Velm at ten o'clock at night found a fat louse on the back of his neck when he got home. Whenever the louse was killed, there was another one the next day. In the end the louse was put in the fire. After that the man got no more lice.
157325: A farmer had an excellent wheat harvest, but he had no barn to store it in. One day the farmer met a stranger, to whom he told his problem. The stranger wanted to build a new barn for the farmer, but in exchange he wanted the farmer's best possession. The farmer consulted his wife, who immediately understood that 'the best possession' was the farmer's soul. The farmer went back to the stranger and said he did not agree to the proposal. When the stranger said the farmer could stay there for another fifty years, the farmer agreed after all. The barn had to be finished by the first cockcrow the next morning. That night the farmer's wife stayed awake to pray, while it thundered and lightninged. At three in the morning the farmer's wife clapped her hands, which made the cock crow early. At that moment there was still an opening of one square metre in the barn. The devils had to leave and the farmer could keep his soul. Several attempts were made in vain to close the hole in the barn. One day a blind man came, who had also been bewitched by the devil. That man bricked up the hole in the shape of a cross.
157333: If people saw a star whose tail touched the earth, the world would end. When the war broke out, people said: "Now the comet has touched the earth."
157338: A sorcerer could fix people in place by magic so that they could not take another step. Afterwards the sorcerer could make them move on again.
157342: A woman whose two children had fallen ill sought advice from a bad woman in Leuven, who advised her to give her children milk into which she had grated a boterpoot (?). The first woman to come by would be the one who had bewitched the children. This is how the mother found out that her own aunt had bewitched her children.
157376: A man who had to haul trees cursed because the roads were in such bad condition. When he saw a woman standing in the doorway of her house, he said: "If you went inside, it would go much better!" When the woman had gone inside, the man could drive up the hill effortlessly. That woman was always out at night. Wherever one went, one always ran into her.
157413: In Oetingen there lived a woman who was bewitched. One day people tried to get her to church, but it took a terrible amount of effort. The witch was a woman with five or six children. She had a hunchback and had been widowed young. To earn her living she had to dig sand.
157415: A feared witch often visited a farm. Because there was much misfortune on the farm, the farmer once went to the monastery. A father came to look at the farm. Just at that moment the witch came to visit. The farmer gave the witch a beating and chased her away.
157424: A man had gone to play cards in Geetbets. At that place, trees had been carted away with horse carts. The workmen had forgotten a bucket there from which they had let the horse drink. The man took the bucket home. On the way, however, it became so heavy that he had to put it down. By the road stood a tall woman, who said: "Now I've got you, haven't I!", but the man went on. He arrived home terrified.
157437: A woman was always followed by a man when she came home at night. Sometimes the man turned into a mewing cat, only to take on his human form again a little later.
157444: A farmer from Baal had no barn to store his harvest in. The farmer met a gentleman dressed in black, who would build him a barn in a single night. In return the farmer had to sign a note selling his soul. The barn had to be finished before the cock crowed for the first time the next morning. The farmer did not believe a barn could be built in one night and went to sleep. When his wife heard the noise towards morning and woke up, the farmer told her what he had done. The woman got up and ran to the henhouse, after which the cock began to crow. In the barn there was still a small hole, which could never be closed afterwards. When the farmer and his wife were standing outside, the note fell at their feet.
157447: In Zoutleeuw a white friar walked around at night, reading a book.
157481: If you met a black cat on the way, you had to be careful, because black cats were witches.
157485: A man had seen a will-o'-the-wisp in d' Else (?) in Halen. Will-o'-the-wisps were the little souls of unbaptised children. If you wanted to baptise such a light, you had to say: "I baptise you alone and no other". Otherwise you would be overwhelmed by will-o'-the-wisps that all wanted to be baptised.
157487: In an orchard in Meldert stood an old temple said to date from the seventeenth century. Few people dare to enter it because they believe it is haunted. The temple was built by two miserly, wicked sisters. In a time of famine those sisters built the temple with grain flour. God will probably have punished them for it later.
157509: In Kersbeek a woman had got a deformed hand through witchcraft. She was then operated on.
157515: A boy had heard that the girl he was seeing was a witch. After all, the girl's mother was a witch too, and it was believed that witchcraft passed from mother to daughter. When the boy was visiting his girlfriend one Sunday, he pretended to have fallen asleep. The boy secretly peeked at the girl and saw her rub her hands with an ointment she had hidden in the chimney. Then the girl said: "Over hedge and over heath" and flew away. A little later the boy copied what the girl had done and said: "Through hedge and through heath." Because the boy had made a mistake in saying the magic formula, he flew through everything and arrived at his destination badly injured.
157517: Priests and friars said prayers against witchcraft. Some people told of witches who could turn themselves into black cats.
157556: A mother had a six-month-old baby who was ill. At two o'clock at night the baby always started crying until half past six in the morning. Someone had already said the child was probably bewitched, but at first the mother did not believe it. The doctor who regularly visited the emaciated baby finally advised the mother to go to the brown fathers (Capuchins) of Leuven. After a father had said prayers over the child, the clergyman said: "Pray that the child may die, for it has been touched by the evil hand". The mother was also given a relic to hang on the door. Then the witch would no longer be able to come in. The witch was the sister-in-law of the informant's grandfather. When that woman wanted to come visiting, she tripped over the threshold.
157565: In the churchyard of Peizegem a grave had sunk. People were so impressed that they came from Steenhuffel and the area around Vilvoorde to look at it. It was even said that the flowers lying on the churchyard at night fell off it during the day.
157571: At a café where a sorceress lived, all the horses came to a standstill. Only after the carters had gone into the café for a drink did the horses start moving again.
157596: A man knocked a black cat off a gate. A bit further on, the man saw the same cat sitting there. The man struck at the cat a second time, and it answered: "If you chase me off one more time, you'll see something else!"
157599: When people saw a sleeping dog or cat somewhere, they often believed it was a witch.
157613: Some people had gone walking along the Varkensputten in Westrode (1). When the men came back from a café by moonlight, they saw a ghost by the Varkensputten. The ghost kept growing bigger and bigger. The men did not dare say a word to each other until they were home. There it turned out that everyone had seen the ghost. Later the men discovered that the 'ghost' had been the reflection of the moonlight in the brook.
157617: On a farm, a farmhand called on the devil to bind the grain in the field quickly. But later, when they wanted to thresh that grain, they could not untie the sheaves. So they went to great lengths to bring that farmhand back.
157639: A woman who had picked up a bag of sweets somewhere was bewitched. She constantly felt as if she were being strangled, and she saw before her the woman who was doing it to her. The other people, however, could not see that witch.
157660:
In Oppem (Brussegem) there stood a barn that had been built by devils.
A farmer who had a rich harvest told a gentleman that his barn was too small to store all his crops in. The gentleman then said to the farmer: "If you sell your soul for nine years, you will have a new barn holding four harvests by three o'clock tomorrow morning. At three o'clock, before the cock crows, you must sell me your soul." The farmer told his wife what had happened to him. At night the farmer and his wife heard the devils making a lot of noise. At a quarter to three the farmer's wife went outside and clapped her hands, which made the cock begin to crow. The barn was not yet finished, however, for a two-metre section still had to be put into the gable. That hole could never be closed afterwards. The farmer could keep his soul because the barn was not finished.
157681: A man sitting on the toilet saw a toad approaching. The man could not catch the animal. If he had killed the toad, one of his relatives would have died.
157703: Something strange once happened in the monastery of the Montfortians on the road from Leuven to Aarschot. A nun who had left the convent came back to haunt after her death. Strangely enough, the nun's absence had never become known.
157705: People who were ridden by the mare at night felt a knee pressed against their chest and their throat squeezed shut.
157757: A farmer who had run out of money was visited by the devil, who said: "If you give me your best horse, you will have everything you want." The condition was that the farmer would give the devil half of everything he acquired. The farmer agreed. When the grain was ripe, the farmer asked the devil which part he wanted: the bottom or the top. The devil thought the grain grew best on the lower-lying part of the field, and said: "The bottom." The farmer, however, gave the devil the stubble and kept the ears of grain for himself. The next year the farmer again asked the devil which part of the harvest he wanted. The devil decided not to be caught out again and said: "The top." This time, however, the farmer had planted potatoes in his field. The devil got the leaves and the farmer had the potatoes.
157790: People who were ridden by the mare walked in circles all the time. Perhaps these people were really drunkards who could no longer find their way.
157807: Two men had been sitting in a café, where a witch had talked to them. As the men walked home, they found that the beard of one of them was on fire. A moment later the fire was gone, but the other man's beard was on fire.
157821: In Kaggevinne an unmarried woman is said to have died after being bewitched.
157836: If you were confronted with the werewolf, you had to throw your blue apron at the beast. The werewolf then had to unravel the cloth completely. One day a man who had played the werewolf was unmasked during the midday meal because he still had the threads of the apron between his teeth.
157837: In Humbeek a woman often went around asking people for all sorts of things. Wherever that woman had been, people and animals fell ill.
157878: In Overwinden there lived a witch who went to a farm to ask for peat for her chickens. They refused to give her peat and said: "The peat we have left is for our own chickens". That afternoon the farm had no more water. They went without water there for four years. When the woman went to fetch her first tub of drinking water for the cows, something flew into her eye and she got 'the spot' on her eye.
157887: A man had been bewitched after eating an apple he had been given by a woman.
157889: A boy going to the field was given a sweet by a woman who worked on his parents' farm. Shortly afterwards the boy got a headache and had to go home. On the way, however, he fell into a hedge, and someone brought him home in a wheelbarrow. The doctor visited the boy twenty-seven times. But because his health did not improve, the parents went to the fathers of Affligem. There the mother was advised to do a nine-day penance and take communion. She also had to put the child in a tub of water into which she had to sprinkle hayseed and bran. The mother did not do the latter, but she did keep the penance. Nine days later the child was cured.
157895: On a farm where a cow was ill, they called the vet and the father, but in vain. All the animals on that farm died except one pig. When that pig was slaughtered, the meat turned out to be rotten. A dean from Asse came to advise the people to do penance. He said that otherwise the illness would soon pass to the people. Moreover, they were not allowed to accept anything for free. For everything they gave away, they had to ask money, even if only one centime. The people believed the evil had been done to them by a witch who lived a little further on. That witch had once come to measure the butter churn because she claimed she wanted to buy one too. Twenty years later, however, she still had no butter churn.
157943: A man went to the witch doctor because his wife was ill. The witch doctor said to the man: "When you come home, someone will have visited who wanted to give your wife something. If your wife has accepted it, she will die". When the man came home, he was told that his wife had been given a pear by a visitor. The woman had eaten the pear and eventually died of it.
157949: On a farm potatoes were found under the threshold of the cowshed. A witch had done that.
157950: People who were ridden by the mare felt as if they were going to die. When going to bed you must never put your shoes or slippers with the toes under the bed. Otherwise you could be ridden by the mare at night. For that reason you must not put your shoes at the foot of the stairs either.
157965:
Three women stood at the castle of Horst. Two of them saw at the castle a coach with two horses, hung with gold. A moment later the coach had vanished. The other woman had not seen the coach.
Some believed that people who had seen such an apparition would not live much longer.
157986: A man had sold his soul to the devil in exchange for a new barn that had to be finished the next morning before the first cockcrow. At night the devils came to build the barn. The farmer's wife got up in the night, went outside and clapped her hands, which made the cock crow early. The devil had lost because the barn was not yet finished at that moment.
157987: A man in Antwerp fell victim to the mare. It was an old woman who came in silently and then hovered over him. As there was light in the room, the man could see the mare very clearly. The man could only move once the mare was gone. The man was so frightened that he no longer even dared to sleep in his little room.
158001: A man from Tollembeek claimed he had seen a returned dead person appear, who had said: You will live only two more years. The prediction came true.
158004: A farmer who had no room to store his harvest was approached by a gentleman who said: "I will build you a barn before the cock has crowed three times tomorrow morning. In exchange, I want your best possession." Not knowing that the gentleman meant his soul, the farmer agreed. At night the farmer's wife wondered where all the knocking and rumbling came from, whereupon the farmer told her about his agreement with the gentleman. The farmer's wife immediately understood that her husband had sold his soul. She got up and went to the henhouse, where she clapped her hands and imitated a cock's crow three times. Then the cock crowed three times. The devils dropped everything and ran off. The barn was almost finished at that moment, but there was still one hole in it. There was not a single cross in the building.
158015: A woman from Zoutleeuw had a baby. A neighbour who often came to visit always took the baby in her arms. Although the child ate and drank enough, it grew very thin. The child's mother went with her sister to the fathers of Sint-Truiden to have prayers said over the child. They also had to put a prayer under the child's pillow and a relic under the threshold. Then the witch would no longer be able to come in. And so it was. The child recovered and grew up to be a healthy woman.
158032: A girl was covered in black pimples for a whole year because she had accepted a sweet from a woman suspected of being a witch. When that woman stood at the door of a byre, the cows suddenly gave no more milk.
158034: On a farm in Opheule the people lived off the income from their butter. One day butter could no longer be made on that farm and the butter churn was full of stinking water. The farmer became convinced that he had been ridden by the maar (nightmare spirit) and went to the friars. A friar came to read prayers over the farm and gave the farmer a medal to put under the churn. After that the farmer could make good butter again. He also knew which woman had bewitched him.
158043: In an inn, a three-year-old child had had convulsions. People said the child was bewitched and took it to the fathers of Affligem. The father placed a dove on the child's head, but the bird let its wings droop. The child died of the convulsions.
158055: Near the Nesselberg, four priests sat playing cards at night by the light of four candles.
158057: A newborn baby that cried all day was prayed over by the parish priest. The priest asked the mother to open the mattress the baby slept on. When the woman did so, she found in the mattress a scrap of cloth from each of the child's clothes, along with pins and parts of birds. The woman took all of it to the priest, who said: "If all this had become one whole, your child would have died."
158080:
When a gravestone had risen up in the churchyard of Meise, people believed a dead person had risen from his grave.
In the end it was discovered that a nest of moles had pushed the stone up.
158087: A woman was ridden by the mare twice in one night.
158130: A woman who had accepted something from a witch was seized by the throat the following night. The woman quickly said: "Jesus, Mary, Joseph" and then immediately threw what she had received from the witch into the stove. A burst of flame shot up to the ceiling and a hellish noise could be heard.
158167: Four poachers from Hekelgem had often seen a few hares playing right in front of them near the chapel of Sint-Anna, without ever managing to shoot even one. One day one of the poachers went home to fetch a paasnagel (an Easter nail, a blessed nail). When he came back, however, the hares ran away. The next time the poacher kept the paasnagel hidden and put it in his gun. This time he did manage to hit the hares.
158190: A farmer sent for a sorcerer because his cow gave only a few litres of milk. When the sorcerer entered the farmyard, fire could be seen everywhere. The sorcerer said: "Oh dear, oh dear, there is an evil one at work here". The sorcerer was busy there for a long time and finally said: "Yes, that woman has already caused many animals to die".
158193: A will-o'-the-wisp was a light that flew around people all the time. Such lights were the souls of children who had died unbaptised. If you baptised a will-o'-the-wisp, it flew to heaven.
158199: Stalkaarsen (will-o'-the-wisps) were glowing candles standing in the field that always leapt further away when you tried to come closer. Stalkaarsen were the souls of unbaptised children.
158211: A woman had given birth to twins. One boy grew up to be a healthy man. The other did not live much past thirty and could not walk or speak. The mother believed that someone had picked that boy up and bewitched him.
158237: At de Vaart there was a sick child that had to be walked about every night. Every Tuesday the child was taken to the parish priest to have prayers read over it. People claimed that the child was bewitched.
158254: When bringing in the harvest went smoothly, people sometimes said the devil had helped in the field.
158261: A man who had vowed to go on pilgrimage to Scherpenheuvel died before he had kept his promise. When the man came back to haunt, people asked the ghost what it wanted. Because the people did not say "Go ahead" when they set off for Scherpenheuvel, they had to carry the ghost the whole way.
158274:
A woman could make grain white and black. She could also fly with her umbrella. That woman had been given a book by a witch in the Scherpenheuvel field. In the end the priest of Averbode took that book away from her. 
The woman wanted to go on a pilgrimage around an apple tree in which, according to her, there were lots of little children. Those were the children who came to torment her because she had bewitched them.
158300: In Haasrode a woman was milking her cow when suddenly a large black spider fell into the bucket. The woman went to fetch a stick, but when she came back the spider was gone. When the woman went to wash at the brook later that day, a little old woman suddenly stood behind her and said: "Well, you went after her with a stick, but you couldn't hit her, could you!"
158302:
A mother had put the cradle of her newborn child by the kitchen door, because the weather was fine and that way the child could enjoy the fresh air. A neighbour always came to ask how the child was doing. Whenever the neighbour reached out her hand towards the cradle, the mother pulled her child away because she knew the neighbour had special powers. Eventually the neighbour said: "It seems like a porcelain child, because nobody is allowed to touch it!" 
One day, however, the mother had not been quick enough, so the neighbour had managed to touch the child. The following night the baby lay trembling and crying. The mother sent for the parish priest, who said some prayers and sweated like a horse while doing so. The clergyman said: "I think it will be too late after all". Shortly afterwards the baby died.
158305: A woman from Boutersem was crying because her son had to report for military service. The son then said: "You needn't cry, mother. If I die, you will know". Some time later the woman always heard a knocking on the bed at night. Because she was worried, she went on pilgrimage to Scherpenheuvel. During the consecration the woman suddenly felt a blow on her shoulder, after which she fainted. The priest stood by the altar and said to the people: "Go away, for here a woman has saved a soul from purgatory". A hand was burned into the woman's shoulder cloth. Since then the woman has heard no more knocking.
158308: In a distillery in Moorsel a stoker was murdered every night. The priests advised the people to watch for the first cat that came in there. A brave man who went to keep watch there at night with an axe in his hand saw a grey cat come in and sit on the rim of the kettle. A little later there was a knock, and the grey cat said: "Jan has said you may come in." In this way dozens of cats came in, and they all sat around the kettle. Then the big grey cat said: "We can begin." The man cut off one of the big cat's paws with his axe, after which all the cats ran off. The next day the maid did not come downstairs. She lay in her bed because she had lost an arm. She was the witch.
158321: A toad always came into a house through the water drain hole. One day the people seized the toad with red-hot tongs. The next day a woman was walking around with a burnt nose.
158323: In Geetbets lived a boy who could make white mice from the earth he scraped off his shoes.
158325: A man from Bierbeek who had no barn to store his harvest in made a pact with the devil, who had said: "If you sell me your soul, you will have a fine barn even before the cock crows for the first time tomorrow morning." Around four in the morning the barn was almost finished. The farmer's wife got up and clapped her hands, which made the cocks begin to crow. At that the little devils quickly fled. In the barn there was still a hole, which afterwards could only be closed by placing a statue of Mary in it. If the statue of Mary was taken out, the hole was open again.
158340: In Woluwe lived a witch who always tried to give sweets to the children. The children were not allowed to accept anything from her, or else they would be bewitched. When people walked past that witch, she stood grumbling the whole time.
158341: Several members of a church council and of a choir were said to be involved in witchcraft. One of those men was even said to have passed the magic arts on to his son when the son was still a child.
158348: When the church in Kokejane (a hamlet of Herne) had just been built, a priest left his missal open after Mass. When the priest came back later that day for the evening service, he found that some people were still sitting in the church. They were witches who could not get out.
158352:
Three farmhands working on a farm were not allowed to go to the fair in Asbeek until they had threshed three sacks of grain. Because the work was going slowly, the lads stood there cursing and moping. A shepherd who learned what the problem was said: "That's nothing." He stuck his staff into the heap of grain and the next moment the three sacks filled up.
When the lads came back later to carry on threshing, everything was empty.
158362: A boy had heard it said that his girlfriend and her mother were witches. One evening the boy left his girlfriend's somewhat earlier. Then he went for a glass of beer with his friends. On their way home the boys felt a terrible wind and saw a woman come flying on a broomstick. Terrified, the boys fled home. After that incident the boy left his girlfriend.
158375: A woman from the neighbourhood always came to visit a family who had a small child. The little boy would not grow and had thin little legs. At night it seemed as if the child was having a heart attack. The parents took the boy to Sint-Pieters-Leeuw to have prayers read over him. The friars also gave the mother something to put under the door and said: "On your way home you will meet a woman. She will speak to you, but you must not answer her". What the friars had predicted came true. The mother was insulted and abused by the witch. After the mother had put the holy object under her threshold, the witch could no longer come in and shouted: "You filthy shrew! What have I done to you that I may not come in here any more?" After that the woman never visited again.
158389:
A boy from Wommersom was coming back from the fair with his girlfriend. On the way the boy said: "You go on ahead. I still have to ask a friend something. If a dog comes up to you, throw your handkerchief at its jaws." The girl went on. When her boyfriend rejoined her, she saw that he had the fibres of the handkerchief between his teeth.
When a certain hour had come, the werewolves had to put on their skin and go out.
158404: On a farm in Werchter where all the animals had died through witchcraft, the people went to the friars. The clergymen advised them to dig a deep pit in the stable and put something in it. The people followed the advice and were thus freed from the evil.
158408:
A girl often played with a friend whose godmother was a witch. The girl's mother had often urged her daughter never to go into the godmother's house. One day, however, the girl did go in. She was given a sweet by the witch. Luckily the girl had no trouble, but after that she never went into that witch's house again. 
A neighbour girl, however, did become bewitched after she had found a book in the witch's house. The girl had started reading the book. When the witch saw it, she became angry and snatched the book out of the child's hands. Because of the influence of that book, the girl and her family were always thrown into the brook when they were almost home.
158422: If you were ridden by the mare, a sorceress lay on you and grabbed you by the throat, so that you could not move. In reality such experiences were probably caused by poor digestion.
158435: Black cats that sat on the roof at night were witches.
158461: The sister of a blacksmith held needles in the fire to torment people. As a result the victims became completely emaciated. Witches also sometimes gave apples and sweets to children to bewitch them. To find out whether such a child would survive, people went to Lourdes with a piece of the victim's clothing. If the garment floated, the child would survive. If it sank, nothing more could be done.
158499: A boy's father told him to take a sack of coal to a woman people were afraid of. Because the boy did not dare, his brother went. When he came home, he found he was covered in fleas from head to toe.
158546: A sorceress is said to have once lived in Hamme. When a farmer with his six-horse wagon passed the spot where that woman was cutting grass, the horses suddenly would not go on.
158565:
Women who were poorly dressed were suspected by many people of being witches. 
One was not allowed to accept anything from such women, because then one would be bewitched.
158630: During the First World War a beer merchant was bewitched by his own mother. The man suffered greatly and eventually died. Before his death he had said: "If I were to recover, I would hang my mother from a tall Canadian poplar". When witches found no other victims, they had to bewitch their own children.
158639: On a farm that had a lot of misfortune, one day a rat was seen coming in through the water drain hole. The farmer's wife quickly poured boiling water on the rat, which then ran off whimpering. The next day the farmer's wife met her neighbour, who was wearing a bandage around her arm.
158643: In Wolvertem a girl had died at the age of twenty. Because people believed that the girl had been bewitched, they burned all her bedding when she died. At that moment jeering was heard and a crow was seen flying high in the trees.
158649: A man out at night saw a black cat sitting by an old willow. When the man hacked at the cat with his axe, another cat appeared, until in the end the man saw cats everywhere.
158655: Someone dressed up as a ghost, with a sheet over his head, walked around on the church path.
158667: A man riding on horseback to fetch the midwife met a woman on the way, who said: "Now you'll be there quickly". The man had to go along a lane, but there was no way he could get into that lane.
158668: A mother had to keep watch over her children at night because there were always meowing cats around the house. To pass the time the mother started baking pancakes. The mother went outside with a red-hot pan and hit the cats on the head. The next day four women from the village had a burnt jaw.
158690: A thirteen-year-old girl who was picking up potatoes in the field was given some marshmallows by a woman. The woman said to her: "Eat them all by yourself, because the other children have had enough already". The girl ate the sweets. When she got home, however, she felt so bad that she no longer knew what she was doing and ran like a madwoman against the cows in the cowshed. The farmer's wife fetched holy water and blessed roses from the procession and began to pray to drive out the evil spirits. When the girl came to, she did not know what she had done. When she told about the marshmallows, people were convinced that the girl had been bewitched.
158707: On the Rilroheide in Dworp lived a woman who had to sit in a chair for twenty-five years because she could no longer move. That woman had been ridden by the maar (nightmare). A neighbour woman had done this to her.
158713:
If you saw someone you suspected of being a sorceress, you had to say: "Over the hedge and over the heath." Sorceresses would then immediately fly up into the air.
If you made a mistake and said: "Through the hedge and through the heath," you were dragged through everything.
158718: A man saw a hare as big as a calf running in the meadow. The man was too afraid to shoot at the hare. Near that spot lived a woman suspected of being a witch. The man believed the hare was that witch, appearing in the shape of an animal.
158735: A pregnant woman lived in a house in Neerlanden where a witch was said to have once lived. One day, as the pregnant woman was calmly coming down the stairs, she fell all the way to the bottom. The woman's husband died in an accident.
158736: If people heard magpies chattering, they believed misfortune was coming.
158766: A man from Velm had a lot of misfortune with his animals. The man had his farm read over and put a cross or a holy object under the stairs, so that the witch could no longer get in. In a cottage in Attenhoven the people could not bake bread. The dough was always rotten. A woman always came to visit that house, and she covered the children with lice. When people walked past that woman, they tucked their thumbs into their fists to make the witch powerless.
158775: A man who had sold his soul to the devil had to walk the streets every night at twelve o'clock until the devil had been to him. Then the man got his money and had to walk about until one o'clock. That man could open a closed door or gate by striking it with his cap. He could also conjure a house full of rats by throwing his cap into that house.
158797: In the old days cows stood in deep stables without a floor. The cows stood with their heads in a ring fastened with chains. When the cows rubbed their heads against that ring, people often believed the animals were bewitched. Sometimes it was so bad that a beam was rubbed through, so that a new one had to be hung.
158804: Witches could turn themselves into a spider's web to get in somewhere.
158807: A farmer's wife had bought a piglet somewhere. Every day a woman came to look at the piglet. Because the animal would not grow, the farmer's wife sought advice from the friars of Edingen, who advised her not to let that woman into the house or the pigsty any more.
158812: A woman who had been guilty of blasphemy in an inn was followed on her way home by a figure who could make himself so tall that he could look over the window shutters. That was the devil.
158829: A boy who was often out with his dog cart regularly received something from a blind woman. One day the boy fell ill. He had croup. When the blind woman was no longer let in, the boy quickly recovered.
158839: When people were jumped on along the way by someone who made them carry him, they said they were being ridden by the mare.
158854: A farmer's wife had a visit from a cattle dealer. While the farmer and his wife sat in the kitchen haggling over the price with the dealer, the dealer gave the farmer's wife a pat on the shoulder. The next day the farmer's wife had lice all over her head.
158855: In Lint some people had unjustly taken a sum of money for themselves. A while later strange things happened to them; there was always a racket in the horse stable, and a sow died with her piglets and a cow with her calf. The woman of the house always saw a little creature jump in through a crack in the window, but the other occupants did not see it. One day a strange little creature without entrails was indeed found in the bed. Finally the people went to the friars, who asked whether they owed anyone anything. The friars came to read prayers over the house until they were drenched in sweat, and to be safe the people also had a number of masses said. After that no more strange things happened in the house.
158866: A man who had stayed too long at the café had to walk home through the fields at night. In the fields he heard something making a slapping sound, though nothing could be seen. The man hurried inside and shut the door. His coat was still caught in the door, but he was too afraid to open it again.
158898: In France there were people who stuck pins into little dolls to harm others.
158909: A man who was ridden by the mare every night resolved to tie a knife to his body with the blade pointing up. In reality the man was simply dreaming.
158946: A man with an incurable illness sought advice from the friars of Affligem, who told him he had been bewitched by a witch. The friar had told the man: "The first person who passes your house tomorrow is the witch". The woman who came by first the next morning thus became the victim of a painful misunderstanding.
158973: The brewery of K. in Gempe was haunted. One day a priest was found in the wall of the brewery, who had been walled up alive there. After the dead priest had been taken out of the wall, the brewery was no longer haunted.
158979:
In Grimde lived an evil witch who bewitched people by touching them or giving them something. 
One day a little boy was given a plate of chips by that witch. From the day the boy had eaten the chips, he had terrible dreams. At night he saw dogs coming at him. Sometimes he also saw images of a black beast or of the witch's face. Eventually the father took the boy to Sint-Rochus, where prayers were read over the child. After that the boy had no more problems.
158981: A woman claimed she had been bewitched by a witch from the neighbourhood. That witch had in fact visited the woman. Before she was down the hill, the woman was dead.
159001: In a house a mysterious knocking on the stairs was heard every two weeks. The man had already called out "Come in", both kindly and angrily, but it had not helped. So the man told his neighbours that he had the evil hand in the house.
159013: A farmer had got into trouble because he had had a bad harvest. The farmer was visited by a gentleman who wanted to buy his field. Because the farmer did not want that, the gentleman said to him: "If you won't sell your field, then sell me your soul. You will have everything you need." The farmer signed a contract in his own blood. One of the farmhands had overheard the conversation between the farmer and the devil. Towards morning the farmhand went to the barn with his lantern, so that the cocks began to crow early and the farmer could keep his soul. Later the devil's barn in Adegem burnt down.
159021: Sometimes a witch would say: "When you dig up potatoes, you will have a pit full of eggs". And indeed there were eggs in the ground instead of potatoes.
159047: A woman from Zichem picked up a baby that was lying in a gutter. At night that baby jumped up as high as the ceiling. It lived a few more days and then died. That woman had bewitched the baby.
159048: If a sorceress was sitting in the church, the parish priest could not leave his altar. Only when the sorceress was outside could the clergyman close his missal and leave.
159066:
Because the weather was bad, the statue of Mary was not taken along on the procession to Scherpenheuvel. The next day the statue was found in the church of Attenhoven, smeared with mud.
That procession had been held in Attenhoven for three hundred years. Back then a plague epidemic had broken out because of contaminated water from a well. The people then promised to walk to Scherpenheuvel every year if the epidemic came to an end.
159082: On the Warande in Rummen there were said to be underground passages where the lords of the castle went to hide when danger threatened. One day a miller came to a woman whose grain he was supposed to have ground. On arriving, however, the miller realised he had forgotten the woman's flour. Because the woman was very upset about it, the miller promised to bring the flour that evening. The woman thought that very kind and treated the miller that evening to a hearty meal. When the miller then took a back road home, at midnight he saw on the Warande a table with young ladies sitting around it drinking wine. The miller was also given a cup of wine. But when the miller said "santé", the whole scene vanished in one stroke. The man went to the parish priest, who advised him to take the cup back to that place in broad daylight. The man did as he was advised. The next day the cup had disappeared.
159084: If people heard a dog howling at a farm all the time, they believed something terrible would happen at that farm.
159093: A witch could make objects disappear or turn them into a cat.
159102: In the church of Winge people always heard bells ringing at night. When the sexton went to look, he saw a ghost in a white shirt come from behind the altar. It was a returned dead person.
159105: Sometimes people would lay bread on the gravestones in the churchyard. If the bread was gone the next day, it was believed that a ghost had taken it.
159122: When going on a pilgrimage for a dead person, one had to put a stick or an umbrella by the door and say: "Go on ahead, I will follow you". Otherwise one would be drenched in sweat from having to carry the ghost.
159123: A girl went to the field against her will to bind the harvest. She would much rather have gone to the fair. The girl was visited by a gentleman, who said: "I will see that all the sheaves are bound if you give me the first thing you bind tomorrow morning." The girl agreed, but that evening told her mother what had happened. The mother said to her daughter: "Before you get dressed tomorrow morning, you must bind a sheaf of straw!" That night the girl heard a terrible noise, but she was saved by her mother's advice.
159127: Two children of a farmer had already died. When the third child was gravely ill, the farmer stoked his hearth hot. A woman who came to fetch milk every day came to ask how the child was. The farmer bolted all the doors and said: "You must undo the harm you have done, or else I'll burn you." At first the woman said she could not do it, but when the farmer was about to throw her on the fire, she said: "Wait, I must first fetch something from home." The farmer replied: "You're not leaving here. One of my farmhands or maids will fetch what you need." The woman sent a maid to her house to take a small wax heart from a chest. The woman pulled lots of pins out of that heart. After that the child in the cradle was cured.
159142: A woman who worked at a castle experienced strange things. The pillow she slept on became very thick. When the French chambermaid hit the pillow, it was suddenly completely flat.
159146: A poacher waiting for hares in the hedge heard laughter and saw the hedges moving back and forth.
159163: In the past people believed that will-o'-the-wisps were the souls of unbaptised children.
159178: On a farm a toad was found in the cellar. The farmer's wife threw the toad outside with her coal shovel. Because the toad was back the next day, she threw the animal into the fire. When she then took her child out of the cradle, she found it was covered in ants. The next day the toad had disappeared, but the ants were still there. The farmer's wife went to the friars of Affligem, who said to her: "Every day a woman comes to your house to drink coffee. You must not let that woman in any more, but you must not harm her either". When she got home, the farmer's wife sent the visitor away. The child, however, never grew up healthy. The farmer's wife sold her house and went to live elsewhere.
159188: In Rumsdorp lived a girl who could make mice by throwing away a little earth. A priest was sent for to pray over the girl. After that the girl could no longer make mice because the priest had taken away her magic power.
159194: A woman who lived on the Vinkeberg saw three cats sitting along the way. A man advised the woman on no account to hit or kick the cats. After that incident the woman was so frightened that she no longer dared to come home by that road.
159198: On Christmas Eve people were playing cards in the café 'De Oude Eik'. Around midnight one of the players got up and said: "It's Christmas. I'm going to Mass". The other three players stayed seated. They were playing whist and were one player short to continue the game. One of the men said: "We need a fourth man, even if it's the devil, we'll play on". The next moment a strange man sat down at the table, whom no one had seen come in. When one of the players bent down to pick up a dropped card, he saw that the strange man had horse's legs. The player became afraid and told the landlady that the devil was sitting with them. The landlady then informed the priest, who came to sprinkle the café with holy water and opened the door. The devil said: "You can shut the door, for I'll leave the way I came". Then the devil disappeared up the chimney.
159213: People who had a lot of bad luck believed they were being ridden by the maar (nightmare).
159225: People who were ridden by the mare had fallen victim to a sorceress.
159227: In Hever lived a witch who had a quarrel with a woman from the neighbourhood. She caused that woman to have much misfortune and her children to fall ill. The youngest child even died.
159229: A farmer's wife whose cows always died often had a man visiting. The woman therefore believed that the man came to bewitch her cows. When that man had died, no more animals died on the farm.
159234: A man who went to play cards every evening was in the habit of coming home late. One dark night the man was approached by a gentleman, who said: "Friend, I have a nice piece of cheese here for you." When the man came home with the cheese, his wife said: "Throw that cheese out into the garden!" At first the man would have none of it, but in the end he followed his wife's advice. The next morning the piece of cheese had turned into a skull.
159278: A girl who had lost her job promised one evening to the soul of the faithful person who had died most recently that she would have a mass said with the first wages she earned once she had work again. At the street corner the girl met a young man, who said: "Go to that farm, for there is work there". When the girl entered the farm, they asked who had sent her. The girl described the young man and saw his portrait hanging on the wall in the farmhouse. "That cannot be true", they replied, "that young man is dead!" After the girl had received her first wages from the farmer, she no longer thought of the mass she had promised. When the money began to rattle in the chest, the girl remembered her promise and had the mass said.
159299: If the family of a deceased person had not kept certain promises, the dead person came back at night to haunt. One could even get into a quarrel with a dead person who had returned.
159305: A man often went to the fields to fetch feed for the rabbits. One day the boy saw an old woman walk past. When the boy went home that day, he itched all over and found he was full of lice. By saying a certain word, one could make witches powerless.
159306: A poultry dealer was at a widow's to choose some chickens he wanted to buy. The dealer was to come and collect the chickens a week later. When the dealer came to the widow the next week, the chickens were still running around. The dealer said to the widow: "But you still haven't caught those chickens!" The widow replied: "That doesn't matter" and she brought out a book containing strange words. A little later the widow picked up the chickens and put them in the dealer's basket. When the dealer was then standing in the widow's house, all the doors flew open, although there was no wind outside. That widow was a witch.
159316: Sorceresses were usually old women. They owned a small wax doll. If they pricked that doll with pins and wished a child harm, the child felt pain.
159322: A farmer and his wife driving to the market in Vilvoorde suddenly saw a stallicht (a ghostly light) appear by the horse. People believed that such lights appeared because something still had to be done for someone who had died.
159323: In a house two children had already been born with an eye ailment. One day an old woman came there to ask for alms. After she had been given alms, she said: "The third child will be healthy". And so it was.
159332: In a haunted farmhouse a wind could sometimes be heard rising, after which all the doors and windows flew open.
159339: A boy from Oplinter could make mice by throwing earth on the ground. One day the priest came to the boy. The clergyman read from a book. The boy had to put his foot in the priest's shoe. Afterwards the child began to cry because it could no longer make mice.
159345: A man walking to his daughter's house was followed on the way by a big black dog. When the man reached the farm, he quickly went inside and shut the half-door behind him. The dog, however, jumped up against the door with its paws, and the man crept into his bed terrified. The man had a heart attack from fear and died.
159361: In a house a baby in the cradle had fallen ill after a woman had come to visit. Because the doctor could not help, the people went to a clergyman, who advised them to keep that visitor out from then on. In the end the child died. At that moment the people's black dog howled. The witch was standing at the gate.
159376: The owner of a liqueur shop was a beautiful woman who was very popular with the farmers' sons of the village. A married farmer with three small children also often went secretly to the liqueur shop and only came home late at night. The farmer no longer knew what he was doing. At two in the morning he took the horses out of the stable to go to the field. Nobody could make the man understand that it was not yet morning. The doctor was called. The man was put to bed and a kind of white cap was wrapped three times around his head. Then the man cried: "Stop that, because I have to go!" When the cap was removed, the man was dead. Everyone knew that the owner of the liqueur shop had special powers. After the farmer's death, prayers were read over the farm. The priest who did it sweated heavily.
159378: An innkeeper's wife had asked her sister to bring a bottle of holy water. The sister brought the bottle and put it on a table in the inn. A while later a witch came into the inn and asked for a glass of gin. The innkeeper's wife took the bottle of holy water, but the witch immediately said: "I don't want that, that's holy water".
159382: On a farm people were praying the rosary in the evening. Suddenly they heard the sound of the mill in the attic, although no one was there. That was haunting.
159384:
A man who was often ridden by the mare felt as if he was being grabbed by the throat and could not call out or breathe. The man was freed of the mare by hanging a 'losse moëlle' (1) at the foot of his bed.
That man's father hung two stones tied together above his bed to protect himself against the mare.
159403: In the past people believed that black cats were witches.
159424: In Sint-Martens-Lennik lived a woman four of whose children had died. Only her eldest child had survived. The woman had prayers read over her by the friars of Affligem. After that she had two more daughters, who survived. The woman believed her other children had died through witchcraft.
159441: A five-year-old girl could make mice by throwing a handful of earth on the ground. People believed the child had not been baptised and took her to the priest. The priest baptised the child and prayed over her. Afterwards the child received a beautiful book from the priest. But the girl began to cry because she could no longer make little mice.
