159443: A stable hand who was changing jobs yet again moved all his clothes and other belongings to his new lodgings. On the way the man drank jenever in a café. It was around Sint-Andries (30 November); that was also the day the rent fell due, which left many small farmers in great financial trouble. At the Diepestraat (also called Zes Wegskes) the man had a strange experience. From that crossroads one could go to the Kaarlijk, to Amelgem, Oppem, Wolvertem and Meise. There was also the grave of a commander from the time of Napoleon. When the farmhand reached that crossroads at midnight, he saw an old woman coming towards him, surrounded by a big brood hen and a good thousand black chicks with shining eyes. The man could not take another step and was attacked by the chickens. He could get no further and sank down against a tree trunk. When the man woke many hours later, there was no trace of the haunting left and he could continue on his way to the farm in Amelgem.
159451: In Elewijt people often saw stallichten (will-o'-the-wisps). Such lights looked like long beams of light that floated over the field and suddenly plunged down. People believed that stallichten were the souls of unbaptised children.
159458: Between Bever and Tollembeek a light used to be seen in the wood every night. Nobody dared to point at that light. If you did, the light would settle on that person's hand and the person had to throw it into the water. Then there was a lot of work baptising all those unbaptised children.
159468: In the Gustaaf de Donderstraat lived a farmer whose piglets had all died because of a witch. To protect the house against witches, medals were put under the doors.
159494: Some people went to the priest because they saw a dead man returning and did not know what to do. The priest advised them to make a pilgrimage to Scherpenheuvel. The dead man was said to have promised that pilgrimage but never to have kept his promise. After the pilgrimage had been made, the man no longer returned.
159505: On a farm strange things always happened when a certain woman had come to fetch a litre of milk. Afterwards the cows gave no more milk and no butter could be made. A friar came to bless the farm and said: "Someone always comes here to fetch milk, but you must not give that person anything any more". The advice was followed and there were no more problems.
159536: When people saw a cat run between their legs, they believed it was a witch. Old women were often suspected of being witches. When misfortune struck somewhere, the witch was blamed.
159542: Some people who were picking spurrey suddenly saw a violent storm wind rise, which made the grain spin in circles. The people were frightened and ran home quickly. A boy who turned around on the way saw his father's mother running as never before. The grandmother was even home before them. Yet that grandmother normally always walked with a stick. When the boy told his mother, she said: "Was she there again, that witch?"
159551: On a bewitched farm the carts rattled, the threshing machine made noise, the horses were sweaty and the calves lay dead in the stable. Because the place was swarming with witches, the people went on a pilgrimage in honour of Saint Bernard. Afterwards the priests came to exorcise the place until they were completely drenched in sweat. If the people went to confession and communion for nine days, they would be freed from the witchcraft.
159552: A twelve-year-old boy rode his bicycle out of the Klarenbos. He had to cross the Rillaarsebaan. On that road the boy was run over by a car. People believed that a witch from the village had made the boy invisible and that this was why he had the accident. After all, the witch lived near that road.
159574: A brave man who was afraid of nothing saw a figure ahead of him on his way home. He grabbed at the figure, but felt only wool.
159579: A man took his mare across the field to a stallion in Heylissem. Although people said the witches came to dance in that field at night, the man was not afraid. Suddenly an old woman spoke to him and said: "Before you get home, your mare will be dead." And so it was.
159609: A man prayed every evening for his drowned brother-in-law. One evening the ghost of the dead brother-in-law appeared to ask for a mass. The man told his wife he had seen her brother's ghost. When the woman went to ask the priest for advice, the clergyman said ghosts had existed in the past but no longer did. After the man had the mass said, the ghost appeared one last time to thank him. "C., I will put in a good word for you every day", said the ghost.
159617: A stalkaars (stable candle, a mysterious light) was something that flew through the air. In places where the stalkaars hovered still, something serious would happen.
159628: A man who got up at night to go to the toilet heard a clamour of a hundred voices in the air. It sounded like birds flying through the sky, though there was nothing to be seen.
159660: On a farm in Meldert lived a miserly farmer who would give nothing to any beggar. After his death the farmer came haunting in a cart with four horses that drove around the dung heap. A friar read prayers over the farm and banished the ghost for ninety-nine years.
159696: A witch is said to have once pulled a child up to the ceiling.
159704: In France the devils had built a barn in a single night.
159710: Crows, black cats and magpies brought bad luck, or so people believed.
159721: A woman from Humbeek who could not have children looked after other women's children for payment. One day she had to look after a newborn child. That baby fell ill, however, and eventually died. The child's mother became pregnant again and also brought her second child to the same childminder. That child got the same illness and also died. The childminder wanted to get to the bottom of it and fetched a piece of Easter nail from the parish priest to place under the threshold. When the childminder had to look after that woman's third child, the child's grandmother could not get in.
159724: A rich farmer's daughter had a relationship with a boy from Kerkom. When one day the girl was coming back from the fair with her boyfriend, the boy said: "Go on ahead, I have to relieve myself. If you meet anyone, throw your handkerchief." That is how the girl discovered that it was her boyfriend who went about as a bear.
159733: One winter evening some men were playing cards at a farm. Suddenly a strange gentleman came in and asked if he could join in. The gentleman played along. A little later one of the players bent down to pick up a dropped card. At that moment the player saw that the strange gentleman had two horse's legs. It was Kledde (a malevolent shape-shifting spirit).
159754: Many sorceresses lived on the Malheide. A man from Lembeek who was coming back from the fair on the Malheide at about a quarter to twelve lost his way. The man sat down on the ground and fell asleep. The next morning he woke up on the dung heap of a farm. The man had been bewitched.
159755: In a house in Zichem where people sat in the kitchen in the evening, noises were heard as if pebbles were being thrown in the attic. People had gone to look, but there was nothing to be seen. One day the woman went upstairs, sprinkled everything with holy water and prayed the Gospel of Saint John. Since then no strange noises have been heard in that house.
159763: A farmer out with his horse heard a woman say: "Oh farmer, break your neck on your horse!" Then the woman jumped off the gate she was sitting on. The farmer fell off his horse.
159776: A woman carrying flour in a wheelbarrow met someone she suspected of being a witch. At that very moment the wheelbarrow tipped over and the witch began to laugh.
159778: People who were ridden by the mare lay stiff as a board in their beds.
159782:
In Oudenaken a woman was bewitched. The woman had been to Affligem, but it was already too late. That woman died of the witchcraft.
Two girls who were bewitched always started crying at midnight. They fell silent when their father got up and danced with them.
159784: A man was taking lessons from a wizard, who flew through the air with him. The man hit the weathercock of the church tower with his ear.
159797: A man who had almost finished harvesting his grain decided to eat lunch only once the job was done. Suddenly an old woman came by and said: "Go home, because you won't get that finished anyway." The farmer replied: "But look what a small piece I still have to do!" The woman said again: "You won't get that finished this afternoon." The man kept working until he was completely drenched in sweat in the evening. However hard the man worked, there was always just as much grain standing. The old woman had bewitched the grain.
159800: Some men were walking back from Tienen. Along the way the group split up, so that one of the men had to go home alone. As the man walked down a hill, he saw a figure come out from behind the trees. A little later he felt something walking beside him and touching his elbow. Yet the man saw nothing. When the terrified man came near a farm, he called out: "Who is there?", but there was no answer. Past the farm, the man experienced nothing strange anymore.
159805: In a shop in Essene there was a little son who lay in a cradle next to the stove. A woman who always came to shop there often played with the child in the cradle. One day the child's mother said to the woman: You must not come and do that here any more. A long time later, when the child could already walk, the visitor came to pay a debt of fifty francs. After she left, the child became so ill that it had to stay in its cradle all the time. The visitor had made the mare ride the child.
159821: In Orsmaal-Gussenhoven there was a small house where a little woman lived who was bewitched. If that woman held out her hand to someone, that person was bewitched.
159824: A man who had met his dead father died of fright. The man had to fulfil a vow that his father had neglected.
159839: A man who took onions to Gent twice a week one day met a little woman in a cloak. After that the man's horse would no longer move forward. When the bell rang the Angelus at five in the morning, the little woman had vanished and the horse went on. That woman must have been a sorceress.
159849: During the night after his father's funeral, T. heard a hellish noise in the house. The doors flew open and the chairs were thrown over. When the man went to the dean for advice the next day, he was advised to go to confession and communion. If he heard anything after that, he was to get up and go and look. That night the man got up and asked: "Is that you, father? What have you come for?" The ghost answered: "I hid ten francs in a catskin in the wall there and sealed the hole with clay." After that the ghost did not appear again.
159880: Many sorceresses lived on the Malheide, people believed. A man coming back from the fair in Lembeek had to cross the Malheide. There, however, the man lost his way, so that he had to wander about until the next morning. The man believed he had been bewitched by the witches, but perhaps he had simply drunk too much.
159887: In 1939 a man had seen a blood-red cloud in the sky moving in the direction of Antwerp. The man believed it was an omen of the war. In 1912 or 1913 a comet with devils' heads could be seen as an omen of the First World War.
159900: In Oorbeek there lived a farmer who had a beautiful daughter. For fear that the girl would go astray, the farmer never let his daughter work in the field alone or go out. When there was a fair in the village and the girl was not allowed to go, she said angrily: "I'm going anyway, even if it's with the devil himself!" The girl was locked in her room. When she had been sitting there for a while, she heard someone knocking on her window. She saw that it was a man with eyes like a Chinese man's and with a tail hanging out from under his black coat. As soon as the girl realised she was dealing with the devil, she became frightened and cried: "God help me!" The next moment the devil had vanished and the girl's room smelled of sulphur.
159901: A man claimed that he was often ridden by the mare at night. One night the man pinched the mare because she had supposedly pinched him in the neck. Afterwards the man heard the mare crying. Once the man had scattered sand in his bed because he wanted to know what kind of feet the mare had. That is how the man found out that the mare had feet like a sheep.
159908: An old farmer's wife always had bad luck on her farm in Druimeren (Herfelingen). The cows and horses died and in time the children also fell ill. A priest from Affligem came to exorcise the farm and put a candle under the threshold. An old woman always used to come to the farm. After the priests' intervention that woman did not come again and the misery was over. People believed that woman was a kind of sorceress.
159917: In Sterrebeek lived a sorceress who caused a farmer much misfortune. The animals were bewitched and the farmer's children fell ill.
159928: In Oppem (between Meise and Brussegem) devils had built a barn during the night.
159942: People who believed in witchcraft often assumed that a dead person was returning when they heard a noise somewhere.
159944: A woman went to the market in Aarschot on Thursdays. On the way she always went for a cup of coffee in a café. Someone there must have made little crosses over her cup, because the woman was warned by an acquaintance, who said: "Watch out!" The woman drank her coffee anyway. Afterwards she lay in bed for six weeks. Next to the bed stood a paraffin lamp. One day the woman saw the person who had bewitched her sitting in the glass of that lamp. The witch wore a neckerchief. When the glass suddenly burst, the woman was freed from the witchcraft.
159945: Some people going to early Mass in the morning passed an orchard that was shaking violently. On their way back they were therefore surprised to find that not a single apple had fallen from the trees.
159957: In the past children were frightened by being told that a white or a black madam roamed about in Beigem.
159976: In Roosbeek several children had already died at birth. The father had been advised, at the next delivery in his house, to check whether there was a toad in the water drain hole. If so, he had to chop off one of the animal's legs. No sooner said than done. The day after the next child was born, the child's grandmother came to visit. The woman had lost an arm. She was the witch.
159979: In Wezembeek lived a woman who could bewitch children by laying her hand on their heads. The child would then die or fall seriously ill.
159991: In Opvelp there stood a barn that was said to have been built by devils. The devils had not managed to finish the barn because the farmer's wife had got up and made the cock crow early.
160011: In some houses people heard music, although nothing could be seen. In those houses there were witches, who had to be driven out by the priest.
160018: If you could strike a werewolf in the middle of its head until it bled, you knew who it was.
160049: A girl of fifteen or sixteen had to go from Nieuwrode to 't Rot on an errand. In the moonlight the girl saw a strange apparition walking at a crossroads in the fields. Frightened, the girl ran to a café and said: "I've seen the werewolf. It's coming!" Everyone ran outside, but there was nothing to be seen. On Sunday morning some people claimed they had seen tracks of the werewolf. You could unmask a werewolf by sticking a knife into the sand and then stabbing it into the werewolf's forehead.
160053: According to people, black cats were witches.
160056: A girl who had been allowed to cut grass in the garden of a deceased man suddenly heard knocking in the house. When the girl looked through the window, she saw the deceased couple S. and B. standing there. The next day the frightened girl went on a pilgrimage to Scherpenheuvel with her mother. Since then she has not seen the deceased couple appear again.
160074: The mare grabbed its victims and tried to strangle them. A man from Vollezele had already been ridden by the mare twice.
160076:
One evening a farmer from Houthalen called his farmhand because a cow was about to calve. But the farmhand was nowhere to be found. So the farmer went to his neighbour to help him. A ladder stood against the hayloft where the farmhand slept. Shortly after a dog had been seen climbing up the ladder, the farmhand appeared. He was a werewolf.
One day the farmhand was out walking with his girlfriend when he said to her: "If a dog comes at you, throw your handkerchief at its jaws and it will not harm you. You will then see the pieces of the handkerchief hanging between my teeth." Everything happened as the farmhand had predicted.
160097: When people were bewitched, they had themselves exorcised by the priests of Our Lady of Halle.
160133: People who had been ridden by the mare saw something approach that looked like a man. Sometimes the person could be recognised. You would then feel stifled, as if your throat were being squeezed shut. Since the Gospel of Saint John was read after Mass, such things had disappeared. Some people claimed that such phenomena were caused by eating too much before going to bed. A woman claimed that you could protect yourself against the mare by putting your clogs upside down next to the bed.
160141: In a house in Vlezenbeek a toad had come in through the water drain hole. They chopped off one of the toad's legs. The next day people said that a woman from the village had lost her hand. It was believed that this woman was a witch.
160143: A clog maker could torment people. By speaking a magic formula he could make mice appear on people's tables or walls.
160166: A farm in Wieze was plagued by rats. The misfortune was blamed on a woman who always came to visit there. After the priests had been sent for, things fortunately improved.
160167: In a house in Meldert the devil, in the shape of a black dog, came and sat under the stove.
160175: A woman whose child was seriously ill went to the monastery of Affligem. The priest prayed over the child and then said: "Now it will be over, madam." The mother went home, but her child's health got even worse. So the mother went back to the priest, who said that the first woman to visit in the morning would be the culprit. The next morning the mother was indeed visited by a jealous woman.
160178: A man from Hoeleden heard a rushing noise near a castle on his way home. When the man stood still, he heard nothing more. Near the castle the man always saw something like a sack of leaves flying at his feet. A little further on the man saw nothing strange anymore.
160200: On a farm in Oudenaken they had much misfortune. Banging was heard in the attic and people believed the witches were there.
160205: During a witch's funeral, the dead woman's sister was lifted up from her chair. Her nails came right through her mittens.
160213: Strange things happened in a house in the Pelokenstraat. The plates, cups, spoons and forks all rattled on the table. One night the lord of the castle asked someone to keep watch there. He had said: "If you see anything, just shoot, even if it is a mouse". The man who had to keep watch, however, noticed nothing strange that night.
160227: When people went to fetch buttermilk and spilled a little on the road, they immediately wiped the drops away with their foot, because they were afraid that otherwise passers-by would bewitch them.
160239: A farm in Laar was haunted. At night the cows and pigs were seen walking in the meadow there. In the morning the animals were all back inside.
160244: In Busingen lived a witch who handed out sweets to the children at the Tuesday market in Lennik. The children who had eaten those sweets had to keep walking around the market until the witch said: "Now you may go home."
160265: Hundreds of years ago old Zoutleeuw sank. In the marshy Ven, beneath which the old village lay, bells could be heard ringing on Christmas Eve. On the day before Whitsun a poor widow dared to go and cut grass in the Ven for her cows. At the Ven the woman heard the bell ringing. She also found a silk thread there of a coral-red colour. The woman pulled on the thread for a long time, until a tower cross came up above the water. When the woman cried out: "Jesus! Mary!" the thread broke, and the tower cross disappeared into the depths again.
160290: In the old days, when people had misfortune in the stables or in the household, they believed they were bewitched. On a farm where there was much misfortune in the stable, a man from Oplombeek was sent for to read over the farm. The farmer and his wife went to a man who could drive out evil. That man said: "You need seven new reins, a kilo of flax and elderwood popguns." A few days later the man came over and made a thick ball of the flax. The people were not to let anyone into the stable. So when the neighbour woman came to ask if she could see the pig, she was not let in. The next day the neighbour said: "I've seen your pig and it's nice and fat already." The farmer did not know how the neighbour had got into the stable. When the man came back a few days later, the farmer's wife was full of lice. The man said to her: "Take a louse and throw it in the stove." The woman did so with two lice and was promptly rid of the vermin. After that those people had no more problems with the animals in their stable.
160331: A man who always heard loud knocking at night went to the friars for advice. The clergymen had the house cleared and began to pray. After a few days the knocking stopped. It must have been the ghost of a sinner who had to come haunting there.
160337: A man was in a café in Brussels. The landlady asked where the man came from, and the man said he lived in Teralfene. Then the landlady asked: "Are those trees still standing there in the Bolheide?" The woman explained that as a sorceress she had once held meetings at that spot. She was glad, though, that she was no longer among the sorceresses.
160345: A twelve-year-old boy worked in the mine in Wallonia. Sometimes the boys had to work until two o'clock. When that boy then came home, a friend was always with him. It sometimes happened that the two met a little woman who gave them sweets. The boys refused the sweets because they were afraid of being bewitched.
160352: A woman saw a toad in a room that had come in through the water drain. The woman believed the creature was a witch and carefully chased it outside. Then she kicked it into the dung pit. Ever since that incident there were always two or three toads in the room. After the people had been to the friars, there were no more toads in the house.
160378: A farmer was desperate because his barn was too small to store his harvest in. One day in the field the farmer met a black gentleman, who said to him: "Well, farmer, I will see to it that there is a barn standing tomorrow morning before the first cockcrow. In exchange I do want your soul." The farmer, who was also a freemason, agreed to the proposal. When a hellish noise was heard the next night and the farmer's wife asked what was going on, the farmer told his story. The farmer's wife got up at once, ran to the henhouse and knocked her clogs together. The next moment the cock began to crow, at which the devils immediately fled. In the barn, however, there was still a hole that could not be closed. One day the bricklayers set a crucifix into that hole. In that way they did manage to close the hole after all.
160400: In Elewijt a witch is said to have bewitched the farmer's stable, so that all the animals died. Everyone avoided that witch.
160411: A boy set off for work on Monday morning. His parents watched him as he left. At a certain moment they saw the boy put down his sandwiches and back away. The boy had seen an unknown woman, who slapped him round the ear. The parents, however, had not seen the woman.
160425: One day a farmer from Overhespen went to the field with a large horse-drawn cart. When the man headed home in the evening, not a single horse would take another step. The animals were foaming at the mouth. The farmer called to a man standing a little further off: "She's got me again! Go and fetch her and tell her she has to come!" For if the witch did not come, the horses would never be able to walk again. When the witch came to the horses, the animals started moving, without the witch having said or done anything. The farmer then gave her a sound beating. Witches were people who had sold their souls to the devil.
160426: A man saw someone lying in the snow. He went over to the poor fellow and said: "Dear friend, it's far too cold to stay lying here". The figure lying in the snow replied: "Go home and leave in peace what is at peace". Terrified, the man ran home. He looked back a hundred times to see whether the figure was following him.
160437: In 't Graalputje in Mazenzele a bell had sunk, which could be heard ringing at twelve o'clock on Christmas night. The bell had flown out of the tower. A man who had stuck a hop pole into the pit claimed he had felt the bell.
160454: Some girls who went to plant beets in Kapellen often could not get off the small field where they were working. That had something to do with witchcraft.
160468: On a farm in the Beverstraat a cat sat in the horses' manger every night. One night someone chopped off one of the cat's legs with a hatchet. The next day a witch from the neighbourhood had lost her leg.
160505: A man who had to take cherries to the market in Mechelen lost his way and ended up at 't Sas. The man claimed that someone had made him lose his way.
160507: If witches found no victim to harm, they had to harm themselves. They stuck pins into a doll.
160513: A black cat was a witch and a crow was the symbol of dark powers.
160514: Two boys going to the fair were surrounded by a big tree by witches dancing around them. When one of the boys sneezed, the other said: "God bless you." The next moment the whole scene had vanished.
160520: In a house there worked a farmhand who was suspected of being Kledde (a werewolf-like spirit). When the farmhand's skin had been found, the boy was sent away and the skin was thrown into the oven. A moment later the farmhand was already standing by the oven to save his skin. The sweating farmhand had to be held back until the skin had burnt up completely. Afterwards the farmhand was happy because he had been released.
160534: In the Steneveld in Linden a chapel is said to have sunk once. The pit where this happened can still be seen. If you pressed your ear to the ground on Christmas night, you could supposedly still hear the bells of that chapel ringing. Many people from the village had already heard it.
160536:
A woman from Houwaart claimed that her mother had been bewitched by her neighbour, who appeared in the form of a black cat. That neighbour always came to visit at a certain time, which made the bewitched woman ill. The people sent for a spiritist. The clergy exorcised the house until they were completely drenched in sweat.
In the past people always blamed witches for the misfortune they suffered.
160542: A woman whose chickens were haunted and flew about sent for the parish priest to read prayers over her chicken coop. After that the haunting was over.
160547: In the past people often held gatherings in the evening to tell stories. Not infrequently they dreamed that they were ridden by the mare.
160550: In Breedhout there lived a witch who always tried to get into people's houses. On a farm where there had already been much misfortune caused by this witch, the farmer asked the priest at Easter for a piece of the blessed Easter candle. The farmer put that piece of candle under his threshold. After that the witch never set foot in his house again.
160554: Someone who had moved a boundary post during his life had to haunt after his death with the post on his back.
160576:
One day a boy was followed by a witch. The boy quickly ran inside somewhere and drew a cross on the threshold. Because of that the witch could not get in.
Shortly afterwards that boy, who slept in the cowshed with his brother, had a terrible nightmare. He dreamed that he was lying on the edge of hell. There were three devils trying to drag him into hell with flat hooks. The boy struggled so hard in his sleep that the wattle and pieces of clay broke off the wall. If his brother had not grabbed him, the boy would have fallen right through the wall.
In Halen lived a woman suspected of being a witch. A girl who went to cut fodder in the field struck at a hare running in front of her. She missed, however, and the hare said: "You won't be walking here much longer." Shortly afterwards the girl died.
160580:
Witches had to do evil. Instead of people they could also choose animals as victims.
On a farm many pigs had already died. The insurance agents took the pigs to the laboratory, but they could not find any disease. A witch often came to visit that farm, however. After the parish priest had exorcised the farm, there was no more misfortune there.
160585: People who had bad luck were said to be ridden by the maar (nightmare).
160601: A man lying in bed one evening heard beautiful music and singing in the distance. The sound came closer and the man's wife heard it too. Then the sound turned into the wailing and screeching of cats. The man quietly opened the window and only just managed to jump aside. Otherwise he would have been struck on the head.
160603: In the churchyard of Peizegem a dead person is said to have risen from his grave.
160608: In the dark people sometimes saw will-o'-the-wisps in the meadow. Those lights were the little souls of children who had died unbaptised. When a will-o'-the-wisp had been baptised, it disappeared.
160617: A man and a woman were bewitched by a neighbour who came every day to bring them an apple or a plum and rubbed them on the knee or the head as she did so. After that woman's death her house had to be demolished. The ground also had to be disinfected because nothing could be built on it.
160625: A newly married man who lived near Zellik station could not sleep at night because a sorceress always came to his bed. After the man had walked to the monastery of Affligem, his problems came to an end. A sorceress who lived near him had caused the harm.
160626: In Wever lived a witch who caused her own son to become disabled. At certain times witches were forced to do evil. If they found no other victim, they harmed their own children.
160634: One evening in May a girl had been to the evening devotion (lof). As she left the church, a woman grabbed hold of her. "Let me go!" said the girl. After that incident the girl had such severe stomach pains that the doctor almost had to be called. The woman who had grabbed her had a bad reputation.
160641: A woman who walked to Bever always got a nosebleed when she passed a house in Torrezele (Bever). Some believed that the woman who lived in that house was a sorceress.
160659: A young man had married a girl whose mother was a sorceress, and had moved in with his wife and mother-in-law. One day the young man saw something that made a great impression on him. His mother-in-law was frying chips. The woman said: "Look, lad, you wouldn't dare do that, would you?" and put her hand in the hot fat without getting hurt.
160680: Some pensioners were on holiday in Mallorca. One night a woman woke up. She had seen a man who took her by the hand and had her on his teeth. The other pensioners said that the woman had been ridden 'by the moon'.
160687: A man who had come back from the city on the last train came into a café in a fright. The man claimed he had seen something terrifying, but in reality it will just have been the wind.
160693: In Houwaart lived a sick woman who every night saw something or someone appear, though the others could not see it. The parish priest came to pray over everyone in that house. He also advised the occupants to cut down the two apple trees in the garden because there was something under them. People believed the woman had been bewitched by her niece who lived in America.
160694: A sorcerer made rats and mice run to a farm.
160706: A man from Waaienberg was coming home one Sunday evening through the woods of Kartelo. The man met a stranger. A little later he came to a castle where he was allowed to join the festivities. When one of the guests sneezed, the man said: "God bless you." The next moment the castle had vanished and the man was sitting on a dung heap with a pot of dung in his hands.
160717: A woman from Halle had caused a child to get a hunchback. When that woman pricked the child on the head with hairpins, she felt pain herself.
160741: Some people going to Kortenbos saw on the way a beautiful tent in which people were dancing to lovely music. When they came back from Kortenbos, there was no trace of the tent left, and a copper jug lay in that spot.
160760: A man had come under the influence of the evil hand through a woman who sold him milk. The man's twelve-year-old son then died and the man himself also fell ill. The man had already been to three doctors, but none could help him. Finally the man went to a spiritist, who advised him to throw his blankets and bedding outside and to eat nothing but a slice of black bread for eight days. The man also had to walk four hours every day. When the man had followed that advice, he was cured.
160789: On a farm in the Koninklijke Kasteeldreef there was much misfortune with the animals. Moreover, every evening a big black dog was seen walking there. One day the village policeman managed to shoot the dog. When he went to pick up the dead dog, the animal had vanished without a trace. In Oppem (a hamlet of Brussegem) a woman lay dead. That woman had always been suspected of witchcraft.
160793: A man who could not fall asleep believed he had been ridden by the mare.
160801: In the past people believed that black cats were witches. In the Lakenstraat children often threw stones at a cat they called the 'witch cat'.
160854: A man lived with his mother-in-law, who had been ill for twenty years. No doctor knew what was wrong with her. The woman did remember that a suspicious woman from her neighbourhood had very often visited her and often touched her. That woman's two children always had scratches on their faces and often wore bandages around their legs. After all, if a witch found no other victim, she had to bewitch her own children.
160855: A man always heard someone calling at night: "Post moved, post moved!" People kept hearing that calling until someone put the post back in its original place.
160856:
A mother who had already lost two of her four children suspected a woman from the neighbourhood of having bewitched them. If the children saw sweets lying on the road, they did not dare pick them up because they believed the sorceress had put them there.
People who handed out sweets with good intentions were often suspected of being sorceresses.
160869: On a willow tree one could sometimes find a branch as flat as a ribbon. That was a stick that had been ridden by witches.
160903: A carter from Vissenaken took the dealers to Binkom, where they were going to buy calves. When the carter passed a certain house, his horses would not go a metre further. At a certain moment the woman who lived there came outside and said: "Put the brown horse where the black one is and the cart will go on." The carter did what the woman advised and was indeed able to go on without any trouble.
160913: A woman who had lost her wedding ring went to a neighbour for advice. In the evening the woman saw her wedding ring hanging on the latch of her front door.
160916: A boy fell ill after accepting a sweet from an old woman. Eventually the boy died.
160919: A farmer's wife who was churning butter was visited by a woman who said: "I'll help you." The woman fetched a cup of water and wanted to pour it into the churn. The farmer's wife quickly snatched the cup from her hands and threw the water into the coal scuttle. In this way she made sure her buttermilk was not bewitched.
160924: After the death of a sorceress, people believed her magic power had passed to her son.
160927: On a bewitched farm in Waasmont the pigs crawled on their knees. One day a woman from the neighbourhood had touched a fine foal on that farm. The next day the animal had a big lump on its back. Two priests came to exorcise the farm. The evil was caused by a witch from Waasmont. Eventually that witch died.
160933: At a certain place in Geetbets, chains always flew across the road. If you were afraid, the chains would even chase you.
160955: A farmer had made a pact with the devil, by which he would lose his soul after twenty years. The farmer became very restless and was not happy with the wealth he had gained. When the twenty years were up, the farmer heard a loud thunderclap, followed by a blinding light. The devil appeared and the farmer was carried off to hell with a terrible noise.
160972: A family in Sint-Lambrechts-Woluwe had a beautiful daughter. One day the girl was given syrup sweets by a woman, and she ate them with great relish. That night, however, the girl fell ill and had terrible pain in her mouth. Her mother put compresses on her mouth, but that did not help. The next day the girl had a red rash around her mouth, so that she looked dreadful. The family went to the doctor, but he could not help. Then the mother went to a woman in the village who prayed all the time and who was said to be able to overcome evil. That woman said she would come and pray the litany against evil spirits and that afterwards they should go to the friars. No sooner said than done. The friar had to work hard to fight the evil. Then he gave the girl a relic to wear. A few days later her face looked normal again.
160991: A man coming back from the All Saints' fair in Wespelaar could no longer find his way home, although he was not drunk. A witch had made the man lose his way.
161048: In a house lived a boy whose head grew between his legs. One day a man came to visit and said: "What's wrong with this boy? I can cure him. Fetch a bundle of straw and set it alight. A woman will come by, who will say: 'I must go, I must go.' But you must not say: 'Go then.'" Indeed a woman came and sat by the fire and could not leave. The next moment the man was covered in lice. But he said: "Yes, go ahead, that's the only thing you can do to me. If you don't cure that boy, I'll throw you in the fire." The woman claimed she could not and wanted to go home. The man said: "Go home then. You'll soon be forced to come back." The woman fetched from her home a wax doll whose head she had bent downwards. She gave the doll to the boy, who set it upright again. Two weeks later the boy was cured. That man was never seen again.
161073: A farmer went to Mechelen every week with some horses. When the farmer's wife was seriously ill, she advised her husband not to go, but the farmer would have none of it and said: "There's no danger yet. I have to go to the market." The farmer had gone barely a hundred metres when a black cat landed on his horse, making the animal rear. The farmer cut the cat in two with his whip. On arriving in Mechelen the farmer found that his horse was drenched in sweat. When the farmer came home that evening, he saw that his wife had been cut in two.
161074: Between Leuven and Tienen lived a farmer who had no money to build a new barn. One day the farmer met a gentleman, who said to him: "If you sell me your soul, your barn will be finished before the first cockcrow tomorrow morning." The farmer agreed. In the evening he told his wife what he had agreed to. But the wife did not trust the matter, and in the night she got up and knocked her clogs together by the henhouse, so that the rooster began to crow early. At that moment, however, the barn was not yet finished; there was still a hole that had to be closed. No one has ever managed to close that hole.
161096: A boy who worked as a farmhand slept in the stable with the animals. Once the boy saw a witch come in. The witch said: "Oh, oh, beast, that I must now do this to you." Shortly afterwards that animal was dead.
161101: People who had eaten too much were ridden by the mare at night.
161135: If people on their way to market saw a black cat walking by, they believed they would not have much luck at the market.
161150: A girl did not know that a friend of her mother's was a witch. One day that friend struck the girl on the head. Because the girl could not strike higher, she fell ill afterwards.
161152: Witches could change a cat into a dog.
161160: A woman working in the beet field found her work not progressing at all because she was the victim of a witch.
161162: A son of the S. family had fallen from a tree at 't Kruis and died shortly afterwards. Before he died, the boy had promised to have some Masses said. Every time the dead boy's brother went to fetch water, he saw the boy's spirit standing against a tree. When the parents had told the friar everything, the clergyman said: "Next time you go to fetch water, take a white cloth and ask what the spirit wants. The spirit will then give you its hand". In this way the boy learned that his dead little brother had promised a Mass in honour of Our Lady when he fell from the tree. The spirit burned its hand into the cloth. After that the parents had the promised Masses said.
161169: In Edingen lived a woman whose children had all died because of a witch. The woman had the friars of Affligem read prayers over her. Later the woman found out that her neighbour was the witch.
161176: A boy had to pick leaves of a certain plant for his mother, who had sores on her legs. During the day the mother had spoken with a neighbour who was suspected of being a witch. The boy came home with the leaves and put them on the cupboard. The next morning the witch came to ask whether they had any leaves in the house. The boy answered: "Yes, I have a handful." But when he went to look on the cupboard, there was not a single leaf left. The witch must have spirited the leaves away.
161197: A medium received a message from a dead person. The dead man asked for his statue to be removed, because otherwise he could find no rest.
161206: A mother was coming back by train from East or West Flanders with her little child. The child was given a piece of chocolate by a woman sitting opposite them on the train. After that the child got worse and worse, so that in the end it had to go into an institution. Witches always tried to touch people or give them something. To break a witch's power, one had to strike higher.
161211: A witch could only die after she had passed her power on to her daughter. When that daughter went into a café to ask for a cup of coffee, they refused to give her anything, saying: "We have no hot water, because our stove has gone out." The witch asked whether she could put the pot of water on the cold stove. Two minutes later the water was boiling.
161252: A man from Leerbeek heard beautiful music in the stables at night. After new mangers had been built, the haunting came to an end.
161274: Witches were people who dressed strangely and wore a scarf on their heads. A man from Bever could cure bewitched animals by reading prayers over them.
161285: A woman who always walked my dog in the evening was tormented by her mother-in-law. The mother-in-law was a witch who could leave her body. While the woman was walking, she felt she was suffocating. That was her mother-in-law seizing her by the throat in invisible form. So the woman often fell ill in the evening and had to go to the doctor. The doctor listened to her heartbeat and found nothing wrong. But the woman had to pay the doctor every time.
161312: A widow who had remarried late in life had had a baby. Because the child was not healthy, the mother had been advised by a friend to go and see a fortune-teller. The fortune-teller claimed that the child had been touched by the evil hand and had fallen ill from the bewitchment. The witch was a woman who often came to visit the mother. The fortune-teller advised the mother not to let anyone touch the child any more. The child would recover a few days later. When the mother went home together with her friend, the friend offered to carry the child. The mother refused, however, and accused her friend of having bewitched the child. Then the two women quarrelled. A few days later the child died.
161322: A woman who was ridden by the mare lay stiff as a board in her bed and felt as if a thousand people were sitting on her. When the woman said, "And the Word was made flesh and dwelt among us", she was suddenly set free.
161339: On a farm in Halen lived an old farmer who went to sleep elsewhere at night. Next to the farm stood a hut in which an old woman lived. At night, noise and rumbling could be heard in the farm's attic. One night the farmer went up to the attic with a dung fork, where he found thirty or forty cats. The man managed to break the leg of one of the cats. When the farmer came back from his field the next day, his wife said: "I haven't seen our neighbour today. Her door hasn't been opened yet." The farmer knocked at the neighbour's house, but no one opened. The farmer then went to the police, who came and broke down the door. In the house lay the neighbour with a broken leg. The farmer told the police what he had experienced with the cats. The police called a doctor, who established that the neighbour's leg had been broken by a blow...
161349: Will-o'-the-wisps were the little souls of unbaptised children that flew towards people. When you said: "We baptise you", the will-o'-the-wisp flew away. A man who had said: "I baptise you" only just managed to slam the door shut in time, because the will-o'-the-wisp came at him. The next day there was a bloodstain on the door.
161356: The mare was a woman who crawled on top of people. A man who was ridden by the mare every night claimed that his tongue was pulled down into his throat. Even when the man had tied a knife over his heart with the blade pointing upward, he was still ridden by the mare.
161367: A girl was coming back from the fair in Essenbeek with her boyfriend. On the way the boyfriend said: "Give me your handkerchief, because I have to relieve myself here. If Kludde (a shape-shifting spectre) comes with his chain, I will throw that handkerchief and then he will leave you alone." But the boyfriend was himself Kludde with his chain. So when she got home the girl noticed that her boyfriend had the threads of the handkerchief between his teeth. She ended the relationship at once.
161373: On a farm the cows stopped giving milk after a certain woman had visited.
161374: It was sometimes said of rascals that they had been ridden by the mare.
161395: In Budingen there lived a witch of whom the children were very afraid. Witches covered people with lice and made children die. Sometimes a witch made sure that no butter could be churned. If the witch moved the staff in the churn just once, there was butter.
161400: In Oppem-Brussegem lived a farmer who could not store his grain because his barn was too small. The farmer sold his soul to the devil, who in return would build a barn for him. The barn had to be finished before the rooster had crowed three times the next morning. In the night, however, the farmer grew afraid and told his wife everything. The farmer's wife got up before three o'clock and clapped her hands, so that the rooster began to crow early. At that moment the barn was not yet finished. The hole in the barn could never be closed.
161402: People believed that stallichten (will-o'-the-wisps) were the souls of murdered people who came back. In reality the light was caused by the gases given off by animals.
161417: A woman from Oetingen who worked as a maid on a farm always saw kludde (a shape-shifting spectre) with his chain walking in a meadow after ten o'clock at night. A German shepherd also worked on that farm. One evening as the woman was walking home, she met the werewolf and threw her handkerchief at the beast, saying: "Unravel this thread by thread!" The next day the maid sat at table with the German shepherd. He had the threads of the handkerchief between his teeth.
161429: In the Ipsvoordestraat there was a farm with four cows and an ox. When four cows had already died, the farmer went to the priest for advice. The clergyman came to read prayers over the farm. Somewhere a black cat had been seen that could not be caught. People believed that cat was a witch.
161433: A woman who was staying in the woods was laughed at by some passers-by. Then the woman said: "I'll get him yet! He won't get home tonight". That night the man indeed did not get home. The man wandered about near his house the whole time. When the man heard the church bells strike the hour, he suddenly found his bearings again.
161434: People who always had bad luck believed that their house had been ridden by the mare. A woman who lived on the Malheide during the war had a small child who was often ill. The mother had a blessing read over her child by the fathers of Halle. The child died nonetheless.
161462: A boy found it strange that his girlfriend always had to leave whenever he came to visit. One evening the boy pretended to have fallen asleep to find out what his girlfriend and her mother were up to. When the women thought the boy was asleep, they took out an ointment, which they rubbed on their fingers. Then they said: "Over hedges and over hedgerows..." and flew away. Then the boy also rubbed his fingers with the ointment and said: "Through heath and through hedgerows, straight to the wine cellar." When the boy arrived in the wine cellar, he saw fine ladies and gentlemen enjoying themselves there. But he was badly injured because he had made a mistake in saying the magic formula. The sorceresses in the wine cellar gave him a pig and told him not to say anything to the animal. The boy sat on the pig, which then flew away. When the pig had crossed the sea, the boy said: "Goddamn, that's some jump for a pig!"
161471: A girl who had been bewitched had fallen ill and kept seeing strange things. When the family had prayers read over the girl, the friars said: "If someone comes knocking at night, you must not answer and must not let that person in." One night there was indeed a knock. The father opened the door and asked what the visitor wanted. The woman answered: "I have come to fetch some dried pitch." The father said: "If you have something to look for here, come in." But he should not have said that. The girl died.
161476:
A woman came to fetch butter and milk from a mother whose newborn baby lay in a cradle. The woman said to the mother: "You won't have your child much longer." Out of fear the mother went to stay with her own mother with her two other children, so that the father was home alone with the baby. When the man got up in the night, he saw that the baby's shadow on the wall was coloured.
The mother went to the convent to pray for her child, but the child died all the same. The woman who had caused the harm had to throw all her evil books into the fire. But the books would not burn. After that the woman came to say that the couple's next child would not survive either. The mother was given cards and pills to put into her walls, so that the witch would not come into her house again.
161482: A man coming back from Kortenbos saw in the woods by the castle of Nieuwenhoven a beautiful hotel where people were dancing and leaping about. When the scene had vanished, the man was standing in a thornbush.
161483: In Geetbets a pond was once filled in. A little night light always appeared above that pond. A woman had murdered a child there and buried the little body.
161487: In winter, a man from Goetsenhoven went in the dark to Neerheylissem to help basket pigeons. On the way the man saw a big black dog with a chain walking beside him. Because the dog annoyed him, the man gave the animal a hard blow with his stick until it bled. A moment later the man saw his own nephew standing before him, who said: "You have released me."
161499: In Heikruis a family lived in a feud with their neighbours. One day a twenty-year-old girl in that family died. The family accused the neighbour woman of having bewitched the girl.
161506: One day a man was visited by a beggar woman. After the beggar woman left, the man found that he was covered in fleas. The man went to the monastery in Landen to fetch a holy object. After he had fastened it to the inside of his door, the beggar woman never visited him again. The man was also immediately rid of his fleas.
161514: In the old days people believed that witches put a mark on the gate when they had visited somewhere. If an animal on that farm then fell ill or died, people believed the misfortune had been caused by the evil hand. People to whom this had happened went on pilgrimage to Sint-Brixius-Rode (Meise), to Meusegem (Wolvertem) or to Scherpenheuvel.
161534: A brave man coming back from the shoemaker met a werewolf on the road from Hoeleden to Gelbergen. The man hung his shoes on a branch and decided to take on the werewolf. When the man in the animal skin came closer, he was attacked with a stick fitted with a copper tube filled with lead, with a nail stuck in it. A moment later the brave man saw one of the richest farmers of the village standing in front of him. If you could make the werewolf bleed, you could unmask him.
161548: The kattebossen were haunted after a woman had murdered her child there. Cats and tomcats roamed about, and someone had even seen a man there whose head rose above the trees.
161553: A farmer had sold his soul to the devil in exchange for a new barn that had to be finished before cockcrow. The farmer got up earlier to make the rooster crow, so that the devils had to flee and the farmer could keep his soul.
161565: Stalkaarsen (will-o'-the-wisps) were the spirits of children who had died unbaptised. Stalkaarsen moved up and down so that people would understand that they needed help.
161572: Witches and other people who had done much wrong had a hard time dying, or so the old people used to believe. Later, however, it was often observed that it was the good people who had to suffer greatly on their deathbeds.
161573: In Baardegem lived a girl who went to sew at a tailor's every day. On her way home the girl was always pestered by a big white dog. One day the girl asked her master if she could go home earlier, but he would not allow it because there was too much work. That night the dog was so fierce that it tore the girl's apron to pieces. The next day the girl noticed that her master had the threads of her apron between his teeth. "You have unmasked me," the master then said. After that the tailor led a good life because he had been freed from the devil.
161582: At harvest time a farmer from Hamme had sold his soul to the devil in exchange for a new barn. The barn would be built in the night and would be finished before the first cockcrow the next morning. The farmer's wife got up in the night and began to clap her hands, so that the rooster crowed early and the devils had to leave. The hole in the barn could never be closed afterwards.
161594: A farm was visited by a neighbour woman who said: "You have a fine cow." The neighbour stroked the cow's back for a few seconds. After that, however, the cow would no longer eat. The farmer went to the friars, who gave him some holy oil to put in the cow's drinking trough. From then on the cow ate normally again.
161600: The Tillekesjacht (a flying troop of witches) flew over the houses and woods at night. When that happened, people could hear beautiful singing in a strange language. The witches flew on broomsticks over hedge and hedgerow to the wine cellar at the foot of the hill. A man who had heard the witches' magic formula made a mistake and said: "Through hedge and hedgerow." That man's face was scraped all over.
161627: In Hoegaarden lived a man who went about as a werewolf. He jumped on people's backs and made them carry him.
161630: A student in Vlekkem asked the way to Gent. A man was kind enough to take the student as far as Kwatrecht. When the two arrived there, however, it had already become evening and the man no longer dared to go home alone. The student then said: "You need not be afraid. Nothing will happen to you. Something will walk with you the whole time." A moment later the student had disappeared. The whole way the man was accompanied by a big dog, which vanished without a trace when he got home.
161648: In the old days, when people had bad luck, they believed they had been ridden by the mare.
161649: Where the chapel of Our Lady of Krewinkel in Lubbeek now stands, there used to be a straw chapel. The freemasons are said to have once broken in there and destroyed everything. The next day the freemasons had scabs and pimples everywhere, which never went away.
161659: A man who felt something walking over his bed could no longer move or call out and was drenched in sweat. He had fallen victim to a witch.
161692: In Galmaarden lived a woman who was said to have bewitched her children. Children who had been with that woman usually fell ill, so that they had to be taken to the friars of Edingen. After people had laid a relic under their threshold, that witch could no longer come in.
161697: A farmer whose barn had burned down had no money to build a new one. The devil was willing to build a new barn in a single night on condition that he would get the farmer's soul. No sooner said than done. That devil's barn still stands and must by now be hundreds of years old.
161702: On the border between Brussegem and Merchtem stood a farm where many animals died. The geese had their necks wrung in the pond and the cows lay dead in the meadow. That farm was haunted.
161706: A woman was tormented by her mother-in-law, who was a witch. Even on the wedding day the mother-in-law claimed that her son would leave the woman. The mother-in-law looked after her grandchild and would no longer let the child go to its mother.
161711: A man from Sint-Pieters-Kapelle lost all his children. The Capuchins of Edingen read prayers over the house. A woman always came and looked at the children, after which they died a short time later. People claimed that the children's father was bewitched too.
161722: A suspended priest sometimes came to a family in Grimbergen to sell medicines in the form of herbal sweets. One day the son was home alone when the priest came by. The boy had always heard that the priest could do magic, and he did not dare open the door. He rudely tried to send the priest away, but the clergyman came in and looked the boy straight in the eyes once. After that the boy experienced strange things. He was tormented every day by an animal that looked like a cat. When the animal was near, the boy could not move a finger. The boy was convinced the priest had done this to him.
161725: A girl was visited by a pedlar, who asked: "Have you got a fairing from the kermis yet?", to which the girl replied: "No, but there's no need". That evening the girl was covered in lice. The girl slept with her sister, who strangely enough was not bothered by the lice. The girl only got rid of the lice by means of 'Pentecost water'.
161743: People who had been struck by the evil hand saw mice running across the table at certain times, which then vanished without a trace. Those people went on pilgrimage or had the priest read prayers over them.
161750: A witch could change frogs into fruit. If children had eaten a bewitched apple, for example, they got a toad in their belly and died.
161753: Two people from Nieuwenrode had agreed that whoever died first would come and tell the other what things were like in the afterlife. When one of the men had died, he came back and shook the other's hand. The handshake left a blackened, scorched mark. The frightened man told the priest what had happened to him. "If he comes again, you must make the sign of the cross", the priest had said. When the man made the sign of the cross the next time, the ghost vanished at once.
161760: When many animals had died in a stable, people believed the stable was bewitched. On a farm in the Molenstraat in Nieuwenrode one or two animals had already died. When the farmer came back from the market with a new heifer, he was immediately visited by a neighbour woman who came to look at the animal. The farmer said to the woman: "Filthy witch, are you planning to bewitch that animal again?" and sent her away.
161779: A man on his way to work found a loaf of rye bread on the ground. He took the bread home for his animals. In the following days the man always got a headache when he came to the spot where he had found the bread. So the man believed he had been bewitched by picking up the bread. Old people who went about somewhat untidily were often suspected of being witches in the old days.
161781: Some people keeping watch over a dead person saw the corpse move under the sheet. Then someone struck the dead man down with the words: "Oh no, no, no, what is dead must stay dead!"
161783: A witch lived in Grimde. When that witch stood in her doorway, nobody dared look in her direction for fear of being bewitched.
161801: A house in Haacht had much misfortune in the stable. The cows would no longer eat and kept lowing all the time. The people went to the friars of Dendermonde, who asked whether anyone had been in the stable. A woman had indeed visited and had leaned over the stable door. The friars gave the people a relic to put under the door. After that the woman never came in again.
161821: A place in Steenhuffel was so badly haunted that the branches of the bushes there beat against the ground.
161822: The devil appeared at midnight in the freemasons' lodge. After their death the freemasons had themselves cremated. When a brewer who was a freemason lay dying, the house was guarded by the devil so that the dean could not convert the dying man. The devil looked like a handsome gentleman.
161850: Stalkaarsen (will-o'-the-wisps) were floating lights that you were not allowed to point at. If you did, the lights came closer. People believed that the lights were the souls of dead children.
161860: A farmer had sold his soul to the devil in exchange for a barn that had to be finished before the rooster had crowed three times the next morning. The man lay restless in his bed and told his wife what he had agreed to. The wife stood next to the henhouse and made a crowing sound, so that the rooster began to crow. When the rooster had crowed three times, there was still a hole in the barn. The devils fled, and that hole could never be closed.
161865: When a gravestone had sunk right down or risen up in a single night, people were very afraid.
161874: A woman who worked somewhere as a maid always saw the mare appear at the skylight in the evening. The woman tried to call out, but no sound came. When one evening the woman wore her rosary, the mare no longer had any power over her.
161885: A woman walking alone to Mass in the dark in Vollezele met a black cat. Black cats seen in the evening were witches.
161888: A man from Houtem always went to play cards on the Heide. When the man came home one evening, he found a black brooding hen with chicks in the field. The man took the animals with him. When he got home, however, he found that the hen and the chicks had turned into stones. When the man took the stones back to the field, they turned back into animals.
161893: A farmer was driving his horse and cart through the village. At a certain spot, however, the horses stood still. When a woman from the neighbourhood went up to the horses and gave the animals a pat, the cart started moving again.
161908: In a house a child fell ill after a witch had visited. That witch was, of all people, the child's godmother. The child's parents went to the monastery. Two days later the witch came to ask how her godchild was. The child's mother lashed out at the witch with a chopper.
161924: A sick man could not be helped by any doctor. At night an owl always sat singing at the window of the room where the man lay. A spiritist was sent for from Rillaar, who went around the stable with a relic. The spiritist began scratching the ground between the cow's legs and pulled out a bone with meat on it. If the spiritist had not done that, the sick man would have died.
161952: A man who lived on the Rot was annoyed by a kitten he always saw in the evening. One evening the cat said to the man: "Jan called to me: pussycat, what are you doing?" The man was scared to death.
161967: When people had misfortune after someone had visited them, they often believed the visitor had bewitched them. Men were hardly ever suspected of witchcraft.
161988: A man who had moved a boundary post to get more land had to haunt after his death with a boundary post in his hands. The ghost kept calling: "Where shall I put it? Where shall I put it?" One day a brave man answered: "Well, damn it, put it where you got it!"
161989: A man claimed on coming home that he had been ridden by the 'moon' (the mare).
161992: A poacher who went hunting every night once heard loud laughter above his head. He looked up but saw nothing. The man raised his gun and fired, and the noise stopped at once. A little later, however, the man was given a beating and heard someone cry: "You've shot Trees, you've shot Trees!"
162002: Three fearless men were mocking stalkaarsen (ghost lights) and said: "If stalkaarsen exist, let them come and sit on my hand!" A moment later the men saw a black dog in front of them as big as a calf. At that the men ran away in fear and crawled under the haystack of a nearby house.
162042: In 1365 the castle of the counts of Loon was occupied by the people of Liège, who were helped by the inhabitants of Sint-Truiden. After a siege of seven weeks, it was forbidden to rebuild the castle for the next hundred years. Since then the castle was haunted. As punishment, the dead lords had to ride around the castle ruins in a fiery coach every night. Three boys from Rummen who did not believe in the haunting went to spend the night in the castle ruins by the light of a candle. Around midnight the candle flame suddenly grew bigger and bigger. A little later a fiery coach appeared. The coachman struck the three boys in the face with his whip. The next morning the boys were found unconscious in the ruins. On their faces they had a red welt from the whiplash.
162047: On a field path next to d' Hoeve a ghost walked about, calling: "Post, post, where shall I put you?" One day a drunkard answered: "Where you damn well took it from!" The ghost then replied: "That is a good idea" and he was released.
162050: In Heikruis there once lived a man and a woman who were said to be able to work magic. When people wanted to do something and it failed, they believed they had been bewitched. The woman who was said to be a witch had a disabled child who always sat in a pram. So people believed that the child had been bewitched.
162061: One day a farmer found a horse lying dead in the stable. A woman had visited the farm and had touched the horse several times. The friars came to the farm. They cut the horse open and took out the heart. Then they wanted to throw the heart onto a burning woodpile, because the witch would then have to jump into the fire too. At that very moment the witch arrived and said: "No, don't do that!" Because the witch screamed so desperately, in the end the heart was not burned.
162064: If you saw a cat walking in the evening and kicked at it, you never managed to hit it. In other cases the cat changed into a woman or a man after being kicked at. Cats you met in the evening had to be left alone.
162067: A house in the Motstraat was haunted. Someone walked around in the house, scraping the paper off the wall and holding a flame in his hand. The fathers read prayers over the house, but it did not help.
162103: A farmer's wife always found a woman in her pigsty, sitting there with a beet leaf. Because the pig would not grow, the vet was called. The pig had to be slaughtered. When that was done, knots were found all through the animal's intestines. The pig had been bewitched by that woman with the beet leaf.
162110: There used to be a church in the woods of the Merode. One day that church sank into the ground. At midnight the bells could still be heard ringing there. A forester who was always out at night had heard it once.
162121: A man who had stolen a great deal was banished to the sea for a hundred years. After that the man would come back to return what he had stolen.
162123: A boy in Beert was bewitched. One day, namely, a live lizard had crawled out of the boy's nose.
162151: Some families were in the habit of playing cards. They would gather in the house of one of the families and played and cursed to their hearts' content. The players played for money, which was shared out afterwards. Laughing, they said that part of the money was for the devil. Suddenly the light went out, after which the devil came out from under the table, beat up the players and made off with the money.
162157:
A farm in Pepingen was haunted for three years. People saw light and heard knocking, although nobody could be seen. The people then went to the fathers.
A man had sewn a medal from the fathers into his wallet to protect himself against witchcraft.
162206: A man who walked home through the woods of Blauberg in the evenings always met a black cat at the same spot. One day the man put a stone in his pocket to throw at the animal. When the man took hold of the stone, the cat said: "Just you dare throw it, filthy X!"
162215: In Eppegem lived an old woman who peddled paraffin. People always bought something from her because she was known for her witchcraft. One day a man did explain to the woman that he did not need any paraffin for the time being. The woman said: "That's fine," and stroked the man's little child on the head. The next day the child was gravely ill. After the priest had read prayers over the child, it recovered at once. The peddler had bewitched the child.
162218: A man from Webbekom went to play cards in a café every Sunday. When the man came home one Sunday, he took a shortcut along a narrow field path. Two hundred metres further on the man was followed by a small dog. The little dog walked close at the man's heels for a while. Because it was such a small dog, the man left the animal alone. When the man turned around a little later, however, he saw that the animal had changed into a big dog. About ten metres further the man had to cross the water by a small bridge. The dog ran ahead of him and sat down in front of the bridge. The man did not dare to step onto the bridge and so jumped over the brook instead. When the man looked back a little later, he saw that the dog had changed into a headless foal. The man gave the beast a hard blow. When he got home he took his gun and went back to the place where the beast had appeared. But there was nothing more to be seen. Two days later the man saw someone walking around the village with a bandage around his head.
162232: In the Bosstraat a man lay sick in bed. A rat that could not be hit was always running on the bed. At around four o'clock an unknown woman was sitting in the field. People believed that woman could turn herself into a rat.
162234: Women suspected of witchcraft were pointed at by everyone and in the end did not even dare go to Mass. In Halle lived a witch who could make mice from earth, or so the superstitious people believed.
162259: Will-o'-the-wisps arose from vapours released during rotting. In the past people believed that will-o'-the-wisps were the returned souls of sinners who wanted to be released.
162294: A bell is said to be buried in Dilbeek. When you drove past there with a cart, you heard screaming. There was also a little spring.
162298: In Hoegaarden lived a witch who was feared by everyone. One day the witch was in a shop where they had a young dog. The witch patted the animal on the rump and said: "You have a fine dog, madam!" Then the witch said to someone else: "Now go and say I bewitched it." The next day the dog could no longer stand on its legs. The vet could not make a diagnosis. A week later the dog was dead.
162306: It was said of black cats that they were witches.
162323: Two brothers who were Freemasons worked at the gin distillery of Metsteren. When one of the brothers lay dying, the priests and friars wanted him to make his confession. The other brother, however, said: "No, my brother must die as he has lived." After the man had died, a dog came into the gin distillery every night at twelve o'clock. That was the dead Freemason coming back to haunt.
162324: A boy of eight or nine had to go to catechism in the church at Zichem. The boy said to the other children: "Would you believe that I can throw the church door open with my little hat?" The boy suited the action to the word. In church the children told the priest what the boy had done. The priest had the boy repeat his trick and then took him to the presbytery. After that the boy could no longer work magic.
162328: Whenever a man came home in the evening from playing cards, he always saw a cat sitting on a hedge in the same spot.
162349: When a child had convulsions, people sometimes believed it had been touched by the evil hand.
162356: In Bierbeek lived a stingy farmer who had too little room in his barn to store his harvest. One evening the farmer was visited by a man with a fringe beard and a top hat, who said: "If you sign these papers, I will help you. Before the first cockcrow tomorrow morning your barn will be standing." The farmer agreed and signed. When he told his wife everything, she understood at once that her husband had made a deal with the devil. In the night the farmer's wife got up and walked around with a light, so that the rooster began to crow. All the workmen who were working on the barn vanished. A hole remained in the barn that could never be closed afterwards. The farmer was saved.
162387: In the evening a coach came from the direction of Dormaal and stopped for a moment at the crossroads. The horses did not want to go right, because the church stood there, and that was an enemy. They could not go left either, because the presbytery was there. So the coach drove straight on, towards a house where the barrier opened automatically. Then the coach turned back and took the direction of the presbytery, where the barriers also opened by themselves. As soon as the horses had reached the presbytery, the coach vanished without a trace.
162389: A woman from Charleroi went with her child to the kermis (fair) in Grimde. The little boy had beautiful curly hair that reached down to his shoulders, because in those days children's hair was not cut before their First Communion. A woman who lived there came outside, stroked the boy's head and said: "What lovely hair!" The next day all the boy's hair had to be cut off because it was full of lice.
162403: After his wife had died, Suske heard a strange knocking in the house. In the toilet the man met his wife's ghost, which was first white and then turned black. The ghost changed colour four times. Suske asked the ghost: "Trees, is that you?" The next moment the ghost had vanished. In the following days the knocking began again.
162407: A woman was always terrified whenever she saw a black cat anywhere, because she was convinced the animal would bring bad luck.
162430: In Edingen a whole family had died out. When a toad appeared there, the boy kicked the animal. Later it became known that the boy's maid was a sorceress.
162438: A woman who was ill fell to the floor beside her bed. The woman saw her deceased mother appear, together with her husband who had been dead for fourteen years. The ghosts were somewhat smaller than the people had been in life. The man said: "Let's take her with us", but the mother said: "No, no, she is not well". When the woman came to, she no longer saw the ghosts, but she heard her mother say: "You see, she wasn't feeling well just now!" Then the ghosts disappeared.
162481: In 't Broek there were hundreds of will-o'-the-wisps. Some people claimed that the lights were the little souls of unbaptised children. According to others they were the souls of dead sinners who had to return after their death.
162508: A cattle dealer went to the market in Tongeren. He had arranged with some other dealers to walk to Sint-Truiden and take the train from there. On the way to Sint-Truiden station, however, the man suddenly saw a white shade behind him. When the man slowed his pace, the shade also moved more slowly. When the man quickened his step, the shade went faster. The man never used that road again for fear of meeting the shade once more.
162513: A man surrounded by white and black cats made the sign of the cross or said a short prayer, after which the cats disappeared and the man could continue on his way.
162515: In Moorsel, at the time of the French, a bell had been thrown into the pond. A man who had betrayed this is said to have said: "I won't say where it is, but I'll drop a rose there." That is how the bell was found again.
162528: In Waasmont lived a witch who had caused a child to die.
162530: A man had to go to work in Nonnemielen (Metsteren) in the morning. To earn a little extra, he always went an hour early to feed the oxen. One morning the man saw a horse approaching. On the horse sat a small black gentleman. The man did not manage to stop the horse. The man walked home backwards because he did not dare turn around. When he got home, the man crawled into his bed and never got out of it alive.
162532: A girl had a relationship with a man. At midnight the man had to leave. When he came back a little later, he had threads of a shawl between his teeth. That man was a werewolf.
162537: Every night a ghost wearing only a shirt appeared in the churchyard. A few drunkards were sitting in the café next to the churchyard. One of them had bet a barrel of beer that he dared to go and take the ghost's shirt off. After the drunkard had done so, he had no more peace, because nobody wanted to take the shirt from him. The priest said to the man: "You must go back tonight and return that shirt to the ghost." That evening, when the man had put the shirt back on the ghost, the ghost struck him in the face. Three months later the man was dead.
162552: In Bunsbeek a black cat roamed about that always bothered people. One day the cat is said to have sat on a man's shoulder. After that incident the cat was never seen again.
162560: When people had much misfortune in their stable, they often believed it was due to the evil hand or to witchcraft.
162564: When people pushed their wheelbarrows up the hill by the castle of Groot-Bijgaarden, they kept seeing a black lady in front of the wheelbarrow. One day a man said to the apparition: "Wouldn't you rather sit on the wheelbarrow instead of walking in front of it?" The next moment the lady sat down on the wheelbarrow, which then weighed almost nothing. When the man reached the top of the hill, he said to the lady: "Madam, I have no business with you, but thank you for the help." The next moment the wheelbarrow tipped over and the load fell to the ground. The man could no longer lift the sack back onto the wheelbarrow. He quickly called on a saint, after which he was able to put the sack on the wheelbarrow.
