162588: A man who had been out hunting saw a red tomcat leaping about on his way home, and it followed him all the way to his house. The man had the greatest difficulty keeping the tomcat outside. Some people claimed that the tomcat was bewitched.
162597: A farmer from Oppem had so much grain that he could not store it all in his barn. One day a gentleman came to the farm who wanted to build a barn for the farmer in a single night. The farmer did have to sign a contract in his own blood. The farmer agreed. While the devils were building in the night, the farmer lay sighing in his bed. In the end he told his wife what he had done. The farmer's wife understood immediately that her husband had sold his soul. Before morning came, the farmer's wife got up and knocked her clogs together. This made the rooster crow, so that all the devils had to leave. The barn was not yet finished, for there was still a hole that had to be closed. No one ever managed to close that hole. A large red cross was made in the gable of the barn, which the devils could not pass. After that the hole could be closed.
162602: A woman who lived on the Bunsbeekse Steenweg had eaten an apple that she had been given by a witch. Four days later the woman saw the apple come out again through her belly. The woman consulted a fortune-teller, who told her: "I will make the woman who did this to you appear." The witch appeared in the mirror and the fortune-teller asked: "Will you take over these wounds?" Because she would not, the boy died.
162609: A witch could conjure black patches into a wheat field.
162619: Franske claimed that his dead wife came to sleep with him every night. The priest claimed the woman was haunting because she had promised a pilgrimage. Eventually the clergyman managed to make the ghost disappear. After her death, Celine came to haunt her sister, with whom she had been angry all her life. At night the dead woman's sister was dreaming. When she opened her eyes, she saw her dead sister, dressed in black, standing in front of the bed.
162683: A farmer who one evening saw a toad crawl out of the water drain threw the red-hot stove poker at the animal. The next day the farmer met a woman who had two burns on her cheeks. That is how people found out who the witch was.
162686: A man had told a friend: "If I die before you, you must not pray for me". When that man had died, the friend always heard: "Pray, pray, pray!" After people had prayed for the deceased, the ghost was no longer heard.
162731: A farm had a single cow, which the children took out walking so it could graze. A shopkeeper who was suspected of being a witch had given the cow a bundle of beet leaves. The farmer's wife did not trust the woman, however, and threw the leaves into a bramble bush. Shortly afterwards the cow died. The children had taken the cow out walking. Perhaps the animal had eaten the beet leaves while the children were playing.
162734: In Keerbergen lived a man who always wore an old coat that reached down to his knees. When that man had been dead for some time, his ghost was seen appearing in the woods. He walked to the oven of his house and then went away again. People claimed that the man had hidden money there. You were not allowed simply to shake hands with a dead person; you always had to hold a cloth in your hand, or else the dead person's hand would burn right through that of the living. The priest himself had said so.
162736: At the beginning of the First World War a woman lived in Groenendaal who was suspected of being a witch. A man whom the woman had tapped on the arm could not use his arm for a whole month.
162767: One Sunday a man had gone to play cards in the inns 'De vuile voorschoot' and 'De hemel'. When the man came back along the Steenhuffelstraat, he heard organ music and laughter. The man saw a big tent and went inside. In the tent sat elegant ladies and gentlemen and young misses. The man was kindly received and was allowed to dance with the young ladies. Afterwards the man got hungry and decided to eat something. Before he started eating, he made the sign of the cross. The next moment the whole scene had vanished and the man was sitting on a molehill.
162773: A man coming back from Wieze kicked at a black cat running under his feet. But the man missed, and a little later he saw a good hundred cats. Scared to death, the man went on.
162780: A poacher was followed by a cat at the Kestergat. The man wanted to shoot the cat, but his friend advised him against it.
162798: People were very afraid of those who came back after their death.
162818: A boy was walking with his girlfriend along the woodland path from Elsleuken to the Molenhei in Wolfsdonk. At a certain moment the boy said to his girlfriend: "I have to go off for a moment. Here is my handkerchief. If a dog comes at you, throw the handkerchief over its head and the animal will do you no harm." Shortly after the boy leaves, the girl sees a big black dog coming. The girl throws the handkerchief at the dog's head, whereupon the animal disappears. A little later the girl's boyfriend comes back. He has the fibres of the handkerchief between his teeth.
162822: A man walking past the Zavelputten in the Rasselstraat in Wemmel suddenly saw a large black dog approaching. Because the man was afraid of the animal, he turned back. When he took another road the second time, he met the dog again. The third time the same thing happened once more. The man claimed he would have hit the dog if he had had a stick with him.
162830: On a farm in Sterrebeek the people had much misfortune with the children and the animals. Because the farmer's wife often gave away two or three litres of buttermilk, the priests told her: "You must not give anything away for free any more. People must do something for it, for example pray a Hail Mary or pay something." The farmer's wife went with a neighbour to the priests of Scherpenheuvel and to Leuven. When the farmer's wife had taken communion in Leuven and had confessed, she could barely get out of the confessional. In the end the farmer's wife was freed from the influence of evil.
162848:
A man who suffered greatly from the death of his wife always went and stood under the same apple tree. People believed that a sorceress from the neighbourhood had bewitched that man. Later the man went to an old people's home.
Of a man who always chopped trees at night, people believed that he could do witchcraft.
162897: People who were ridden by the mare were suddenly seized and felt as if they were going to die. A man who was ridden by his mare every evening always felt the mare coming, but he could not resist. He tried to call out, but no sound came. Afterwards the man was drenched in sweat. If one recited an act of contrition or hung a rosary on the door, the mare could not come in.
162906: A man from Rummen had a witch as his neighbour. The man often heard cats fighting in his attic. The witch was causing that noise.
162908: A hot-tempered man who worked for a farmer began to curse one day during the harvest because his work was not going well. The man always saw a white cat walking in the field. He lashed out at the animal but could not hit it. The man knelt down and began to pray until he was sweating. Afterwards he worked a little longer and then went home.
162921: A mother went to the priests because her little child was wasting away completely and was sometimes flung back and forth. The trouble had started after a witch had come to visit and had wanted to pick the child up. The mother had then said: "Leave the child lying there, because it is asleep." The next day, however, the child had fallen ill. In the end it died.
162926: In Meise a girl had died. That girl was always visited by a neighbour, who brought her a sweet. Afterwards people said that the neighbour had bewitched the girl. In reality the girl died of tuberculosis.
162930: People who associated with a witch were ridden by the mare at night. They could not move for a quarter of an hour, so that they seemed to be dead. A woman who was ridden by the mare because she associated with a witch was freed from the torment when the witch died.
162941: A sick farmer was regularly visited by a neighbour woman. Because the farmhand did not trust her, he once spied on her. He saw that at every visit she stuck a pin into the farmer's pillow. When she came again the next day, the farmhand said to her: "If you don't take all those pins out of the pillow at once, I'll pour petrol over you and set you on fire." The neighbour did as she was told, and after that the farmer was cured. The pins had ended up in his heart.
162980: A man coming home with the midwife was followed the whole way by a cat. The man asked: "What are you doing here, kitty?", but when he opened the door the cat jumped on him and scratched his hand. Because his hand hurt badly, the man expected to see a bleeding wound, but there was no wound to be seen at all. That was witchcraft.
162988:
A Partisan had taken the church bell out of the tower of the church of Meldert. When the French found out, an altar boy ran off with the little bell to the Kravaalbos in Mazel. In the Graat, however, he could no longer carry it and dropped it. At that spot the bell sank into the ground. Every year at twelve o'clock at Christmas the little bell could still be heard ringing there. Some boys from Doment who wanted to hear the ringing once came to the spot before twelve. Shortly before twelve a tremendous roar was heard, and the boys ran away in fear.
The Molenbeek is said to have sprung up at that spot.
In the seventeenth century bluestone and a treasure were dug up there. The pit was more than four metres deep.
162995: A girl heard from her mother that a light that appeared by a box shrub was the soul of an unborn child.
163009: Stalkaarsen (will-o'-the-wisps) were lost little souls that you sometimes met in the woods. If you had pointed at such a little flame, it came and sat on your finger.
163019: On a farm in Sint-Pieters-Rode worked a maid who was a witch. At night the maid had to bake bread. Between midnight and one o'clock the maid sometimes stood stock-still with her hands in the dough. As soon as the hour was over, the maid behaved normally again. She was dismissed immediately afterwards.
163022: The daughter of a witch worked at the sugar factory in Tienen. When that woman had struck someone on the knee, the knee was completely swollen the next day. A pregnant woman who had worked next to the witch's daughter found at midday that her sandwiches were full of vermin.
163026: A man coming back from Neerwinden around midnight and going to his girlfriend in Wange had to stand still at the crossroads for at least an hour because an endless line of rats was crossing the road.
163045: In the Hollestraat in Hakendover there used to be a hare every night that no one could catch. It was the ghost of a dead person who had returned.
163048: Two girls coming home from school saw two women come out of a house. One of the women stroked one of the girls on the head and said: "What a good child she is". That evening the girl had lice. Strangely enough, her sister did not have a single louse on her head. The mother, who had combed the lice out of her daughter's hair, believed the girl had been bewitched.
163060: People who had bad luck believed they had been ridden by the mare and went to a monastery to have a blessing read over them. Sometimes the priest gave them a scapular.
163068: A strange horse always appeared in a hop garden. When people went digging there one day, they found money. The ghost had hidden the money there.
163070: A woman was ridden by the mare every night. The mare crept in through the window and then sat on its victim.
163087: In the past people always kept watch over a dead person, because they were afraid the dead person would come back to life. People who had died before fulfilling a vow they had made had to come back after their death.
163088: People could sometimes lose their way through sorcery.
163115: A farmer from Bierbeek had no barn big enough to store all his grain. The farmer called on the devil, who was willing to build him a barn in a single night, to be finished before the first cockcrow the next morning. But the rooster crowed before five o'clock, so the barn was not finished in time. The hole in the barn could never be closed.
163133: In a small house in the village lived an old woman who always carried a stick. Wherever that woman came, people could not make butter. One day the woman wanted to enter a house where a cow was about to calve. The people, however, had put a holy object under the threshold, so the woman could not get in.
163137: A woman was tormented by her mother-in-law, who was a witch. One winter evening the woman got a phone call because something was wrong with her daughter. The girl was standing in a certain spot and could not move a foot or utter a word. However hard people pulled at the girl, she would not budge from the tile she was standing on. The mother had to hurry to Meensel-Kiezegem with her own pillow, her husband's and her daughter's, because the pillows had to be burned before midnight. When the parents arrived in Meensel-Kiezegem, they saw that their daughter had big red eyes, as if she were possessed by the devil. The parents had to pray and hold a candle from the grotto of Our Lady. At seven minutes to twelve everyone went outside. Through the window they saw the candle bend down to the floor. At five to twelve they tried to set the three pillows on fire, but it did not work. Just before midnight the pillows did catch fire. When the pillows had almost burned up, a snake with a devil's head with two horns was seen inside them. After that intervention the girl could move and speak again. If no one had come to her aid, she would have died.
163143: In Waasbeek a witch had covered a boy in lice. The witch even covered the priest's maid in lice. Fortunately the priest was able to take the lice away again.
163150: In Opdorp there lived a witch who could give people the kwade hand (the evil hand, a bewitching touch). People who had fallen victim to her went to the abbey of Dendermonde, where prayers were read over them and they were given an Agnus Dei to put under the witch's chair. This left the witch powerless.
163163: In Laar lived a woman who was suspected of being a witch. That woman could even get in through a closed gate. If that woman had touched a child, the child had been struck by the evil hand.
163167: In Bogaarden lived witches who could cause people to have much misfortune with the animals in the stable. The people then had to send for a priest to have prayers read over the stable. After that the witch could no longer step over the threshold of the stable.
163185: Some Bohemians came to a farmer's wife to ask for some hay or straw. One of the Bohemian women had swished her skirt against the farmer's wife. From this the farmer's wife knew that something would happen to her. When she stood on the ladder, her skirt got caught on a hook.
163198: People who were ridden by the mare could no longer breathe in their sleep and then woke up.
163199:
A witch from Charleroi was said to have once appeared in the form of a black cat. The cat always walked along with two men going to the railway station. Because the men were annoyed by the cat, one day they struck it on the head. The next moment a little old woman stood before them and said: "You'd beat me to death like that!" The woman had a big cut on her forehead, so people asked her what had happened. She would answer: "I fell off the haystack."
No child dared go to that woman to sing for the New Year. When memorial cards had to be brought to her, the children did not dare ring the bell and slid the card under the door.
163211: When people went to dig up potatoes, they did not dare pick up a potato on which a witch had cast her gaze.
163212: If you were touched on the head by a witch, you always had to strike her higher. If you had been given something by a witch, an apple for example, you had to leave it lying for a night. Sometimes the next day maggots were found in the gift.
163219: On a farm the calf could always be heard lowing at night. When people went to look, strangely enough there was nothing to be seen. As soon as the people went to sleep, the lowing began again. The evil hand had something to do with it. That is why the people had to go on a pilgrimage.
163242: On his way, a carter had come across a black cat, which had jumped onto his cart and sat behind him meowing. The carter had already struck at the cat several times, but the animal stayed on the cart. Finally the man hit the cat with his whip as hard as he could. The animal lay still and stopped meowing. When the carter got home, he could hardly believe his eyes: there was a dead woman lying on his cart. That cat had been a sorceress in animal form.
163257: A cat appeared in a house every day at twelve o'clock. The people there had much misfortune and saw many cows die in their stable. The farmer sat by the door when the cat came along. But the cat did not come in and stayed on the threshold, mewing. The farmer went to a man who gave him a holy relic and said: "The first person to come in early tomorrow morning is the guilty one." The next day a little old woman came to ask for salt. She had to be held back or she would have walked into the fire.
163285: When K.L. was coming back from the inn one evening, he saw on the Rot (Nieuwrode) a will-o'-the-wisp that kept flying around him. Will-o'-the-wisps were the souls of children who had died unbaptised. After K. had baptised the will-o'-the-wisp, it disappeared.
163293: A girl found it strange that her boyfriend always had to go home so early when they went to the fair together. One day before leaving the boy had said: "If you meet anyone on the way, throw your handkerchief in his face and say that the person must first unravel the handkerchief with his teeth before he may lay hands on you." The girl did as she had been advised. When she saw her boyfriend again a few days later, she noticed that he still had the threads of the handkerchief between his teeth. He was a sorcerer.
163306: In Teralfene a girl had had a child. After a pedlar woman who sold darning needles had stood by the cradle, the child was bewitched. The mother went with the child to Affligem, where she was advised to keep an eye out whenever that pedlar was nearby. The girl followed the advice and her child recovered.
163307: A sorceress who came to fetch milk from a pregnant woman said to the woman: "You will have to wait a while yet for your child." When the mother asked: "How do you know that?", the sorceress said: "I know it." The mother had to suffer pain for seven days before the child was born. That witch was responsible for it.
163317: A poacher who complained that he always came home with a meagre catch was advised by someone to try poaching in the Heylissemveld. The poacher had barely settled there with his gun when he saw a hare running. When the poacher shot at the hare, the animal said "Pssssst" and vanished. A little later a second hare appeared, and exactly the same thing happened. When a third hare appeared, the poacher aimed his gun at it, and the animal said: "Did the other two pass by long ago?" The poacher believed that the man who had sent him to that field could work magic.
163340: A boy had a relationship with a girl from Walsbets. When the boy met his girlfriend in the evening, he always had to leave at a certain time. The girl then went home alone. One evening on her way home the girl met a werewolf. She struck the beast's jaws with her handkerchief. When she saw her fiancé again the next day, she noticed that he had the fibres of the handkerchief between his teeth.
163376: Two girls had died in a house. In the evening two little flames could be seen leaping in the two apple trees opposite that house. People claimed that those stalkaarsen (will-o'-the-wisps) were the returned souls of the dead girls.
163392: A witch from Bost had bewitched her three daughters. When the witch lay on her deathbed, she climbed the walls with pain. In the end one of her daughters took over her mother's magic power out of pity.
163414: A farmer from de Opot had no money to build a new barn to store his harvest. The farmer was visited by a smart gentleman who offered to build him a barn in exchange for his soul. The barn would be finished before the first cockcrow the next morning. The farmer agreed to the proposal. In the night the farmer lay tossing and turning restlessly in his bed. He told his wife what he had done. The farmer's wife threw open the window and knocked her clogs together, so that the rooster began to crow early. At that moment, however, the barn was not yet finished.
163415: After a cat had been wounded somewhere, it was found that a woman from the village had lost her hand.
163418: In Ruisbroek there used to be a beggar woman who always came by and who was afraid when a crow flew over her head. She believed that it would bring bad luck.
163425: In Linden there lived many witches who could take on another shape and so do people harm. At certain times of the year the witches held meetings. The witches then flew through the air after saying: "Over hedge and hedgerow." A man who had heard this made a mistake in saying the magic formula and said: "Through hedge and hedgerow." That man arrived in Cologne badly injured and never came back.
163432: Two men were coming back from a café in the evening. On the way one man said to the other: "I have to go into the bushes for a moment. You go on. If anything comes at you, throw my handkerchief at the figure." A little further on the other man saw a werewolf coming at him and threw a handkerchief at the beast. A little later the first man rejoined his friend. But when he took out a handkerchief to blow his nose, it turned out to be torn completely to shreds.
163457: A pruner setting off for work with his knife in his hand saw two dogs blocking his way. The man stood against a tree and threw his knife at the animals. He hit the smallest dog, whereupon the animal ran away, followed by the big dog. They were ghost animals.
163475: People who were drunk often believed they were being ridden by the mare.
163481: People who were ridden by the mare were jumped on in the evening by someone who made them carry him.
163506: A woman was always tormented by her mother-in-law. One night the woman woke up because she needed the toilet. However, the woman could not move, so she could not get out of bed. Her husband said: "Wait a moment, because she is at you again." The man did something and the next moment the woman could get up without any trouble to go to the toilet.
163550: People who were ridden by the mare had to grab at the mare with a rosary. Then they had to put the mare under an upturned manure tub, so that the next day they could see who it was.
163556: Witches usually entered houses through the water drain. In a house on the road to Engsbergen, a cat also came in through the water drain. People wounded the cat with an axe, and in this way found out which woman was the witch who had turned herself into a cat.
163571: A man coming back on a summer evening from the rehearsal of the music society in Hoeilaart suddenly saw a big dog standing in front of him. The man was terrified, but the dog did him no harm.
163573: People who were ridden by the mare lay sweating and could not breathe. They tried to call out, but no sound came. The mare was a woman.
163577: A man heard the devils making a lot of noise in his attic. Suddenly two dogs jumped into a stone well that stood by the house.
163588: Some women from Assent coming back from the fair saw something moving in the meadow on the way. One of the children said: "Look, there's something there." The mother answered: "Oh, that's a cow or something," but she knew better. People knew that the place was haunted.
163603: On a farm all the pigs died through witchcraft. The people knew who was to blame, but they had gone to the priests too late.
163611: In one family someone was always ill. At a certain moment the people's little daughter began to cry without stopping. A witch probably had power over the child.
163628: In Wolvertem there was a little child who was always struck in its cradle so that it flew up against the ceiling. It was a witch who tormented the child in this way. In the end the child died.
163629:
A woman had bewitched a little child. The parents had quickly gone with the child to Kapelleveld to have prayers read over it. There the people were advised to slip one of the child's nappies under the chair of every visitor, to find out who the culprit was. The witch would not be able to get up from it until she had undone the harm she had caused.
A while later a neighbour came to visit. When the child's father, without batting an eyelid, slipped a nappy under the woman's chair, she stayed sitting stock-still. At a certain moment she jumped up and said: "I have to go home!" The child's parents were speechless. After that the woman never came to visit again.
163637: Will-o'-the-wisps were the souls of the dead that followed people. Some people claimed that the lights were caused by phosphorus.
163659: Stallichten (will-o'-the-wisps) came from damp places or from rotting matter. People were very afraid of the stallichten that followed them, because they believed they were the souls of unbaptised children.
163683: A farmer had misfortune with the cows in his stable. The animals stopped eating and fell ill. The farmer went to a vet, but he could not help him. When someone from the village said: "It looks as if it has something to do with witchcraft," the farmer went to a man in the village. The farmer had to set fire to a tree stump. Then the farmer and the man sat down by the fire. They had set out a third chair, with a relic under it. A little later a neighbour woman came in and sat on the third chair. It grew hotter and hotter, and the farmer fetched another tree stump to put on the fire. The woman became so hot that she wanted to get up, but she could not. She begged to be released. They said to her: "If you undo the evil you have done, we will let you go. Otherwise you will burn here." The woman promised to undo the evil and stood up after the relic was taken from under her chair. Then she went to the stable door, made the sign of the cross and said: "Well, friend, may the evil be over within three days." The cows that were still alive at that moment did not fall ill.
163718: People who were ridden by the moon (the mare) lay stiff as a board in their beds and could not move or call out.
163761: Some people from Meldert had met a witch, who always wore a headscarf and long clothes. When they got home, the people found their rabbits lying dead in the hutch.
163780: A farmer was desperate because he could not store his harvest in his barn. On the way the farmer met a gentleman, who told him: "If you sell me your most precious possession, a barn will be standing tomorrow morning before the rooster has crowed." When the farmer told his wife what he had done, she advised him to get up in the middle of the night, which made the rooster crow early. Because the barn was not yet finished at that moment, the farmer could keep his soul. The hole in the barn could never be bricked up afterwards.
163783: People who were ridden by the mare had no luck.
163788: A poacher who saw a fat hare running in the field loaded his gun to shoot it. Just then a black cat walked by a few metres from the poacher. The man fired, but his gun did not work. He tried six or seven bullets, but it would not work. When the man got home and tested his gun in his garden, it worked. The man then said: "Damn it, that witch has fooled me again by turning into a black cat!"
163800: A poor man had buried his dead child without a shroud. In the evenings the man always heard a cry: "My little shirt, my little shirt!" The man hung the little shirt on the shutters. The next day the shirt was gone.
163810: In Bierbeek lived a farmer who never went to church. One day the man was visited by the devil, who asked: "Is there nothing you need?", to which the man answered: "Yes, I need a barn, because I cannot bring in my grain." Then the devil said: "If you sell me your soul, you will have a barn tomorrow." The farmer agreed, but demanded that the barn be finished the next day before the first cockcrow. When the rooster crowed at five o'clock that morning, the barn was not yet finished and the building collapsed. The barn had been made of whole trees with the roots still hanging from them.
163812: A man who lived by the church of Egenhoven walked through the Pastoorsboske to work in the mornings. From the farm of the Jesuits to the Langenstraat the man was accompanied by a ghost in a long black skirt. That ghost appeared again every morning.
163837: In Tienen lived a woman who was suspected of being a witch. When children passed that woman's house, they had to make the sign of the cross and say: "God protect us." A wire was stretched in front of the witch's house. One day a boy threw a stone at a black cat walking there. Shortly afterwards the witch wore a bandage around her arm. She also had abscesses on her face and neck.
163841: When the street beside the churchyard in Nieuwerkerken was to be widened, a number of skeletons had to be dug up. A man sitting in a nearby café one evening told his friends he dared to go and fetch a skull from the churchyard. In the churchyard, however, the man heard a voice saying: "Leave that head where it is, for that is my father's head!"
163852: A farm was plagued by rats. For nine days in a row the people walked around the farm while praying the Gospel of Saint John. They did have to leave one spot open through which the rats could escape. On the ninth day they were rid of the rats. Someone had sent those animals.
163861: The Knight of Hoxem wanted to go to the fair in Leuven with a friend. When the friend said: "It's so late already. We'll never get there in time!", the Knight said: "Just hang on to my coat. We'll be there in no time." The two reached Leuven just in time. The friend had hit the tower of the Sint-Pieterskerk with his foot.
163863: A farmer was ploughing his field while a little further off an old woman was cutting fodder. That woman was suspected of being a witch. When the farmer's horses would no longer pull the plough, the farmer shouted: "If you don't let my horses go now, I'll come over to you!" At that the old woman became frightened and made sure the horses could go on again.
163870: When children were ill, people often believed that they were bewitched. They then had prayers read over the children to fight the evil hand.
163891: In Wespelaar a dead man was said to have returned because he had moved a boundary post. Because at night a voice could be heard calling all the time: "Post, post, where shall I put you?", one day a drunkard answered: "Put it where you got it!" After that the voice was heard no more.
163895: When people saw a toad somewhere, they were quick to believe it was a witch in animal form.
163908: On a farm a woman came to look at the sheep. The next day the sheep was dead. Whenever the woman came to visit, she always brought something with her. That time, for example, she had brought a kilo of sugar. When the woman came by another time, she wanted to see the cow. The farmer, however, had made sure the cow was in a remote meadow, so that was not possible. Because the farmer knew that the woman was bewitching his farm, he decided to move.
163940: A little boy had been given some cherries by a neighbour who had a bad name. Afterwards the child fell ill. The mother went with the boy to the priests of Affligem, who read prayers over him. The child recovered, but the mother went to the witch and said: "If you do that one more time, I will put something blessed on my gun and shoot you dead!" The witch did not do it a second time.
163945: Anyone who had been touched by a witch from Molenbeek-Wersbeek had to go to Leuven to get an injection.
163958: A man passed a bewitched tree stump with his cart. At that spot the man could go no further with his cart. He dropped dead there.
163961: When the priest of Kokejane (a hamlet of Herne) forgot to close his missal, one woman could not leave the church.
163981: Witches usually left an object behind, such as a handkerchief or a sock. If one picked up that object, one was bewitched.
163983: Witches deliberately put a sweet or a biscuit on the ground, in the hope that a child would pick it up.
163990: A haunted castle had been sold many times because nobody dared to live there. One day a young lord moved into the castle. When the lord was cooking on the first evening, all kinds of body parts fell down the chimney into the cooking pot. A little later a complete skeleton stood in the room. When the ghost gestured to the lord to go to the cellar, he replied: "You first". In the cellar stood a chest that the lord was supposed to open. The lord made the skeleton open the chest itself. When the chest was opened, a deep abyss appeared. When the ghost had to sneeze, the lord said: "God bless you". At that the ghost suddenly vanished. Since then the castle has never been haunted again.
163994: A man whose rabbits always lay dead in the shed whenever he wanted to take the animals to market was at his wits' end. The man's wife complained to a friend, who said: "But surely you know who you live next to? Go to the white canons and that misfortune will soon be over." The woman followed the advice and was given a holy object by a priest to put under the threshold. After that no more rabbits died at those people's house. It was the neighbour who had done those people harm for so long.
163998:
In the Gijmel (a hamlet in Langdorp) lived a sorcerer who could turn himself into a dog. That dog roamed everywhere in the evenings. A man who believed in nothing also saw the dog one day. The animal had eyes like flashlights. The man cycled home as fast as he could.
Another man who met the dog had to carry the animal on his shoulders until he was home.
164023: During the war some people went to saw down chestnut trees in the wood by the castle because there was no coal to be had. At a certain moment the men saw a witch go by. However much they sawed after that, they could not get the tree to fall.
164034: Stalkaarsen (will-o'-the-wisps) were lights that followed people. People believed that stalkaarsen were the little souls of unbaptised children.
164046: A man went with an exceptionally strong horse to fetch pine trees from the woods for a sorcerer. Strangely, the horse would not pull the load. The carter's brother cut some mud off a spoke of the wheel with a little knife. The next moment the horse could move on effortlessly.
164049: For a whole year a man was forced by a mysterious power to go to the Amelgemmolen in the Bosstraat. There the man heard ghosts walking on the stairs and banging on the door, though there was nothing to be seen.
164078: In Humbeek there lived a black madam who was always out at night and followed the men.
164086: A man went to fetch the midwife for his wife, who was about to give birth to her first child. On the way the midwife saw all kinds of terrible things, which only disappeared when she knelt down. Curiously, the man saw none of these things.
164104: A man went to the fair with some friends. On the way the men saw a fine café. They went into the café and said: "Oh, what is this here, Jesus, Mary, what is this here?" The next moment the men were sitting on a dung heap.
164115: In a parish where a witch lived, several people were bewitched in the church. Some urged the parish priest not to let that witch into the church any more. The priest refused, however, since the pope wanted everyone to be allowed into church. One day a woman had a miscarriage after she had been given a false holy object by the witch. When that woman went to the churchyard, she broke her leg. During mass the priest saw the witches sitting by the pulpit. He preached: "Beware of the witches, especially those under my pulpit."
164121: On a large farm in Sint-Martens-Lennik the animals' manger was full of needles. That farm was ruined by evil. The unmarried farmer's wife, who owned many dogs, then gave up farming. On Saturdays the church bells were often heard ringing because so many masses were said for the soul of that farmer's wife.
164131: A woman from Nieuwenrode was so ill that people believed she would die. So the priests were sent for. The clergymen found a wreath of leaves under the woman's pillow. Because the wreath was not yet finished, the woman was still alive.
164163: Nobody dared to spend the night in the Duvelkasteel because it was haunted. One day a brave man came to ask whether he could spend the night in the castle. To reach his bedroom, the man had to open thirteen doors, each with thirteen locks. At night a ghost came into the bedroom, took out a razor and set a chair beside the table. The man jumped out of bed and let the ghost shave his hair and beard. Then the ghost lay down in the bed. The man took the razor himself and gestured to the ghost to come and sit on the chair. After the man had in turn shaved off the ghost's hair and beard, the ghost said: "I am the owner of the castle. I once had a mishap with a barber. Now I cannot reach heaven until that incident has been made right. You have shaved my beard and I yours. Now I am happy. The same must happen thirteen nights in a row, and then I will be released. After those thirteen days I will write my will and see to it that the castle and its grounds are yours". In the morning the man told the castle's owner that his hair had fallen out from fear. Thirteen days later the castle belonged to the man.
164165: In Overhespen lived a woman who could cover people in lice by touching them.
164178: Eight or nine people came to catch rats in a house that was full of them, but no one managed to catch even a single rat. The man who lived in the house died in despair. The rat plague had been caused by a witch who lived in the village. Once, when a carter was out with his ox, the witch had said: "He won't drive any further, just wait until you get to the village!" In the village the ox did indeed lie down.
164212: A man from Meldert had seen a black cat and had become bewitched after being touched by a witch.
164219: When many animals died on a farm, people soon believed they had fallen victim to the evil hand. A priest would then come to read prayers over the farm. He also often gave the people a medal.
164221: On a haunted farm in Gelrode the cows were always untied. The people attributed these events to witchcraft. In the ivy by the stable a clattering could often be heard, which was caused by the witches. In the end the farmer's wife moved to Wilsele. There she was no longer troubled by witchcraft.
164274: In Outgaarden a rich childless farmer had died. At night the maid woke up because she heard chains rattling in the farmyard. Yet there was nothing to be seen. One night the farmer's wife and the maid stayed awake to keep watch together. As soon as she heard the rattling of the chains, the farmer's wife opened the window and asked: "What do you want?" The voice of her dead husband said she had to go to Scherpenheuvel seven times. Otherwise he would not be able to leave purgatory. When the farmer's wife and the maid had been to Scherpenheuvel seven times, they no longer heard the rattling.
164307: A man always saw a ghost come down the chimney. It was the ghost of someone who had committed a mortal sin. When the ghost appeared for the third time, the man said: "What God keeps is well kept". Since then the man has not seen the ghost again. If a ghost was not released, it killed the person to whom it had appeared.
164310: On her way home from school a girl was taken by the hand by a witch. That girl was paralysed for the rest of her life.
164312: A woman claimed that her husband had lost his way because of a neighbour woman.
164335: The bells of the abbey of Kessel-Lo had flown away and sunk into the surrounding meadows when the Dutch invaded the abbey and set it on fire. At certain times of the year those bells could still be heard ringing. The kettle of the abbey's old brewery is also said to be buried somewhere there. That kettle was supposedly filled with gold and silver. Many people have searched for it, but in vain.
164369: A boy from Merchtem was cycling to his brother in Steenhuffel. He had been on his way only ten minutes when he saw a white cat jump in front of his wheel. The cat was a good forty or fifty centimetres long and had a black spot on its back. Its tail was almost as thick as the man's arm. The cat followed the boy for a quarter of an hour, then jumped over the ditch and disappeared. A while later, strangely enough, the boy saw the cat appear again. That cat was a witch. The boy often met that cat on the way.
164373:
A farmer bringing in hay could not get on, even though several horses had been harnessed to the cart. A sorceress, however, leaned against the cart and said: "Go on!" When the sorceress asked: "Not going well, farmer?", the farmer answered gruffly: "No." At that the sorceress said: "Wait, I'll help push." When the sorceress put her hand against the cart, the horses started moving.
Children were not allowed to accept apples from that sorceress.
164374: One night a woman from Leuven heard her name called three times in a row. The next day the woman received a telegram saying that her best friend had died that night.
164377:
A woman who sold books of magic always asked her customers whether they really knew what kind of book they were bringing into their house.
A book of magic described how to make the door of a house open by itself, so that one could easily commit a burglary.
164382: A soldier came home on eight days' leave. Near the soldier lived a witch who always gave the man a pat on the shoulder, saying: "You're such a smart little soldier, you are!" Every time the witch had done that, the man was covered in lice.
164407: In Linden lived a man who suspected that his wife was a witch. One night the supposed witch had to go with her husband to the smithy. At midnight the man saw that his wife had fallen asleep on a chair. A little later he saw something on the chair burst into flames. At first the man thought his wife was on fire, but a moment later he saw that it was a sheaf of straw that had caught fire. So the woman really was a witch. The man left his wife.
164410: A woman who had been ridden by the mare lost her way. She wandered around the village and suddenly saw a large white horse.
164427: When people had bad luck, they believed they had been ridden by the mare.
164434: A man who had gone to work in his field saw an apple lying on a windowsill on his way home. The man ate the apple and a few hours later lost his mind. The fruit had been bewitched. The white fathers of Gent read prayers over the man, but he still had to be taken to a psychiatric institution. After he had stayed there for a year, he was healthy again.
164435: A witch from Budingen is said to have made her own child's leg wither.
164457: On a farm where a witch had been in the stable a few times, the cow fell ill. The farmer's wife went to fetch the butcher, who advised her to have the cow slaughtered quickly if she still wanted to sell the meat. No sooner said than done. The witch found out from someone what had happened on the farm. She went to the farmer's wife and said: "You can keep quiet well too!", to which the farmer's wife replied: "Yes, silence is golden." Then the witch left. The next day the farmer's wife had to have all the beef taken away without earning a cent from it.
164471: A witch always tried to keep her granddaughter near her so that she could pass on her magic arts to the girl.
164488:
A woman who was baking cakes heard a cat meowing at the door and threw a cake at the animal. The next day a neighbour lay in bed with a burnt face.
In the old days, the old people had dealings with the devil.
164501: Some people claimed that they dealt with the devil. A farmhand who had to bring in the harvest for a farmer could work three times as fast as anyone else.
164511: In Wemmel lived a man who had once been ridden by the mare. The man had started sweating, could hardly breathe and felt as if a thousand kilos were resting on him. This state could last as long as three or four hours. The doctor claimed that the mare was a stoppage of the blood.
164536: When someone had committed suicide, the family had to pay seven stuivers. When V. had hanged himself, the family had paid nothing and buried the body in the wood of Heinke A. A woman gathering leaves in the wood accidentally scratched the corpse uncovered. From that day the ghost wandered through the wood every night saying: "Berloe, Berloe". Nobody dared to go into the wood of Heinke A. any more. One evening Pie V.L. heard the calling. The man called out himself too: "Berloe, Berloe", and then hurried inside. The next moment three loud blows sounded on the door.
164556: A man walking on a hill with a walking stick in his hand suddenly heard a shrieking, although there was nothing to be seen. One night that man was ridden by the moon (the mare), which left him in so much pain that he did not know how to lie down. When the man put his hand under his side to fall asleep, that hand became very warm and began to hurt.
164572: A poor man had bought a cow from a dealer in exchange for his goat and a sum of money. The dealer went with a friend to deliver the cow. But the poor man's wife did not want to give up the goat and stood guard with a knife. In the end the dealer gave in and left with only the money. As he walked home with his friend, the dealer was pestered by a cat that kept rubbing against his legs. The dealer believed the poor man's wife was a witch. The friend, who was not bothered by the cat, began praying the Gospel of Saint John, after which the animal ran off. When the dealer was home, his friend went on alone to his own house. Further on he saw a hundred thousand mewing cats sitting behind a wall. Not a single cat jumped over the wall.
164581: In the past there was little hygiene in the stables, so the animals often fell ill. It also sometimes happened that a cow ate a needle or a knife, which pierced the animal's stomach. Of animals that died of such things, people said they had been struck by the evil hand.
164605: In Eppegem it often happened that a witch bewitched the animals. When a witch was angry with someone, she brought the evil hand over that person's stable.
164622: A man brought a bowl of buttermilk and a loaf of bread to a woman who had a bad name. After that the man had problems with all his children. The fathers of Affligem advised the man to stay away from that woman and not to let her into his house either. Witchcraft existed in the past, but not anymore.
164634: Whenever people came to a certain place at night, they always saw the ghost of a woman standing there.
164645: The bells of Mazenzele were hidden in the Mazelegroot, also called 't Graalputje. When people wanted to bring the bells back up, it turned out not to be easy. The carter swore several times. The next moment he fell with his horse and cart into the pit where the bell lay.
164662: People who were ridden by the maar (nightmare) had an incurable sore somewhere. 'To be ridden by the maar' was also an expression often used when someone was flustered or confused.
164664: In Nieuwrode there lived a man who could make someone's bicycle stop by shouting "Whoa!"
164682: Because Trees had built a new house, she let an old woman live in her old house. One day the old woman died. Because she had promised during her life to go on pilgrimage, she had to come back to haunt after her death. Trees, who heard noise in the house every night, asked: "What is your burden?", to which a voice answered: "I still have to go on pilgrimage to Scherpenheuvel". Trees then said: "Well, I'll do that". On the way to Scherpenheuvel Trees had to carry the old woman the whole time.
164688: When a witch from Lombeek was sitting in church, a neighbour stuck an Easter nail under the grating lying on the floor of the church porch. The witch could not leave the church and looked around to see whether a window was open somewhere. In the end the Easter nail had to be removed from under the grating.
164692:
A boy who was out every night roaming about in an animal skin was coming back from the fair with his girlfriend one night. When his hour had come, the boy said to the girl: "I don't feel well, I have to relieve myself. If you see a beast, throw this handkerchief into its jaws." The girl quietly went on. When a little later she saw a beast with fiery eyes appear, she threw the handkerchief into its jaws and was left unharmed. A little later the boy came back. The girl noticed that he had the red threads of the handkerchief between his teeth. The girl screamed and ran home. She never wanted to see the boy again.
He was a werewolf who had made a pact with the devil.
164704: Some girls were ridden by the mare at night. They then felt a heavy weight on their bodies.
164716: A man who went ferreting at night was confronted by a werewolf. When the werewolf shook back and forth, fire could be seen everywhere. The skin of a werewolf was stuck in a tree stump. If you could make a werewolf bleed, you could unmask him.
164746: A midwife had to go to Sint-Martens-Lennik on a Tuesday. The woman lost her way because of a sorceress from Gaasbeek. Only when the woman reached the large chapel in Vlezenbeek could she find her bearings again.
164757: Many people did not dare to go to the churchyard because the ghosts of the returned dead wandered about there.
164777: A boy walked in a witch's footprints. He put his right foot in the print of her left foot and his left foot in the print of her right foot. At that the witch said: "Go on, you silly fool, move along!"
164785: A soldier on his way to the station of Neerwinden met a woman, who gave him a pat on the shoulder. Because the soldier had been bewitched by that woman, his finger was crushed between two parts of the train. When people saw that this woman had touched their child, they believed their child was bewitched and went to fetch the priest. The witch's daughter-in-law moved house several times because she always saw her mother-in-law appear in her house at night.
164790: Children who could already walk well could not walk for at least three months after being touched by a witch. After that the children were forbidden to go near that witch ever again.
164793: A farmer's wife who was plagued by the evil hand sent for a woman from Jette. That woman said to the farmer's wife: "Plates and other objects are missing here. But everything will be brought back." Some time later the missing objects, including the farmer's tie, were brought back to the farm. All those objects had to be destroyed.
164795: Witches could cause the animals in the stable to die or to be unable to become pregnant.
164843: People who were ill for a long time sometimes believed they had been ridden by the mare. On a farm on the Lotse Steenweg there was a pig that did not grow. People said that the animal had been ridden by the mare. After the priest had read a blessing over the pig, it grew fat.
164857: A woman always came to a farm to fetch milk. One day, however, the people had no milk, so they could not give the woman anything. Shortly afterwards the people on that farm could no longer make butter. They went to the pharmacist in Edingen. Because they still could not make butter after that, they went to the fathers and told them their problem. The fathers advised the people to be careful and gave them holy water to take home. The people had fallen victim to someone suspected of being a witch.
164864: You could make a witch stand still by walking crosswise in her footprints; you had to put your left foot in her right footprint and your right foot in her left footprint.
164883: When Octavie's grandfather had died, the girl heard footsteps in the room at night. Octavie went to look together with her mother, but there was nothing to be seen. The next night the noise was a good deal louder. A day later the mother found a money box with four hundred francs hidden under the bed in the dead man's room. After that the ghost was no longer heard.
164895: People who were ridden by the mare had a stoppage of the blood. This only happened when one slept on one's back.
164902: The Pollepelstraat was haunted. Some people pushing their wheelbarrow there suddenly found that one of its handles had broken off. At night a lot of noise could always be heard at that spot as well.
164917: The church of Tielt was haunted. At midnight a loud rumbling was always heard there. One night the parish priest tried to open the church door to see what was going on. The door, however, would not open. Then Father M. went to the churchyard to sprinkle the whole ground with holy water. Since that night the church has no longer been haunted.
164918: A girl went for a walk with her boyfriend. At a certain moment the boy said to her: "I have to relieve myself. Should you meet anything, strike with this handkerchief." After the boy had jumped over the ditch, the girl saw a big dog. She threw the handkerchief at the beast and then ran home. An hour later her boyfriend came in there too. He still had the threads of the handkerchief between his teeth.
164932: A girl who was running errands in the Leuvensestraat suddenly received a blow on her head. When the girl got up the next day, her hair had turned completely white on one side. The girl had been touched by a witch.
164938: A man who was ridden by the mare could no longer speak and felt as if he was being seized.
164945: In Eppegem lived a witch who owned a book of magic. When that witch was angry with someone, she read from that book, which brought misfortune to the victim.
164947: The zwarte madam (black lady) walked about near the Bethanië chapel in Zoutleeuw. After the three masses she had asked for were said for her, the zwarte madam (black lady) no longer appeared.
164970: A man who felt he would die soon insisted on pulling down a shed in August, in which peaches, cherries and redcurrants used to be stored. The man pulled down the shed in Nieuwrode and took the materials by tractor to Rillaar. There he built a shed meant for the chickens. In that shed he wrote the year: 1981. A month later the man died. The mother-in-law of that man's daughter certainly did him harm.
164976: A man coming back from the rehearsal of a music society met a woman who did not dare go on because she had seen an apparition. The man went to look and found there was nothing to be seen but a bush. Still, the woman did not dare go on.
165014: A house where there was a small child received a visit from a woman. When that woman stroked the child, the mother and father were very afraid. The next day the child was ill. The illness kept getting worse, until in the end the child could no longer move its legs.
165038: In Leerbeek lived a woman who was suspected of being a witch. One Sunday evening a girl had to fetch water from the spring in the snow. When she came in front of the witch's house, the girl always fell flat on the ground. After that the girl no longer dared to fetch water.
165041: In a house where many children had already died, a cat was seen sitting on the windowsill. People poured a bowl of hot water over the animal. The next day a woman walked around the village who was burnt all over.
165056: If you could make a werewolf bleed, he had to reveal who he was.
165081: A man who went to Hondzocht at six in the morning to sell his butter met a woman on the way, to whom he said: "Well, redhead, you're no good one!" When the man arrived at the market, it was found that every kilo of butter weighed a little less than a kilo.
165082: A boy was courting a girl from Willebringen. When he walked home at night, he always carried a small axe. When one night the boy saw a werewolf at the Drogenberg, he said: "If I see you again, you won't get up anymore." The following Sunday, however, the werewolf was there again, and the man gave the beast a hard blow with his axe. The werewolf bled and changed into a man from the village, who said: "If only you hadn't done that! My time was almost up and now I have to start all over again!"
165100: People who were ridden by the mare could no longer do anything right.
165114: In a street in Neerwinden a werewolf roamed that made passers-by carry it. One day a victim managed to wound the werewolf with a hook. That is how people discovered that the werewolf was a human.
165125: In the old days children were frightened with stories about people who had been ridden by the moon (the mare).
165139: Some people went to the fields with the horse cart. By the Keskessteeg they saw a group of people sitting at a beautifully laid table drinking wine. When one of those people had spoken a certain word, the whole scene vanished in one stroke.
165150: People who were ridden by the mare were really imagining things. They went to have a blessing read over them by the father. The fathers then sweated because they were struggling so hard to drive out the devil, or so people believed. In reality the father simply sweated because it was warm in the room where he sat.
165154: Three men who had been out on a Sunday in Opstal were coming home in the evening. On the way the men saw a dog. When one of the men wanted to kick the dog, another said: "Leave alone what leaves you alone." A bit further on, the men saw to their great fright that the dog had grown twice as big.
165157: Old women who came peddling laces, shoe polish and stockfish could not enter anywhere until someone had said: "Come on in." Those peddlers were probably witches.
165163: A girl from Linden was walking home with her boyfriend. On the way the boy said: "Go on ahead, I have to relieve myself." Further on the girl got a fright when a black dog jumped up at her. The dog bit into the black neckerchief the girl was wearing. The next day the girl's boyfriend visited her and she noticed that he had the black threads of the neckerchief between his teeth.
165179: The Blauwe Schuur (Blue Barn) in Bierbeek had to be finished before the rooster began to crow in the morning. The first cockcrow was usually heard at three o'clock in the morning. A farmer had sold his soul to the devil in exchange for a new barn. When the farmer saw in the night that the barn was almost finished, he went outside and clapped his hands. At that the rooster began to crow. No one has ever managed to finish that barn.
165180: As part of a bet, a witch challenged her husband to see who could get across the sea first. The witch would fly, and the man would sit on a donkey. On the way, however, they were not allowed to say anything. The witch smeared herself with a kind of ointment and said: "Over hedge and over hedges." The man said: "In one leap!" But when the man was halfway, he said: "God, what a leap for such an animal!" and he fell into the sea. The witch, however, did make it across the sea.
165188: A woman lay in bed for twenty-four years. She constantly had nervous twitches. The woman was not allowed to eat egg white. When the woman's mother had died, the woman made a novena. After that she got up from her bed. The woman is said to have been bewitched by her own mother.
165196: During the fair, a farmer and his wife decided to go and fetch a bundle of fodder together with their two daughters. When they walked past the Rottemse winning, they heard a bang as if the gate had been slammed shut. The farm was on fire and many onlookers stood there with a shovel, a dung fork or another tool. A small light could be seen by the house. No one knew what it was. The building had once been a smithy, but no work had been done there for years. The farmhands who lived in the house could not sleep because of the noise. In the smithy seven or eight smiths could be heard working, but when people went to look, there was nothing to be seen.
165203: Two friends who went to fetch coffee beans in Werchter met a witch, who said: "Put that wheelbarrow down, because it will tip over." One of the friends answered: "Oh no, I have a firm hold on this wheelbarrow." A little later both friends' wheelbarrows tipped over and the witch stood there laughing.
165217: In Oudenaken lived old women who were suspected of being witches. Children ran away from those women. Witches always tried to touch people. A witch from Breedhout threw apples on the ground so that the children would pick them up. The parents, however, knew the witches' tricks and warned their children about them.
165218: A boy who felt he got too little money from his father had managed to obtain a book of magic in the army. The boy's father put his money in a locked chest and said: "You good-for-nothing, you waste my money! Now you can't get at it!" The boy threw his cap on the chest, and the lock sprang open.
165228: A girl who was playing outside was given a box of sweets by a woman walking past. A relative advised the girl to ask her mother for other sweets. The girl did as she was advised and her mother threw the sweets she had received into the stove. When the woman walked past again the next day, she said: "I didn't give sweets to be thrown into the stove!" After that the girl was bewitched. The child was taken to a certain place where the witchcraft could be removed. Those people said to the girl's parents: "A woman will come to you to ask for something, but you must not mistreat her. Give her what she asks for." Shortly afterwards the woman came by to ask for a few bricks. The mother, however, could not hold her tongue and said: "Are you bewitching our child again?" and she gave the woman the bricks. After that nothing more happened to the little girl.
165238: One evening a girl was returning from Aalst with her godmother, where the two had gone to buy clothes for the child's First Communion. A witch had said to the godmother: "If you come back from Aalst in the evening and are afraid, come to me." On the way the godmother suddenly saw something lying on the cobbled road. It was as big as an elephant. The godmother walked past the strange shape with her eyes closed and then went to tell the witch what she had seen. The witch replied: "What a fuss you make! I'll come along." When the witch went with them, they saw a little nun walking back and forth the whole time. The strange shape had vanished. The witch had made that shape appear so that she could walk along with them.
165244: In Gelbergen near Hoeleden stood a building that was rented to a steward. The owner, however, had another house in which no one would stay because it was haunted. When the house was let to a family, there was no sign of the haunting. One Sunday afternoon the owner's farmhand came to visit. The tenant said to him: "What could be true about it? We haven't noticed anything of that haunting". The next moment the soup bowl moved by itself out of the cupboard to the farmhand's feet. Shortly afterwards the occupants found that their animals were always being untied. In the end the woman went to ask the parish priest for advice. The people stayed there until their contract ended, but their hair turned grey with fear.
165257: It was said of children who got up to a lot of mischief that they had been ridden 'by the moon' (the mare).
165267:
A man was on the road with a horse and cart. At an inn in Aarschot the horse suddenly stood still. Only after the carter had drunk a few glasses of beer in the inn could the horse go on again. Because of this, people believed the innkeeper's wife was a witch.
In reality the horse stopped because it was used to getting a sugar lump at that inn.
165274: A man from Eliksem was able to buy his house very cheaply because a rattling could always be heard there, so people thought it was haunted. The man, however, dared to sleep in his house for only one night. After that he moved in with his parents-in-law.
165291: People who were ridden by the moon (the mare) had a stifling feeling. They wanted to call out, but no sound came. In reality the 'moon' was probably a bad dream.
165307: If a piece of a blessed candle had been put under the threshold, no witches could enter. A woman from Gaasbeek had received this advice from a priest. When the woman saw someone approaching in the distance whom she suspected of having bewitched her daughter, she noticed that the witch turned back.
165325: People who were ridden 'by the moon' (the mare) lay sweating in their beds at night.
165329: A farm was often visited by a woman with a bad name. On that farm they could no longer make butter. After they had been to the fathers, the churning worked again.
165339: A woman who had died in childbed had said before her death: "You will do nothing for me". One night the dead woman appeared to her sister, who slept in the bed in which she had died. After the sister had said: "If you are sent by God, speak. If you are sent by the devil, be gone", the dead woman said that two people had to make a pilgrimage and offer four candles. Then her husband and her sister went on the pilgrimage. The man had to carry the weight of his dead wife the whole way.
165366: Anyone walking through a marsh could often hear a deep sigh. That sound was made by air bubbles rising from the ground. Such air bubbles also caused lights, which people took for will-o'-the-wisps. After all, when someone had been murdered, the body often ended up in the marsh. Sometimes poachers also failed to return from their poaching because they had sunk into the marsh. People then believed that the soul of the dead person found no rest and came back to haunt in the form of a will-o'-the-wisp.
165373: A man who went catching water beetles had to go with his basket through the woods as far as Luik. A witch made a big heavy tree fall onto the road in front of the man's feet.
165389: In Lubbeek a farm was bewitched by a witch from Binkom. Because all the animals on the farm died, the people went to the brown friars in Leuven. The clergymen explained that they could do nothing and that everything would be lost. For the stable, the walls and the animals were full of little copper pins.
165393: In Gelrode lived a witch. In the evenings that witch always played cards with the men of the village. The daughter of one of those men always started crying at exactly midnight. In the end the girl was taken to the white fathers of the Boeleberg (Keizersberg) in Leuven. However, one was not allowed to say that one suspected the person had been struck by the evil hand, or else the fathers would not want to read prayers over the person. After prayers had been read over the girl, she no longer cried at night.
165402: A farmer and his wife whose animals were dying suspected a woman from the neighbourhood. When that woman came to visit, a blessed candle had been put under her chair. They said to the woman: "Go on home, for your husband will be home soon," but the woman could no longer get up. People whose animals were dying had the white canons come to pray.
165403: A man going to visit his girlfriend on the Heikant saw, during a thunderstorm, a large dark apparition rushing towards him. The man jumped onto a verge and let the apparition pass. When he got home, the man was driven into a corner. He only got out of that corner after his mother had called him.
165443: At 't Hoeksken (1) a twelve-year-old boy had died after falling from a tree. Every time the dead boy's brother went to fetch water, he saw the boy's spirit standing against a tree. When the boy had told the priest everything, the clergyman said: "Next time you go to fetch water, take a white cloth and ask what the spirit wants. The spirit will then give you its hand". In this way the boy learned that his dead little brother had promised a Mass in honour of Our Lady when he fell from the tree. The spirit burned its hand into the cloth.
165453: A farmer's wife had sold her soul to the devil. In return the devil had to build a barn before the first cockcrow. But when the rooster crowed, the barn was not yet finished: there was still a hole in the wall. That hole could never be closed afterwards.
165469: If one had wounded a cat, it could happen that the next day one met a woman who had a similar wound.
165487: In the past spiders were often associated with witchcraft. For instance, people believed that witches sent spiders into houses to eavesdrop on conversations.
165498: Some people who had visited their family in the evening met their deceased uncle E. on the way back, walking ahead of them. At a little bridge the people suddenly could go no further. Fearing they were bewitched, they began to pray until they got past the bridge. The ghost of uncle E. crept through the hedge by the wayside crucifix and then disappeared.
165499: Two men who had gone to fetch potatoes found in a sunken lane that their horse would not go forward. A little old man came walking up and said: "Well, you're having trouble, aren't you? I'll take hold of that horse and then it will go on." The little man did so, and the horse went on. Later a tree was cut down at that spot, and an animal skin was stuck inside it. That was the little man's skin.
165515: A man returning from a visit to his girlfriend was followed by a black cat in the Krommestraat in Meise. When the man said: "What God protects is well protected", the cat had vanished.
165517: A nun from Heverlee was startled by noise in the night. A little later the voice of a deceased fellow nun said: "If you do not believe that anything exists, then I will show you how fiercely I must burn and how much I suffer!" The handprint of the deceased nun was burnt into the door.
165535: A joiner who lived in Manhove (a hamlet of Sint-Pieters-Kapelle) worked in Bever. One day the joiner had to make a four-franc coffin for a poor person who was being buried in Bever. In the evening the man walked along a little path with the white coffin on his shoulder. People believed that a white horse came haunting at that spot and cried: "Look, the white horse is there!"
165541: In the past people often hollowed out beets to put a candle in them. A woman who often went to Brussels on Friday mornings sometimes saw lights. Those were the souls of children who had not been baptised. A man who was baptising such lights suddenly saw countless lights coming towards him.
165549: A witch could not leave the church because an Easter nail had been placed under the door of the women's exit. The witch had to go out by way of the sacristy.
165556: Witches usually kept owls and black cats.
165575: A boy went with his three cousins to the draw for military service. When the four passed the house of a witch, the boy said: "We'll be drawn, because the witch is standing at her door and she's already making signs of the cross." Indeed, all four boys had to join the army.
165595: A child who was always being ridden by the mare was taken to the fathers of Affligem and to the Capuchins of Edingen.
165598: In a house where a toad was seen walking about, people grabbed the animal with tongs and threw it outside [probably meaning that the toad was thrown into the fire]. The next day the sorceress was burnt.
165601: An old farmer was going from the Brusselse Steenweg to Strombeek. On the way the farmer was accompanied by a horse that followed him everywhere. The farmer was terrified of the animal and believed that something unnatural was going on.
165608: A man who had talked with a witch was advised by a neighbour to pray an Our Father, because otherwise he would be bewitched. The neighbour had already suffered much misfortune because of that witch. When he went to plant potatoes, the witch laid her hand on the basket of potatoes and predicted that the plants would not come up. And so it happened. When the witch had held her hand over a basket of cherries in that house, the fruit went rotten.
165616: A man who had already had much misfortune wanted the priest to read prayers over his house, because his wife was pregnant and he did not want to risk anything going wrong. Because the priest feared he would have too much work if he started with such things, he refused to come and read prayers over the man's house. The man then became so angry that he threatened not to have his child baptised and never to go to church again. So the priest came to read prayers over the house after all. After that the man had no more misfortune. He had been a victim of the evil hand.
165631: A witch would sit in a clover field in the evening. She cut away a piece of clover and it flew up into the air. After that nothing more could be seen, and the witch had vanished too. One day a man said to the witch: "Keep your hands off my clover." The witch acted as if it had nothing to do with her. The next day all the man's sheaves of corn had been knocked over.
165640: A witch could turn herself into a toad or a cat. If one managed to wound such an animal, one could recognise the witch in her human form by her wound.
165676: A man from Breedhout had a little daughter who would not grow. He believed his child had been struck by the evil hand.
165686: A farmer who had too little room to store his harvest met a gentleman who was willing to build him a large barn. In return the farmer would have to give up his soul ten years later. The farmer agreed, for he thought ten years was a very long time. On Wednesday evening the devils started on the barn, which had to be finished before the first cockcrow the next morning. When he got home, the farmer told his wife what he had done. In the night from Wednesday to Thursday the farmer's wife got up at two o'clock, went outside and began to clap her hands. When the rooster then began to crow, there was still a small hole in the barn. The devils dropped everything and the farmer's wife ran away. Because the barn was not completely finished, the farmer could keep his soul. That Blauwe Schuur (Blue Barn) still stands in Tienen today.
165688: At the station a girl met a woman, who said: "My, what lovely curls you have!", to which the girl replied: "Yes, my mother makes them". When she got home, the girl's head itched terribly. The girl's hair was full of lice.
165690: People believed a house in Beert was haunted. In that house the doors always flew open and the children saw something spinning in front of their bed. It was believed that these apparitions had something to do with evil, so someone was sent for to exorcise the evil. The sorcerer or witch always came in with a little bundle of straw, which she then made spin. The man set the straw alight with a match, so that the evil was driven out of the house.
165694: A priest went to a farm where the pigs were ill. At the farmer's wife's request, the priest read prayers over the pigsty. When the clergyman left afterwards, he was laughed at by the witches under a tree.
165721: In Attenhoven the people went on pilgrimage to Scherpenheuvel every year. Once, when the weather was very bad, the procession was postponed. The next day the statue of Mary was found in the field with her robe covered in mud. Since that event the procession has been held every year, however bad the weather.
165727: A woman who was said to be a witch went into a farmer's stable one morning, where she slapped a bull calf on the rump and said it was a fine animal. The next night the calf lay dead in the stable. That woman could work magic. The farmer often lent his horse to other people who wanted to work their land. One day a farmer from the neighbourhood had come to fetch the horse. When the woman saw the horse in the field, she went to the farmer and said: "I didn't know that horse worked for you too. I thought it only worked for my husband." A little later the horse would not take another step. However much the farmer swore, the animal would not move. In the end the man had to go and fetch another horse.
165741: At a farm where many animals and even children had died, an old woman came every day to ask what time it was. A friar from Gent came and said: "The guilty one will come by. You must make a big fire and keep luring her closer to it." The people did so and saw the sorceress move her chair ever closer to the fire. In the end the sorceress had to confess and promise to undo the harm. She pulled lots of pins out of the children's bodies and said: "This one child will recover, but with that other one the witchcraft has gone too far." That other child did indeed die.
165749: A man named Louis H. had been killed in an accident by a sand pit along the road to Binkom. When people came back from the fair around midnight, they saw the returned dead man sitting by the sand pit.
165781: A maid who had been dismissed went to the church to have a mass said for one franc for the faithful souls and for the people who had recently died. As she left the church, the girl met a gentleman, who said: "Are you looking for other work? If you ring the bell at that house in that street, you will find work." The gentleman was the most recently deceased person in the town.
165796: A pregnant woman had eaten a sweet she had been given by a woman a few years older than her. When the pregnant woman lay in her bed, she saw a whole pack of rats coming up the stairs. The woman asked her mother to sleep with her because she no longer dared to sleep alone. The morning after the woman had given birth, the woman who had given her the sweet was standing beside her bed. Three days after the child was baptised, it began to cry incessantly. The child also had a very dark colour. In the pouring rain the mother went with her child to the priest to have prayers read over it. On the way back the mother saw the woman who had given her the sweet standing by the little chapel. At that moment the mother could go no further. Nine days later the mother had to go to the priest again. After that she had no more problems with herself or the child.
165801: Six or seven women could not leave the church of Bever because the priest had left his missal open.
165806: A miller often sat in his mill at night, especially when there was a lot of wind. A black cat often came into the mill and rubbed against the miller's legs. The miller grew tired of this and one day gave the animal a hard kick so that he could sleep in peace. When the man went to breakfast in the morning, he saw that his wife had black and blue marks on her face and was therefore wearing a thick shawl around her head. That is how the miller found out that it was his wife who came to spy on him at night. After that the cat certainly left him alone!
165807: A man saw a horse walking along a tree-lined lane. Convinced it was an animal that had broken loose, the man went after the horse. The horse, however, then grew larger and larger.
165826: A man had frightened some friends with stories. When they went home together later that evening, they heard footsteps behind them. The men quickly fled into the 'jeneverkotje' (gin shed) (1) and a moment later heard a blow on the door. They saw the imprint of a horseshoe in the door. If they had not fled inside, they would all have been dead.
165835: If thirteen people sat at table together, someone from that company would die within the year.
