The people then said: "Yes, but the catechism does say you must beware of witches and witchcraft". The priest answered: "Well, if that's how it is, I'll read prayers over you". After that the ants stayed away.
169252: In Sint-Kwintens-Lennik lived a woman whose husband was a shoemaker. At night this woman went to a meadow to milk a farmer's horses. She used the milk to strengthen her own health and that of her children. After about a hundred days the animal gave no more milk, so the woman went to milk two other horses. These, however, were dangerous animals. One night the woman was caught by the farmer. And so she got the name of a witch.
169265: On a hill people could not move on as long as a glow could be seen. That was witchcraft.
169270: A farmer's wife had a litter of pigs that would not grow.
169277: A mother whose little son had been struck by the kwade hand (the evil hand, witchcraft) went to the Picpus Fathers. When the friars refused to come and read prayers over the boy, the mother grew angry. Then one of the friars said: "Little lady, I will come. I will be with you in an hour." That friar then read prayers over the child. He made the sign of the cross, used holy water and read prayers from a book. Shortly afterwards the child recovered. When the boy grew up, he never went to the doctor. "The friars of Averbode are my doctors," he always said.
169280: A farmer who did not manage to build a new barn in time met an elegant gentleman who wanted to provide a new barn in exchange for the farmer's soul. The barn had to be finished the next morning before the rooster crowed at five o'clock. When the rooster crowed three times that night, thousands of devils ran away. There was still a hole in the barn that could never be closed afterwards. Postcards of the devil's barn on the Neerveld were even sold.
169291: A man who had to fetch the midwife for his wife met a dog at an oak in Kiezegem, and it crept between his legs.
169293: A woman who suffered from epilepsy died before she was fifty. She died on a Sunday in the presence of her son. At that moment a neighbour was standing in the hallway. That neighbour was a witch. The sick woman had been given a little prayer to Saint Anthony to protect herself against the witch.
169294: One winter morning a woman found a pretty parcel containing three slices of white bread and an apple. She took the parcel home, where her father immediately threw it into the cesspit. A while later he took it out again and buried it deep in the ground. The people went to tell the priest of Mollem what had happened. The clergyman said the parcel came from a woman who had already caused various ailments in the children. He named the woman and also rebuked her personally. After that the people experienced nothing strange anymore.
169300: On a farm there was a wheat field. A witch who wanted the wheat for herself made the field turn completely black. The witch succeeded in claiming that piece of land.
169336: In an old cottage in Gussenhoven lived a little woman who could work magic. She could stop a horse and cart. Whenever a baby was born somewhere, the witch always came to visit. A while later the child would be dead, although the witch had not touched it.
169354: A man believed he was being plagued by a witch. When one of his children fell ill after a visit from a certain woman, the man believed she had bewitched his children. The man also said there were ants in his house. The same ants were at the witch's house. The man did not dare tell the witch she could no longer visit, but from then on he kept his doors shut.
169366: A man was coming back at night from the fair in Eliksem. On the way the man was followed by a foal. When the church bells struck twelve, a herd of piglets appeared. The man was terrified and went to sit in the church. In that church witches appeared, who began to ring the church bells.
169375: When people had misfortune in their stable, they went to the friars of Affligem because they believed they were bewitched. A woman who had misfortune went to the friars together with her neighbour. The clergymen asked her whether there was a woman who came by every day. When she said yes, the friars replied: "You must not let that woman in anymore. Tomorrow she will come again and knock. If you tell her she may come in, you are lost." The woman followed the friars' advice and had no more misfortune.
169380: In the churchyard of Peizegem the gravestone of a young disabled girl had risen up. Countless people came from far and wide to look at the grave. The gravestone had probably risen because of a mole burrowing.
169391: In the past, when people had misfortune in the stable, they blamed a witch. At the home of a woman suspected of witchcraft, a large animal had fallen into the cesspit and drowned. The butcher had dressed the animal, but nobody dared buy the meat because people believed it was bewitched.
169406: On a farm that had been struck by the kwade hand (the evil hand, witchcraft), a farmer's wife went to Lourdes every year for her sick daughter. She believed the witch had bewitched her daughter too.
169418: Het Blok was a monastery that had been sold as confiscated church property during the French Revolution. The man who had bought both 't Blok and Terleenen for a pittance was carried off to hell at his death by the devil in a coach with two black horses.
169420: One morning a farmer's wife found that her dairy cows had been untied. Although she had not taken any cow to a bull, one cow was nevertheless in calf. The woman believed the cows were bewitched and went to have prayers read over her at the monastery of Affligem.
169424: If you did not place your shoes upside down next to your bed, you could easily be ridden by the mare at night.
169433: An old woman who lived on a hill had to contend with the harassment of a witch. Every time a cow was about to calve, the witch came running to the stable. The calf always died immediately after birth.
169463: In a house in Gelrode, a returned dead man appeared every night and wrote something on the wall with his finger that nobody could read. After a while the people found the courage to ask: "What do you come here for and what does that mean?" The ghost answered: "You have deceived me. A pilgrimage was promised, and it still hasn't been made!"
169518: In Sint-Ulriks-Kapelle lived a woman who did not shrink from lies, deceit and theft. Some people believed that she could work magic.
169542: A toad always came into a house through the water drain. People threw the toad outside, but the next morning the animal was there again. One day hot water was poured over the toad. The next day a woman with a burnt leg walked around the village.
169548:
Kludde wore a sheepskin and roamed at night with a bell or a rattling chain. Kludde leapt on cowards, who had to carry him until they were drenched in sweat. If you threw a handkerchief at Kludde, the tormenting spirit was powerless until he had completely frayed the handkerchief.
At the tower in Lieferinge (a municipality in East Flanders) worked a farmhand who had to play Kludde. A girl who had to go out at dusk to do some sewing somewhere claimed she was not afraid of meeting Kludde on the way. But the girl had barely set off when she saw Kludde coming and threw her handkerchief at the apparition. When the girl sat at breakfast the next morning, she was asked: How did it go last night?, and the girl explained what had happened to her. The farmhand sitting at the table grinned, baring his teeth, between which the threads of the handkerchief could still be seen. The girl saw it and cried: You swine! It's you! The lad replied: Yes, I had to go about as Kludde for one more night. After that the farmhand was never seen again.
169568: In Kortenberg lived a woman whose children had died through the kwade hand (the evil hand, witchcraft).
169589: A dead man who had agreed with someone that he would return to tell how things were in the hereafter made himself known by knocking and said: "It is very good over there, but not much is forgiven."
169604: Parents who could not control their children sometimes said: "You really are a naughty one! You've been ridden by the mare!"
169609: Army officers lived in the small castle opposite the church of Pepingen. After their death those officers came back to haunt in a white robe. Many years later the silver heart of one of those officers was found in the wall of the church. Because nobody dared to live in the haunted castle, the farmers used the space to store their grain. That is how the farmers one day discovered money in one of the walls of the castle. That money was used to build a white tomb in the church.
169620: A house in Bos was haunted. At night the house always seemed to be on fire, but what people saw was a ghost fire.
169624: On a farm butter had been made that was already spoiled after two days. The people had fallen victim to a witch. They went to a fortune teller, who said: "Behind your house you will find a large bone. You must burn it, and then you will burn the witch too." The people found the bone but did not dare burn it. The witch lived another ten years, but she no longer dared go outside because she knew she had been unmasked.
169629: Witches could enter a church, but they could not leave the building again. When three witches were sitting in the church, the sexton stuck a blessed candle under the threshold. After mass those witches could not leave the church until the priest let them out.
169637: The B. family had promised to have a mass said for a dead person. That promise, however, had not yet been fulfilled. At night the bed of those people began to dance. As soon as the people got up, the bed stood still again. After the promised mass had been said, nothing strange happened any more.
169648: Children who did not grow up normally had been 'ridden by the mare', so people said.
169680: In the past, when children saw a light in the evening, they did not dare point at it because it might be a stalkaars (will-o'-the-wisp). That was the soul of an unbaptised child. If you did point at such a light, it came and sat on your finger.
169684: If you slept on your back, you could not be ridden by the mare at night.
169687: A werewolf was often seen in Bekkevoort. Some people saw the werewolf, but others did not. One day a man set his dog on the werewolf. Because the dog refused, the man shot at the werewolf with his gun. That is how people found out that it was a man from Tielt who was playing the werewolf there.
169700: A pig dealer had remarried after his wife's death. One day, when the man came to a bend with his second wife, the horse suddenly refused to pull the cart any further. As soon as the strange apparition had disappeared, the horse went on again. When he got home, the man saw a bundle of brushwood moving back and forth. When the man asked what the apparition wanted, a voice answered: "Three more pilgrimages to Averbode". After the man had fulfilled that wish, he saw nothing strange again.
169706: In a field in Rumsdorp a man was working with his cows while his wife was baking bread. On top of the oven the woman had found the animal skin with which her husband played the werewolf. The woman threw the skin into the oven. The skin had barely caught fire when the man was already standing by the oven to save his skin.
169715: Witches could turn themselves into a cat.
169732: If one heard the cry of a peacock, someone in the neighbourhood would soon die.
169736: A maid who worked on a farm was very afraid of toads. Wherever the girl went, she always saw a toad. The farmhand laughed about it and advised the maid to knock off one of the toad's legs the next time. The maid did as she had been advised. The next day the farmer's wife had a broken leg.
169737: When a stalkaars (will-o'-the-wisp) died, you could see lots of little stars.
169742:
If you broke a mirror, you got seven years of bad luck.
Whoever sat against a table leg when drawing up to the table would have to wait another seven years before marrying.
169753: The Tillekesjacht (a spectral hunt) were cats that sat meowing in the Klein Baantje.
169766: A man was cycling through the warande (wooded park) in Humbeek by full moon. Suddenly the man saw a car behind him that made no sound. Because the car never overtook him, the man jumped off his bicycle. Between the trees the man saw the moon hanging. The man quickly jumped back on his bicycle and rode on. The will-o'-the-wisp stayed hanging on the chimney of a man who hanged himself three months later.
169767: If you went and sat at a crossroads at midnight with a black hen, the devil appeared and you could sell your soul to him.
169771: When a woman had been struck by the kwade hand (the evil hand, witchcraft), someone forced the guilty witch to come to her victim at midnight. The sick woman's husband stood ready with a manure fork.
169785: People whose neighbour had recently died always heard a knocking on the wall at night. The brown friars of Leuven gave them this advice: "If it happens again, don't be afraid, and ask what they want". So the next night the people learned that the farmer was suffering terrible pains in purgatory. Seven of them had to go on pilgrimage to Scherpenheuvel. After that the farmer found rest.
169788: One day in a house a black cat was seen walking through the fire. The next day a woman from the neighbourhood walked around with her arm in a bandage. That woman had turned herself into a cat. In the old days it could sometimes happen that the priest had not baptised someone properly. When such a person bought a book of magic, he or she could practise witchcraft.
169791: A soldier was lodging with people in Ruisbroek who had a child that was always sick and pining. The doctors could not help the child. The soldier asked the people: "Isn't there one of the neighbours who acts a bit strange?" When the people said yes, the soldier said: "That woman deserves the stake. She is jealous because she has no children of her own, and so she torments your child. She has a wax figure into which she sticks pins, to torment the child slowly." The soldier went with the parents to the guilty woman and said: "You are the cause of this child's illness and you must tell here what you are doing to that child." When the woman denied her guilt, the soldier threatened to call the police and have her taken to prison. In the end the woman did bring out the wax figure. After the figure was destroyed, the child recovered.
169794: It was wrongly said of a woman from Roosbeek that she made animals die. When the woman had gone to borrow a wheelbarrow somewhere, people said she had bewitched the stables. The priest had given those people this advice: "If the witch comes again, you must never say 'yes'." When the witch wanted to borrow the wheelbarrow again, the farmer's wife said: "You may help it," but the witch left the wheelbarrow where it was.
169796: When Baardegem was plagued by rats and mice, an old woman was suspected of having sent the vermin. If people spoke ill of a certain person and that person passed by at that very moment, you could be sure that person really was responsible for the harm. This had once happened with that old woman. After the priest had come to read prayers over the bewitched places, things improved.
169807: In a house where everyone had gone to bed, a knock was heard on the door. The next moment all the doors flew open. The man went outside to look, but he saw nothing. When he was back in bed, the doors flew open again. The same thing happened three times.
169824: A man who worked as a stable hand on a farm in Strombeek-Bever went to visit his girlfriend in the Robberechtsstraat in Wemmel. When the man came home along the Jagersweg in the evening, he heard a rustling behind him. The man believed he was being followed by klerre (a demonic spectre) with his chain and quickly fled into a farm. A little later a loud bang was heard on the farm gate.
169825: A man coming back from Bevekom heard lovely music on the way. He saw many people and joined in their dancing. When the dance was over, the man was sitting with his backside on a dung heap.
169841: At a house in the Pereboomstraat a man's voice was heard every evening. It was the voice of a ghost that came to haunt. After the people had prayed for the ghost on the priest's advice, they no longer heard the voice.
169845: People who were ridden by the mare at night began to sweat and could not escape. It was believed that the mare was a witch.
169853: Sometimes people had to carry the werewolf. When they came to a chapel, the werewolf jumped off their back. The people then ran to the first house they came to.
169883: A woman went to a séance where she had to put photographs in a little basket. The clairvoyant took the photos out and told all sorts of things about the people shown in them. The man began to shout loudly when he found that the woman was no longer bewitched.
169884: A boy came home with beautiful ripe pears that he had been given by an old woman. The boy's mother threw the pears into the stove because she was afraid her son would be bewitched by them. A little later two toads were walking across the floor.
169893: Kleudde (a werewolf-like spirit) had hidden his skin in a hollow willow. On the advice of the priest, the people threw the skin into the oven. When the skin caught fire, kleudde immediately stood by the oven crying. After the skin had burnt up, however, the man was glad because he had been released.
169895: A mother standing in a shop with her child was told by a woman: "But do you give your child enough to eat?", to which the mother replied: "Of course! Can't you see how well it looks?" The next day the child could no longer eat. The mother had prayers read over her child by a woman from the village. She was also given a red ribbon to tie around the child's arm. The mother had to go to the chapel at the Hekske (1) for nine consecutive days and pray nine Hail Marys and nine Our Fathers there. After nine days the child was cured. The woman from the shop never again asked the mother how her child was doing.
169904: In Everberg lived a woman who could work magic. The witch made a great many people incurably ill.
169916: One evening a man from Goetsenhoven was walking back from Wulmersum in the dark. When the man had walked a little way, he saw five or six women sitting in a beautifully lit place, drinking from a small barrel and making merry. The man was invited to have a glass with them. When the man said: "God bless you", the whole scene vanished and he was sitting in a puddle of water. Only the cups were left standing. They belonged to one of the fattest farmer's wives in the village.
169923: A man from Nieuwenrode had to go and fetch hay in the Bemmeren in Mechelen at around half past three in the morning. Because his helper stayed away unusually long, he decided to go and have a look. On the way he met his helper and asked why he had stayed away so long. The helper answered: "I had come earlier, but I saw a horse walking there. Because I was afraid, I went back home." Yet the grandfather had not seen any horse. It must have been witchcraft.
169937: On a farm in Sterrebeek a woman was visited by her neighbour, who said: "You have such a big garden. Why don't you buy an animal in Leuven to eat all that grass?" The woman followed the advice. But when the animal was in the garden, a witch came to visit and stroked it. The next day the animal was so fat that it had to be sold and was good for nothing anymore.
169955: A woman from Vlezenbeek always tried to get near small children. She would go to the cradle and make a little cross on the child. One day she said to a child's mother: "If you ever have another child, take it to the cesspit. Then you won't have any more trouble with it."
169957: Witches sometimes appeared in the shape of a cat or a dog. One was not allowed to kick those animals, or else one would get into trouble.
170000: Near the Neigembos in Gooik there was a hamlet called 'de Woestijn' (the Desert). A chapel was once built there in honour of the Holy Cross. A shepherd's dog is said to have found a copper cross there. The people took the cross to the priest, who hung it in the church. The next day, however, the cross had disappeared. It was found again at the spot where the dog had dug it up. A chapel was then built on that spot. The chapel was visited by many sick people. The pope said that pilgrims on their way to Compostela had to venerate the Holy Cross at the Woestijn to earn an indulgence. An inn was then set up there, called 'De Drie Egypten' or ''t Zjipt'.
170024: The lord of the castle of Nieuwrode always went hunting on Sunday mornings. The priest was not allowed to begin mass until the lord had returned from his hunt. One Sunday the priest began mass anyway at one minute to twelve, because he was not allowed to begin a mass after noon. When the lord found that mass had begun without him, he shot the priest dead. After the priest's death the missal could no longer be closed; a drop of blood had spattered on it during the murder. Every time the missal was closed, it lay open again the next day. That is why the book had to be read over. Every night at twelve o'clock the lord came back to haunt in a burning coach, with which he drove into the press house. The priest came to say mass in the castle at midnight.
170033: On a farm a skin had been found with which the farmhand played Kledde (a werewolf-like spirit). The farmhand was sent away so that there was a chance to burn the skin. A moment later the farmhand was already standing by the fire begging to get his skin back. After the skin had burnt up, the farmhand was released.
170038: A man driving home with his cart saw a little light floating above the water in the distance. When the man said: "If that came over here, I would like to baptise it", the will-o'-the-wisp immediately came closer. The man scooped water until the next morning, because more and more will-o'-the-wisps kept flying up. For the man should have said "I baptise you alone" instead of "I baptise you".
170046: On a farm lived a farmer who walked around all day in a tall black hat. One day the butcher had to slaughter a pig near the Panhuysbeek. On his way back the butcher had to pass that haunted farm. There the butcher was attacked by a black cat, which scratched his face. The next day the butcher went to the farmer and said: "If you do that again, I'll make you pay for it!" The farmer replied: "Stay away from there. You shouldn't be so curious about other people's business!"
170050: In winter there was always a werewolf in the Weiebroek, a remote meadow with a high hedge around it. That werewolf sometimes made passers-by carry him, but he did them no harm.
170054: In a meadow the animals were ridden by a witch who came from across the sea in an eggshell. Eggshells always had to be smashed.
170099: A woman went to a neighbour to fetch buttermilk to make porridge. When she gave the porridge to her husband in the evening, he would not eat it and claimed it tasted of manure. The neighbour should not have lent the woman anything, because she was doing a novena to Saint Benedict, as her children had been bewitched. When the witch came to her for beet plants, she made the witch pay to be on the safe side, but the witch refused.
170107: A man who saw a little black cat walking in front of his feet the whole way believed that the kitten was a witch.
170110: Many kinds of misfortune among farmers could be attributed to the kwade hand (the evil hand, witchcraft) or to the devil. The pigs sometimes caught a disease that turned them red and blue.
170113: For three days a hen without a beak had been walking around a farmyard. One day an old woman came by and said: "Just wait, tomorrow she will have her beak back." The next day the hen did indeed have her beak back. The animal had been bewitched.
170123: On a large farm in Kumtich lived a man who was bewitched and therefore did strange things. Sometimes he walked in manure up to his neck and sometimes he stood stock-still because he could not move forward. For nine years the man could not sleep in his bed. Prayers were read over him, but that did not help. In the end the man went to live in Houtem.
170131: In the past people often fetched the Capuchins of Edingen to drive evil spirits out of a house or stable. After all, witches could transfer an illness from one person to another.
170144: A woman who had a stomach ache went to complain to her neighbour, who said: "That's nothing. You should drink some holy water." After the woman had drunk holy water, she had to be rushed to the doctor. People believed the neighbour had bewitched the holy water.
170149: A boy from Orsmaal had mocked a woman he met along the way. The woman had said: "Just you wait, little man!" The boy walked in his clogs all the way to Leuven, from where he had to find his way home without a penny in his pocket.
170164:
A carter who worked at the brewery in Betekom went to deliver beer with a cart and two strong horses. One day, when the carter was coming back with an empty cart, the animals suddenly stood still at the Eversveld. Some people came to help, but no one managed to get the cart moving again.
A little boy saw an old woman standing behind a hedge. He told his mother and pointed towards the old woman, who immediately vanished. The next moment the cart shot forward with a jolt. People said that old woman was a witch.
170180: A woman had seen the fire in the Brussels department store 'Innovation' in a dream a few days beforehand.
170185: A woman had stuck a pin in the hair of a baby lying in a cradle. The next day the baby's hair fell out. The child's father then went to the woman with a manure fork and said: "If you don't come, I'll stab you to death." The woman came to the child and wanted to be alone for a moment to undo the harm.
170197: A man going to the church of Oudegem in the morning ended up in the fields. When it grew light in the morning, the man found himself by the little chapel. He had been ridden by the mare.
170200: A boy had found a book of magic and had started reading it. The boy rubbed ears of wheat between his hands, after which thirty or forty mice suddenly ran across the ground. After the priest had baptised the boy again, he had lost his magic power.
170205: Witches still exist. A man and a woman had a child who was not healthy. The child knew it would die young and sometimes said to its mother: "Mummy, what will you do now? Then you won't have any children anymore." The child had 'the old man'. People believed it might have been bewitched.
170234: Witches could make animals ill by grinding the dried skin of a toad into powder and mixing that powder into the animals' food.
170238: A boy had been bewitched by his own mother, which gave him unbearable pain in his leg. The mother was supposed to go to the little friar of Hasselt for her son, but she did not.
170277: People were often very frightened when they were followed by black cats, because they believed those animals were the devil.
170308: A fisherman's wife was bewitched. In the kitchen she leapt up to the ceiling and crawled from one beam to another.
170312: You could be ridden by the mare especially when lying on your back.
170316: When there was a lot of wind, the wreaths on the gravestones could be heard rattling. On cold, dark winter evenings people would then say: "Oh dear, oh dear, there is life in the churchyard. That is a sinner coming out of his grave!"
170342: Some girls were playing when one of them suddenly said: "Shall I make some mice?" When the girl had made a hole in the ground with her finger, mice ran everywhere. The children were very impressed and asked the girl to make mice at school too. When the mother superior had seen what the girl could do, she sent for the priest. The priest took the child to the dean of Aarschot, for the girl had not been baptised properly. After the dean had baptised the child again, it could no longer make mice.
170345: A girl was approached by a witch who carried a little bird on her hand and said: "Look what a pretty little creature." The girl was on her guard and replied: "I need nothing from you." Then the witch said: "Then I'll let it go," and put the animal on the ground. The little bird followed the girl all the way to the church.
170366: Some soldiers had to transport Napoleon's war chest. At a spot where a farmer was manuring his field, however, the chest fell off the wagon without the soldiers noticing. The farmer hid the war chest under manure. The soldiers came looking for the war chest, but they did not find it and were therefore shot on the orders of their commander. After their death the soldiers returned to the farmer's stable, where they made a hellish noise. The boyfriend of the farmer's daughter went to the priest for advice. Later the clergy banished the sorcery for ninety-nine years.
170369: Around 1300 the castle of the Warande of Rummen was inhabited by the last of the counts of Loon. The castle was seized by the prince-bishop of Liège. Later a coach with four horses drove past the ruins of the castle at night.
170371: In Hamme a dead woman had come back to life. The haunting woman sat squatting.
170384: Witches could turn themselves into a toad. A man who grabbed at a toad saw the animal fly away in the shape of a hen. The man believed the animal was bewitched. Most people avoided black cats.
170396: A man on his way to Wulmersum was hindered the whole time by a hare running between his feet. The man had tried several times to catch the hare, but had not succeeded. When the man finally did have the hare in his hands, the animal said: "So you've caught me after all?" The next moment the hare had vanished.
170413: A woman cutting cabbages in her garden always saw a cat sitting at her feet. The woman cut the animal in the legs. The cat then began to bleed and turned into a man from the neighbourhood. He could turn himself into a cat.
170431: A man had quarrelled with the landlady in a café. Afterwards the man had misfortune on his farm. At midnight his cows were untied and his pigs became restless. The man had to be taken to a psychiatric institution. The friars of Affligem could not help the man, but while they said their prayers, the landlady suffered terribly. After advice was sought from the Norbertines of Tongerlo, the misfortune came to an end.
170447: A nun who was setting out the cups in the evening for the visitors who would come to eat porridge the next day heard three knocks. The nuns informed the priest, who said: "I received a gift from someone who may still need something. I will say a mass for that person tomorrow." The next morning the knocking was no longer heard.
170464: A man walking home at night saw a large herd of hares running. At the back ran a hare that was limping.
170465: A man who worked shifts was met one evening at ten o'clock at the wiekfabriek (sail factory) in Halle by his two sisters, who came to tell him that his brother was dead. The man went with his sisters to Essenbeek, where the dead man lay laid out. At a quarter past eleven the man left for home. In the Kruisstraat in Halle, however, he was surrounded by mewing cats with eyes like lanterns. The man began to murmur his prayers, after which the cats moved aside and let him through. When he got home the man could not utter a word from fear.
170476: In Bever lived a woman who claimed that witches could get people in their power by touching them.
170478: In Waresaet lived a man whose daughter was ill. A neighbour who was suspected of being a witch came to bring the child a bunch of grapes. As soon as the neighbour had left, they told the girl: "You must not eat those grapes!" They threw the grapes into the stove, but they would not burn. That proved that the neighbour really was a witch.
170495: A witch could only be shot down if the bullets had been blessed by a priest.
170504: Some men were playing cards in an inn in Loksbergen. One of the men always lost and said: "I wish the devil would come and help me". A little later an elegant gentleman came into the inn and sat down next to the loser. From that moment that player won every game. When the innkeeper's wife bent down to pick up a dropped card, she saw that the gentleman had horse's legs. It was Satan. The innkeeper's wife's husband sent for the priest, who came to pray and said to the devil: "Your place is in the abyss of hell". The devil then asked for a place in that house to stay. He would even be content with the eye of a needle. In the end, though, they managed to drive the devil out.
170508: A man who had been digging potatoes near his house could not find his house again afterwards. A witch had made the man lose his way.
170529: A witch could turn herself into a toad.
170537: A man who had been to the horse market in Brussels met a woman on his way home, who said: "Oh, that is a fine horse!" and gave the animal a slap on the rump. The next morning the horse was so lame that it walked on three legs. When the man sought advice from the Damiaan fathers, he was told: "You must not believe in that". The man was also given a medal to put under the threshold. When the woman came by again afterwards, she could not get in.
170543: If you wanted to become a sorceress, you had to stand at a crossroads at midnight with a black hen. The devil would then appear in the form of a gentleman dressed in black with a fist and a tail. The devil would then ask: "What do you want to become: a sorceress, a werewolf, or kludde (a shape-shifting spectre) with his chain?" You then received a lot of money and everything you wanted. But you had to sell yourself to the devil for a certain period.
170549: A girl was always cuddled by a neighbour, who gave her a jug of buttermilk and said: "You really are a pretty child!" When the girl was riding her bicycle in the Koestraat a few years later, she saw three or four cats come out of a hollow ditch. The cats kept running in front of the bicycle's wheel, so the girl began to pray. The girl also gave one of the cats a kick. The next day a woman walked around the village with a bandage around her head.
170559: In Ternat lived a man who had to roam about as a werewolf at a certain time. People took that man's werewolf skin away to burn it. As soon as the skin had caught fire, the man came running to save his skin.
170560: People who consorted with the devil were sometimes ridden by the 'maan' (the mare) in the old days.
170587:
On her way to Mie Maan, a woman always saw a goat with a scarf on its head sitting in a tree.
That woman's son could turn himself into a werewolf.
170593: Some children were selling calendars in Rotselaar for Oostpriesterhulp. Most of the children did not dare to knock at the house of a woman who was suspected of being a witch. One of the girls, however, was not afraid and knocked there. She sold a calendar for five francs. When the children counted their money later that day, they were five francs short. They believed the witch had magically taken her five-franc coin back.
170610: People who were ridden by the mare had a kind of illness, like the flu.
170616: In Lembeek lived a woman who was said to be a witch. When people went somewhere to fetch a litre of milk, they always had to pay a token sum of one cent. After all, if nothing was given away for free, one could not be bewitched. Also when people had wheat ground, they always had to pay the miller something. If someone gave you a cake and you could not avoid accepting it, you had to break off a piece and say: "That is your share". Nor were you allowed to pick up fruit lying along the road.
170619: In the past people were afraid of a black cat because they believed it was a witch.
170635: In the old days in Rotselaar people told stories about a nun who rode on a sow or about a sorceress on a pig.
170646: Near Walshoutem there was a wood called 'de Lazerij' or 'het Hoebroek'. In the past, lepers were said to have been banished to that wood. Werewolves also came into that wood. They were people who consorted with the devil and who threw a sheet over themselves at night to frighten others. If you could make a werewolf bleed, he took on his human form. That is how people sometimes found out that the werewolf was a man from the village.
170658: People who did not feel well often said they were being ridden by the mare.
170662: A man shot at a black cat sitting behind his house, but could not hit the animal. At night the doors in that house always flew open and there was a lot of noise.
170671: In Hoegaarden people used to talk a lot about the werewolf. A man walking from Kumtich to Hoxem was at one point leapt on by the werewolf. The man had to carry the werewolf a long way.
170684: If the priest left his missal open, the witches could not leave the church.
170697: People who were ridden by the mare at night had to scream to be set free.
170711: A farmer's wife wanted to go to the market with a litter of young piglets to sell. The day before, however, she had been visited by a woman with a bad reputation. When the farmer's wife wanted to leave in the morning, she found that the piglets had all been fighting and were covered in blood.
170715: Some men wanted to play cards at a farmer's. There were only three of them, so they were looking for a fourth man. At a certain moment a strange man came in who wanted to join the card game. After the men had played for a while, one of the players bent down to pick up a dropped card. The strange man turned out to have horse's legs. It was kludde (a malevolent shape-shifting spirit).
170719: A mother from Tienen had twins who cried all the time. A neighbour suspected that the children had been touched by the evil hand and sent the mother to the Lieve Vrouwkerk (1). The mother had to leave the church by a different door from the one she had entered by. When the mother had done so, she immediately saw the witch walk past. One of the children died.
170721: Being ridden by the mare was something akin to witchcraft.
170733: A man wanted to know whether the woman he was visiting was a witch. Although the woman had asked several times: "Aren't you leaving yet?", the man calmly stayed seated. The man would not be brushed off and said: "Where do you need to go? Do you have to go and do witchcraft?" At that the witch began to cry. She rubbed ointment on her hands and said: "Get out of here, or you'll fly along!" Then the man quickly left.
170739: A boy went with his sister to fetch eggs. A woman gave each of the children an apple. The boy, however, had a rotten apple. The next day the boy had a fever of forty degrees. Three doctors came to see the boy, but they did not manage to bring the fever down. Even when the boy was put in a bath of cold water, the fever stayed dangerously high. After a few days the boy was in a coma. Moreover, the ticking of a watch was heard by the boy's bed. The boy's parents prayed all the time and finally sent for the parish priest. When the boy came round, he saw that the priest was drenched in sweat. The clergyman said to the boy's father: "When your child is fully healed, a woman will come by. But you must not do her any harm". As soon as the boy felt better, he decided to clean his father's bicycle. At that moment a man with a barrel organ came past. A neighbour gave that man a coin with the words: "Because a boy here was dying".
170754: In Baardegem a boy had died in an accident. After the boy's death there was always knocking on a door somewhere. When a man finally had the courage to open the door, he saw the dead boy standing there. The boy led the man to a certain spot, pointed at the ground and vanished. At that spot the boy's money was found.
170760: A mother bewitched her own children. When a toad came into the house, the son kicked at the animal. Meanwhile his own mother sat laughing. Thanks to the help of the priest the boy did not die after all.
170761: Stallichten (will-o'-the-wisps) were the souls of unbaptised children who flew to people to be baptised. A barber on his way to shave someone saw a light flying over the field. It was a stallicht. Such lights could only be made to disappear by baptising them.
170773: In Pepingen lived a woman who was said to be able to do witchcraft. If you saw an egg lying in the street, you were not allowed to pick it up, because the witch might have put it there. If you picked up the egg, you could be bewitched. One day the witch came knocking at a family's door with a hen. The witch asked: "Is that your hen?", to which the people answered: "No, that is not our hen". Then the witch said: "I'll just let it run around here, because it isn't mine either". A few days later all those people's chickens were dead.
170774: Stallichten (will-o'-the-wisps) were often seen hovering above the Leibeek. They were the souls of unbaptised children. In reality, some men had tied a lantern to a stick so they could swing it back and forth along the Leibeek.
170794: A man who had gone to fetch hay at his grandmother's was coming back with horse and cart. On the way the horse suddenly stopped. The road was blocked by a ghost wearing a priest's hat on its head. A little later the ghost had vanished.
170802: A woman who drank a lot and was always nervous went to clean in a building. When the woman was there, she always heard all kinds of noises. In the evening the woman closed the doors and windows there, but when she arrived in the morning, all the windows and doors flew open at the same time. In the end the woman was too afraid to go cleaning there any more. In the building stood a statue, which was removed one day, because people believed the haunting was caused by that statue.
170834: A man who was ridden by the mare could not breathe and felt as if he were being seized by the throat. The man could not move.
170845: In a house where someone was ill, they sent for the doctor. People believed that a woman who often visited there was responsible for the illness. So they had the sick boy prayed over by the parish priest, after which he was healed.
170874: A man had shot himself in the head. When the widow was praying for the salvation of her husband's soul, she suddenly smelled sulphur and something burnt. The widow had also seen a flash. It was the ghost of her husband letting her know that she should not pray for him, because she herself had been the cause of his suicide.
170890: A farmer's wife had been visited by a woman who had gone to stand by the water barrel and had said: "Now you may make three wishes". The farmer's wife had wished that her sister-in-law, who was 48 years old and already had many children, would have another child. That farmer's wife must therefore have been of ill will. Some time later her sister-in-law became pregnant at the age of forty-nine.
170903: In Kersbeek lived a witch who could make horses stand still. The animals only started moving after the witch had given permission.
170904: In Melkwezer lived a little boy who suffered from epilepsy. The parents promised to go on pilgrimage to Leuven for their son. Shortly afterwards, however, the boy was already cured. Not long after, the mother fell ill and died before she had made the pilgrimage to Leuven. A few days after the funeral the boy fell ill again. People wondered why and remembered the promised pilgrimage. The boy then went to Leuven himself. First he had to hold a collection in the village, and he then had to offer that money to a particular saint in Leuven.
170909: A witch lived in the same house as her daughter and her daughter's husband. The son-in-law could make cigars. One evening some neighbours came to learn how to make cigars. All that evening the witch kept shifting restlessly on her chair. One of the visitors had put a piece of a blessed candle in his pocket.
170913: A butcher was known for the tasty pork sausages he made every Tuesday. One day, however, people came to bring their sausages back because the meat began to stink as soon as it was in the pan. Because the butcher had to refund his customers, he got into trouble and was often cursing. One evening the butcher got quite drunk and told the landlord of the inn what had happened to him. The innkeeper asked: "Does x come into your shop?", to which the butcher replied: "Certainly, she is always one of my first customers". Then the innkeeper said: "That woman is one of the most powerful maren (witches) in the region. Go quickly and have the fathers pray over you". The father who prayed over the butcher sweated heavily and said: "Put this relic under your threshold. Then the woman will not come in any more". The butcher followed the father's advice. That particular woman never came into his shop again and the butcher had no more complaints about his meat.
170937: A little boy of seven months cried all the time. Someone had been seen taking the child by the hand. The Jesuits said the child had been touched by the evil hand and came to pray over it. But it was already too late, for the child died in the end.
170946: A man who was coming back from the fair in Kattem with his father was followed by a meowing cat. That cat was a witch who had spoken with the men at the fair.
170955: On All Saints' Day a farmer saw a magpie sitting next to his house. Although it was a feast day, the farmer fetched his double-barrelled gun and shot at the animal twice. The magpie, however, sat there unperturbed. The farmer then fetched a blessed bullet and fired again. This time the magpie was hit in the wing. When the farmer came closer to pick up the magpie, he saw a little old woman sitting there, wrapping a cloth around her bleeding finger. It was a sorceress who had turned herself into a magpie.
170976:
A woman who believed her grandmother was a witch saw a cat come in one evening. Because a boy in that house was bewitched, a man broke the cat's leg. The next day the woman went to her grandmother. The grandmother had a bandage around her arm and claimed she had fallen.
The witches gathered in the Rode in Testelt, so it was said.
170977: On a farm a neighbour came to milk the cow because the farmer's wife was ill. Shortly afterwards the cow died because it had been bewitched by the neighbour.
171080: A woman was visited daily by an old neighbour. Because the woman's two children got croup, the woman went to the fathers of Dendermonde. There she was given a piece of the Easter candle to put under her threshold, so that the witch could no longer get in. After that the neighbour never visited the woman again. Her children recovered.
171103: In a family living at 't Rot, three boys had already died. Because the people believed it had something to do with witchcraft, they sent for a spiritualist from Wallonia. The spiritualist began hacking into the wall of the stable and took out three rotten apples. Each apple had caused one child to die. Then the spiritualist found a fourth apple with a rotten spot. That apple stood for the daughter who could still be saved.
171113: On a farm in Grimbergen they always had bad luck with the horses whenever a black cat had been nearby.
171118: A man who came from Paris stayed with his family, who lived at the Klarenbos. At night the man was restless. He made wild movements, but no one could wake him. So they sent for a doctor, who found that the man had been ridden by the mare.
171136: The Tillekesjacht were witches who flew through the air and made beautiful music. A man who wanted to fly to the priest's wine cellar made a mistake in saying the magic formula and said: "Through hedgerows and verges" instead of "Over hedgerows and verges." The man was found badly injured in Bierbeek.
171155:
A man walking home at night saw two beautiful cats and said: "Those are beautiful cats!" Then one cat said to the other: "Mother, he said to me: 'Spotted little cat, where are you going?'"
Those two cats were witches.
171169: In Bost lived a witch who did a lot of harm. When the grain had to be brought in because of bad weather, the witch's grain had to be brought in first. Otherwise the horses went off on their own and left the grain standing.
171179: On a farm where many cows died, someone was called in to drive out the witchcraft. The farmer had to bury the cow in the stable. He also learned that a certain woman was said to be responsible for the harm. When that woman came to visit, the farmer had to put a relic of a saint under her chair. Then the house had to be heated very hot. When they did so, the woman tried in vain to move her chair. When she prayed and begged to be let go, they removed the relic, so that the witch could get up. But first she had to promise to undo all the harm she had done.
171192: A farmer from Bollebeek needed a new barn. He made a pact with the devil, who would build him a new barn that would be finished before the first cockcrow the next morning. While the devil was working on the barn in the night, the farmer went outside and woke the rooster, which then began to crow early. Because the barn was not yet finished at that moment, the farmer could keep his soul. But there was still a hole in the barn that could not be closed. A cross was bricked into that hole.
171212: Freemasons were damned souls who wandered about.
171217: Glow-worms were the souls of unbaptised children. If you held out your finger, a glow-worm would come and sit on it. You then had to make a little cross to baptise the child.
171219: A girl from a good family became pregnant before she was married. The girl's parents did not want their daughter to marry the child's father. One day the girl left for early mass and never came back. The girl's boyfriend tried furiously to find out the truth about the girl's disappearance. When the missing girl's father was dying, his wife stayed with him the whole time because she was afraid her husband would tell the priest something during his death struggle. Later the man's grave was opened again to see whether the missing girl was buried there as well. The neighbours had noticed that the girl was not in church on the morning of her disappearance. Some even claimed that the parents had burned the girl in the oven. The man who later came to live in the house had the priest of Budingen come because strange things were happening. One time a painting had disappeared, another time a chair, and so on.
171224: A woman was constantly tormented by her mother-in-law, whom she suspected of witchcraft. Since 1987 the woman and her husband never visited the witch again. The mother-in-law no longer visited her son and daughter-in-law either. In 1995 the witch died. Her son and daughter-in-law did not go to her funeral. That witch could harm people by touching them. On her deathbed she asked several times for her granddaughter, but the girl did not come to see her.
171275: People who were ridden by the mare saw someone come in while they lay in bed. The mare jumped on her victim and seized it by the throat. The victim lay there sweating and tried in vain to call out. After a while the mare jumped away and the victim woke up.
171285: A man was coming back from Breestraeten (Merchtem) by moonlight. On the way the man met a small black dog, which came to stand in front of him and suddenly grew as big as a horse. The dog howled and had fiery eyes. It was the devil. After the dog had disappeared, the trees swayed back and forth and the branches beat against the ground. When the man went to look at that place the next day, he found that not a single twig had been broken. Klerre (a demonic spectre) had made those trees move like that.
171298: In a hut in Elingen lived an old woman who was suspected of being a witch. People who did not take care of themselves were often suspected of witchcraft. Children were often advised by their parents to stay away from such people.
171312: On a farm in Haacht the animals had fallen ill after being touched by the evil hand. At night a dog always walked around the house. The people went to fetch something blessed. After that the animals recovered and the dog no longer appeared at night.
171338: A witch could turn herself into a toad. In a house in Attenhoven lived an old man and woman who were at odds with their son. When the son's wife was pregnant, the old woman had said that her daughter-in-law would have a deformed child. At the moment the newborn child was being taken to the washtub in a nearby room, a toad was seen sitting there. People were convinced it was the old woman, come to bewitch the child. When the man was about to strike the toad with a stick, a voice was heard crying: "Don't kill me, I'm your mother!"
171351: A boy of sixteen or seventeen had fallen over a dog on his bicycle. The boy died of his injuries, although his parents had tried all sorts of things and had even promised pilgrimages. The parents moved to Kester and rented out their house in Herfelingen. In that house a knocking was heard around one o'clock at night. The owners were informed, so that they could come and listen to the inexplicable sounds themselves. After the priest had prayed in that room until he was drenched in sweat, he said: "That is a spirit in distress. Did you never promise a pilgrimage that you have not yet made?" The parents remembered one pilgrimage they still had to make. After the parents had made the pilgrimage and had taken the grave wreaths down from the attic, no more knocking was heard in the house.
171374: On a farm where a witch had been in the house, they could no longer make butter. A father came to visit and advised the people to put dung in the butter churn. When they had done so, the witch always had dung in her churn, while the people themselves had good butter.
171375: A farmer's wife was visited by a witch from Kapellen, who came to look at the cow. When the farmer's wife had sold her cow to her brother, the animal kept falling to the ground. The farmer's wife's mother had also once bought a cow that had been touched by the evil hand. The animal had something wrong with its udder.
171388: In France stood a devil's barn with a hole that could not be closed. People said that the devils were in that hole.
171396: A girl did not feel welcome with her parents-in-law. Whenever the girl came in, conversations always suddenly fell silent. When the girl had a child in June 1964, her mother had a broken arm, so she took the child to her parents-in-law. Because the girl had to get up early in the morning and work late in the evening, the child stayed with the parents-in-law for several years. When the mother and father went to fetch their child on a cold day in November, the mother-in-law said to her son: "You know what to do when she gets it". A few hours later the child had convulsions. The mother-in-law had known this beforehand and had brought it about to torment her daughter-in-law. Some time later the mother-in-law had the child prayed over. Against all advice the parents held their child under cold running water. When the child was five or six years old, it recovered.
171398: In the old days people would say, as a figure of speech, that slow, dull people had been ridden by the mare.
171407: A werewolf had hidden his animal skin in a hollow willow. A woman had seen this, however, and decided to burn the werewolf's animal skin. Because the werewolf came running very fast at that moment to save his skin, the woman had to flee quickly to her house. The werewolf came too late, though, for his animal skin had already burnt up.
171414: A farmer from Amelgem (Brussegem) could not store his harvest in his small barn. A gentleman declared himself willing to build the farmer a new barn in a single night on condition that he got his soul. The barn had to be finished before the rooster crowed for the first time in the morning. The next night the farmer's wife went to the henhouse at two o'clock with a lantern, so that the rooster began to crow. There was still a hole in the barn that could never be closed afterwards.
171421: On a farm in Vollezele lived a man who was not afraid of the devil or hell. During a heavy thunderstorm three gates on the farm stood open. The man's three-year-old child was standing close to one of the gates. The wind slammed one of the gates shut, killing the child instantly. After that the man no longer dared to go outside when it thundered. The man is said to have prayed on his bare knees with his arms spread. One day the man claimed he had seen the devil, with two horns and two ugly eyes, in his attic. The man had been so frightened that he had fallen out of his attic.
171460: A witch made sure that horses could not get past a certain spot.
171465: In Keerbergen an unmarried girl's baby was stillborn. Because the child was not allowed to be buried in consecrated ground, a man from the neighbourhood was asked to take the little body away. As the man was walking there with the farmhand, he saw behind him a beast with flaming eyes, as big as a calf, that kept coming closer. When the men prayed the Gospel of Saint John, the apparition vanished.
171516: On a farm where many animals were dying, the fathers of Gent were sent for. A friar came in without opening the door. After that the animals recovered and the farm was rid of the evil hand.
171520: When people were dancing in a dance hall in Tienen on Christmas night, a black cat suddenly appeared at midnight and played the organ. Everyone ran away in fright.
171523: A brave man went to keep watch at night in the haunted castle of Roi. At midnight ghosts came walking in and began playing skittles with bones and a skull. The man wanted to join in, but he had no money with him. The next night the man took money and went to the castle again. This time the man played along, and soon lost all his money. When the man asked the ghosts what they came there to do, they answered: "We come here to look for a treasure." In reality, however, the ghosts did nothing but play skittles.
171533: In the evening a ghost appeared that called: "Posts moved, posts moved!" One day a cursing passer-by answered: "Put it back where you got it!"
171557: A boy said to his girlfriend: "I have to go round the back for a moment. You go on ahead." The boy gave the girl his handkerchief and said: "If you meet anything, throw this handkerchief at the apparition." When the girl saw her boyfriend again, she noticed that he had the fibres of the handkerchief between his teeth. The boy had gone to play the werewolf because the time for it had come.
171583: A man was bewitched after a beggar woman came to borrow a colander from him. After that all the children in that house fell ill. Six of them died.
171584: One evening a boy went to visit his girlfriend, the daughter of a woman who ran a pub. On his way back, in Strombeek-Bever, the boy saw a white lady whom he could not get past.
171630: During the procession a mother went to the parish priest with her child. A woman standing among the group said to the mother: "Tonight the child will die!" That evening the child's father sat beside the stove with his gun, ready to deal with the witch. A little later the witch knocked on the window. But the father could not catch her, because she flew over his head.
171638: In Attenhoven a pilgrimage to Scherpenheuvel was made every year. Once, when the statue of Mary had not been taken along because the weather was so bad, people found the next day that the statue was standing in the field covered in mud. The statue of Mary had gone to Scherpenheuvel of its own accord.
171640: People who were drunk often believed they were being ridden by the mare.
171642: In Halle a bald man lived next to a witch. Whenever that man was working in his potato field, the witch came out to tease him. She would call: "Baldy!" or "Slaphead!" One day the man got so angry that he struck the witch on the head with his hoe. The woman bled heavily and had to be put to bed. When the doctor came to her, she was lying in bed with a bottle of champagne. The witch survived, however. Later she turned her teasing on the son of the man who had wounded her. Every Thursday when the witch saw the boy standing on the canal bridge, she began to dance around him like an eighteen-year-old girl. But she could not harm him because he always kept his prayer in his head. When the boy met the witch on a Monday at the Varkensmarkt in Halle, he thought to himself: "Filthy redhead". When he came back from visiting his girlfriend the following Thursday at about half past eleven, he saw two extraordinarily large cats standing on the Steenweg naar Bergen. The boy began to sweat with fear, but he said his prayer and went on. When the boy turned round a little further on, he saw that the cats had changed into dogs. Although the boy normally had only five minutes left to walk, it took him three quarters of an hour to get home. He was sweating heavily and when he got home he could not utter a word. After that the boy fell ill and he never fully recovered. The witch had done all this to him because on that Monday he had said "Filthy redhead" to himself.
171657: A man coming home in the dark saw a strange apparition that frightened him.
171659: In Beert lived a woman who was suspected of being a witch. When that woman visited a neighbour, she asked: "What are you making?" and lifted the lids of the cooking pots.
171672: A woman whose child cried all the time had to go to church when the fathers of Sint-Truiden were in the village to preach. Although the child was still very small, the woman sweated terribly as she walked to the church. The father laid the child on the communion rail and began to pray. The mother and father had to bow down. Then the father laid the child on the altar and began to pray again. The parents had to bow down again. After that the child slept for two or three days and finally recovered. The child had been bewitched by a well-known woman.
171682: N.B., a nineteen-year-old boy from Baardegem, had died. In the house of K.P. people could speak with the boy's ghost, which appeared in the form of a dancing little light.
171700: One night a large hole appeared in a barn in Bierbeek. People wanted to close the hole, but the devils opened it again every time. The barn was called 'Blauwschuur' (Blue Barn).
171758: A boy shot at a witch several times in vain. Strangely, the others in his household could not see the witch.
171799: In a house where a black cat always came, the animal was chased away. A little later the street was full of black cats.
171819: A girl from Waarbeke who had married in Grimmingen had a child of about three years old. The child fell ill and got a swollen belly. The people had a little goat that sometimes lay writhing as if it had been touched by the evil hand. When the goat was ill, the child was healthy, but as soon as the goat had been killed, the child fell ill. Finally the people went to the fathers, who asked them whether anyone came to visit. The people told them about their neighbour who came by regularly. The fathers advised them to keep that neighbour out from then on. After that the child recovered.
171833: People said that cats were witches.
171838: In Sint-Pieters-Leeuw lived two women who were suspected of being witches. When people teased that woman, she always said: "I'll bewitch you, I'll bewitch you!"
171851: In Booienhoven there once lived a man who could make mice by throwing a handful of dust into his clog.
171854: A man often went out in the evening with his gun. He had planted some cabbages in a field so that he could shoot a hare there in winter. When the man walked through the snow to his field, he saw hare tracks everywhere. After a quarter of an hour he saw a hare by the cabbages. He pulled the trigger, but he could not shoot. He had a second bullet, but on the second try his gun did not work either. The man had to go home because he had no more bullets. When he shot at two crows in the field the next day, his gun worked. The man went back to his field. This time he had to wait half an hour before a hare appeared, which stayed sitting seventy or eighty metres away. A little later a second hare appeared. The man fired but could not hit either hare. On his way home the man met an unknown woman, who said to him: "You didn't get him!" The next day a woman in the village who was suspected of being a witch died.
171862: A man from Wilsele who had got lost saw a little light moving back and forth by a pool. The man went up to the will-o'-the-wisp and said: "I baptise you in the name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit". At that the light vanished into the pool, but a hundred others appeared. The man had to baptise all the lights.
171897: People who were ridden by the 'maan' (mare) sweated heavily and suffered a great deal, even though no one could be seen.
171906: Two boys were trying to pull apart two spring mattresses. The boys had already been at the job for two hours when a witch came past and said: "I'll do that". The witch finished the job in a few seconds.
171912: A girl worked as a maid for a married couple in Halle. When the woman fell ill, the girl took good care of her. One day the woman said to the girl: "Thank you for taking such good care of me. After my death I will come back to you once more." Shortly afterwards the woman died. For their mother's funeral the two sons had to wear a black tie. The dead woman appeared to the maid with the words: "Look, there is the key to a trunk. Tell the master that the ties the boys have to wear are in that trunk."
171946: A man who had a relationship with a woman who was said to be a witch always got hopelessly lost at night.
171948: A man who crossed a witch's footprints in the snow found that the witch stood still.
171991: On the common land in Halle customary law used to apply. Anyone who could build a house on that land in a single night without blocking the traffic was allowed to stay and live there. People who had built a house there did not go to Mass and went stealing chickens from the farmers. The daughter of those people once made mice at school. The nun had seen it and went to warn the priest. After the priest had read the Gospel of Saint John over the child, it could no longer make mice.
172004: Some people who worked in a factory in Zaventem came home together late in the evening. In the wood between Zaventem and Woluwe they sometimes met a black cat that would not be chased away. Only when the people reached a place where there were houses did the cat run off.
172009: A man who was ridden by the mare saw a woman approach, who lay down on him, so that he could no longer move and felt he would suffocate. Only when someone called the man's name was he freed from the mare. Other people could not see the mare.
172018: A man who worked on a farm had trouble breathing at night because he had been ridden by the mare. That man was the victim of a notorious witch from the area.
172034: A woman from Halle had met a neighbour in the street, who had said: "You have lovely socks" and had briefly touched the woman's leg. When the woman got home, she found she was covered in lice. The woman washed herself, but she could not get rid of the lice. The next morning the lice were gone.
172041: An old woman who lived alone in a castle employed a workman. When the old woman had died, the workman came to live in the castle with his wife. One evening, at the stroke of ten, the little door of the grandfather clock opened and a ball rolled across the floor to the cellar. On a friend's advice, the workman went looking for money said to be hidden in the castle. The workman found nothing, however. Ten days later, at ten o'clock, a card with the number 100,000 on it fell out of the grandfather clock. The priest was at his wits' end when the workman told him what was going on. A few days later the workman's wife heard a knocking under the ground in the cellar. The workman went down and knocked a hole in the floor with his hammer and chisel. In this way the workman and his wife found a small chest in which Roman gold coins from 1240 were hidden.
172046: In Pamel stood a castle where haunting always began at midnight. Nobody dared to pass by there any more, because the ghost of a dead person returned there.
172049: In the past people believed that stalkaarsen (will-o'-the-wisps) were the souls of children who had died unbaptised. In reality such lights were probably glow-worms.
172063: A forester who worked at Terborg often went out at night with two dangerous dogs. One night the man saw something move beside him that looked like a bundle of wood. The dogs crept fearfully between their master's legs.
172086:
To protect themselves against evil, people went to the friars of Edingen.
The friars of Affligem had a mirror in which they could make the sorceresses appear.
When the friars had to fight evil, drops of sweat rolled down their faces. Sorceresses owned dolls or candles into which they stuck pins to torment people. When such a doll or candle was completely full of pins, the victim was dead.
172087: In the old days many people had lice. It was believed that people who could give someone lice were witches. People often said: "The first person you meet when you go to the shop is the witch".
172096: A mother whose little daughter was bewitched was visited by the witch, who came to ask how the girl was. Afterwards the mother sent for a sorcerer, who crawled under the mattress and began to pray until the drops of sweat rolled from his head. After that the girl got better. Some time later the witch came again to ask how the girl was. The witch also asked for a slice of bread, which they gave her, although the sorcerer had said that was not allowed. After that the girl fell ill again. This time the sorcerer could no longer help her.
172100: In the old days, if people saw a star flickering somewhere, they believed a war would break out.
172124:
A woman who had died came back after her death in the shape of a cat. 
A man on the road came across a whole row of cats. One of the animals sang: "Janneke P. asked of me: 'Minneke puss, where are you going?'"
172136: In a house where there were twins, a woman came to visit one day and said: "They really are such sturdy boys!" After that woman left, the children began to cry ceaselessly. The people went to the fathers of Affligem for the children. The clergymen gave the people salt to put in the children's porridge, which healed them.
172142: In the evening a meowing black cat came and sat on the windowsill of a house. The occupants of the house were afraid, and the man said: "I'm going outside with a dung fork." The man managed to wound the cat. The next day a woman was seen walking in the village with a bandage around her head. That woman had turned herself into a cat the night before.
172165: A farmer had been to the market with his horse several times. Each time the farmer arrived at the market, the animal was lame through the doing of the evil hand. When the farmer once took a different road to the market, the horse did not go lame.
172189: A man was followed by a little dog that grew larger and larger. In the end the little dog turned into a foal that jumped onto the man's neck. The man was ill with fright.
172192: On the road to Binderveld Broek, a man often saw witches, ghosts and women dancing. One day the man had bought an earthenware jug. The man had to carry that jug on his shoulders through Binderveld Broek on his way home. On the way the man, to his great fright, heard noise. When he looked back, however, there was nothing to be seen. The faster the man walked, the louder the noise became. The man knocked at a door somewhere and had a friend accompany him. When the friend also heard the noise, he said: "Damn, it's true!"
172213: In Houwaart there once lived a witch who often gave the children a sweet when she came back from the market. When she saw the children again the following week, she refused to give them another sweet and said: "You won't get any more, because you threw the others away". The witch knew what the children had done with the sweets.
172244: On a farm that had much misfortune, there worked a farmhand. One day they had wanted to sell a horse, but the sale had not gone through because the buyer had offered too little. When he heard this, the farmhand slapped the animal on the rump and said: "Offered so much and you didn't agree?" The next day the horse lay dead. On a loft the farmer found a wolf skin. The priest advised the farmer to send his farmhand to the animal market in Gent to buy a new horse. Meanwhile the farmer had to light the oven and throw the skin into the fire. He was not allowed to touch the skin with his hands, however, and had to throw it into the oven with a dung fork. As soon as the skin caught fire, the farmhand was already standing by the oven. After the skin had burnt up, he was released. The priest came to the place and threw straw into the moat around the farm. The straw caught fire and the moats burnt out completely. That is how badly that farm was bewitched.
172271: A man who heard chains rattling went to see what was going on. However, the man saw nothing.
172307: On a farm in Pepingen the people were tormented by a witch. That witch even pulled the wool out of the beds to torment the people. The parish priest of Bogaarden sweated water and blood when he had to pray over that farm. The clergyman banished the witchcraft to the Black Sea.
172308: A man who was playing cards went outside for a moment to relieve himself. At 't Steenkapelletje he saw a stallicht (will-o'-the-wisp) come flying towards him. He quickly went inside to tell his friends what he had seen. When they all went outside, there was nothing more to be seen. Stallichten were the souls of unbaptised children.
172317: A woman had been inside a house and had brought the evil hand over the house. The woman had been gone barely two minutes when the woman who lived in that house got a fever. Her granddaughter got diarrhoea. A doctor did not know what was wrong. After the woman had been prayed over by the parish priest, she recovered.
172328: A man was visited every evening by a woman who bewitched him. After the woman had left, the man felt a tightness in the area of his heart. In the end the witch died of a heart attack. After that the man had no more problems.
172358: In the past people often used the expression 'to be ridden by the maar (nightmare)'.
172403: A family had a disabled child. A while later those people suddenly had another child. From then on a little light was always seen moving back and forth on the Oemsberg. People believed the parents had murdered their disabled child. Because the will-o'-the-wisp kept appearing, people searched the woods for the place where the murdered child was buried. Once the little body had been taken to the churchyard, the will-o'-the-wisp was no longer seen.
172412: On a farm people were playing cards one Sunday evening. At midnight they heard shouting and the sound of footsteps. The people went outside, but there was nothing to be seen. The haunting lasted until one o'clock. Because the friars could not help, the farmer was finally forced to give up farming. None of this is surprising, however, since the building had once been a monastery that had been sold as zwart goed (confiscated church property).
172427: Veronica always heard loud sighing when she lay in bed at night. One night the priest came to ask the ghost what it had come for. "I had promised to go on pilgrimage to Scherpenheuvel, but I did not keep my promise. That is why I come to ask Veronica whether she will go on pilgrimage for me. I cannot ask my family, because those people are not worthy of doing it", said the ghost. When Veronica left for Scherpenheuvel, the priest had advised her to hold a handkerchief in her hand. In Scherpenheuvel Veronica met a pale person who said: "Thank you" and shook her hand. The handprint was burned into the handkerchief.
172433: People who had had to carry the werewolf found on getting home that their money had disappeared. They would often say they had given their money to the werewolf, because they did not dare say the werewolf had taken it.
172437: Stallichten (will-o'-the-wisps) were the souls of unbaptised children. If you made the sign of the cross on seeing such lights, the souls were released and no longer had to wander.
172454: One evening a girl was walking home with a wes (1) (a head pad) on her head and a basket of eggs on top of it. When the girl met a witch, she wanted to hurry on. In no time her basket of eggs ended up in a bush.
172456: Two neighbours from Denderwindeke had quarrelled. One of them had said: "I'll get you yet!" When the other farmer came into his horse stable that evening, he saw hundreds of rats running around. The farmer shut the stable door and went inside to tell his wife what he had seen. But when the wife came into the stable, there was not a single rat to be seen. Three quarters of an hour later the farmer went to feed his animals. Again he saw hundreds of rats in the stable. The farmer shut the door and called his wife again. Again the farmer's wife saw nothing and began to think her husband was mad. The third time the farmer saw the rats, he did not shut the stable door and called his wife. The farmer's wife took a blessed palm sprig in her hand and went to the stable. At the sight of the palm sprig the rats shrivelled up one by one. The farmer's wife sprinkled the whole stable with holy water. The farmer went to the friars of Hekelgem, who advised him not to quarrel with his fellow men in future. The farmer never had a rat plague again, but the next day the rats were in the stable of his neighbour, who had sent the rats!
172466: A man who went to Busingen station around half past four or six in the morning to go to work passed a chapel standing by the roadside on Solheide. That man always saw a cat there.
172471: On a farm, a farmer's wife went outside one evening with the lantern to give the cows some more straw. Suddenly the farmer's wife heard a noise as if a hundred bumblebees, wasps and beetles were buzzing. The light in the lantern went out and the noise moved to the horse stable. The farmer's wife no longer dared to go outside in the evening, so the next day she sent her farmhand. The farmhand found that prints of the moddereenden (mud ducks) could be seen on the walls of the stable. The horses' manes had been braided and three horses had been tied together by their tails. The farmhand even had to fetch a pair of scissors to cut the animals' tails loose.
172475: A man returning from a café in Walfergem got lost and, around midnight, knocked on a door somewhere to ask the way. The man had been ridden by the mare.
172515: A boy from the Osseweg in Zoutleeuw had to go to catechism class to prepare for his First Communion. That boy could make mice appear from a little ball of earth. After the dean had read prayers over the boy, he could no longer make mice, which made him very sad.
172516: A man and a woman coming from the Allerheiligenberg went to visit the daughter of a witch. When the man and the woman went outside again, they saw a white spotted dog that kept following them. The woman was convinced that the dog was the mother of the girl they had been visiting. When the man and the woman got home, they no longer saw the dog.
172524: A toad was a witch, so people believed.
172532: A priest saw a little woman on the Pelsberg scratching in the sand. After the priest made the sign of the cross, the little woman had disappeared.
