179126: On a farm lived an old woman, one of whose children suffered from a bone disease. The doctor had said that the woman had to throw away everything the sick boy had used. The mother did not do so, however. The woman then went to the White Fathers of Ghent. The next day a daughter of hers also had croup. The father came to the house, went around the little room and said that he was just in time. The girl was saved.
179140: Every evening a boy saw a strange apparition at a farm in Strombeek-Bever. People believed the apparition was a witte madam (white lady). In reality it was a girl who walked about there in her nightdress because she was in love with the boy.
179147: A man suddenly could no longer make butter after a witch had put her finger in the churn. The man went to the fathers of Edingen to have himself overlezen (exorcised by prayer). The father predicted: "The person who caused this evil will come back to undo it. But you must not harm the woman. You must not let her in." What the father predicted came true.
179151: A pigeon fancier had visited a woman who was suspected of being a witch. When the man came home, he saw his best pigeon fall down. The man immediately pricked the pigeon in the toenail. The pigeon still came back after all (?).
179152: A strange farmhand worked for a farmer and had to manure the field one Monday. But the farmhand was still tired because he had enjoyed himself at the inn the day before. He waited until evening, then went to the field and called: "Each to his own." The next moment the whole field was manured.
179168: Many witches had a wishing stone. If you touched that stone, you could move in no time to wherever you wanted. That is how the witches flew to the wine cellar. A man had overheard the witches, but he made a mistake in saying the magic formula and said: "Through shed and stick" instead of "Over shed and stick." The man arrived in the wine cellar badly injured.
179194: A black cat walking on the road would jump on people's necks. You then had to ask: "Pretty spotted little cat, where do you come from?"
179197: When a man in Holland (Kester) was milking the cows, the bucket was taken away by a ghost and emptied. That was probably a returned dead person.
179208: A schoolgirl from Bost made mice by throwing some earth on the ground in front of her. When the priest found out, he baptised the girl again, for a word had been forgotten at her baptism.
179211: In the Bosstraat in Hekelgem a large meadow was haunted every night, so that people no longer dared to go outside. One night an old pious spinster decided to put an end to the haunting. She stood in the meadow and called out: "If you are sent by God, come closer. If you are sent by evil, go away." After that the haunting was over.
179221:
At a farmer's in Alsemberg a black cat always jumped through the window. That farmer could never churn butter. After the priest had come to read prayers over the farm, butter could be made.
Witches could go about in the shape of a black cat.
179222: In a factory lay a man who could not get up because he had been ridden by the mare. That man had a stoppage of the blood and could no longer breathe.
179233: On a farm in Dormaal the horses and cows were always untied in the evening. People then said the place was haunted.
179234: A farmer from Asse had sold his soul to the devil in exchange for a new barn, which had to be finished before the first cockcrow the next morning. Towards morning the farmer's wife got up, went to the henhouse and woke the rooster. When the rooster began to crow, there was still a hole in the barn, so the farmer got to keep his soul.
179247:
It was believed that toads and black cats were witches in animal shape. Between Oudenaken and Breedhout there used to be a castle with an avenue of elms. In that avenue ran a little black cat that always jumped in front of people's feet. If one tried to kick the cat, strangely enough one could not hit it.
The little black cat people supposedly saw was perhaps their clothing being blown between their legs by the wind. After all, people wore long skirts with gathered hems back then.
179263: A man walking home along a back road in Londerzeel tripped over something. The man found that it was a calf that had escaped from a nearby meadow.
179274: Some boys were out with the pigs between Dormaal and Neerlanden. When a witch approached in the distance, one of the boys said: "You filthy one!" The witch said to the boy: "You have a nice pipe." Not ten metres further on, the boy had lost his pipe. The witch had spirited it away.
179279: If a crow was heard cawing three times on the left side of a certain person, that person could expect misfortune.
179281: A man who was ridden by the mare could not breathe and felt as if he were being seized by the throat.
179338: After some altar boys had placed a piece of a blessed candle at the back of the church, seven witches could no longer leave the church. Only when the piece of candle was taken away did the witches go outside.
179349: A woman always felt a heavy load on her shoulders when she lay in bed in the evening. In the end it became so bad that she could no longer do her housework. Her neighbours advised her to place her slippers with the heels pointing towards the bed. Someone else advised her to lay a bread knife on her chest with the blade pointing upwards when she went to sleep. When the woman did so, the woman who had bewitched her lay dead on her chest the next day.
179352: A man was bringing a wagon full of fodder home with his ox. At a certain spot the wagon could not go on because of witchcraft. A little old woman had just passed by. When that woman was gone, the cart started moving again.
179358: On a farm there were two large 'rennen' (?) in the stable. Every time an old woman had visited, those rennen were so restless that they had to be brought inside. The farmer went to the fathers of Dendermonde, who advised him to make a novena and put a medal under the threshold of the stable. After the farmer had done that, the woman could no longer come in.
179360:
A mother lying in childbed received gingerbread from a child who came to visit her. A woman from the neighbourhood had sent the gingerbread with the child because she had no time to visit herself. She would, however, soon come by in person.
The mother ate a piece of the gingerbread. That evening, however, she got terrible stomach cramps. The doctor came, but he could not help. When people learned that the woman had eaten gingerbread from a certain neighbour, someone said: "Don't you know she is a maar (witch)! Wherever she comes in, there is misfortune. Fetch the father quickly or this woman will die!" A father came to overlezen (exorcise by prayer) the house and threw the gingerbread into the fire. During the exorcism it seemed as if the father was constantly pushed away by a strange force. After that intervention the mother gradually recovered.
179367: An old woman who had gone to fetch a bundle of wood met a woman on the way back, who took her by the hand. The old woman could no longer use her hand after that.
179387: People who got lost even though they were close to home believed they had been ridden by the mare.
179408: A cat always came into a house, and it would not be caught and always escaped through the water drain. One day someone stood guard at the drain with an axe in his hand. In this way the man managed to hit the cat on the head. The next day a woman from the village walked around with a large bandage around her head. She claimed that she had fallen from the 'vooreere' (1) at home.
179424: In a house a child fell ill through the kwade hand (evil hand, witchcraft). When the child had recovered, the animals fell ill. Two animals even died.
179441: People who were ridden by the mare were under the influence of evil spirits.
179443: A man who was ridden by the mare (here called the moon) was in a wood and could not get out of it.
179444: On the heath in Kester there was a café where people went to play cards in the evening. Sometimes a hen was seen sitting on the shelf with the glasses. When someone came closer, the animal vanished. That hen was a witch.
179465: When people got lost, they believed they had been ridden by the mare.
179501: Two friends coming back from Stok saw a black cat. They struck at the cat, but the animal ran off unharmed.
179514: A boy could make mice from earth because he had not been baptised properly. During catechism some children told the priest that there was a boy who could make mice. The clergyman had the boy make mice in his presence, so that he could see whether it was true. Then he said: "Come along with me, my boy." After the boy had been baptised again, he could no longer make mice. The boy cried, however, because he had lost his magic power.
179548: A woman had been to Geraardsbergen on foot with her sister. When the women came back in the evening, they got lost in the wood, so that their clothes were completely torn. The women sat down and began to pray, after which they could find their way again. The women had been 'led astray by the evil hand'.
179561: A mother had a child who began to cry every night at around the same time. Near the mother's house lived a woman suspected of being a witch. One day the mother's grandfather went to the witch, grabbed her and threatened her with the words: "If the child is still crying tomorrow, I'll knock your head off!" The woman replied: "The child will not cry any more." And so it was.
179565: In the barn of a woman who had been dead for a few weeks, some people were binding flax into bundles. When a strange apparition was seen outside the next morning, people believed the dead woman had come back. The bundles that had been left standing outside overnight were covered with a layer of snow, which gave the whole scene an eerie look.
179568: A man and a woman went to the field with a large basket to gather potatoes. When they came home along a back road in the evening, they heard some twenty cats meowing. The man and the woman climbed into an apple tree to wait until the cats were gone. As chance would have it, however, the cats came to dance around that apple tree. When a potato suddenly fell out of the woman's basket, the cats took fright and ran away. The next day the man went to look at the spot and found that there was no grass around the apple tree. So the witches came there regularly to dance.
179571: A man coming home at night was ridden by the mare. The faster the man walked, the further he went backwards.
179596: Near a wood in Buken, a stillborn baby had been buried in a garden. After that a little light always appeared in that garden. After the mother of the stillborn baby had asked what the light needed, the light no longer appeared.
179606: A woman who had been married for two years woke up at night because she felt someone tapping her on the shoulder. It was the ghost of a former boyfriend of hers. The ghost asked: "How are you?" Convinced she was dreaming, the woman turned over and went back to sleep. The next night the ghost appeared again at twelve o'clock in his best suit. "You come to me," said the woman, "and I am already married. I can see you are a ghost. Go away." After the woman had prayed the four acts for the repose of the dead man's soul, the ghost disappeared.
179625: When the mayor was coming back at night from a visit to his parents, he saw a figure with a white sheet in the field. The ghost made a lot of noise and made the branches of the trees shake.
179650: A farmhand working for a farmer always met a werewolf when he went to Willebringen. The werewolf sat on a gate and leapt on the farmhand when he passed by.
179672: A soldier from Schoonderbuken always went to the station early in the morning with his wife. On the way the man was followed by a red cat as far as his parents' house. In that house the cat leapt onto the table, the cupboard and into the fruit bowl. The people tied the cat to the table leg and went back to sleep for a while. When they got up, they found the cat lying dead. The animal was buried in a deep pit. The next day the man wanted to know whether the cat was still in the pit. The carcass had disappeared. That must have been the evil hand.
179687: When people went somewhere in the evening, they sometimes thought they saw a returning dead person. There was no way they could get closer to the apparition.
179694: A woman from Brussels had moved to Tremelo after her husband died. Every time the woman came to the house in Brussels, she saw her husband there again. After the woman had her husband's remains moved to Tremelo, the dead man found rest.
179701: A farmer from Meise had made a pact with the devil. The devil would build the farmer a new barn, which had to be finished before the first cockcrow the next morning. The next morning the wife got up very early and struck her clogs together, so that the rooster began to crow too early. The devils then flew away through an opening in the barn. That hole in the barn could never be closed afterwards.
179711: In Essenbeek lived a witch who had fine gooseberries in her garden. When some boys in the woods saw the witch leave, they quickly crept into her garden to pick some berries. The boys each had only three berries in their hands when the witch was already standing beside them, shouting: "You nasty thieves!" Then the boys ran home as fast as they could.
179724: At Christmas three men did not go to Midnight Mass and said: "If only we had a fourth man now, we could play cards. Even if it were the devil from hell!" A fourth man did indeed appear and wanted to join in. When one of the men bent down to pick up a dropped card, he saw that the fourth man had a horse's leg. It was the devil playing cards with them.
179727: In Oetingen lived a woman who often pulled people by the arm or bumped into them. That woman was suspected of being a witch. People who had visited her sometimes believed they had been bewitched.
179737: In Houwaart lived a man who could do magic. He could turn two or three women into a little red creature or cover someone in lice. The man explained that he had learned his magic from a book of spells. When other people tried to read that book, they could not. The man threw the book into the oven, but it would not burn.
179751: A man walking home past the churchyard and the field lost his way. In the end the man sat down somewhere to wait until it got light. The man had fallen victim to someone who had made him lose his way.
179755: Three men were playing cards in an inn. A man who always lost said: "If I can't win my money back, I wish the devil would come and get it!" A little later a gentleman came into the inn. When the innkeeper's wife bent down to pick up a dropped card, she saw that the gentleman had horse's legs. After that the other players always let the disgruntled loser win, so that he had earned his money back. As soon as that had happened, they stopped playing cards.
179767:
A nineteen-year-old girl had gone to the coal merchant to fetch a hundred kilos of coal. The following night, between twelve and one o'clock, the girl became so ill that she could not even get down the stairs. The girl's father told a colleague from Sint-Pieters-Leeuw what was wrong with his daughter. The colleague said: "I'll come by one evening, but you must all be at home." When the man came, he brought prayer cards of Saint Benedict. The family members all had to kneel before the crucifix and make a novena. If someone knocked, they were not allowed to open the door. After that the girl slowly recovered. When the girl had recovered, they wanted to slaughter a fat pig. On the day they meant to do it, the pig suddenly dropped dead. If the man had not put the illness onto the pig, the daughter would have died, and soon after the other children of the family would have fallen ill too.
People believed that a witch had brought the kwade hand (evil hand, witchcraft) upon the girl.
179775: One winter evening people were playing cards in Mazel. But they were one man short. Suddenly a stranger came in and said: "I'll play along". When a player bent down to pick up a dropped card, he saw that the stranger had goat's legs. It was Kledde (a malevolent shape-shifting spirit).
179786: A girl had been bewitched by a woman from the neighbourhood. Every time her brother came back from the coal mine, the girl saw the witch standing at the window. Her father, however, could not see the witch. In the end the girl became so frightened that she had to stay three months in a psychiatric institution in Lovenjoel. When, during that period, the girl's mother was cutting fodder for her rabbits by the roadside, the witch came by to ask how the girl was. The mother replied: "That's none of your business. You've already driven things so far that my daughter is in there, and now you must leave her alone!" The mother had her daughter overlezen (exorcised by prayer) by the White Fathers in Heverlee, after which the girl was cured of her fear.
179789: A poor woman with many children could not manage to finish her work on time. She still had a whole basket of shirts that needed mending. The woman complained to a neighbour whom she did not know was a witch. The neighbour mended the shirts for the woman, who was very happy about it. When the woman's son had put on one of those shirts, he was covered in sores in no time. He went on pilgrimage to Sint-Job, but that did not help. A father overlas (exorcised by prayer) the boy until the sweat rolled down his face. The clergyman said: "The first person who wants to come into your house is the one who is doing you harm." The people had barely got home when they saw the neighbour standing at their threshold. It seemed, however, as if the neighbour was pulled away from the threshold by a strange force. After that day the neighbour no longer showed herself. So nobody doubted that she had caused the evil.
179795: A woman who had been to the fair in Kester with her sister's little child went with the child to Oetingen. When the woman passed the house of a witch, the witch suddenly stood in front of her and said: "What a lovely child!" When the witch took hold of the child, the woman was alarmed. At night the child began to cry incessantly, so that the aunt had to take the child home. The child got a swollen throat. The mother had the child overlezen (exorcised by prayer) by the fathers of Affligem. The child had already been bewitched for six months and could no longer eat or drink. The father who exorcised the child sweated heavily.
179799: In the past people were afraid of black cats because they believed these animals were in reality sorcerers or witches.
179810: A maid was always harassed when she went home in the evening. She believed it was a Walloon, who always came up to her in a lane. The maid was advised to throw her shawl at her attacker's mouth. She followed the advice. A few days later she saw that her boyfriend had the threads of the shawl between his teeth.
179860: In a family in Buggenhout eight children had died. The children died when they were seventeen or eighteen months old. One day the father grabbed a witch by the throat.
179862: A farmer's wife whose animals had all died through the kwade hand (evil hand, witchcraft) went to the little father of Hasselt. The clergyman said to the woman: "Your two brothers are quarrelling. They must forget that quarrel and then the cows will recover. You must also put a medal under the threshold of your house. Then the woman who is causing this evil will no longer be able to come in. This evening your cow will already give a cup of milk. Tomorrow she will low and then she will give some more milk." The farmer's wife did what the father had advised and her cow recovered.
179905: People who had eaten too much and suffered from indigestion at night, causing them to dream, believed they had been ridden by the mare.
179907: On his way to work a man always heard a rustling in the bushes, although no one was to be seen. In the end the man decided to leave for work half an hour later from then on, and after that he no longer heard the rustling.
179913: Witches flew through the air after smearing themselves with a certain substance.
179920: A farmer and his wife could not churn butter and they also often had dead cows in their stable. A father who came to look at the farm said to them: "I think a woman always comes here. You must keep her out." After that the neighbour did not know why she was no longer welcome at the farm.
179923: A bewitched man jumped up from his chair as many as twenty-five times. One day the man crawled into the stove and then went out through the chimney. A while later he came back with an apple tree and three fine apples in his arms. Later the man moved to a wool mill in Antwerp.
179941: When people heard a lot of noise in the house, they believed it was a dead person who had returned to look for his money.
179946: People who had died and had failed to keep a promise during their lifetime came knocking on the windows after their death.
179956: At full moon one could be ridden by the mare (here called the moon). People to whom this had happened were tired and had stiff muscles when they woke in the morning. It was sometimes also said that the mare was a witch who lay down on people.
179971: A man who raised pigs experienced strange things with his animals. At three or four months old, the pigs were smaller than on the day they had been bought. When the floor of the pigsty was broken up, lots of toads were found there.
179978: A farmer was driving a cart of manure behind a patrol of soldiers carrying Napoleon's treasure chest. The soldiers lost the treasure chest and the farmer hid it in his manure cart. The soldiers were all beheaded for losing the treasure chest. The farmer was tormented by fire.
179994: When people could not make butter, they believed they were bewitched. A farmer who always went to Brussels with a woman suspected of being a witch had cows with full udders that nevertheless gave no milk. People believed the butter from those cows was being stolen by the witch.
179999: A farmer's wife had sold her soul to the devil in exchange for a new barn. The barn had to be finished before the rooster had crowed three times. The farmer's wife had got up at three in the night and struck her clogs together, so that the rooster began to crow too early. There was a hole in the barn that had not yet been closed.
180001: A woman could make mice by throwing some sand or earth on the ground.
180053: Witches had to touch children or animals to pass on the evil.
180062: If people heard a crow screech, they believed something bad was going to happen. Crows were witches.
180064: Some men saw will-o'-the-wisps coming towards them in the marshland. When one of the men said: "Come, I will baptise you", hundreds of will-o'-the-wisps suddenly came flying up. The man died on the spot because he could not baptise all the lights. For he should have said: "I baptise you alone".
180075: On a farm there worked a farmhand who played Kledde (a werewolf-like spirit). One day Kledde's skin had been thrown into the oven. A moment later Kledde came running home, all sweaty, to save his skin. After the skin had burnt up, Kledde was glad because he had been released.
180084: A farmer who often fetched hay from a meadow between Hoxem and Meldert often saw a man there walking home behind his cart. People said that the man had been struck by the kwade hand (evil hand, witchcraft). When that man sat down somewhere, he could not get up again unless he was given water.
180128: On a farm in the Beverstraat lived a woman who was said to be a sorceress. When the farmhands came past that place with their horse and cart, the horses could not go on. They believed the sorceress had held the horses back.
180135: A witch could take the shape of any animal except a sheep and a dove. She often appeared as a black cat, a white rabbit or a dog.
180137: A farmer whose harvest had turned out so well that his barn was too small to store it all made a pact with the devil. In exchange for the farmer's soul, the devil would build a barn that would be finished before the first cockcrow the next morning. The farmer had signed a contract with his blood. At night the worried farmer told his wife what he had done. The wife crept out of bed very early and clapped her hands, which made the rooster begin to crow. The next moment the devils stopped working. But there was still a hole in the barn that had to be closed. The hole in the devil's barn could never be closed. That devil's barn stood in the Amelgemstraat between Meise and Oppem (a hamlet of Brussegem).
180138: A man who went down to the cellar one evening to fetch bread saw a witch from the village sitting in front of the cellar window. The witch often knocked on people's shutters to frighten them.
180140: A man always went to work on the farm of a witch. Because the man always got fruit from that witch, he fell ill one day. The man had terrible stomach ache and tossed and turned all night. At night the man heard the dog bark and someone coming up the stairs, although nothing could be seen. The man sent for a White Father, but he could not help him because the witchcraft had already gone too far. To find out who was guilty, the people had to boil the sick man's underwear. The next day the witch would have burns all over. That is how they discovered that the woman the man worked for was guilty. The father had put a piece of the 'hagelkaars' (?) under the threshold. When the witch came by to ask how the sick man was, she could not get in. In the end the man died. That witch caused four other people to die by giving them fruit.
180141: A woman lost two fingers through witchcraft. Only when the woman had been on pilgrimage to Sint-Truiden did the misfortune end.
180155: A man was coming back from Oudergem through the woods around midnight. Suddenly the lamps on the Avenue Tervuren went out, so that the man could hardly find his way. The man walked towards a glow of light that he thought was the edge of the woods. As he walked on, he saw that the light came from a castle. Yet he had never seen a castle in that area. The man walked towards the castle and noticed that a mass of cats was also heading that way. The cats were not behaving normally and were jumping over each other. The man saw that he would not get home that way and walked in another direction. Wherever he went, he always ended up back at the castle. At the moment the man heard a church bell ringing in the distance, the castle and the cats suddenly vanished. The man could suddenly find his way again, and he was already on the road to his house.
180158:
A mother from Vissenaken lost all her children just after birth. When the woman was pregnant again, her husband was advised by the parish priest not to let anyone into the room. The man had to strike the first thing he saw.
The man followed the advice and kept the room shut. When he stood in front of his house, he saw a fat toad crawl out of the drainpipe and hit it with a piece of wood. That day the man's mother-in-law lay in bed with a broken shoulder. She was the witch who had caused the misfortune in the house. The children born after that survived.
180190: During catechism class a little boy from Halle made white mice by throwing the sand he had in his pocket on the ground. When the priest had seen this, he took the boy behind the altar and baptised him again there.
180193: A man was on the road with his horse and cart. When a witch had jumped onto the cart, the horse suddenly stood still.
180215: A chicken dealer was taking chickens to the Brussels market with his dog cart (1). When the man was on the Steenweg to Merchtem, he suddenly saw a small mouse running. The man stamped on the ground a few times, after which the mouse crept into a cellar hole. The next moment a window opened upstairs in that house. A witch appeared and asked: "Sir, did that mouse run into my cellar hole?" The chicken seller was terrified and drove on.
180231: In Blanden lived a child who could make white mice appear by laying little balls of mud on the ground. After the child had been baptised again, it had lost its magic power.
180235: A woman going to mass in the morning suddenly lost her bearings and got lost. That woman had been ridden by the mare.
180265: A girl from Wemmel worked as a seamstress at the IJzerkasteel near the Driesstraat and the Robberechtsstraat. In the evening the girl was always picked up by her mother. When the two walked home, they often saw a zwarte madam (black lady) walking back and forth by the wall around the castle park. It was a woman dressed entirely in black and wearing a shawl. People believed that this black lady was a witch.
180266: A celebration was being held in Kortrijk for the kermis (village fair). Suddenly a crowd of sorceresses appeared and began to dance there. The people stepped aside in fear, until one of them called out: "All of you, keep still." That person made the sign of the cross three times and said: "God bless you!" Then the witches began to scream, and a moment later they vanished.
180272: Sometimes it happened that someone had struck at a cat and the next day met a person who had a wound.
180273: Near the Mollendaalbos a farmer had one night moved one of the boundary posts of his field to have more land. After his death the farmer had to haunt. The ghost could be heard calling all the time: "Post, post, post. I carry you where I want". When Fee came back drunk one evening from the fair in Opvelp, he answered: "Damn it, put it where you got it!" Since that night there has never been any haunting at the Mollendaalbos again.
180293: Kludde (a werewolf-like spirit) with his chain often had himself carried by passers-by. One day people managed to throw Kludde's animal skin into the oven. When that had happened, Kludde came running, saying: "If I had found even one hair of it, you would have been dead!"
180300: A man who had to carry the werewolf was so frightened that he bit his nails. He was even left with lasting effects from the fright he had suffered.
180324: A witch constantly tormented her daughter-in-law. Because of this the poor woman often felt unwell. When the woman took her husband's arm, she instantly felt better. The witch did not want to harm her own son. Moreover, the witch knew that her son was stronger than she was. It was especially soft-hearted people who always tried to do good for everyone who fell prey to witches. The witch's granddaughter always knew in advance when something bad would happen. Such disasters usually happened on her birthday.
180329: A farmhand had a skin with which he had to roam about at night as kleudde (a werewolf-like spirit). In the morning the farmhand was therefore terribly tired. The farmer went to the priest for advice. The clergyman advised the farmer to burn the farmhand's skin in the oven. The farmer sent his farmhand to Wallonië to fetch coal. Meanwhile the farmer made a fire in his oven. As soon as the skin had caught fire, the farmhand was already standing by the oven to save his skin. When the skin had burnt up, the farmhand cried out in relief: "Now I am saved."
180330: A bewitched woman from Sint-Martens-Lennik had herself overlezen (exorcised by prayer) by the mission fathers.
180333: People believed that will-o'-the-wisps were the souls of the dead who had to go to purgatory because they had committed small sins. A man who had seen will-o'-the-wisps by the wood one evening went back to the spot the next day. He found burnt specks of dust there. Whoever found such specks had to pray for the souls in the evening, or he would not be able to sleep because his conscience was not clear.
180351: The beguinage of Zoutleeuw was haunted. Farmer Jan saw the ghost early in the morning while it was still dark. Jan thought the beguine said: "I am still a beguine and turn my wheel so wondrous fine". Jan, holding his revolver, cried out in fright: "Get away or I'll shoot!" The ghost answered: "Who will stop me setting my little wheel down here? A hundred years ago I spun this court and with this wheel I earned my bread." Jan said to the apparition: "I want to know who you are, where you come from and what you are doing here!" The beguine answered: "In this ground I hid my purse. I'll keep looking for it, even if it takes till tomorrow." Jan struck at the beguine with a stick, and she fell over. The next day a bundle of black clothes and a sheaf of straw in the shape of a person were found at that spot. A little further on lay an old spinning wheel with the following text: "Who will stop me setting my little wheel down here, I am still an old beguine and turn my wheel so wondrous fine. A hundred years ago I spun this court and with this wheel I earned my bread. Oh Lord, where is my old cell now? It has been torn down, I thought as much. In this ground I hid my purse, I'll keep looking for it here even if it takes till tomorrow. I would gladly find my old coins, perhaps they now lie outside here. If I don't find them in this ground, then you may look for them, or else they're the dog's."
180353: A woman had been bewitched by a fat maar (witch), who made her dry up completely. The people sent for the fathers, but the power of the kwade hand (evil hand, witchcraft) had already grown too strong. A few days later the woman was dead.
180365: Some men driving a cart to market saw lots of cats on the way jumping from one tree to another. The horse was so frightened of the cats that the animal panicked and ran into the canal.
180369: On a farm, every two weeks a goat standing under a hole in the ceiling fell ill. The people went to a fortune teller, who had a vision of a man and a girl. The fortune teller asked whether the people had not forgotten to make a promised pilgrimage. The farmer's wife explained that she had kept all her promises. When the goat later recovered by itself, the people attributed the incident to the kwade hand (evil hand, witchcraft).
180393: A man who lived with a witch had terribly long nails and his wife would not let him cut them. The tears were often seen rolling down the man's cheeks.
180401: Witches could turn themselves into cats. Those black cats pestered people and would not be chased away.
180444: A mother out walking with her baby met a woman, who said: "May I hold that baby?" The next day the baby fell ill and that night it died. Before the parents had told anyone their child was dead, the witch went to the neighbours to say that the baby had died. So the witch knew the news before anyone had told her.
180461: A man from Helen who went ferreting at night saw a horse coming along the road. The horse flew through a hedge and ended up against a gate a bit further on.
180472: After his death, Evelien's father came back as a ghost that knocked on the window all the time. The family still had to make a great pilgrimage so that the dead man would find rest.
180489: A man was playing cards in an inn. Everyone found it strange that he always won. One evening another player, picking up a dropped card, found that the man had cow's feet. The man stood up and made the sign of the cross. After that the man who always won had disappeared. Everyone now knew he was the devil.
180500: In Nieuwrode, lodder (a mischievous spirit that jumps on people's backs) was often seen at night, so that people no longer dared to go outside for fear of having to carry the tormenting spirit. A man once had to carry lodder at 't Rot. Another man had managed to make lodder bleed, at which the spirit cried: "What have you done! I only had to roam for ten more years and then I would have been released. Now I have to go to the seaside again for ninety-nine years."
180522: If you could make a werewolf bleed, he took on his human form and you could recognise him.
180533: A woman grew very thin because she was always ridden by the mare at night. When the woman placed her clogs with the heels pointing towards the bed, she was freed from the mare.
180542: After her master had died, a housekeeper heard someone coming down the stairs every evening, although nothing could be seen. One evening three people approached the ghost and asked: "What do you need? Just say it now." Then a voice was heard answering: "They must still go to Scherpenheuvel with nine people." When this had been done, the housekeeper no longer heard the ghost. The man was in heaven.
180544:
A mother with a three-month-old child was visited every week by someone peddling wool and laces. Every week the mother bought something from the peddler, although people had often warned her about that woman. One day the mother bought a little bonnet for her baby from the peddler. The mother could not pay the exact amount and the peddler could not give change. The peddler said: "Never mind, I come here every week anyway." The mother would rather have paid, but because the peddler had no change, she had to wait until the following week. The next day the mother went with her baby to visit her own mother. The baby had barely got the new bonnet on its head when it had convulsions. The woman panicked and stayed home. After she had taken off the bonnet, the child calmed down again. That evening the baby began to cry as if it were in pain. The crying went on for many days, weeks and even months. The woman had already taken the child to the doctor, but he could not help. In the end people believed the child had been struck by the kwade hand (evil hand, witchcraft). When the child had grown very thin, the mother went to the fathers at the beguinage of Laken. "Oh madam, there's nothing more to be done," the fathers said. Then the mother went to the fathers of Dendermonde. There a clergyman said: "No, it has gone too far. That will be a little angel for heaven." The woman was at her wits' end until someone advised her to go to a father in Zemst-Laar. Although that father had no hope either, the mother begged him to overlezen (exorcise by prayer) the child just once. The father began to pray until he was drenched in sweat. The mother had to pray at the same time. On her way home the woman had to keep praying until she had closed the door behind her. If she heard a bird call anywhere, she must not look back. When the mother got home, the baby was asleep. The child slept for two days and nights in a row, so that people thought it was dead. After that the child was carefully given food. After six months it was cured. The child grew up to be a strapping man who lived to 78.
The mother was convinced that the peddler was a witch.
180548: A man from Rumsdorp who went to Halle always saw a werewolf on the way, following close on his heels. One day the man managed to stab the werewolf with a small dung fork, so that the beast began to bleed. Then the man found that the werewolf was his best friend, who had wanted to protect him on the way. The werewolf said to the man: "Now I have to start my ten-year term all over again!" Werewolves were men who consorted with evil.
180560: A farmer's wife who was churning butter was visited by a neighbour, who asked: "Are you churning?" The farmer's wife answered: "Yes, but I'm not getting any butter." The neighbour replied: "That's because you don't know how" and began turning the churn herself. Five minutes later there was butter in the churn.
180562: A farmer's wife lived next to a woman suspected of being a witch. Because the farmer's wife often helped her neighbour pick fodder for the animals, she often got a wheelbarrow of fodder from her. The farmer's wife never noticed that her neighbour was supposedly a witch. She did not have much luck in her stable, though. She had to sell her last cow because it would no longer get in calf.
180564: A witch could turn herself into an animal.
180569: People who were ridden by the 'moon' (the mare) had a nightmare.
180571: On a bewitched farm that had much misfortune, people shot at a cat that often came past. The next day a neighbour woman lay in bed because she had lost her leg.
180573: People believed that witches had difficulty dying. About a suspected woman from Oudenaken people said: "I'm curious whether she'll ever die." The woman died after being kicked by a cow. That woman did not pass her magic power on to anyone else.
180582: A man from Essenbeek often visited his girlfriend. When the man went home at around half past eleven, he saw by the church of Essenbeek a dog as big as a calf. The animal's eyes looked like two lanterns. When the man had to pass the dog, he quickly said a prayer. At that the dog went to sit in the ditch to let the man through. The man was terrified when he reached his house.
180584: If thirteen people sat at table together, it was believed that one person from that company would die within the year.
180590:
There was haunting at a crossroads by a lime tree. Many people did not dare to walk past the lime tree at the Toren. There was also a crossroads there.
The witches gathered at a crossroads between twelve and one o'clock. Afterwards they flew away on a broomstick.
180600: In a family with sixteen children, one of the children fell ill. They took the child to a doctor and to a quack. The quack said that the child was bewitched and that the wizard or witch would come to visit within twenty-four hours. A while later an ugly woman came to visit, who had the habit of peering under the curtains. That woman was given a thrashing by the child's father.
180602: A woman fell victim to the kwade hand (evil hand, witchcraft) after someone had patted her on the shoulder.
180634:
A poor woman from Oudenaken whose six- or seven-year-old daughter was ill believed the child had been bewitched. The woman went to the Capuchins in Brussels for the child and was given a prayer. She also had to pray a novena. Before those nine days were over, all the family members had to go to confession and take communion. A woman would also come by to ask for something. That woman was not to be let in. A broom had to be laid across the threshold so the woman could not come in. A neighbour did indeed come to visit, and she could not get in. Because the child's condition did not improve, the woman went with her daughter to the parish priest of Elingen. The child could not be cured, however, for it had tuberculosis! In those days people did not know such diseases.
In fact the priests and fathers themselves encouraged superstition by accusing certain people of the evil people were faced with.
180642: A house in Miskom was rented to a woman of English descent. A painter from the area staged ghostly scenes in that house. At night the plates and glasses could be heard rattling. In the morning everything was back in its place. The painter worked together with a man who lived near the house in Miskom.
180645: A pigeon fancier had been visited by two men from Aalst who wanted to buy a pigeon from him. The buyers had had to make do with a pigeon they did not really want. So they bewitched the pigeon loft, which in no time was full of lice and fleas. The pigeon fancier's wife went to Affligem and had to do a nine-day penance. During that time she was not allowed to lend anything to anyone. So when an old woman came to ask for a tar can, the woman refused. After that things improved.
180653: In Oppem (Brussegem) there stood a barn that was called 'the devil's barn'. In that barn was a hole that could not be closed.
180662: A meeting of Freemasons was held in a café. A Catholic man came into the café to eat. Before he began eating, he made the sign of the cross. At that, one of the Freemasons became very restless. Those present suddenly saw that he had a tail and goat's legs. The Freemason ran off and kicked the door shut with his hoof. The door with the devil's hoofprint is said to still be on display in some museum.
180672: A woman had arranged with a friend to go to the early market in the morning. When her husband woke her, she could not answer because she was being ridden by the mare. When the woman finally got out of bed to open the door, her face was covered in blood.
180676: A witch tormented her daughter-in-law, so that the poor woman often felt ill and had the feeling she was being strangled. The witch's husband died in a similar way; he too had the feeling that someone was strangling him. A witch had to kill someone every year, otherwise she had to harm her own children.
180711: In a house between Kerkom and Boutersem lived a woman whose mother had died. The woman had promised to go on pilgrimage for her mother, but she had forgotten her promise. After her death the grandmother came to haunt. The next day the family, nine people in all, went to Scherpenheuvel. Since then the ghost has not been seen again.
180720: A woman with blonde curls fell victim to a witch who had filled her head with lice.
180743: It was said that a woman often rode around on a sow near the convent in Rotselaar.
180769: A farmhand had hidden a skin in a tree, with which he had to roam about as a werewolf. When it was discovered that the farmhand was a werewolf, the tree with the skin was set on fire. The farmhand, who was working somewhere at that moment, sensed instinctively that something was wrong and hurried to the tree. He had to be tied up until the skin had burnt up and he was saved.
180771: People who were ridden by the 'maal' (the mare) had a tight feeling around the heart.
180779: A farmer who had already lost twelve cows went to the friars. The clergymen said: "Under the cow you will find a toad. You must hold it in the fire for a moment, but not burn it." The man followed the advice. Afterwards he saw a woman in the street who was completely burnt. Because nobody wanted to take over the witch's magic power, it was passed on to an animal.
180802: In one house three children had died within the space of one hour. In the evening the children fell ill and at night they had convulsions. When the mother was pregnant again, she went to have herself read over by the fathers of Affligem. The priest sweated terribly as he sat praying. Then he said to the woman: "Madam, when your child is born and it is a girl, she must always wear blue clothes for three years. This misfortune is being done to you by a woman. I will give you something to put under your threshold and then you will see who that woman is, for she will no longer be able to enter your house." The woman gave birth to a daughter and always dressed the child in blue for three years. Shortly after the birth a woman came asking for milk. She lifted her leg a good fifteen times, but she could not step over the threshold. After that the woman never visited again.
180819: A mother and her four-year-old daughter met a maar (nightmare spirit). For the next eight days the mother had nothing but trouble with her child. The girl was eaten up by hair worms. In the end the child died. The mother then had her house read over by the parish priest.
180820: A man returning from Hoegaarden saw a woman from the village sitting by the roadside. The woman had been cutting fodder for her rabbits and asked the man whether he would carry her sack. Although the woman had a bad name, the man agreed. When he got home, the man found that he was covered in lice. His mother even had to throw away all his clothes.
180828: A man returning from Orsmaal, where he had gone to play cards, was soaking wet when he got home. On the way, in Dung, he had seen his mother standing there; she grabbed him and threw him into the pulp tank twice. The man's mother was suspected of being a witch. When he got home the man saw his mother lying in her bed, but he shouted, "Damn it, filthy woman!"
180834: A farmer had a daughter who worked as a maid in Wallonië. One day the daughter came home deathly ill. The girl had slept with a farmer's son. Among her clothes a black skin was found. The priest claimed it was a real devil's skin. The clergyman advised the farmer's wife to burn the skin when she baked bread. When the skin lay in the fire, cursing was heard in French, Spanish and German. After the skin had burnt up, the farmer's wife found that her bread had disappeared from the oven. The farmer's wife walked around the oven three times and prayed three Our Fathers. Then the bread was back. The girl, however, wasted away completely and in the end she died.
180846: If people heard ravens screeching, they believed misfortune was coming.
180890: A girl was coming back from the fair with a boy. On the way the boy said: "I'm going into the woods for a moment. If you see anything, don't be afraid." When a little later the girl saw a bear come out of the woods, she threw her handkerchief into the beast's jaws. A little later the boy came back. The girl noticed that he had the threads of the handkerchief between his teeth. The girl ran home as fast as she could. She never saw the boy again.
180895: A man went on pilgrimage with a sick child to the parish priest of Elingen to have the child exorcised. When the man had to pass the house of a sorceress with his horse and cart, he could not go on. Some time later the man went again, but this time on foot. The sorceress came outside and said: "You have been."
180901: A cat that rubbed against someone's legs was a witch.
180910: Some people were visited by a man peddling rat poison. Because the people bought nothing, the peddler said: "Just wait, next week you'll be eaten by the rats!" That very night the people already had a real plague of rats. After the friars had read prayers over them, the rats immediately disappeared.
180911: A man who was afraid of nothing went at midnight to the little chapel of Sint-Anna because a hare had been seen there. When the man wanted to shoot at the hare between twelve and one o'clock, the animal grew so big that the man fainted with fright.
180919: A farmer had told a woman that she was not allowed to harvest. The woman had replied: "You're not off the field yet." A little later the farmer indeed could not get off his field because his horse stood still.
180935: A woman who had already lost four children believed the evil hand had something to do with it. When her two other children also fell ill, she sent for a priest. On entering the house the priest was immediately held back, so he knew he was dealing with the evil hand. He began to pray and said: "For the boy it will be too late, but the girl I will save." The little boy died during the night, but his sister recovered. After that the children in that house grew up healthy.
180938: A witch who had learned her magic from her husband made a little boy ill. But there were women who were much stronger than witches and could undo the harm done in this way.
180947: If farmers had taken their cow to be bred and met a sorceress on the way home, they knew their cow would not be in calf.
180959: On a farm the cows were untied in the stable at night. A girl also died on that farm. When her pillowcase was shaken out, everything inside it was found to be blood red. The evil hand was on that farm.
181004: A woman who had been bedridden for years could suddenly walk again after her mother died. If sorceresses could find no other victim, they had to bewitch people from their own family.
181020: If a sorceress passed by while wheat was being sown, all the wheat turned black.
181062: On a farm no butter could be made. A neighbour woman who often came to the farm was suspected of having bewitched the butter. After the farmer's wife had been to the fathers of Affligem and the fathers of Ghent and had done penance, she could make butter again.
181070: In the churchyard a returning dead person could sometimes be seen appearing. When people saw such an apparition, they were very frightened.
181085: A man who had been touched by the evil hand sometimes drove his cart into the Demer through the witch's doing. No one could get the man out of the water. If you had been touched by a witch, you had to strike her on the head with your left hand at once to make her powerless.
181125: A man often went to a house nearby that stood at a crossroads. By that house stood a tree stump that was said to chew the cud.
181131: An unbelieving farmer who wanted to bring in his harvest needed a bigger barn and so made a pact with the devil. The devil had to finish the new barn before the first cockcrow. But the rooster had crowed too early, so the devil had to flee. There was still a hole in the barn, which could never be closed.
181138: One day a superstitious man from Wieze went to a fortune teller to have his future told. The fortune teller said the man should beware of white horses, because a white horse would be the cause of his death. Whenever the man saw a white horse somewhere, he always fled quickly into a house. When the man saw a horse coming again on a summer's day, however, he had no chance to get into a house. So the man went into an inn instead. As he set his foot over the threshold, the inn's signboard fell on his head. The man was killed on the spot. The signboard read: 'The White Horse'.
181141: On a farm in Strijtem all the doors flew open at midnight. The people had a friar come, but the clergyman could not help.
181187: In Zepperen it had not rained for six weeks. One morning a witch from the village came walking along with an umbrella in her hand, although the sky was still clear blue. A man who saw the witch said laughing: "Are you going to make rain, since you've brought your umbrella?" The witch replied: "It will rain soon enough". That same evening it rained terribly. The next day the man was covered in lice.
181208: A woman walked past a field with a horse in it and said to the person with her: "Shall I make that horse come over here?" The woman had a carrot in her hand, and the horse came running at once. After that nothing could be done with that horse.
181209: Pretty young girls were never suspected of witchcraft. It was always old women, whom everyone avoided. In Bogaarden lived a woman who behaved strangely and was therefore suspected of witchcraft. That sorceress always lingered near pregnant women going to mass on Sunday.
181229: People who had misfortune believed they had been ridden by the mare.
181245: A man was returning at night from visiting his girlfriend in Gelrode. On the way he met a woman carrying a bundle, who asked him to carry it for a while because she was tired. The man took the package, wrapped in a cloth. It was extremely heavy. At another road the man suddenly saw that the woman had vanished. He threw the bundle on the ground and ran away. The whole time he heard revolver shots. That was witchcraft.
181262: If you had pointed at a stallicht (will-o'-the-wisp), the light came and struck the door. A man taking clover to Brussels saw the stallichten sitting by the side of the road. Such lights were the souls of children who had no rest because they had not been baptised. If you said: "I baptise you in the name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit, Amen," the stallichten could kill you. You had to say: "I baptise you alone in the name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit." Stallichten always moved back and forth.
181267: People with some kind of disability were said to have been bewitched by a woman. A pregnant woman did not dare walk past the house of a possible sorceress for fear of being bewitched, so that her child would not be born healthy.
181291: The mare lived in the woods. People who were ridden by the mare were crushed flat. To keep the mare away, people hung mistletoe in the stable.
181321:
An eighteen-year-old girl from Huizingen who had fallen ill saw every night around one o'clock an apparition with a long sword, which said: "In a day or two it will be your last night." Whenever the girl saw the apparition, she asked her eleven-year-old sister, who slept with her, to turn her over. After the sister had done so, the apparition was gone. The girl's parents sent for a priest from Sint-Lambrechts-Woluwe to read prayers over the girl. When the priest came to the hill where the girl lived, he began to sweat and had the greatest difficulty reaching her. For he was right at the spot where the witch lived who had caused the evil. After his intervention the priest said: "Something must die." He then put the evil onto a pig in the stable. The next day the sow lay dead. The girl was cured. However, she was never again allowed to go about without carrying a medal of Saint Benedict.
One day, though, the girl forgot to pin a medal to her clothes. When she was almost home, she was attacked by a big black cat. After that the girl fell ill again. As she lay in bed, she saw a woman appear and heard bells ringing. A voice said: "Do you hear the bells ringing? In three days they will ring for you!" The girl had been bewitched at the moment she bought a house that a witch had wanted to buy. Because the girl was not wearing a medal then, the witch got her in her power. The first bewitchment, in the girl's youth, had been meant for her father, but because he was too strong he had escaped it, and the evil hand had fallen on the daughter.
181329: People believed that witches could make animals and children ill.
181347: In Schaffen a witch had covered a man in lice, not knowing that the man also had special powers. The man said to the bystanders: "That witch has given me lice, but before she is two hundred metres further on, she'll have the lice herself." Later the man's house burned down. All his books were destroyed in the fire.
181356: Stalkaarsen (will-o'-the-wisps) were lights that descended on the churchyard at All Saints. Some stalkaarsen called out the name of a dead person.
181376: On a farm the horses rode around at night. The grain mill started working by itself and there were cats all over the roof. The cows' tails were tied together. All of this was the work of a witch. One night the witch flew around on her pig. A farmer on the road with his horse suddenly could not go on. Suddenly the witch came up to him and said: "Go and stand by your horse, I'll push." A few seconds later the horse started moving.
181409: A woman who could not make butter was visited by a witch, who said: "Can't you make butter? I see you're churning." The woman answered: "No, I can't churn butter." The witch replied: "Let me try. If I push a few times, you'll have butter. But then you must give me half a kilo." After the witch had worked the churn, there was indeed butter at once. So it became the custom always to give the witch a pound of butter. But when at some point the witch no longer got butter, she said: "Ah, I don't get butter any more. I'll know where to find you!" From then on the people could no longer make butter.
181415: In the old days old women were often suspected of being witches. Sickly children were said to have been struck by the evil hand.
181427: A farmer's wife did not know why her animals were always being tormented. After a while she found that money was always being stolen from her. If she had put her money under her pillow, in the morning it was gone, although she had seen or heard nothing. In the end the woman went to a priest.
181433: A man who had not been baptised properly could make white mice by throwing some sandy loam on the ground in front of him.
181452: An innkeeper went eel fishing. Because a black cat kept running off with his eel, the man ran home angrily. When he got home he saw his mother sitting there panting as if she too had been running hard. She had turned herself into a black cat.
181459: A white figure always sat on a gate bar in a meadow in Geetbets. It was a witch who chased people away. If someone asked the witch something, she did not answer but vanished.
181462: On a farm butter could no longer be churned after a certain woman had visited.
181480: A rural policeman who had gone for a drink by the church of Kapelle one evening was walking home. On the way, near the castle, he suddenly saw a white lady emerge from behind a hedge. The apparition always walked about five metres ahead of the man. If the man stopped, the white lady stopped too. When he got home, the man said to the apparition: "Stay there a moment" and went inside to fetch his hunting rifle. But when he came back out, the white lady had disappeared.
181483: In Oplinter there was a child that cried incessantly. The father said the child had been struck by the evil hand and suspected his sister of having bewitched it. When his sister came to visit again, the man stood ready with an axe to cut off her head. He threatened his sister, who then went to the cradle. At that moment the child stopped crying.
181487: On a farm in Tienen a ghost always came knocking on the walls at night. One day someone asked the ghost what it wanted. The dead farmer said that he had promised to have candles burned in the 'grotteke' (little grotto). In the end this had to be done for him.
181491: In Halle there was a bewitched farm. In the evenings cats crept under the gate of that farm. The foal in the stable always began running at midnight for an hour. At one o'clock the foal shivered and lay down next to the horse. The farmer then had to rub it dry because it was drenched in sweat. The farmer went to the fathers of Sint-Truiden, who said: "That foal may be possessed by the devil. We'll come and see." When the foal began running at midnight, the priest sat alone in the stable and prayed until the sweat rolled down his face. After half an hour the foal began to slow down. After three quarters of an hour it stood stock-still and then dropped dead. The foal had not survived the exorcism. But the priest said to the farmer: "You must be careful, for the devil is still here. He is brought here by someone from the neighbourhood who often comes near your animals. Think about who that could be, for this can have very serious consequences." After long thought the farmer named a neighbour woman. When that woman was kneading bread dough, she would sometimes stand speechless, and then a bumblebee flew out of her mouth. The bumblebee then flew around bewitching people and animals. The priest gave the farmer a relic to put under the threshold. When the neighbour came by that evening, she could not get over the threshold. She began to curse and went home. After that the farmer had no more trouble in his stable.
181526: A man who was ridden by the mare got lost. When the man had ended up in a brook, he decided to knock on a door somewhere and ask the way. That is how the man managed to get back to his village after all.
181532: Near Bierbeek lived a poor little woman whose husband made her spin all day long. When the woman died, she was buried in a shift that had only one sleeve. After her death the woman came back to haunt. The ghost sat down at the spinning wheel and said: "Oh dear, oh dear, I always have to spin and then I only get a shift with one sleeve."
181535:
A farmer's wife had a cow that had just calved and gave forty litres of milk every day. One day, as she was milking, a witch came and stood at the door and said: "What a cow and what an udder! She must give a lot of milk!" But the next day the cow gave almost no milk. The vet came and asked whether anyone had been in the stable. When the people told him about the woman who had come to look, the vet said: "Then I know enough. You have been bewitched."
In Baal lived a woman who could lift witchcraft by reading backwards. She also gave people a stone to put under the threshold of their stable door, so that the witch could no longer enter the stable. If the woman came to visit again, they were not to invite her in. A few days later the witch did indeed come by. When they asked, "What have you come for?", the woman answered: "I thought I'd come and look at your fine cow, but I can't quite get over the threshold."
The next day the cow again gave forty litres of milk.
181543: People who were ridden by the mare felt as if they were going to die. To protect yourself against the mare, you had to turn your clogs upside down beside the bed.
181553: When V.H.'s father-in-law came back drunk from the fair in Lebbeke, he heard someone calling: "Posts moved, posts moved". The drunkard cursed and answered: "Put them where you stole them!" The next moment the ghost had vanished.
181578: When Pie L. was going to the Motte, he saw on the way a will-o'-the-wisp coming towards him that asked to be baptised. The next moment a hundred will-o'-the-wisps came flying up. Pie got away as fast as he could.
181579: In a cowshed someone was secretly milking the cows. The farmer believed witchcraft was involved.
181580: People who had got lost believed they had been ridden by the mare. A man from the Verbrande Brug who was coming back in the dark from a visit to his girlfriend got lost near the Lintstraat and the Kerkhofstraat. That man also believed he had fallen victim to the mare.
181585:
When a man married, he had to let go of the wedding ring he slid onto his bride's finger as quickly as possible. For as long as the man held that ring, the witches sitting in the church could ruin his life.
Witches could be recognised by crossing their footprints.
181604: Through the doing of sorceresses a man had already lost two little sons at the age of a few weeks or months. In the end he went to the doctor and to the parish priest of Vollezele, after which the misfortune ended.
181608: A man claimed that he was ridden by the 'moon' (the mare). When it came, the man heard a thumping on the stairs.
181617: If you pointed at a stalkaars (will-o'-the-wisp), the light came and sat on your hand. It was often said that stalkaarsen were lost souls for whom no one prayed.
181635: Sorceresses could make children cry incessantly.
181665: If you saw a black cat running ahead of you on the highway, you could not go on. Such a black cat was in fact a witch.
181671: Two brothers coming back from the fair in Bost saw a little blue light along the way, by the road to Zoutleeuw. It was a will-o'-the-wisp. It was said that will-o'-the-wisps were the souls of unbaptised children.
181672: The end of the world is near. According to the Protestant Bible, this can be deduced from omens such as wars, floods and disasters. According to the Bible, a witch was someone who consorted with the devil and could change into the shape of an animal.
181721: Stallichten (will-o'-the-wisps) were the souls of unbaptised children who floated about at night. They were souls that wandered because they could go neither to heaven, hell nor purgatory. If you pointed at a stallicht, you went blind.
181762: A little boy had been bewitched after a woman took his dummy and put it in her mouth. The parents took the child to a doctor and then to a pendulum diviner. The diviner told them: "Go to the fathers quickly, or the child will die." The people had their child read over by the fathers of Tongerlo. As soon as that was done, the child crawled around the church full of energy.
181763:
The dead could only be made to return if the family had not grown larger.
When one day a dead person who had returned was asked what the hereafter looked like, the dead person answered: "They keep strict accounts there and they forgive nothing".
181772: A cattle dealer from Sint-Truiden had to come back and haunt after his death.
181773: 'Ridden by the mare' was an expression people used.
181774: A farmer from Halle wanted a new barn, but he had no money to pay for it. One day the devil came to the farmer and said: "If you sell me your soul, I will build you a barn that will be finished before the rooster crows at three tomorrow morning." The farmer agreed to the proposal, but he was still a little afraid. At night the man told his wife what he had done. The wife got up at once and ran to the henhouse, where she began to beat and kick the roosters, so that the animals immediately began to crow. The barn was not yet finished at that moment, so the farmer got to keep his soul. That barn on the Kapelveld was called 'the blue barn'.
181780: A family from Aarschot had a little son who was often ill. They had already taken the child to Scherpenheuvel and consulted doctors. Since none of this had helped much, they took the child to a man known as a sorcerer. The sorcerer found that the boy had been bewitched by a neighbour woman who passed by every day and stroked the child's head. The parents were advised to put a nail from the Easter candle under their threshold. When the neighbour came by, they must never say, "Come in." The woman would not come in of her own accord. After that the little boy recovered.
181784: In one family several children had already died young. The people went on pilgrimage to the fathers of Dendermonde. One of the fathers said the children were being bewitched by their own mother.
181787: A man saw a piglet running towards him in the moonlight. The man tried to grab the piglet, but missed. When the man looked around, there was nothing to be seen.
181815: Sorceresses could bewitch people, for example by giving them milk. In Bever there lived two children who had become skin and bone through witchcraft.
181820: A man who always saw strange apparitions in a walnut tree went on pilgrimage to the Antoinists (1) in Ecaussines (2). Those people believed that the dead came back in the shape of an animal.
181831: A woman had slept restlessly for several nights because she always heard or saw something. Her husband advised her to pray before going to sleep. One night after eleven o'clock the woman heard a bang. She saw an old woman come in through the window, grab the bedside table and sit down with her back to the bed. The woman wanted to call her husband, but no sound came from her throat. When she began to pray, the sorceress vanished. After the woman hung a little bag of powder she had received from the witheren (Premonstratensian canons) at the window, the strange old woman did not appear again.
181833: Lubbeek used to swarm with sorcerers. These people owned books from which they learned magic. The priest knew who the sorcerers were. When one of them had died, the priest hurried to the house to collect the books and hide them in the attic of the presbytery. One day a servant working at the presbytery found those books of magic. The servant was careless and could no longer stop the magic. In no time all of Lubbeek was full of white mice. No one ever knew how the priest resolved the matter.
181838: The procession of Hakendover could not take place because the weather was bad. So only a short round was made in Hakendover. Afterwards it was found that the statue of Christ in the church had a big clump of mud on his robe. Since that event the procession has always been held, even in bad weather.
181849: A man coming home from work in the dark at night met something on the way that looked like a dog. The man quickly threw his red handkerchief at the beast. The dog unravelled the handkerchief completely. The next day in the village the man saw someone walking about with the red threads of the handkerchief between his teeth. The man never dared tell anyone who the werewolf was.
181854: Every week a woman was visited by a beggar woman who came for bread. One day, when the beggar woman did not get her bread quickly enough, she grabbed the leg of the child the woman was holding in her arms. A little later the child's leg was full of lice. The people went to the Crosier Fathers to have prayers read over the child. But the clergymen said it was nothing serious and that anyone could get lice. They advised the people to go to the chemist. With the ointment they got from the chemist, the child was rid of the lice.
181856: One morning at a house a little heap of sand was found on a bench. The sand had been pressed into a cylinder shape with an upturned glass. But the woman living in the house had no glass that fitted it. She had seen a glow in the room during the night, but no person.
181861: On the way back from the fair in Pamel, a man was given a mattentaart (curd tart) by a woman in an inn. The tart was meant for his children, but the man got hungry on the way and ate it himself. A week later the man had problems. His eyesight deteriorated so badly that he was in danger of going blind. He had himself read over by someone from Brussels and was cured of his ailment. People believed he had been bewitched by eating the tart.
181874: A white goat that could work magic always got under people's feet in Zemst. People kicked at the goat, but they missed. Because the goat gave off light in the dark, people were inclined to follow the animal, and so they lost their way.
181879: A man going to Sint-Truiden stopped at a café on the way for a drink. The landlady turned out to know the man's name. The man asked: "But woman, how do you know me?", and the woman answered: "I've known you for fifty years! I've sat often enough with a whole group in the walnut tree by your house!" If people put their dirty laundry outside with some food, the laundry was done the next morning. If they left dirty plates, they found them clean again. If they put out clean plates, they found them dirty.
181900: A man had been bewitched after lending coffee to a neighbour woman, although he had too little himself. He should not have done that. The fathers advised him never to lend that woman anything again. When the man went to town on a Friday, the woman asked him to bring her back some tobacco. The man refused. After that he had to pray for nine days with his whole family. During that time there were several knocks at the door and the light was put out.
181906: In Oppem-Brussegem the devils had built a barn for a farmer. Because there was still a hole in the barn when the rooster first crowed, the devils had to flee and the farmer got to keep his soul.
181936: Some people who had already had a lot of misfortune went on pilgrimage to Couture St.-Germain. They had set off at night because they wanted to arrive in time to attend mass. Near Tervuren, in the Zoniënwoud, the people saw three black figures. The people walked up to the figures and said 'Good evening'. But there was no answer. When the people looked back a moment later, the three figures had vanished without a trace.
181940: Three sisters lived near Sint Kwintens. When the French invaded the town, the girls were abused and then murdered. Because the three sisters were buried in unconsecrated ground, they came back to haunt at night after their death. One sister had no arm, another no head and the third no leg. Eventually the bodies were buried in the churchyard, and a statue of the three sisters was erected in the little chapel of J.D.G.
181953: A good woman who always pointed at people and talked about them was suspected by people of being a sorceress. In reality she did no one any harm. When people were ill, they believed she had bewitched them and sent for the parish priest.
181955:
Empty houses were often haunted.
A woman who lived alone in a house called the police because, to her great fright, she kept hearing knocking on the wall. The police discovered that it was a prankster causing the knocking.
181984:
You always had to place your shoes or clogs with the heels towards the bed. Otherwise you could be ridden by the mare at night.
A man who was ridden by the mare felt as if a chain fell on his heart. You could only be ridden by the mare if you lay on your back. Another time the man saw a large black shape fly over his bed. The mare looked like a woman sitting on her knees.
182012: One day a farmer's wife found that all her animals had roses and bows on their heads. She sent for a healer from Zepperen. The healer said to her: "You go inside, make coffee and put the cake on the table." When the woman said, "But I have no cake," the healer said, "Yes, you do," and the farmer's wife did indeed have one.
182037: Stalkaarsen (will-o'-the-wisps) were the souls of unbaptised children. You were not allowed to point at those lights, or they would jump on the person who had challenged them. A boy who once did point at a light quickly fled inside and slammed the door. A moment later he heard a blow against the door.
182050: A man walking in the churchyard at night saw a brooding hen with chicks there. The man took the hen and the chicks home. When he got home, the animals had all turned into skulls.
182100: There were a good hundred rats in an inn. A wizard could send the rats to another place.
182115: In Sint-Kwintens-Lennik lived an ugly old woman who was often out at night. When her daughter one day became lame and ill, the woman's son claimed his mother had bewitched the girl. The boy then shot his own mother dead.
182117: A little boy had something wrong with his hand because he had been struck by the evil hand. He was taken to the brown friars, who read over him. The boy had been bewitched by a neighbour woman. The people were not to take any steps until the neighbour had come by. The neighbour came to visit, rubbed the boy's hand and said: "My child, there's nothing wrong with your little hand. It will heal."
182120: Ghosts of the dead often floated around in old castles.
182122: A girl had a relationship with a man who had special powers. That man could cut up the clothes of the people sitting in church in Scherpenheuvel. Because people knew that man was a werewolf, he had no girlfriend for a long time. That girl, however, did not know the man was a werewolf. He was handsome and wore a smart little hat. One day the girl had gone dancing with that man. On the way back the man said to the girl: "I have to run an errand. You needn't be afraid. If anything comes at you, throw this red handkerchief with white dots at the apparition." When the girl saw a dog appear, she threw the handkerchief at the animal, as her boyfriend had advised. A bit further on the girl saw her boyfriend again. To her horror she found that he had threads of the handkerchief between his teeth. When the man came to fetch the girl the next Sunday to go to the fair in Herselt, the girl's mother came to say that her daughter was going nowhere. The man grew angry and said: "I'll get her all right!" The girl died not long afterwards from the fright she had suffered.
182143: In the old days people believed that black cats brought bad luck.
182144: Will-o'-the-wisps were often seen in the meadows of Attenhoven. They were the souls from purgatory. In the past, on All Saints a candle was lit at twelve noon and left burning until All Souls, because people believed the souls came out of purgatory on All Souls.
182148: On a farm people noticed the sow behaving strangely. The animal kept running from one wall to the other, so the people decided to have it slaughtered. The butcher came and said: "But don't you see the animal has been struck by the evil hand?" The people did not take his words seriously and had the sow slaughtered anyway. The butcher had the greatest difficulty killing the animal. It took hours and hours and the butcher sweated terribly.
182153:
If you saw a black cat in the morning, you would have bad luck that day. People also said:
"In the morning luck
at noon busy
in the evening less
that is what the spider brings"
182166: In a stable an animal always lay dead after a rabbit had come in. One day the rabbit was shot dead on the dung heap. That is how people discovered that the rabbit was a witch who appeared in the shape of an animal.
182176: A man went to fetch the vet at night because his cow was about to calve. The vet went with the man along the Heirbaan to the farm.
