On the way the two men met a strange fellow, who picked ten clover flowers, threw them at their feet and said: "Here, pick out the prettiest!" The next moment the ten flowers turned into ten dogs.
182178: If you went from Attenhoven to Gingelom after midnight, you could see the witches dancing on a slope there. If you came closer, the witches jumped on their broomsticks and flew away through the air.
182202: When the mare opened the door, you could no longer breathe. The mare leapt onto her victim and seized him or her by the throat. The victim sweated terribly and grew very thin.
182210: A farmer's wife began baking bread at ten or eleven at night, while the farmer had already gone to bed. When he had been lying in bed for quite a while, he no longer heard any sounds from the kitchen. He got up and saw his wife standing stock-still at the trough. Believing she was dead, he quickly fetched the parish priest. The priest said to the farmer: "Your wife is not dead. She is away. You must not touch her." Half an hour later the farmer's wife was kneading the dough again. That farmer's wife was a sorceress.
182213: A priest met a man who was always playing pranks and fixed him to the ground by magic. The man could not move a foot. The next day the priest was visited by another man, to whom he said: "Tell the man standing over there on the road that he may go on." Only after that had been done could the joker move on again.
182272: Before they died, sorceresses had to pass their magic power on to someone else. In one family a neighbour woman came every morning to look at the four-year-old child. One day the woman brought the child a little painting of a cat. It was hung beside the child's bed. But the boy was ill and would not get better. His condition even worsened. When the witheren (Premonstratensian canons) came to see the boy, they immediately pointed at the painting and said: "Get that out of here at once!" The sorceress died at the age of ninety.
182285: In the Dendermondestraat in Ganshoren there used to be a farm that was haunted. Sandstones were thrown. The police came to the scene. People no longer wanted the milk from that farm because they believed it was bewitched. Someone is said to have caused the haunting to drive away the farmer who lived there.
182290: On a farm in Kortenaken they decided to buy a new cow. When the people came back from the market in Diest with the animal, they had to pass a woman's meadow. The woman slapped the cow on the rump and said: "That's a fine beast!" The next day the cow was dead. A few days later the same woman bewitched the farmer's wife's washing so that it was full of fleas.
182306: In Halle lived a farmer who had no money to build a new barn. The farmer made a pact with the devil, who was willing to build him a barn on condition that he sold his soul. The barn would be built in one night and had to be finished by the first cockcrow the next morning. At night the farmer told his wife what he had done. The farmer's wife got up in the night and clapped her hands, so that the rooster began to crow too early. The devils fled, although there was still a hole in the barn. That hole could never be closed afterwards.
182326:
Witches could make mice by throwing a clod of earth on the ground.
People who were bewitched had to send for the priest to lift the spell.
182327: A woman heard someone knocking on the door at night. A moment later she heard the voice of her dead husband, who made himself known and asked whether he could come in. But the woman was far too afraid to open the door.
182340: A boy did not know that his girlfriend and her mother were sorceresses. One evening the boy had fallen asleep by the stove in his girlfriend's house. The boy heard the mother and the girl take a little pot of ointment from the corner of the chimney, rub themselves with it and then say: "Over hedge and hedgerow to Cologne into the wine cellar." After the two had left, the boy also rubbed himself with the ointment and said: "Through hedge and hedgerow to Cologne into the wine cellar." He arrived at his destination badly injured.
182352: When a friar came to preach in Pepingen, a drunkard had been egged on to talk back to him. As punishment the friar fixed the drunkard to his chair by magic. After the sermon people wanted to beat the drunkard, but the friar stopped them.
182361: A man who was followed by a cat on the road asked: "O you sweet little pussycat, are you mine?" Then the cat answered: "X asked me: 'O you sweet little pussycat, are you mine?'"
182387: If you wanted to know whether a woman was a witch, you had to walk in her footprints. A witch would then look back.
182408: A child who cried all the time because it was possessed by evil was taken to the monastery. A priest advised the mother to stop letting in a visitor who always came asking for a cup of coffee and a slice of bread. After that the misfortune came to an end. Before this, a little daughter of the mother had already died because of that witch.
182418: A boy was coming back from the fair with his girlfriend. The boy said: "I need to pee. Go on ahead. If you see anything, throw my red handkerchief with white dots at the apparition." When the girl saw a dog approaching, she threw the handkerchief at the beast. A while later her boyfriend rejoined her. When she got home, the girl noticed that her boyfriend had the fibres of the handkerchief between his teeth.
182482: Witches could make horses unable to move forward.
182494: Some men had been telling stories about Kleudde (a werewolf-like spirit) one evening. When one of those men, who was a priest, left for his home in Assent, a friend said to him: "Now you'll surely see Kleudde, because you've talked about him so much." To this the priest said: "Well, I wish he would see him for once." On the way the man was indeed confronted with Kleudde. He did not let himself be intimidated, however, and unmasked Kleudde as a prankster who lived in the Groenstraat. The prankster's animal skin was then thrown into the fire. As long as the hide burnt, the prankster was on fire too. Afterwards the priest said to the prankster: "Why did you choose me as your victim? You know you are powerless against a priest."
182497: Two farmer's sons who were threshing were plagued by a witch. Every time they had to thresh, a magpie sat in the two oak trees in front of their house. One day one of the boys fetched the gun and shot at the magpie. The magpie flew away, but had lost a few feathers. Less than an hour later the farmer's sons heard that a woman from the village lay in bed with a broken arm.
182508: A man had a child who regularly suffered attacks of an illness. Because it did not seem to be a normal situation, the father wanted to go to Brussels with his child. The day before he was to leave, the child died. People believed the child had been bewitched by a woman from the neighbourhood. That witch was also said to have made four girls who lived next to each other die suddenly.
182518: A carter often let a little woman ride along who never came into his house. One day the carter and his family had misfortune in their stable. They went to the priests of Lier, who said: "There is always a woman riding along who never comes in. It is her." The people were given rose petals to put in the animals' feed. When the woman in question found out that the people had been to the priests, she never rode with the carter again.
182532: A family's place on the road to Elingen was haunted. The cows were sometimes found up in the hayloft. Children whose parents had died lived on that farm.
182536: A farmer had much misfortune because of a woman from West Flanders who had come to live next to him. The farmer's field was not fenced, so the neighbour always stole some of the farmer's soil when digging. One day the farmer said to his neighbour: "Keep your paws off my land!", to which she replied: "You can have your land, but I will have you too!" The next day the farmer's son, who was in a wheelchair, suddenly began to tremble. The child's hands were completely stiff. The farmer took his child to the doctor, who said: "I don't understand this at all." The farmer hurried with his son to the White Fathers. The clergymen read prayers over the child and then gave it holy water with rose petals to drink. The boy no longer trembled and his hands became supple again.
182537: A man in the Driesstraat in Wolvertem saw a large light that kept coming closer. Suddenly the light had vanished. A little further on the man met a black cat. He kicked at the animal because it kept getting under his feet. A moment later, to his great fright, the man was surrounded by countless cats.
182540: In Hespen lived a woman who was a witch. One day the witch visited a mother who had a small child. There the witch said: "What a strange child that is!" After that the child fell ill. People hardly dared to wash it because it was in so much pain. They then took the child to the parish priest, who claimed the child was bewitched and read prayers over it. After that the child's health visibly improved.
182580: In Wezemaal it happened several times that someone was spoken to by a black cat and afterwards met with misfortune. Black cats were a symbol of bad luck.
182583: In a haunted house in Pepingen noise was heard at night, although no one was to be seen.
182588: Around twelve or one o'clock at night a man had several times met a zwarte madam (black lady) who wore a black shawl over her head. Other people had also seen the woman and they too were afraid of the black lady. Only three or four years later did people find out who the woman was. She turned out to be someone from the neighbourhood. In the past people were also afraid of a woman with a mental disability who was always wandering about.
182594: In the old days, when a butcher had slaughtered an animal somewhere, he walked through the streets blowing a horn to let people know they could come and buy meat. On a farm where a fine cow had been slaughtered, the meat was laid in the stable next to the kitchen. While the farmer's wife was arranging the meat on the table, a neighbour came to stand in the doorway and said: "Fine meat, but you won't earn a franc from it." The next day the farmer's wife found that the meat had turned as black as coal.
182603: In the Beverstraat in Sint-Pieters-Kapelle worked a German shepherd who went to Germany every Saturday to fetch clean laundry. One day a farmhand went with the shepherd to Germany. When the two returned, they found that the farm door was locked. The German shepherd said to the farmhand: "Never mind. Take off your cap and throw it against the gate." The farmhand did so and the gate opened.
182638: At a farmer's in Sint-Pieters-Rode all the piglets died because of a witch. The brown friars advised the farmer to pray a lot and to go to communion. The farmer also had to look around carefully, for he would see the witch. When the farmer's son wanted to load the piglets onto the cart, he found that the first piglet he took hold of was dead. The farmer looked around and saw only a crow. The second piglet was dead too. Again the farmer saw only a crow. The farmer fetched his gun and shot at the bird, which fell down dead. The next day a woman from the neighbourhood was injured.
182641: In the woods of Londerzeel some men were cutting down trees when suddenly a gypsy wagon came by. At that very moment a tree fell, killing an old woman. Since that accident people said a ghost light could be seen in those woods. Later it was discovered that the apparition was caused by someone waving a light on a stick.
182648: Witches could not leave the church if the missal had been left open.
182649: People who were ridden by the mare felt as if a hundred kilos lay on their body. They tried to call out, but no sound came. They could not move either. The mare was a sorceress who put the evil hand (a curse) on people.
182668: When witches found no other victims, they harmed their own relatives. A witch's daughter was always ill. She went to the priests and was cured, but afterwards someone else in the family fell ill.
182669: A witch predicted that people would ride on iron objects and that iron horses would come. Those were bicycles. She also predicted that people would fly through the air and that this would make a roaring noise. Those were aeroplanes. She further said that during the war iron pigs would fly in the air. Those were the zeppelins. That witch always drank cognac. One day she made a mistake and accidentally drank petroleum instead of cognac. Yet the witch did not die.
182686: Two boys and a girl saw a woman dressed in white appear in 't Spithoek. The priest advised the boys and the girl to approach the ghost with a white cloth. The white woman burned her hand into the cloth and disappeared.
182729: In a clay house in Esselveld (Dworp) singing and noise were always heard at night. By the stairs a pair of men's clogs suddenly appeared, which disappeared again a moment later.
182781: A farm had been visited by a woman who brought misfortune everywhere. The next day the cow that was eight months pregnant miscarried.
182792: A boy who was out walking with his girlfriend went away for a moment because he had to play the werewolf. When the boy came back, he had taken on his human form again. But the fibres of the handkerchief that had been thrown at the werewolf could still be seen sticking out between his teeth.
182801: A man was annoyed by a black cat that always came to him. When he had beaten the cat until it bled, people discovered that the cat was a witch in animal shape.
182820: Two farmhands who worked on the same farm slept in the horse stable. One Sunday one of the farmhands lay alone in the stable, because the other was not yet back from visiting his parents. Suddenly the boy ran outside in fear because a strange force had thrown the horses' harness onto him. Only towards morning did the boy dare to enter the stable together with the other farmhand. But nothing strange was to be found there.
182826: A man coming home drunk one evening saw a hen with chicks on the Astridvest. The man took the animals home and put them in an oak chest. When the man's wife said: "But what have you brought home now? You're going to have trouble here," the man was beaten under the bed by witches. The witches would only go out by the back door.
182847: A woman who was ridden by the mare tried to call out but could not make a sound. She felt stifled and could not get a word past her lips. The woman even experienced this once in the middle of the day.
182859: In Kester the procession did not go out because the weather was too bad. When the priest came into the church, he saw that the statue of Mary was covered in mud. After that the procession was always held, regardless of the weather.
182869: People who were ridden by the 'maal' (the mare) felt oppressed in their sleep.
182892: A man who lived in the Moerassenstraat lay ill in bed. Every night he was tormented by a black cat sitting on his bed. The man would then cry: "Mum, she's here again!" The people got up to look, but saw nothing. After the friars had read prayers over the man, the problems were solved.
182893: A mother had already had misfortune with her pregnancy four times. She miscarried or gave birth to a stillborn child. During her fifth pregnancy the mother again felt very ill. She was taken to the priests, who read prayers over her until the sweat ran down their faces. When they got home, the people heard a voice in their garden cry: "Ha ha ha, she thinks she's rid of it now!" This time, however, the pregnancy ended well. The mother gave birth to a daughter who was already ninety-two in 1967. The misfortune had been caused by a neighbour who was a witch.
182905: A woman from Oetingen had had a child. A woman always came to visit the mother and said: "Oh, what a beautiful child!" The mother did not trust that woman. The child was bewitched.
182914: A farmer who heard that the witches were dancing in his meadow took his sabre and went to the meadow. The cats were dancing there in a circle and taking rice pudding from a dish with their paws. With his sabre the farmer cut a paw off one of the cats. When the man got up in the morning, he found that his own wife had lost her hand.
182915: In a house in Hoeleden lived a woman who had promised to have a mass said in Scherpenheuvel. At five o'clock in the morning the woman was woken by knocking on the window. Then the woman heard a voice saying: "It is time to get up!" The next night three men from the neighbourhood came to keep watch in the house. That night, however, nothing was heard.
182917: In the old days, when people had misfortune with the animals in their stable, they often attributed it to the 'red hand' (evil hand). People would then go to church or make a pilgrimage. Sometimes they also went to the priests of Dendermonde. They were then given a medal to keep evil out of their stable.
182923: A farmer had a cow that gave him excellent butter, which he sold at the market in Geldenaken. A woman regularly came to visit the farm. When the farmer came back from the market, he found the cow tied to the manger back to front. Afraid of losing the cow, the farmer placed a relic under the threshold. After that the woman did not come any more.
182942:
In Wolvertem lived an old woman whose husband had a disabled leg. For several nights the man had noticed that his wife lay beside him in bed as motionless as a stone. He had also heard that a young man living a little further on had not been able to get into his house at night because a large dog lay in front of his door. Someone had advised the young man to take a rosary and a club with him from then on. When the young man made the sign of the cross one night, the dog ran away. A few days later, however, the animal was lying there again. The young man made the sign of the cross, held his rosary and shouted: "If you don't get away from my door now, I'll hit you with this club!" To his astonishment the young man then heard a voice saying: "Don't hit, it's me!"
The witch had turned herself into a dog. When that witch was old, she could not die. The priest then had to be called. The priest could not read the evil away onto a dog or a cat, but had to pass it on to a child. That child grew up to be a healthy woman who had four children of her own.
182944: A man had put ten or fifteen eggs in a nest for a hen to hatch. One day, however, the hen had disappeared from her nest. While the man was searching for the hen in the field, a woman came walking up and said: "Well, are you looking for something?" The man explained that he was looking for his hen. The next moment the lost hen came running out of a bush.
182947: An old man who owned books of magic one day gave one of his books to a friend. The friend began reading the books and made mice out of clay. When there were so many mice that the man was in despair, the priest came to hear his confession. After that the mice were gone.
182965: No one was allowed to go into a haunted castle in the evening, because at a certain hour the candles lit by themselves.
182968: A man often went out with a friend who was the son of a witch. One night the two came back from the village on foot. On the way the men suddenly saw seven or eight white cats. The witch's son said: "Damn, she's at it again!" and he kicked at the animals. A moment later not a single cat was to be seen.
182970: A man lost his way because of a witch. Only when it got light could the man find his house.
182981: Witches flew in the air, calling: "We are seven already, seven, seven." A man who went to steal red cabbages met a witch, who said: "If you like, you needn't steal any more, because you can earn your bread elsewhere. But you must stand at a certain place at midnight." The witches then came flying and you could hear their skirts whooshing in the air. Witches flew in formations, just like aeroplanes.
182993: When people saw a black cat, they did not dare go on, because they believed the animal was a witch who could bewitch them.
183000: A farmer who had moved a boundary post found no rest after his death until he had put the post back in its original place.
183013: The mother of a girl who had been struck by the evil hand went on a pilgrimage. She also visited a spiritualist in Brussels, who said: "Your child has been struck by the evil hand. Go home, for it is over for your daughter." When the woman got home, her daughter had indeed died. The mother had been given medals to put under her door. The daughter had been bewitched by a woman who visited regularly.
183021: A man who was out walking suddenly noticed that his cap had flown off. The man could not find the cap again. That was the work of ghosts.
183033: A man who worked for a farmer had to manure a field of more than a hectare. The man made a bet with the farmer that he could manure that field in an hour. The man walked to the field, took the manure fork and shouted: "Each his own!" The next moment there was a devil at every heap. The field was manured in no time. The farmer lost the bet, but he decided to dismiss the farmhand at once.
183076: In Moorsel lived a man who had to carry Kledde. The man had the fathers of Affligem come to read prayers over his stable. The fathers predicted that the culprit would come to visit to ask for tools. She would, however, not get across the threshold. The father's prediction came true.
183080: A man went with his father to deliver a calf. On the way the men saw something lying in the pine wood that looked like a dog or a foal. That wood was haunted.
183107: When people thought a dead person had risen from the grave because the gravestone had been pushed up, it usually turned out later that a mole had caused it.
183121: One Wednesday morning a sawyer went to work for people who were said to be able to practise witchcraft. While the sawyer was still working, the woman of the house left for the market and said: "I have to go, but your money is ready on the mantelpiece under a candlestick." Although the sawyer had not known beforehand how many hours he would work or how much he would charge, the money under the candlestick was exactly right, down to the last centime. The sawyer concluded that the woman must really be a witch.
183131: Many people believed that crows and black cats were bad omens.
183132: A man who was working in the field hurried home because it began to rain. He knocked on the door and saw through the keyhole that his wife had little wax dolls on her lap, into which she was sticking pins. When the man came in, the woman quickly hid the dolls. The man searched the whole house but could not find the dolls anywhere.
183148: A man was always woken by the pattering of a mouse on the frame of a painting. The mouse could be heard squeaking, but nothing could be seen. In that house a child was also ill. The witch, who wore a black neckerchief, came to take the evil away.
183152: A farmer's wife fell victim to a witch who bewitched her goat, making the animal ill. The goat kept jumping around bleating. In the end the animal died.
183160: A haunting dead man came to pull the toes of the people who had done him harm during his life.
183161: A boy always got a flat tyre whenever he cycled past the house of a certain woman in Kasteelbrakel. The boy therefore believed he had been bewitched by the woman.
183191: Because a dead person came back to haunt the old churchyard of Humbeek, the priest was sent for. The priest decided he had to say three masses for the dead person. After that he had to stamp on the dead person's grave at midnight. If there was no response, the dead person was released.
183204: Some people believed that black cats were witches.
183206: Some people had bought a fine cow. The next morning, however, the animal was skin and bone. The cow could not even stay on its legs. When the farmer's wife got up at night, she saw three untied cows dancing in the stable. The woman was convinced she had become a victim of witchcraft. Anyone afflicted by such evil had to have prayers read over them.
183214: A man who worked near Aarschot had often visited a sick girl who eventually died. After the girl's death the man often heard a rustling in the verge. He was convinced the sound was caused by the dead girl, who had supposedly come back wearing a cloak.
183224: When a fifteen-year-old boy died, two witches sat at the foot of his bed. Those witches were said to have caused the boy's death.
183234: Sometimes people were ridden by the mare at night.
183274: In a small castle in Bekkevoort worked a maid who caused all the cows to miscarry, the animals to be untied in the stable and their horns to fall off. It even went so far that the maid could make apples grow on the trees in winter. The maid would throw apples upwards, after which the fruit all stayed hanging. The White Fathers of Sint-Truiden freed the maid from her witchcraft.
183277: A man from Achterbos worked in France during the harvest. There he heard someone say: "Over hedge and over hedgerow, to France." A moment later that person was already in France. A man who had heard this wanted to imitate that person, but made a mistake and said: "Through hedge and through hedgerow, to France." That man arrived in France badly injured.
183303: Some women walking near the castle of Sint-Pieters-Rode suddenly began to scream because white mice were running everywhere.
183307: A man who was ridden by the mare walked around Wieze two or three times and kept ending up in the same place. In the end the man was able to find his bearings again.
183324: A witch lived in Budingen. When people had had that witch visit them, they could no longer churn butter or bake bread.
183327: In a house in Ternat lived a woman who was said to be able to practise witchcraft. Someone had told a man: "If you go and kick that little house in the evening or at night, you won't get fifty metres before the witch keeps running past you again and again." The man tried this more than ten times but saw nothing. Some boys coming home drunk on a Sunday night from visiting their girlfriends also decided to put it to the test and kick the front of the little house. A bit further on the boys kept seeing a small figure with a sheet jumping in front of them in the street. A little later the figure appeared in a heap. One of the boys wanted to set fire to the heap, but the others held him back. The boys were sober at once.
183337: One was not to accept anything from anyone, otherwise one could become bewitched.
183350: A man who had long arms and whose hands looked like claws told a blacksmith that he dealt with the devil. To do so, the man had sat at a crossroads with a black hen, where he had signed a contract in blood.
183354: Some young men sat in an inn talking about two witches. When the men went outside, one of them fell into a pit used as a dung pit. The man clambered out of the pit and went back to the inn to tell what had happened. The people said to him: "You won't dare go outside a second time." He did, and landed in the pit again. The same scene then happened a third time. It had been those two witches...
183364: When people had misfortune or when the animals in their stable died, it was said that they had been ridden by the mare.
183374: On a field where the harvest was being brought in, a woman walked around who wanted to take part of the crop. The farmer said to the woman: "You must wait until the mandels (sheaf stacks) are gone, and then you can gather as much as you like." Then the witch magically moved the sheaves to someone else's field, so that the farmer had to go and look for them there.
183387: A man coming back from Tienen in the dark got lost. The man was exhausted and sat down in the field, calling out: "God or the devil, get me out of here." A little later a large black foal appeared. The man jumped on it and the animal carried him to Goetsenhoven. When the man was in Goetsenhoven, the foal rode with him into a pond, and he escaped death by a hair. Shortly afterwards the man died anyway.
183389: A man going home one evening met a werewolf in a sunken lane. The man struck at the werewolf twice with a small axe, and it then began to bleed. This unmasked the werewolf. However, the man was not allowed to tell anyone who the werewolf was.
183412: On a farm in Neerlinter lived two unmarried men who had a lot of money. That farm was haunted. Sometimes two or three horses were seen fighting each other one evening. Another day a priest and an altar boy were seen walking around the barn with the Last Sacraments. The haunting sometimes stopped for a few weeks, only to start again afterwards.
183420: A dying woman saw a black hand appear on the wall. Under the table lay a black dog that no one could chase away. In the end the parish priest was sent for, who read prayers over the room and sprinkled it with holy water. After that all the strange apparitions disappeared and the woman was able to die.
183423: One had to beware of black cats, for they were witches, so it was believed.
183436: A man had got an eye inflammation after a woman with a bad reputation had visited him. When prayers were read over the man, that witch was there too.
183437: In the old days people believed that bats brought bad luck.
183453: If someone had thrown something at a black cat and hurt the animal's paw, it could sometimes happen that the next day they met a woman wearing a bandage around her arm.
183458: Sometimes people were beaten at night by witches, without being able to see anyone.
183461: Of people who had misfortune, it was said that they had been ridden by the mare.
183465: When someone was not doing well, people often said: "He's been ridden by the mare."
183477: If Kledde's (a werewolf-like spirit's) skin was found, it had to be burnt in the oven. That released Kledde.
183480: A woman from Kaggevinne had fallen ill through the evil hand. A neighbour had done this to her.
183529: One evening a man came back from Brussels on the last tram. On his way home, after midnight, the man saw an enormous dog crawl out of a hedge. The dog came and sniffed at the man for a moment and then ran off. In a field between Grimbergen and Meise the man saw a partridge fly up with a great deal of noise.
183532: A farmhand who claimed he was afraid of nothing went walking in the cemetery at night with a stick. When the farmhand suddenly saw a white figure standing behind a gravestone, he struck with his stick and shouted: "What is dead must stay dead!" At that the white figure ran away. The farmhand was so frightened that shortly afterwards he himself lay in the cemetery.
183535: On a farm a cow, a pig and a fine dog died within six months. The animals died suddenly, although an hour earlier they had looked perfectly fine. The farmer's wife went to a fortune-teller, who told her she had probably been bewitched. After that the farmer's wife had somewhat better luck.
183565: Two men out for a walk in the fields came to a patch of wheat. There one of the men said: "If I want, I can make this whole spot black." The man raised his hand. The next day that part of the field had indeed turned black. That man could also make mice.
183577: A mother had a little daughter who was always ill. The woman moved house, but the situation did not improve. The parish priest advised the mother to go to the priests of Halle. One of the priests came to read prayers over the child and the woman's house. The clergyman said to the mother: "There is a woman who comes here almost every day. From now on she will never come here again." The priest's prediction came true and the girl grew up healthy. When the girl was grown up, she married and had a child. Two years after her wedding the girl died.
183578: A mother and father went to a restaurant with their daughter because the daughter had earned her black belt in judo. The family had only just got home when the phone rang and they heard that the grandmother had fallen. The father quickly jumped into his car and drove to his mother. The mother cycled to her mother-in-law. The old woman had fallen over her black cat. She had the habit of going to sleep at her brother's, who lived next door. The woman could not bear a girl staying the night at her brother's. Because of this the man still had no wife when he was sixty. The mother and father also believed the old woman had tried to spoil their dinner at the restaurant by her fall. That woman did everything to torment other people.
183587: A devout Christian who had resolved to go on a pilgrimage tried to convert a Jew who worked with him at the sugar refinery. The man told how at a crossroads he had seen a figure coming towards him. When the man had begun to pray, the figure had turned into a cow. A little later the cow had become a man again. At a spring at the crossroads of Kumtich, Vissenaken and Tienen, the man met the werewolf with its chains. The man knocked out two of the werewolf's teeth. Then the man saw his best friend standing before him, who shook his hand and said: "You have saved me." That man had sold his soul to the devil.
183603: Many people came to play cards in a café in Meldert. One day a gentleman came in for a drink. A man suddenly saw that the gentleman had goat's legs. He made the sign of the cross, at which the devil ran outside and kicked the door shut with his hoof. The print of the devil's hoof stayed in the door and could not be removed.
183616: A man returning from a visit to his girlfriend, who lived on the Rot, struck at a cat that kept walking along with him. The next moment the man was surrounded by countless cats, so he went back to the Rot.
183628: In a stable in Kaggevinne an ox was found to have gone lame after a witch had visited. After prayers had been read over the stable, the ox was cured.
183642: T. from the Kaboutermannenstraat lived with her husband at her in-laws' house. After T.'s mother had died, a strange knocking was heard every night. After a while T. admitted that she had promised to have a mass said for her mother and that she had forgotten. As soon as the mass had been said, the knocking was no longer heard.
183656: When people went to fetch 'draf' (?) at a brewery, a little light sometimes came and sat on their finger along the way. Those lights were stalkaarsen (will-o'-the-wisps). They were faithful souls asking for help. According to others, the lights were luminous animals.
183668: A boy who had to fetch a doctor in Schepdaal at night for a woman in childbed had to pass the house of a witch. The boy could not get past it on his bicycle because cats kept jumping into his wheel. When he got home, the boy was deathly pale with fear.
183677: A woman who had been struck by the evil hand was helped by someone from Brussels. In the end, however, the woman died of cancer.
183681: The watermill of Hasselt was said to be haunted at night. A man who often came home drunk always slept in that mill. Because the man found that the mill was haunted, he moved to Wallonia. In that little village he always heard drumming at one o'clock at night. Scared to death, the man came home.
183708: Witches could turn themselves into animals. A man who worked in a factory often read books and had the reputation of having special powers. A neighbour boy saw a dog or a cat appear on the wall of the house at night, so that after a while he no longer dared to go to sleep. People believed it was that wizard appearing in the boy's house. One day the worker knocked at the boy's door and asked whether his mother was home. When the boy said no, the worker said: "I've brought some serial stories for your mother to read," and he handed the boy some books. When his mother came home, the boy threw the books into the stove, saying: "There, now they've been read."
183722: Rats that had been sent by a witch were everywhere, even on the roof and in the trees.
183734: A woman went somewhere to fetch two packs of coal. The coal seller laid her hand on the woman's head. A little later the woman was covered in lice.
183741: A house whose owner had died was sold. It was said that the house was haunted, because a little light had supposedly flown around in it. A man was able to buy the house for a low price. Later the house was sold again. Hardly anyone dared to rent it, because people claimed the dead owner came back to haunt it.
183751: The call of an owl brought misfortune.
183760:
The witches flew through the air. That was the Tillekesjacht (a flying troop of witches).
A woman went out every night after rubbing herself with an ointment and saying: "Over bush and over heust to the wine cellar!" But the woman had aroused the suspicion of her husband, who spied on her one night. After his wife had left, the man also rubbed himself with the ointment and said: "Through bush and through heust to the wine cellar!" The man arrived at his destination badly injured.
183771: A woman who was out one evening with a dung fork in her hand suddenly saw lodder (a mischievous spirit that jumps on people's backs) jump onto the road and cried: "If you don't stop, I'll stab you!" Because lodder kept jumping around, the woman stabbed him in the upper lip. At that lodder cried: "But Louisa, what have you done!" Lodder was a neighbour of the woman.
183772: A man was coming through Buggenhoutbos in the dark at night with his dog cart. Suddenly the man saw a rich woman with rich men and many horses standing in the middle of the road, so that the dog cart had to stop. All at once it became as light as day. The horses began to speak and said the man could drive on. The man answered: "I can't, because my dogs are blinded." The next moment a horse with gleaming eyes came out of the ditch and said: "Come, I will go ahead." After that the man got home without any trouble. But he always carried a blessed rosary or a medal with him, so that ghosts or witches could do him no harm.
183796: If the priest left his missal open, witches could not leave the church.
183800:
On a farm in Halen there worked a farmhand who played the werewolf. One day the farmer fought the werewolf with a small shovel on the Elsekant. At that moment the farmer had begun to suspect that it might be his farmhand who played the werewolf.
The farmer sent his farmhand to the Tienboenders, near the Beuken, to work there. Meanwhile the farmer heated the oven to throw into it the farmhand's skin, which he had found on an old pigeon loft. The skin had barely gone into the oven when the farmhand was already standing by the fire. It took two people to hold him back, or he would have jumped into the oven to save his skin.
183804: To protect themselves against the mare, people hung up two crossed bricks.
183826: If one put a blessed medal or a piece of the Easter candle under the threshold, witches could not come in.
183827: By the Langebrug in Molenstede lived a superstitious woman who ran a café. One day the woman went around the house together with Jan C. Suddenly the woman saw someone come out from behind the painting and said: "That is Treezemoeike." When the woman asked the ghost what it wanted, she was told she had to go to Scherpenheuvel seven times.
183830: A man from Bellingen who often came home drunk from the fair in the evening often felt as if a heavy dog were sitting on his shoulders, letting itself be carried. The man would then say he had been ridden by the mare. He was soaked in sweat by the time he got home. When people saw a willow in the dark, they often believed it was a man coming towards them.
183831: A man walking along the Oude Stok and the Wilgeputstraat saw a black cat sitting by the side of the road. The cat meowed and the man said: "Pussycat, will you come with me?" At that the cat jumped onto the man's back. The man had to carry the animal all the way to the Kleinopperstraat. The cat was a witch who had turned herself into an animal. Because she was a stout woman, the man was dead tired when he got home.
183855: A woman who had promised to go to Scherpenheuvel died before she could keep her promise. That is why she came back to haunt after her death. After someone had gone on pilgrimage for her, the dead woman no longer appeared.
183858: On a farm in Nieuwenrode many animals died. Such misfortune was often attributed to the evil hand, but often it had more to do with poor care of the animals. People who believed they had fallen victim to the evil hand often went to the priests of Dendermonde.
183896: Whenever the vet of Zoutleeuw went to play cards, a black dog always ran between his legs on the way. As soon as the vet reached the churchyard, the dog jumped into the churchyard. The man thought the dog was a dead person who had returned.
183917: A young man from Terhagen often visited his girlfriend in Zoutleeuw. For two Sundays in a row, on his way home, the young man had been frightened by a werewolf in the wood by the Gete. The next Sunday the young man tied a knife to his walking stick and struck at the werewolf with the knife. A few days later a man was seen walking around Terhagen with a bandage around his head. That is how people found out who the werewolf was.
183922: A mother with a small child always avoided a certain neighbour because she knew that woman was a witch. One night the small child began to cry because it had convulsions. The curate was sent for; he had the greatest difficulty getting into the house and then said: "People, it will already be too late." The child did die.
183929: A boy who called on his girlfriend one evening unannounced saw that the girl was all dressed up. The girl took a little box from behind the chimney, rubbed her nose with a certain substance and then flew out up the chimney. The boy went inside, copied what the girl had done and ended up in a great hall where finely dressed ladies came to dance. The leader of the company said: "Our family has grown." They began to count and discovered the boy was there. He could stay if he signed his name in a large book. But then the boy grew frightened and wrote the name of God in the book. The next moment he was sitting in a thorn bush in the field.
183935: On the road from Booienhoven to Zoutleeuw stood a small tree where, people said, a werewolf appeared every evening. It was a man who had thrown an animal skin over himself and made passers-by carry him.
183975: A man went into the woods with his labourer to fetch walnut wood. At a certain moment the labourer said: "I need to relieve myself. If you see a dog, throw your handkerchief at the animal." A little later the man did indeed see a dog. He threw his handkerchief and wounded the dog. When the labourer arrived the next day, he had a wound on his face. The man informed the priest. When the werewolf sat in the confessional, the priest began to read from his books.
183978: In Leuven black ravens always flew over a house. The ravens sat down on the roof. One day a man shot at the birds. The next day that man's great-grandmother lay in bed with a wound.
183981: A woman was terrified whenever she saw a rat in her bedroom, because they believed the animal had something to do with the evil hand.
184008: Near the Motte lived a woman whose husband had died. One night the woman woke with a start because she heard her child crying. The next moment someone pinched her legs hard. It was the ghost of her dead husband. The man had once made a pilgrimage while drunk. After the woman had made the pilgrimage again, the ghost no longer appeared.
184017: When a witch had died in Hever, it was found that the coffin was empty. The coffin was then simply buried as it was.
184036: In a castle in Zoutleeuw lived lords who led a very sinful life. One day that castle sank. Afterwards people often still heard the bell of the castle chapel ringing in the marsh.
184056: A man who was ridden by the mare at night put his clogs upside down beside his bed. But someone came and turned the clogs over during the night, so the man was troubled by the mare again and sweated terribly. The man heard the mare bleat like a goat when she left.
184057: If someone touched you on the head, you had to touch that person too, otherwise you were bewitched.
184062: A girl who could make mice filled the church with mice by magic at her Solemn Communion.
184088: In Meerhout there lived a father with two sons who played musical instruments. One evening the boys had to go and play somewhere. On the way, to their great astonishment, they saw a castle standing where there had never been anything before. In the castle women were dancing and leaping. They cried: "Now we have players! Come on, start playing! But won't you have a drink first?" Wine was poured into large cups bearing the names of the witches. The younger of the musicians accepted a cup and said: "God bless you!" The next moment the whole scene had vanished and the two musicians were sitting on a kempschrank (a field-boundary bank) in the field. But the musician still had his cup in his hand. He found that the cup belonged to a witch from Hasselt. The man took the cup to Hasselt and asked in a café where that woman lived. The witch turned out to own a fabric shop. When the man rang the bell, the witch said to her maid: "You go on working, I'll open the door myself." For the witch was afraid. She took the cup and said: "Please don't tell my husband about this, or he'll beat me to death." As a reward the musician received four tailored suits.
184091: A farmer and his wife who went in the evening to fetch their horses from the clover field saw a horse that kept growing larger and larger. The man and the woman therefore ran away in fright.
184101:
A man who had dressed up as a ghost with a sheet over his head walked around the church of Scherpenheuvel.
Sometimes people also saw will-o'-the-wisps, which in reality were glow-worms. People believed those will-o'-the-wisps were evil spirits who wandered the churchyard at night because they had something on their conscience.
184108: A strange sorcerer came to Linden who told people they could become witches if they wanted. If people looked back at him (?) they were witches.
184121: On the Duivelsborre stood a large castle where people often played cards. When one day they needed a fourth man to play, they called out that the devil could come. The devil appeared and the castle sank into a pit that was given the name 'Duivelsborre'.
184124: When a witch had died, her ghost returned near her house with a great deal of noise.
184133: Witches could bewitch a house so it filled with rats. People to whom this had happened had to move because they could not drive the rats away.
184140: When the children were given a piece of chocolate by someone, they were overjoyed. But on the evening after eating the chocolate they were deathly ill.
184144: A mother with a ten-day-old son was visited by a peddler woman selling towels. The mother, who had not yet been churched, bought nothing. But the peddler kept insisting and threw the towels over the woman's shoulder. So the woman paid for the towels. The next day her son had a swelling on his shoulder, although the towels had not lain there. A few hours later the child had swellings all over his body. Because the doctor did not know what to do, the mother took her son to the parish priest of Elingen. But on the day the woman wanted to leave, the child had convulsions, so she decided to stay home. The next day the child had convulsions again, but this time the mother left with her child anyway. In Elingen the priest read prayers over the child and then said to the mother: "You must do a novena with me. Before the novena is finished, you will be delivered from this misery." A few days later the mother and father sat up at night watching over the child. When the parents cried, the child cried too. When the parents were silent, the child was silent too. That night there were three knocks at the door. They asked "Who is there?", but there was no answer, so they did not open. After that the child died. After that those people had no more misfortune in their lives.
184155: A man coming back from the fair in the evening was followed the whole time by a donkey. The man could not chase the animal away. When he got home, the animal had disappeared.
184161: On a farm lived an old woman who was said to be a witch. The old woman often visited her neighbours, but the neighbours did not like that. So they put a scapular under the doormat. People who believed they were bewitched had the friars read prayers over them.
184168: A child had been given a sweet by a witch. The child walked home with its mouth open. The sweet had got stuck in the child's throat and could only go down once the witch's power had worn off. The child's mother was given a relic from Groot-Lourdes by a rich woman to hang above the hallway door. Because of that the witch could no longer get into the house.
184178: Some men always came back together from a café in Halle, where they made dates with their girlfriends. On the way one of the men always saw a figure standing behind a tree. One evening that figure jumped through the man's legs. The man tried to hit the figure with a stick, but did not succeed.
184187: In Herne lived a couple whose children all died at the age of two or three months. A girl from the neighbourhood was always asked to carry the dead child's coffin to the churchyard. One day that girl was told by a friend: "If that old woman keeps coming to that house, not a single child there will live. That woman is a witch." It was a grey-haired woman, poorly dressed and without any teeth left. When the unfortunate lady from Herne was pregnant for the fourth time, she said to her husband: "That woman is not coming in here any more, or else all our children will die." They threw the witch out on her first visit. The fourth child lived.
184192: People believed that will-o'-the-wisps were the souls of unbaptised children. You were not allowed to point at those lights, or the light would bang against the door. When you saw a will-o'-the-wisp, you had to say: "I baptise you."
184207: A man was having a drink with a friend in a hotel in Brussels. Suddenly the friend said: "I have to go home. Something is happening. I can feel it." The friend went home and found that his wife was dying.
184215: A man who had mice in his attic was told by a friend that the mice had been made by someone who wanted to harm him. The friend had seen someone throw dust on the ground and then make hundreds of mice appear. In Overwinden there also lived a man who could make mice.
184217: A butcher who had to go and salt a pig said to a woman: "Tonight I have to pass by here. And I've heard that you're a sorceress." That evening the butcher could not get past the sorceress's house. Only when he had asked the sorceress for forgiveness in the morning could he go on.
184231: Witches could not die before they had passed their magic power on to someone else. If a witch had daughters, she passed her power on to them.
184238: A witch could torment children by sticking pins into a doll.
184288: The werewolf roamed the Heksenstraat in Boutersem. Some people had to carry the heavy werewolf all the way to their house. A man who had to carry the werewolf to his house saw on arriving home that the werewolf jumped onto the woodpile. The man then ran inside to fetch his gun and shot the werewolf dead. In this way the man was able to unmask the werewolf.
184292: A farmer from Oppem who could not get his barn finished made a pact with the devil. The devil would finish the barn before the first cockcrow the next morning. But when the rooster crowed at three in the night, the barn was not finished. There was still a hole in the barn.
184309: In a café in the Nachtegaalstraat music and the noise of cats and dogs were suddenly heard one evening. A man fired twice at the tree the noise was coming from. But when the man went to look the next day, he saw no dead animal lying by the tree. That evening the noise was heard again, this time behind the crucifix in the Nachtegaalstraat. When people went outside, it suddenly became quiet. They believed it was witchcraft.
184328: A witch had made butter on the day her little daughter died. The next day she went to ask the neighbours whether they would take the butter to market for her. When the neighbour came back from the market, the witch offered him two francs, but he would not accept the money. One day the man went to borrow a butter churn from someone. When the witch saw that, she said: "You won't be able to make butter from morning till night." The witch was proved right.
184350: In the sunken lanes of Rummen a leg lay in the road every night.
184369: Sorceresses had to sign a pact in their blood, which allowed them to fly along to the sorceresses' night. After midnight they could no longer fly there. If they had not said "over hedges and hedgerows," they flew through the hedges and hedgerows instead.
184377: Three or four women could not leave the church because the priest had not yet closed his missal. Those women were witches.
184396: A witch from Eliksem covered children in lice by stroking their heads and saying: "You have lovely hair!" When they died, witches passed their magic power on to someone else.
184399: Stalkaarsen (will-o'-the-wisps) were glow-worms that sat in the verge. Some people believed those little lights were the souls of children who had died unbaptised.
184402: On a farm where a cow had just been bought, a lot of noise was heard in the stable. The cow had pulled loose its rope and was standing the wrong way round in the stable. The animal, which had always been healthy and fat, was completely emaciated two weeks later.
184412: A man coming back from Tienen between eleven and twelve o'clock met twelve parish priests by the churchyard, who were praying a paternoster. When the man turned around a little further on, there was nothing left to see.
184419: In Oppem, a hamlet of Brussegem, there stood a barn that was called 'the devil's barn'.
184429: On a farm they could not make butter. One time there was a chicken in the churn, another time something else. The witch took the butter away and put something evil in its place. After the people had been to the friars, the trouble came to an end.
184432: A man who had sold his soul to the devil had to walk about every night at twelve o'clock wearing a bearskin and a chain around his neck. People were very frightened when they met this apparition. One night a man went with his friend to fetch the doctor for his pregnant wife, who was about to give birth. On the way the men and the doctor could not cross a bridge because a large black dog was lying on it. The doctor said: "Never mind, we'll go round." But the men could not take another road, because the dog followed them everywhere. A passer-by said the dog had to be addressed with three words and he shouted: "Go away, go away, in the name of that devil..." Then the dog left and the people could cross the bridge without trouble.
184434: A woman had promised to go on pilgrimage to Scherpenheuvel for her sick father. But the woman forgot the promise. Her neighbour came by her house every evening to ask whether she was asleep yet. One evening, however, the neighbour was already gone before the woman could answer. When she asked him the next day why he had left so quickly, he replied: "Well, I saw your father coming from behind the gable with his nightcap on his head." After that the woman quickly made the promised pilgrimage. Her dead father walked ahead of her the whole way.
184440: In the past, when people had misfortune in the stable, they sent for a man from Charleroi. The man went round the stable with a little box of relics in his hand. Then he dug a hole and pulled a bone out of it. That bone had to do with the witchcraft in the stable.
184449:
If someone died while they still had money hidden somewhere, the witches had power over that money. In the castle in the Daelestraat in Bellingen, beautiful music was heard on the roof every night. Whoever dared to spend the night there would get the castle as a reward. Strong Jan went to the castle and baked pancakes there. While he was doing so, a leg suddenly fell out of the chimney. Jan pushed the leg into a corner and went on baking. A little later more bones fell out of the chimney, which turned into a witch. The witch said Jan should carry on baking pancakes. "Yes, I'll bake them," answered Jan, "and I'll smack one in your gob too!" 
Then the witch said: "Follow me", to which Jan replied: "I won't follow you", but he followed her anyway. When the witch said: "Bend down", Jan said: "I won't bend down", but he did it anyway. The witch lifted a stone under which gold lay hidden. After that the castle was freed from the witches and Jan became its new owner.
184455: A woman who had cancer in her face believed she had become the victim of witchcraft. For one day there was a knock, and the person who had bewitched her stood at the door. In the end the woman died of the cancer.
184467: A man walking at night between Heikant and Zallaken saw a cat there and asked: "Why, pussycat, where are you going?" The cat ran to the woods and a little later came back with a whole pack of cats, who said: "Janneke P. asked me: pussycat, where are you going?"
184500: At midnight a farmhand had to fetch the doctor in Kortenberg with the horse and cart for his master. When the farmhand came to a crossroads, the horse suddenly refused to go on. After a lot of effort the farmhand managed to get the horse across the crossroads. When the farmhand drove back home with the doctor, he was no longer afraid because there were two of them.
184503: In a village there was a laundry where the daughters of the mistress had to work like slaves. People believed the mistress herself was a witch. The eldest daughter fell in love with a handsome young man from Oudergem. The mother begrudged her daughter this happiness and began to torment her with all kinds of witchcraft. One day, when the girl had arranged to meet her sweetheart on a little square, she had to stop at a tree because she could no longer move. At that moment her mother came walking up to send her back home. Her mother would not allow her to marry her sweetheart, not even when she became pregnant. Since the girl was of age, she decided to leave her parents' house. The girl's mother, however, made sure the young man caught pneumonia. When he had recovered, the girl was able to marry him after all. Together they had two sons, who were always ill. The man died young of tuberculosis. The girl was tormented by her own mother all her life.
184506: In a house in Pepingen people saw the hats dancing on the shelf, although no one was nearby. People also often heard noise without anything to be seen.
184508: A man saw a dog that had goat's legs and kept growing bigger. He believed the dog was the devil. The dog put its paw against the door of a house to get in.
184518: If you met a black cat in the evening, it meant that a witch was nearby and that you would have bad luck. Old women were often suspected of being witches.
184530: On a farm a woman had pressed her hand into the stable door. The handprint always remained in that door.
184541: People who were ridden by the mare every night once managed to catch the mare with a pocketknife. They had laid the knife down open, and when the mare passed by, the knife snapped shut.
184552: A witch lived in Leuven. The people who lived near her all hung a medal above their door so the witch could not come in. At midnight the witch always made strong coffee. She walked in her clogs in the attic, where she caught dozens of mice with her hand. Some people could not become a witch's victim. A man who always went to drink coffee at the witch's was one of them.
184554: A farmer from Wommersom had sold his soul to the devil in exchange for a new barn. That barn had to be finished before the rooster first crowed the next morning. At night the farmer told his wife about the barn. The farmer's wife got up in the night and went to the henhouse with a candle in her hand, so that the rooster began to crow too early. The devils all ran away, although the barn was not finished. The hole in the barn could never be closed afterwards.
184584: On a farm there worked a farmhand who went off somewhere every evening. The boy went to a hollow tree in which he had hidden a bearskin, with which he played Kledde (a werewolf-like spirit). One day the farmhand was sent to the field in Opwijk, so that meanwhile the skin could be thrown into the oven. As a friar had predicted, the farmhand immediately came running at that moment to save his skin. When the skin had burnt up, the farmhand cried out in relief: "Now I am released!"
184589: An innkeeper's wife was always visited by a woman who came to look at the children on her way to the shop. One day the children had fallen ill, so people advised the innkeeper's wife not to let that woman in any more, for they suspected she was a witch. The innkeeper put a blessed candle under the threshold. The next time the witch came in by the back door. When another child fell ill the next day, the innkeeper also put a blessed candle under the threshold of the back door. After that the witch never visited again.
184590: Some men who were out at night with the horse cart could go no further because a large coach with two black horses stood across the road. Terrified, one of the men called out: "If you are of God, go away. If you are of the devil, sink away!" The next moment the coach sank into the ground.
184598: A witch who often came to Meerbeek one day gave a sweet to a child there. After that the child became very ill.
184604: In Bellingen lived a woman who was always out at night and was suspected of being a witch. A boy who had to draw lots for military service had taunted the witch, whereupon she said: "You and your brothers should all have bad luck in the draw!" The boy and six of his brothers all had to join the army. Only the eldest brother was allowed to stay home.
184631: When cats walked in the street, people believed they were devils.
184645: A man had taken a brooding hen with chicks from the churchyard to his house. The next morning the man found that the hen had turned into a black cat.
184651: A woman cutting grass for her animals was plagued by a witch who made the jute sack holding the grass always tear. A young man who was also working there in the end did not marry the girl because she had been bewitched so often.
184654: It was said that will-o'-the-wisps were the souls of unbaptised children. One had to speak a certain formula to release will-o'-the-wisps.
184684: During the First World War there was a seventeen-year-old girl in Nieuwenrode who was only as big as a three-year-old child. The girl had fallen victim to the evil hand. She had eaten something she had been given by a witch. Because of that the witch had the power to make the girl walk round the bean poles in the attic.
184703: In a bewitched house there was always tapping and music to be heard. The woman of the house beat the clothes the sound came from and said prayers. Afterwards the witch's face was completely blue.
184719: In Kattebeek lived a man who had an extramarital affair. When that man had died, all the doors in his house opened. After someone had made a pilgrimage to Scherpenheuvel for the dead man, the ghost no longer appeared.
184737: In the old days, when people saw a cat sitting by the road somewhere, they believed it was a witch.
184746: A man from Attenhoven was visited every day by a woman from the neighbourhood. One day the man's child fell ill. When the man saw a toad sitting somewhere, he chopped off one of its legs with a spade. When he got home, the man saw that his mother had lost a hand. After that the man refused to let his mother into his house. The child died when it was seven or eight years old.
184759: A man on his way home could make no headway and was sweating terribly. He was being followed by a black cat. When the man kicked at the cat, the animal vanished and he could go on again.
184768: Near Nieuwrode three brothers had built three castles. There was, for example, the castle of Horst in Sint-Pieters-Rode. There was also a castle on the Kratenberg. One of those castles is said to have sunk into a marsh. In Sint-Pieters-Rode bells could always be heard ringing at midnight.
184771: Black cats and toads were witches, so people believed.
184782: A farmer was worried because his barn was too small to store his rich grain harvest. The farmer met a handsome gentleman who claimed he could provide a new barn. If the barn was standing before the first cockcrow, the farmer would not have to pay. The farmer agreed. The next night the farmer's wife heard a lot of noise, although there was nothing to be seen. The farmer's wife clapped her hands, which woke the rooster and made it crow too early. The next moment the noise stopped. The barn was standing, but there was still a hole in it that could never be closed.
184790: Old women were often suspected of being witches. Such women were always out to give someone something. People with a newborn child were very afraid of such women.
184791: In a house in Boortmeerbeek a ghost came in through the fireplace. On seeing the ghost, the people all ran away.
184796: A man returning from Diest was followed by something on the way. Because the boy could no longer stay in his bed at night, the priest was fetched. The boy had been bewitched by a woman who had also once covered someone in lice.
184806:
In the old days people said about spiderwebs:
"In the morning busy
at noon luck
in the evening less
that is what the spider brings".
184827: When the priest said 'Dominus vobiscum' and turned to his parishioners, he could see the witches sitting in the church. One of the witches had gone to ask the priest whether he would close his books on the altar. One day some people asked a boy who had studied for the priesthood whether witches still existed. The boy answered: "Oui, il y en a encore!" (Yes, there still are!)
184831: A sorceress had put a doll under a chair and was always sticking needles into it. In this way the sorceress could torment a child. The friars of Dendermonde managed to break the spell.
184839: On a farm where the cows were always falling ill, a certain woman was no longer allowed in. When one day that woman came to ask for half a litre of milk anyway, a farmer who happened to be visiting said: "You mustn't let her in any more, because she caused the death of your cows."
184847: Two soldiers were lodging at a farm in Halle. One evening the farmer's wife put on a large shawl and went outside. One of the soldiers said: "Is the farmer's wife going out now?", to which the farmer replied: "Yes, she is going witching. It is the same every evening. She comes home at three in the morning. Ever since my wife has been involved in such things, I have had one misfortune after another." At midnight the soldiers heard cats yowling. They got up and saw outside as many as twenty cats dancing in a circle. At a certain moment all the cats had vanished. At three in the morning the farmer's wife came home. The next day the farmer's wife made a big bowl of rice pudding. Because the soldiers could not finish the rice pudding, the farmer's wife put the bowl on the counter. Around ten in the evening a few cats came in through the drain hole for the water. The cats were given the rice pudding to eat. But one of the soldiers stood by the drain hole with his sabre and cut off a paw or a piece of tail from the cats. That night the farmer's wife was again heard coming home at three. The next day the soldiers had to leave. They wanted to thank the farmer's wife for looking after them so well. The farmer said that his wife was still in bed because she was not feeling well. The soldiers went to look and found that the farmer's wife had lost an arm.
184850: A man struck with a stick at a cat he saw sitting somewhere. The next moment there were at least fifty cats.
184865: A boy who always suffered from eye diseases went to a fortune-teller in Oudergem, who said a prayer and then said: "The one who comes past your threshold and keeps rubbing her eyes is the guilty one." When they had seen who the guilty one was, the boy went back to the fortune-teller, who gave him a little plaque to put under the threshold against witchcraft. After that the woman in question no longer came in and the boy was rid of his eye diseases.
184867: Near a tower lived an old widow whom the children believed to be a witch. The children often went to stick pins into her window frames with a thread attached, and then pulled on the thread. Sometimes in the evening they also walked past the widow's house with a candle. If the widow got angry, that was a sure sign she was a witch. In Aarschot, Scherpenheuvel and Zichem some people had very dark skin because they were descended from Italians who had besieged the region. Women with such dark skin were often suspected of witchcraft.
184872: A man visiting friends one evening filled the house with mice by striking the floor. Because the people did not like it, the man made the mice disappear again in an instant.
184929: A woman had laughed at a witch who was walking past her house. A little later the woman saw rats running everywhere.
184935: In Sint-Paulus there was a little shoe shop. One day a woman came in and said to the shopkeeper: "I'll just take a quick look at your child." After that woman's visit the shopkeeper had a lot of trouble with her child. The child cried every night. In the end the woman went to the parish priest, who read prayers over the child. After that it cried no more.
184951: A man claimed he had met his dead father. The ghost had said: "You are the best of my children, and that is why you can help me now."
184984: A farm in Booienhoven was haunted. Bundles of straw flew around there and the horse stood with its tail tied to the manger. The doors and windows of the stables flew open at night. In the end those people moved away. The friars then came to bless the farm.
184985: A farmer who had no barn to store his harvest in was close to despair. One day the farmer met a gentleman who said to him: "If you like, you will soon have a barn. If you sell me your pledge, your barn will be finished before three o'clock tomorrow morning." For this, however, the farmer had to sign a contract in blood. The next night the farmer was restless and told his wife what he had done. When the wife heard what was going on, she jumped out of bed and struck her clogs together, so that the rooster began to crow. At that moment the barn was not yet completed, for there was still a hole to be closed. That hole could never be closed, because the stones always fell out. In the end a statue of the Virgin Mary was placed there. That statue stayed put.
185011: Some people secretly went out one evening to cut birch wood to make brooms. On a gangplank they saw a cat sitting. When a man struck at the cat, a great mass of cats suddenly appeared.
185023: Two unmarried women were coming back from vespers in Herfelingen. When they got home, the women found that their house was full of rats. Rascals had put the rats into the house with a rat trap through the water drain. The women did not know this, however, and went to fetch the priest to bless the house. After all, they believed, their house was full of witches.
185067: Will-o'-the-wisps were spirits of returned dead who attacked people. Such lights were seen especially in the Rotting, in the Veulenstraat and in the meadows. Sometimes people even drowned because they were dragged along by a will-o'-the-wisp.
185073: In a house troubled by the evil hand, a glow could always be seen. One day the man struck out at the shape, after which nothing more was seen. The next day one of the neighbour women had a wound on her hand.
185117: Two young girls going home in the evening saw a large black dog walking by a hedge. That was Pleudde. All the way, the girls were accompanied by a light.
185140: In the churchyard of Meusegem someone had seen the earth move. After all, in those days there were no headstones on the graves yet.
185148: A man always saw will-o'-the-wisps flying around the pool by his house. One had to sprinkle a will-o'-the-wisp with water and say: "I baptise you alone". People who accidentally said "I baptise you" fell into the water and drowned, because countless will-o'-the-wisps then came flying up.
185160: When a witch came into the stable, the animals began to pine. Since a vet could not help in such a case, people went to friars in the Ardennes, after which things improved.
185169: In Oppem there is a barn that was built by devils. In the barn is a hole that no bricklayer can close.
185171: A woman often went to do some sewing at a neighbour's. One day the woman sent her little son to the neighbour to ask whether she would come by. By a bush on the Barakkenberg (a hamlet of Herfelingen) the boy found a big apple. He took the apple home, and his mother put the fruit on the stove, for the boy loved baked apples. But a little later there was a loud bang and the apple was found to have vanished. The neighbour did not come. She had fallen ill and suffered a great deal. The neighbour had put the apple by that bush in order to bewitch the boy. Because she had not managed to bewitch the boy, she died herself.
185188: A boy had hung an old cloak over a bundle of wood to frighten his friend J.
185205: In Roodebeek lived a woman suspected of having special powers. A man who was a member of the brass band had been given one and a half cartloads of coal as a wedding present. Because the man's wife worked at her mother's from early morning till late at night, they never needed to light the stove. Strangely, though, the coal in the cellar could be seen dwindling. The man fitted a different lock on the door, but it did not help. When the cellar was almost empty, the couple moved to another street.
185223: In a stable where there had been much misfortune, people fetched the friars to exorcise the place. While this was happening, the stable door sprang open and a large pheasant ran out. The farmer said: "That could be the witch!" When witches could not torment others, they had to torment themselves.
185226: A man promised his dying wife that he would have a mass said for her. But when she had died, the man had forgotten his promise. One night a shade appeared by the man's bed. The man cried out in fright: "Yes, I forgot that mass. Tomorrow I will go to Scherpenheuvel." When the man went on pilgrimage the next day, he had to carry his dead wife all the way to Scherpenheuvel.
185228: Some people returning from the field with a horse and cart suddenly had to stop because the horses could not go on. A witch from Glabbeek made sure the horse could move again.
185259: People who were ridden by the mare felt something heavy come and lie on them. Those people could not move.
185296: The Leurreschuur stood on the border of Sint-Pieters-Leeuw and Zuun. In that barn was a hole that could not be closed. The devil always blew the hole open again.
185307: A man from Velp played in the brass band of Bierbeek. One day the man had taken a cart of grain to Leuven. On the way back he had lingered a while on the Kauberg, where he had enjoyed himself. When he then drove home, he saw a strange light burning in the field. The man went closer and saw that the Tillekesjacht (a flying troop of witches) was dancing there. The man heard the most beautiful music he had ever heard. A waiter was giving everyone beer. When the man got his beer, the waiter sneezed, whereupon the man said: "God bless you." The next moment the whole scene had vanished. The man was sitting on a dung heap with a glass of beer in his hand. He took the glass home. He was just ready to go to bed when someone knocked on his window three times. A voice cried: "If you don't return that glass within five minutes, you'll be torn into a thousand pieces!"
185322: A woman who worked as a maid had to go and fetch shoes in Opwijk one evening. To save time she went through the meadow. On the way, in the moonlight, she met her uncle. When she saw someone standing behind a tree a little further on, she quickly called her uncle, who said: "You go and fetch the priest while I stay with this fellow." The priest came and fixed the man to the ground by magic. He was an escaped prisoner.
185343: People who had eaten too much could sometimes be ridden by the mare. A man to whom this happened cried: "I've got her!" In the morning the man found that his hair had turned as white as snow.
185344: Above the marsh by the Zijpstraat, stallichtjes (will-o'-the-wisps) appeared. They were the souls of unbaptised children. When one saw such a stallicht, one had to say "I baptise you" and then quickly run away. In the morning a little bloodstain would be found on the door. One day a man had said: "I baptise you all". The next morning the whole door was smeared with blood.
185367: A woman had a friend who often visited a sorceress. At the sorceress's house there was a candlestick on the table. When the candle was burning, the black cat sitting on the table would itself stick some pins into the candle. The friend told the sorceress that there was someone who had been doing her harm for a long time. The sorceress gave the woman a scrap of cloth and said: "When you know when that tormentor will come home, you must blow this scrap of cloth under her door just before." The friend did as she had been advised. When the tormentor came home and opened her door, she screamed loudly and then ran away.
185375: A woman could find out all sorts of things about people by sticking pins into a cushion.
185380: On a farm they could no longer churn butter after once lending the churn to a neighbour. The people were advised to pour a bucket of manure into their churn and then clean the churn thoroughly. After they had done that, they could make butter again. It was believed that the neighbour, a witch, had the manure in her butter.
185411: A man was coming back from Rillaar by way of the Biezenhuiskens and the Gelrodeveld. But he ended up in Wezemaal and walked back and forth four or five times. He was lost. At four in the morning the man asked the way somewhere, after which he could find his bearings again. That man had been ridden by the mare.
185438: A boy often visited two young ladies in the evening. At a certain hour the ladies would get ready to go out and say to the boy: "Now you must be off, because we have to leave." Because the boy wanted to get to the bottom of it, one evening he pretended to have fallen asleep. The ladies came and shook him, but he just kept snoring. So out of the corner of his eye the boy saw the ladies take a hollow pot from the chimney. They rubbed the ointment from that pot on their feet and then said: "Over hedges and hedgerows, to Leuven into a wine cellar." A moment later the ladies had vanished. The boy got up, rubbed his feet with the same ointment and said: "Through hedges and hedgerows, to Leuven into a wine cellar." Because he had made a mistake in saying the magic formula, the boy arrived at his destination badly battered. In Leuven the man was allowed to drink with the ladies. When he said: "God, Jesus, that's good," the whole scene vanished and he was sitting on a dung heap.
185483: A woman did the washing for a café landlady. When the washerwoman had a child, the landlady was allowed to be godmother.
