The mother knew the landlady was a witch, but had not dared refuse her request to be godmother. A few days after the child was baptised, it cried all the time. They took the child to a healer woman who looked in her books and then said: "The child will keep crying, but on the ninth day it must stop. If it does not, the child will die." On the ninth day the child was dead. The witch was a short, fat woman whom all the children ran away from.
185502: A farmhand from Orsmaal was bringing in the harvest. A woman walking about there always took from the mandels (1), so the farmhand said: Listen, there is enough lying around to pick up, but keep your hands off the mandels. When the farmhand wanted to leave the field after work, the four horses that were to pull the cart would not move. The animals began to sweat and foam at the mouth. The farmhand took his little axe and said to the woman: "If you don't let me leave right now, I'll strike you dead on the spot with my axe." "Yes, farmer, drive on," the woman then said. After that the cart moved off without any trouble.
185505: A witch who had caused all her own children to die gave two pears to a neighbour boy who was manuring the field. When the boy got home, the witch asked: "Were the pears tasty?" The boy answered: "Yes, yes, very tasty," whereupon the witch said: "Liar, you threw the pears away!"
185509: A man coming home heard a blow on his door. It was a stallicht (will-o'-the-wisp) that had flown against the door because someone had pointed at it. Stallichten were the souls of unbaptised children.
185530: A little girl who slept restlessly or sulked around the house was told by her father: "There's nothing to be done with her, she's been ridden by the mare again!"
185560: A boy was suddenly grabbed by the leg in his sleep. When the boy cried out, his father came running with the stove poker. But there was no one to be seen. The mare was a sorceress who threw something on people.
185568: A man had toothache and regularly lost consciousness. But neither the doctor nor the dentist could help him. So the man believed he had been bewitched by a certain woman.
185570: A girl with special powers who lived on the road to Diest was going out with a boy. The girl's mother was also a witch. When the boy was visiting his girlfriend, the girl's mother eavesdropped on their conversations, although she was sitting outside in a tub. At the witch's house one sometimes found tripe sausages, other times oranges. After the witch had visited a man at 't Schabroek, two arms were found there in a tub. Many people avoided being touched by that witch at all costs. During the war grain was not allowed to be milled, so people did it secretly at night. While the witch waited for her fifty-kilo sack of corn to be milled, she shelled the beans for the woman who owned the mill. That woman knew it was said her customer was a witch, but she let her help with the food anyway.
185581: A woman from Gaasbeek who owned a lot of property went round everywhere in November to collect her rents. At the home of tenants in Sint-Agatha-Berchem the woman was given a cup of coffee. But the woman was suspicious and did not drink the coffee. When she wanted to get up, she could not. It was as if she had been bewitched fast to her chair.
185585: Sometimes at midnight a farmer heard his cows lowing, while there was nothing to be seen in the cowshed.
185586: A woman who was being followed by a werewolf threw her handkerchief at the beast. Later the woman noticed that a certain man had the threads of that handkerchief between his teeth.
185588: The farmer's wife on a farm in Linden was a sorceress. In the stable human heads could sometimes be seen dancing. The animals died and the harvest went badly. In the end the farmer sent for the brown friars. A friar shot at a crow sitting in a walnut tree, but missed. He missed on a second attempt as well. The friar asked everyone to pray and said: "All of you, pray. It will be either my death or hers." Then he did manage to hit the crow in the wing. The crow fell down the chimney. After that the farmer's wife was never seen again.
185603: A man had always said that after his death he would come back in the shape of a horsefly. When the man was dead, a horsefly flew into the house where the man had lived during the fair.
185612: A witch could make a cow die if she did not like the animal. She could also make a horse unable to pull an empty dung cart. When the witch came past and removed a small stone from in front of the cart, the horse could suddenly move. The people went to the priests in East or West Flanders. There they were advised to hang a medal in every room and never to let the witch in again.
185616: In a house often visited by a woman from Walfergem, there was a four-year-old daughter who could not walk. The mother took the child to the monastery of Affligem. The mother believed her child had been bewitched by a woman who lived two houses away. Three months after the friar had visited the family, the child could walk.
185617: On her way to school a girl passed the house of a witch. She was a tall woman who wore thick stockings and a long dirty skirt. Another witch went out with an empty basket and came back a little later with a full one.
185626: In the church of Meldert sat two witches who could not get out because the sexton had stuck a piece of the Easter candle under the threshold.
185642: A man walking home drunk suddenly saw a fat black cat running at his feet and gave it a hard kick. When he got home, he saw a tall woman standing by the dung heap, who said: "Before you come in, you must go and set right what you knocked down." The man instantly sobered up and went back to the meadow where he had kicked the cat. After he had set the cat upright, he heard it speak: "In future you won't kick anymore!" The next moment the cat had vanished, but the man saw the woman standing before him again. He quickly ran away and never went to that place again. The cat was a mare (nightmare spirit) who lived in his neighbourhood.
185647: A man was coming back with some friends from the rehearsal of the music society. In the Grachtstraat in Oetingen the men were followed by a beautiful cat. The men had the greatest difficulty catching the cat. The man who carried the cat was scratched by the animal, so that his hands were badly hurt.
185655: People who were ridden by the mare were drenched in sweat and had a lot of trouble at night.
185673: If a witch touched you on the head, you had to quickly do the same and touch the witch's head to break her power.
185687: A man was coming back from the fair between midnight and one o'clock. At the Coquiane in Heikruis the man saw a black cat. When he wanted to kick the animal, a passer-by said: "Be careful with that, because that is a witch in the shape of a cat!" The man walked on, but when he fell, the cat jumped onto his neck. The harder the man shook his shoulders, the more fiercely he felt the cat's claws in his neck. When the man had walked three times around the chapel of Terlinden in Heikruis, the cat jumped to the ground and ran off. That night the man lay sweating heavily in his bed. His parents saw that something was wrong. When the man had told them what had happened, he had to read the Gospel of Saint John on his knees with a blessed candle in his hand. That freed the man from the witchcraft.
185735: Some people were praying the rosary beside a dead nun who was lying in state. During the night the corpse suddenly began to speak: "You must not pray for me, for then you are praying for a damned soul. In my life I committed a mortal sin that I never told anyone."
185740: A mother who had just had a baby daughter was visited by a neighbour who wanted to see the child. When the child was a year and a half old, it still could not walk. So someone advised the mother to go to a cattle dealer from Zepperen. When the mother knocked there, a woman opened the door. The woman went to call the cattle dealer, who was working in his garden, saying: "There's a woman with a child at the door." The man replied: "I needn't come in, I already know what that child has." For that man could cure all kinds of illnesses. The little girl had little holes in her heels, which was why she could not walk. The mother was advised to go to a chapel in a field in Oerdingen. There she had to fetch a red ribbon and tie it round the child's foot for nine days. The mother also had to pray a novena. Then she had to bring the ribbon back to the chapel. "Before you get home, your child will be able to walk," the cattle dealer had said. The mother did everything she had been advised. When after nine days, on the way back from the chapel of Oerdingen, she came into the station of Sint-Truiden, a woman was sitting there eating an orange. Because that was very unusual in those days, the little daughter climbed off her mother's lap and walked to the woman, who gave her a piece of the orange. The child could walk.
185778: Some men were playing cards with someone who, strangely enough, never lost. When one of the men bent down to pick up a dropped card, he found that the odd player had cow's feet. It was someone who had sold his soul to the devil.
185788: A girl who could make caterpillars was taken to task by the priest. The clergyman said to the girl: "Is it true that you can make caterpillars? Then put some caterpillars on this bush." The girl did as she was asked. The priest fetched his book and began to read from it. After that the girl could no longer make caterpillars.
185801: A man always lay sweating and screaming at night because he was ridden by the mare. The priest had to be sent for.
185826: In a house a son and a daughter had fallen ill through the evil hand. The boy had prayers read over him by the Augustinians of Ghent. The following night at twelve o'clock he was cured. The girl was taken to the friars of Affligem, and she too recovered.
185840: In the Sint-Annastraat people sometimes said that music came from a cesspit. The people who lived there, however, were drunk every day.
185859: A poor woman found an apron on the road. She took it home and folded it up. When the woman opened the cupboard where she had put the apron the next day, a cat jumped out and cried: "If you don't take me back to the place where you got me, you'll be in for it!"
185885: In a house, cats always sat miaowing in the evening. The cats could also be heard speaking: "I will keep Mieke. And I will keep Mieke."
185893: A man going home between midnight and one o'clock saw a man in a tall black hat and a black coat approaching. Although he was normally never afraid, at that moment he ran home as fast as his feet could carry him. He told everyone he had seen the devil.
185907:
One evening on his way home, a man came across a young black kitten. He took it home and showed it to his wife, who was delighted. Because the kitten kept wailing in the house at night, the man got up and put it in the pigsty. But he could still hear the kitten meowing there. The next morning the man's cows were gone and all the window shutters were open. Because the man had had nothing but bad luck since he took the kitten in, he once kicked at the animal. In doing so he lost his shoe. When he went looking for it in the morning, he found it completely chewed to pieces on a willow stump. The man was convinced the cat had something to do with witchcraft.
One night he saw that his neighbour's chairs were still outside. The man wanted to play a trick on his neighbour and went to put the chairs in the field. At that moment a crowd of pigeons flew up out of the field and followed the man all the way to his house. Terrified, the man ran home.
185914: One morning a girl had to fetch tobacco at Schoonaarde before her father left for work. On her way back the girl saw a large hare running in front of her feet, which frightened her badly.
185915: Witches could bewitch people by giving them a cake or a sweet.
185917: A woman staying in Westerlo always saw toads sitting on newspapers in her bedroom at night. The toads crawled up her legs. The woman was convinced that those toads were witches.
185920: A boy who went to visit his girlfriend got lost. The boy had walked all night, only to find in the morning that he was still in the same place. The boy had been ridden by the mare.
185937: A farmer went to the fair in Hoegaarden with his sister. Suddenly the sister said: "Look, I can make mice." She took a little heap of earth and rubbed it, after which the earth turned into white mice. A bit further on, at a cornfield, the woman said: "I can make all the grain fall down." Then she suited the action to the word. The farmer turned back at once and had the priest read prayers over his sister. After that she could do nothing any more.
185953: People who had been ridden by the 'moon' (the mare) got lost through witchcraft.
185974: Werewolves were people who came out in the evening and jumped on passers-by's backs. The victims then had to carry the werewolf a long way.
186000: In Glabbeek lived a rich farmer. In the house opposite the farm lived the farmer's farmhand. At the farmer's house there was always haunting in the evening. Knocking was heard in the clock case, although nothing could be seen there. In the end they found out that the farmhand's wife, a witch, was knocking on the door of the clock case.
186004:
In Mazel some boys decided to go and take a bird from a nest, although their parents had forbidden it. The boys drew lots to decide who would do it. The boy chosen by lot climbed the tree, but a little later began to writhe and fell down. The other boys ran away in fear. When the police came to look, the victim was dead. That boy's mother was a witch. She caused seven of her children to die.
Later the witch was found on the kiln where the hops were dried.
186010: People were sitting in a stable with a horse that could not give birth to its foal. Suddenly a witch came by, and the farmer's son said: "What are you doing here, witch?" After he had chased the witch out of the stable, the foal was born at once.
186025: On a bewitched farm the man rolled his eyes and flailed his arms. The children there were completely emaciated. The people went to the friars, who advised them not to let the cat in any more. But the cat came in and immediately leapt at the children. In the end they managed to catch the cat and beat it to death. It was a wizard who owned books that he read. He lived in a cellar and could make his cat bewitch people.
186029: A sorceress once lived in Halle. Her neighbours always heard her in her attic at around eleven o'clock. That was the time when the sorceress took a powder out of a piece of bone and sprinkled it on her body. The sorceress would then say: "Over hedge and over hedgerows, then she flies over everything." If the sorceress said by mistake: "Through hedge and through hedgerows," she flew through everything, and the next day you could see that her face was scraped all over.
186048: A man lost his way on a road he knew very well. The man was convinced that his own mother had bewitched him.
186084: In Waasmont there lived a witch who went around stealing chickens everywhere. That woman always knew what was happening in the whole village.
186098: People who were ridden by the mare were victims of witchcraft. Old women and old men were often suspected of being witches or sorcerers. Those who practised witchcraft were mainly women.
186150: A woman had bewitched her own son.
186160: A woman who worked in a brewery in Werchter was walking home with a man from Baal. On the way the woman saw seven stallichten (will-o'-the-wisps) settle on her arm. They were the souls of children who wanted to be baptised.
186172: In a village where a witch lived, a man was mowing his grass. The man was annoyed by a cat that kept running in front of his mower. At a certain moment the man accidentally ran over the cat's paw. The next day the village witch was missing part of her finger. She claimed she had cut her finger.
186212: At the dairy in Pamel they could no longer make butter. A baker who had always done good business suddenly sold nothing after a witch had paid him a visit. The next day the baker's goats lay dead.
186220: A girl of eight or nine always got an apple from a woman who carried a basket and wore white socks. That woman also had a sister. She herself was a witch, but her sister was not. When the girl came home, she found that she was covered in lice. The lice were everywhere except on her head. The girl took off all her clothes and threw them in the water. After the child had been read over by the priest, she was rid of her lice.
186226:
When people went to a farm to fetch a litre of milk, they always had to pay a cent or five centimes. After all, if you accepted something for free, you could become bewitched. If the children had not been given any money, the farmer put some holy water in the milk.
When people had to churn an hour longer than usual on a Wednesday, they often believed they were bewitched. Old women who wore a headscarf were often suspected of being witches. People suspected of being witches were not let into the house.
186269: People who had been ridden by the mare had terrible nightmares.
186273: A woman who had four daughters and two sons always had great difficulty giving birth. When the woman had already been in childbed for days and nights, the midwife said: "But what is going on here?" The mother answered: "It is my mother-in-law tormenting me!" The mother-in-law was the woman's neighbour. At the moment the mother-in-law's spirit weakened, the child was born.
186297: In Rotselaar people used to tell of a woman who was suspected of being a witch. Most children did not dare accept an apple or a pear from that woman.
186303: A man was followed by a cat on his way home. The man kicked at the cat but could not hit it. When the man went into his house, the cat sat down on the windowsill of his bedroom. The animal stayed there all night. That cat was a witch.
186321: During catechism class the children saw a girl who could make white mice by pouring water on a little earth. When the priest saw what the girl could do, he read prayers over her. After that, to her great sorrow, the girl could no longer make mice. The girl had been baptised wrongly.
186325: A boy of seven or eight could do magic. The boy put some sawdust in his clog and then peed on it. Afterwards the clog was full of fleas. The priest took away the boy's magic power.
186326: A man who was ridden by the mare kept ending up at the same farm, even though he did not need to be there at all.
186331: A man who talked about the devil all the time was one day pulled through the rungs of his chair. Two devils were sitting on the edge of the bed and another one on the mantelpiece.
186334: Farmers who had misfortune in their stables had the friars come to bless the animals. On one farm there was a cow that was very small in the morning. When people began to pray for the cow, the animal kept growing larger. That cow's milk was always spoiled.
186396: A woman always went to bake bread at a witch's house. But the quality of the bread visibly declined. It even got so bad that the bread could no longer be eaten without getting sick. In the end the woman went to bake elsewhere. There her bread was excellent.
186414: A farmer always drove into the ditch when he brought in his hay. A little further on, fat cats would sit meowing. The farmer believed he had become the victim of a witch.
186424: A woman from Sint-Kwintens-Lennik foretold to a man from the village that all his children would die. Later, indeed, many of that man's children died.
186461: A man who was tormented by a witch heard as many as a hundred thousand rats running about in his house. In the end the man moved.
186490: Strange things happened on a farm that a neighbour often visited. Sometimes the chains in the stable could be heard rattling and the horses were found drenched in sweat. One day a calf with a pig's head was even born after that neighbour had visited. The people went to the fathers of Affligem, who gave them a medal to put under the threshold. When the neighbour came for coffee again after that, the farmer's wife said: "Come, let's go and look at the animals." But just before the entrance to the cowshed, the neighbour said: "I have no more time. I have to start the cooking. I'll come back sometime during the week." The neighbour never visited again. The farm had no more misfortune.
186491: In Vollezele lived a woman who was said to have been ridden by the mare. That woman sometimes lay stiff as a board on the ground, as if she were dead.
186523: Two sweethearts were coming back from the fair in Outgaarden. When they were halfway, the boy said to the girl: "I need to pee. If you meet anything, strike at the apparition with your handkerchief." The boy had only just left when the girl saw a big growling dog standing in front of her. When she threw her handkerchief at the dog's mouth, the beast vanished at once. A little later the boy came back and the two went home together. When the girl saw her boyfriend in the light the next day, she noticed that the fibres of her handkerchief were hanging between his teeth.
186547: In the churchyard of Overhespen, people saw little flames every evening that moved up and down and danced in a circle. The priest advised the people to pray. The more the people prayed, the more flames disappeared. After a while all the flames were gone. Such lights were the souls of the people buried in the old churchyard who had not yet been released.
186553: Along a lane between Velm and Walsbets stood many bushes and trees that swayed back and forth in the wind. A certain man believed that the place was haunted.
186554:
A girl lying in bed at night called out: "Father, come downstairs! There are three gentlemen sitting here!" The man went downstairs and saw three gentlemen dressed in black sitting at a table, writing. The man struck at the apparitions with a medlar stick, and they vanished. When the man went back upstairs, the devils appeared again. The same thing happened several more times. In the end the devils went to the attic, where they began throwing all sorts of things about.
All such evil has since been banished.
186564: One night a man took the midwife home. From the meadow next to the churchyard the pair saw a large dog come running towards them. The dog walked along with them and lay down on the ground by the brewery. People believed the churchyard was haunted at midnight.
186583: A man played strange tricks when he went to the fair with his friends. He could throw open café doors with his cap. He could also make people sleep for as long as he wished. On Christmas Eve he was challenged to show whether he could make someone come from far away. The man answered: "We'll see about that", and he made a girl from Sint-Pieters-Rode come to him barefoot through the snow in her nightdress. When the girl reached him, the wizard woke her up. She still had to go back home through the cold. She fell ill from it, but the priest was able to save her. The wizard's power was, however, limited to a certain area.
186584: Will-o'-the-wisps were the souls of unbaptised children. If one could sprinkle a will-o'-the-wisp with water, it disappeared.
186595:
When the witches came at midnight, you could hear the cats screaming. A nursemaid from Beert who was bewitched flew up with her bed at night. Many people came to watch the spectacle. The priest who exorcised the girl died. If a clergyman said even one word wrong, he himself became the victim of the evil.
Toads and black cats were witches. Toads always appeared in the evening to get into the houses.
186606: A boy was out with his girlfriend. When the girl needed to pee, the boy said: "If you meet anything strange, throw my handkerchief at the apparition." Further on the girl did indeed see a big black dog. She struck at it with the handkerchief, which the beast ate. A little later the girl saw that her boyfriend had the red fibres of the handkerchief between his teeth. He was the werewolf.
186611:
When people had a day on which everything went wrong, they believed they had been ridden by the mare.
When someone had had a nightmare, it was also said to be the mare's doing. You then felt a heavy weight on your body, so that you could no longer move.
186612: A man went to work on the roof of a witch's house. That witch had had fourteen children, of whom only one survived because someone had come to pray over it. After the man had worked for a while, the witch brought an apron and said: "Sit on this for a bit. I'll fetch you an apple." The man ate the apple. When he went home that evening, he fell ill and died.
186614: A road mender often saw a returning dead person appear on his way home in the evening.
186652: In a house a girl lay stiff and deathly pale on a chair. In that house knocking was always heard, but when someone went to open the door, nobody was to be seen. The residents of that house went to the priest, who urged them not to tell anyone what had happened.
186671: If knives lay crossed on a table somewhere, misfortune could be expected.
186673: In a haunted house the children always heard three knocks on the window in the evening. When their parents came to look, they saw nothing. Sometimes the children's bed also shook. The father's bicycle normally hung on a hook in the hallway. One day the mother saw a man lying under that bicycle in the hallway. She did not tell her children what she had seen. In the end those people moved away.
186713: Sometimes a farmer could no longer make butter because of a witch. He then had to send for the fathers of Affligem to fight the witchcraft.
186753: A man whose father had recently died heard a strange knocking at night. But there was nothing to be seen. The next night there were nine knocks. Because the man did not know what was going on, he sent for the priest. When the priest heard the nightly knocking, he asked: "What is that?" But no answer came. The priest advised the man to go to Scherpenheuvel. After the man had done so, he no longer heard the knocking.
186756: On a farm in the Bosstraat several children had already died. When one of the sons had been visiting somewhere, he heard it said that people believed his mother was a witch. Back home the boy said to his mother: "What do you believe: what many people say or what few people say?" The mother answered: "What many people say." Then the boy said: "Well, many people say you are a witch. Now you must take the spell off me, or I will split your head with an axe." And so the boy stayed alive.
186784: In Wolvertem there lived a woman suspected of witchcraft. When that woman had visited a farmer, the animals were restless afterwards. A farmer who worked for the fathers in Dielegem (Jette) received a medal from Jerusalem from one of the clergymen. The farmer put the medal under the manger or under the threshold. After that the witch never set foot in the farmer's house again.
186838: A man got lost at night in the Kouter, even though he knew the area like the back of his hand. At daybreak the man asked the way somewhere. After that he was home in no time. That man had been ridden by the mare.
186846: In Waasmont an old woman had bewitched her own little grandson. Because the woman in the end no longer had any power, she could not lift the spell. And so the child died.
186855: A bell is said to have sunk near Gaspeldoorn once. When people who had missed Mass were asked where they had gone to Mass, they answered: "In Gaspeldoorn."
186869: A little boy was always scolded by the priest during catechism class because he did not learn his lessons. One day the boy said to the priest: "If you get angry again, I'll make some mice." When the priest saw that the boy could make white mice by throwing some earth on the ground, he read prayers over the child before the altar, after which it could no longer make mice.
186870: In Kraainem it sometimes happened that a farmer could not make butter because of a witch.
186872: On the Raasbeek in Rummen lived a boy who could make mice by sweeping his hand through dust. After the priest had read prayers over the boy, he could no longer make mice, which made him very sad.
186873: A woman had fallen ill after a witch walked past her window. The woman recovered after someone prayed over her.
186887: Two sisters had agreed that whichever of them died first would come and warn the other, so that she could go on pilgrimage to Our Lady of Halle for the dead one. When one of the sisters had died, the other heard a noise one night. The woman asked: "Is that you, sister?", and heard a voice answer: "Yes." The next day the woman went on pilgrimage to Halle together with her dead sister. The priest had advised the woman to hold a handkerchief in her hand. On arrival in Halle, the ghost gave the woman its hand, which left a burnt mark in the handkerchief. When the woman asked: "How is it?", the ghost answered: "Everything you have done in the world is reckoned precisely. You must atone for all your sins in purgatory."
186913: Two farmhands worked on a farm. One of them had hidden a skin in a tree stump, with which he had to roam about as a werewolf. The other farmhand became suspicious and told the farmer of his suspicions. The priest advised the farmer to give the werewolf a task at a faraway place and burn his skin in the meantime. The farmer sent his farmhand far away to manure a field. Meanwhile he threw the werewolf skin into the oven. The skin had barely caught fire when the farmhand was already standing by the oven to save his possession. So they just gave the farmhand his skin back.
186917: Sorceresses could change themselves into an animal. Sometimes people struck such an animal and found the next day that a woman from the neighbourhood had been injured. In this way a sorceress could be unmasked.
186929: People who encountered the werewolf had to carry the beast on their back.
186930: Some people going to Mechelen saw ghosts flying through the air on the way, towards the plain of Ninde.
186931: People who had a lot of misfortune believed they were being ridden by the mare.
186938: A witch often visited a family in Edingen. The witch would lean over the child's cradle and say: "My dear little child!" After that the child was bewitched. When it was already too late, the people went to the fathers of Affligem, who foretold that someone would come and ask for something that no longer existed. In the middle of winter the sister of the child's mother came to ask for cherries.
186960: In Linden a silversmith had fallen into an underground passage. The man could not free himself and died in the tunnel. After his death the smith still haunted the tunnel. Whenever the smith fell down again with his silver, people always heard a jingling. At the bottom of the passage was a thick iron door with a hand burned into it. Only the priest's hand fitted that print.
186999: A woman from Neerlinter who worked in Tienen was often visited by her family because she could not settle in the city. When her brother was walking home across the fields one evening, he was jumped by a werewolf near the Branchenberg. The man trembled like a leaf, began to sweat heavily and fled to a nearby house.
187004:
On the Wulmerse Steenweg lived a woman whose child always said at bedtime: "Mum, why is that big cat always sitting at the foot of our bed?" The mother would answer: "But child, I don't see a black cat." The girl's sister could not see the cat either. The mother said to the child: "If you see that cat sitting there again, give it a good whack with this stick." The girl did as she was told. The next day her godmother came to visit and said she had a lot of pain in her back. That godmother was a woman with large black eyes.
The mother became frightened and had the fathers pray over her daughter. The father said the child had probably been touched by the evil hand and gave the mother a holy relic to hang above the door. That would stop the witch from being able to open the door. Every night the girl dreamed of mills and animals. At the age of twenty-eight the girl bled to death. After that the witch bewitched the girl's godfather. That man suffered a great deal of pain and in the end his leg even had to be amputated.
187008: A man going on pilgrimage saw a black cat along the way. He tapped the animal with his stick and said: "Pretty kitty". Then the cat's tail took the shape of an umbrella. The cat walked along with the man for the rest of the way.
187010: On the day before she died, a witch still wanted to visit people whose son had been killed in an accident. It was believed that the witch had had something to do with that accident. The witch's daughter-in-law often felt unwell because of the witchcraft. A healer advised the woman not to wear her wedding ring when driving the car. Otherwise she might have an accident.
187041: Strange things happened at a farmer's in Halle. The farmhands who worked there and the people who came to visit were struck by a strange force, although they saw nothing. Rats ran about in the stables.
187044: Witches bewitched not only children but also adults. So it could happen that an adult felt so bad that he could no longer sleep a wink at night.
187066: A soldier wrote to his family that he was coming home because something was wrong with him. When he got home, the soldier said he had felt a heavy weight on his body. Because everyone laughed at him, the soldier told his problem to the chaplain. When the chaplain was with him, the soldier said the weight was lying on his feet. "Make the sign of the cross with your sabre," said the chaplain. When the soldier did so, a jet of fire appeared. Then the chaplain asked the soldier whether he had had contact with girls or women. The soldier replied that he had bought cards from a shopkeeper and that this woman had asked him all sorts of things.
187071: In one house three boys had died after a woman had touched them. The neighbours advised the people not to let that woman near their children any more. The witch later tried to visit the little son who was still alive, but she was no longer let in. And so that child stayed alive.
187103: Trees had given her brother M. a piece of land of seven or eight zillen (furrows). In return M. had to give the paralysed Trees board and lodging and build a little chapel for her. When Trees died, the man still had not built the chapel. One winter morning the man was cooking over the fire when he suddenly saw the dead Trees appear. The man asked what Trees had come for, and the ghost answered: "You need not ask that." M. immediately jumped on his horse and rode to the masons in Beringen. That very same day the little chapel was built. That same day the dead Trees had also appeared to her sister Antalie. The ghost had said: "I've come to say hello. I'm still here too." When M. came back from the masons he went to Antalie, who immediately said: "Yes, I know why you've come. Trees came by your place too, didn't she?"
187121: A witch could cause a horse's mane to be full of knots.
187131: People who were ridden by the maar (nightmare) could no longer move. It looked as if they had had a stroke.
187134: Maggots were always seen in a child's cradle. It was believed that a certain woman had bewitched the cradle.
187140: Two pigeon fanciers walking home along the Steenhuffelstraat suddenly saw something run between their legs. A little further on they saw a black cat with eyes like burning coals. Because the men were convinced the cat was a witch, they quickly made the sign of the cross. A moment later the cat had vanished.
187146: A man had to go on pilgrimage to Dendermonde for his sick little sister. The girl had become paralysed through witchcraft. The man had been advised not to talk to the witch. After the man had walked around the church three times, he met the witch, who said: "What you people think isn't true, you know."
187165: A card reader from Hever had fled to France during the war. A woman staying in a psychiatric institution in Hever could not sleep because the card reader was jealous of her. When the card reader returned to Belgium after her stay in France, the woman had to be prayed over several times to be able to sleep again.
187182: A man from Beigem suddenly saw a black cat dancing in front of his feet.
187192: Witches sat in the chimney in the form of a cat. Such cats normally could not be hit. If someone did manage it, the next day a woman would be seen with a swollen cheek or a graze.
187210: People said that stallichten (will-o'-the-wisps) were the souls of unbaptised children.
187221: A sexton had fallen off his bicycle in front of a house where a witch lived. The woman later said to the sexton: "If I had known it was you, I would have picked you up."
187226: A farmer from Oppem had sold his soul to the devil in exchange for a new barn that had to be finished before the rooster had crowed three times. But when the rooster crowed the third time and the devils ran off, there was still a hole in the barn.
187235: A man who had let his horse out in the meadow went to fetch the animal and rode it home. When the man reached his stable and had dismounted, the horse ran off. The man went under the house and saw a figure with long hair and irons on its feet standing by a small window. He grabbed at it, but his hands grasped only air.
187240: In the old days people were afraid of black cats because they believed those animals were witches.
187241: In a house in Buken a toad came in every day through the drain hole for the water. One day hot water was poured over the animal. The next day a neighbour woman had burns.
187248: In Sint-Ulriks-Kapelle lived a woman whom some suspected of being a witch. Some people believed that woman could make children ill.
187257: A boy from Wieze who had fallen victim to the evil hand had to be carried outside in a sheet. People went to the fathers of Dendermonde for the boy, because they could ward off the evil.
187266: In the old days, little lights were sometimes seen above the meadows in the evening. People said those lights were the souls of unbaptised children.
187292: A mother from Helen had a child that cried all the time. The neighbours said to the mother: "It is X who is bewitching the child. If your child cries again, you should secretly look through the window of X's house." When the mother did so, she saw that X was holding a heart-shaped pincushion. Every time she stuck a darning needle into the cushion, the child felt pain and began to cry.
187296: A boy from Outgaarden could make white mice by throwing a little heap of earth into the air. A word had been forgotten at that boy's baptism. After the priest had baptised the boy again, he could no longer make mice.
187316: A farmer from Wever had much misfortune because he had been bewitched by a woman from the neighbourhood. The farmer sent for a brown friar, who shot with a gun at a crow sitting in a tree by the farmer's farm. The crow was hit and fell to the ground, but a moment later it had disappeared. Afterwards it was found that that particular neighbour woman had a broken arm.
187352: During the First World War a family had gone to live with a witch in Ganshoren. The witch had a donkey, which she fed chicory roots. The animal always had sore legs, so one day a woman said: "It looks as if that animal has rotten legs!" The next day that woman could not go to market because her legs were all swollen. The doctor came, but he could not cure her. In the end the woman had herself prayed over. The man who did it sweated water and blood.
187376: Many sorceresses lived on the Malheide in Lembeek. The sorceresses also often held gatherings there. They flew to that place on their brooms after saying: "Over hedgerows and hedges." The women who made a mistake and said: "Through hedgerows and hedges" arrived at their destination badly injured.
187391: In Rotte Bos in Merbeek there was once a large monastery of Norbertines. Later the monastery was sold as confiscated church property and then demolished. When Louis S. went poaching at that spot many years later, he saw the dead Norbertines passing by in prayer. Louis was so frightened that he died three days later.
187410: If people failed to have a promised mass said for a deceased person, the dead person came back.
187411: Some people who went out singing saw stallichten (will-o'-the-wisps) by the canal along the dike. It seemed as if the lights came out of the water and flew along with the passers-by. People said such lights were the souls of unbaptised children.
187489:
In Sint-Brixius-Rode (Meise) a woman had died giving birth to her fifth child. A girl who worked there as a nursemaid was visited one day by a woman who came to fetch butter. When the maid afterwards had to take water to the animals in the stable, she saw that the sow was foaming at the mouth and had bitten two of her piglets to death. The farmer sent for a father from Dendermonde, who advised him to bring all his animals inside and shut the door. The farmer followed this advice and left only the dog outside. The next morning the dog lay dead. The father had also said that the farmer should make a cross in all his drink with a medal. He also had to put a medal above the door. The father had foretold that the guilty party would come by and ask if she could come in.
One day, when the farmer was eating with his children, there was a knock at the door by the woman who had come for butter. The woman asked if she could come in, and the farmer answered: "Yes, good spirits may, but bad ones cannot get out of here fast enough!" The woman left and never came back.
Since the Gospel of Saint John has been read after Mass, witchcraft no longer exists.
187492: Under an apple tree stood a witch who suddenly vanished after clapping her hands.
187526: To prevent being ridden by the mare, people sometimes put a flat branch under their bed. Whoever prayed the Gospel of Saint John would not be ridden by the mare.
187531: A witch's daughter had had a baby. The woman who was to carry the baby at the baptism had said beforehand: "That witch will have to be godmother, but I won't accept a sugared almond from her!" When they went to the café after the baptism, the witch offered sugared almonds to everyone except that woman. Witches knew everything.
187543: A man who had sold piglets to a gentleman had not yet been paid. At night the man always heard the gentleman talking to him. One day the man decided to go with his wife to the spiritists of Luik, because he had heard that those people could make contact with spirits. At the spiritists' the man heard a voice that said: "I could not possibly pay you then. You will get your money back. You must pray for the rest of my soul." The man and woman had set out with a brand-new umbrella. When they came home, the umbrella was full of holes.
187548: A man going to Peizegem (a hamlet of Merchtem) was surrounded by a good thousand screeching cats. They were all wizards.
187573: On a farm in Tildonk the stable had been touched by the evil hand, so that all the animals died.
187596: In a large house in Nieuwrode there stood a stick. Everyone who entered that house had to walk around the stick, whether he wanted to or not. For a witch lived in the house.
187601: Some men went to play cards in the inn on Sunday instead of going to Mass. Cats kept coming into the inn. When one of the men bent down to pick up a dropped card, he saw that the cats had goat's legs, just like the devil. The men were terrified and hurried to the church, where the priest was giving the sermon. After that those men went to church every Sunday.
187603: Will-o'-the-wisps were the souls of unbaptised children. A woman who had quickly slammed the door on seeing a will-o'-the-wisp found the next morning that the door was covered in blood. The will-o'-the-wisp had baptised itself in its own blood.
187617: In the old days black cats were associated with the devil. People believed these animals brought bad luck.
187622: A man who saw toads crawling in the evening claimed he had seen a witch.
187634: A man was walking with his wife and little son past a witch. The boy shouted something at the witch and began to laugh. When the family reached their house a hundred metres further on, the child could not get his cap off his head because his ear was completely swollen. The father took his dung fork and said: "I'll make sure the child is cured quickly!" The man went to the witch and said: "If you don't cure my child right now, I'll stab you to death here with my dung fork!" The witch answered: "Go home, man. There's nothing wrong with your child!" When the man got home, his son was indeed cured.
187664: On a farm in Vertrijk lived a maid who could do magic. When the farmhands had to go and bind the wheat, they asked the maid to come along. The maid answered: "Just go. Everything will be fine." When the farmhands reached the field, all the work had already been done. The maid urged the farmhands not to tell anyone about what they had seen. But one of the farmhands could not keep his mouth shut. At night he was thrashed by the devils.
187670:
Children who did not grow and wasted away were said to suffer from the 'oude man' (old man) (1). It was believed those children were bewitched.
A little boy had been bewitched in an inn while sitting on his mother's lap. Next to the mother sat a witch. After the child had been prayed over by the fathers of Affligem, it recovered.
187681: In the old days people sometimes heard knocking in the chimney. They believed it was witchcraft.
187683:
When children had seen an ugly woman somewhere, it sometimes happened that they woke up every night at the same time and began to cry.
People believed those children had become victims of the Zwarte Madam (Black Lady). They then often went to the fathers of Halle to have a blessing read over the child.
Sometimes it was also said that children who woke up every night at the same time had been ridden by the maar (nightmare). This happened, for example, in a family in Lembeek, where a little woman who sold sweets was suspected.
187717: A girl who had seen a large black cat had fallen ill. The girl believed she had been bewitched by that cat. The girl's father went to the friars of Dendermonde.
187726: A woman came past the house of a witch in Leerbeek with her cow. The witch came up to the cow and said to the woman: "You have a fine cow!" Shortly afterwards the cow had to be slaughtered.
187737: In Kessel lived a man who could only walk backwards. The man's family sought advice from the brown friars, who said the man must no longer go to a dance hall. In this way the man was freed from his problem. To celebrate this good outcome, he went for a drink at a café with some friends. There, however, he let himself be persuaded to dance again, and a little later he was bewitched once more. This time it was for good.
187772: A man from Weizele saw a police dog with fiery eyes in a wood. The dog jumped on the man. The werewolf made itself carried. A little further on a second werewolf jumped onto the man's other shoulder. A moment later yet another werewolf jumped onto the man's head. When the man began to pray the Gospel of Saint John, the werewolves all disappeared. For a long time the man was out of his mind from the fear he had endured.
187796: A boy coming back late in the evening from visiting his girlfriend was followed in the Biezemstraat by a large black dog. The boy was scared to death and rode home as fast as he could.
187800: In the Outgaardeveld in Bost lived a man who had moved the boundary post of his land to have more land. After his death the man haunted every night with the boundary post on his back, calling: "Reen, reen, where shall I throw my stone?" One day a drunkard answered: "Throw it where you like". When the ghost had thrown the boundary post away, he was released.
187821: On the Osseweg lived a boy who could make white mice. When the priest was told about it, the clergyman said: "That's not serious. Something was forgotten at the baptism." After the priest had baptised the boy again, he could no longer make mice.
187844: A man who read books of magic had special powers. When he made a little hole in the ground with his shoe, as much money came out as he wanted. That man could also make a wagon stand still or drive on without horses.
187862: On a farm in Houwaart that had much misfortune, one cow after another died because of a witch. When the farmer had to take a load away, he could not manage it even with five horses. In the end the farmer said to the witch: "Oh, do let me drive," to which the witch replied: "If that's all it is." The farmer was able to transport the load with one small horse.
187863: A stalkaars (will-o'-the-wisp) was a light that appeared above the brook and which people believed was the soul of an unbaptised child.
187873: Some people had gone to live in France, where they bought a piece of land from a farmer. The people had to manure the land for two years. After that they had to give the land back and would receive another piece. However, they were not pleased with the piece of land they got afterwards. Out of revenge the woman caused all the farmer's animals to die. After that had happened, she made the children die. When people began to suspect that the woman was responsible for the misfortune, she came back to live in Belgium.
187887: Someone who had moved the boundary post of his field during his life had to come back after his death to put the post back.
187906: If you went to a little chapel at midnight, you would see the devil there with a werewolf skin. You had to wear such a skin until morning. If someone struck a werewolf so that he bled, he was also allowed to take off his skin.
187931: A rich farmer from Kumtich had seen a woman steal part of his harvest and had given her a slap. "You will come to regret that," the woman had said. After that the farmer had bad luck. Sometimes he could no longer walk forwards or could no longer speak. Eventually the farmer went to the parish priest of Butsel, who said: "Go home. The first woman you see sitting on the way, you must give a two-franc coin without saying anything. You may also no longer go to a ball or a party." In this way the farmer was freed from his troubles. When there was a fair in Bierbeek, the farmer went to the ball again after all. He had not been there five minutes before he was bewitched again.
187969: In Ezemaal lived people who were said to be able to make others ill. Farmers therefore wanted at all costs to keep those people out of their stables. When someone had bought a new cow, they led the animal into the stable over a five-cent coin to free it from the evil hand. Afterwards they offered that coin in the church.
187995: A woman who had borrowed money from a man died before she had paid it back. At night the dead woman's husband heard someone knocking at the window and calling: "That money, that money!" From his bed the widower answered: "I will give it back." The widower believed it was his wife come back to haunt him. In reality it was the man from whom the dead woman had borrowed the money. That is how the man got his money back.
187999: By the Bostsepoort stood a house that remained empty for years because people said it was haunted. At night chairs and tables flew around and the windowpanes were smashed. A man who did not believe in the haunting moved into the house and never had any trouble.
188013: In the old days people often said that black cats were witches.
188025: People who had been bewitched by the mare had the black friars read prayers over them.
188052: In a house where a witch lived, people were playing a game of cards. When a man bent down to pick up a dropped card, he saw that one of the players had a cow's or a horse's leg. That was the witch.
188061: Witches could turn themselves into animals.
188078: A woman from Sint-Brixius-Rode (a hamlet of Meise) always advised her pregnant daughters to go on pilgrimage to Dendermonde. The woman herself had lost two children through the doing of a rag-picker woman.
188088: People who had been ridden by the mare had in fact been bewitched.
188114: A girl was out walking with her boyfriend when the boy said: "I'll be right back. Take this red handkerchief." A little later the girl met a young horse. She threw the handkerchief at the animal. When the girl saw her boyfriend again, she noticed that he had the fibres of the handkerchief between his teeth.
188117: A man who had moved a boundary post appeared after his death in the form of a plaaggeest (tormenting spirit) that sat on the dog kennel and made itself be carried. Earlier the man had agreed with a friend that whoever died first would come and tell the other what things were like in the hereafter. When the man had died, he could say nothing, but appeared in the form of a plaaggeest (tormenting spirit) that made itself be carried. Other people, however, did not see it. Because the friend grew thinner and thinner from misery, he told the parish priest about his problem. Feeling that the priest did not take him seriously, he went to the friars of Mechelen. "Well, my boy", said one of the friars, "you must go to all the farmers to ask for corn and wheat and sell it. With the proceeds you must have masses said. That will bring much release. When you see the spirit sitting on the dog kennel again, you must open the window, wrap something around your hand and say: 'If you come from God, speak; if you come from the devil, depart' ". After the man had followed the friar's advice, he was no longer troubled by the strange apparition. In the handkerchief he had wrapped around his hand when approaching the spirit, a hand was burnt. In this way the friend had made known that he was burning. The village priest wanted the handkerchief to frame it and hang it in the church, so he could make people realise that one could indeed burn in the hereafter. But the man would not give up the handkerchief. He was no longer troubled by the ghost, but he did die young.
188122: A man returning from work in the evening often saw glow-worms on the way. People believed such lights were the souls of dead children.
188137: In the past many people heard knocking on the roof at night. Later they found out that it was a prankster who wanted to frighten them with the knocking.
188146: A man walking home one evening saw a will-o'-the-wisp dancing above a meadow. After the man whistled at the light, it came flying at him and threw him violently against a wall. It was said that will-o'-the-wisps were the souls of unbaptised children.
188153: A man playing cards in an inn said to the innkeeper: "Go and light the stove, because it's getting cold." When the innkeeper went to the stove, a big black dog stood in front of him. People were afraid of that wizard.
188193: Two girls were coming back together from the fair. At the end of the Peizegemstraat in Buggenhout, one of the girls was suddenly jumped on by a big black dog. The girl screamed and a moment later the dog was gone. A woman with a white cloth on her head was seen, who walked along for a bit and then disappeared. That woman must have been a sorceress.
188195: When Bettes M.'s brother came home one evening, he saw a will-o'-the-wisp and said: "I will baptise you, but you must not tell anyone". Will-o'-the-wisps were the souls of unbaptised children. Because the man had said "Amen", he was overwhelmed by countless will-o'-the-wisps. The next morning the man was found covered in blood. You were allowed to say "In the name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit", but you must not add "Amen".
188203: In a house where a woman often came to fetch milk, a toad always came in through the drain hole for the water. One day the man struck at the animal with a knife. Afterwards the little son of the woman who usually came for milk came to visit. "Is your mother ill?" asked the farmer, to which the boy replied: "No, but yesterday she cut her hands and she has lost four fingers."
188206: In Oppem (Brussegem) a farmer had sold his soul to the devil in exchange for a barn that had to be finished at the first cockcrow the next day. But the farmer's wife had struck her clogs together, so that the rooster began to crow too early and the devils had to flee. There was still a hole in the barn that could never be closed.
188221: In Sint-Ulriks-Kapelle lived a woman whom some suspected of being a witch. That woman owned a cloth with a bloodstain from a mole, with which she could cure warts and erysipelas. Sometimes people had bad luck after that woman had visited them. People then believed they had been bewitched.
188224: A woman who was often ridden by the moon was advised to lay a sharp knife on herself with the blade pointing upward. The moon would then fall onto that knife.
188230: It was said that will-o'-the-wisps were the souls of unbaptised children.
188232: A Christian woman always warned people to beware of evil. When her son said that his children were not doing well, she went to the young man's house and immediately threw out a female visitor who was sitting by the cradle.
188253: A three-year-old boy from Sint-Katharina-Lombeek had been bewitched after being touched by an old woman. The next day the boy could no longer walk. When a white friar came to undo the witchcraft, he sweated terribly.
188267: In Zoutleeuw there once lived an old woman whom people feared because they suspected she was a witch. A farmer's wife going to tend her pigs met that woman, who said: "You have a fine pig!" and stroked the animal's head. The next day the pig's head was crooked. That defect never went away. When that witch had stroked a child's head, the child was afterwards covered in lice.
188277: A crow sat in the trees on a hill in Glabbeek. When someone had shot at the crow, a woman fell out of the tree. The woman had a wound on her arm.
188292: Sorceresses sometimes held gatherings, which they went to in disguise and where they feasted and drank. A man who was present at such a gathering suddenly had to sneeze, after which the whole scene had vanished. The man, who had been turning a barrel organ, was now standing with a cat's tail in his hands.
188324:
A girl always had to bring a bowl of soup to her employer's aunt. The girl was always afraid and did not dare to go into the aunt's house. The aunt had a little son and was often visited by her mother. That mother could not leave the child alone. The child became crippled and died later in life. When the child was dead, the doctor said: "You can be glad the child died, because it would have become a monster."
In the neighbourhood lived another child whom the woman often visited. That child got a disability in its foot. To protect yourself against witchcraft, you had to say: "Today is Good Friday."
188330: A man coming home by moonlight on a cold evening saw a figure in the field that went faster when he went faster and slowed down when he walked more slowly. When the man stopped, the figure stopped too. Then the man asked: "Who are you? Are you going to Hespen too?" There was no answer. As soon as it grew light in the morning, the figure had vanished. The man told a farmer what had happened and was told: "Don't you know what that is? We see it here regularly. It is the soul of a man who was murdered here some time ago. The murderer was never found. The ghost was probably going to the murderer's house. If you had followed the figure, we would have known who the murderer was."
188353: The Rokapel farm was once a monastery of black friars. Later the building was sold as zwart goed (confiscated church property) and the chapel was converted into a cowshed. All the calves born there were deformed. Later the space was converted into a bakehouse.
188374: Werewolves usually wore a rattling chain. They chased passers-by and jumped onto their backs. People who fell victim to the werewolf usually fell to the ground.
188380: In a house two sisters were jumped on by a dog every night. The cow was also always untied and people often saw a fireball flying away. Sometimes music was heard there too. The sisters went to the friars, but they could not help them. In the end another friar came, who put an end to the haunting.
188414: When something strange had happened somewhere, people often blamed a witch.
188417:
In Vlezenbeek lived two old people who were distrusted by many. It was said that the old woman was a witch, and people with small children at home were warned about the danger she posed. A neighbour heard her baby start crying at three o'clock at night, which it otherwise never did. By five o'clock the baby was dead.
A man who drove to market every Wednesday with butter and buttermilk always came back dead drunk. On that day the man, as usual, visited the people whose baby had died the night before. "Had I known," said the man, "your child would not have died. It has 'the great bear'." When the dead child was undressed, they saw a black bear on its back, gripping the child by the neck.
The old woman who lived nearby moved away afterwards.
188426: On a farm in Rotselaar where they had several cows, a cow that had just calved strangely gave no milk. Near the farm lived a woman suspected of being a witch. The farmhand had seen the witch lean over the half-door of the stable and say: "What a lovely udder that cow has!" When the farmer's wife heard the farmhand's story, she sent her husband to the friars in Leuven, where he was to fetch a relic to put under the threshold. Three days later the witch came by again. When she stopped at the relic, no one was allowed to say "Come along" or "Leave." The witch had to stand there until the relic's power had worn off. After standing there for ten minutes, the witch went home. She was never seen again after that.
188429: On a farm the bread always went bad because of witchcraft. They then had to have leaven made elsewhere, put it in the kneading trough, make little holes in it and sprinkle salt in them. If one did that, the bread could not be bewitched. One always had to pay something for the leaven, for example one cent.
188436:
A mother who had already lost two daughters sought advice from a woman in Jette. That woman told her: "When you get home, you must put your daughter in a bath of salt water. Then the witch will come by and ask for a slice of bread. Your daughter will live." The mother also received a medal and a prayer card of Saint Anthony. She had to put something blessed under the threshold.
The girl did indeed survive. Her two sisters had died of meningitis at the age of three.
188444:
A man whose pig had been ridden by the maar (nightmare) sent for the priest to read a blessing over the animal. Afterwards the clergyman said to the farmer's wife: "You must put a brick in the pig's trough and the food must never drop below that brick." Soon after, the pig was cured. In reality the animal had been underfed.
People could also be ridden by the maar. Between eleven and twelve o'clock they would then lie rigid in their beds.
188464: Zeelke V.D.V. had received twenty francs from a farmer to go on pilgrimage for him. Because the farmer died shortly afterwards, Zeelke did not make the pilgrimage. From then on the woman heard noise in her room every night. One night Zeelke saw the dead farmer lying under her bed. After the woman had gone on pilgrimage to Scherpenheuvel, the dead farmer was no longer heard from.
188470: In a house where someone had died, knocking was heard at night. People then believed that the dead person had returned.
188473: Kludde (a werewolf-like spirit) with his chain was a farmhand who roamed about in the evening with an animal skin. One day the farmhand's skin had been found and thrown into the oven. Before the skin had landed in the fire, however, the farmhand came running to save his skin.
188474: A woman often came to visit a farm just when they were baking bread. In the old days bread was always baked on the same day. When the dough had been left to rise and they wanted to knead it again, they found it full of pins.
188484: In Spieringen a woman is said to have bewitched all her children. Only one child survived.
188490: On a farm in Koningshooikt the windows and doors flew open every night at twelve o'clock. People would then close the windows and doors, but a little later they flew open again.
188495: A man saw a stalkaars (will-o'-the-wisp) in the Kraaimeersch in the Dorpsstraat in Beert. This was a damp meadow from which luminous phosphorus vapours rose. In the same way phosphorescence could be seen at sea when a thunderstorm was coming in warm weather. People, however, believed that stalkaarsen were the souls of unbaptised children.
188528: A witch from Nieuwrode bewitched people by sticking pins into the stalks of the cabbages that had been left standing in the field.
188585: A man returning in the evening from a visit to his girlfriend had to pass the convent of Grazen. On the road the man saw a table at which four nuns sat playing cards.
188590: In Moerbeke and in Atembeke (1) there was a lot of dancing to organ music. The priest said in his sermon: "If this doesn't stop, the devil will come and cure you of dancing!" On the evening of Epiphany there was dancing in a café. Suddenly the devil came in and danced with the café owner's daughter. The girl was so frightened that she died shortly afterwards.
188609: Some girls had to go and fetch flour. On the way they had to pass the house of a witch. In that house there was always a burning candle by the window. When the girls passed the churchyard, they suddenly heard noises in the flour, so that they almost fainted with fear. They were convinced that the witch had caused those noises.
188610: A family in Metsteren had a baby that cried all the time. In the child's pillow there was a wreath of yarn of different colours.
188622: On a farm the cows were untied on Christmas night. Everyone was sitting around the stove when at midnight a sudden noise of chains was heard. In the cowshed they saw that all the cows were standing up and had been untied. The cows were tied up again, but a little later they were loose once more. Shortly after twelve the cows stayed tied up.
188628: In the old days there were many owls in the churchyard that made a wailing sound. They were the little souls of unbaptised children. The priest would then come to read prayers over those souls and banish them to the sea.
188681: A witch lived in Meldert. A goat was often seen flying through the air there. On a farm where only unmarried people lived, the winnowing machine in the barn began to turn by itself, although everyone was in the house.
188682: The werewolf jumped onto people's backs and made itself carried.
188706: The witches flew off after saying: "Over hamlets and hills to Cologne into the wine cellar." In Cologne the witches drank wine from silver cups. One day a woman from the village had flown along with the witches. But she was not allowed to say anything. The woman was so startled, however, that she cried: "Lord Jesus, where are we!" The next moment the whole scene vanished and the woman was sitting alone in the field.
188731: An unmarried farmer was working in the field. At a certain moment a woman came to work in a nearby field. The next day the farmer had 'the black pox'. Hardly anyone dared to visit the man, except a neighbour who brought him food. When the neighbour said that a certain woman wanted to visit the farmer, he said: "No, that woman may not come in here, because it was she who bewitched me when she was working in the field."
188739: In Tienen there was a house where two women lived who were not well liked. A girl who had to bring eggs to those women smelled candles and sulphur in the house. The old women sat praying around the table. One woman led the prayer and the other repeated after her. It was about Satan and hell. Eight days later the First World War broke out.
188741: On a farm in Halle the horses always broke loose at night, even though the meadow was well fenced. The farmer did not know what was wrong with his farm. A friend told him that the evil hand might have something to do with it. The farmer had to check whether there was a handprint anywhere on his gate. The farmer did indeed find such a print. He poured boiling water over it, as his friend had advised. The next day the farmer saw a woman walking in the field with a bandage around her arm. That is how the farmer knew who the witch was.
188756: A girl had fallen ill from drinking bewitched milk. Because the girl always had headaches, the sisters of Rillaar went to Hasselt with a photo of her.
188761: A man coming back along a remote road one evening from visiting his girlfriend saw a pack of cats walking ahead of him. The man gathered all his courage and walked through the pack of cats, kicking some of the animals. When one of the cats lay dead, the other animals cried: "Mother is dead, mother is dead!" The man arrived home in a sweat. The next day an old, thin, grey cat came to those people's house. The people let the animal in and fed it. When the man told of his experience and said that the cats had cried "Mother is dead!", the grey cat sprang out from under the stove and ran away.
188781: In a café in Koningshooikt the doors and windows flew open at midnight.
188788: At the house of a woman suspected of being a witch, beautiful plums could be seen lying around in winter.
188793: The toads sometimes seen sitting in the ditches were witches. You were allowed to kill a toad, because the animal would come back to life by itself.
188800: A maid had bet some men that she dared to take off the shirt of a returned dead person who appeared in the churchyard of Schaffen. As soon as the maid had taken the shirt from the ghost, the ghost kept crying: "Give me back my shirt, give me back my shirt!" When the maid came in with the shirt, the others suddenly knew who the ghost was; it was a family member who had died long ago. Together with the priest the maid had to go back to the churchyard to put the shirt back on the ghost. Shortly afterwards the maid died.
188804: A boy was peeling potatoes in a house where there was a five-year-old daughter. The child's parents had gone to Aarschot when a little old woman came to visit. Because the boy did not trust the woman, he said: "If you come any closer, I'll cut with my knife." The next day the boy heard that the girl had fallen ill. The woman had come by again and the mother had given her two slices of bread, both of which she had given to the little girl. When the child was ill, she slept all the time with one little foot in the cradle and the other hanging over the edge. The child grew up with a crooked head.
188819: A woman who could not churn butter was visited by a man who said: "There is evil involved here. A witch must be coming into this house!" The man gave the woman three packets, which she was not allowed to open. She had to hang one packet above the stable door, one in the house and one in the barn.
188882: A man was staying in a castle where three or four people had recently died. The man was very frightened because he always heard a strange calling in the castle. When one day the man asked what the ghost wanted, a woman's voice answered: "You must go to Scherpenheuvel, or else I cannot enter heaven." After the man had been to Scherpenheuvel, he no longer heard the calling.
188893: A drunkard who often beat his wife when he came home drunk had to get up one night to go to the toilet. But the man did not know that a cow had broken loose from his stable that night. When he saw a horned beast standing in his house, he was convinced the devil was before him. The man immediately thought of the beating he had given his wife the evening before and crept back into bed to tell his wife the devil was in the house. He promised at once that he would never beat his wife again. The woman got up and saw the cow. Then she laughed at her husband and told him he had only seen a cow. The woman would have done better to keep the truth to herself, for because she told her husband it was just an ordinary cow, she was still beaten afterwards.
188901: In Ezemaal people spoke of witte wijven (white women) or 'des blonkès femmes'. White women could sometimes be seen in the mists by the bridge over the Gete.
188915: In the old days people did not want an old woman to lay her hand on the children's heads.
188925: A farmer coming from the field with a full wagon saw a cat approaching, which ran between the horses' legs. Because of this the cart overturned. The man grew angry and beat his horses. A man from Landen came up and said: "You're mad to beat your horses like that! Do you see that cat running there? Take your whip and strike the wheel's axle. Then you'll hear her scream." When the man struck the axle, the cat had turned into a woman, who clutched her head and cried: "Ow, my head!" If you put a holy object under the stairs, no witches could come in. The man went to the priest and told him what had happened. The priest answered: "There is no harm here."
188928: Being ridden by the mare had something to do with sleep.
188944: A man lived next to an old woman who was said to be a witch. One day the man saw a crow flying and shot at it. The next day he saw that his neighbour was wearing a bandage around her arm.
188970: A woman who behaved strangely because she was bewitched had someone pray over her to lift the spell.
188994: A girl who was ridden by the mare had prayers read over her by the fathers of Teralfen. The girl died young. Two or three years later the parents had a second daughter. That girl had no health problems.
189003: On a farm a woman often wandered around, coming into the barn where the animal feed was prepared. Because three animals had died on that farm in one week, the people went to the friars of Dendermonde. There they were advised to let in no more visitors. The farm was also blessed and prayed over. After that there was no more misfortune there.
189036: One night in a hospital, a man began screaming so badly that the nurses came running. The man had been ridden by the mare. If you slept on your back at night, you could be ridden by the mare. You then felt as if you were being strangled and could no longer move. You tried to scream, but could not. Only when you had called out that person's name did the mare disappear. Whoever was ridden by the mare had a stoppage of the blood.
189062: Some young people were coming back from the fair. One girl in the group, however, did not get home. The girl was missing and was found again in Mechelen. After she came home, the girl kept receiving strange letters and books. For example, she got a book about Father Damien with a gold edge on the cover. The girl's father stood by the door with his gun, but when a letter was slipped under the door, strangely enough no one could be seen. In the end the books and letters were put on a wheelbarrow and taken to the convent. The girl was under the devil's influence. Perhaps she had danced with the devil at the fair.
189092:
On a farm in Moorsel they had some animals. They also grew flowers there. The farmer's son had just turned eighteen and wanted to modernise and expand the business. More animals were bought and a new stable with modern machines was built. When the stable was just finished, a woman came by to look at the building. But because that woman was suspected of being a witch, she was not let into the stable. From that day the people always had bad luck. The animals fell ill, miscarried or died.
When the butter friar made his annual round, the farmer's wife told him about the misfortune that had struck the farm. The friar advised the woman not to lose heart. A year later, however, there was still no improvement. This time the friar went up to the attic holding the exorcism of Saint Anthony. The man prayed over all the rooms. At the oven he stood for a good twenty minutes. Then the friar left the farm walking backwards. The cow that was still alive at that moment stayed healthy.
189114: A will-o'-the-wisp was the soul of an unbaptised child. In the evening, will-o'-the-wisps flew around people all the time. If one had baptised a will-o'-the-wisp, it disappeared.
189118: A man who had to go to Mechelen accidentally left too early because his watch had stopped and he wanted to be on the safe side. In Keerbergen the man suddenly saw a woman with loose hair, in her shift, coming from the churchyard. The woman sat down on the road right in front of the man with her arms in the air. The man was terrified. He believed the apparition was a dead woman who had come out of her grave because she had no rest.
189138: On his way to work one morning a man found a blue apron. The man took the apron with him and gave it to his wife in the evening. She, however, did not trust it. A while later the man found a fine black hat on the ground. The man put the hat on his head and showed it off, although someone warned him that the hat belonged to a witch. A few days later the man's boss found several hats and aprons and burned them in the oven. After that the man who had found the clothes fell ill and died.
189144: People who had been ridden by the mare were very frightened.
189165: A tree sawyer setting out at three in the morning saw something come down the Pelsberg and fall in the middle of the road. The figure stood there nodding. The man was scared to death. Later, however, he discovered that it was a loosened clump of earth on which a small tree was nodding in the wind.
189168: A child of about eighteen months always began to cry at eight o'clock in the evening. The boy had been given two and a half cents by someone. One day the parents went with their son to the friars of Affligem. On the way there the bus shook back and forth the whole time. On the way there everything went well. After the visit to the friars there were no more problems. The mother always received clothes from a woman from Lennik, and someone had warned her not to do that any more. The day before the people went to Affligem, that woman stood ready with a package to hand over. The boy's mother buried that package by the trees in the field.
189172: A healer who had to go to a sick cow had to walk through snow, although it was the middle of summer.
189183: In the old days people said that black cats were witches.
189200: A boy had heard a story from a man about a dead person who came out of his grave at midnight if one knocked on the ground and called: "Satan, Satan, come out!" The boy was so impressed by the story that, while drunk, he went and knocked on the ground somewhere and called: "Satan, Satan, come out!"
189202: A man who saw a cat walking beside him believed it was a witch and anxiously quickened his pace.
189217: In Bever many old people went to visit newborn children. If the child died shortly afterwards, people believed those people had bewitched it. An old woman who fell victim to such a situation was no longer welcome anywhere.
189235: A woman who had to go to the tax collector in Lebbeke was ridden by the mare and got lost. In the end she asked the way in Baasrode.
189258: On a farm in Okselaar they could not churn butter. One day they threw out a woman who regularly came to visit. After that they could churn butter again without any problems.
189261: A girl whose father was a prisoner of war went to her godmother to tell her that her sister had died.
