On the way the girl met a witch who already knew the child was dead, although no one had yet been with the dead child. The mother believed the witch had bewitched her daughter, causing the child to die at the age of eight months.
189301: When people went somewhere to borrow sourdough to bake bread, they often fell ill through witchcraft.
189312: People who had lost their way often believed they had been bewitched.
189321: A werewolf roamed a little lane behind a house in Willebringen. A farmer who went to the barber one evening to have his hair cut was attacked by the werewolf. But the farmer had a stick with him and hit the werewolf on the head with it until the beast bled. A moment later the man saw his neighbour standing beside him. When he got home, the man said to his mother: "Go to mass tomorrow and you will see someone come in with a wound on his forehead. That is the werewolf."
189334: When the animals were bewitched, a friar was called to pray over the stable with the Gospel of Saint John. The friar also said the prayer to Saint Benedict, because it was the most powerful prayer in the Catholic religion. In addition the people themselves had to pray nine Our Fathers, nine Hail Marys and the prayer to Saint Benedict every day.
189351: A witch walked around a coffin standing in the church. The next moment all the candles fell over.
189395: A farmer's wife from Krokegem always got maize or grain on her head and in the milk pail when she went to milk the cows in the evening. Strangely, no one could be seen. During the day nothing strange could be noticed at that spot.
189401: A woman knew that her neighbour's grandmother had a bad name. When the grandmother was visiting the neighbour one day, a loud bang was suddenly heard. A little later the neighbour's little son was dead. Meanwhile the woman had gone to her meadow to have her sheep tended. When she came back from the meadow, she met the grandmother, who said: "Well, he is dead, but you will get it." After that the woman was never healthy again. She was operated on two or three times in Leuven.
189411: Near the Waggelbrugge there once stood a castle called 'hof Texel'. In that castle lived a robber knight who attacked people and consorted with the devil. One night, during thunder and lightning, the castle collapsed as God's punishment. Whenever there was a thunderstorm at midnight, a fiery coach with bloodied horses was seen riding three times around the hill of Moorsel. The lord of the castle sat in the coach.
189421: A man was walking home with his girlfriend. On the way the man said to the girl: "I need to relieve myself. You go on ahead. If you meet anything, throw this red handkerchief at the apparition." Further on the girl met a werewolf and threw the handkerchief at the beast. When she got home, the girl noticed that her boyfriend had the red fibres of the handkerchief between his teeth.
189431: In a house in the Geilinckstraat in Bogaarden a strange knocking was always heard. When people went outside to look, there was nothing to be seen. On the third day the spirit appeared of a dead woman who had promised to build a chapel if she recovered from an illness. After the dead woman's wish had been fulfilled, the spirit was seen no more. On the priest's advice, the people had placed a white handkerchief on their hand and shaken the spirit's hand that way. The print of the dead woman's hand was burned into the handkerchief.
189461: A woman was accompanied on her way by stallichten (will-o'-the-wisps). They were the souls of children who wanted to be baptised. Stallichten usually appeared near woods.
189463: Every day an old woman came to a mother who had a small child and said: "What a lovely child!" One day the child was covered in fleas. After the mother had put a blessed candle behind the door, however, the woman could no longer come in. The mother said to the visitor: "Come in and make those fleas disappear." But the witch could not come in.
189468:
Near the factory in the Gasthuisstraat in Tienen, people had seen white floating figures in the evening.
One day a boy had said to a rag-picker woman from Tienen: "You are a wicked woman, because you frighten everyone. I'll make sure you can't carry on any more." At that the woman bewitched the boy so that he could no longer move his arm. The boy said to the woman: "If you don't undo the witchcraft, I'll kick you and hang you." After that the boy could move his arm a little again.
189471:
In Kester there was a robbers' den where the tongsnijders der Heide (tongue-cutters of the Heath) hid. People told children stories about the tongue-cutters to frighten them.
On a farm there were suddenly countless rats. At a certain moment the rats had disappeared, but the horse was dead. People then believed that witches had changed themselves into rats.
189474: Toads and cats were witches in the shape of an animal. If those animals were injured, a woman from the neighbourhood was often injured as well.
189475: In Bollebeek (Brussegem) lived a witch who made everything start shaking and the plates fall off the cupboard.
189521: A seamstress always found two fat lice on her body when she came home in the evening. The seamstress had been given those lice by a witch.
189570: In Huizingen lived a dirty woman who was suspected of being a sorceress. That woman could make people unable to get away and make them ill.
189594: A man from Averbode was coming back drunk from Okselaar at night. Suddenly the man saw a gentleman come out of the woods, who beat him up. That gentleman must have been the devil. After that incident the man always went to church. Before, he did not even go to church at Easter.
189605: A woman had bought a scapular from the Capuchins, together with a medal to put under the threshold. When the medal was lying there, a witch who was visiting could not leave the house. She tried to jump over the threshold but nearly fell to the ground. The witch could not get out by the back door either, because a medal lay there too.
189620:
In a house a hen was seen sitting by the drain hole for the water every evening. Because those people also always had misfortune, someone advised them to pour hot fat over the hen. When they had done so, the next day they saw a woman with bandages around her feet. That woman was a witch who could change into a hen.
A little devil was always seen sitting by the well.
189621: On a farm in Wolvertem, the cows in the stable were found untied one morning. To ward off the evil hand, the friars put a medal under the stable floor. After that the cows were no longer untied at night.
189647: A man coming home past the 'hierebos' (?) on the Muggenberg saw four nuns in the woods sitting at a table on which there were little lights.
189673: When people had misfortune in their stable or household, they believed they had been ridden by the mare. They would then go on a pilgrimage. Sometimes they also walked around the parish with a rosary to drive away the devil or a ghost.
189701: A butcher could not manage to stab a pig in the heart. When the butcher began to pray the Gospel of Saint John, he succeeded at once. An old woman who lived nearby had bewitched the pig.
189714: One was not to let a witch touch you. Sometimes, during a conversation, someone would tap you on the shoulder. People to whom that happened often became sick with fear and no doctor could help them.
189738: A man whose child was ill went to the friars, who said: "When you get home, there will be a toad in the house. You must take the animal and throw it into the stove. But make sure the stove door is properly shut, or else the toad will get away with just a burn." The man did as he was advised, but the door was not properly shut. Afterwards it was found that a certain woman had a mark on her cheek.
189753: People who were ridden by the 'moon' got up at night and were very restless. They sleepwalked. Such people were completely in the grip of the moon.
189794: A man who claimed he had been ridden by the mare was drenched in sweat when he came home.
189802: People who were ridden by the mare believed they had been touched by the evil hand.
189833:
A couple from Sint-Pieters-Leeuw had three daughters. Because all three girls had died, people believed their children had been struck by the evil hand. One of the girls had died in childbed in Ukkel. On the evening before her death she had said to her mother: "Mama, sleep with me, because tonight she is coming to get me."
Another man claimed that evil had no power over him because he always wore a medal.
189853: In the old days, when people had a lot of misfortune in their stable, they blamed it on a witch. The sexton brought those people a nail from the Easter candle. The nail was buried under the threshold of the stable. The woman who could not cross it was the guilty one. A woman who turned around before entering the stable was then branded a witch.
189876:
A woman noticed that her horses were always very sweaty and that their manes were braided. The horses had been ridden by the mare.
People could also be ridden by the mare. When that happened, they sweated heavily in their sleep.
189945: A man who had just become a father went on foot to Schriek to inform the child's godfather. On the way the man was hindered by a cat that jumped in front of his feet. The man said: "Pussycat, go away." The cat then answered: "Had pussycat not spoken so nicely, he would have broken his neck." On returning home the man went to the haystack, where he fell backwards and landed with his back on the harrow.
189951: A boy and a girl went to the dance. When the boy went home at midnight, he said to the girl: "If you meet a black dog, throw your white handkerchief at its mouth." A black dog did indeed come and the girl did as she had been advised. When the girl saw her boyfriend the next morning, she found to her great horror that he had the fibres of the handkerchief between his teeth. The girl died of the shock.
189956: In a house a few people gathered every evening to talk. In the washroom the people always heard noises, although there was nothing to be seen. But in the neighbourhood lived a woman with a crooked back who was suspected of being a sorceress. One evening the people boiled water. Around eleven or half past eleven one of the men stood with the bowl by the drain hole for the water. But it got later and later without anything crawling through the drain hole. The people decided to try again the next day. The next day a big black cat crawled in through the drain hole. The man quickly poured the boiling water over the animal. The sorceress who lived in the village was burnt. The friars of Leuven had to come several times before that woman could die.
189969: A wizard lived in Bekkerzeel. A man going to the field with his cow passed the wizard, who said: "That cow won't pull." The man went on and harnessed the cow to the plough. But the animal would not take a step. The wizard had bewitched the cow.
189972: In Kiezegem lived a witch from whom people did not dare accept pears or plums. If you did, you were struck by the evil hand. Witchcraft existed because priests sometimes forgot a word at someone's baptism.
189974: A woman who was married to a blacksmith and had four children fell ill one day. The doctor could not help her. The doctor advised the smith to go to a fortune-teller in Tienen for his wife. The man left at once. The fortune-teller said: "Wait, I must just fetch some holy water, but then I will help you." When she returned after a quarter of an hour, she said: "Your wife is ill, that I know. There is one person who can cure her. I will not say her name, because you know her better than I do. She brought your wife a hare only last week." The fortune-teller gave the man nails from the Easter candle to put under his threshold, so that the witch could no longer come in. The people also had to make a novena, and on the ninth day the witch would appear. When he got home, the man saw a great fire beside him. He did everything the fortune-teller had advised. On the ninth day a knocking was heard on the window. The man got up and said: "I will not let you in." The woman kept insisting, but the man stood firm. The woman said: "Do what you like, but I will come in, even if it is only with my head." Then the door was opened and the witch let in. She went to the room where the sick woman lay, took her hand and said: "Are you still lying here?", to which the sick woman replied: "You know that better than I do." When the witch said: "Come on, get up then," the woman got up and was never ill again. The witch never set foot in that house again.
189993: Will-o'-the-wisps were the souls of unbaptised children. The lights appeared mostly in winter around seven o'clock. A man returning from the fair saw a blue light moving back and forth. The light followed the man until he was home.
190050: A witch lived in Schoonderbuken. In the end the mission friars took away her magic power.
190073: A farm in Linden had been haunted for years. Every night the pigs and the horses there were sweating. In the end the people went to the friars of the Koud Water, who advised them not to pick up anything lying on the ground. The haunting lessened and the friar came once to have a look. He saw a crow sitting in a walnut tree and told the people to pray. Then the friar shot at the crow and hit the animal in the wing. The next day a neighbour woman lay in the ditch without an arm.
190090: A man no longer dared to go out on the street alone in the evening. Behind a bush on the Zavelberg sat some jokers who had dressed up as kludde (a shape-shifting goblin) with his chain. Some men who had got lost and ended up in a meadow in Tollembeek believed they had been bewitched by a sorceress.
190092: Since the Gospel of Saint John has existed, there has been no more witchcraft. If an Easter nail was stuck under the threshold of the church, the witches could no longer leave the church.
190098: In Hamme near Dendermonde a woman went to the monastery of Affligem. The friars said to the woman: "Watch carefully who comes into your house." When the woman opened the door in the morning, a fat toad came in. The woman kicked the toad to death. After that she had no more bad luck.
190100: The Germans tried to move a wagon, but could not do it even with eight horses. A witch had bewitched the wagon fast.
190106: Opposite a carpenter lived a woman suspected of being a witch. One day the carpenter's children got convulsions. The carpenter immediately sent for the brown friars, who said: "Yes, they are at work on you." A friar read prayers over the children and said: "Tonight at twelve o'clock the guilty one will come knocking here, but she will not be able to harm you any more." That night the carpenter and his wife indeed saw their neighbour coming, wearing a veil. The neighbour came and knocked on the door.
190116: A man who worked on a farm went to the field with two horses. On the way he met a woman who said: "Ah, your horse won't pull!" At the chapel the man indeed could no longer get the horses moving. The man cursed the woman, but she stood further on, laughing.
190142: In front of the sisters' school in Hakendover people always saw a hare running back and forth in the evening that no one could shoot. A large hare always sat on the windowsill of a woman from the village.
190181: Clergymen could fix people to the ground by magic, so that they could not go on.
190185: People who after their death did not know where they had to atone for their sins wandered about on earth and did people harm. The air is full of invisible spirits.
190214: In Keerbergen lived a witch with special powers. She made a woman who could not have children become a mother after all. But the woman had to suffer greatly for it. When the witch was with her, she saw a hundred witches.
190248: When butter would not come, people believed there was a witch in the churn.
190250: A farm in Meise was haunted. A farmer went to the cowshed with his gun, where he saw the bull's neck being wrung by an invisible figure. The farmer could not shoot at the ghost because he could not see anything.
190253: The Bleibergenhof in Keerbergen was said to be haunted. Some men driving to Mechelen had given a witch a ride. On the way the witch said: "I'm so thirsty, I'm so thirsty." A little later the men saw a whole row of redcurrant bushes along the road.
190269: A boy from Pamel took butter to the market in Ninove every Tuesday. While he was away, he had a witch look after his house. A few weeks later the boy had only half as much butter as before. A friar came and predicted that the witch would come knocking on the shutters of the house at midnight. At twelve o'clock the boy did indeed hear knocking.
190279: In Wemmel lived a woman who could do witchcraft. Whenever mothers went to be churched, that woman always came asking to see the baby. Later those children were bewitched. The only way to keep her out was to put something blessed under the threshold.
190331: Under the influence of witchcraft, people could sometimes get lost on a road they knew well.
190339: In Oppem (Brussegem) a farmer was close to despair because he could not store his rich harvest in his small barn. As the farmer walked around sadly, he met a gentleman dressed in black who offered to build him a new barn that would be finished before the first cockcrow the next morning. In exchange for the barn, the farmer had to give the gentleman his soul. The farmer agreed, but in the evening he grew very restless. Finally the farmer told his wife what he had done. The farmer's wife jumped out of bed at once and ran to the henhouse with the lantern. She struck her clogs together, so that the rooster began to crow too early. The next moment the farmer's wife heard all the devils of hell fleeing. In the morning a large barn stood in the farmer's yard. Because there was still a small hole in the roof of the barn, the farmer got to keep his soul. That hole could not be closed later until the parish priest had sprinkled it with holy water. That barn was called 'the devil's barn of Oppem'.
190344: On a farm worked a farmhand who dealt with evil. He always sat in the hedge and leapt onto the backs of passers-by. At the fair the farmhand said to his girlfriend: If you meet something, throw your handkerchief at it. When the girl saw a large figure appear, she did as she had been told. The next day she saw that the threads of the handkerchief were between her boyfriend's teeth. He himself was Kledde.
190380: A sorceress lived in Sint-Kwintens-Lennik. When people saw her, they suddenly could not go on and it seemed as if they were nailed to the ground. People who truly believed in her magic power waited, to be safe, until she had passed. Perhaps that is how the belief arose that the sorceress could make people stand still.
190388: Between Merchtem and Brussegem lived a coal merchant. By the man's house was a pond with ducks on it. At night ghosts wrung the necks of those ducks, although nothing could be seen. People who had been struck by the evil hand went on pilgrimage.
190410: A man went at night with a small axe to a turnstile where a werewolf sat. When the werewolf was struck by the man and began to bleed, he turned into a man from Wezeren. On Sunday that man sat in church with a bandage around his face.
190416: Because a man had moved a boundary post during his life, he had to haunt after his death.
190424: Many witches used to live in Herne. Farmers whose animals died from witchcraft went on pilgrimage. The friars of Affligem advised one farmer to stick the heart of a dead sheep full of pins and bury it in a remote place. The friar also predicted that the witch would fall ill and die. And so it happened.
190451: A man coming back one evening from visiting his girlfriend in Sterrebeek grabbed at a hen with chicks standing on the road. The hen then said: "Let go what goes, let stand what stands, and may you fare so well in future." The man then ran home as fast as he could.
190463: People who behaved strangely were sometimes said to have been ridden by the mare. People then consulted a woman who told them to make a novena before a statue of a saint and to pray three Our Fathers every day.
190465: In an old house lived a woman with a bad reputation. Because she was so old, she walked with a stick. One of her grandchildren had to keep the old woman company, but the boy always teased his grandmother. One day, to her great annoyance, the boy was playing with a friend. The two children were pelting each other with earth. The grandmother scolded her grandson, but he would not listen and threw earth at her. Suddenly the woman cried: "Watch out, boy, the coach driving there will overturn at the top of the hill!" The boy laughed at her, but a little later the coach did overturn. The coachman had great trouble getting the horse back on its feet. People believed the grandmother had bewitched the horse to frighten her grandson.
190470: A woman was tormented by her mother-in-law, whom she suspected of witchcraft. The mother-in-law wished, for instance, that her daughter-in-law would die in childbed, so that her son and granddaughter could come and live with her.
190472: A carpenter's son had heard that a certain woman was a witch. When he told his mother, she said: "Little man, you must not say that. Then you must not visit those people any more." When the boy saw a rabbit sitting on the road in Mazel, he grabbed at it, but it jumped away. His father said to him: "Leave that rabbit alone." If his father had not been there, the boy would have killed that rabbit.
190475: A man promised his sick wife that he would go on pilgrimage to Kortenbos if she recovered. A short time later the woman died, leaving the man alone with seven children. When the man came home from work in the evening, strange things always happened. The tobacco flew out of his pipe and his chair began to shake. When the man told his neighbours about the strange goings-on, he remembered the pilgrimage he had promised his wife. The next day the man hurried to Kortenbos. The whole way he felt as if he had to carry a heavy load. On arriving in Kortenbos the man felt the burden fall from him.
190476: On a haunted farm the cows were tied up back to front. The slaughtered pigs turned out to have no innards. The cows were in calf but never gave birth.
190478: A man had to drive a dung cart across a ditch. A farmer's wife suspected of being a witch said to him: "You'll never get across the ditch with a cart like that!" The cart did indeed get stuck in the ditch. The farmer's wife went over and said: "Come, let me have a try." She managed to free the cart and the horses.
190501: Two musicians coming home one evening were so scared that they began to sing. The men started sweating and got lost. They had been 'led by the als' (led astray by a spirit) or ridden by the mare. The men had to wander about all night and only reached home towards morning.
190508: A man who claimed he was ridden by the mare could not breathe at night. It felt as if a heavy load lay on him. By going to the fathers of Affligem, the man was eventually freed from the mare.
190509: A farmer was out with his horses. When the horses suddenly stopped, the farmer could not get them moving again in any way. A workman who was with him said something, after which the horses went on without any trouble.
190510: A man walking through the snow to a café in Breedhout saw a black cat sitting in the moonlight along the way. The man was afraid but walked on anyway. When he turned around a little further on, he saw that the cat had turned so that it was facing him.
190512: One evening in Attenhoven, a butcher from Dormaal was jumped by a big black dog. The butcher struck at the dog with his axe, at which the animal began to scream. Terrified, the butcher went home. The next day he saw that his neighbour was wearing a bandage around his arm.
190513: Children in Letterbeek were sometimes frightened with tales of an old woman. If she laid her hand on their heads, they would be bewitched.
190518: A man was returning from an inn with a friend at closing time (1). On the way he saw a young black cat jump out of a hedge. The cat kept rubbing against the man's legs. When the man grew annoyed with the cat, he kicked at it. His friend then said: "Watch out, you're not rid of it yet! That cat is a witch." A little later the cat came back, and the man chased it away again. When the two said goodbye and each went his own way, the man heard his friend praying the Gospel of Saint John.
190527: By the Brusselse Steenweg on the grounds of the abbey of Affligem there was a pit called 'the devil's pit'. A castle is said to have once stood nearby. The lord of the castle had criminals hanged on the gallows and then had their bodies thrown into the devil's pit. At night people heard murmuring and noise at that pit from the dead, who were said to have turned into devils.
190560: A woman was always afraid when she saw a black cat or a black crow, because she believed it was a witch in animal shape.
190563: Some men went poaching in the Emperbos and the Bezembos. Suddenly a large herd of hares came out of the Bezembos, which frightened the men so much that they did not dare to shoot. A little later a lame hare came by and asked whether the other hares had passed long ago.
190583: In Moerbeke a child lay dying. Because the child could not die, the priest was called, who said: "If that woman comes to see your child once more, let her in." No sooner said than done. After the woman's visit the child died almost at once. The priest had also said: "You will finally know who did this to your child. When it is buried, that person will come and look over the churchyard wall."
190592: Two sweethearts went to the fair. On the way the man said to his girlfriend: "I need to relieve myself for a moment." When her boyfriend was gone, the girl saw a dog approaching, which kept running around her. The dog bit off a piece of the ribbon of the apron the girl was wearing. When the girl saw her boyfriend coming back a little later, she noticed that he had that bit of ribbon between his teeth.
190610: In Aarschot lived a woman said to be a witch. Out of fear, everyone put small holy objects under their thresholds so that the witch could not come in.
190627: Two brothers who walked to Sint-Truiden always saw a little white rabbit that came to play at the crossroads by the Brustumpoort.
190646: A man never saw strange things in the evening when he held his small axe in his hand on the way. There was, however, always a man standing in the doorway of a house. But if the man did not take his axe, a dog jumped out of a tree stump and the man had to fight it. One day, however, the man put his axe in his pocket and held only his stick in his hand. When the man came back that evening, he had to fight the dog again. The man took his axe and threw it at the dog. The next moment a naked man stood before him. It was the man who always stood in the doorway of his house. That man, who was a werewolf, said: "If you tell the village that I am a werewolf, I will kill you, even if I have to do it while you lie in your bed at night."
190663: When the animals in the stable were sick, people went on pilgrimage. A farmer and his wife had bought a fine grey heifer. Shortly afterwards a woman from the neighbourhood went into the stable where the heifer stood and stroked its back. Soon after, the heifer miscarried. Once the farmer had made a pilgrimage to Grimbergen and bricked a nail from the Easter candle under the threshold of his stable, nothing strange happened any more.
190669: In winter, will-o'-the-wisps were often seen in damp places. People believed those lights were the souls of unbaptised children. In reality the lights were simply sulphur.
190688: A witch always carried a basket of fruit and had a black cat with her. One day some people came to tell the witch that her horse had fallen into the ditch. The witch replied: "By the time I get there, it will be out. Here is a basket of fruit." Of course the people did not eat the fruit but threw it away at once. By the time the witch reached the marshy meadow, the horse had indeed already climbed out of the ditch.
190705: By the Essenbeek on the Malheide a dead man walked about with a boundary post on his shoulders. The man kept calling: "Where shall I put it? Where shall I put it?" One day a drunkard answered: "Damn it, put it where you got it!" After that the ghost was never seen again.
190727: On a chilly November night a farmhand went to fetch water for his horses. When the boy scooped water from the pool, a thousand dooplichten (baptism lights, will-o'-the-wisps) came flying towards him, wanting to be baptised. Because there were so many lights, the farmhand could not baptise them all. The lights pushed the farmhand into the water and he drowned.
190739: In Meldert a child of seven or eight had a fever of forty degrees. The doctor came and said: "That will take time." When the child was still not better after three days, the priest was called, because the child behaved strangely at night while sleeping between its mother and grandmother. It flew up into the air and sometimes crawled up the walls. After the doctor had come a second time, the priest read prayers over the child. The next day the child was cured. The father was convinced the priest had cured his son, but the doctors would not admit it. To prove his house had been struck by the evil hand, the man had his neighbour come over one evening, who saw the ghostly happenings with his own eyes. The priest warned the father that the person who had caused the evil would return, but that he must not harm her. When the woman came by, the man stood ready with his dung fork to stab her to death, but he did not dare touch her after all.
190744: A man who lived on the Welvaart in Kiezekom had promised to have a number of masses said. Because the man died before he had kept his promise, he had to come and haunt after his death. The dead man's family heard knocking on the wall and a voice asking for the promised masses to be said. When the man's wife had the masses said, the dead man no longer appeared.
190769:
If a witch had touched a towel, the towel would afterwards disappear. Animals touched by witches fell ill. That was the evil hand.
Sometimes a thump was heard on the door, and shortly afterwards people found a black hand on the door.
190781: A woman saw a big dog standing on the Lieve-Vrouwweg in Halle. That dog was a neighbour woman standing there in the shape of an animal. If such a dog was kicked, the neighbour woman felt pain.
190782: A witch from Attenhoven had given her own son a hunchback. She had even bewitched her granddaughter, so that the girl could only walk on crutches. In the shape of a bird, the witch bewitched the child of a man from Halle, which then died. In that child's little pillow a small bird's nest made of thorns was found.
190794: Three people coming back from Denderwindeke at night were surrounded by a dog. The men tried to shoot at the animal, but their revolver did not work.
190809: Witches could turn themselves into animals.
190819: A woman from Diest always came to a house in Loksbergen asking for a slice of bread. When two children died in that house, people believed that woman had caused the misfortune.
190823: In a house the potatoes in the attic began to dance. The parish priest came to the house to put an end to the haunting.
190827: In Kaggevinne lived a woman suspected of being a witch. Anyone the witch struck on the head always had pain somewhere.
190829: In Tollembeek lived a certain woman from whom children were not allowed to accept sweets.
190834: An old woman was cutting grass for her cow along the side of the ditch. A farmer's wife working in a nearby field came over and said: "Why don't you sell your cow", whereupon the old woman struck her on the shoulder and replied: "You sell your cow!" The farmer's wife then hurried to strike the old woman on the head so that she would not be bewitched.
190835: A man who worked in a brewery always came home rather late. On the Vlieringenberg he always heard a little dog barking. But when he looked back, he saw no dog. The man never knew where the sound came from. He believed it had something to do with witchcraft.
190841: Women who had a black cat were often suspected of being witches.
190854:
When witches laid their hands on the animals in a stable, the animals fell ill.
On a farm that had a fine calf, a man had laid his hand on the animal. The next day the calf began to pine. A short time later the people had a great deal of misfortune in their stable.
190867:
On a farm in Ganshoren a new cow had been bought. Right away the people had a visit from a woman asking for a litre of milk.
A few weeks later the people were working in the fields during the day. When they came home around half past three or four in the afternoon, they saw that the cow had been shorn. The animal no longer gave even a litre of milk. At night the witch could often be seen crouching somewhere to frighten people.
190870: A man delivering two pigs saw an old woman coming over the dyke at the Uil. Whenever the pigs reached that spot, they backed away in fear. After twenty failed attempts the man began to pray the Gospel of Saint John. After that the pigs could cross the dyke.
190872: A little boy had fallen victim to a sorceress, who had conjured his body full of pins.
190885: Two men were sawing wood in a saw pit in the meadow. Two women came there to gather wood chips. At eleven o'clock one of the women left because she had to start cooking. The other woman stayed, so the men said: "You're still here! How will you have the meal ready by noon?" The woman answered: "Oh, that's no problem. I'll just swing it between my legs and it will be ready." When the second woman finally went home, her cooking pot was already simmering before she was even inside.
190897: In Oetingen a child had fallen ill after being touched by a woman. After a visit to the friars of Affligem, the child was cured.
190898: If you could take seven steps in a witch's footprints, she could go no further. One winter, after it had snowed, a man decided to test whether a woman from the village was a witch. After the man had taken five steps in the witch's footprints, she turned around and said: "Go on ahead, for you can walk faster than I can." On the way back the man did exactly the same, and the witch said the same thing again.
190899: A man returning from the fair at Esse walked past a bewitched house. There he saw a pretty kitten, which followed him. The man wanted to keep the kitten, but when he tried to pick it up, it crept into the hedge. The man lured the animal into his house with some milk. After the animal had drunk two plates of milk in no time, the man put it in the attic because it could not escape from there. When the man went to look in the attic the next morning, the cat had vanished.
190908: A man was taking a basket with a parcel to the station at Neerwinden. When he saw a white hare sitting in the ditch, he kicked at the animal. Then he saw the hare a long way further on. The same thing happened several more times.
190925: A girl worked as a maid on a farm where there was also a farmhand who was said to be a werewolf. One day the werewolf's animal skin had been found and thrown into the oven. At that very moment the farmhand stood in front of the oven, even though all the doors had been shut. If you could make a werewolf bleed, you could unmask him.
190927: In Meldert a man met the priest, who had brought him home from the station when he came back from the army because his father had died. The man told the priest that everyone in his family had died except his daughter and his youngest son. The man believed witchcraft was at play, and the priest admitted that it did indeed exist. The priest told how one day he had had to read prayers over a house in which knocking was heard every night. After he had read over the house and its occupants, the knocking stopped. The woman responsible for that evil passed her arts on to her daughter. That daughter in turn passed them on to her daughter, and that daughter passed them on to her husband.
190929: A child had been born in a house in Kraainem. The people took the midwife home in the horse and cart. On the way the cart was suddenly pushed over by an invisible hand. The people set the cart upright again, but the horse would not go on. All this was caused by the evil hand.
190945:
In Sint-Lambrechts-Woluwe lived a couple with one son and one daughter. The mother loved her son dearly and hated her daughter just as much. The mother was a witch. When she could not bewitch strangers, her own daughter became the victim of her torments. Further along lived a man and a woman who had two daughters. The witch often sent her son to the elder daughter, who was very beautiful. But the girl wanted nothing to do with the boy. When she became engaged to another man, she became the victim of the witch's torments. One day a violent storm broke out as the girl was coming home from work, so she had to shelter in the doorway of the witch's house. The witch opened the door and said: "Come in, my son is home!" The girl answered angrily: "My fiancé is enough for me!", to which the witch replied: "We'll see about that." A few days later the girl got a high fever. The doctor found she had tuberculosis. The bewitched girl's mother sent for a White Father. The priest could hardly get into the house because the bewitchment was so strong. After the priest left, the girl died.
At school the witch's daughter said: "You see; whoever doesn't love my brother won't get any other man!"
190950: A woman who lived in the village always sat at her window talking to herself. A man taking his cow to the bull had to pass her little house. At that moment the woman came to the door in her nightshirt. The cow ran off, and the man had to chase it for an hour before he could catch it.
190953: A man who dealt with the devil and had to manure the field said: "Each his heap." After that the field was manured in no time. People could not believe their eyes.
190956: A woman sent for the priest for her sick husband. The priest told her: "You must take a kilo of salt to Onze-Lieve-Vrouw ter Steen. You must not go on living here either, for something is not right here." A witch lived in the neighbourhood. So the people moved away.
190959: Some people from Hekelgem drove their dog cart to the early market in Wolvergem. On the way they saw cats, which they supposed were the wizards and witches of Wolvergem.
190974: During the popinjay shooting in Kortrijk-Dutsel a witch said: "As long as I stand here, no one will shoot down the bird." And so it was. The bird was hit once, but it did not fall. Only after the witch had left did someone manage to shoot the bird down.
190980: To protect themselves against the mare, people placed their slippers or clogs upside down next to the bed.
190989: In a family in Halle a little child had died. The parents believed the child had been bewitched by a woman who often visited them. When they told the priest, the clergyman said: "You must put a blessed candle in a corner of your house, and then the witch will no longer be able to come in." After the people had followed his advice, the witch indeed never crossed their threshold again.
190999: A woman from the Engelbeekstraat in Schaffen was churning butter. It would not come, so in the evening she was still churning without any result. Meanwhile a witch from the neighbourhood had already gone to sell the butter at the market in Diest.
191013: In the neighbourhood of a woman who was said to be able to make children die, it was noticed that a striking number of young children were dying. The people went to the friars, who asked: "Are you on good terms with the neighbours?", to which the people replied: "Yes, they give us butter and melted fat." Then the friars said: "Then they will be the guilty ones."
191016: A man who had got lost in foggy weather knocked at a house. The woman who lived there said to her husband: "You mustn't let that man in, because he has been ridden by the mare! He could bewitch our whole house!"
191021: At the Kregelberghof in Bierbeek there worked an insolent farmhand who cursed all day long. When the farmhand was coming back cursing from the fair in Hasselt one night, he met a lit coach with two horses. The coach wanted to take him along, but he managed to flee into the field just in time.
191044: Toads had to be killed, because those animals were witches.
191068: A man stood at a crossroads with a black hen, where he talked with the devil. One day a farmer and his son met that man in the form of a werewolf. When they met the man again at the fair, he said to them: "You will meet a werewolf, but you must throw a handkerchief at the beast." Later the man was seen with the fibres of the handkerchief between his teeth. Since the Gospel of Saint John has existed, such evil no longer exists.
191077: In the old days there were many will-o'-the-wisps in the woods. Those lights moved back and forth all the time. They were the souls of unbaptised children.
191078: People who were ridden by the mare felt as if their throat was being squeezed shut.
191086: A girl went to the shop with her sister. On the way the girl met a woman who had a little black dog. Although the woman knew the girl was afraid of the dog, she said to the animal: "Go on, get Marie!" Then the little dog grew as big as a cat, and the girl, terrified, ran away with her sister.
191106: On a farm in Grimbergen, the farmer's wife saw a strange woman walk past the animals' fodder every day. The next day the farmer stayed at home to keep an eye on things. When the farmer saw the witch walking around a heap of clover, he shouted: "What on earth are you doing here? Get out of here or I'll pour a bucket of manure over your head!" After that the woman never came to the farm again.
191112: In Battel (a hamlet of Mechelen), a woman came peddling herring. A little girl always got a small herring from the woman that she did not have to pay for. One morning the girl kept screaming: "The herring woman is there! She's there, mum!" The girl's neck had also turned blue. One morning the herring seller sat on a bridge saying that the child was dead, although nobody knew that yet.
191118: In the old days, when walking through a cornfield, one often saw lights that kept retreating. At a certain spot the light would hang in the air, as if to say: "Here I am on my ground". People believed that an aborted or newborn child was buried in such places.
191126:
The husband of a pregnant woman often went to a café in the village to drink jenever. One day the café owner's daughter came to ask the woman if she could be the baby's godmother. The woman was reluctant, but her husband felt she could not refuse such a thing. So on the day the child was baptised, they went to the godmother's house. The woman there kept walking from one room to another, saying: "What a beautiful baby! What a beautiful baby!" When the mother was at the godmother's with her child the next day at about the same time, the child's head swelled up. The mother believed her child had been bewitched and went to the convent of the Poor Clares in Leuven. She took half a franc and a red cabbage to give to the sisters. One of the sisters said to her: "Go home, little lady. One of your children will recover, but the other will become a little angel for heaven." What the sister foretold came true.
Some time later the woman was pregnant again. In all she had ten children. The café owner's daughter again asked if she could be godmother to that second child. But the mother answered: "That child stays here and I will have it baptised myself!"
191127: In the Kerselarenstraat in Meldert stood a haunted house. Every night the furniture flew around there and the windows opened by themselves. In reality the haunting was probably down to coincidences.
191136: A man was convinced that someone had bewitched his cows during the night, for he had heard the animals kicking and stamping. When the man went to look in his stable in the morning, he found that the door was still locked.
191163: A farmer's wife out with her cow had to pass a witch in Sint-Pieters-Rode. Suddenly the cow stood still. Three quarters of an hour later the cow died. The animal had probably seen the witch. Two women were coming back from Leuven with a stable hand, where they had bought three pairs of clogs. When they had to drive past a witch's house, the stable hand said: "You mustn't talk about the witch now, because she can hear it." Some way further on, a little boy spoke to them and said: "You've lost your clogs." The clogs were standing neatly in a row in front of the witch's house.
191187: In a house in Tollembeek, the child began to cry after a visit from a woman suspected of being a witch. The child died at the age of seven or eight months.
191197: A man had built a fine new house in Lanaken. In that house he always heard noise in the attic at night, although nothing could be seen.
191205: A farmhand worked on a haunted farm. The farmhand wanted to put an end to the witchcraft and decided to keep watch one night. Towards midnight the farmhand saw lots of cats coming in down the chimney. The cats danced paw in paw while singing: "The farmhand is not dead yet." The farmhand took the cooking pot and poured boiling water over the cats. The next day a good many women from the neighbourhood had burns.
191223: A woman often saw stallichtjes (will-o'-the-wisps) between Woluwe and Opheule. They were the souls of unbaptised children.
191245: In Eliksem lived a woman who was said to have special powers. Perhaps she had not been baptised properly. One day, when the milkman was returning from Oplinter, the witch stood by the roadside and said: "You won't go one step further." The milkman laughed, but his horses did indeed stand still. The milkman cursed, but it did no good. The horses only went on after the witch had made the sign of the cross.
191246: A farmer and a farmhand who had gone together to put the horses in the meadow decided to rest for a while. When the two men woke up, they saw two ghosts sitting at the table counting money. Back home, the farmer and the farmhand resolved to overpower the ghosts the next day. The plan went completely wrong, however; one of the men was beaten to death by the ghosts and the other was so badly battered that he looked like an old man.
191260: Farmers who had a lot of misfortune often believed they had been struck by the evil hand. In Beigem, for instance, there lived a strange woman who was always out and about between midnight and one o'clock. If that woman tapped you on the shoulder, you always had to strike higher to protect yourself. If you put a medal under the threshold, a witch could not come in.
191269: A man always saw his mother appear before him on the road at night. She had promised a pilgrimage to Brustem but had still not fulfilled that promise. After people had gone begging for money so the pilgrimage could be made, the dead woman no longer appeared. But the man spent the money on drink, so that after a while his dead mother appeared again.
191281: A farm suffered a great deal of misfortune. Healthy piglets suddenly got blue ears and dropped dead. The people went to the friars of Affligem, where a cleric told them: "You must not let just anyone near the animals' sty. Only the butcher, the vet and a buyer may be let in." The friars also came to bless the farm and the people had to do a novena. After that the misfortune ended. It was discovered that a neighbour was responsible for the evil. She was the mother of a friend of the farmer's wife. When a mare was about to foal at midnight on the farm, someone rattled the gate. It was that neighbour, asking whether her son was there. Fortunately the foal survived.
191290: Of a woman who had died of a lung disease, it was said that she had fallen victim to the evil hand.
191296: One night on the Sollenberg in Huizingen, a man was pounced on by a black cat. That cat was a witch. Crows were also often witches.
191302: The little nun of M. had secretly left the convent to live with a man. Our Lady took her place in the convent. After her death the nun had to come back to haunt riding on a sow.
191323: On a farm there were seven sons who had to manure the field at night. The first son set off, but came back a little later pale with fright. He claimed he had seen a ghostly apparition. The second son set off, but he too returned frightened. And so all seven sons came back without having done the job.
191340: When people saw a white cat on their way home in the evening, they ran away because they believed they had seen the devil.
191359: In the past people were not allowed to put their clogs crossed next to their bed, because then they would be ridden by the mare.
191364: In Keerbergen there lived a witch who had the finest hens and the best eggs in the whole region.
191368: A girl had been given a piece of gingerbread by the wife of her godfather. Because the girl fell ill afterwards, people believed she had been bewitched by that woman. The parish priest prayed over the girl until the drops of sweat rolled down his face.
191373: People who had got lost and kept ending up in the same place said they had been bewitched.
191379: On a farm in Neervelp people heard wheelbarrows being driven in the barn in the evening.
191382: In Schaarbeek a farmer was struggling with a plague of rats. One day an old woman came, walked three times around the farm and advised the people to leave the stable door open. Two weeks later the rats were on another farm.
191394:
A certain Jan going to Lubbeek saw a black cat, which sang: "Jan asked me: pussycat, where do you come from?" The man struck at the cat, but the more he struck, the more cats appeared.
A woman who had struck at the tillekesjacht (a spectral hunt) with a stick afterwards found that the stick had been bitten all over.
191426: In the old days there were people who had books with which they could turn earth into mice.
191429: A witch lived in Hespen. One day a brewer's wagon came driving past, and the witch said: "Whoa, no further." The horses stood still. Whatever the carter did, he could not get the horses to move. Only when some people had given the witch a thrashing with a whip did the horses start moving again. Everyone was afraid of that witch. She was a small woman who always wore a cloth on her head.
191430: On the little path beside a pond, a man was always followed by a cat. In his panic the man fell onto a harrow near the Schriekdreef in Wolvertem. At the bend by the barn the cat always disappeared. Perhaps that cat was a witch.
191432: Black cats were witches in animal shape.
191437:
One morning a woman who could foretell the future said to a man: "Congratulations on your baby son!" But the child had not yet been born.
The friars had told the father: "The first person to call on you in the morning is the witch." That woman was the first to visit.
191441: A woman from Oppem (Brussegem) had fallen shortly after giving birth, leaving her with a wound on her leg. The doctor found that the wound could not be healed and that amputation was the only solution. Because the woman did not want her leg amputated, she went with her husband to a healer in Jette, who was also clairvoyant. She said to the man: "Tomorrow you must fetch such and such from the garden and put it on your wife's leg. In the evening someone will come by to ask for something, but you must not give it, for that is the person who caused this harm. Next week go and see your mother in Wolvertem, for it has been three months since you were there." That evening an eighty-year-old woman did indeed come to ask for a box of matches. They did not give it to her and said: "No, I can't give you that, I'm on my last box myself." A week later the wound on the woman's leg had healed. A neighbour did not believe a word of the healer's miraculous intervention and said: "That's all sorcery." Some time later, however, that neighbour got toothache and asked the woman to go with her to the healer in Jette. The healer said to the neighbour: "There is nothing you can do here, because you laughed at me. I have no power over you."
191445: A mother who already had seven children gave birth to twins. When the girl and the boy were about six years old, the mother was visited by a woman from Neervelp. The woman asked the mother if she could pick up one of the children, and the mother did not dare refuse. The woman picked up the little boy. As soon as the woman had left, however, the child began to cry incessantly. The doctor was at a loss. Shortly afterwards the child died crying.
191447: One Sunday a farmhand went home to fetch clean clothes. When he came back to the farm, he felt a wind blowing behind him. At night the farmhand also suffered a great deal; he then felt the wind in his chest. When the man carried a blessed candle with him, he was freed from the mare.
191453: A suspicious woman lived in a clay house in Sint-Kwintens-Lennik. When she was out in the street and saw children nearby, she often knelt down to breastfeed them. The husband of this witch was a Bohemian.
191454: Wizards could make people stand still by looking them in the eyes.
191475: On a farm in the Hoogstraat, the friars were called in because the horse had been bewitched. A friar prayed over the horse and hung a medal around the animal's neck. After that the bewitchment ended.
191478: A woman whose child cried all the time sought advice from the friars of Edingen. The friars advised her not to let a certain woman come near her child any more. In reality the mother did not have enough time to care for her child properly.
191483: Witches could turn themselves into a black cat.
191487: The Zwarte Madam (Black Lady) was a shadow that followed people at night in the moonlight.
191491: People who could not make butter often believed they had fallen victim to a witch.
191493: Klurre was a water spirit with a chain. Anyone who came too close to the water was pulled in by Klurre. When a homosexual man had died in Gooik, people believed his ghost came back. A man who saw lights appearing in the evening knelt down and said: "Ghost, what do you want?" In reality the man saw the lights of woodcutters working in the forest.
191522: A woman sitting in her parlour was seized by the wrists by the devil. The woman's wrists were burned, and the carpet was burned where the devil had walked.
191528: In the woods of Pellenberg there used to be many lodders (mischievous spirits that jump on people's backs). People who had to carry lodder had to try to make him bleed. That was how you could unmask lodder.
191539: In Vlezenbeek lived a man who could take the shape of a cat, a dog or a donkey.
191559: At night a woman always heard the doors slamming open and shut, and she felt her pillow being pulled. When the woman went to the parish priest for advice, the cleric asked: "Did you not perhaps promise a pilgrimage?" and the woman answered: "Yes, I did promise that." After the woman had the mass said that she had promised, the ghost stayed away.
191562: A woman who lived next to a marl pit had a lot of misfortune. Two children had already died in her house. Before each death the stairs could be heard creaking in the house. When a woman in the family was pregnant, the stairs were heard creaking. The woman had a miscarriage. People were convinced that the neighbour had bewitched the unborn child.
191568: Anyone who still had to go out in the evening was advised to take a black shawl along for protection against sorcerers and witches. They could not harm their victim until they had completely unravelled that shawl. The next day the sorcerers or witches could be recognised by the black fibres between their teeth.
191587: In the Asbroek a man was jumped by a werewolf. When the man came into the café he was almost dead, because he had had to carry the werewolf a long way.
191589: A witch could turn herself into a toad.
191598: One evening a mother had put her laundry outside to soak. After the mother had a visit from a witch, her baby fell ill. She took the baby to the sacristy of a monastery.
191603: In Oppem (Brussegem) there is a barn that was built by the devil. A farmer who needed a barn had sold his soul to the devil in exchange for a new barn, which had to be finished before the first cockcrow the next morning. When the rooster crowed in the morning, there was still a hole in the barn. That hole could never be closed afterwards.
191606: Will-o'-the-wisps were the souls of murdered children who had died unbaptised.
191613: If you could make the werewolf bleed, he did nothing and disappeared immediately.
191630: At the farm of the Plein, the farmer's wife was home alone one Sunday evening. Suddenly the woman heard a knocking, after which a little white dog came in. The dog walked to a corner and lifted a floor tile. The dog brought up a box containing the money it held in its paws. Then the dog went away again. After the farmer's wife had dug up the money, the little white dog no longer appeared.
191636: A woman always had problems giving birth because her waters would not break. One day the woman's husband went to seek advice. Afterwards the man noticed that a toad always came into his house through the drain hole for the water. One day the man struck the toad's legs off. The next day it was found that one of the neighbour women no longer had any hands.
191654: A girl whose mother had died saw the ghost of her dead mother standing by her bed every night. The priest advised the girl to wrap a sheet around her hand and shake hands with the ghost that way. When the girl did as the priest had advised the next night, the ghost's hand was burned into the sheet.
191669: A midwife could not die. When the woman was finally dead after all, a dog always appeared in her house to haunt it.
191697: A man was often ridden by the mare, so that he could not speak. Only when someone managed to call out to the mare did the tormenting spirit leave. If you put your clogs upside down next to your bed, you were protected against the mare. People who wanted to be freed from the mare went to the monastery of Affligem. Many people have already died because of the mare.
191700: In Gaasbeek there lived a witch who would pull loose the ties of people's aprons. People to whom this happened believed they had been bewitched.
191714: A man was run over and killed the day after he had visited a witch. In the past some seventeen witches lived in Rillaar.
191724: A witch lived in Orsmaal-Gussenhoven. Sometimes this witch made it impossible for the farmers to go on with their horse and cart. A man returning from Kermt with his cart one evening found that his horse stood still at the house where the witch lived. The man had to have the witch come to the cart. After the woman had said: "Come on now. As far as I want and no further," the cart moved again and the man could go home.
191745: A boy was bewitched after accepting a sweet from someone. The neighbour had fetched the parish priest, who gave her a medal. The cleric had predicted that the witch would not come in again. The witch came by once more afterwards, but the farm was closed and she could not get in.
191749: In the house of a sorcerer from Kampenhout, baskets hung from the ceiling. With spells the sorcerer could make a black cat jump from one basket to another. The animal would then say: "Menneke Pek."
191769: On a farm plagued by rats and mice, an old woman was suspected of having sent the vermin. When the farm had bought a cow, they had to lead the animal past the witch's house. At that moment the witch must have put the evil hand on the animal. Three days later the cow stopped giving milk.
191773: In a haunted castle in Sint-Joris-Winge people always heard something rattling. That castle remained empty for a long time.
191800: Whoever turned around to look at a witch fell to the ground. If you crossed a witch's footprint, she could go no further and looked back. If that happened, you would do well to make the sign of the cross, but you could be sure the witch would take revenge.
191802: Will-o'-the-wisps were wandering souls of unbaptised children, who followed people.
191803: A woman staying somewhere heard the gates slam shut at night, although nothing could be seen. The friars came to bless the stables there because the people had so much misfortune. Old farms where one could live cheaply were often haunted.
191805: In the old days children were not allowed to spin knives on the table. The person the blade pointed to would then suffer misfortune.
191808: Two men walking home at night saw twelve cats walking one behind the other.
191812: On a farm in Viane one of the animals had died. The next day a witch came to visit.
191834: A werewolf or a foal often haunted the Houtveld. A man from Velp was not afraid and claimed that he would not carry the werewolf but would give it a sound thrashing. The man managed to make the werewolf bleed, whereupon it took on its human form. The werewolf said to the man: "If you dare betray me, you're dead." Werewolves worked on the devil's orders and always had seven stuivers in their pocket.
191835: A man coming back from the inn along the Steenhuffelstraat on a Sunday evening saw, next to every telephone pole along the road, a man standing who was even taller than the pole. Suddenly the man remembered that it had been a long time since he had last gone to Mass at Easter. The man hurried home, for he was convinced he had seen devils.
191865: Two poachers out hunting hares saw a dog running in the moonlight. The dog crawled into a tree stump and reappeared a little later, but in the shape of a man. In the tree stump the poachers found an animal skin. They went to tell the werewolf's wife what they had seen. The woman went to the priest, who advised her to take the animal skin out of the stump and throw it into the oven. That proved not so easy, however, for the skin kept flying back out of the oven. The farmer meanwhile was working in the field with his oxen. At a certain moment he left his oxen and ran home, saying: "Are you burning me now?" The priest read prayers over the farmer, and after that his skin could be burnt.
191877: A man coming back from Tienen saw a friar in the Witteboomstraat and asked: "What's wrong with you, or who are you?" The friar answered: "I am a friar, and I still have to hear three masses. Won't you do that for me?" Franske K. agreed, but forgot his promise. Some time later the man met the haunting friar again in the same place. "Well, lad," said the ghost, "you haven't heard a mass yet!" Franske answered: "I'll start tomorrow." When Franske met the haunting friar one last time, the friar said: "Thank you. Now I don't have to come back any more."
191899: At a certain spot in Helen-Bos there sat a little white rabbit.
191921: A midwife who met a strange apparition on her way said: "If you come from God, speak. If you come from the devil, be gone." After that the woman saw and heard nothing more.
191934: A woman with a bad reputation always came to a house in the Molenstraat. She always went to the child there. After a while, however, the child did nothing but cry, so the neighbours advised the people not to lend that woman anything any more. They followed the advice and the child stayed healthy.
191935: In Merchtem-Peizegem dozens of people came to look at a grave that had risen up. The phenomenon had been caused by a burrowing mole.
191936: Women who had given birth and had not yet been churched made sure nobody came near the child. For witches could bewitch the child as long as the mother had not yet been churched.
191959: Some people went on pilgrimage to Halle on foot. On Sunday morning they went for coffee in a café in Halle. The old woman serving them asked where they came from. When they explained they came from Moorsel, the woman said: "I've been there often. I usually came there at night in 't Hol. You needn't be afraid of me any more, because I've been to the friars to be freed from witchcraft." The people asked how the woman had ever got to Moorsel, and she said: "A wind rises, and it takes you straight to your destination."
191992: One evening a man had to carry death notices to people through the snow. On the way he met a gentleman, who said: "Well, you're out late," to which the man replied: "Yes, I still have to go to Rommersom." The gentleman then said: "I'm going there too. I'll take those notes along for you." The man agreed. The gentleman had barely left when a big dog crawled out of the ditch and kept getting under the man's feet, so that he lost his way and had to knock on a door somewhere. After the man had been brought back to the right road, he saw a large foal coming, running so fast that his cap flew off his head. When the man passed a small chapel, the foal had vanished. After that the man found his way back. The moment he learned that nobody in Rommersom had received a death notice, the man was sure he had met the devil.
192006: On a farm the pigs raged for several days as if possessed. A neighbour who was said to be a witch had visited the farm several times. The people had the farm blessed by the parish priest, who advised them not to let that neighbour in any more. By following this advice, the people were freed from the evil hand.
192022: A shepherd who was married to a witch was thrown out because, according to his wife, he drank too much. The man had probably taken to drink because of all his misery. It was often said that witches lay in bed with the devil at night. They drew their power from their dealings with the devil.
192047: A boy went with his mother to take potatoes to the market. Ahead of the pair went a woman from the village who was reputed to be a witch. It seemed as if the woman could not move forward. When she was urged to hurry, the woman said: "Yes, but I can't get on. There's always a cat running in front of my wheel."
192057: A werewolf roamed the fields of Attenhoven. Some men had found the werewolf's skin and thrown it into the oven while the werewolf was tending the sheep. The werewolf came home roaring like a lion, but his skin had already burnt up.
192061: One evening a man from Grimde was coming back from the Polderveld along the Keistraat. Suddenly the man heard a noise in the air. It was the Tillekesjacht (a flying troop of witches) flying past. These were seven women who had sold their souls to the devil and who made beautiful music. The man went to the women and they treated him to a drink in an inn. When the man said: "God bless you," the women had vanished again. The next day the man brought the cup back to a fat farmer's wife who lived near him. The farmer's wife said to the man: "Tell no one what you have seen. If you keep quiet, you'll get the best cow in my stable. In two years my term is up. If you betray me, I'll have to start all over again."
192077: In a disreputable café between Moorsel and Lebbeek people danced to accordion music. One day a man with horse's legs and horseshoes came into the café. It was the devil.
192092: On a farm many cows and horses died. In a period of ten or twelve months no fewer than eighteen cows died there. The cows that survived no longer became pregnant. Finally it was decided to call in the brothers from Leuven. After that the situation improved. On the Rot there lived many people who had fallen victim to witchcraft.
192093: People who were ridden by the mare were very nervous and perhaps even had a nervous disorder.
192098: People who claimed they were ridden by the mare were in reality drunkards who were hallucinating.
192118: A man whose father had died heard knocking in the attic at night. The next day the man told his mother what he had heard. "That is your father," the woman said, "you must pray for the repose of his soul." When the man and the woman had prayed for the dead man, they no longer heard the knocking.
192126: In Sint-Kwintens-Lennik lived a woman suspected of being a witch. One day this witch had said to someone: "Just wait, before you're down the hill your clogs will be full of water!" The person in question did indeed get wet feet after walking into the brook. Whenever people walked past the witch's house, they always met a black cat.
192148: A man driving his horse and cart to Diest had to pass the house of a strange woman. Exactly at that spot the horse reared, so the cart tipped over and landed in the ditch. Then the witch came out of her house and said: "That's not so bad."
192150: A woman suspected of being a witch often visited young mothers. Afterwards those mothers had problems.
192169: One evening a man and his godfather pushed a wheelbarrow over a grave. The grave caved in and a little blue flame appeared. It was a will-o'-the-wisp.
192174: A schoolchild threw a little heap of earth on the floor in class and said: "Look, as many heaps of earth as fall on the floor, that many mice will run away." The schoolmaster told the priest what he had seen. The child then had to go to the priest to be read over. The child was also baptised again. After that the boy could no longer make mice.
192175: Some people had seen that the devil had appeared to a little boy who had cursed terribly. The people quickly fetched the priest. The clergyman said prayers until the sweat ran down his body.
192184: A man and a woman had a little daughter who cried all the time. The mother had a priest come to bless the house and sprinkle everything with holy water. If you went to the friars of the Keizersberg (Leuven), you were not allowed to say that you believed the child had been struck by the evil hand. Otherwise the friars would not come.
192189: A woman said to a neighbour: "You have lovely spinach!" The neighbour gave the woman some spinach, whereupon the latter said gratefully: "That's good, because we have none and our daughter loves it so." The woman cooked the spinach for her five-year-old daughter. When the child ate the spinach, she kept pulling hair out of her mouth and said: "But mother, there's always hair in it." The parents had also eaten the spinach, but they had no trouble with hair. Eventually the child fell ill, so they had to go to the doctor and then to the Capuchins. The friars said: "Sorcery does not exist. We'll pray over the child." After a friar had prayed over the child, she recovered. The friar advised the people never again to accept anything from anyone without giving something in return.
192190: Some jokers made stalkaarsen (will-o'-the-wisps) by hollowing out a beet, putting a candle in it and laying a leaf on top. It then looked like a skull, which scared people out of their wits. After all, some of the dead did return.
192195: A wizard could make someone stand stock-still.
192198: A woman coming back from church visited two old women who had many walnut trees. Suddenly a strange woman came into the house, drank some coffee and left a little in the cup. Then she said to the other visitor: "Here, you drink the rest." Fortunately the woman did not, or she would have been bewitched.
192200: In a shop regularly visited by a certain woman, they could no longer make ice cream. The people had the parish priest come to bless the place. Afterwards the cleric said: "Now she will not come in any more and you will be able to make ice cream again." Shortly afterwards the witch died.
192204: A man who had to go to the bank in Brussels met a woman while crossing a street. She patted him on the shoulder and said: "They'd run you over yet!" The man went on and ended up at the Molenbeek market. Although he had walked that way a thousand times, he had got lost.
192211: A farm in Kumtich was haunted. A man coming back from Meldert in the evening always saw a light burning at that farm at the same time, although no one lived there.
192213: Butcher J. was asked by M. to come and make sausages from the pig she had slaughtered. J.'s mother advised her son not to go, because M. was a witch who had already bewitched many people. When J. was grinding the meat at M.'s, he saw a dancing light in the chimney and something that looked like a skeleton. Terrified, butcher J. threw all the mince against the wall.
192238: A witch made it impossible for a farmer to go on with his horse and cart.
192239: A boy was going out with a girl from Schepdaal. One day when the boy was sitting in a café in Schepdaal, the landlady said to him: "Which way do you go home? Aren't you afraid of that girl you're going out with? She sometimes goes about in the shape of a big growling dog." The boy answered: "Well, if I meet that dog, I'll know who it is, and I'll give it a kick up the backside." The boy went out with that girl for two or three months and never saw her in the shape of a black dog.
192264: On a little lane stood a tree stump in which a small light burned. The werewolf always came to that spot. A man managed to strike the werewolf, and so it was unmasked. The werewolf said to his attacker: "If you make my name known, I will kill you!"
192268: A ten-year-old girl from Neerlinter could make mice. When the girl did so during catechism class, the priest took her with him to read over her. Something had been forgotten at the girl's baptism. After the priest had read over the child, she could no longer make mice.
192271:
A man kept kicking at a cat that had come to sit at his feet. The next day a woman from Meise said to him: "So you were stamping on me yesterday! But today you will suffer pain!" That day the man did indeed suffer a lot of pain.
Since the gospel has existed, there has been much less witchcraft. Friars who came to read prayers over the stable read from the gospel and then prayed five Our Fathers.
192292: Many maids and farmhands worked on a farm in Willebringen. On Sundays they went to mass in Vertrijk. One farmhand always had to stay at home. As soon as the farmhand was home alone, the grain mill began to turn and the butter churn started working. When the farmhand went to look, everything stopped. That farm was bewitched.
192295: In the past you could die of the evil hand just because someone had pointed a finger at you.
192301: At the time of Bamis (St Bavo's Day, 1 October), young people often put hollowed-out beets with candles in the hedge. These lights were sometimes called 'stalkaarsen' or 'will-o'-the-wisps'. Some believed they were the souls of newborn children who had died without baptism.
192304: A man in Halle saw a fat hare sitting in the ditch and threw a stone at it. When he did, the hare changed into a little old woman from the village. She was a sorceress.
192321: People who were bewitched could sometimes go astray, so that they no longer knew the way.
192335: On a farm worked a farmhand who went about at night as Kledde (a shapeshifting spook). One night the maids threw a black apron at Kledde. When the farmhand sat at the table the next day with black threads between his teeth, they knew what was going on. The farmhand was sent to the field with the horses so that meanwhile his skin could be burnt. As soon as the skin caught fire, the farmhand was already at the oven to save his property. They had to hold him back, for he even wanted to jump into the fire. Once the skin had burnt up, the farmhand was released.
192353: A mother went to the shop with her little daughter. The girl followed a woman and did not want to come home. The child was bewitched by that woman, so that her little foot stopped growing. When the girl was a woman of thirty-five or forty, she walked on crutches.
192354: Some old women were said to be witches. If several children died one after another in a place, it was said that the evil hand had something to do with it.
192397: A farmhand worked on a farm in the Molenstraat in Herfelingen. One day he had to manure the field. The farmhand calmly sat down in the field. When the farmer brought him his food at midday and said: "But you haven't done anything yet!", the farmhand replied: "It will be done by this evening." At four o'clock, however, the farmer saw that still nothing had been done. The farmer said: "Well, lad, I'll have to dismiss you, because this won't do." The farmhand then said: "And would you like to see the whole field manured within five minutes?" The farmhand took his manure fork and said: "Each his own!" Five minutes later the whole field was manured. The devils had probably helped. Because the farmer was afraid of the evil the farmhand was involved in, he dismissed him anyway.
192423: In the past there were witches who brought diseases into the stable and who made sure the cows could not have calves. Sometimes the animals also fell ill or the butter went bad. People who suffered such misfortune had the friars pray over them.
192440: "You've been ridden by the mare" is an expression people often used in the past.
192458: Some friends wanted to know, out of curiosity, what it was like to hang oneself. One of the men tied the noose around his neck while the others stood ready to save him. At the crucial moment, however, a hare came running by. The men ran after the hare, and so the man really was hanged. That hare was the devil.
192492: Every night at twelve o'clock a woman heard the dodenwekker (death-watch, a ticking that announces death). That woman could not keep any of her children alive. After the woman had prayers read over her, she no longer heard the dodenwekker (death-watch).
192518: A young couple lived at a crossroads in Moorsel. The wife kept house and the husband went out to work all day. One afternoon the wife had a visit from a neighbour woman who had a bad name. The wife said to the neighbour: "I'd like to make porridge for my husband, because he likes it. But first I have to go and fetch milk." The neighbour replied: "I wouldn't do that now if I were you." But the wife was determined to go. The neighbour said: "You go and fetch milk, I'll wait here." At first the wife didn't want that, but in the end she left anyway. When the wife came home, she had the impression that her whole house had changed. That evening she told her husband, but he did not take her seriously. When the wife woke up the next morning, she was deathly ill. No doctor or priest could help her. Sometimes in the evening frogs came in through the drain hole for the water. People tried to burn the frogs in the stove, but they always jumped back out. A woman from Jette advised the sick woman to do a nine-day penance, and to go to confession and communion. During those nine days the sick woman was not to let any strangers in. On the eighth day the woman's sister was mopping the floor when the doorbell suddenly rang. The sister knew she was not allowed to open, but she was so dazed that she did it anyway. The neighbour was standing at the door. She put her foot against the door, squeezed her way in and made her way through the house to the room where the sick woman lay. The neighbour pulled off the blankets and gave the sick woman five kisses on each cheek. Then she said: "There, now everything is accomplished." The sick woman again consulted the woman from Jette, but she could not help her and said: "If I helped you, it would cost three human lives." The sick woman did not want that. The woman became completely emaciated and in the end lived on orange juice.
