192537: Many sorceresses lived on the heath in Kester. A butcher who had come home late saw two kittens walking at a crossroads. The man kicked at a kitten, but the animal would not be chased away. A little later the kittens even started playing. The man became furious and struck the cat on the leg. The next day the man found that a woman from Kester had lost her leg.
192546: A man was returning with a cart full of bricks from the brickworks on the Grootveld. When he passed a witch's house, his horse suddenly refused to go on. The man hit the animal with the whip, but that did not help. Some people had seen what happened and went to tell the man's father that his son was mistreating the horse. The father was terribly angry, but when he himself came to that spot one day, the same thing happened to him. As soon as he got home, the father fetched the priest to have his horse read over. The clergyman sweated and finally said: "T., you were bewitched."
192549: In the past people were afraid of men or women who lived alone and did not take care of themselves. In Nerum (Wolvertem) lived a man who peddled nuts at fairs. That man's wife was suspected of being a witch. She often ran after the children.
192550: A woman whose father had died without a priest wanted to know whether her father had ended up in a good place after his death. One night the woman's husband sat up in bed without saying anything. The next night the same thing happened again. The man thought he had heard something in the house. He was convinced the sound had been caused by his dead father-in-law.
192553: A rich farmer from Velm had been touched by the evil hand. After the funeral of a friend the farmer went to a café. The people there knew that the farmer had been touched by the evil hand and asked him to do something. The farmer hypnotised the people and conjured the inn full of mice. As the people ran outside, they shouted: "We have seen the devil!"
192574: In Sluizen a headless white woman walked through the meadow in the evenings. Nobody dared go near there.
192583: An unmarried woman who owned a few cows and lived with a shepherd often said she was bewitched whenever she had some problem or other.
192591: A farmer's wife was approached by a woman who came to ask for a rope. Because the farmer's wife did not know the woman well and did not want her rope to be damaged, she refused to give it. About five kilometres further on, the wind suddenly began to blow and everything flew off the farmer's wife's wheelbarrow. That woman was suspected of being a witch. The children were not allowed to accept sweets from her, or else they would fall ill.
192597: A farmer from Zoutleeuw was ploughing with his ox and found a statue of Mary in the ground. The farmer took the statue to the big church, but the next morning it was back at the spot where it had been found. The same thing happened several more times, from which people concluded that Our Lady wanted to stay in that place. A chapel was then built there on the Osseweg with the remains of the castle (Castelberg).
192637: A farmer whose stable had been struck by the evil hand was on the verge of bankruptcy because his animals had Saint Catherine's wheel. The farmer then went to the fathers of Jette to have prayers read over him. There he was also given a scapular and a medal to carry with him.
192642: A farmer who had moved a boundary post found no rest after his death and had to wander about with the post all the time, calling: "Where do I leave my post, where do I go with my post?" When one day a man answered: "Damn it, take it back to the place where you got it", the dead man replied: "I have waited a long time for that". After that there was no more haunting at that spot.
192646: A woman out walking with her cow suddenly could not get the animal to go on because a witch was standing on the road a little further ahead. The cow stood stock-still.
192665: In a café where people often played cards, strange things always happened between eleven and one o'clock at night. A man who seemed to be having a heart attack moved restlessly and made movements as if he wanted to bite into something. They then quickly put a spoon in his mouth, afraid that he would otherwise bite his tongue. When the landlady sent for a Norbertine priest, the clergyman said to her: "Madam, a woman comes to visit here every morning. What does that woman do when she comes?" The landlady answered: "She opens the door and asks: 'May I come in?'" The priest then said: "When that woman comes again tomorrow morning and asks whether she may come in, you must say her name and say: 'If you can.' But you must not hate that woman. Here is a little bag with relics that you must hang above your door." When the woman came the next morning and the landlady did as she had been told, the witch turned around at the door and walked away. She could not come in because of the relics hanging there.
192678: The Mergentoren, built as a defensive tower during fighting, is said to have been built with bran to make the structure stronger. The same was done when building the church of Zichem.
192702: During the Second World War a man was staying on a farm in Wallonia. At night two people always had to keep watch by the horse cart there to chase away the rats. When the man kept watch together with a Walloon, he said: "I'll sort that out quickly." He laid straw in the courtyard and left one corner free. Then he walked over the straw. A little later all the rats came running to the straw. The man said: "There's still one with three legs to come." A little later that rat came running too. The man set the straw on fire and was rid of the rats.
192704: A woman who strongly believed in witchcraft told a shopkeeper: "I've had a lot of trouble lately. The farmer who lived near here and who died comes haunting my cellar in the shape of a tomcat that makes a lot of noise. This week I threw a pot of hot water over the cat."
192714: On a farm where the animals and the children were always ill, the fathers were sent for. The woman who had bewitched the farm often came to visit, but the father predicted that the woman would no longer be able to get in. And so it was.
192724: When the priest forgot to close his book in church, seven witches could not get out.
192727: A man who always came home past the churchyard saw one evening a ghost standing with a sheet over its head. Convinced that it was some joker, the man pulled the sheet off the ghost's head. When the man was home, he heard someone knocking on the door. A voice said he had to give back the sheet. It was the ghost itself coming to ask for its sheet back. A clergyman advised the man to bring the sheet back to the churchyard. No sooner said than done.
192737: Stallichten (will-o'-the-wisps) were lights seen in the distance that suddenly hung still. A man who saw a stallicht sitting on his horse's harness said: "I baptise you in the name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Ghost". Then the horse was surrounded by countless lights, all wanting to be baptised.
192738: In Bogaarden lived a woman who was suspected of being a witch. A man who had gone to live with the witch because she was a relative of his could never get across the brook on his moped in the morning. The moped always stalled there. The witch was said to have caused the deaths of three or four of her relatives, because the doctor had not been able to establish that those people had died of any particular illness. The woman owned books.
192743: In Herfelingen there was a meadow where Kludde (a shape-shifting goblin) came haunting with his chain in the hay. Kludde had pulled up a boundary post and kept asking: "Where shall I put it? Where shall I put it?" When one day a drunkard answered: "Put it where you got it", Kludde appeared no more.
192768: When someone lay dying who had not kept a promise they had made, something always hung above the well the next morning.
192800: A farmer from Oppem (Brussegem) who could not store all his grain in his barn was visited by someone who said: "If you will sell me your soul, I will build you a barn." In the end the farmer let himself be persuaded and agreed to the proposal. But the barn had to be finished before midnight. When the farmer lay in bed that evening, he grew afraid and told his wife what he had done. The wife said to him: "Take a candle and go to the henhouse." When the farmer lit the light in the henhouse at a quarter to twelve, the rooster began to crow. The devils had to stop their building, although there was still a hole in the barn to be closed. No one ever managed to close that hole afterwards.
192801: In Tienen lived a witch who always gave people flowers from her garden. Afterwards those people fell ill or ran into trouble. The witch had filled her house with candles into which she had stuck pins. The neighbours in whose garden the witch came to sit in the evenings suffered misfortune and had their house overlezen (exorcised by a priest's prayers). Later no one ever managed to find a tenant who wanted to live in the witch's house for long.
192806: Some men returning from the fair in Groot Haleer saw a woman on the way with a scarf on her head. When the men asked her the way, she answered: "You must go this way. Then you'll be in Waasmont right away." The men followed her directions, but ended up at a large body of water and could go no further. Only at dawn could the men find their way home. They had strayed twenty kilometres from Groot Haleer.
192840: If you saw a black cat at a crossroads, you could expect misfortune. If you heard magpies chattering in a tree outside, news would come.
192841: A priest had seen a little boy make white mice by throwing some earth on the ground. The priest had the boy come to him and took away his magic power. Since the last gospel has been read at the end of mass, such magic no longer exists.
192858: A man met a black cat in the street at night. After he had stabbed the cat with a knife, the animal changed into a human.
192867: A girl of sixteen or seventeen was bewitched by a woman who often came to visit her. The witch was thrown out by the girl's brother, but the bewitched girl died anyway.
192868: A man who worked for a miller had to transport grain and flour. At a certain house his horse and cart always came to a stop. The man stopped taking the grain of the woman who lived there, so the woman brought her grain to the mill herself. Every time she did, the mill broke down. When the woman had died, nobody wanted to buy her house. In the end someone did buy it, but it has stayed empty.
192889: A woman on her way home in the evening heard music in the trees.
192909:
In Sint-Ulriks-Kapelle lived a woman who did not go to mass because she was not a believer. When the woman was buried, people said: "If you go there, you're going to a witch's funeral." Her coffin bore no cross, but instead two hands were depicted on it.
During her life the woman had been in the habit of offering sweets to the children. Not a single child dared to accept them.
192910: A man was ridden by the mare every night at the same time. Doctors could not help victims of the mare.
192944: The house of a butcher was haunted. Above the man's meat tub people always saw little glow-worms. The butcher believed it was a ghost and shot at the lights. On the butcher's mantelpiece stood a statue of Mary with glass eyes. The butcher always saw the eyes of that statue move and believed it was a ghost. In reality it was trees swaying back and forth that were reflected in the glass eyes. When people got up in the morning, the chairs were knocked over.
192950: The man who had to guard the abbey's cows by the Meulenvijver saw a funeral procession pass by one night. The guard was so shocked that he ran straight to the abbey. The next night one of the fathers went with the guard to the meadow. When the funeral procession appeared again, the father walked up to the apparition. A little later he came back and said: "Now you can rest easy. You will never see anything here again."
192964: A witch came into a house every night through the drain hole for the water. That house had much misfortune and the children fell ill. One day the father stood guard by the drain hole with a saw knife. He managed to hit the cat in the neck. The next day it was discovered that one of the neighbour women had lost a hand.
192969: On a farm the cows stopped giving milk after a witch had been in the stable. A priest came to read prayers over the animals and sprinkle the stable with holy water. After that the cows gave milk again.
192981: When people had a lot of misfortune, they believed they had been ridden by the mare.
192990:
A boy from Sterrebeek worked on a farm where he had to clean chicory. The boy was well liked by the farmer's wife, who always saved the tastiest morsels of food for him. The boy understood that she wanted him as a son-in-law, but he did not fancy marrying the ugly farmer's daughter. One Sunday the boy had said in front of his friends: "I'd rather hang myself than marry such a monster!" The farmer's wife had found out about this.
From that day on the boy had nothing but bad luck. When one morning he had twenty blood boils on his face, he went with his mother to the fathers. After a father had read prayers over the boy, the clergyman said: "There is no doubt about it. You have been struck by the evil hand. Put this medal around your neck and you will be saved." The boy followed the clergyman's advice, and his boils quickly healed. The boy never went back to work on the farm, because he was convinced that the farmer's wife had bewitched him.
193005: In Neerlinter lived two pretty little girls. After a witch had visited the girls' house, they always had some problem or other.
193030: A butcher who liked to drink jenever and feared neither devil nor hell met a woman on his way home in Busingen, who said: "Have you been slaughtering pigs?" The man answered: "Yes, and I have to come back this way tonight. I hear you're a witch, but watch out!" That night the butcher got lost and got not one step closer to home.
193032: In Orsmaal-Gussenhoven lived a man who was no longer right in the head. That man came every evening to dance around a linden tree. He also sometimes went about as a big dog, so people believed the place was haunted. One evening a few men armed with a piece of iron went to that spot to beat the 'ghost'.
193041: One night a girl was coming back from the Stokkel fair with her boyfriend. By the Stroitbeek the boy kicked at a black cat running under their feet. After that the two heard a voice behind them calling all the time: "Set upright again what you kicked over." The girl and the boy ran home as fast as they could.
193042: A man from Nieuwenrode had dreamed that he had been to heaven during the night and had then come back. In his dream the man had died and had seen Saint Peter, who said: "My friend, just sit down there. The rich sit up top and the poor wretches have to sit below, just like on earth." In the morning the man said that life in heaven was not much different from life on earth.
193049: Some brave miners coming back from the inn had to pass along the Bosstraat, which led to the churchyard in Bever. Because the men thought they saw the devil standing on that little road, they went back to the inn. The men were drenched in sweat and finally turned around. The men made a half-hour detour so as not to have to pass along that road again.
193056:
A woman woke up one morning with painful scabs on her head. She went to get ointment, and after a while her head healed. But she also had a scab on her arm that did not go away with the ointment. The woman then had to go to a doctor in Oudergem, who was able to remove the scabs with tweezers.
The woman blamed her misfortune on her landlady's mother, for that mother was a witch.
193081: A man had said that after his death he would return in the shape of a horsefly. About two years after the man's death, his wife saw a horsefly flying around in her house and asked: "Hey X, is that you?"
193090: On a farm there was always misfortune after a black cat had come by. Sometimes an animal died, sometimes a person. When a cow had died, the farmer threw a stone at the cat and hit it high on the leg. The next day a little woman from the village was seen wearing a bandage around her shoulder. That is how people found out she was the sorceress.
193106: In the past some twigs were said to have been ridden by the mare. People cut off such branches and hung them in their house to protect themselves against the mare.
193110: When people could not sleep, they believed they were being ridden by the mare.
193111: People from Krabbos (Dworp) who went to work in Lot around six in the morning often came across stalkaarsen (will-o'-the-wisps). These lights were the souls of prematurely born children who had died unbaptised. With this in mind, people made sure a newborn child was baptised as soon as possible.
193115: In Huizingen the sorceresses sometimes made it impossible for people to go on. One day a butcher who cursed a lot and liked to play billiards was thrown into the Molenbeek by a ghost. After that the man never drank so much again.
193118: If the priest left his missal open, witches could not leave the church.
193149: The parish priest of Dworp is said to have once declared in his sermon that the sorcerers and witches had to stop their practices, or else he would name them by name.
193156: On a farm that had much misfortune, the priest was sent for. Because the clergyman suspected a certain woman of causing the misfortune, he hung a small cross on the farm gate and read prayers over the whole building. When the woman came to visit afterwards, she could no longer get in.
193159: A farmer who needed a new barn made a pact with the devil. The devil would build the farmer a new barn that would be finished before the first cockcrow the next morning. While the devils were working in the night, the farmer got up and began to crow himself. The devils believed it was the rooster and fled. At that moment there was still a hole in the barn, which could never be closed afterwards.
193193: The devil was to build a barn that would be finished before the first cockcrow in the morning. But this did not work, because the farmer had gone to the henhouse in the night with a lantern, so that the rooster thought it was already day and began to crow. At that moment the barn was not yet finished.
193194: In the past it was believed that an owl announced death. When people were keeping watch by a sick person and heard an owl call, they believed there would soon be a death in the house. That often came true. A possible explanation, of course, was that a light burned at night in a sick person's house and the owl was attracted by the light.
193204: Some people were coming back late in the evening from the kermis (village fair) in Vaalbeek. On the way the men saw a house with a light burning. They went to look through the window and saw a whole group of dancing women. When the men grew tired, they tapped on the pane. Then all the women had vanished and the light had gone out.
193221: A man who was followed by a cat on the road asked: "O my pretty little pussycat, where are you going?" Then the cat answered: "X asked me: 'O my pretty little pussycat, where are you going?'"
193239: In Wespelaar lived a woman who always carried a black cat with her. It was said that at night the woman could also turn herself into a black cat.
193255:
If an old woman came near a small child, the child was bewitched.
When a child was ill, people often believed that the child had been bewitched. That was superstition.
193259: A woman who always wore rags was feared by the people. It was said that she was a witch. One mother even claimed that her child had died of an illness after the witch had stood by the cradle. The mother never wanted to let the witch in again.
193275: A woman whose husband had died not long before did not dare to sleep alone and had a neighbour girl stay with her. One day the girl had ridden through the cold and then crawled straight into the warm bed. At that moment something came over the girl, so that she lay stiff as a board in her bed. She had been ridden by the mare.
193286: During catechism a girl saw a boy make mice run through the church. When the priest found out, he read over the boy, after which he could no longer make mice. The boy had not been baptised properly.
193313: A sixteen-year-old girl worked at the machines in the nitric acid factory. The men who worked at the furnaces where iron was extracted from the ground had to do heavy labour. They had to work twelve hours and then rest twelve hours. Those men were often given gin. When the men then began shouting and raving, people would call: "Come, hurry with the broomstick, he is possessed by the mare! We're going to beat the devil out of him!"
193317: A girl is said to have once disappeared on a farm in Budingen. On that farm clothes went missing and knocking was heard in the attic. The curate came and said to the people: "You must get rid of everything here that belonged to your mother." After that no more strange things happened on the farm.
193332: On 15 August witches had to make someone die. If they found no victim, they had to pay for it with their own death. In Walsbets lived a witch in whose house two children had died on 15 August.
193336: A man had promised to go on pilgrimage to the three sisters in Bertrée. But the man died before he could keep his promise. So the dead man's brother went on pilgrimage to Bertrée. Before leaving, he set a stick against the door and said: "I am leaving on pilgrimage." Whoever did not do this would be followed by the ghost the whole way.
193344: During a game of skittles at half past eleven, a man said to his friends: "I have to go to Brussels, because I have to be there at twelve o'clock." When one of the friends said that was impossible, the man said: "Come along, and you'll see something." At a crossroads the two flew up into the air. The friend bumped his feet against the church of Leuven. Half an hour later the two men were in Brussels.
193354: In a café a sorcerer put out the light and said to the people: "Put your hands in your pockets, for many rats will come." A little later a good hundred rats could be heard running about. As soon as the light was lit, the rats had vanished. That sorcerer had sold his soul to the devil.
193364: Two men went to the woods in the evening because they had seen many hares running there. One of the men tried to shoot at a hare, but his gun did not work. When that man came home that evening, his gun did work.
193369:
If you wanted to know whether someone was a witch, you had to cross the suspected person's footprint. If the person looked back, you knew you were dealing with a witch.
A boy put it to the test and found that a suspected woman from the neighbourhood was not a witch after all.
193374: A woman came to visit a house where there were five children. She stroked one of the children on the head and said: "What a pretty child!" After that the child's head was turned back to front, so that the child had to be taken to the fathers of Leuven. Fortunately everything turned out all right again.
193386: People who had bad luck said they had been ridden by the mare.
193389:
A man who was ridden by the moon no longer knew where he was.
Being ridden by the mare, however, was something else. Whoever was ridden by the mare in bed could not sleep and could no longer move. During the First World War a man was ridden by the mare in Baisy (Wallonia). The man was staying on a farm there to help with the beet harvest. Two pious spinsters who lived a little further on had Flemish parents. One woman worked as a seamstress and the other as a farmer. One day that farmer came to the farm where the man was staying and said: "I have a small potato field. You may come and dig up those potatoes." The man accepted the job, but that meant he had to sleep in the house of those two women. In that house the man was ridden by the mare. Those two women were witches. After that incident the farmer would not spend a second night in that house for a hundred thousand francs.
193397:
Two women from Rumsdorp went to visit their parents one evening. When the women set off home again, their father went with them as far as the door of a house where a werewolf lived. The man then called out: "Attack me instead of my daughters!", but of course the werewolf did not appear.
One day the werewolf's clothes were thrown into the oven. The clothes had barely caught fire when the werewolf was already standing by the oven.
193413: On a farm with four cows, one of the animals was 'brul' (?). The cow was sold and a new one bought. Because the people on the farm kept facing the same problem again and again, they went to the sexton, who gave them a piece of the Easter candle to put in the stable. Someone was said to have brought the evil hand into the stable. After the people followed the sexton's advice, they never had a 'brulkoe' (?) again.
193422: In a house where some women were telling stories, a toad sat under the stove. Because the women felt the toad was eavesdropping on them, they struck at the animal with the red-hot poker. The next day a woman from the neighbourhood had a burn on her cheek.
193444: In the meadow next to the churchyard of Attenhoven, between midnight and one o'clock, all sorts of people dressed in white walked about. They were the spirits of the dead.
193459: Sickly children had prayers read over them by the Friars Minor of Halle or by other clergy, because people believed they had been ridden by the mare.
193460: If you met a cat in the evening, you must not strike the animal, or else you would be bewitched. Cats that roamed about in the evening were witches, so people believed.
193471: A woman was ridden by the mare. The mare was a woman with a hood and a black goat. The victim felt how she was worked over with a knife from her toes up to her heart. Strangely enough, she was not injured afterwards.
193479: A father came to a house in Kampenhout that had been struck by the evil hand, and said: "Everyone come inside and lock the door. Don't open it until I say so." Then the father shut himself away in a small room, where he prayed for four or five hours. Meanwhile the people heard noise as if the house were being torn down. Then the father came back drenched in sweat and said: "Now you may open everything."
193485: Two poachers wanted to shoot at a hare. But something held back their arm and called: "You shall not shoot!" A little later a large white cloud appeared with a hare in it. Terrified, the poachers ran away.
193504: A woman was advised by her mother-in-law to put a blessed medal of Saint Michael under the threshold or under the doormat, since this kept witches from coming in. The woman followed the advice because she suspected her mother-in-law of witchcraft. After the woman had put a medal under the threshold, the mother-in-law stopped visiting.
193511: People who had misfortune with the animals in their stable often went on pilgrimage to the chapel of Gezule in Bever. People who believed they were bewitched also sometimes went to have prayers read over them by the Capuchins in Edingen.
193555: A girl had been left alone after her father and mother died by witchcraft. The girl went with photos of her parents to a fortune teller, who asked her whether she had lent anything out. The girl answered: "Kramiek pans (pans for raisin bread)", whereupon the fortune teller advised her to give the pans back. On returning home the girl threw the pans over the wall, but the neighbours threw them back. When the child fell ill some time later, the girl went to the fortune teller again, who advised her to give a loaf of bread to the first poor person she met. No sooner said than done. But the girl had given the bread to the person who was bewitching the house. The fortune teller said to her: "You have thrown the bread into the dog's mouth."
193556: A woman suspected of being a sorceress lived on the heath. Not far from her house lived a farmer whose cow was ill. The vet said the cow had to be slaughtered. When that had been done, a toad jumped out of the cow's body. The farmer stabbed it with his dung fork. The next day he found that the sorceress had a large wound on her jaw.
193594: A man walking through the woods at night suddenly heard branches cracking behind him. The man saw that he was being followed by two black ladies. The man quickened his pace, but the ladies caught up with him. The ladies greeted the man and the next moment they had vanished. In the woods all was quiet. Those ladies must have been ghosts.
193607: One night S.P. came back drunk from the fair in Kerkom. On the way the man saw a little light burning in the stump of an oak tree. S. blew out the candle and put it in his pocket. When S.'s wife wanted to hang her husband's clothes in the wardrobe the next day, she found in one of his trouser pockets not a candle but a child's hand. Scared to death, S. went to the parish priest for advice. The priest gave him this advice: "You must take that hand back at midnight. Take my stole with you." As S. was on his way to the sunken lane, something walked along with him, saying: "If only that stole did nothing." As soon as S. had put the child's hand back in the tree stump, it turned into a burning candle again.
193608: A witch came to visit a house where there was a child, stroked the child and said: "Oh, that is a lovely child." A little later the child was covered in lice.
193614: In Grimde (1) there lived a wicked witch. A farmer's wife coming back from the market, where she had bought wire to put around a meadow, saw the witch standing in the doorway of her house. The witch asked: "Have you bought wire?" to which the farmer's wife replied: "Yes, it is to fence off my chicken coop." Then the witch said: "Well, then I'll fence you off now" and threw the wire over the farmer's wife's head. When she got home, the farmer's wife found that she was completely covered in vermin.
193617: Strange things always happened at night in a building in Zellik. One night the building was even completely torn down.
193621: Crossroads were often dangerous. Sometimes black cats could be seen there. At the crossroads of the Heirbaan and the Veldstraat people always heard cats wailing.
193623: On the Steenweg in Heikruis there used to be an old house. The people who lived there had promised to build a small chapel. One evening the people heard knocking on the window. They went to look, but there was nothing to be seen. The same thing happened several more times. When the people told the parish priest about the strange events, the cleric asked whether they had perhaps made a promise. Then the people remembered their promise about the chapel, which had still not been built. As soon as they had built the chapel, the knocking stopped.
193624: A cat that was completely black brought luck into the house. Many farmers were afraid of black cats. Sometimes a black cat was accidentally shut in the room where the milk was kept. By morning that cat would have drunk all the milk.
193639: A woman came to fetch water at a farmer's in Rummen. After that the farmer had nothing but bad luck. The calf born in his stable died. The foal that was born also died. In the end the farmer did not even have milk left to give his children. When the man gave his children a piece of chocolate, they got diarrhoea. The farmer's wife also ate some of the chocolate and got diarrhoea too. The farmer did not believe it and ate some of the chocolate as well. He too got diarrhoea. After a while they decided to go to the fathers, who gave medals to put in the house and in the stables. When the woman came to fetch water the next morning, she hesitated at the gate and had to walk on for ten minutes to get water there.
193646: At the mill on the Gete in Utsenaken worked a farmhand who would rather be idle than tired. This farmhand sold his soul to the devil in exchange for a mill barrel full of gold coins. He had to sit at a crossroads at midnight with a black hen until he saw the devil coming. After a year, however, the farmhand repented and had prayers read over him to free him. At night the farmhand could no longer sleep for the terrible noise the devil made around the mill. He had iron bars put in front of his windows. Although the windows were very narrow, the devil still pulled him through them, and he drowned in the Gete.
193674: The doors were sprinkled with holy water to keep out the devil and evil spirits. The devil prowled around children only a day old to seize their souls.
193680: A man who had often moved boundary posts had to haunt after his death with a boundary post in his hands. At midnight the ghost walked around the field saying: "Where shall I put it? Where shall I put it?" One day someone answered: "Well, take it back to where you got it!" With that the ghost was released.
193688: A farmer's wife claimed she had seen a ghostly woman in a hedge. That was a witte madam (white lady).
193722: In the old days people sometimes told stories about the dead who returned.
193751: If a cow had died on a farm, people often believed the farm was bewitched. Witches burned candles to send evil to someone. People struck by the evil hand went to the fathers of Affligem, where they had to put money in the offertory box and make a novena.
193783: A strong man who was out at night shouted: "If there are werewolves, let them come." A moment later the man felt something heavy jump onto his back. The man had to carry the werewolf to the door of his house, where he collapsed from fright. The man nearly died of fear.
193791: One Saturday a man from Bontegem was coming back in the dark from band practice. The man was drunk and played a tune to keep up a good pace. A little later he saw a mewing cat rubbing against his legs. The man said: "Oh pussy, are you there?" and played on. A little later he was surrounded by a whole pack of cats. Because he was very frightened, he knocked on a door somewhere. The next moment the door was slammed shut with a loud bang. No one dared go outside to look, and the man stayed the night with those people.
193823: A woman always came to play cards with a family in Langdorp. Whenever she came, she always brought a sweet for the child. Because the child was always ill, the family consulted the fathers of Tongerlo. The grandmother had said that the visitor might well be a witch because she always gave the child a sweet. After that the woman never came to play cards again.
193834: A drunkard was walking home along the Zoutleeuw-Dormaal road. Suddenly the man was jumped by a werewolf. The man ran off quickly and was drenched in sweat when he got home.
193837: The little castle of Miskom was haunted. At night the windows flew open and the Jurei (?) sat in his window.
193840: A man got lost after he had taken a detour so as not to walk past the house of a witch. That witch was always sitting reading a book.
193846: A man coming out of the woods was followed by a kitten. The man kicked at the animal but could not chase it away. When he got home, the man heard a loud bang against the door.
193848: The Mollershof in Oetingen was haunted. The windows always flew open there.
193851: On the Mannenberg in Scherpenheuvel lived a man who said: "My mother-in-law is not a person like any other, because if you have something wrong with you, it doesn't heal."
193853: A man who had done evil during his life had to haunt after his death to undo the evil and to point out his money.
193858: Witches and sorcerers had to pass on their magic arts to someone else when they died. A witch lying on her deathbed called her daughter to her. The girl knew what was intended and refused to take over the magic arts. Then the witch passed her magic arts on to the cat. But the witch knew her daughter was standing at the door listening. In this way the daughter heard everything, and so she became a witch herself.
193861: A woman worked for a fortune teller who read cards in Brussels. One Friday the fortune teller laid out the cards for her cleaning woman, since the woman claimed that she was strongest on Fridays. When the fortune teller had laid out the cards, she immediately put them away again, saying: "There's nothing good in them". The cleaning woman kept insisting, however, and the fortune teller said: "You'll get pregnant and have a very difficult delivery. You'll lose your child, fall ill and leave here. A sick stranger will come to your home". The woman went home and told her husband what the fortune teller had predicted. The husband did not believe any of it. But less than a month later the woman was pregnant. When the husband was home alone some time later, the doorbell was rung by a Portuguese man sent by the landlord. This handyman was to paint the hallway and first came to see exactly what needed doing. The husband asked if the handyman wanted a cup of coffee, to which he replied: "Non, je suis malade" (No, I am ill). Shortly afterwards the man's wife fell ill. She was in hospital for fifty-six days. The couple left their rented flat and wanted to move to a nice house near the station in Neerwinden. At the last moment, however, the move could not go ahead because that house in Neerwinden was not free. The owner was building a new house, but because the work had been delayed, he stayed on in his house a bit longer. After a long search the man found another house. It was a very old little house in Laar. Something strange had once happened in that house. Some men were playing cards there when suddenly one of the players jumped out through the window. At that moment they saw that this player had a cow's leg.
193874: If there was a black patch in the wheat field, the field had to be sprinkled with holy water. The black patches were caused by women who consorted with the devil and were paid to do evil.
193875: In Manhove (Sint-Pieters-Kapelle) lived a man whose three children had all died in the same way. It was believed that the woman who came to the house was responsible for the children's deaths. At the birth of the fourth child, the gate was locked so that the woman could no longer get in. When the child was a few days old, the woman was at the gate again wanting to come in. That child did survive.
193883: In one family two little children fell ill and died within eight days. Both children had died on a Saturday. The people believed that this calamity had been caused by a woman who had been in their inn after mass. That woman had a beard like a man.
193890: In Akrenbos lived a woman who had bewitched her son's children.
193902: A girl who was playing made white mice come out of the ground. That girl could also turn a patch of the wheat field black. In the end the priest of Bekkevoort was sent for, and he baptised the girl again. After that the girl could no longer do magic.
193904: People who had eaten too much before going to bed often had bad dreams, which made them believe they were being ridden by the mare.
193906: On a summer's day two witches were walking along the Beertstraat, where some children were playing. One of the witches stopped and gave a piece of chocolate to one of the children. The child's mother saw it and chased the witch away. At home she put the piece of chocolate on the mantelpiece until her husband came home. When the father was home, he said: "Now you must all come and sit around the stove. You will hear the witch leave. If you had eaten that chocolate, you would have got a toad or a snake in your belly." Then the man threw the chocolate into the fire. That night the people could not sleep a wink; such a terrible noise had they heard when the witch left by way of the chimney.
193925: When a friar forgot to close his missal, not a single witch could leave the church.
193930: A woman was bewitched by her mother-in-law, who conjured three fat lice onto the head of her grandchild. The mother-in-law also caused her son and her daughter-in-law to separate for thirteen months.
193931: A man went to sleep in a bewitched house. When the man lay down in his bed, it suddenly became even brighter than in daytime.
193967: Two boys regularly visited their girlfriends. One of the girls always sent her boyfriend away around eleven o'clock. Because the boys found this strange, they decided to spy on the girl one time. At midnight the door of the house flew open and a pack of black cats came in. They were witches. They had come to visit the girl's mother, because she was ill.
193969: People believed that will-o'-the-wisps were the souls of children who had died unbaptised. Such souls could be released if one baptised them.
193998: A soldier who came home on leave said to his father: "Our mother is dead," to which the father and the other relatives replied: "No, not at all!" The soldier answered: "She is, for last night she appeared in the barracks wearing a cap with brown bows on her head."
194014: In a lane on the Kloosterberg a dog with a grey muzzle and vicious eyes was roaming. A man quickly fetched his gun, on which he had put a small blessed palm branch. But the dog had already vanished and could no longer be hit.
194016: If you walked in a witch's footprints, the witch looked back.
194032: A man whose sister had died of the flu used to pray a great deal for his dead sister. The man saw his sister appear as a ghost beautifully dressed in white. The ghost said: "Charlowie, I am in heaven."
194037: In Silly (Wallonia) some people went to Saint-Hubert to find out who was doing them harm. The image of their grandmother appeared in the mirrors. If something holy was placed under the grandmother's chair, she could no longer get up.
194039: On a November evening a farmhand went outside to fetch water. When the boy began turning the handle of the well, will-o'-the-wisps suddenly came flying towards him. The lights thought the farmhand was beckoning them to baptise them. The farmhand got scared and hurried inside. The next moment there was a loud bang on the door. In the morning the farmhand found that a handprint had been burned into the door. Decades later will-o'-the-wisps could still be seen above those marshes by the abbey.
194060: A boy who worked at a brewery in Rodenem found a little dog in the horse's stable one morning. When the boy struck at the dog with the whip, it grew as big as a cow. The boy quickly fled inside and did not open the door again until it was light. After that the boy never struck a little dog again.
194104: In Herfelingen lived a widower who had remarried. One day the man saw the ghost of his first wife sitting next to the stove. The woman was dressed all in white. A little later the ghost had vanished.
194131: When people saw a black cat, they were afraid. A black cat would not get out of anyone's way.
194148:
A man from Booienhoven visited his girlfriend in Zoutleeuw every Sunday. On his way back, by the chicken coop on the Osseweg, a large dog was always on his heels. The dog followed the man as far as the castle and there it ran ahead of him.
One evening a man and a woman were walking to Zoutleeuw station because they wanted to visit their family in Runkelen. At the Osseweg they saw the dog too. The dog always lay waiting in the ash pit of an oven. A man who went to fetch the doctor in Zoutleeuw at night because his sister had coughed up blood was accompanied by the dog all the way to Zoutleeuw and afterwards brought home again. The dog did the man no harm.
194154: A woman heard her husband coming up the stairs at midnight. Yet at that moment her husband was away in the army as a soldier.
194166: A baker from Beert often took his wife's little brother along on his rounds. A woman suspected of being a witch always wanted to pay the little boy, but the baker forbade him to take the money.
194171: In Rumsdorp a man had died whose children had promised to go on pilgrimage to Scherpenheuvel. But the children had not kept their promise. When the windows and doors flew open one night, the eldest son asked: "What is it you wish?" and a voice answered: "Do what you have promised." The boy left for Scherpenheuvel at once. Since then he has not seen his father's spirit again.
194184: In a café where people often played cards, there was terrible cursing. One day a gentleman came in who cursed even harder than the others. The gentleman sat down, quickly put his legs under the table and joined the card game. When one of the players bent down to pick something up, he saw that the gentleman had horse's legs. Then all the customers left the café because they were afraid.
194193: In Sint-Genesius-Rode lived an old woman of whom it was said that she rode a goat at night and practised magic behind a sheet in her house. One day a schoolgirl went to bring the woman a Sacred Heart prayer card, as schoolchildren usually did. But the woman was ill and called out: "Come this way, because I'm lying in bed." The girl was afraid, because her parents always told her not to accept food from that woman. Money she was allowed to accept. The girl went in and received a coin. The woman did her no harm at all.
194212: On a farm in Neerlinter a man had died. His youngest daughter was the only one who saw her father appear after his death. One day the girl asked the ghost: "Father, why do you follow me?" and the ghost answered: "Oh, you could have helped me long ago by going to Scherpenheuvel for me." Then the dead man's family, nine people in all, went to Scherpenheuvel. During the consecration the dead father came to give his daughter his hand, which left the girl's hand completely burned. Since then the dead man has not appeared again.
194234: In Waarbeek (Asse), a young girl worked as a maid in the city. She had become acquainted with an elegant gentleman, to whom she had sold her soul. She had had to sign a contract in her own blood. The girl lived restlessly for years. One day she told her parents what she had done. For the rest of her life the girl was tormented by the devil, who made so much noise that she could not sleep, who pestered her in the shape of a black dog, or who made her bed stand upright against the wall at night. One day the girl was found in a ditch near Asse. She had been strangled.
194244: A white farmhouse in Sluizen was haunted. All kinds of things always happened to the animals in the stable. The farmer claimed he knew the woman responsible for it.
194245: A girl who always made mice at school was taken to the priest by her mother. After the girl had been read over, she could no longer make mice.
194255:
Two friends went to the fair in Zoutleeuw one Sunday. By the lime tree next to the churchyard the girls suddenly saw a fireball falling down. The girls ran away in fear. When they looked back a little further on, they saw that the fireball had turned into a black dog that was following them. The girls ran as fast as they could to Zoutleeuw, where they went into the first inn they came to. They told two men who came to ask them to dance what had happened. The men said they need not be afraid and offered to go with them to the fair tent. When the four went outside, the dog lay waiting by the side of the road. Around eleven the girls set off home alone. The men could not go with them because they did not live in Zoutleeuw themselves. The girls were again followed by the dog and ran quickly all the way to Wezeren. At a crossroads they went into a house where a light was still burning. They told the occupant that they were being followed by a dog. The man took his knife and went outside with the girls. The man managed to stab the dog with the knife. Because the animal lay there wounded, the girls went home and the man went to bed. But the next morning the man saw a whole crowd of people standing next to his house. Where the dog had lain, there lay a woman with a knife in her chest. The dog was a witch.
The girls never went to the fair in Zoutleeuw again.
194256:
A strange woman always came to visit a house in Kerkom. Because the lady of the house did not trust this visitor, she once went to the friars of Leuven. There the woman was given blessed palm and told that no more witches would be able to enter her house. After the woman had stuck a sprig of palm above her door, the visitor never came to her again. The witch did not even greet her anymore.
One day someone saw the witch sticking pins into a cushion while keeping her eyes fixed on her daughter. People believed that the witch was destroying her daughter in this way, for a short time later the girl died.
194260: A sorceress was always out and about in the evening and at night. She went looking for her son, who went to the inn with his friends. Because the son did not like this, he decided to give his mother a fright together with his friends. One evening the boys hid by the road and jumped out to catch the sorceress. But they failed, because the sorceress flew into the air.
194262:
People who were ridden by the mare had to place a knife on their heart. The mare would then sit on that knife and die.
In reality, people who were ridden by the mare probably suffered from a kind of anxiety.
194268: On a farm a cow got a growth in its throat through the doing of a witch. The white canons (Norbertines) had to come and read prayers over the house and keep everyone outside.
194276: When the tailor Pierre was coming back from Walshoutem along the Waasmontse baan, he found a sheet fluttering by the roadside. Stingy Pierre took the sheet with him and put it in his chest at home. From then on Pierre heard a hellish noise in the chest every night. The priest had said to Pierre: "You must bring that sheet back to the place where you got it. You had best take a child with you." The man did as the priest had advised and so was rid of the sheet.
194277: A girl walking past K.'s house in the evening was startled when a ghost in a white sheet suddenly jumped over the barrier.
194298: A father from Attenhoven sent for the doctor because his little son was deathly ill. But the doctor did not know what to do and suspected that the child's illness had something to do with evil. The father believed his aunt was to blame, for he always went to his aunt's to fetch milk for his child. The man went to his aunt's house and forced her to come with him. The woman said: "But I'm in my nightshirt! I have to get dressed first!" When the woman was in the man's house, she advised him to take away the child's pillow. The pillow turned out to be full of pins. Although it was night, the man lit a fire to burn the child's bedding. After the child got new bedding, it recovered.
194300: Suspected witches were by no means always women who lived alone. Sometimes women were also accused of having bewitched their own family.
194311:
A boy met a woman in the street who was carrying a bucket of carrots. The boy asked for a carrot and got one straight away. Then he went home to have his grandmother clean the carrot. When the boy said who had given him the carrot, the grandmother threw it away at once.
Whenever the boy had to get up at night to help with the brewing, he always met that same woman.
194317: A child died through the evil hand. People knew who had bewitched the child.
194337: When lying on your back in bed, you could feel a weight on you, start to sweat and feel short of breath. You had then been ridden by the maar (nightmare spirit). All this was the result of witchcraft. You had to urinate in a bottle and put a firm cork on it. When the witch appeared the next night, she had to make herself known. She would then plead with all kinds of promises for the stopper to be taken off the bottle. But on no account were you to do so.
194362: A widow who went outside one evening with her child was startled when a stone suddenly fell to the ground. The same thing happened three days in a row. When the woman was working in the field, she heard a strange sighing. When one night she again heard sighing at the door of her room, she asked: "What more can I do for you?" Her dead husband answered: "You must go to the parish priest and have a mass said." Because the priest refused, the woman went to another priest, who said: "Oh dear, that is even worse than my first mass. Wait first and see whether he comes back." That night the woman heard the voice of her husband, saying: "Until the fortieth day." Forty days later the ghost burned his five fingers into the handkerchief the woman had thrown. Since then the woman has neither seen nor heard her dead husband again.
194391: The grotto of Poelk (a hamlet of Pamel) was built after a man had dreamed that a grotto had to be built for the soul of his grandfather. Because the man did not do so immediately, some time later he heard his grandfather's voice at night. The stones for building the grotto were taken from a meadow and came from an old castle.
194411: Someone who was ridden by the 'moon' (mare) was bewitched.
194435: A man coming home at night saw a woman from the village standing by the road and said: "X, what are you doing here?" The man shook the woman, but she did not move. That woman was a witch. She had, for example, made the apples in a stable go rotten.
194443: Stalkaarsen (will-o'-the-wisps) were seen mainly near water. It was said that stalkaarsen were the souls of unbaptised children.
194453: A man coming back around eleven o'clock from band practice met a mewing cat. The man threatened the animal but quickened his pace because he was afraid. The faster the man walked, the faster the cat followed him. A little further on the man saw a hedge open by itself when the cat passed through it.
194471:
A woman had a maid who could work magic because she had worked for a priest. The woman sought advice from the fathers of Leuven to get rid of the maid, for she had already had many troubles. Once she had fallen into the well. She also could not churn butter. One day the maid had come in with an apron over her head and the woman had been given a beating.
The fathers sweated terribly while freeing the maid from her magic. The fathers even claimed they were risking their lives by intervening.
194475: In Kester lived a woman who was said to be a sorceress. A woman who had walked past the sorceress's house claimed she had been bewitched. That woman could not walk for twelve years. Only when the sorceress had died could the woman walk again.
194513: A woman from Vlezenbeek went to the tram stop at Juwet and said: "Tram, stay put!" The next moment the tram really did stand still until the woman had reached the stop.
194544: A woman from Molenbeek-Wersbeek who was said to be a witch sometimes said: "Just touch my leg". If you did, you afterwards had something wrong with your hand.
194559: A woman claimed she could not sleep if she put her shoes next to her bed with the heels pointing towards the door. The woman was then ridden by the mare.
194582: Some people harvesting in a wizard's field could not get away until the wizard had been to them.
194586: In the Veeliedenstraat lived a man who was said to be a werewolf. People did not dare walk past that man's house at night. A werewolf was a man who carried a chain with him and had passers-by carry him in order to frighten them.
194605: A man returning from his field met a witch. The man tumbled into the water with his horse and cart. He was convinced the witch had bewitched him.
194613: In Sint-Kwintens-Lennik lived an old woman who was said to be a sorceress. At the market this sorceress always tried to give sweets to the children. A child who had eaten such a sweet kept walking around the market the whole time until the sorceress herself left.
194622: Lights were often seen in the Borremeers and the Langewei. Those lights were the souls of unbaptised children. A girl whose father had advised her not to point at the lights saw a light fly against the door with a loud bang.
194633: People who were ridden by the mare sweated terribly and could not breathe. They got lost. People who were ridden by the mare were sometimes also said to have been 'led by the als' (led astray by a spirit).
194634: Some people set out in the dark one morning to take a cow to market. On the way they saw a cat leap in front of their feet. One man began to pray the Gospel of Saint John. A little later the people saw a good hundred thousand cats around them. When it grew light, the cats were gone. The people did not manage to sell their cow at the market. The cow had grown terribly thin from fear.
194641: A woman whose children all died was often visited by the daughter of the man with whom her husband went to clear timber in Wezemaal. The daughter often sent the woman into the garden to fetch something. Meanwhile the witch would go and stand by the child, causing it to die.
194657: Will-o'-the-wisps were the souls of unbaptised children, or so people used to believe. Such lights appeared mostly in the marshland and in the meadows. A man who had fearlessly gone up to a will-o'-the-wisp ran home quickly because he believed the werewolf was chasing him. When the man got home, he heard a loud bang on the door. The next day a hand was burnt into the door.
194662: Near Zichem station a woman had seen a black cat three times. Because of this the woman was bewitched and went mad. People even considered taking her to the psychiatric institution in Geel.
194665: In Halle stood an old loam cottage where a blind woman lived. Because the rural policeman's threshing machine kept stopping, he believed the blind woman had bewitched him.
194671: Whoever dropped a mirror would have seven years of bad luck.
194679: A man who did not believe in witchcraft claimed he was ridden by the mare.
194683:
The devil was constantly recruiting victims. Those people in turn had to recruit others.
A woman who was possessed by the devil could not die. The doctor and the priest came, but the woman refused the Last Rites. In the end the doctor said: "We'll lock the door and she'll have to see for herself." The next day the woman was found dead under the Leuven stove. She was smeared with blood, for she had had to fight the devil before her death.
An investigation was held because the doctor and the priest were suspected of murdering the woman. Later the doctor and the priest were acquitted.
194688: On a farm in Sterrebeek there was much misfortune with the animals. In the evenings the people had often seen a toad walking about. One day the farmer struck at the toad with the poker, and it then leapt away through the drain hole for the water. A few days later the wife saw a neighbour woman wearing a bandage around her arm. That neighbour was known to be a witch.
194694: In Orsmaal lived a woman suspected of being a witch. If you were touched by that woman, you were covered in lice. When that woman was out in the evening, you could sometimes see her vanish from one moment to the next.
194713: On a farm where the cows gave hardly any milk, the maid found a big toad in the cowshed one winter morning. The maid quickly went to the farmer to tell him what had happened. They searched everywhere for the toad, but the creature was never found again. That toad came to milk the cows.
194715: Someone going to fetch milk met a witch on the way. When she got home, the woman found that the milk was full of lice. However much the woman boiled the milk, she could not get rid of the lice.
194720: A man who worked in the factory in Tienen had to walk home across the fields. One evening, in a sunken lane, the man felt someone jump onto his back. The man had to carry the apparition all the way to Kumtich. When he came to a crossroads, he was freed of his burden. It was the werewolf.
194774: A woman suspected of witchcraft was shot by a man from the village, for she had already done much harm. The man who collected the money in church lost his wife and was left alone with five children. He was widowed three times and remarried three times. One of his little daughters also died through the witchcraft. After the girl's funeral the father went home with his other children. People could hardly get into the room, which was full of black creatures. The father went to the stable and fetched a few bundles of straw to burn the creatures.
194802: Many people believed that black cats were witches.
194823: A girl was advised by her mother not to accept an apple from anyone, because sorceresses were always out to give children all kinds of things.
194857: One evening a girl came running to the café, crying out in fright: "It's haunted in the churchyard of Wange!" The people in the café did not believe her, so the girl said: "Come and see, come and see!" In the churchyard a little light could be seen that kept disappearing and then reappearing a moment later. Moreover, the light appeared above the grave of a seventeen-year-old girl who had died not long before. The next day a few men went to the churchyard with a revolver to get to the bottom of it. On the girl's gravestone lay a wreath under a glass plate. In a little clay house further on, a paraffin lamp stood on the table. The mysterious light was caused by the reflection of the paraffin lamp in the glass plate.
194888: A farmer's wife whose cow was about to calve went to a wedding. When she wanted to leave that evening, she heard that the bride's mother had cut her leg with a sickle. The mother came limping out of the room and the farmer's wife said: "Oh, that's a misfortune". The mother then said: "Today it's here and tomorrow it's at your place". When the farmer's wife got home, she saw that the cow about to calve was lying on the dung heap.
194920: A man whose little son lay in bed with a fever suspected a neighbour of having made his child ill. The family had the fathers of Affligem read prayers over the child and were told that on the third night someone would come knocking. On the third night there was indeed a knock at the window. The child's father went to look, but saw nothing.
194931: A man knocked at a farm and asked: "Well, farmer, can I earn something here? Are there any rats here? If you give me two francs, I'll make sure all your rats are gone." The farmer answered: "Yes, I have a few rats, but I won't spend two francs to get rid of them." A few days later the farmer had a good two thousand rats. Then he was glad that the peddler came by once more to drive the rats away.
194952: A boy who had been visiting his girlfriend came home during a heavy thunderstorm. It was haunted at the Eiken Bomen behind the Zevenzillen. A figure dwelt there that could turn into a toad, a bird or another animal. When the boy slipped in the mud at that spot, he felt a dog's hair in his hands. The dog followed him to the paved road, walking very close against him. That was Pleudde.
194961: People who were ridden by the mare could no longer breathe and felt as if someone was sitting on them. Just when they thought they were about to die, they woke up.
194984: One night a man went to the vet because one of his cows was about to calve. He had to go along a lane in Humbeek that was haunted. Suddenly, to his great fright, he saw a foal walking beside him. Bathed in sweat he arrived at the vet's and told him what he had seen. The vet said that foal walked there every night and that he no longer noticed it.
195001: One evening a man from near Vissenaken was coming home from work. By the churchyard the man heard hissing, whispering and grunting. When the man reached the gate of his house, a white figure with green eyes suddenly stood before him. People believed the figure was the ghost of a dead person who had lived badly and therefore had to wander in the churchyard.
195005: A farmer whose cows were ill suspected that a woman who had been at the farm had bewitched the animals. The farmer sought advice from the Capuchin friars of Edingen. A fat friar said to the farmer: "Go home. On the way you will meet a toad. You must catch that toad and kill it." When the farmer was almost home, he did indeed see a toad. He grabbed the animal and put it in his trouser pocket to throw it into the stove when he got home. When the farmer did so, he heard a loud bang and the lid of the stove flew into the air. A few days later the farmer was visited by a beggar woman with a bandage around her arm. "Get out of here!" shouted the farmer. The beggar woman never came back. The farmer had no more problems in his stable.
195006: A man going to the church of Bekkerzeel saw a light in a tree as a little bird hopped from one branch to another. After the man and his brother had pointed at the light, they hurried inside. A little later there was loud banging on the door three or four times. People believed that stallichten (will-o'-the-wisps) were spirits of the dead who still had something to do on earth. Perhaps the light the man had seen was nothing more than the bird's shiny little beak.
195017: If the priest opened his missal or forgot to close it, witches could not leave the church.
195023: If a child had been touched or spoken to by a witch, it was bewitched. The child would then be covered in lice or fall ill.
195026: A man going to watch a cycle race in Neerwinden met a woman by the railway, who tapped him on the shoulder and said something. The man did not understand what the woman had said, but muttered "yes, yes". A little later the man began to itch all over. When he got home, he found that he was covered in lice. If you had been given lice by a witch, you were not allowed to tell anyone.
195033: People who were abnormal or said things that made no sense were said to have been ridden by the mane (nightmare spirit).
195034: A woman was always tormented by her mother-in-law, who was a witch. When the witch felt she was going to die, she kept asking for her granddaughter, because she needed someone to pass her magic on to. But the granddaughter knew what was going on and refused to visit her grandmother. The witch had a terrible death struggle. For example, she lost her toes and went blind.
195035: On a farm struck by the evil hand, six or seven cows once died.
195039: A man had an ironing business where his daughter R. worked with some other ironing women. The daughter accepted all the work people brought her. Whenever the daughter went outside in the evening, a fat black cat always lay by the threshold. Around midnight the daughter got an ailment of the eyes so that she could no longer see. The doctor was at a loss. People went to the Kalvarieberg to pray litanies to Saint Godelieve, but it did not help. Every night at twelve o'clock the daughter was in terrible pain. A woman sometimes came to the ironing business, always bringing collars. The woman touched the daughter's eyes and asked how she was. An ironing woman told the father this and said: "I'm sure that woman is a witch! You'd better go to the card-reading healer of Oudergem. Take a piece of your daughter's clothing with you". That same day the father went to Oudergem. The card-reading healer dipped the girl's shift in holy water and the father had to pray the great litany against witchcraft together with her. Then the father was given a scapular. The healer also said: "Make sure your daughter never again opens the door to that woman who only brings collars, for she is the one bewitching your daughter!" The man followed the healer's advice. Shortly afterwards the girl's eyes healed. The witch tried to get in, but could not because all the doors had been locked. The witch then said: "You won't open up? Just you wait!" The witch never came back and the black cat was never seen again either.
195041: In Kersbeek there lived children who could make mice. The schoolmistress told the priest, who then came over and said to the child in question: "Girl, you will get two pieces (coins?) if you make white mice." The girl did it and got her reward. Then the priest said: "Girl, you will get four pieces if you make mice again." This time, however, it no longer worked. The priest had probably read over the girl.
195042: A farmer had two children who could not bear light. When the farmer fell ill one evening, a spiritist came and said: "Someone comes here every day who gives something to your children. If he comes again, you must go to your room and pray the Gospel of Saint John." When the man was with him again, he did as the spiritist had advised. The man kept saying: "I must leave, I must leave. I have to be in Sint-Truiden at twelve o'clock", but he could not get away. Only when the farmer came out after a long while could the man go outside. The man never came to him again and the farmer's children recovered.
195046: A sorceress who had slaughtered a pig went to offer the meat at a certain house. But the people refused it. They had a small child lying in a cradle. When the sorceress left, a long pin was sticking in the child's back, so that it cried the whole time. The parents immediately suspected the sorceress and had the fathers of Affligem read prayers over their child. The clergymen said: "The first person you meet on your way home will be the sorceress". When the people were nearly home, they met the sorceress who had wanted to sell them the meat. One was not allowed to greet the sorceress, for then she would again gain power over them. Shortly afterwards the people's house was full of ants.
195054: A farmer's wife whose cow had dropped dead asked a sorceress if she wanted some of the meat. The sorceress replied: "No, I would rather turn a kettle of water into a kettle of eggs." The farmer's wife was angry. When some time later a cow of the sorceress had dropped dead, the farmer's wife did not want any meat either and said: "I cannot turn a kettle of water into eggs, but I don't want that meat." A little later the farmer's wife saw a cat walking around her legs. Because the cat would not go away, the farmer's wife poured hot water over the animal. The next day the sorceress had a large red mark on her body.
195062: In Orsmaal-Gussenhoven a man was driving a horse and cart. He saw a woman standing by the road, who said: "Your horses won't go on anyway." Then the cart did indeed come to a stop. That woman was suspected of being a witch.
195064: People struck by the evil hand sent for the parish priest to have prayers read over them.
195066: A man often saw something 'tapping' in the curtains. After the man had sprinkled salt over his curtains, he no longer saw the tapping.
195070: In Sint-Lambrechts-Woluwe lived a water witch who always went about with her basket to pull 'cress' (?) out of the streams. People said: "If you see such water at your door, you can be sure she has bewitched you".
195078: People who were ridden by the mare lay stiff as a board in their beds. Anyone who wanted to be rid of the mare had to pee in his wooden shoe (klomp).
195087: People who had bad luck said they had been ridden by the maar (nightmare spirit). The maar was a sorceress.
195093: In Molenstede or Tessenderlo lived a witch who sent a man flying into the water. Fortunately the man could swim and reached the bank. Three times over that man was flung into the water by the witch.
195106: In a house in Dworp the fathers had to be called because it was haunted. A knocking could always be heard in the house. Moreover, the sheep, the goat and the pig had died. After a father from Dendermonde had read prayers over the house, no more strange things happened.
195111: A witch had to prepare food for her father, who was working in the field. Around noon the man saw a little bird sitting on his rake, which told him to come and eat. If you walked crosswise in the witch's footprints, she could not go on. If the priest said "Dominus vobiscum" and turned around, he saw the witches in the church sitting with their backs to the altar. If you put a piece of the Easter candle under the threshold, the witch could not come in. When a girl was ill, she was told that the first woman to pass by would be a witch. The girl looked outside and saw a young woman of about thirty walking by. She was the guilty one. Later that witch was taken away.
195136: When the stables were bewitched, the fathers came to read prayers over them.
195147: In Bost lived a witch who sold sweets to the children at the market. It often happened that a sheep somewhere was about to suffocate, so that people had to demand that the witch undo the harm she had done.
195170: If people saw two magpies, they believed misfortune would come.
195198: A carter had to bring church bells to Mazel. Because the horses could not get up a hill, the carter began to swear. The bells then flew away to the Kravaalbos. There were pits there where sandstone had been quarried. The bells sank into that pit. On Christmas night the bells could be heard ringing because they had not been consecrated.
195226: In the past people were afraid of black cats. They believed that witches in the shape of a cat could enter houses through the water drain hole.
195228: A man riding home in the evening was annoyed by a bat that kept flying around his head. He tore the animal to pieces. When the man got home, his son lay dead in bed.
195261: A man from Klabbeek repaired springs. One day a woman came to ask him to repair a spring. Because that woman was suspected of being a sorceress, the man was warned by his own wife: "Aren't you afraid? She'll bewitch you!"
195264: A woman churning butter suddenly saw a cat creep into the butter churn. The woman quickly took a knife and cut off the cat's tail. The cat then said: "It doesn't matter, it's only a bit of tail."
195269: A farmer and his wife went to Wolvertem at five in the morning with their sick cow. On the way the couple saw a sorceress come out of her house, who said to the cow: "Will you get better?" The farmer and his wife were terrified, but the farmer answered: "Ah, we'll see about that". Since the Gospel of Saint John has existed, such evil no longer exists.
195283: In a house in the Molenstraat in Hakendover there was always misfortune. At night the animals were untied and chains could be heard rattling. A light also wandered through the stables. The people went to the brown fathers of Sint-Truiden. One of the fathers came to the farm and prayed until he was soaked in sweat. The clergyman said: "If I miss, it will be the end of me". When the father went outside, he shot at a black crow sitting on the roof. He hit the bird in the wing. The next day the farmer's wife lay in bed with a broken arm. She had bewitched her own farm.
195308: A man on his way home was followed by a kitten. Because the man could not chase the animal away, he finally picked it up and carried it with him. When the man got home, the kitten had vanished and there was a skull on the table.
195350: Strange things always happened in a house in the Kerselarenstraat. The rats played the accordion and the people believed they were bewitched. They were even afraid of their own cat.
195351: In Neerlinter a dead father walked about at night, pacing back and forth reading a book in his hand.
195369: In the past people were frightened of black cats in the evening, because they believed they were witches.
195393: A witch is said to have once lived in Rumsdorp, whom people feared. That witch is said to have caused five or six children to die. She had predicted that a certain woman would not be able to keep a single child alive.
195394: One night a boy was walking home along the road he always took. Through witchcraft the boy stumbled into a meadow he could not get out of. Sometimes music could be heard high in the trees. That was witchcraft too.
195398: Some people coming back from Schoonaarde saw a pretty kitten sitting by the road. The woman picked up the kitten and held it in her apron. When she got home, the cat had turned into a big cobblestone.
195403: A man who slept in the horse stable always woke with a start when he heard a bang above his head, which also made the horses restless. Because people believed the strange noises were caused by witches or returning dead, they went to the White Fathers. After the White Fathers had blessed the stable, nothing strange happened any more.
195425: A farmer's wife had become bewitched after going to eat at the house of a woman from the neighbourhood a few times.
195435: Someone kept hearing a voice calling: "Post moved, post moved!"
195439: A man from Kaggevinne went to Kortenaken to buy a horse. On the way, however, the man got lost and ended up in Waanrode. The man was convinced he had met a witch who had led him onto the wrong road.
195445: A woman from Sint-Joris-Winge was alarmed by a violent storm wind. For a moment the woman thought a witch had caused that wind.
195452: On a farm there was a washing line that the neighbours also used. Whenever the farmer's wife went to bring in her washing, five or six posts always fell to the ground. Yet the neighbour who also used the line had driven the posts into the ground. Still, the posts always fell over when that woman brought in her washing.
195456: Some people took a cart of hay to the meadow. When the men drove home again, the four horses could not pull the wagon up a hill. On the other side of the road sat a sorceress with a thick black hood.
195457: On a farm at 't Solleveld there was much misfortune in the stables. Because all the cows were dying, the farmer's wife went to the fathers to have prayers read over the stables. After that was done, the misfortune came to an end. People also found out which woman had caused the harm.
195479: Three farmers from Neerwinden had danced with some young ladies at the fair in Hal. When the men left for home, they said they would come back the following Sunday. "You won't come back," said the young ladies. The men insisted, and one of them said: "Yes we will, we'll take these scissors with us and bring them back next Sunday." When the men reached the Heilig Kruis on their way home, they saw a crowd of meowing cats approaching. The man who had the scissors in his pocket threw them on the ground. One of the cats took the scissors. The next moment all the cats had vanished. The witches had turned themselves into cats.
195484: A witch worked for a farmer, helping to bring in the harvest. When the farmer heard the rumour about the witchcraft, he sent the woman away. She then said: "You'll often think of me yet!" From that moment on the man always walked backwards instead of forwards. The man sought advice from the parish priest, who told him not to go to a dance hall any more.
195486: On a farm an unusually large number of animals had fallen ill in a single night. The animals must have been bewitched.
195492: A man who had to keep watch over the piglets at night took a break to go and have a drink. When he then wanted to go back to the pigsty, he could not get in because the door of the sty had been tied shut with a cord. People believed a sorceress had done it.
195496: At an inn there was a little girl who did not grow and lay crying in her cradle the whole time. One day the child's mother found a strange piece of laundry in the laundry basket. The mother suspected a woman from Teralfene of having bewitched her child and went to the fathers. After prayers had been read over the child there, it recovered.
195515: A schoolgirl rolled a little ball from the mud on her clogs. A little later the ball turned into mice, and everyone started laughing. After the priest had said prayers over the girl, she could no longer make mice.
