195623: There was a tree by the Lintersepoort. People coming home late from work often saw a woman dressed in white walking around that tree. One day some men tried to attack the woman. But when the men came closer, the woman suddenly vanished.
195627: A girl who always went dancing saw one day that her dance partner had goat's legs. The girl was dancing with kludde (a malevolent shape-shifting spirit)! After that incident the girl mended her ways.
195649: One evening a man caught a hare in the feed shed. When the man came inside with the hare, the animal suddenly vanished. That hare was a witch.
195678: Toads were often sorceresses in the shape of an animal. If someone struck at a toad, a big flame could be seen.
195735: In Bellingen some people had become frightened of a cow that was standing somewhere.
195779: During the First World War many farmers had bad luck with their harvest. The ears of wheat were black and empty. Many farmers believed a sorceress was responsible for this calamity. If a woman had stood watching while the farmer was mixing the manure for his field with lime, he believed that woman was a sorceress. Many people went to the fathers of Affligem, where they were given a medal to protect their crops.
195818: A man taking a fine cow to the smith in Meldert met a woman who 'had a name'. The woman said: "What a fine animal!" and wanted to touch the cow. But the man would not allow it and said: "Keep your hands off, it's a vicious animal". The woman turned and walked off grumbling. That night, when the man was sitting in the pigsty with a sow and piglets, he heard his dog barking. He went to look and saw something moving by the dung heap. He came closer, but there was nothing more to be seen. The same thing happened three or four more times. It was the witch still trying in vain to get to the cow.
195873: People who were ridden by the moel (nightmare spirit) went to have prayers read over them by the fathers of Affligem.
195900: In Werchter lived a sorceress. Whenever she had visited somewhere, the people always met with misfortune. A man who once went to borrow that sorceress's wheelbarrow was also bewitched.
195913: A man transporting trees met a little woman by the presbytery of Rummen who was going to fetch water from a large pond. The man's horses stood still at that spot, so the man said: "Filthy little woman! It must be you holding me up here." The woman answered: "Oh no, drive on. The horses will pull all right." After that the horse and cart started moving again.
195933: In Essene lived a sorceress who was said to have bewitched children.
195934: A boy from Hever was ridden by the maar (nightmare spirit) every night. The boy sought advice from a priest, who said: "A hundred metres further on there is a post. There she will set down her wheelbarrow to rest. That woman is the culprit. You must not speak to her, but you must put a plank with a knife through it in your bed. The point of the knife must stick upwards." The boy followed the priest's advice and after that was no longer ridden by the maar.
195966: A girl who lived with vramassons (freemasons) was allowed to fly along with them one evening. When the girl felt a little jolt on the way, one of the vramassons said: "We're a bit too low. We bumped into the church tower."
195978: On a farm in Boutersem there was a cow that behaved very strangely a month before she was due to calve. The people sent for a friar from Tienen, who had himself dragged through the manure by two people. In the ground they found shovels, picks and other tools. After the tools had been removed, the cow got better and better. The friar said: "I will make the witch appear in a bucket of water". That is how the culprit was found.
195990: On a farm the animals fell ill through the work of the evil hand. The farmer's daughter went to the friars of Affligem and was given all kinds of things there. At midnight the daughter had woken up and seen the sorceress on the farm. After that the farm was freed from the evil.
196004: Some people who were out at night saw a lit-up fairground tent. They went into the tent and enjoyed themselves all evening with pretty girls. When the people suddenly spoke the name of God or made the sign of the cross, the tent suddenly vanished.
196042: People who were ridden by the maar (nightmare spirit) always saw sorceresses at night who seized hold of them. These people could be freed from the maar by having prayers read over them by the fathers of Affligem.
196047:
When animals had died in the stable, people believed the evil hand had something to do with it. The friars would then come to read prayers over the stable. The friars of Dendermonde were very popular for such tasks. 
When people had boils, the friars advised them to add sulphur to their food.
196095: In Landen people told of witches who could cause illnesses. People troubled by witchcraft had the parish priest come to bless their house or read prayers over it. A woman found it strange that the pots in her house were always standing in a different place and blamed the events on witchcraft.
196115: A farmhand saw a brooding hen with chicks sitting by the Bosbeek. After the man kicked at the hen, he was suddenly covered in cats. Only when he reached the farm were the cats gone.
196123: Next to the church of Orsmaal-Gussenhoven stood a haunted house. The occupants of that house did not go to church and always sat reading books in the evening. Coffins were even carried around in the house. In the morning the chains of the animals in the stable were completely tangled. Some men who kept watch in the house one night saw a priest appear, carrying a coffin.
196147:
In Aarschot lived an old woman who was said to be a witch. A man whose first child had been stillborn was told by his friends: "You owe that misfortune to the witch who came to visit you". Yet that woman had done nothing wrong at all. Later the man and his wife received a great deal of help from the supposed witch. Whenever one of their children was ill, that woman always came to babysit. 
In the old days black-haired women were often accused of witchcraft.
196157: Two farmers with adjoining plots of land were jealous of each other. One farmer, a miser, had moved the boundary post so that he had a bigger field. This deceit led to quarrels and lawsuits. One day the other farmer saw a white figure in his field that kept calling: "Where shall I put it? Where shall I put it?" Because the man was annoyed by the calling, he said: "Damn it, put it where you like". After that the farmer heard nothing more. The next day, however, he saw that the boundary post was back in the right place. The ghost of the dead miser had come to put the post back.
196162: A farm was often visited by a woman. After they had once given her a slice of bread, they could no longer make butter on that farm. The people went to the friars and were then freed from their problem.
196169: In a house in Werchter the butter churn often started working by itself.
196188: A man who was ridden by the mare at night could only be freed when someone called his name.
196194: At school the priest had heard from the pupils that one of the girls could make white mice by throwing a heap of sand on the floor. After the priest had baptised the girl again and read over her, she could not make a single mouse any more. The girl had not been baptised properly.
196203: Someone who had returned from the dead had said: "Good will be rewarded, and evil will be punished." Free V.B. had hanged himself. After his death he walked around the house at night.
196214: A woman from Kester who did not have much time to go to the market herself was sometimes helped by her neighbour, who did her shopping for her. One day the woman asked her neighbour to bring six herrings from the market. When the woman got the herrings, she saw that one fish had no head. Afterwards the woman had many problems with her little daughter. Every morning the child's eyes were stuck shut. They had to be washed out with running water. In the end the woman had the parish priest of Kester read prayers over her daughter.
196223: Witches could turn themselves into a black cat. Such cats crept into houses through the water drain hole.
196241: One evening a man went to the Kouterstraat with his gun. When he saw a large hare running, he shot at it. The hare lay stone dead on the ground. The man came closer to pick it up, but just then the hare got up and ran away. A little further on, at 'de zeven dagwand', the man thought he saw the same hare sitting. He fired again, but the same thing happened. When the hunter had experienced the same thing three times, he went home. On the way he met an elegant young lady wearing fine clothes. The man was convinced that the lady had turned herself into a hare.
196256: In a house in Pamel a fat toad was seen coming in through the drain hole for the water. The people kicked the animal, so that it fled outside. The next day those people were visited by a woman who was injured in the face.
196259: On a farm in Westrode (Wolvertem) the cows were found in the morning tied to the manger by their tails. The people of that farm then went to the friars.
196286: A boy saw his girlfriend sleeping in the orchard. While the boy was sitting beside the girl, a neighbour came by and said: "What a lovely child she is. You will be very happy with her". The following Sunday the boy again saw the girl sleeping in that meadow. Suddenly he saw a nasty creature come out of the girl's mouth. Terrified, the boy ran away. When the girl fell ill, the boy went to her to tell her about the neighbour who had stood by her. They took the girl to a healer, and she became well again.
196316: On All Saints' Day a mother said to her son: "You must pray, or else they might grab you by the neck!" But the boy did not pray. The next night he began kicking and hitting in his bed because something was holding him. It was the dead punishing him because he had not prayed for them.
196326: Whenever a woman was milking, she always saw a cat sitting on the cow's back. The woman struck at the cat, but the animal would not be chased away. The woman's husband did not see the cat. The people went to the friars, who advised them to lay a broomstick by the door, because witches could not step over it. That is how the people found out who the witch was.
196341: A man lying on his left side in bed felt the maar (nightmare spirit) crawling onto him. The man grabbed the small hand of the maan and sat upright. The maan pulled her hand away and vanished. After that incident the man was afraid at night for another three months. He even wanted a knife to lay on his heart at night.
196364: A man with a wooden leg often came to play the accordion in a café in Booienhoven. One day this man told of a farm that was haunted. At that farm people sometimes saw a grey sack come in, walk around the table and then disappear again. Nobody had seen the sack come in or go out. Not everyone could see the sack.
196375: A man remarried after his wife had died in childbirth. The man's second wife had no children of her own and was fond of the dead woman's little son. A short time later, however, the little boy died. The man often said that he heard a lot of noise in his attic at night. There was noise, clapping and banging. In the room where the dead woman had lain there was always noise too. When the man went to look, there was nothing to be seen.
196392: In a factory where work went on even on holy days, a black dog appeared on Christmas night, and all the doors opened for it.
196402: A young man who was home on leave from the army went to play cards in an inn. On his way home he saw a little dog walking in the street. He stroked the animal and wanted to pick it up. The more he stroked the dog, the bigger it grew. A while later there was a dog standing in front of him that was bigger than he was. The young man became very frightened and hurried home, where he had to lie down. He stayed in bed for two weeks and was ill for a long time afterwards.
196405:
Children who had accepted fruit or other food from a sorceress fell ill. A child who had eaten cherries from a sorceress had also fallen ill. The child's mother went on foot to the Torekens in Dendermonde. The friar said: "It was time you came here. I knew you were on your way". The friar read prayers over the child until he was drenched in sweat. Then he said: "May I transfer it to a little one?", to which the woman answered "Yes". When she got home, the woman saw a hen with chicks. One of the chicks kept turning round and round and finally died. After the woman had done a nine-day penance, she went back to the priest, who told her: "Now you must put a nail from the Easter candle under your threshold and you must not lend out any pins. And you must never say 'Come on in'". 
Two hours later the mother was visited by the witch, who came to ask for darning needles. The woman could not come in. The mother answered: "I can't give you anything, because I only have one darning needle myself".
196438: A man who went to fetch a bucket of water at the public pumps on the Dries one evening saw a fat pig walking about. The man asked the people in the neighbourhood whether the pig was theirs, but everywhere the answer was no. When by eight o'clock in the evening nobody had claimed the pig, the man put it in a pen. The next morning, however, the animal had vanished. The pig was never found again. It was a witch in animal shape. For on the Dries lived a witch who was as wide as she was tall.
196452: A man who went to wash outside in the dark because he still had to go somewhere saw a woman without legs floating in the cabbage field. When the man went inside, he and his family heard noise in the stable. The man went to look in the stable and saw the cow standing there shivering and sweating.
196455: If the Capuchins of Edingen left the missal open after Mass, the witches could not leave the church. They then had to go and ask the friars to close the book.
196457: A woman whose sons were all in the army in 1940 was working in her carrot field. When she saw a magpie sitting there, she said to her neighbour: "Look, that magpie has been sitting there all afternoon. There is news coming again." The neighbour replied: "It could also be good news." A short time later someone came to call the woman with the message that her son would be returning from Germany.
196478: One morning a dead beggar was found in a hedge in Winge. People mocked the beggar and put his bread bag under his head. The man was buried without a mass because the priest would not hold a service for him. The next night the church was lit up and a mass was going on inside.
196483: A woman who had died before fulfilling a promise had to come and haunt after her death. People saw the ghost appear as a shadow on the wall. The people had to fulfil the promise in the dead woman's place.
196494: A man always took his mother, together with a neighbour, to a club for pensioners. The neighbour would cycle to the house where the man and his mother lived and then ride along in the man's car. One day the woman had rubbed the mother's head, saying: "You are such a good woman". After that the man had a lot of trouble with his mother. Because the mother's health worsened badly, the man took her to a pendulum dowser in Tienen. The dowser sent the man to Diest, where another pendulum dowser lived. The woman suffered from memory loss and had to take a lot of medication. In the end it became so bad that she no longer knew on which day she had to wash or go to the shop.
196507: One night on a farm they could not get the horse into the manger. Yet there was nothing to be seen in the manger. The horse was bewitched.
196512: On a farm on the Schriekse Steenweg the farmer saw a hat flying through the air one night. When the man said: "If you are of God, speak. If you are of the devil, be gone," the hat exploded with a bang and vanished. The haunting there was banished for ninety-nine years.
196518: When cows were stung by horseflies, they might suddenly break loose from whoever was leading them and run off. There were people, however, who in such cases believed their cow was bewitched.
196532: Some people often took the produce of their orchard to the market in Halle. One of these men had asked the farmer he worked for whether he could borrow his horse and cart to drive to the market. When the man was ready to leave, a woman came up who was suspected of being a sorceress. She came to ask whether she could put her basket on the horse cart. At that moment the man's baby began to cry loudly. Because the child kept on crying and the doctors did not know what to do, they had a friar from Halle read prayers over the child. The friars also promised to have a mass said the following Tuesday at nine o'clock. In Halle the parents had also had the child examined by a specialist. When the mass was over the following Tuesday, the baby stopped crying.
196602: A man who claimed he was bewitched consulted the friars, who told him: "The first person to call on you tomorrow morning is the culprit". The next morning the man was visited by a woman who had the reputation of being a sorceress.
196606: A man who walked to work at five in the morning was sometimes waited for by a woman who lived in an isolated house and called out: "Come and have coffee!" Each time that happened, the man was followed by black cats that hung on his trousers and tried to jump on his neck. When the man stopped going for coffee with that woman, such things no longer happened to him.
196615: A dead person who had returned had burned his hand into a cloth. The people from Nieuwenrode to whom this happened kept that cloth.
196619: In the old days, when people saw a light in a bush, they believed it was a stallicht (will-o'-the-wisp). These were the souls of unbaptised children.
196669: A man who met a witch at night did not answer her questions, because then she had no power. The man fell into a pit. He screamed and prayed, but did not drown. When the man finally got out of the pit, he knocked at a nearby farm, where he was given dry clothes. The people of that farm were already used to such incidents.
196685: A mother had a three-year-old daughter. The caretaker who lived with the woman had a six-year-old daughter, whose godmother was a sorceress. One day the six-year-old girl had visited the sorceress with the three-year-old. The children had been given a slice of bread there. When the mother saw her three-year-old daughter come home, she saw that the child could no longer close her mouth. When she finally managed to, the girl told her mother whom she had been with. Then the mother said: "You mustn't go there any more, because that is a wicked woman. You can see what she does to you".
196700: One day there were two customers in an inn in Veerle. The two men wanted to play a game of cards with the innkeeper, but they needed a fourth man. A little later a stranger came in. They started playing cards, but found it odd that this strange fellow did not say a word. When the innkeeper bent down to pick up a dropped card, he saw that the stranger had horse's legs. The man quickly got up, fetched a bottle of holy water and poured it over the stranger's head. Then the strange fellow flew away. The innkeeper, frightened, said to the two customers: "Now I've really seen something! Didn't you see that fellow had horse's legs?" The men laughed at him, but when they looked at the floor, they saw that a horse's hoofprints had been burnt into it.
196704: Zoutleeuw is said to have been flooded once, which is why people sometimes speak of 'Verzopen Leeuw' (Drowned Leeuw). Because of the floods, the ground in and around the church was supposedly raised. As a result the most beautiful part of the church was not visible. When the Ven in Zoutleeuw froze in winter, many people came to skate. On Christmas night the sunken bells of Verzopen Leeuw could be heard ringing in the Ven. Someone had found a silk thread by the Ven. By pulling on that thread, people tried to bring up the sunken church, but they did not succeed.
196716: In Waasbeek a pregnant woman was about to give birth. Just at that moment her mother-in-law went away for two days. The child died after the birth. The mother-in-law had come in through the water drain in the shape of a toad to make the birth fail.
196719: On her deathbed a woman saw all kinds of strange beasts, which were probably devils. That woman had perhaps once told a lie.
196725: If you could make the werewolf bleed, he took on his human form.
196755: A sorceress who talked to herself all the time was not allowed near a child.
196761: People who were ridden by the mare had a dream in which they felt something moving over them.
196773: A postman often had to come home at night past a castle where the ghosts made a hellish din. Someone had to haunt the castle because a lot of money had once been squandered there. Several friars had to come to drive the ghosts away.
196791: During the First World War the Germans were shooting. A man who fled was astounded when he saw a hedge open up to let him through.
196800: A girl out with her mother and her aunt suddenly thought she saw a lantern in the sky. Her mother explained that it was not a lantern but a stallicht (will-o'-the-wisp). The light kept floating through the air. A little later there were even three lights. The priest said that stallichten were the souls of children who had died unbaptised, searching for heaven.
196826: A man coming back from the fair in Schoonderbuken suddenly saw a beautiful tree-lined lane at the spot where a witch lived.
196858: A vet came to a farm in Asse where one of the cows was ill. The farmer's wife said to the vet: "You can't do anything about it, because the cow is bewitched". The vet replied: "Yes I can. I can even show you the sorceress, but I have to fetch my book for that". The next day the vet had himself shut in the stable with a bucket of water. There he spoke all kinds of strange words and some Latin texts. Then the vet had the door opened and called the farmer's wife over, saying: "The face of the sorceress appears in this bucket". When the farmer's wife looked into the bucket, she said: "I see nothing but the reflection of my own face". The vet then said: "Then you are the sorceress. You always keep your stable shut, so no light or air can get in and the cows fall ill".
196861: A girl was often asked to help out in a rich family's house on the Grote Markt in Tienen. The girl was given clothes and all sorts of other things there. After a while the girl's parents heard from their neighbours that a witch lived in that house who was often after their daughter. Because the girl had also become completely emaciated, she was sent to a farm in the countryside, where she fully recovered.
196878: A woman who had already had much misfortune called N. a 'filthy fat maar (witch)' because she was convinced N. had bewitched her. N., however, would not stand for the insult and went to court. When the judge asked: "What punishment can I give that woman for it?", N. answered: "Give her a fine of one franc". In those days one franc was a lot of money. The woman had to pay the fine and the neighbours said: "To get compensation like that, you must be a witch!"
196914: In Sint-Lambrechts-Woluwe lived a witch who was married to a drunkard. One day the drunkard stole five francs from his wife's pocket. But the witch had seen it and said: "If you spend that money on drink, I'll make you mess your trousers!" The man did not listen and went to the inn. He had not even finished his first glass when the witch carried out her threat. After that the drunkard never stole money from his wife again.
196937: Will-o'-the-wisps were floating lights. A man who had fled inside from a will-o'-the-wisp heard a thump on the door a little later. A red hand was burnt into the door. Will-o'-the-wisps usually arose in summer near marshes. People used to believe such lights were the souls of unbaptised children.
196938: On a farm a farmer's wife was said to have died through witchcraft. This was only discovered, however, when the sorceress set her sights on the farmer's eighteen-year-old daughter.
196944: When people had thrown something at a cat, it could sometimes happen that the next day they saw a woman with a broken leg.
196962: A woman went to Leuven together with a witch. Behind the cemetery by the big linden tree in Linden, the witch said: "Go on ahead, I need to go to the toilet". The woman went on and did not see the witch again. But when the woman reached the station in Leuven, the witch was already standing there waiting for the tram. The witch had already done her shopping. The witch had probably seen a devil and flown with him to Leuven.
196963: A woman was visited by a female pedlar, to whom she gave a slice of bread. The pedlar said to the woman: "I can see from the whites of your eyes that you are still healthy". The next day, strangely enough, the woman had a swollen foot. After that the pedlar did not visit for a long time. When she came once more, the woman urged her husband to send the pedlar away as quickly as possible.
196972: People who were out at night were sometimes jumped by the mare and had to carry her.
196974: One day on a farm the sheep and horses were all lying against the dunghill. The farmer sent for a friar from Leuven, who came to inspect the farm. At one spot the farmer said: "We'll skip this one, it's an empty pigsty". But the friar said: "No, that must certainly be opened". The witch was in that sty.
196979: People who were ridden by the maar (nightmare spirit) had a bad dream.
196997: It was always haunted between the Eikske in Opwijk and the Ravenstraat in Opstal (Buggenhout). A man passing there one evening saw ten cows lying by the side of the road. When he came closer, the cows stood up and went along with him until he turned into another street.
197021: People who were ridden by the maar (nightmare) had an illness and lay sweating in their beds. Such people were advised to place their clogs upside down next to their bed, but that did not help.
197044: People believed that black cats were witches.
197068: Around three o'clock at night a man was walking home along an avenue of Canadian poplars. When he was about halfway, he felt two clods of turf fall on his shoulders. The next morning the man went back to look at the spot, but there was no trace of the clods.
197069: On a farm four animals had died within a month. There was blood in the cows' milk. The sorceress causing this misfortune came every day to ask for buttermilk, but one day she got no milk because there was none. That day the sorceress had said: "I wish everything here would rot". The farmer went to the witheren (Norbertine canons) of Ghent. The friar who came to read prayers over the farm predicted that in church a woman would give the farmer's wife a pat on the shoulder. When that happened, she had to strike the woman higher up. What the friar predicted did indeed happen. The farmer's wife struck higher and so put an end to the witchcraft.
197097: Two drunkards coming back from the fair saw a cat sitting along the way. One of them threw something at the cat. That man was dead before his friend got home.
197100: A woman with a bad name kept a hen with chicks. That way she could do harm to the animals and did not have to take people as victims.
197118: A woman always heard knocking when she lay in her bed, although there was nothing to be seen. The woman went to the fathers of Affligem to have the ghosts driven out.
197125: When people had misfortune in their stable, they believed they had been ridden by the maar (nightmare spirit).
197127: The devils worked on the white barn in Blauwput. Because the rooster had crowed too early, the barn was not finished in time.
197152: In Grazen there lived a woman who was said to be a witch. When people met that woman in the street, they walked away. A man who had met the witch one morning found in the course of the day that his house was full of lice and fleas.
197170: A woman made mice by throwing earth from a molehill on the ground.
197173: People who had been ridden by the moel (nightmare spirit) were bewitched.
197181: Toads were witches, so people believed. When people sat eating at four o'clock, a toad often jumped over their feet.
197190:
A boy worked as a stable hand at the castle in Terborg. Near that castle lived a woman known as a witch. One day the witch was cutting grass. The stable hand said: "You're getting on well with that!", to which the witch replied: "I have a good sickle" and handed the sickle to the boy. The stable hand was not afraid and took the sickle.
The same witch came into the parish priest's house while his servant was bringing in coal. Because it was so cold and the servant had no gloves, the witch said: "I'll go and get my gloves". When the man put on the gloves, he felt a stab in his hand. The hand then rotted away completely, and no doctor could do anything about it.
197200: At the bottom of a pond in Alsemberg there is said to lie a bell that had been hidden there.
197206: A farmer from Brabant needed a new barn because his old barn had blown down. One day the farmer was approached by the devil, who offered to build him a new barn in exchange for his soul. The barn would be built in a single night and had to be finished at the first cockcrow the next morning. At night the farmer told his wife what he had done. While the devils were working in the night, the farmer's wife got up and struck her clogs together, so that the rooster began to crow too early. But there was still a hole in the barn, which could never be closed afterwards. That barn was called 'the Blue Barn'.
197211: A woman was ridden by the maar (nightmare spirit) during a dream. She was completely rigid and could hardly breathe. The woman tried to call out to tell her husband she was dying, but no sound came. People could be ridden by the maar especially when they slept on their backs.
197230: If you lay down at a crossroads at midnight and asked the devil for a calfskin, you could become a werewolf. Werewolves had to frighten people and make themselves carried.
197235: A man had to make a pilgrimage for his dead wife, who had not been able to find rest.
197244:
A man whose wife had a bad reputation said to her one day: "Why do you always wear that black blouse?" The woman answered: "That is my power!" When the woman was dying, she said: "You must bury me with that black blouse when I die." The woman did not want a priest at her deathbed.
Eight days after the woman's death the widower kept hearing noise upstairs in the house. He went to look, but there was nothing to see. It sounded as if rats were running violently back and forth in the attic. The noises always started at midnight. When the man became plagued by lice and fleas, he had the fathers of Edingen say prayers over him. After that all the trouble came to an end. The dead woman had caused it.
197248: A man coming back drunk from Aalst one evening saw, near the Houten Hand, a fine inn he had never seen before. The man went into the inn, where people were dancing and the women were jumping over a fire. The man cried: "Jesus, Mary, you'll burn yourselves!" The next moment the inn had vanished and the man was standing in the grain. When the man went back to that spot the next day, he found some little chairs and a gold ring in the grain. On the ring was the name of a rich woman from Aalst. The man took the ring to the woman, hoping for a nice reward. When the man asked the woman whether the ring was hers, she answered: "You know that very well!" and slammed the door.
197253: A Capuchin friar found lots of pins in the cradle of a bewitched baby. To be able to work magic, one needed salt that had been used at a child's baptism.
197264: A man who consorted with the devil worked on a farm in Nijverzele. When the maids wanted to go to the fair in Moorsele, they were sad because they still had a lot of work to do. The man then said: "In an hour the work will be done. Lie flat on your stomachs and don't look at what happens." Then the man took a little creature out of a box. After that, a good hundred little men appeared who got the work done in an hour. Afterwards the maids could go to the fair after all.
197271: A man had moved the boundary post of his land to have more land. After his death the man haunted with the boundary post in his hands.
197273: Witches could turn themselves into a cat or a dog. A man going to work at ten o'clock in the evening saw a meowing cat behind him at the Duivelsborre. When the animal jumped on his back, the man ran off in fear. He believed the cat was a witch.
197312:
People who were ridden by the maar (nightmare) had a stagnation of the blood because they had met a witch during the day. A witch could bewitch someone by touching them or stepping in their footprints.
People who were ridden by the maar went on pilgrimage.
197327:
An old woman who was not feeling well was given a cushion by a neighbour to put in her armchair. The old woman claimed that the cushion was full of pins and had her daughter throw it into the oven. Afterwards the neighbour's face was completely burnt.
Witchcraft had something to do with old books bought at the market in Brussels.
197333: On the road to Tienen stood a farm that had once been a convent. During the French Revolution the convent was destroyed and the clergy murdered. Since then silent nuns and fathers in white clothes walked across the yard there every night.
197350: A man who had met a sorceress was ridden by the maar (nightmare spirit), which made him keep going round in circles. Had the man made the sign of the cross, he would have been freed at once.
197354: A woman whose husband had been a drunkard all his life had become a widow. Three nights in a row the woman saw her dead husband appear in the room. Her six-year-old son Dolf had seen nothing, although he had stayed awake. The priest told the woman that her husband had to wander as punishment for all the evil he had done during his life.
197356: To a farm in Orsmaal came a little old woman who had pain in her heart. As soon as she had been given something, the animals in the stable fell ill. The friars came to the farm and advised the people to hang a sheep's heart in the chimney. When the heart had decayed, everything would be all right again, provided they gave that woman nothing more.
197368: A woman had promised to go to Scherpenheuvel once a month for nine months so that her sick husband would recover. Because the man died after seven or eight months, the woman did not finish the novena. When, exactly one year after her husband's death, the woman was decorating the statue of Our Lady, she heard her husband's voice saying: "L., have you not forgotten me?" The woman answered: "No, for I still think of you and I still pray for you." "Yes, but," replied the dead man, "that's not what I mean. I mean that ninth one; until you have been to Scherpenheuvel once more, I can find no rest." The woman went to Scherpenheuvel at once. She was so shaken by the event that two years later she was completely emaciated.
197374: During catechism class a little boy made mice by shaking some earth off his shoe. That boy had not been baptised properly. After the priest had read over the child, he could no longer do magic.
197376: A man from Hoegaarden saw little lights flying back and forth in a meadow by the Gete. The lights were the little souls of children who had died unbaptised. The souls appeared close to the water because they wanted to be baptised.
197406: One Sunday evening L. was sitting in a café with H.V. At a certain moment L. got up to go home. On opening the door he saw a brown friar standing there. Frightened, L. said to his friend: "H., come and look, there's a brown friar here." L. and H. went outside together and followed the friar. When the friar reached the Vrankestraat, he suddenly disappeared. A while later a fireball almost as big as a haystack rose up in the marshland.
197407: A boy went walking with his girlfriend in the evening. At a certain moment the boy said: "I need to relieve myself. You walk on. If you meet anything, throw my handkerchief at the apparition." When a big dog came running up a little later, the girl threw her handkerchief at the animal. A little later her boyfriend came back to her. He had the fibres of the handkerchief between his teeth. He was the werewolf.
197426: The Kattenhuis was a convent of nuns that was seized by the French in 1770. The farmers who later came to live there saw the silhouette of a nun appear every night. Moreover, the animals in the stable were untied every night. The farmers went to the brown fathers of the Benedictine monastery in Bornem to have the farm blessed.
197427: A man saw a strange apparition in a well and began to pray the Gospel of Saint John. Then the apparition disappeared.
197432: A sorceress lived in Sint-Kwintens-Lennik. Whenever she stood in her doorway as a beer merchant drove past, the horses could not go on and began to rear.
197436: Anyone who had walked past a witch got a blow and a little later could no longer lift their arm. Those people would then go to the doctor. Only if the doctor could not help did they go to the parish priest.
197441: In Houwaart lived a woman who was said to be a witch. She had had no training, but served many young mothers as a midwife. One day the witch had to go to a pregnant woman who was about to give birth. The woman was in terrible pain. The witch just sat in a corner watching and did nothing. The pregnant woman was wearing a relic, you see. Only when the woman herself said: "Will you please come and have a look now?" did the witch fly from her chair and deliver the child.
197451: One evening a girl and her father saw a whole swarm of night lights near the woods. When the man pointed at the will-o'-the-wisps, one flew into the hedge at great speed. Pastor V.D.P. claimed that will-o'-the-wisps were the little souls of unbaptised children.
197458: Sorcerers and witches could make people over whom they had power lose their way.
197509: One Saturday evening a father and mother went to the inn with their little son. While the father was playing cards, the boy became fretful. A woman sitting in the inn wanted to comfort the child, but the mother did not like that. When the woman brought a slice of raisin bread, the child grabbed it and eagerly ate it. Shortly afterwards, however, the child fell ill, so the parents quickly went home. Because the child was deathly pale and began to tremble, the mother sent her husband to the presbytery. After the priest had read prayers over the child, it recovered. That woman in the inn was undoubtedly a maar (witch).
197510:
In a family a baby had fallen ill after a female visitor had sat beside the cradle. When that woman came to visit again, the child's mother put a wedding ring under the chair. At that the visitor stood up and left. She never came back.
People who were bewitched had prayers read over them.
197520: After C.'s wife had died, his child always heard knocking in the attic at night. The attic floorboards had already been broken open, but nothing was found. When the knocking was heard again one night, they asked: "What do you want? Must we go on a pilgrimage? How many times?" Then there were three knocks. After they had gone on pilgrimage three times for the dead woman, no more knocking was heard in the attic.
197528: A strange woman went somewhere to pick hops. But the hop vines kept falling from her lap. The farmer's wife explained to the woman how to hold the vines, but it was no use. The woman was bewitched. A little later she left without anyone seeing.
197542: When people got lost, it was said that they had been ridden by the maar (nightmare spirit).
197563: If you saw a black cat in the morning, you could invariably expect misfortune.
197565: A farmhand from Velp could hear the maar (nightmare spirit) coming every night. Then the maar tugged at the farmhand's chest, so that he felt he was going to die. The farmer's wife advised the farmhand to hold a knife on his chest with the point facing down. But the farmhand thought better of it and held the knife with the point facing up. When the maar came to ride the farmhand, her heart was pierced by the knife. The maar turned out to be the farmer's wife herself.
197575:
The sorceresses went dancing at night on the Vierdreef near the Hallerbos in Dworp. 
A man who had been bewitched was ill and always danced on his bed at night. During the day the man was cured. People claimed that he had been bewitched by his godmother.
197580: A family from Sint-Joris-Winge saw a black cat sitting in a tree every evening. One day the woman stabbed the black cat with a dung fork. The next day the woman met a widow who had pain in her back and her ribs.
197583: In the house of a woman who had been bewitched, people found sweets, chocolate and oranges. The woman had received all of it from a witch. A man put all the food under his clog and said: "Just see what you find under here tomorrow." The next day all the food had vanished and there was a toad under the clog.
197584: A farmer made a pact with the devil, who would build him a barn. The barn had to be finished before the rooster first crowed the next morning. But when the rooster crowed, the barn was not yet finished, so the farmer got to keep his soul. The hole in the barn could never be closed afterwards.
197603: Two brothers, probably Jews, were saying mass in the evening just like the priest. The devil came to serve the mass.
197607: Some people who had been murdered returned at night after their death wearing a little white cap on their heads.
197621:
When an exceptionally broad leaf grew on a plant, people believed that leaf had been ridden by the maar (nightmare spirit). This often happened, for instance, with beet seed plants that had a broad stalk.
People could also be ridden by the maar at night in their sleep.
197630: Toads and black cats were witches. If you threw such animals outside or wounded them, you could soon afterwards meet an old woman with a wound.
197635: Shepherds were nature spirits with a powerful mind. They could fix people to the ground by magic.
197646: P. always saw a strange man walking around the bakehouse, who disappeared after a while. Nobody else saw the apparition.
197655: A farmer's wife was herding her cows by the thorn of Saint Ermelindis when at one point a witch passed by. In the evening all the cows were ill.
197668: During the night after his father's funeral, T. heard a hellish noise in the house. The doors flew open and the chairs were thrown over. When the man went to the dean for advice the next day, he was advised to go to confession and communion. If he heard anything after that, he was to get up and go and look. That night the man got up and asked: "Is that you, father? What have you come for?" The ghost answered: "I hid ten francs in a catskin in the wall there and sealed the hole with clay." After that the ghost did not appear again.
197672: A farmer had a farmhand who often went out at night. Moreover, a dog or a werewolf was often seen in an alley in Dormaal. One day the farmer managed to make that werewolf bleed. The beast then turned into the farmhand who worked for him.
197689: A man walking home in the evening was hindered by a black cat that kept jumping between his legs. When he kicked at the cat, he was told: "You mustn't do that! Kicking a black cat is dangerous!" When the man went to bed that night, he kept hearing a sound. It sounded like a cat purring. The man looked and saw the cat lying at the foot of his bed.
197690: There was a hole in the devil's barn because the rooster had begun to crow before the barn was completed.
197703: If you had been touched by a witch, you had to stand still.
197708: People who had cramps in their legs at night and could not move said they had been ridden by the maar (nightmare spirit). Something similar also happened when people had eaten too heavy a meal in the evening.
197710: A young man and his wife had promised his father to have a mass said for him. But when the father had died, the man and the woman forgot the mass. Whenever it got dark, a moving wind was always heard in a corner of the house. When one day the priest asked: "What is it you want?", a voice answered: "A mass." At that moment the man and the woman remembered the requiem mass they had promised. When the mass had been said, no more wind was heard rustling in the house.
197725: A man driving his horse and cart to market found that his horses always stopped at a certain spot. A cat would then jump onto the cart and the man could do nothing with his whip. One day the man went to the priest and asked: "Father, may I leave my whip with you for two weeks to drive out the evil hand?" The priest agreed. When the man came to collect his whip two weeks later, the witchcraft was over. By way of thanks, the man brought the priest a piece of pork.
197736: People who slept badly and felt something lying on them at night said they had been ridden by the maar (nightmare spirit). The maar was a horse that lay on its victims at night, so that they could no longer move and could hardly breathe.
197754: Stalkaarsen (will-o'-the-wisps) were the little souls of mistreated children who had died unbaptised. The little flames that moved back and forth were seen mainly in low-lying areas.
197766: In Moorsel lived a woman whose child suffered from a strange illness. At night the child was thrown up against the ceiling. In the end the mother went to the friars, who said: "When you are home, someone will come and ask what time it is, but you must not let that woman in". The mother had been home only ten minutes when someone indeed came by. The mother told the woman the time, but did not tell her she could come in. After that the child's health improved day by day.
197787: A mother whose twenty-four-year-old daughter had died always believed she saw her daughter at night. People who came back after their death usually asked those left behind to pray for them.
197790: The werewolf sometimes jumped onto passers-by's backs and then made itself carried.
197810: A woman whose mother had died met a witch and said: "I ought to be able to cry." The witch replied: "Oh, if that's all, just go home and you'll see." When the woman went home, she felt as if pins were being stuck into her body, which made her cry for five days.
197816:
If you walked in a witch's footprints, the witch could go no further.
When a man followed close behind a woman to find out whether she was a witch, the woman turned around and boxed his ears.
197825: In a village lived a woman everyone was afraid of. One day a girl came home with a bag of sweets. When she told her mother she had got the sweets from an unknown woman, the mother threw them away. A few weeks later the same woman came along to shelter from a thunderstorm. The girl said to her mother: "Look, mummy, that's the woman who gave me the sweets!" The mother got scared and did not dare open the front door, after which the woman came round the back. The mother quickly sprinkled her threshold with holy water. The woman stayed outside the whole time, even though they told her: "But madam, do come in".
197840: A woman came to feel the body of a man who had died and said: "I have heard that if a body does not go cold quickly, another body will follow within the month". Afterwards that woman bewitched the dead man's daughter. The girl got headaches, just as her father had had. But they sought advice somewhere for the girl, so the witch was unable to make her die.
197848: Witches could cover people in lice.
197868: On a farm a dead woman appeared in the form of a white ghost that lashed out around her.
197873: A witch who lived in a little clay house had a walnut tree. The children often climbed into that tree to steal nuts. Through a gap in the hedge the boys saw the witch coming with a sack of fodder on her head. The boys ran away, but their friend who was still in the walnut tree could only escape later with his sack of nuts. When the boy wanted to share out the nuts, he could not; all the nuts had vanished.
197880: In a house where there were seven children, the youngest child began to cry every night. People had a good idea who was responsible for the evil. The priest therefore advised the family not to let that woman in anymore and not to accept anything from her. When they did so, the evil came to an end.
197897: On a verloren maandag (Lost Monday, a holiday after Epiphany) a man went with his violin to play music in a café in Halle. When after a while the man moved on to another inn, he saw a cart of dancing and singing women drive past. The women cried: "Play on, oh Jantje, play on!" The man played the violin until the drops of sweat rolled down his face. If anyone spoke the word 'God' or 'Jesus' at such a moment, the whole scene vanished at once. The women had brought the man a chair to sit in. When the man sat there out of breath watching the dancing women and said: "Oh Jesus," everything vanished. The man was sitting on a stone on the ground and had a cobblestone in his hands.
197900: A woman was bringing in the washing one evening. After all, if the laundry was left hanging outside at night, it could be bewitched by witches. Suddenly the woman saw a crow fly over her head, and she fearfully thought that her son, who was a soldier in the First World War, might well be dead. After the war, however, her son came home safely. When the mother told him what she had seen, the son said: "Yes, it was a close call. My two horses were shot dead, but I came out of it alive."
197905: People who were ridden by the maar (nightmare spirit) had a nasty dream in which they felt someone was sitting on them.
197934: Stallichten (will-o'-the-wisps) were little lights that came out of a marsh. They were the little souls of unbaptised children.
197939: A farmhand who worked for a farmer was always dead tired when he came home in the evening. When his wife asked why, the farmhand said: "I don't know what it is, but when I'm in that street, something always jumps on me. It's something heavy that I have to carry the whole way. When I get to the door here, it suddenly disappears. If the figure jumps on me again tomorrow evening, I'll stamp my feet hard and you must open the door, so that I can throw the weight on my back inside." No sooner said than done. That is how they discovered that the man was being jumped by a beast in an animal skin. They gave the beast a good thrashing. When the farmhand came to the farm the next day, he saw the farmer sitting by the stove covered in bruises.
197956: At the cavalry barracks of Glabbeek six cows had already died. When two calves died as well, a friar was called in to bless the place with prayers.
197957: In Sint-Martens-Bodegem lived a woman from whom people did not dare to accept an apple. They put a drop of holy water in their milk so as not to be bewitched by that woman.
197965: A woman from Opheule sold goat's milk. Two mothers who were neighbours bought milk from her for their newborn babies. After a while, however, they noticed that the children were not growing. Because the children suffered from 'the old man' (rickets), a pilgrimage was made for them. That did no good, so one of the mothers went to a holy man who would tell her who had bewitched her. After the man from Ukkel had muttered prayers for a long time, he took out a glass ball with holy water and said: "Now you will see her." In the ball appeared a woman cutting grass with a sickle. That was of course the woman who sold the goat's milk, for she was always cutting grass for her goats. After that the mother bought no more goat's milk. She remained very friendly to the sorceress, however, because the holy man had advised her to. The other mother also went to the holy man and stopped buying goat's milk. After that both children quickly recovered.
197972: A woman was tormented by her mother-in-law, who was a witch. Because the woman's daughter often had fits, they took her to a healer in Borgloon. There the girl had to drink holy water. When the girl had another fit on the spot, the healer concluded that the devil had something to do with it. The girl had to be held down, for she sat trembling on a chair and kept pushing the water away. In the end the girl did drink the holy water.
197974: In a house where a wicked woman came in, the visitor was thrown out. A while later, however, a black cat came in and let the children stroke it. The people thrashed the cat, and the animal ran away. The next day that wicked woman was covered in bruises.
198002: When many animals had died on a farm, people believed the evil hand had something to do with it. In reality the animals may have eaten something bad, but people always blamed the misfortune on a sorceress. They would then seek advice from the friars of Dendermonde. When a new house was built, people also often bricked a little cross or a medal in under the threshold.
198014: You could hear the mare coming and hear the door slam. Then you could no longer move. People who were ridden by the mare grew very thin.
198019: At a school in Walshoutem the children had seen that a girl could make mice by throwing earth on the floor. When the children told the priest, the clergyman read over the girl, after which she could no longer make mice.
198024: Strange things happened in the woods of Houwaart. People who came there to cut grass got a punch in the back and fell forward, although there was nothing to be seen. People believed that a treasure lay hidden there. Someone must have dug up the treasure, for after a while the haunting stopped.
198027: It was said of a certain woman that she could turn herself into a dog and that she went to steal hay from a farmer.
198029: The witches held yearly gatherings in a wine cellar in Cologne. Before leaving they said: "Over bush and over hedge." Then they flew through the air. A man who had once overheard the witches and decided to follow them made a mistake in saying the magic formula and said: "Through bush and through hedge." That man arrived in the wine cellar badly injured.
198033: People who were ridden by the maar (nightmare) had bad luck in whatever they did.
198042: On a farm troubled by a plague of rats, someone was called in to overlezen (recite a charm over) the farm. That person said: "There's still one left behind." Then that person did something that made the last rat come running too.
198072: Stallichten (will-o'-the-wisps) were the souls of the dead who came to sit by the water. If you pointed at a stallicht, it came and sat on your finger. Some people believed that will-o'-the-wisps were really just vinkhout (?).
198094: By a witch's house stood a large rhubarb plant under which a black cat always lay. People would say: "That is no cat. That is the witch lying under there." A man threw stones at the cat, but the animal would not be chased away.
198144: In Grimde lived a witch who had caused her daughters to die by bewitching them.
198150: In the old days, when people saw an ugly old woman, they often suspected her of being a witch. One morning a man found that he was covered in lice. However much his wife washed or scrubbed, the lice could not be driven away. After the man had been read over by the Friars Minor in Sint-Truiden, he was rid of his lice.
198159: In Beigem the devil had set a stable on fire.
198162: When people had bad luck, it was said they had been ridden by the maar (nightmare spirit).
198171: Jan had once promised to have a mass said for a relative. When Jan had heard knocking in the wardrobe at about the same time for several days, he remembered the promise. After Jan had the promised mass said, he no longer heard the knocking.
198176: A witch could stick pins into children's pillows, which made the child cry all the time. Witches could also give people lice. The witch's craft could be passed down from mother to daughter.
198179: A farmer needed a new barn to store his harvest in. The farmer sold his soul to the devil, who would build him a new barn during the night. That barn had to be finished before the first cockcrow the next morning. When he got home, however, the man grew anxious and told his wife about his agreement with the gentleman who had appeared in the field. When the devils were heard working in the night, the farmer's wife took the lantern and went to the henhouse. There the rooster began to crow too early. At that moment there was still a small hole in the barn, but the devils flew away because they had heard the rooster crow. The farmer got to keep his soul. The hole in the barn could only be closed by walling a cross into it.
198188: On a farm in Goetsenhoven there was nothing but misfortune. The children fell ill and it was said that some animals in the stable 'burst'. A woman often came to that farm to borrow something. Someone advised the people not to put the requested object into her hands next time. If the woman then did not pick it up herself, they could be sure she was a witch. Shortly afterwards the woman came to ask for a hatchet. When she did not pick up the hatchet, the farmer knew enough. He went to the friars in Sint-Truiden to fetch a relic. After that he had no more trouble in his house.
198217: If a broom had been laid on the ground, a witch could not step over it.
198258: Witches could turn themselves into animals, for example a rabbit or a cat.
198276: A man going to fetch his little daughter in the evening met an old woman on the way, who said: "What a lovely child!" The next day the child could no longer walk. She had been bewitched. A visitor advised the father to take his child to the church of Mere. Near the church door the parents saw a sorceress sitting on a stone. The mother went up to her and asked what she was doing there. "I've come to get seed," the sorceress answered, to which the mother said: "How can that be?! You have no land at all! Get away from here!" After the people had made a novena, their child could walk again.
198285: When one heard an owl screech, someone would soon die.
198298: Sorceresses read evil books from which they learned wickedness. Sorceresses could even enter a house through the keyhole.
198309: On a farm there was much misfortune in the stable. The soft white cheese they made stank terribly and the work the people did never came to anything. At their wits' end, the farmer's wife went to the friars at the Heyzel to have prayers said over her. The friar told her: "When you get home, hold two bricks behind your back at the farm gate and let them fall crosswise. Leave the pieces lying there." The woman did as she was advised. After that a woman from the neighbourhood 'who was known for it' no longer came to visit.
198316: A one-year-old girl had fallen ill and was wasting away. Because people believed the child had been struck by the evil hand, they went to the friars of Sint-Truiden, who advised them to give up their best animal and to put a black hen in a certain place. The person who was the cause of all the misery would come and take the hen. The mother hid behind the bushes and soon saw a woman come and take the hen. At that moment the family's best cow died, but the child recovered.
198328: In Nieuwenrode lived a nun who could work magic. One day that woman had given biscuits to a little child. Afterwards the child died.
198339: A man from Okselaar went one evening to visit a friend, who said: "I'm afraid. Every night when I lie in my bed, I hear noises as if trains were running across my attic. Something is wrong with the stove too, because the lid keeps flying up and rattling." The man replied: "Yes, my friend, then the witches are in here." The man had heard it said that his friend's wife was a witch. He advised his friend to stop up the drain hole in his house, because he had heard that witches often came in that way. When the friend heard noise again that night, he got up and found that his wife was not in bed. In the room sat two black cats, which leapt towards the drain hole. The friend struck at the cats with an axe. One of the cats was hit on the paw and the other escaped unharmed. Afterwards the friend found that his wife was the witch.
198384: One day a woman had visited a farm. The next day a pig lay dead in the stable. The animal immediately turned completely black.
198387: If people heard a crow screeching above their heads, they believed misfortune would come.
198423: Many people were ridden by the mare. These people felt something crawling on their bodies when they lay in bed. They could not move and sweated terribly. To protect themselves against the mare, people placed their wooden shoes crossed beside their bed. Some put a crucifix or an axe with the blade facing up under their bed.
198478: The framassons (freemasons) flew through the air to drink wine in a wine cellar in Cologne. A man who was flying with the framassons for the first time bumped into the cross on the church tower. That man never came back.
198483: In a house the door to the cellar stairs inexplicably flew open and shut at night. People said that the house was haunted.
198499: People who were ridden by the mare could not sleep at night and were very restless.
198508: In Vissenaken will-o'-the-wisps were often seen above the Velp. It was said that these lights were the little souls of unbaptised children who still wanted to be baptised.
198516: In a family in Oetingen three people had already died through witchcraft. In those houses the plates were thrown off the shelves after midnight. The family's son had once met the sorceress when she asked whether he would carry her oats. The man had refused, however. He died of fright.
198521: After the fair, a woman had gone to a café to fetch beer dregs to give to the pigs. Afterwards the pigs behaved very strangely. They became so wild that they bit each other's ears off. The woman was convinced she had been bewitched.
198529: One day a witch from Bogaarden had given a pear to a child. When the child got home, it felt like vomiting. When the child told about the pear it had been given, the father went to the witch and said: "If you don't undo the harm you have done to my child, you're dead." The witch then laid her hand on the child's shoulder, after which the child vomited up a fat toad.
198537: People who did not want to be ridden by the mane (nightmare spirit) had to ride a stick flat.
198554: A mother had murdered her child and buried the little body in a remote place. After a while people saw a will-o'-the-wisp moving back and forth above the Kratenberg. As soon as people had found the child's body in the woods, the will-o'-the-wisp disappeared.
198559: A woman had agreed with her husband that whichever of them died first would come back after death to tell how things were in the hereafter. When the man had died, the widow heard a strange noise one night. The ghost of the dead man pushed aside a roof tile, crawled inside and said: "There everything is strictly reckoned, but little is forgiven." The ghost laid his hand on the widow's shoulder and then vanished. The handprint was burned into the woman's shoulder.
198575: A woman who was ridden by the mare lay stiff as a board in her bed and saw nothing.
198576: When a man came back from the churchyard one day, he cried: "Mother, open up, for I have seen a dead man in the churchyard!"
198635: Witches sometimes went about in the shape of black cats.
198643: J. lived at the Grevensmolen in Sint-Truiden. When the boy lay in bed at night, he often heard someone walking from one room to another. One night the door of his room opened and a little old woman came in. After that night the boy was so frightened that he no longer dared to sleep alone. When the boy told his grandfather what was going on, the old man replied: "Have you seen her too? This farm used to be lived in by B.J. Because B. had only a daughter, at her death she left the farm to her son-in-law. But he had had to promise always to have a mass said for B. on fair day. After the French had invaded the farm, the son-in-law never had a mass said again. B. still comes haunting to claim the promised masses."
198662: In the old days women wore a big red handkerchief with dots. One day kludde (a shapeshifting spook) had completely unravelled such a woman's handkerchief. The next day that woman met someone who had the fibres of the handkerchief between his teeth. That is how the woman found out who kludde was, and she cried: "You attacked me yesterday and took my handkerchief!" At that kludde began to weep, because his time would have been up a few days later and now he had to start all over again.
198673: In the village an old woman lived alone in a little house. People were afraid of her. Sometimes she could make the horses refuse to go on, so the carter went to fetch her from her house and said: "If you don't let me go quickly, I'll beat you black and blue!" The woman got scared and muttered something, after which the horses started moving again.
198684: A witch who had turned herself into a hunchback came to a farmer. Afterwards one of the farmer's horses died.
198691: A sorceress had a black cat which she used to bewitch people. Sometimes she took someone by the arm and led them to a place where they could no longer move.
198693: A man who had been visiting a neighbour who lived a few houses away could not get home because he could no longer find his house. In the field the man saw a house with small windows, although he knew very well that there had never been a house there. The man was forced to go back to his neighbour's house to ask the way.
198700: A man sleeping in the attic was tormented one night by the maar (nightmare spirit). The maar made a buzzing sound like bees. The maar crawled up to the man's face and pressed on his chest. The man grabbed at his chest and threw the maar onto a cart. The other people were woken by the pounding of the man's heart. On the cart a thick ball of hair was found.
198730:
A woman who suspected she was bewitched went to the friars to have prayers said over her. The clergymen told her: "Someone has power over you. It is someone with a cotton neckerchief. You must avoid that woman and make sure your children accept nothing from her. The woman will no longer be able to enter your house if you put a relic under the door."
Such a friar could make the sorceress responsible for the evil appear in the mirror.
198732: On the road from Dormaal to Landen there once stood an old cottage where a witch lived. That witch had made a pact with the devil. If the witch touched a child, the child was possessed by the devil. Once the witch had uttered a curse when she was chased out of the wood where she wanted to gather firewood. The farmer who had chased the witch away then suffered much misfortune. His horse, his cows and his pigs died, and one morning the farmer's family lay dead in bed. The farmer was doomed to wander forever. In gloomy weather his soul could often be heard calling for help.
198734: At the home of a man from Westrode (a hamlet of Wolvertem) there was always rumbling at night, as if a pack of dogs were in the attic. When people went to look, there was never anything to be seen.
198739: On a farm there was a lamb whose legs were twisted into the straw every morning. The farmer's wife believed the evil hand was in her stable and had the priest come to bless the place with prayers. The clergyman gave her a medal to put under a stone at the stable entrance. After that was done, nothing strange happened to the lamb anymore. The people were therefore convinced that the evil hand had been in their stable.
198740: A mother had a nine-year-old son. One day the boy said he had a headache. The mother took him to the doctor, who said: "That will be a cold." He gave her a medicine to spray into her son's nose. The child, however, got sicker and sicker. After a while the mother decided to go to another doctor, as the local doctors had fled because there was a war. That other doctor claimed the child had appendicitis and gave her medication for her son. But the child did not recover. An acquaintance advised the mother to take her son to a woman in Brussels. Because the mother did not feel up to it, a neighbour went to Brussels in her place with a photo of the sick boy. The woman in Brussels told the neighbour: "If the boy is still alive when you get home, he will live. But tell the mother she must not give the child any medicine from the doctor. Tell her also that she must pray a lot and get up at night to pray." When the neighbour got home, the child was still alive. The mother did as she was advised and got up at night to pray. After a while the boy recovered. One day the mother went to the woman in Brussels herself and asked: "But madam, what was wrong with my son?" The woman claimed the boy had fallen ill through an evil hand. She was not allowed to say, however, who was responsible for the evil.
198782: Sometimes horses under the influence of the evil hand suddenly stood still in the dark.
198789: In Laar lived a witch who could make animals ill by entering the stable. On one farm the cows gave no more milk after the witch had been in the stable.
198791: Some drunkards went to the churchyard at night to mock the dead and to play skittles with the skulls. When one of those men passed the churchyard some time later, a skull rolled after him until he got home.
198802: A mother whose baby no longer wanted to breastfeed went to the priest because her child was losing weight. The clergyman said she should put the child to the breast again. "That's no use," the woman answered, "the child won't drink anyway." Nevertheless she followed the priest's advice. Her child drank milk and recovered. From then on she was not to let in a wicked woman who had visited her.
198808:
A scrawny woman with three or four children was suspected of witchcraft. The woman had a moustache.
At New Year not a single child dared to go singing at her door.
198818: A broom maker from Schoonderbuken set off one morning with his cart when suddenly wild cats jumped onto the cart. The man struck at the animals with his whip and drove on. That whole day, however, he did not sell a single broom. The next day the man told an old woman what had happened to him. The woman said to him: "You shouldn't have done that. You should have asked whether the cats wanted a ride." When the man wanted to set off with his cart a week later, the cats were there again. The man asked whether the animals wanted a ride, but not a single cat jumped onto his cart. The man sold all his brooms in less than half a day.
198832: On a farm where one of the sows was not growing well, people put an Easter candle under the threshold. After they had done so, a certain woman could no longer get in.
198836: A witch caused black birds, much bigger than starlings, to be seen everywhere. A girl smashed her head right through the door as a result of the witch's torments.
198839: A man kept hearing someone calling: "Post moved, post moved!" After someone had given the dead man a releasing answer, the dead man was heard no more.
198856: In Bever lived a girl who was very ill. After people had gone to the white friars of Gent for her, the child's health improved. The friars predicted that the woman who had bewitched the child would come to visit the next morning. The next day it turned out that the child had been bewitched by two women. Those women always came bringing something, such as grapes or oranges.
198866: During a plague epidemic the inhabitants of Attenhoven had promised to go on pilgrimage to Scherpenheuvel every year. Once, when the procession was not held because the weather was too bad, people found the next day that the statue of Mary was smeared with mud.
198885: In Sint-Pieters-Rode lived a dangerous witch who had bewitched a woman on one farm and caused a calf to die by stroking it. On another farm she had touched piglets and said: "Those are fine animals!" Not one piglet survived. It was said that this witch could fly noisily through the air with a ham bone between her legs. The witch was never home at night and did not go to church. In the end the witch's husband told the priest everything.
198900: In a house in Bortmeerbeek knocking was always heard at night. The knocking always began at a different time. Sometimes the people stayed up all night because they could not sleep anyway. All the people from the neighbourhood came to keep watch in that house.
198959: Between Bierbeek and Neervelp lived a farmer who had a fine harvest but no barn to store it in. One day this farmer met the devil, who said to him: "If you give me your best pledge, you will have a very large barn tomorrow." The farmer did not quite understand what the man meant, but agreed to the proposal. When the farmer lay in bed, he heard a hellish noise and told his wife what he had done. The farmer's wife jumped out of bed at once and clapped her hands. After that the devils stopped working. There was still a hole in the roof of the barn, which could only be closed by putting a cross in it.
198976: Some young men often went to dance halls and fairs together. The men had already noticed that someone from their group often disappeared for a while. Whenever that happened, the men were frightened by a dog. An old man advised them to throw a red handkerchief into the dog's mouth. No sooner said than done. When the man who had stayed behind rejoined the group, the red fibres could be seen sticking out between his teeth.
198977: On a farm struck by the evil hand there was always misfortune. The cows died and all sorts of other strange things happened. People troubled by such misfortune had to pray a lot and go to the friars of Dendermonde. They then received medals to put under the door, so that the sorceress could no longer come in.
198979: In a house on the Wimersestraat, people heard a commotion in the stable at night. The farmer went to look and saw a goose sitting on the stable door, which flew away a moment later. The cows' chains were so tangled that the animals were nearly strangled. The same scene was repeated several times. In the morning everything was always back to normal. When the house had become dilapidated and was demolished, money and little gold coins were found in the stable.
198999: A man who drank a lot was coming back at about one in the morning from the fair in Eliksem. In the Galgenstraat he thought he saw a chain hanging in a Canadian poplar. He was afraid and stood stock-still. When he went on a little later, he heard the chain rattling. Whenever he stood still, the sound could no longer be heard. When he went on, he heard the clinking of the rattling chain. The man walked as far as a farm, where he heard something and began to scream loudly. The next moment a pack of piglets came down the ladder. The piglets ran to the church and in their fury battered in the church door.
199003: Some people went for a glass of beer to celebrate a child's baptism. While they were sitting in the inn, someone came in through the back door. Afterwards the child's mother fell ill. Every evening a good twenty-five white cats walked under the skylight where the sick woman lay. Those cats had been sent by the witch. The friars were able to free the woman from the evil, and she recovered. The child, however, could not be saved and died a short time later.
199028: People who were ridden by the maar (nightmare spirit) dreamed that they could not move forward. In reality these people had a stoppage of the blood.
199038: A man who saw a ghost leap out of the verge wanted to give the apparition a beating. He did not manage it, however, because the ghost vanished at once. Still, the man's hands were battered.
199041: If someone had done a piece of work beyond human strength, people believed that person had been helped by the devil. This was said especially of someone who was an unbeliever or did not often go to church.
199059: In Kruis lived a man with special powers. One day the wizard said: "Tonight people will come to pick my cherries, but tomorrow we will know who the thieves are, because they will be standing in front of the bridge." And so it happened. The thieves had been fixed to the ground by magic.
199074: In Wolvertem the devil had to build a barn, which had to be finished before the rooster had crowed three times. But he did not succeed. In the devil's barn there is a hole that could never be closed.
199079: In Neerlinter people often ran away from a certain witch. That witch harmed her own children when she could find no other victim. A boy from Neerlinter who had only half a hand was said to have fallen victim to his mother's witchcraft.
199080: A man coming back from the fair fell on a bridge and broke his leg because of a sorceress.
199086: A woman suspected of being a sorceress went listening at windows and doors everywhere. She very often brought people an apple or something else. When that sorceress lay dying, a clergyman had to be called because she could not die.
199096: A woman standing in the shop suddenly felt a breath of wind on her neck. When the woman came home, she found that she was covered in lice. That woman was stuck with the lice for exactly one year. Whatever she tried, she could not get rid of the vermin.
199107: People believed they could become bewitched by seeing a black cat.
199118:
Around three o'clock at night a man was cycling back from his work in Liège. On the way he saw a woman dressed in white standing at the window of a house. The man believed it was the lady of the castle, visiting her daughter-in-law's house because perhaps someone there was ill. But when the man went to the house the next day to ask whether someone was ill, the answer was no. No one ever knew who had stood at the window. In the oak door of the house, however, little crosses were stuck. A week later that house burned down. In a pond not far from that house, one body after another was found.
In a house where rich people lived, the woman had disappeared one morning. Her body was found in the Gete.
199122: In East or West Flanders an Augustinian nun came to a house where someone had died. In the room where the dead person was laid out, the nun saw a dog appear, which put its paw on the corpse. The nun was convinced that the dead person had been a freemason, whose soul was now being taken by the devil.
199132: A witch who kept being made pregnant by her husband burned the man in the oven.
199152: At a wedding there was a woman who had special powers. When at one point the woman slapped the table with her flat hand, mice ran everywhere. Everyone became frightened and in the end the families even quarrelled.
199158: A postman returning in the evening from a visit to his girlfriend was ridden by the mare at a crossroads. Because of this the man turned back, and at three in the morning he was standing at the gate of his girlfriend's house again. Many people did not dare go to crossroads at night.
199184: When people had misfortune in their stable or when their children died, they often believed they had been bewitched. In Elingen there once lived an old woman whom many people avoided because they thought she was a sorceress.
199188: Some poachers went to spy on a man in the Doleeg. Suddenly bells could be heard ringing, and the poachers quickly fled.
