The next year the poachers went to that spot again and heard the beautiful music of the Tillekesjacht (a phantom hunt). Many centuries ago a chapel is said to have sunk in the Doleeg. On Christmas night, between twelve and one, the bells of that chapel could still be heard ringing.
199213: In a house in Beert the chairs began to dance at night. An old priest came to bless the haunted house. Afterwards that priest died.
199215: A mother had many problems with her little daughter. It seemed as if the child had epilepsy. The girl kept twisting her little arm. Some people claimed the evil hand did not exist, but the mother would say: "Then why is it written on the memorial card: 'It is better to die early than to be tormented long by the Evil One'?" After a curate had said prayers over the child in honour of Saint Quirinus, the child was cured.
199217: In a house a little boy had fallen ill. The child claimed he saw an old woman standing by the ceiling, pricking his body with pins. Because the father believed witchcraft was involved, he sent his wife to a pious spinster in the village. She gave the woman a piece of Easter candle and a medal and said: "If your son recovers through this, then it was the evil hand." The boy did indeed recover. A few weeks later, however, the medal was lost, and the boy fell ill again. As soon as the medal was found, the boy recovered again.
199244: A bell that had not been consecrated had fallen into a pool in Zepperen. There was a thread attached to the bell, but people did not manage to pull the bell out of the pool.
199246:
Between Houwaart and Nieuwrode lived a woman who was said to be a witch. Two girls always walked to school together. One day one of the girls said that strange things were happening in her house. At midnight a fly flew around the paraffin lamp and the light went out. The people were terrified and believed that the witch was responsible for the strange events. A neighbour did not believe these stories about witchcraft and decided to keep watch in the house for a night. The man sat by the stairs with his gun. When the fly appeared, he fired several times, but he did not manage to hit it.
One day the man drove to the field to fetch fodder for his animals. On the way he met the witch. The witch said to him: "You wanted to shoot me dead, but you couldn't hit me after all!"
The people then sought advice from the priest, who advised them to pray. Nine days later the fly no longer appeared. While the priest was praying, the sweat ran down his face.
199258: In Sint-Pieters-Kapelle lived an old woman who was suspected of being a sorceress. She walked with a raised shoe because she had been poorly treated after breaking her leg. That woman lived to be over ninety.
199267: A man walking home at night often saw a big dog with a long chain. The man believed that dog was the devil.
199270: In winter a man was always followed by a black dog at around nine or ten o'clock in the evening. One evening the man wanted to shoot at the dog. But it did not work, for the bullet lodged in a door and the dog was unharmed.
199275: Two friends were on their way to Landen. On the way one of the friends said: "I need to go number two. You go on ahead. If you meet a black dog or another beast, you must strike its mouth with a handkerchief." The friend did as he was advised. When the other man came back a little later, he had the fibres of the handkerchief between his teeth.
199279: When an animal died on a farm in Sint-Lambrechts-Woluwe, people often said it had been bewitched by a woman who worked on the farm.
199310: In Vissenaken there stood a Mission Cross where people came to pray. One day the priest had the cross removed. Whenever Miss M. sat in the church, she always saw a white father come out of the confessional. The third time Miss M. stayed seated because she wanted to know what the ghost wanted. The white father said that people must pray at the Mission Cross again. Where the ghost had touched the young woman, her arm was completely burned. After that the Mission Cross was put back.
199320: In the Kravaalbos in Mazenzele there was a pit, the Mazelegraat, in which a bell had sunk. People had hidden the bell there during the French Revolution so it would not be confiscated. When they later wanted to get the bell out of the pit, however, they could not. When the carter swore, the rope broke and the bell sank so deep into the Mazelegraat that it could no longer be seen. Every year the bell could be heard ringing at twelve o'clock on Christmas night.
199323: A man had a child who cried all the time because it was ill. It was said the child had been struck by the evil hand. Whenever the child became fretful, it had to be put on the swing at once. When the friars came to say prayers over the child, they said: "The witch will come in at ten o'clock tonight, but no one may offer her a chair." In the end the child recovered. The witchcraft had probably been caused by a sweet the child had received from the witch.
199358: A few men went to keep watch in the castle on the Pers, where it was haunted every night. At midnight the door flew open and a skull was thrown in. A little later there were bones lying in the room as well. Nobody dared to speak or draw his revolver. The skeleton said: "Follow me" and led the men to a stone. When the skeleton said: "Lift it up", the men answered: "Do it yourself". Then the skeleton, cursing, lifted the stone. Under the stone were pots filled with money. "Now I am released", said the skeleton, and it vanished.
199371: A man in a wheelchair claimed that his own wife had bewitched him since their wedding. That way she had made sure her husband could not follow her when she went out.
199384:
A woman who was having trouble with one of her children suspected a neighbour of being a witch. The mother put a piece of a blessed candle under the stairs. After that, the suspected neighbour could no longer get outside!
The child, who was seventeen months old, eventually died.
199415: In the wood on the hill someone had moved the boundary post of his land. When the man died thirty years later, he had to haunt with a boundary post in his hands, calling: "Post, I have moved you, I carry you where I want".
199454: Ugly old women who did not look after themselves and who rudely chased children away were often accused of witchcraft.
199455: A woman was tapped on the shoulder by a witch. The next day the woman could no longer lift her arm. She was bewitched.
199466: A child who was growing but would not eat and was wasting away completely could not be helped by the doctors. The family took the child to the friars of Edingen, who asked: "Is there not a woman who comes to your house and gives the child sweets?" The people confirmed this, and the friars advised them to keep that woman out of their house. The people also had to put a blessed candle under the doormat at the front door. When the woman came to visit the next day, she stood stock-still and could go no further. The woman went back home and never visited those people again. The child was cured.
199467: On a farm in Haasrode all the cows died, so the people went to the parish priest. The priest advised them to place a burning bundle of straw in the meadow during high mass the following Sunday. The witch would then come to the bundle of straw. The farmer did as he had been advised. The bundle of straw had barely caught fire when the witch came running and shouted that they must put the fire out. The farmer said he would only do so once the witch had undone the spell. The witch then went to the cowshed and took a cushion with pins out from under the manger. After that the witchcraft was over.
199486: Two brothers who had been playing cards met a white cat on their way home and gave the animal a good kick.
199501: A man had heard that a certain place was haunted. The Tillekesjacht (a flying troop of witches) gathered there. The man went to that place and heard the witches say: "Over hedge and over hedgerow to Cologne into the wine cellar!" The man wanted to follow the witches and said: "Through hedge and through hedgerow to Cologne into the wine cellar!" The man arrived at his destination badly injured.
199506: A mother who had just had a child received pensen (Flemish blood or meat sausages) from a neighbour. While the mother was breastfeeding the child, she suddenly saw blood running from the baby's mouth. A little later the child was dead. Afterwards someone said to the mother: "You didn't eat those pensen, did you? They were bewitched!"
199515: Will-o'-the-wisps were the souls of unbaptised children who wandered above the sea. When 'the German' from Neerwinden saw a will-o'-the-wisp, he tried in vain to hit the light with a stick. In the end the man ended up at the church of Wange, where the will-o'-the-wisp suddenly disappeared.
199526: In Kestergat there was a house where the cows jumped into the manger and where the doors were slammed shut by an unknown force. A friar went to bless that house.
199547: A man walking at night on a little field path between Helen and Melkwezer was hindered by a horse that kept bumping into him. The man went to another meadow. A little later he found that the horse was standing there too.
199559: A woman left Sint-Ulriks-Kapelle and opened a butcher's shop with her husband in another village. When the woman had a two-month-old child, she was constantly visited by a neighbour, who touched the child's little hands and face. One day the child began to cry without stopping. The mother was advised to go to the abbey of Affligem, where a friar advised her to pray. But because the child's condition got worse, the woman went to the friars again. This time the clergymen asked whether she perhaps had visitors in the house. The mother told them about the neighbour who regularly came to see the baby. The mother was then given an Easter candle to put under the threshold of her house. That way the person who had done the harm would no longer be able to enter. When the neighbour stood at the door a short time later and was invited in, she refused, saying: "No, my leg won't come along." After that the mother once told the neighbour exactly what she thought of her and sent her away for good. From that day on, the baby's health began to improve.
199566: A woman suspected of being a witch had an orchard where fine fruit grew. Whenever her neighbours took her apples or pears at night, the witch knew at once.
199582: A man coming back from the fair heard a coach with two black horses approaching near Orsmaal. People said it was the devil driving around. The man had to jump aside so as not to be run over.
199605: A man who worked on a farm in Goetsenhoven always carried a blue apron under his arm on his way home in the evening. One evening the man was bothered by a big black dog that followed him. Because the man was annoyed by the beast, he struck at the dog's mouth with his blue apron. The next day in church the man saw someone sitting there with blue fibres between his teeth.
199607: Werewolves were pranksters who had disguised themselves in a bearskin. A woman who was attacked by a werewolf threw her handkerchief at the animal's mouth. The next day that woman saw a man who still had the fibres of the handkerchief between his teeth. A werewolf who worked as a farmhand had hidden his bearskin in a hollow willow stump.
199613: A man from Edingen was ill. The doctor could not help him. The man saw all kinds of old and ugly people appear and did not know what was wrong with him. It felt as if he was constantly being beaten, though no one could be seen. The man's wife asked a girl from the village to keep her husband company. The girl went to the Capuchin friars. A woman from the village had seen her walking and had patted her on the shoulder. The girl then ran home, fetched a clog and hit the woman on the head with it. After that incident the girl fell ill. She had fits five or six times a day. The girl then had the friars read prayers over her. She was also given a blessed nail to keep in her pocket. After that the girl was cured. The bewitched man, however, died, even though the friar had gone to bless his house. In the witch's house the friar found all kinds of books, which he burned.
199633: In Huizingen there lived a man who was suspected of being a sorcerer. A few months after the man had died, his children suddenly heard a strange noise. They believed their dead father had returned. In reality a tile had blown off the roof.
199635: A man claimed that a werewolf had jumped onto his shoulders with its front paws.
199655: In Waasmont lived a woman who had special powers. A miller driving his horse and cart past her house suddenly could not go on. The man began to curse and became exhausted. A little later the witch came outside and tapped the horse once. After that the horse went on. After the priest had read over the witch, she lost her magic powers.
199661: A man from Lummen who always went to fetch wet barley in Diest in the evening saw a ghost ploughing by a double hedge. Some time later money was found at that spot. It was all crowns. Since then the ghost has not been seen again.
199669: A maid who worked in Waanrode went to the fair with her boyfriend. On the way home the boy said to the girl: "If you meet a beast, throw this handkerchief into its mouth. I need to relieve myself." A little later the girl saw a big black dog and threw the handkerchief into the animal's mouth. When she got home, the girl saw her boyfriend pulling the pieces of the handkerchief from between his teeth. He was a werewolf.
199672: On a farm in Spieringen (a hamlet of Vollezele) there worked a farmhand who owned a skin with which he played kludde (a werewolf-like spirit). The farmhand had hidden his skin in the oven. One day the farmhand's skin had been burnt, as a result of which he had to play kludde all over again for a whole period.
199687: People who were bewitched went to have a parish priest or a friar read prayers over them. Sick people went to the doctor, but if he could not cure them, they believed they had been struck by the evil hand and went to have the priest read prayers over them.
199703: A man was annoyed by a black dog that always ran against his cooking pot when he wanted to pour the water off his potatoes. One day the man poured the hot water over the animal. Afterwards one of the neighbour women had burns.
199748: Whenever a farmer was churning butter, cats always came and sat by the butter churn. One day the farmer stabbed the cats with a dung fork. The next day the farmer found that his wife had hurt herself and asked: "How did that happen?", to which the woman replied: "You know very well. You did it yourself."
199752: If you saw a little light in the evening, it was believed you were seeing the soul of an unbaptised child. You were not supposed to point at such lights, or else they would come and sit on your finger, so it was believed.
199758: A child from Sterrebeek was bewitched for a long time by a jealous woman.
199764: A young man went to visit his girlfriend, who lived near Herfelingen. His parents always told him: "Make sure your girlfriend's mother doesn't touch you or make a little cross over you, because then you'll be bewitched!" One evening the mother did make a little cross over the boy. The boy went home on 'carrot slices' (?).
199773: On a farm lived a farmhand who was often ridden by the maar (nightmare spirit) at night. When the man woke up, he was drenched in sweat. This man was also often drunk. One night some of his fellow workers decided to play a trick on him by crawling on top of him at night. The next morning too the man claimed he had been ridden by the maar.
199784:
A man had made people afraid of a little white rabbit that always roamed about in Zoutleeuw. Some people believed the rabbit was a witch in animal form.
A woman going to milk the cows with a friend got a fright when a robber suddenly leapt out of the hedge.
199807: A man who worked for a farmer in Breisem was always jumped on the neck on his way home by a werewolf, which made itself carried all the way to Kumtich. The werewolf wore chains and a skin.
199811: You must never accept anything from the hands of a witch. If the witch made a little cross over the object, you would be bewitched. You must also never lend anything to strangers.
199825: On the Plein stood a farm that was haunted. When a tramp came to ask the farmer whether he could spend the night there, the farmer answered: "I have no room. You can't sleep in the bakehouse, because a ghost comes there every night. If you want to sleep there, it is at your own risk". The tramp still wanted to sleep in the bakehouse and asked for a pan and some flour so he could bake pancakes. When the tramp was baking around midnight, a human leg suddenly fell down the chimney. "Go ahead and fall", said the tramp, "but not in my pan". A little later a complete skeleton stood in the bakehouse and said: "Lift up a paving stone there in the corner", to which the tramp replied: "Do it yourself". At every order the skeleton gave, the tramp replied: "Do it yourself". Under the paving stone a pot of money was hidden. After the ghost had counted the money and hidden the pot under the paving stone again, it vanished. When the farmer asked the next morning: "Well, are you still alive?", the tramp answered: "Certainly, and there will be no more haunting in the bakehouse, because I have the ghost in my pocket!"
199842: A man from Hauthem who always walked backwards instead of forwards was said to have been struck by the evil hand. When the man was dead, people cried out that he was walking in the gutter of the church roof.
199845: A man who went round shearing sheep was at the house of a woman who was said to be a witch. Because the man could not manage to shear the sheep there, he cursed and said: "Hurry up and get into the house!" After that the man was able to shear the sheep.
199863: A little boy could make mice by throwing marbles into a little hole. After the priest had been to see the boy, he could no longer make mice.
199870: In Lennik lived a woman whose two children had died. Strangely enough, the children's bodies did not go stiff. Shortly afterwards the husband also fell ill and died. Because the man's body did go stiff, the gravedigger said: "Now it will be over, but if I were you I would still go to Schepdaal. A man lives there who can do something against witchcraft." After the funeral the woman went to Schepdaal. The man came to look at her house and said: "Woman, have your stone well cleaned." When that was done, millions of pins were found in the well.
199873: Will-o'-the-wisps were the little hands of unbaptised children who sat in hollow tree stumps. In the evening they could be seen floating from one tree to another.
199887: A man walking to Zoutleeuw bumped on the way into a person lying on the pavement. Further on the same thing happened again. In the field the man saw something move. In the distance a little woman was walking with a white sheet over her head.
199888: A mother whose child was ill sent for a fortune teller. She said that a neighbour often came to visit and gave the children a piece of sugar. That sugar then turned into a rubber ball.
199893: In Ezemaal there lived witches who could infest people with lice. If a witch could not find a victim, she had to bewitch herself or a family member. Witches always went about with cloths wrapped around their hands or legs. A woman from Laar who had been visiting her child in Ezemaal met a witch on her way home. The next day that woman's child lay dead. The witch was said to have gone to the parish priest of Raatshoven, who read prayers over her and took away her magic power. Witches usually targeted young girls.
199921: One night a witch entered her daughter's house, even though she had no key. The daughter's husband and children were asleep, so they noticed nothing of the witch's visit. The witch pulled her daughter out of bed and dragged her around on the floor. The daughter went to a brother (a monk), who read prayers over her and gave her a medal. The brother also said: "You must be careful and make sure your mother doesn't come in too often." After that the daughter had no more trouble.
199935: In Spieringen (a hamlet of Vollezele), three girls died after they had supposedly been bewitched by their grandmother.
199941: In the marshland a light could be seen at night. That is why hardly anyone dared to go there, except the old fishermen of Veerle, who were used to being confronted with witchcraft and hauntings.
199948: A farmer had planted potatoes in a field next to the field of a witch. The farmer had manured his field well, unlike the witch, who had done nothing. Some time later the farmer had no potatoes. The witch had the finest potatoes imaginable.
199965: A woman who had been visiting a neighbour set off for home late in the evening. In the dark the two women saw someone pass by with a handkerchief over her mouth. The women said "Good day", but the apparition did not answer. The ghost was the woman's godmother, who had died many years before. Frightened to death, the woman called her daughter, but she could not see the apparition. The woman was so afraid that two people had to take her home. From that night on the woman began to pray. She never saw anything strange again.
199967: A young woman went to have prayers read over her child. While this was happening, the old woman who had come with her began to sweat heavily and tremble. Perhaps she was the witch.
199982: People who were ridden by the maar (nightmare spirit) lay crying and calling out in bed at night. An innkeeper from Kaggevinne was also once ridden by the maar. He saw the maar enter the bedroom and called for help to the brother of the woman he thought he saw. But nobody heard the man calling.
199994: Sometimes a notary had the greatest difficulty selling a certain house because it was haunted and because a knocking was heard there at midnight.
200003: In Oudenaken there lived a witch from whom no one dared to accept holy water. If a dog was howling somewhere, people believed the animal was being tormented by the witch. Whenever people had bad luck, they also blamed the witch.
200015: A man coming back from the fair in Steenhuffel saw a calf slide off the roof of a house in the Molenbaan. The man also heard noise, but he walked on as if nothing was the matter.
200018: A man who had sold his soul knew that his girlfriend would walk past the churchyard of Hever around midnight. He warned the girl, saying: "If you see anything in the churchyard, throw this red handkerchief at the apparition." At midnight the girl threw the handkerchief at a ghost in the churchyard. The ghost tore the handkerchief to shreds. A few hours later the girl met her boyfriend. To her great horror she found that he had the threads of the handkerchief between his teeth. She ended the relationship at once.
200020: In Kortrijk there lived a woman who could do witchcraft. Two soldiers from Kortrijk-Dutsel always saw that witch. Those soldiers would not have gone into the witch's house for a thousand francs. A man ate a fried herring at a witch's house. Afterwards the man claimed he had never eaten such a delicious fried herring. The herring was probably bewitched!
200034: A poacher claimed that he had tried for an hour to shoot at a hare and that each time the animal jumped three metres into the air.
200048:
A farm in Nieuwenrode had a lot of misfortune. The children died and something was always wrong with the animals as well. Because the occupants believed their farm had been struck by the evil hand, they went to the friars of Ghent. When the friar came to the farm, he was drenched in sweat. A beggar woman who had been there had touched the children, and so they were bewitched.
In the past, all the children had prayers read over them, after which they had to eat a small blessed roll and make a novena.
200049: An ugly old woman always came to drink coffee at a farm in Meldert. The woman always went over to the child on that farm. Because the mother noticed after a while that the child could no longer walk, she went to the friars of Leuven. The next time the woman came by, she said: "No, I don't have time for coffee today" and went on. But the child still could not walk.
200051: In Herne lived a woman who was suspected of being a sorceress, because whenever she had visited somewhere, something always went wrong. On the north side of many houses was a food store. In this woman's house a brick lay loose in the store. The husband wanted to mortar the brick in place, but his wife did not want that. One day when the wife had gone to the market in Ninove, the husband decided to mortar the brick in. He lifted the brick and saw that a small wax doll lay beneath it, stuck with pins. The man received a box on the ear and saw his wife standing behind him. Every time the man lifted the brick, he was struck and saw his wife. Two weeks later the man died.
200076: A girl was in a relationship with a boy from Rillaar. One day the boy said to the girl: "Now I have to go home for a bit. I'll be back soon, but first I have to go home." When the boy came back, he had fibres of a handkerchief between his teeth. The girl saw this at once and never wanted to see the boy again. That boy could change himself into a dog.
200097: A woman from Grazen, who had gone shopping in Sint-Truiden to run her errands, was suddenly frightened by a white shape when she reached the village of Grazen. The little woman fainted from fear. After a while she was found and taken home. But the woman was lame for the rest of her life. She was convinced she had been bewitched.
200107:
One day a boy was walking with his little sister past the house of a witch. The witch came outside and wanted to look into the pram. But the boy knew what was said about that woman and quickly pulled the sheet over his sister's face.
In reality the woman was not a witch at all.
200140: A friar had to go to Aalst one morning. In a lane he met a giant of a man who seemed to have bad intentions. The friar was afraid but hid his fear and said: "I am a friar of Affligem, and if I say 'Stand still', you can't go on." Then the man stood stock-still. When the friar had passed him, he gave a sign and the man could move again.
200151: In the churchyard little lights were sometimes seen floating above certain graves. People claimed that these lights were the souls of small children.
200157: A woman with a bad reputation claimed that every year she had to destroy a certain number of living hearts. So as not to have to harm people, the woman chose hens as her victims.
200172: In Blanden there lived a woman who baked bread for herself and sometimes for the neighbours too. One day a neighbour with a bad reputation came to ask whether she could come and bake bread. When the loaves were taken out of the oven, only the witch's bread was baked.
200178: People who were ridden by the maar (nightmare spirit) felt someone was lying on them, but they saw nothing. These people could not move.
200190: A farmer's wife owned two or three goats that had given birth. One day a neighbour who was a witch came to visit the farm. The woman poured something into the goats' drinking trough. Two days later the animals were dead.
200197: A wizard made a man from Boortmeerbeek lose his way, so that the man wandered about the whole time and could not get home.
200206: A certain woman came to a farm to bewitch the grain. When the people wanted to make butter the next day, they found nothing but dung in the butter churn.
200214: A man returned after his death because during his life he had promised a pilgrimage to Scherpenheuvel and had never fulfilled that promise. After others had made the pilgrimage in his place, the man was released and did not return again.
200285: A mother who had had her first child was exhausted because her child cried all the time. When the mother went out on an errand, she met a woman with a bad reputation. The woman asked how she was, and the mother answered: "Not well. I'm very weak and my child cries all the time." The woman immediately replied: "I'll get you." When the mother later plumped up the child's pillow, she saw lots of large pins, some four or five centimetres long, fall out of it. The mother believed the woman had brought the evil hand upon her.
200327: By a tall hedge a strange phenomenon appeared that pressed the hedge down.
200336: A woman who lived on a farm in the Schavolliestraat in Oetingen was always afraid when her husband went to the brass band rehearsal and she was home alone. In the hallway she always heard noises as if someone were walking around in clogs. Once when the man stayed at home, he heard the knocking too. Although the shutters were always closed properly in the evening, they were open in the morning. Because that house was haunted, the woman did not want to stay there.
200342: Of a bricklayer who claimed he was always thrown off the verge in Dworp, it was said he had been ridden by the maar (nightmare spirit).
200343: A man had a nightmare about a wild beast. Then the man got up to help his wife pack before she left for the market. When the man went back inside, he heard a cow lowing. He rushed upstairs and saw a cow standing in his room. A witch had caused that apparition.
200344: A woman had a child who could not walk. People believed the child had been bewitched by its grandmother.
200347: One morning a man saw a wizard in the shape of a cat walking past his house. The man took his gun and shot at the animal. People who could turn themselves into an animal always had to keep something on, such as a belt, a watch or a little chain, so they could take their human shape again afterwards.
200352: A man and a woman from Bunsbeek who were going with their wheelbarrow to the fair to sell something were caught in a rain shower in Stokkem. The woman suddenly saw a light, but strangely enough her husband had not seen it.
200355: A poacher saw exceptionally large hares and, strangely enough, did not manage to shoot them. They were ghost animals.
200359: Some people threw stones at a toad sitting in the ditch. The next day the toad was gone. It was a witch in animal shape.
200371: A farmer's wife who had baked bread found the next day that the bread was full of glue and sinews. The witches had caused this.
200374: A boy saw someone make mice during catechism class. The priest came over and had the child make mice again. But it no longer worked.
200376: A mother always saw a strange woman standing at the window of her house. The mother developed painful legs and had to lie in bed for four years. The woman's four daughters went to Scherpenheuvel, where they had prayers read over the bandages their mother wore around her legs. They also donated money so that the influence of the evil hand would disappear. A short time later the mother was cured.
200378: For three Sundays a man had seen a black cat in the lane near the Warandestraat in Humbeek. From his friends he learned he was not the only one who had seen the cat there. One Sunday the man fearlessly walked up to the cat and tried to catch it. But he failed, because the cat suddenly leapt away. A little further on the man saw the cat sitting again. He tried to chase it away, but the cat came up to him fawningly with its tail in the air. The man then changed tactics. He wanted to throw his coat over the cat and take it home. He thought he had caught the cat, but when he felt under his coat he found the animal had vanished. That cat was a witch.
200381: Two men were coming back in the dark from the kermis (village fair) in Bevekom. On the way the men saw a fine inn full of pretty girls. The men went into the inn and asked for a glass of beer. When one of them suddenly had to sneeze, the other said: "God bless you." Then the whole scene vanished with a hellish din, and both men were standing in a bramble bush.
200396: A man who had special powers could conjure up mice.
200402: A woman from Dormaal who lived in Brussels never went to Mass. One day the woman said to her husband: "Let us agree that whoever dies first must come and tell the other whether there really is an afterlife". After her husband had died, the woman heard the wardrobe rattling one night. Then she said: "Yes, all right, now I know that there is something after death".
200411: People who suffered from a nervous disease believed they were bewitched or were being ridden by the mane (nightmare spirit). At the Ankkerselaar in Sint-Pieters-Kapelle lived a woman who dreamed at night that her leg hurt. The next morning that woman walked with a limp. When the woman had dreamed that her arm was injured, she wore a bandage around her arm in the morning. That woman had been ridden by the mane.
200423: One evening a poacher was sitting in the woods with his gun. When he saw a large hare running, he shot at it and said: "You're mine!" Because he had not hit the hare, he fired twice more. Then the hare came running up to him, tapped its paw on a tree stump and said: "What are you doing here, my friend? Off home with you!" That hare was a woman from the village who could turn into an animal because she was a witch.
200424: A farmhand had to take a sow to be covered. The sow walked along well until she reached a witch's house. There the animal suddenly refused to go any further. Five or six times the farmhand tried in vain to drag the pig past the house. Then the witch said: "Go on, try again," and went inside. After that they could get the sow past the house.
200436: When two sisters and a brother had died in Dilbeek, all their possessions were sold. A man who had bought a tub of money found when he got home that the money had turned into beet seed.
200445: A woman selling wool door to door always came to a house where there was a son suffering from a brain disease. Because the doctor could not help the sick boy, his father went to the friars of Dendermonde, who asked: "Does someone come to your house who has given the boy something? That may be the cause." The friars also read prayers over the sick child. After that intervention the peddler woman never visited those people again.
200464: In an inn where people played cards, drank and cursed, a black gentleman came in. One of the drunken card players jumped up and began to dance with the gentleman. When the drunkard had received two slaps from the gentleman, they fetched the priest, who came with holy water. The black gentleman sat growling in a corner. When it became too much for him, the ground split open and he disappeared.
200473: In Attenhoven there lived a woman who could bewitch children. When that woman had stroked a child's head, the child had lice.
200484:
A woman who was said to be a witch often came to visit a house where two children had died. That woman came to help everywhere when a body had to be laid out.
The people went to a witch master in the Kempen, who said: "If the suspected woman comes to visit again, you must not let her in. Whatever you have borrowed, you must throw over the wall. Then you send her a written order stating that she may no longer come in."
200490: Some boys were coming back from the fair in Winge. On a hill one of the boys said: "Would you believe that witch over there is doing this to us?" Two of the boys had had toothache the whole time. When the group walked past the witch's house, she came outside and said: "Your brother had such a big mouth just now. I'll pull his tongue out."
200506: Someone had shot at a cat sitting on the roof. But they had not been able to hit the animal. The next morning a woman was walking around the village with a bandage around her arm. That woman was the witch.
200517: One night a girl began to cry loudly because she had seen someone in her room. The girl was drenched in sweat from fear. Other people, however, could not see the figure in her room.
200528: Some people believed their oak tree was bewitched because there was one branch that did not lose its leaves in autumn. A witch was said to have sat on that branch.
200543: To become a witch, werewolf or vuurman (fire man, a fiery spectre), you had to sit at a crossroads at midnight with a black hen. The devil then appeared in the form of an old man and jumped over the person sitting there. Then the devil said: "How well an old man can still jump!" If you said nothing in reply, the devil had to leave. If you did say something, you made a pact with the devil and then received goods and money every day.
200551: A man from Tollembeek sometimes visited his girlfriend's parents in the evening. The girl was often frightened with stories about Kludde (a shapeshifting spook) with his chain. The girl always wore a red neckerchief on her head. When the girl met Kludde one day, she threw her handkerchief at the apparition. Kludde had to unravel the handkerchief completely before he could touch the girl. When they sat eating the next day, the girl noticed that her boyfriend still had the threads of the handkerchief between his teeth. The boy was thus betrayed and had to start all over again the period he had committed himself to. People earned something by it.
200552: In Plutsingen (Bogaarden) a woman went to the market with a neighbour. The neighbour gave the woman three pears for her three children. When she got home, the woman hung her basket from a beam by the ceiling so the children could not reach the pears. The woman forgot to give her children the pears. When she looked in the basket a while later, she found that the pears had turned into toads.
200557: A girl coming home with her boyfriend during the First World War was hindered by a black cat. The boy kicked at the cat, but the animal kept following the two until they were home. The next day, when the girl was baking bread, she saw a scarf lying on the windowsill. The girl wondered whose scarf it was and put it on the chair where the bread was rising. A little later the girl put the bread in the oven. To her astonishment, the bread would not bake. The girl believed she had been bewitched through the scarf. After she had burned the scarf, the bread baked properly.
200565: Sinners had to come back after their death to haunt.
200569: A crossroads in Bunsbeek was haunted. One night a man drove past that crossroads with his dog cart. At that spot the dog was so frightened that it crept between its master's legs. Past the crossroads the dog behaved normally again.
200574: Whenever an animal was born on a farm, the people always gave buttermilk to an old woman who was said to be a witch. One day they could no longer make butter on that farm, so the farmer decided to go to the friars of Affligem. The friar said to the farmer: "You must no longer give milk away for free, even if you only ask a pin for it. You must also put some holy water in the butter churn." The farmer followed the advice and could make good butter again. When the farmer's wife gave butter away again some time later, the problems started again.
200581: A man went to Lombeek to buy a calf. When the man laid his money on the table, an old woman kept grabbing at the coins. That evening the man saw that his new calf was sweating in the stable. He opened the stable door and saw a black cat running. After the man had said some prayers, the cat disappeared for good.
200597: In Roodebeek there lived a witch with a crooked back and a long nose. One day the children had shouted at the woman: "x is crazy!", after which the woman went to the town hall to file a complaint for slander. The town clerk laughed at the accusation and said: "But you really are mad!" At that the witch grew angry and said: "I'm not mad, but you could still become so. If you aren't yet, you could become so sooner than you expect!" Shortly afterwards the clerk fell ill. He lay in bed with a high fever and was no longer in his right mind. The clerk's family was convinced that the man had been bewitched by the witch.
200598: In Meldert there lived a witch who often visited a farmer's wife. The farmer's wife's husband had been ill for a long time and nobody knew exactly what was wrong with him. Every time the witch came in, the man could see nothing. In the end the man understood that he had been bewitched by this visitor. The witch never came into the house again, but the man died all the same.
200606: In Rotselaar there lived a woman who was said to be a witch. In the house that this woman rented out, there was a hanging rack. When they moved into the house, the tenants had hung from the rack to check whether it was firmly attached. It turned out that it was. When the man and the woman had lived in the house for a while, the rack fell down one day all the same. The tenants therefore believed that the witch had bewitched them.
200610: A girl was in a relationship with a barber. One evening the girl had arranged to meet her boyfriend at a certain place. "You will meet a dog and you must throw your handkerchief at the animal," the boyfriend had said. No sooner said than done. When the girl saw her boyfriend, she noticed that he had the fibres of the handkerchief between his teeth.
200616: A woman whose father-in-law had died always heard footsteps and rattling in the house at night. One day the woman's husband found thirty-five francs on a beam in the house. The man then said: "That is money my father put here. I am going to take this money to the priest and have a Mass said". The priest, however, did not take the man seriously and said that ghosts did not exist. But the nightly noises did not stop. One night the man's mother said: "Something is lying on me here, something is lying on me here. I will do what I promised". After that the strange noises stopped.
200622: A girl sitting on a hay wagon was struck on the head by a woman walking past. The woman said: "What a good child." The next day the girl could no longer speak or walk.
200639: A girl of twelve or thirteen had fallen ill after eating cherries that someone had given her. The girl no longer wanted to eat. The mother took the child to the white fathers in Averbode, who said: "That child is truly bewitched! The only thing you can still do is to stand your child against the wall at midnight with arms spread and feet crossed, the way Our Lord hung on the cross. The girl must then pray three Our Fathers and three Hail Marys." When they did this, two people had to hold the child. They also had to say all the words of the Our Father for her, because the girl no longer knew the prayer. The girl sweated terribly. After she had repeated the ritual for six days, she was cured and could eat again.
200642: In Oorbeek there lived an old woman with a bad reputation. One day this witch came to visit a farmer's wife who had slaughtered a fat sow and put the meat in the meat tub in the cellar. The farmer's wife had just become a mother. So the witch called out: "What have I heard? May I see your baby?" Because the mother did not answer, the witch could not get in. At that the witch said angrily: "I'll get you yet!" The next day the pork in the cellar was rotten.
200643: Some men were playing cards in a café. Another man did not want to join in and kept looking at his watch. At midnight the man grew restless and left. A little later one of the card players went home past the Driesbos. In the wood the man heard a chain rattling. The next moment he was jumped by the werewolf. The man fought the werewolf and managed to hit it on the spot where it had been baptised. The next morning the werewolf was found lying on the ground there. After the priest had come to read prayers over him, he was freed from being a werewolf.
200658: A shopkeeper who was said to be a witch was supposed to have made a child from the neighbourhood ill.
200666: In Bogaarden there lived a woman who was said to be a sorceress. In a family that this woman often visited, a little child was ill. The woman often came to look at the child, and every time she had been there, the child's health got worse. The people were advised to put a nail from the Easter candle under the door. That would stop the woman from coming in. And so it was.
200671: Twelve people were playing cards in a café in Leuven. A man who had lost the game and could not pay his debt cried: "I wish the devil would come in here to pay my debt". A little later a great flame came out of the floor and then disappeared again. The landlady fell to the floor in fright. The man fell forward and died six weeks later. Only that man and the landlady had seen the devil. Where the flame had appeared there was a hole in the wooden floor. Because the hole could never be closed, a zinc plate was laid over it.
200701: A man from Grazen went to fetch leather in Sint-Truiden. In Sint-Truiden he always had a glass of beer with some friends. One day he was playing cards in a café there when one of his friends said: "I wouldn't go home that way, because it's uncanny there. Something could happen". But the man replied: "I'm not afraid. After all, I have my little dog with me". The man set off home, but on the way his little dog was so frightened that it crept between his legs. A few metres further on the man saw a large dog come out of the wheat field and lie down in the middle of the road. Because he was afraid, he ran home quickly. When he went back to the spot the next day, the dog was no longer there.
200717: A woman who had become a mother had been given baby clothes by a neighbour. The neighbour had also come to wash the child a few times. The child, however, turned black and did nothing but cry, so people believed the neighbour was a sorceress. The mother sought advice from a man who told her: "I will undo the witchcraft. That woman will come to look at the child again in a few weeks." At that the child's father said: "I'll shoot her dead when she comes!" But when the father aimed his gun at the neighbour, it would not work. The man pointed his gun at the sky, and then it did work.
200721: In Meise there lived a woman who had a hunchback and had therefore become somewhat shy of people. People called her 'the witch'. When children stood at her door, the woman chased them away. One day a woman carried a sack of feed past the witch's house. At exactly that spot the sack fell to the ground.
200727: At a castle in Neerhespen worked a maid who was not afraid to walk home in the dark in the evening. One evening on her way the maid saw two fiery eyes looking at her from the hedge. It was a werewolf, which jumped onto the maid's back and made itself carried. When she got home the girl was freed of the werewolf. The girl died after her encounter with the werewolf.
200746: In East or West Flanders people thought a dead man had risen from his grave because the gravestone had been pushed up. That was, however, caused by the burrowing of a mole.
200769: A man driving to town with horse and cart suddenly could not go any further. His own wife, who was a witch, had bewitched him fast.
200778: A woman was always being visited by a witch who lived nearby. The witch always came to ask for all sorts of things. One Thursday the witch visited the woman again. That day the woman could not make butter, so the witch said: "But you must have done something, then?" The woman answered: "I could make butter all right if everyone stayed outside!" Together with her family, the woman had to go to confession and communion for a whole year. That freed her from the witchcraft.
200782: A woman whose son had asthma noticed that a cat always walked in the yard at night. The woman believed her son had been bewitched by that cat. In reality, of course, cats come to places where a light is burning.
200790: You could not see sorcerers and sorceresses coming. They made the animals eat something, which made them die.
200798: On the Mutsaardplaats in Strombeek-Bever a little child once died. People believed a sorceress had stabbed the child with pins.
200810: In the past it was the custom to hang butter in the well so it would stay hard. A woman who went to hang the butter in the well at night, because she would leave for the market the next morning around two or four o'clock, saw a black gentleman in a black cloak approaching in the distance. The cloak was blowing about, although there was no wind.
200811: Someone said to a man: "You won't get home today." The man indeed walked past his house and got lost. Only after he had walked in a circle three times did he find his house.
200814: People who had a lot of bad luck believed they were being ridden by the maar (nightmare).
200820: A man from Haacht had promised a pilgrimage for his sick wife. But the woman died and the man forgot the pilgrimage. Because the man was troubled by haunting every night, he went to the parish priest, who asked him whether he had ever promised anything. The man was reminded of his promise by a voice that kept saying: "Fien in front and I will follow." The priest advised the man to make the promised pilgrimage and to say that sentence before he set out. But the man forgot, and he had to carry his dead wife all the way to Scherpenheuvel, so that he was dead tired when he arrived.
200828: Sorceresses could make the butter go bad. They threw dung into the butter churn. They could also make it impossible to make butter at all.
200829: A woman who was going to a farm to do the washing was followed by a little calf. The woman thought the animal had broken out. When the woman reached the farm, the calf had become very big.
200834: In a class the children had told the priest that one of the pupils could make white mice come out of a little heap of earth. After the girl had demonstrated her skill once more at the priest's request, the clergyman read over her. After that she could no longer make mice.
200855: A man always had headaches. One Sunday morning he went with his wife to a healer in Jette. It was not yet eight o'clock, but there were already thirty or forty people in the waiting room. When the healer came to fetch someone from the waiting room, she saw the man sitting there and said: "This man is in great pain." The healer immediately began to overlezen (pray over to lift a curse) the man. The woman spoke with saints and took the evil upon herself. Then the healer said: "You are freed from your pain. But you must keep the gate of your house closed and let no one in. You must also do a penance of nine days. During those nine days a sorceress will come to the farm to ask you for something. You must put a medal under the threshold." A few days later a neighbour came to visit. "Come in," they said to the woman, but she could not get over the threshold. Some time later a rabbit died at their home. The people went back to the healer in Jette to tell her. "It is good that the rabbit died," the healer said to the man's wife. "It could just as well have been your husband who died! From now on you must not give anything away."
200866: Stallichten (will-o'-the-wisps) were the souls of people who wandered about at night.
200899: Children who had been given a sweet or a biscuit by a woman became completely emaciated.
200901: A man saw before him a ghostly apparition that looked like neither a human nor an animal. The apparition did the man no harm.
200947: Werewolves were people who had sold their souls to the devil and who had to wander about with a lantern or a candle to lead people astray. If the werewolves saw a stick somewhere, they ran away. If a werewolf was struck and began to bleed, he had to start his term all over again.
200958: In a house lived people suspected of being sorcerers. An old woman who lived there had put her hand on a girl's shoulders and said: "Did you see that little bird there?" But there was no bird to be seen at all. The girl fell ill with fear. She had been bewitched.
200970: At night a woman saw the statues in her house shaking. Her mother-in-law had brought the kwade hand (the evil hand, a curse) upon her.
200978: Two men going home around midnight saw a white ghost as big as a horse walking by the churchyard. Terrified, the men ran home. The ghost was a dead person who had returned.
200991: The maar (nightmare spirit) came to people at night and gave them a tight feeling around the heart. You could protect yourself against the maar by placing your wooden shoes upside down beside the bed.
200998: A train driver who always came home at around eleven o'clock in the evening had to pass a café whose landlady was suspected of being a witch. Some people always saw a black cat walking near that café. The train driver, however, did not believe in those stories about witchcraft and said to the landlady: "You can bewitch my bare backside!"
201000: Wherever there was an old woman, people often believed she was a sorceress. When a pig was slaughtered, people said: "She's bound to come by today, and then the meat will be rotten!"
201016: A man out with his horse and cart noticed that the horse suddenly stood still. The man saw a barrel rolling through the hedges. Then the horse went on again.
201021:
In Neerlanden lived a woman who had special powers. When people were harvesting on a field in Attenhoven, she bewitched the horse and cart fast to the ground. So they went to call the witch. After she had said a few words, the cart moved.
In Attenhoven nobody was allowed on the field while the mandels (1) were still lying there. One day the witch was on a field where the mandels lay all the same. A farmer said to her: "Hurry home, or the field warden will fine you." The witch said: "I'll be home long before you." And so she was.
201022: Witches were said to have lived in Beert who conjured the cows up into the loft above the stables.
201023:
The Great Bear was called 'de hellewagen' (the hell wagon).
If people had seen the northern lights, they believed disaster would come.
When someone had heard an owl call, someone in the neighbourhood would soon die.
201031: A farmer's son from Houwaart roamed about as a werewolf. While the boy was ploughing in the field, his parents found his skin above the bakehouse when they wanted to heat the oven. The boy's father threw the skin into the oven. The skin had barely caught fire when the farmer's son was standing by the oven crying and shouting. Had he not been held back, he would have jumped into the oven to save his skin. After the skin had burnt up, he was released.
201056: A man who had been sitting for a while with some card players in a café went home. A little later, however, the man came back to the café as pale as a corpse. On the way the man had met his dead father.
201062: Sis K. was a disabled orphan boy who was looked after by the people of Rotselaar. When the boy had died, he was laid in a chest used for transporting bacon. Because Sis K. had believed in neither God nor commandment, he could not be buried in the churchyard. The chest was nailed shut and put in a pit. As soon as that was done, the men ran away saying: "Men, the devils are there, the devils are there!"
201076: A man who went to visit his girlfriend in Oetingen one afternoon was warned by his mother: "You mustn't go there any more, because your girlfriend's mother is a witch!" But the man would not listen and went anyway to the girl he was in love with. The man's friend was seeing the girl's sister, so the two of them went to the girls' house together on Sundays. The girl was always sad when her boyfriend had to leave for home around nine o'clock, and usually she tried to persuade him to stay a little longer. One evening, when the young man wanted to leave, the girl's mother had suddenly disappeared. She had probably gone to bed. On his way home the young man saw a large, deep pool that he could not step over. The man tried to go home by another route but got lost. In the end he found himself back at the door of his girlfriend's house. But there was no one to be seen there any more. The man decided to make another attempt to go home. On the way he met four black gentlemen. Papers kept flying in front of his feet, so that he had the greatest trouble making any progress. Ten minutes later all the obstacles had vanished and the man could go home without trouble. He never visited his girlfriend again.
201086: In de Gijmel (a hamlet of Langdorp) lived a man who could turn himself into a dog. That man's daughter-in-law could not keep a single animal alive; all the lambs and kids fell ill and died. At the end of his life that man could hardly die.
201087: A man walking home in the evening saw to his great fright someone roll down the hill into the meadow. Terrified, the man jumped away and told his mother everything when he got home. When the man went back to the meadow the next morning, all the 'branken' (?) were standing upright again.
201133: People who were ridden by the maar (nightmare spirit) wore medals to break the maar's power.
201135: A man was annoyed by a cat that kept walking around him and struck at the animal with a shovel. The next day the man met a woman who had a wound on her hand. The woman said: "The day before yesterday I cut my hand with the sickle." The man knew better.
201141: A girl was out walking with her boyfriend when the boy suddenly said: "I have to go away for a moment. You go on ahead. If you see a dog, throw a handkerchief at the animal." When the girl saw a dog a little later, she did as she had been advised. Later that evening the boy sat with his girlfriend in the light. There the girl saw that her boyfriend had the threads of the handkerchief between his teeth.
201152: A woman from Geraardsbergen who believed she had been bewitched by her neighbour went to the fathers of Edingen. There the woman was advised not to let the neighbour in anymore.
201178: Between the school and the Ven in Booienhoven there was a black cat that came and sat on people's feet. No one ever managed to catch that cat.
201184: In Woluwe there lived a woman suspected of being a maar (nightmare spirit). When children in a house fell ill after this woman had visited, people said the children had been bewitched by her.
201195: A man sometimes felt something jump on him at night in his sleep. He was being ridden by the maar (nightmare spirit).
201213: A man from Oplinter was courting a girl from Hakendover. When that man was returning from Hakendover on a Sunday night, he was jumped by the werewolf, which made itself carried all the way to Oplinter. Werewolves were often thieves out to rob people of their money.
201228:
In Vissenaken lived a farmhand who always went out at night and only came back in the morning. People knew that between Vissenaken and Kumtich a werewolf roamed about, which jumped on the backs of passers-by and had itself carried.
One day the farmer sent his farmhand away for two days. The farmer found a skin in a hollow tree and burnt it in a glowing oven. When that happened, the farmhand suddenly stood screaming by the oven. As soon as the skin had burnt up, the farmhand fell to his knees and said: "You have released me." The farmhand had sold his soul to the devil.
201250: Someone had died in the V. family on the Molenstraat. The night after the funeral the people were plagued by a strange presence in the cellar and the attic. After a long time the people started digging at the bottom step of the cellar stairs, because that was where they heard the ghost most often. Under the tile they found a pot of money. As soon as the pot was found, the people never saw or heard the ghost again.
201267: On a farm the chains always fell off the cows' necks. A sorceress was the cause.
201269: A farmer's wife whose cow gave no milk went to a friar for advice. The clergyman said to her: "You must milk your cow an hour earlier." When she did so, the animal did give milk. Before, a witch had always come to milk the cow before her.
201294: At the school at 't Goor there was a girl who had special powers without knowing it herself. The girl was the daughter of a witch who had already died. The girl could conjure the street full of frogs and toads. When the priest once saw this, he took the girl's books away. After that the girl could no longer work magic.
201297: In Oppem (Brussegem) a farmer had sold his soul to the devil. In return the devil would build the farmer a barn.
201298: In Plutsingen (1) lived a woman who was said to be a witch. People passing by there often saw a black hen sitting with chicks. People then believed that the witch had taken the shape of a hen.
201309: In Oudenaken there lived old women suspected of being witches. One of these women died of hardening of the arteries in the head.
201310: A witch from Linden went to a farm in Sint-Pieters-Rode to buy eggs. The witch bewitched the farmer's wife and appeared every night in the shape of a cat to the sick woman. In the end the people went to the Poor Clares in Leuven. There they were given a relic to hang above the door. Because of this, no witches could come in any more unless they were explicitly invited.
201319: A man visiting a witch scratched his head, whereupon the witch asked: "Do you have lice?" The man answered "yes", whereupon the witch went on: "Do you want a hundred thousand?" After the man had said "yes" again, his head was full of lice.
201323: Some children were playing on the triangular square next to the church of Gelrode. Suddenly one of the children said: "Watch, because I'm going to make mice." The boy took sand from his pocket, put it on the ground and stood on it with his heel. Then mice crawled out of the sand. The children persuaded the boy to go to the inn that evening to show his magic there. That evening the inn swarmed with mice. No one ever knew exactly how the boy made the mice appear.
201329: Behind the church of Moerbeke a man had come across a little rabbit. He had taken the animal home. The next day the rabbit had turned into a skull. The priest advised the man to take the rabbit back at around the same time and to bring a young child along. Otherwise the man's arms and legs would be broken.
201339: Strange things happened at the Blauwberghof. The animals went wild in the stable. A black glow was seen flying out of the stable and it stuck to the wall. The glow was triangular like a priest's hat. The next day the horse lay dead there. The bones were taken out of the horse meat and thrown into a basket. At a certain moment the bones began to dance in the basket. The priest came to bless the farm and sweated terribly while doing so.
201340: The witches held gatherings at night at a crossroads. During one meeting the witches were overheard by a man standing behind a hedge. The man heard the witches say: "Over hedgerows and verges, woods and fields to Cologne into the wine cellar!" But the man had not understood the magic formula properly and said: "Through hedgerows and verges, woods and fields to Cologne into the wine cellar!" When the man arrived at his destination, his clothes were completely torn. The witches were sitting there drinking at a party. His wife was sitting there too.
201342: In Sint-Kwintens-Lennik lived a devil who had taken the shape of a servant. When the dean took this servant into service, he did his work very well. That is why the parish priest said in his sermon on Sunday: "I am going to Rome to pray a novena so that my servant may be cured." On his way to Rome the priest suddenly saw a horse flying beside him with his servant on it. The two rode as fast as they could to Cologne Cathedral. When they arrived there, the doors were shut and the devil could no longer get out. He is said, however, to have managed to leave the cathedral through the keyhole. That is supposedly why the lock still squeaks today.
201344: Nobody dared to go into the Langstraat in Neerhespen any more because it was haunted.
201350: People who dealt with evil owned special candles with hairpins in them.
201427: In the old days milk was poured into large round tubs. When the milk was poured out of the tub, the skin stayed behind in it. Sometimes the milk curdled at once, even though the tub had been washed. Because people believed an evil hand caused this misfortune, they went to the fathers of Averbode, who advised them to do a novena.
201491: A few men going home around half past eleven saw a white friar standing in a lane. Although the men quickened their pace, the spirit always stayed the same distance ahead of them. At the corner of the Smisbos the spirit suddenly disappeared. A little further on, the ghostly friar had stuck a stick into the ground on the road. When the men went to look the next day, they found that the stick was already completely rusted. All sorts of things were found at that spot. The ghostly friar had had to come and point out that place.
201493:
An eighteen-year-old boy who was out one evening with some friends saw a light. Because his friends claimed it was a will-o'-the-wisp, the boy grew frightened, but he still went into the field to take a closer look. When he got there, the boy found that the light was the reflection of a plough that had been left in the field.
Children who had been buried unbaptised came back to haunt in the form of will-o'-the-wisps.
201496: A woman lying in her bed felt something knocking on her jaws and fainted. When the woman regained consciousness, she found she had wet her bed. When someone was with the woman, she was not troubled by the mare crawling over her. The woman was tormented by the mare for a whole year.
201507: A boy went through the woods with his girlfriend to the fair. On the way the boy said to the girl: "I need to relieve myself. If a dog comes along, throw my handkerchief at the animal's mouth." Further on the girl saw a dog and threw the handkerchief as she had been advised. When the boy rejoined her a little later, she saw that he had the pieces of the handkerchief between his teeth.
201524: One day on a farm two fat pigs lay dead through the work of the kwade hand (the evil hand, a curse).
201527: In Zoutleeuw there was a black cat that the other cats avoided. That cat caused the animals in a stable to be set loose, so that it eventually came to be associated with witchcraft or haunting. One day a farmhand managed to hit the cat on its front legs with his dung hook. After Sunday Mass it could be seen that a woman from the village was wearing a bandage around her arm.
201530: A bricklayer from Nieuwenrode was often visited by peddlers selling needles and pins. The seller always lingered near the bricklayer's children. When one of the bricklayer's sons had died, the man went to the friars of Dendermonde. On the way the man met an enormous dog that lay down in front of him. The bricklayer walked on resolutely. The friars told him he must no longer let a certain man in. They also said there were pins in the children's clothes. Those pins had to be taken out and burned. The bricklayer also received medals from the friar. He was convinced that the big dog had been a wizard who had wanted to stop him.
201535: One evening a woman from Vissenaken had been visiting her son. She had told the boy that he had to lock the house up well. The boy followed the advice and, to be safe, also brought an iron bar into the house. The boy had, however, forgotten to stop up the drainpipe. Suddenly a fat toad came in that way. The boy hit the toad on its legs with a stick. The next day the boy did not get a visit from his mother. After a week the boy went to visit her himself. He found his mother in bed with two broken legs.
201548: In a stable there was a cow that was untied every night, no matter how firmly it had been tied. Those people then went to the friars for advice.
201556: Along the main road in Neerlinter lived a sick woman who could no longer walk. One day the sick woman was visited by a man who laid out bricks and straw to make a fire. When a woman came in a little later, the man said to her: "You must cure this sick little woman, or else I'll put you on the fire." The witch pulled a long darning needle out of the sick woman's neck. After that the sick woman was cured.
201562: A bell was thrown into a pit in 't Kravaal. On Christmas night that bell could always be heard ringing at twelve o'clock.
201575: You were not supposed to point at stalkaarsen (will-o'-the-wisps) or will-o'-the-wisps, because then the light came towards the person who had challenged it. Some claimed these lights were witches who had returned; according to others they were the souls of unbaptised children. Stalkaarsen appeared mainly near the marshes and by the Oude Zenne in Lembeek. Later it was discovered that they were in fact fluorescent vapours.
201581:
In Herfelingen there lived a woman suspected of being a sorceress. She often bewitched the animals when she went to fetch milk at a farm. One day, when a farmer found his two horses lying ill in the stable after the sorceress had fetched milk, he ran to her house and forced her to undo the evil. The sorceress went with him to the stable and said: "But there's nothing wrong with those animals!" The next moment the horses jumped up perfectly healthy.
The sorceress's neighbour girl was covered in lice and fleas every day.
201583: On a farm one of the calves stood by the door completely drenched in sweat. Since the Gospel of Saint John has existed, such hauntings no longer happen.
201585: A man whose pigs were all dying went to a friar, who advised him to look under the door. There the man found a lot of toads. After the toads had been chased away, the evil hand came to an end. For those toads were witches.
201610: On a farm where the animals were always sweating and many animals died, people believed a sorceress had brought the kwade hand (the evil hand, a curse) upon the farm.
201616: A sick man claimed that a woman who had visited him had made him ill. The man was determined not to let the woman in again, but sadly he died of his illness.
201643: A man from Hauthem who always walked backwards instead of forwards was said to be bewitched.
201657: In the wood a ghost always wandered at night, holding a boundary post in its hands and calling: "Post, post, and where to leave it?" It was the ghost of a man who had moved the boundary post of his field.
201658:
A girl always had nightmares in which a neighbour boy who had died in an accident appeared and called: "Come and get me!" The girl even had to see the doctor because the nightmares made her ill. One day a mass was held for the boy. The boy's aunt was also present at the mass. People suspected that the aunt was a witch as well.
Witches could enter a room through the keyhole, just like cigarette smoke. The dead no longer had food or drink, but they still existed in the form of shadows.
201688: In a brothel the madam said: "I can make the devil appear on the table." The devil did indeed appear, and the parish priest had to be sent for to get him out again.
201707: Stalkaarsen (will-o'-the-wisps) were lights seen in the evening in the stable or in the field, which followed people. Some believed stalkaarsen were the souls of people who had come back after their death because they still had something to say. You were not supposed to point at a stalkaars, because then it came closer. To drive a stalkaars away, you had to pray.
201720: A mother had had her first baby. After the mother had gone for a walk with the child one evening and the child had been given a sweet, it got 'de oude man' (the old man, a wasting illness). The child died.
201721: In Geetbets there lived a witch who harmed her own children if she could find no other victim.
201731: One morning the merchants were going to Sint-Truiden when they suddenly heard squeaking in the streets of Wommersom. The streets were full of rats. A witch had caused this. A friar had a woodpile set on fire. The clergyman then prayed there until the drops of sweat rolled down his face. When the rats came running up screaming, the priest said: "The worst one is not here yet. Now I shall have to sweat some more." A little later the old mother rat came running screaming to the fire.
201740: A widow with five children had not received her rightful share of her mother's inheritance because her father had remarried. About her father and her stepmother the widow said: "I do not wish them misfortune, but they will get it." The child of the stepmother and the father died in an accident and the father went mad. The woman died young.
201747: A man coming home along the Mechelsesteenweg suddenly felt oppressed and could no longer find his way, although he knew the place well. After the man had wandered about all night, the oppressive feeling vanished and he got home without trouble. People said that man had been ridden by the maar (nightmare spirit).
201753: In the old days the fathers used to come and collect butter, eggs and clothes from people. The poor people of the Marollen then came to get these goods from the fathers. When a father came to collect food at a house, he saw a crying baby lying in a cradle there and said: "But mother, can't you see that this child has been struck by the kwade hand (the evil hand, a curse)?" The mother was advised to go with her little son to Elingen and have him overlezen (prayed over to lift a curse). The mother did so, and the little priest in Elingen advised her to do a novena. After that the child became healthy again.
201755: Some people often visited a woman who lived in a white farmhouse. There they played a game in the kitchen. At a certain moment the game would suddenly end, and then the rattling of a heavy chain being dragged over the bluestone floor was heard. The people then believed an animal had broken loose, but when they went to look, that turned out not to be the case.
201758: A tailor from Beert heard so much noise at night that he sent for the priest to free his house from witchcraft.
201761: A boy rode his father's bicycle to the market in Ternat. As he set off, he saw a cat that was a good metre tall and had a big head with fiery eyes. A moment later the cat was gone. On the way, to his great fright, the boy was surrounded by thousands of mice.
201777: On a farm all the cows were ill because a witch had touched them. The farmer's wife went to the church of Our Lady to confess and take communion. The old confessor did not believe in witchcraft. Still the farmer's wife stood her ground and stayed sitting in the church after mass had ended. Then a young priest came to her and asked whether she had daughters. The farmer's wife explained that she had one daughter and that she was a very good girl. Then the priest said: "Don't worry, your cows will recover." When the woman got home, all her cows had indeed recovered.
201794: People who were ridden by the mare got lost and kept ending up at the same place.
201797: An old woman sometimes said to the children: "You must be good, or else I'll make mice!" The woman would then throw a handful of sand on the floor, after which a whole pack of mice ran up the stairs.
201811: Some fishermen and poachers from the heath of Veerle often met in a house in Zichem to talk. One of the men said that his wife sometimes suffered so badly from her witchcraft that she jumped up to the roof and swung from one beam to another.
201815: A farmer's wife from Neerlanden could not sleep because she was ridden by the mare at night. Her farmhand advised her to sleep with a knife on her chest, with the blade pointing upwards. The farmer's wife followed this advice and the next morning found the farmhand lying dead on top of her.
201816: Black cats brought bad luck, people believed.
201822: When going to bed, a man from Lembeek placed his shoes with the toes pointing towards the stairs. If he did not, he would be ridden by the mare at night and be unable to move. People who were ridden by the mare perhaps had poor blood circulation.
201829: A man who played Kledde (a werewolf-like spirit) always hid his skin in the oven. When one day people set the skin on fire, the man was released.
201834: In Oud-Heverlee there was a large pit. A little chapel is said to have stood there once. One day a woman passed by and cried: "Ronk, ronk, ronk, I wish this little chapel sonk." The next moment the chapel disappeared into the ground.
201845: In a house where washing had been left hanging outside one night, a child was struck by the kwade hand (the evil hand, a curse). The people went to the fathers of Dendermonde and to Zwijndrecht, but in the end their child died anyway.
201850: A woman had given birth to a son in a hospital in Leuven. The child was wrapped in a white neckerchief. When they walked with the child to the Brusselsestraat, they met an old woman, who went up to the young mother and said: "May I see that baby? What a lovely child!" Despite her sister's reserved attitude, the mother showed her baby to the woman. When the mother's sister wanted to go to sleep that evening, she saw a bat flying under her bed. She would not go to sleep until the bat had been chased away. Her father and her husband came to look, but they did not see the bat. The woman did see it. What is more, every evening she saw the witch come to the child's cradle. Her mother advised her to pray a novena and to go to Florival. For nine consecutive days the woman prayed nine Our Fathers and nine Hail Marys. Her mother prayed a novena too. Then the woman went to Florival by bus. After that she no longer saw the bat.
201888: To become a sorcerer or sorceress, you had to stand at a crossroads at night with a black hen under your arm. You would then see the devil appear in the shape of someone with a deformed foot, to whom you could sell your soul.
201899: People who believed they were ill although they were not said they had been ridden by the mare. Such people were afraid of everyone.
201916:
People troubled by witchcraft or haunting had themselves overlezen (prayed over to lift a curse) by the Friars Minor of Leuven.
Bewitched cows were pulled up to the ceiling.
201923: A man fired his revolver several times at a dog that was jumping up at him. But he could not hit the dog. So he believed the dog was a witch in animal form.
201928: A dying man was visited by priests carrying crucifixes. Because the man was bewitched, a black cat was brought to his bed to lift the spell.
201941: Around Meldert there used to live many witches who could turn themselves into animals to torment people. One day a witch in the shape of a rat was wounded somewhere. Witches could steal the cream from milk. If a witch met someone with a cow, she would say: "What a beautiful cow!" and stroke the animal's udder. The next day the cow gave water instead of milk. By looking in through the windows of farms, witches could also make people grow crooked.
201975: People who had been ridden by the mare got lost on their way home.
201979: A woman's face had swollen after a sorceress patted her on the shoulder. Only after the woman had been to the monastery of Affligem did her face heal.
201986: A house in the Sint-Annastraat was haunted. Sometimes the plates could be seen dancing on the table there.
202004: Witches could sometimes appear in the shape of a cat, a dog or a sinister person.
202007: A farmer who had no barn to store his harvest in was walking sadly through the field, where he met a finely dressed gentleman and told him his problem. The gentleman said to the farmer: "You will have a fine barn within one day if you give me your best pledge." The farmer agreed. The barn had to be finished before the rooster first crowed in the morning. When the farmer lay in bed that evening, he told his wife what he had done.
