In the night the farmer's wife got up and clapped her hands, so that the rooster began to crow too early. At that moment the devils stopped working. There was still a hole of four or five metres in the barn. That hole could never be closed. The barn still stands today. It is the kwade schuur (evil barn) in Bierbeek.
202041: A man from Heverlee had sold his soul to the devil in exchange for a new barn that had to be finished the next morning. A whole crowd of devils worked on the barn, but in the morning there was still a hole in the building.
202045:
A woman had three children. One of them looked very pale and did not grow. At midday the woman had great difficulty getting this child to sleep. One day a relative advised her to go to the monastery of Affligem. The father of Affligem laid the child on the table and said: "I think your child has 'de oude man' (the old man, a wasting illness). A neighbour is responsible for this evil. You must keep that woman out of your house. Within three days something will happen that will frighten you. The neighbour will come to ask for something that is at your house." The woman went home. On Monday she did the washing. During the night from Monday to Tuesday the woman and her husband were woken by a violent wind. The woman's mother got up and found in the garden a shirt hung on the washing line only by its sleeves. There was no way to get the shirt off the line. When the woman saw the shirt hanging there the next morning, she was terrified. A little later the neighbour came by to ask for the shirt back: "The wind blew it over here," she said. But the shirt could not have been washed, because the folds were still in it. One day the mother visited the neighbour to find out how she was bewitching her grandchild. The mother saw a black cat in the house, where the neighbour sat with a wax doll in her hand. The neighbour stuck pins into the doll, which made the child hurt and unable to sleep. Nine days after they had taken the child to the father, the child grew plumper. On the eighth day, however, the witch had tried to get into the house once more. Because a blessed candle and a medal had been put under the threshold, she failed. The witch wanted the mother to come to her because she had to ask her something. People believed the witch wanted to transfer the spell from the child to the mother.
One night the mother felt the weight of the witch on top of her. Only when the mother began to pray did the witch leave. She could be heard going down the stairs.
When the grandmother felt the witch on top of her one night and fell ill from it, she had recognised the witch's face. They went to the father to tell him who was responsible for the evil. The clergyman answered: "You must be careful for another nine days. On the ninth day the witch will come to ask how you are. You must not look her in the eyes then." They followed the father's advice. After that the grandmother recovered. The witch had probably gained power over the grandmother by getting hold of one of her hairs. In the end the witch came to ask those people for forgiveness, but she did not get it.
One day the witch had come by. The woman, who had seen her coming, quickly made the sign of the cross, so the witch could not get in. "What have you come for?" the woman had asked, and the witch had answered: "You know very well."
Witches were jealous and greedy people. They could make any food they wanted appear on the table. The witch never went to the village church. She may well have gone to the big church.
202059: A man who was married to a sorceress experienced strange things whenever his wife was away. The man would then try to make coffee, but he could not, because the water would not boil. Yet the man was very fond of coffee.
202076:
One evening a young man was called to a farm where a cow was about to calve. He was advised to make the sign of the cross with holy water before leaving, because the woman who lived on the farm was suspected of being a witch. But the young man brushed the advice aside, saying: "She can bewitch me for a drink." When the calf was born, the men got a clear drink and the young man got a red one.
When he got home and had to tell how it had gone, he said: "Well, if you're a handsome fellow, you count for nothing, because I got a red drink while the others got a clear one." "Then she's got you," they answered.
The next day the young man indeed could no longer walk. He was advised to have prayers read over him, but since he was not very religious, he did not. He then went to a spiritist in Liège, who asked: "What should I take away, the illness or the pain?" "The pain," the young man answered. After the spiritist had rubbed him for a while, the young man had no more pain. He was also given a bottle of water and only had to pay half a franc for it. He was also advised to go to confession and communion in Schoonderbuken the following Saturday. When the young man came back to his work at the brick kilns, the witch was there asking where he had been. This witch was no shrivelled old woman but a beautiful figure. The spiritist had urged the young man to be very careful on the ninth day. That night, as the workers at the brick kilns lay in their wooden huts, they heard a cat scratching on the roof. The young man got up and chased the cat outside. The cat jumped into the nettles and vanished. The young man's mother also saw a white figure, but his father did not.
One day the young man had stuck a rake into his leg. The witch advised him to wash the bleeding wound well. Then she laid a little cross of straw on the wound and said: "I'll help you get rid of that." The woman muttered a few unintelligible words. Then the young man went back to work in the mud. His wound did not become infected.
The following winter the young man had to do a job somewhere. Because the door of the workshop was locked, he wanted to break in another way. As he stood there, he saw the witch standing there with the key in her hand. A year later the witch was there again. The young man said to himself: "Now I'll run her over. I'll crush her under my wagon." But the witch had left, and she was never seen again.
202085: On a farm no butter could be made. Moreover, the animals there were always sick. Because the people suspected a certain woman of being responsible for the misfortune, they went to the white friars. After that they had no more misfortune.
202094: A man coming back from rehearsal saw a strange apparition leap out of an elder bush in a lane.
202096: People who had bad luck believed they had been ridden by the mare.
202101: A farmer whose horse was sick went to fetch a wizard. The wizard rode back with the farmer on horseback. On the way the farmer suddenly could not go forward because the wizard had fixed him to the ground by magic. At a certain moment the wizard said: "Come along", and then the farmer could move again.
202117: Some men met a cat on their way home. One of the men ran away in fear because the cat was much bigger than normal. One of the men ran off, stumbled into the ditch and drowned. Afterwards people believed that the cat was a witch who had turned herself into an animal.
202128: A man who worked in the duke's stables fell victim to the mare. The mare was so heavy that he sweated like a horse and could not move. Those who were ridden by the mare sometimes had their blood stand still. If you placed your clogs with the toes pointing away from the bed, you were protected against the mare. You could also protect yourself by putting a colander over your face.
202140: Those who were ridden by the mare at night lay stiff as a board in bed, drenched in sweat, and could not utter a word. Since the Gospel of Saint John came into existence, people were no longer ridden by the mare.
202146: Three men said to one another: "If there were more people here, we could play cards!" A little later a fourth man appeared, who joined in the card game. But when one of the men bent down to pick up a dropped card, he saw that the fourth man had a long tail. It was the devil. Because he had been asked there, he would not leave again.
202153: Drunkards who got lost believed they had been ridden by the mare.
202155: Two old women lived in an old cottage in Dormaal. One of those women could make mice by throwing a clump of earth on the ground.
202167: On a farm in Oetingen all the animals died. When the people also fell ill, the friars of Edingen were sent for to read prayers over the stables and the people. After that the misfortune came to an end. Three people died in that house. Sorcerers and sorceresses also often held gatherings.
202175: A mother lying in childbed had been visited by a woman who gave her a little bonnet for the baby. Six weeks later the mother put the bonnet on the child to go for a walk. The next morning the child lay crying. It had a large swelling on its head. Because the doctor did not know what to do, the mother became convinced that the child was bewitched and went to the friars. A friar came to the house to read prayers over everything. When the friar came to the place where the bonnet lay, drops of sweat rolled down his face. Afterwards the mother burned the bonnet, after which the child became calm and recovered. The mother hung a medal above the front door, which she had received from the friar to protect herself against the evil. From that day on, the woman who had visited after the birth never again walked on the pavement by the house, but always on the other side of the street. The mother was convinced that this visitor had bewitched her child.
202183: At the Kapellehoek (corner of the Kaarlijkstraat and the Diepestraat) in Meise, the devils came to hold their revels. At one point someone came there with a large crucifix, and all the devils ran away. The next day the stench of the devils could still be smelled there.
202200: A woman got up at night because she heard a strange noise. By the mayor's house the woman saw a strange figure. The woman immediately thought to herself: "That must be the ghost of my mother, to whom I promised a mass long ago." In the morning the woman went with her money to the priest and told him what she had seen. The next night, however, the figure appeared again. It was probably the white lady, who came to tease people.
202203: On a farm where they had a few horses, the people went to the monastery. There they were told that one of the horses had been struck by an evil hand. After that the horse's condition improved.
202226: In Sint-Kwintens-Lennik lived a sorceress whom everyone feared. That woman had the habit of giving everyone sweets.
202228: The mill of Morette, which stood between Asse and Ternat, is said to have been built with grain flour by a freemason at the end of the eighteenth century, in times of famine.
202235: In Aarschot lived a gaunt woman who was suspected of being a witch. When the children went to her house to sing for the New Year, they did not accept the biscuits they were given there.
202255: In the Beertstraat in Beert stood a house that was haunted. Every night noise was heard there. After the priest had read prayers over the house, there was no more noise. The priest did fall ill afterwards, though.
202259: A man who had moved a boundary post kept hearing a voice calling: "Post moved, post moved!" The man could not bear it any longer and put the boundary post back in its original place.
202260: A hunter who wanted to shoot a hare accidentally hit his little dog, although he had not fired in that direction at all. A little later an old woman appeared and said: "You've shot your little dog, I suppose?" That woman was probably a witch.
202272: A girl had been bewitched after a visitor came to the house to fetch flour. The girl then died, but two hours later the child came back to life.
202297: A woman had forgotten that she had promised to have a mass said for her dead father. When she kept hearing three bangs on the door at midnight, she went to the parish priest to have the forgotten mass said after all. After that the woman no longer heard the knocking.
202301: In Tienen lived a witch who owned evil books. Sometimes this witch appeared to her family or to other people in the shape of a white cat. The witch's niece had abscesses everywhere. The friars advised that woman to go on pilgrimage to Scherpenheuvel. There she was told she had to take a bath in red cabbage juice.
202309: Witches could make people lose their way. Men who had to go and fetch the midwife especially got lost in this way.
202319: In Galmaarden a girl was born who was healthy and grew quickly. Once, when the girl was staying in her uncle and aunt's shoe shop, a woman came to visit and said: "May I see that little child?" But after that woman had seen the child, there was nothing but misfortune. The child stopped growing and cried all the time.
202329: An old woman whom everyone distrusted often came to visit people. She went mainly to people who had just had a child or whose cow was about to calve. Every time that woman had visited, something went wrong; the child fell ill or the cow calved too early. When people laid out holy objects, the woman could no longer get in anywhere. From that moment the woman had trouble with her own children and animals. After all, she always had to do evil.
202332:
An unmarried mother from Boutersem regularly came begging at the house of a rich farmer. One day the farmer decided to play a trick on her and gave her a slice of bread with dung. But the beggar woman took revenge and bewitched the farmer, so that he fell ill. The farmer could no longer speak when he walked forwards, only when he walked backwards. When the farmer went to Tienen on foot, he sometimes could not go on. He then had to stand still for a while until he could continue. Sometimes the farmer had an epileptic fit in the field. When that happened, he lay down by the ditch and drank a whole bucket of water. People then tried to pull the man upright with three horses, but they could not. The farmer then went to the Dominican church in Tienen, where a friar took away the evil and advised him not to go to a dance hall or a wedding party for a year and six weeks. The friar also said: "When you get home, an old woman will be standing at your door. You must give her a coin." The old woman was the unmarried beggar.
When there was a fair in Hauthem some time later, the farmer was asked to come dancing. The man answered: "No, I may not dance. My time is not yet up." But the farmer let himself be persuaded and went dancing. Halfway through the first dance the farmer fell ill again.
202382: To keep witches from coming in, people placed a holy object under the threshold. If such a holy object was placed under a witch's chair, the witch could no longer get up. A woman who had been given a bread roll by a witch had immediately thrown it into the fire. The next moment a toad crawled out of the roll.
202398: A man whose child was bewitched had been advised by people not to let a certain woman near his child's cradle anymore. When the sorceress came in again and went straight to the cradle, the man said: "Now you must undo this, or else I'll burn you here." The man made a fire, whereupon the sorceress took a cushion out of her pocket. She pulled pins out of the cushion and threw them into the fire. The child, however, was already dead.
202400: Two friends had agreed that whoever died first would come and tell the other what things were like in the afterlife. When one of the boys had died, the other saw the ghost of his dead friend appear one night with the words: "Here everything is reckoned strictly and little is forgiven. But please do not act any more as we did". Then the ghost vanished.
202414: People who could not sleep were said to have been ridden by the mare.
202466: Two men were mowing the last of the harvest. One of the men said the work had to be finished that day, but the other replied: "That won't happen." The man who was determined to keep working struck a black cat with his blade a little later. Shortly afterwards there were a good three or four hundred black cats in the field, so the two had to go home.
202480: In the Langewei along the Nieuwstraat in Herfelingen little lights were sometimes seen dancing. These were the little souls of unbaptised children. If you pointed at such a light, it came and sat on your finger.
202495: On a farm in Kumtich lived a man who sometimes walked backwards and wrote on the ground with his foot what his farmhands had to do that day. The man had a meadow with hay in Hoxem. When he was tired, he sometimes went to sleep in the hay. Five horses could then not get the man off the hay. When the man helped a cow calve, he sometimes stuck to the animal. The man was bewitched. Once he had prayers read over him, but it did not help.
202502: In Budingen there was a house where a girl had been murdered. The girl's body was never found. From then on everything in the house began to rattle at midnight. Nobody dared to live in the house any more because it was so badly haunted.
202521: A woman worked as a maid for a family in Oplinter where a child had just been born. Because the child cried all the time, the parish priest was sent for, and he said to the maid: "You must take that off the child." After that the child no longer cried.
202531: In the past it was sometimes said that a toad was a witch in animal shape.
202558: Some people were often visited by a woman from Humbeek who had gone to fetch coal. Because of this those people always had misfortune. The friars of Dendermonde gave them a medal to put under the threshold. After that the woman never visited again.
202561: A man sometimes stood stock-still because the sorceresses were sitting on him.
202579: In a house where there was a sick child, a holy object from Tongerlo was placed under the door. When the witch came to visit, she could not get over the holy object. The man of the house took a stick and hit the witch on the head. The next day a woman from the village wore a bandage around her head.
202584: Will-o'-the-wisps were the little souls of unbaptised children. If you could make the sign of the cross over the light with a wet hand, it was saved.
202611: On a farm in Werchter many animals died. The people went to the friars of Leuven, who advised them to scatter blessed rose petals between the stones of the stable. After that the misfortune came to an end.
202641: A girl married the son of a witch. When the girl lay in childbed, her husband ran to the doctor as fast as he could. But he made no headway, and so his wife died. The man's mother had caused this.
202655: Once every three months a man began to cry and moan in his bed. When his sister called him by his name three times, he was released. If the man was asked the next day what had happened, he said: "The mare has squeezed my throat again!"
202689: A German shepherd was manuring the field together with a farmhand. The shepherd said to the farmhand: "Sit down." At first the farmhand refused because there was still so much work, but in the end he sat down. A little later the whole field was manured without anyone having picked up a manure fork.
202697: A witch could leave her body while she lay in bed. In this way the witch's soul could take the form of a whistling bird. A woman and her husband were tormented by her mother-in-law. That woman turned herself into a bird, which woke them at night. The witch also made snoring sounds come from the cupboard at night. At night people also heard footsteps on the stairs, though no one could be seen. The man and the woman were tormented by the witch for twenty-seven years.
202701: Stalkaarsen (will-o'-the-wisps) were the souls of unbaptised children who lived in marshes such as in Stillebreek. If you dared to point at a stalkaars, the light came and sat on your finger.
202747: If you saw a black cat in the evening, people believed it was a witch who had changed into the shape of a cat.
202758: When a prankster walked behind someone with a sheet over his head, people believed a dead person had risen in the churchyard.
202768: Sorceresses were always out to torment people. They had sweets to give to children. When the children accepted the sweets, they were struck by evil.
202775: In the past young people sometimes went dancing. They would then come home alone at various hours of the night. Once, on her way home near the church, a girl from Grimde was followed by a black beast that looked like a dog with a chain. The beast rubbed against the girl's skirt and ran after her. When the girl came home terrified, her mother said that she had had a certain local witch behind her. That witch had already brought misfortune to many people in Grimde.
202800: People who played crazy tricks were said to have been ridden by the 'moer' (mare).
202805: A farmer had sold his soul to the devil, in return for which the devil would build him a barn in a single night, to be finished at the first cockcrow the next morning. The farmer's wife got up in the night and began to make noise, so that the rooster began to crow too early and the devils had to flee. At that moment there was still a hole in the barn, and it could never be closed.
202817: A man was always visited by a woman who came to borrow something. Strange things happened in the man's house at night. The furniture flew around, and in the stables there was nothing but misfortune. A friar from Sint-Truiden came to read prayers over the place, but he said: "In a way she is stronger than I am (?)." One night, when the haunting in the house was bad again, the man shot at a white figure with his gun. In doing so the man shot off his own hand.
202819: In Rummen, at half past twelve at night, a wagon with five horses appeared and drove into a meadow. The next day the wagon could no longer be seen.
202865: A girl had found a ribbon on the road close to a witch's house. The girl had tied the ribbon in her hair. When the girl came home, the ribbon could not be taken out of her hair, so it had to be cut out.
202895: Two women had gone to the bicycle repairer to fetch a torch. On the way back they met someone who was said to be a witch. The witch said: "Will you take my milk jug along?" The women did not dare refuse, although they were afraid. At half past eleven the torch suddenly went out. The women were convinced that they were bewitched.
202904: A shopkeeper had a one-year-old child that could already walk well. After the child had once been picked up by a visitor, it suddenly could no longer walk. The mother went with the child to the friars of Affligem. But when she drove up the hill in her car, she could not get to the top. The woman then had her child prayed over by the white friars of Ghent. The clergymen said: "The evil is surely caused by the sorceress who lives across the street. If you hammer an Easter nail under your door, that sorceress will no longer come in." The mother followed the advice. After that the sorceress could no longer get into her shop. The child recovered.
202917: It was said of a lady who had died of leukaemia that she had been bewitched by a woman from the neighbourhood.
202920: In a house the children began to cry every night at the same time because of witchcraft.
202937: A woman who had been visiting her parents on a Sunday suddenly got a slap in the face as she stepped over a ditch. The friend accompanying the woman had felt nothing. A little further on the woman saw an owl flying above her head, which followed her until she was home. When the woman got home, she found that there were still clothes hanging on the washing line. But she would not have brought those clothes in that evening for a thousand francs (1).
202943: Near a farm in Attenhoven lived a woman suspected of being a witch. On that farm the horses were always being untied. One day a pot of potatoes for the pigs stood on the stove. Suddenly the pot flew up to the ceiling, then fell back onto the stove a moment later. People believed the witch was responsible for these torments. They were also convinced that the witch could turn herself into a cat. When the farm caught fire one day, the farmer and his wife fled outside. Suddenly the wife called to her husband: "The cat is still inside!" The farmer went back in to rescue the cat. When he came out, the cat scratched him. The farmer was so angry that he threw the cat back into the fire. The farmer and his wife then went to Liège, where they were told that a woman from the neighbourhood was responsible for the evil. That woman would come by to ask for a pair of sheets. They were to give her the sheets, and then the misfortune would end.
202957: A man who was ridden by the mare at night had met a witch during the day. At night the man always saw the witch again.
202964: On a farm in the Molenstraat in Nieuwenrode the farmer, his wife and the children all died within three weeks. People believed that a sorceress had caused it.
202988: A man who had won a race was addressed by a witch with the words: "You rode well!" As she said this, the witch patted the man on the leg. After that the man fell ill. Only after the witch had come to the man and patted his leg again did he get well.
202998:
The count's hunting dog had bitten a farmer's black cat to death. The farmer was very angry and threatened revenge. The count gave the farmer another cat as compensation. That cat, however, often ran away because it did not like being with the farmer. The cat happened to be ill when the vet was making his rounds. The vet advised the farmer to bury the cat or to throw the animal into the Maalbeek with a stone around its neck.
The count shot the cat. After that, however, he had much misfortune. Several of his animals died and people said he had been struck by the evil hand.
203003: A witch knew in advance that her granddaughter would fall ill on the day of her Solemn Communion.
203004: At the Oude Molen in the Geraardsbergsestraat and at the smithy in the Brikstraat in Sint-Pieters-Kapelle, foals always appeared in the evening. The farmhands were afraid when they came near there. In reality the apparitions were probably caused by a joker who wanted to frighten others.
203019: A sorceress changed herself into a black cat and in that shape went snooping around the houses. When the cat came into the stable, the animals were bewitched. Once the cat had also bewitched a child lying in its cradle. The child stopped growing and lay motionless in the cradle. The people went on pilgrimage to Affligem several times, but the child's condition did not improve. The priest of Onze-Lieve-Vrouw-Tielt came to read prayers over the house. When a cat came in, the grandfather grabbed the animal and threw it into the stove. The next day a woman with burns was walking around the village.
203033: Two girls coming back from the fair in Drieslinter saw a well in a meadow in Helen in the evening. Suddenly, to their great fright, the girls saw a nun walking beside them. Terrified, the girls ran home.
203045: The miller who lived at the Heimolen in Langdorp could fling open his front door with his cap from over by the mill. One night the miller was coming back from the fair with some friends. A gentleman in fine black clothes was standing by the road. The miller said to his friends: "You go on ahead. I have to have a word with that gentleman. Whatever you hear, just keep walking." The miller had never told anyone that he had sold his soul to the devil. A little later the friends heard shouting and raging in the woods. It was the devil claiming the miller's soul. The miller survived the fight, but he was badly beaten up.
203049: A widow who lived alone with her children heard her dead husband put down his spade in the attic every evening. After the priest, at the request of one of the children, had blessed the attic, the dead man was no longer heard.
203063: One night a man who was ridden by the mare saw the trapdoor open. A woman the man knew crawled in. She climbed onto the man and grabbed him by the throat, shouting: "Oh yes, going around telling all sorts of things about me! I'll teach you a lesson!"
203065: Kludde (a shape-shifting goblin) was always at the Doornstruik on the road from Eerdegem to Wieze-Royen. A man walking home one Sunday evening saw a calf. The man went up to the calf and tried to catch it, but his hands grasped at thin air.
203071: At a house where someone was ill, a crow always came to sit in the tree. When someone shot at the crow, the bird vanished and suddenly a woman was standing there.
203091: A man from Overijse was coming back from the fair in Maleizen with some friends. On the way the man said he would stay behind for a moment because he needed the toilet. Further on the friends saw a monster approaching with a white sheet over its head. The friends threw a handkerchief at the monster, which vanished the next moment. When the man rejoined the group a while later, he still had the fibres of the handkerchief between his teeth.
203101: After the priest had met a man, he felt in his pocket and found spurrey seed there. Then the priest said to the man: "Do that again", but the man could no longer do it. The priest fixed the man to the ground by magic.
203110: People believed that will-o'-the-wisps were the souls of unbaptised children. In reality the lights were caused by gases rising from stagnant water.
203111: Cats used to come to a meadow in Dormaal. One day an officer went up to the cats and chopped off one of the animals' paws. Afterwards it was found that a woman from the village had lost her hand.
203142: In Ternat a ghost wandered about, calling all the time: "One too few and two is too many. Posts moved! Posts moved!" One evening a drunkard answered: "You should have left them where they stood!" After that the ghost never appeared again.
203143: In the old days the old people believed there were witches who stuck pins into children's clothes.
203159: In the past there were people who were seized in their beds at night and almost strangled. Such people believed they were being ridden by the mare or had fallen victim to a witch.
203162: Some farmers from Flobecq saw a burning open coach flying through the sky, which flew over a house where a mill stood. The inhabitants of that house all died.
203166: After sunset one was not allowed to go out with a pram, because that was dangerous. A woman who did so anyway met a black cat by the station and said: "Go on, filthy beast, get out of here or I'll run you over". But the cat followed the woman all the way.
203172: Will-o'-the-wisps were the little souls of unbaptised children who came back to haunt.
203178: Will-o'-the-wisps or stalkaarsen (will-o'-the-wisps) were glow-worms that were seen mainly near woods. People believed these lights were the little souls of unbaptised children. When you saw a stalkaars, you had to say: "I baptise you alone". If you said: "I baptise you", thousands of will-o'-the-wisps came rushing up. In the Vijverstad, by the copse on the Degelaenstraat, there were many will-o'-the-wisps.
203183: In the past people sometimes told of people who were ridden by the mare.
203185: A girl had fallen ill after seeing a black cat on her way back from the fair in Nieuwrode. Perhaps the girl fell ill from the fright she had suffered. A witch from the neighbourhood could turn herself into a black cat.
203190: Witches had to kill twelve living beings a year. Some witches kept a hen with twelve chicks especially for this, so that they would not have to harm people.
203217: When people had a lot of misfortune with their children or in their house, they often blamed an old woman who had visited them and held the child. A friar from Teralfen had come to Vollezele to read prayers over a bewitched child. The child flew into every corner and died young.
203222: People believed that will-o'-the-wisps were haunting dead. In reality they were simply flammable gases rising from rotten ground.
203233: A mother went to the friars of Dendermonde because her child cried all the time and she had also seen a woman sticking pins into a doll. The friars said to the woman: "Shall we show you in a mirror who is to blame?", but the woman answered: "No, because I already know." The friars then said: "Well, then it will be over now."
203262: A butcher went to look in a cave next to a farm and was scratched in the face there by a black cat. The next day the butcher said to the farmer: "Where were you yesterday? If you do that again, I'll split your face in two with my axe."
203287: A farmer who had to bring in his harvest needed a barn quickly. So he sold his soul to the devil, who promised to build him a barn in one night. The barn had to be finished before the first cockcrow. When the rooster crowed for the first time in the morning, the barn was not yet finished; there was still a hole in the wall. Because of this the man got to keep his soul.
203291: Some people walking past a field met a black lady who was a good deal taller than they were. The black lady walked past them in silence. When the people turned around a moment later, they found that the black apparition had vanished.
203328: People who were always ill said they had been ridden by the mare.
203336:
In the past there were many sorceresses. A girl who was out with her mother saw beautiful apples hanging along the way. The mother said: "Look at those beautiful apples! But don't touch them!"
A sorceress who lived in Pepingen could open any lock with her fingers. That sorceress lay dying for months. One day she had her brother-in-law summoned to her deathbed. Because that man would not come, her sisters were brought to her. Then the sorceress died. But she suffered a great deal, because nobody had wanted to take over her magic power.
203344: A witch had a daughter who was married and had four children. When the daughter died and her husband remarried, the witch did not like it. One morning the man's second wife went to the stable, where she found that one of the heifers was shivering and completely drenched in sweat. The people sent for a friar. When the clergyman entered the stable, it was as if he had been struck by a hammer. After he had come to his senses, he went in again and read prayers over the stable. He advised the people to sell the heifer and to close off the entrance on the side of the witch's house. The evil probably came from there.
203362: Fons V.W. had resolved to go on pilgrimage to Scherpenheuvel. But the man died before he could keep his promise. At night knocking was heard and the doors flew open. When people went to Scherpenheuvel for Fons, they had to carry the ghost the whole way. To prevent that, they should have set a stick by the door with the words: "Go on ahead, I will follow."
203368: People who left their washing hanging outside at night could fall victim to witches. When a girl had died somewhere, for example, a woman said: "That happened because you left your washing hanging outside at night."
203381: A witch who was peeling potatoes said to a visitor: "Go on, you peel some" and gave the knife to that woman. With the first potato the woman peeled, she cut her finger. She died of the wound.
203393: If you saw a magpie or a crow in the morning, you could expect bad luck.
203394: A man from Blanden was always ridden by the mare at night. He had already been to the friars, but they had not been able to help him. An old woman advised him to unmask the mare by holding a knife on his chest with the point upwards. In this way the man found out that the mare was his own wife.
203395: A boy was in a relationship with a girl from Rumsdorp. When the boy went to the fair with his girlfriend, he said to the girl: "If you meet a werewolf between midnight and one o'clock, you must throw this handkerchief at its mouth." When the girl saw her boyfriend come into the fair tent after one o'clock, she noticed that he had the fibres of the handkerchief between his teeth.
203428: In a house in Halle where people had been bewitched, the Norbertine canons had said: "Watch the spiders carefully. A witch can change herself into a spider and crawl under the door in that form." One evening the man of the house saw a huge spider crawling in under the door. The man stood ready with a knife and cut two legs off the spider. The next morning they met a man in the village who said that his wife was lying in bed because both her hands had been cut off. The man went to visit the woman and asked: "What is the matter with you?", to which the woman replied: "You did that!"
203440: People who had been ridden by the mare were bewitched.
203448: A farmer had bricked up money somewhere. After his death, however, his money could not be found, and so the farmer came back to haunt. Nobody dared to make contact with the dead man. Eventually a letter was found describing where the money was. The money was intended for good works and therefore could not remain unfound.
203451: In the village lived a woman who was suspected of being a witch. One day a man struck at a toad sitting by the door. The next day the witch was limping.
203466: Stallichten (will-o'-the-wisps) were the souls of unbaptised children who came to ask for something to be done. If you dared to point at a stallicht, it came and sat on the tip of your finger.
203467:
A shopkeeper had given birth to a child. Shortly afterwards a woman came to visit who wanted to see the shopkeeper's child. The child turned out to be intersex and had to have an operation.
That witch could also, for example, get people in her power by giving them a piece of chocolate.
203479: A man coming back from the pub met his dead brother on the way. "Come on, jump over the ditch!", said the dead man. When the man had jumped over the ditch, his brother had turned into a large black dog. The man had to fight the dog until he got home.
203489: A woman who was working had taken off her wedding ring and put it in a flowerpot. The woman was visited by a witch who stayed to chat with her for a while. After the witch left, the wedding ring had disappeared. Moreover, two of that woman's children died.
203507: In de Kluis there lived a farmer who worked in the marshes. After his death the farmer came back to haunt in the shape of Pleudde, a tormenting spirit that dragged chains around.
203528: Lowieke saw his dead wife appear at night. The woman came to haunt because her husband used to beat her all the time. Lowieke jumped up and asked: "Rozalien, Rozalien, what are you doing now?"
203538: Some people in Moorsel were keeping watch over a dead person. Suddenly the sheet moved and a voice was heard saying: "I have been dead for a hundred years and my body is still lying here!"
203550: In a house where someone lay dying, a knocking could be heard.
203559: People who had a bad dream were ridden by the mare.
203565: People who had had a nasty dream believed they had been ridden by the mare.
203582: In Vissenaken lived a man who was a werewolf. At night that man always sat on a road to Bunsbeek to jump on passers-by and make them carry him. A farmhand who was confronted with the werewolf bit his fingernails off from fear and became very ill.
203590: In the churchyard of Peizegem someone had seen a cross move. People came from far away to look at the strange apparition.
203608: A woman told the parish priest that she always dreamed about her dead mother. The cleric said: "If you dream about your mother again, you must ask her what she wants." In this way the woman learned that her mother wanted a pilgrimage to Scherpenheuvel. All her life the woman went to Scherpenheuvel every year. Since then she has not dreamed about her mother again.
203613: In Walsbets lived a witch who was out every night and bewitched many people. People whose farm was bewitched went to a clergyman, who advised them to look through a wedding ring. Then the people would see who was responsible for the evil. When they did so, they saw the face of that woman from Walsbets.
203621: Children who had died unbaptised had to roam about as will-o'-the-wisps that led people astray.
203651: A. had agreed with her friend S. that whoever died first would come after death to tell where she was. Some time later S. died of tuberculosis. When A. was home alone one evening, she heard all kinds of noises as if rats were running through the room. The next night A.'s room suddenly grew light. The girl saw a coffin with her dead friend S. on it. S. said: "You're not afraid, are you, A.? Oh, I didn't think I would ever get there, it was such a long way! But I'll come back again, you know". The long way S. spoke of was purgatory. When S. told the priest what she had experienced, the clergyman grew very angry and said: "You must not say such things! Go to Our Lady in Scherpenheuvel tomorrow and ask that Stineke not come back". A. did what the priest had told her. S. never came back.
203657: Every night at twelve o'clock a girl dreamed of her uncle, whom she had never known. The man came to ask whether the girl would go to Scherpenheuvel for him. He had already been to all his relatives, but nobody wanted to do it. The girl went on pilgrimage for the dead man together with another uncle.
203661: If people saw a black cat run across their path, they could not go any further.
203671: A girl was courting a boy from Hoxem. That boy owned an animal skin in which he went about as a werewolf. When the girl had been out shopping and came home late, she told her parents that she had been jumped by the werewolf on the way and had had to carry him.
203677: A mother from Wezemaal went for a walk with her baby. The mother met an old woman wearing a neckerchief, who was said to be a witch. The witch asked the mother if she could see the baby. The witch stroked the child's head three or four times and then said: "Now put it back." The next day the child was so ill that people feared it would die. The doctor examined the child but could not make a diagnosis.
203680: In the past the Gospel of Saint John was read at the end of Mass. If the priest had left his missal open after the Mass, the witches could not leave the church.
203685: Will-o'-the-wisps were the souls of unbaptised children and of people who had hanged themselves, such as Jakke.
203730: When a calf was born on a farm, all the people from the neighbourhood came to look. Sometimes, however, there was a witch among the visitors. If that witch had stroked the calf and spoken a formula, the animal suddenly fell ill.
203731: A woman from Meldert believed she had been bewitched by a witch.
203743: A woman went to a pendulum diviner with her daughter, who was always ill. The diviner swung a ring as a pendulum. If the ring turned in a certain direction, the person in question was possessed by the evil hand. The diviner concluded: "I can't help you, because it is the evil hand. Go to the friar." The girl had the friar read prayers over her. Afterwards she had to wear a medal and make a novena. If one placed a holy object under one's threshold, no witches could come in. The girl's mother had hung a small cross by her door that was barely visible. When a neighbour came to visit, she said: "Ah, you have a little cross hanging here too!" That neighbour was a witch.
203752: In a house in Tremelo there was bacon in the cellar. A witch who knew this bewitched the bacon so that it was full of maggots.
203757: When people saw a miaowing cat somewhere in the evening, they believed the cat was saying their name.
203775: A farmer from Bierbeek had sold his soul to the devil in exchange for a new barn that had to be finished before the first cockcrow the next morning. In the morning the farmer got up and clapped his hands, so that the rooster began to crow too early and the devils had to flee. At that moment there was still a hole in the barn. That barn was called 'the blue barn'.
203781: A man who lost his mind and sometimes went out in his shirt and barefoot was said to have been ridden by the mare.
203789: In Walshoutem lived a man who could work magic. He had learned his magic from gypsies. When a horse-drawn coach came by, the wizard made sure the horses could not move forward. Because the man then got a sound beating, he never dared use his magic again.
203815: A priest who went out in the evenings to give drama lessons always heard a strange croaking when he left his house. Other people, however, did not hear the croaking. One evening the priest began to pray outside. Then he sprinkled the area around his house with holy water. After that the croaking stopped. The priest thought that the frog might well have been a returned spirit.
203830: In the past some people believed it brought bad luck to prepare certain things in advance. When a baby was expected, for example, the cradle was not to be set up beforehand.
203847: A schoolboy threw something up into the air, after which the whole school was full of mice. The priest of Wijer took away the boy's magic power.
203852: On a farm in Bost a girl had been struck by the evil hand. The girl wasted away, so the priest had to be called. The clergyman said: "While I am reading prayers over her, the person responsible for the evil will walk past." They looked outside and saw a peculiar woman from the village walking past.
203857: In Lebbeke there stood a devil's barn that a wicked man and a wicked woman had had the devil build. "You won't get the barn finished," the man and the woman kept saying, and so it was. Every time the hole had been bricked up, it was open again the next day. In Brussegem there was also such a devil's barn.
203881: A poacher saw some hares playing in the woods. The poacher fired, but his gun did not work. Only after the man had put a paasnagel (an Easter nail, a blessed nail) in his gun could he hit a hare.
203892: In Tildonk a dead child came back. When people went on a pilgrimage for the child, they saw a stallichtje (will-o'-the-wisp) ahead of them on the way. When they arrived in Scherpenheuvel, the light had disappeared.
203907: A man who was walking from Oudegem to Mespelare at night heard beautiful music. He walked towards where the music came from and arrived at a fine hall. The man went in and saw beautiful ladies and gentlemen in elegant clothes. When the man was given a cup, he said: "May God reward you." The next moment the whole scene had vanished and the man was sitting in the grass with his cup. He saw that the name of a woman from Dendermonde was written on the cup. When the man brought the cup to that woman, she said: "Never make this known. I won't have anything more to do with it." The man never betrayed the woman.
203911: A woman had several daughters and two sons. Both sons were disabled; one walked on crutches and the other had deformed hands, so he was unable to work. The sons themselves said that their mother was a maar (a nightmare witch), who worked her magic on her own children when she could not find strangers as victims. Both sons died young, so people believed the woman had bewitched her sons to death. The witch was very proud of her daughters.
203936: One day on a farm the cows had all been hung up. The maid went to tell the farmer, but when he came to look, everything in the stable was normal again. One night the maid, who slept in the washhouse, heard the stove making noise and its plates banging up and down. The farmer then also slept in the washhouse once, but then nothing strange happened.
203953: At night people were often ridden by the mare. If they had placed their clogs upside down beside their bed, they stayed protected against the mare.
203957: In Kraainem several people were bewitched after borrowing something from a witch. Through witchcraft their children or animals fell ill.
203961: A man worked for a woman in Zonhoven. One day the woman gave him four waffles: one for him, one for his wife, one for his daughter and one for his son. The man did not trust it and wanted to take no risks, because his daughter was pregnant. The next day he dug a hole in the ground and sprinkled salt in it in the shape of a cross. He laid the waffles in the hole and then covered them with a cross of salt. The man threw earth on the waffles and said three times: "Go back." Some time later the woman he worked for phoned him; she had been ill for a whole week and had already had to call the doctor twice.
203971: In a house in Sint-Martens-Lennik a witch came in through the chimney. The occupants had the friars of Affligem come to read prayers over the house. The people also believed the witch had bewitched their children.
203985: On a farm where an old maid worked, the farmer's only daughter had fallen ill. The farmer sent for the friars of Dendermonde, who searched the whole farm. When they had seen nearly everything, the farmer said: "That's nothing. That's just an empty pigsty." But the friars stood firm and insisted that the farmer open the sty. The old maid was sitting in the pigsty. The farmer's daughter could no longer be saved, because the evil had already gained too much power.
203998: Sorceresses could make people unable to go on. The houses of sorceresses were marked with special signs so that people would know to be careful there.
204007: People who were ridden by the 'maan' (mare) felt someone sitting on their back. They got lost and could not get home.
204015: Two women from Sint-Pieters-Rode went to help their neighbours bring in the harvest. One morning the two saw a woman with a stick standing in front of the farm. As the women came closer, the apparition grew smaller until it finally vanished. When the hired woman had to go and feed the pigs, the strange figure rose up out of the ground again and struck her down. She died of fright.
204021: In Nieuwrode lived a woman suspected of making people ill and die through the black hand. In the past, however, many people suffered from tuberculosis. When someone visited a house where the germs lingered, that person often fell ill himself. He then believed he had been struck by the evil hand.
204027: If a witch found no other victim, she had to do harm to herself. At a witch's house in Boortmeerbeek a little dog died. Then the people bought a big dog, but that animal died too. Next they bought a small horse. The horse died as well.
204028: A stalkaars (will-o'-the-wisp) was a light seen in the marshes. Some people claimed they were the souls of unbaptised children. According to others they were little worms.
204030: When people had bad luck with their cows because they did not feed the animals enough, they believed the cows had been ridden by the mare. That was something to do with witchcraft.
204054: Stalkaarsen (will-o'-the-wisps) were a kind of shell that gave off light in the evening. Some people believed stalkaarsen were the souls of unbaptised children.
204093: In Meldert there lived a witch who could fill a house with mice when she walked past it.
204097: A man who was ridden by the mare at night was too afraid to sleep and too afraid to get up. He lay on his side and felt as if he was being grabbed by the neck. The man said to the mare: "I am lying on my side, so you can't do much to me. But I know who you are, because I've had trouble with you before." The man always crossed his socks to prevent the mare from coming to him.
204121: The sexton always went to play cards at the priest's. On his way home, between two hedges, the sexton was followed by a big black dog rattling a chain. One day the sexton took a stick with him and threw it at the dog, so that the animal bled. The next moment the sexton saw a farmer he knew well standing before him. The farmer said: "But what have you done! I only had two more weeks to go and now I have to start all over again!"
204129: A woman from Booienhoven claimed that her house was haunted. Sometimes the woman could no longer get her door open. The woman had often seen an old man who seemed to put something into her door. When that man rang the bell one day, the woman had to go out by the back door. When she reached the man, she said: "I have to come round the back, because I can't get my door open any more." To which the man answered: "Well, then we'll certainly have to undo that." The next day the door of the woman's house opened again.
204141: One evening four people were playing cards in a house in Averbode. Around twelve o'clock one of the players left for midnight mass. But the other men said: "We'll play on, even if the devil has to join in." A little later a man appeared who was willing to join the game. Strangely, no one had seen the man come in. But when one of the players bent down to pick up a dropped card, he saw that the stranger had horse's legs. They quickly fetched the priest, who began to pray and tried to drive the devil away. Then the devil said: "I'll leave the way I came," and he vanished up the chimney.
204147: A woman who was milking her cow one evening saw a black toad sitting in the stable. The woman threw the toad into the stove, but the animal escaped up the chimney. Afterwards a woman from the neighbourhood had a face that was completely black with soot.
204166: A man always encountered a werewolf when he came back from visiting his girlfriend. The werewolf leaned over a barrier. The priest advised the man to take a knife and stab the werewolf in the middle of its head so that it bled. The man did as he was advised. After that he was rid of the werewolf.
204174: A man was coming back from the market with his dog cart. In Waver (a district of Moorsel) the dogs began to growl fearsomely. This went on for a good hour, until the man realised he had been driving in circles all along. Later he heard people say that a woman in a white hood had been sitting beside him. Strangely, the man himself had not seen that woman.
204186: People who were ridden by the mare had a nasty dream. When they woke up, their muscles were still stiff.
204197: A three-year-old child still looked like a newborn. People believed the child had been bewitched by its grandmother. The child eventually died.
204203: The castle of Roi and the castle on the Kratenberg were connected by a passage. In the past many feasts and drinking orgies were held in the castle of Roi. The castle on the Kratenberg sank into the surrounding ponds. Later, bells could be heard ringing there on Christmas night. Every night ghost coaches drove from the castle of Roi to the Kratenberg. In the coach sat four ghosts who could not agree about an inheritance and therefore kept calling out: "Whose share is that? Whose share is that?" A man who wanted to help went to the ghosts at night and said: "Come this way. I'll divide the money." Shortly afterwards the man fell ill and died.
204208: Some people claimed that toads were witches.
204228: Stallichten (will-o'-the-wisps) were the little souls of unbaptised children.
204229: A man who had made a bet had to go and pick up a bone in the churchyard. When the man did so, he heard a voice saying: "My little bone! My little bone!" The man died of fright.
204235: A pruner coming back from a castle in the evening took a shortcut through the cornfield. As the man walked there, the corn opened in front of him and closed again behind him. Yet there was nothing and no one to be seen or heard.
204239: In a family's house in Edingen the dog kept howling all the time. When the animal died after a while, they sent for the friar to exorcise the house. Because the friar found that one of the rooms was locked, he said to the people: "You are hiding something from me! What is it?" After a while the people said: "Yes, we are keeping something quiet. In that room a priest's old maid hanged herself".
204257:
A man who lived on the heath always had bad luck.
On the 31st of the month one must never go to Rillaar at night, because then the witches gathered around the church. The witches did not come there in the flesh; their souls had left their bodies. The witches had a golden coach and they danced in a ring.
204296:
A farmer's wife whose goat had died took two hundred and fifty francs to buy a new goat. On the way she and her neighbour went into a house in Dorenhout where four women were sitting. One of the women said: "You'd better buy a lamb. X has four lambs." Another woman kept shaking her head the whole time as a sign that she should not buy a lamb. The farmer's wife decided to buy a lamb anyway and went to X's house. There were three sheep there, one of which was due to lamb on Sunday. The farmer's wife wanted to buy that sheep. It cost five hundred francs, however. If X got the wool back afterwards, the price was only four hundred francs. The farmer's wife did not have enough money with her, but her neighbour was willing to lend it. When she came home with the sheep, her husband said: "You went to buy a goat and now you come home with a sheep! And you bought that sheep from a sorceress too!" A man who had bought potatoes from that sorceress found on arriving in Brussels that the potatoes had all gone rotten. Another woman had bought a goat from the sorceress. The animal had given a lot of milk when the sorceress milked it, but when the woman came home with it, it gave hardly any milk. A man who had stayed with the sorceress was ridden by the maar (a nightmare witch) there every night. The sorceress had also once made a girl ill, who fortunately could still be saved by the Witheren (Norbertine canons) of Ghent.
A cattle dealer came to the farmer and his wife and wanted to buy one of the lambs as soon as they were born. On Sunday morning two lambs were born. The animals frolicked about and the sheep's udder was very full. The cattle dealer came to collect his lamb. But when the farmer's wife wanted to milk the sheep, not a drop came out of the udder. They called the vet, who with the farmer's help tied the sheep's four legs together and then stabbed the udder with an awl. Then the vet said: "You must get this sheep out of your stable and bury the two lambs."
The sheep grew thinner every day, although it ate a lot. The sheep was put down and buried.
When the sorceress came to collect the wool and the sheep's chain, the farmer's wife shouted: "You filthy stinking sorceress! What am I to do now? Should I beat you to death?" The sorceress fell to her knees, began to cry and said: "You may come and take another sheep." But the farmer's wife replied: "I want nothing more from you. You've already ruined half of Meldert!" Before she left, the sorceress said: "Now I will do you no more harm."
Two days later the farmer's wife's daughter gave birth to a healthy son.
That sorceress had been married three times and she made all three of her husbands fall ill and die.
204301: A woman walking along the Stationsstraat to the shop suddenly got a blow on the back of her head. Behind her stood a woman known to be a witch. When the startled woman got angry, the witch spat on her. When she got home, the woman found that she was completely covered in lice and spiders.
204310: Meen was supposed to go on pilgrimage for Treeske's mother. But Meen died before she could fulfil her promise. After her death Meen came to haunt Treeske's mother at 't Zwart Water. Stones were always being thrown around the house. Later the ghost was banished to the cream separator on the Vinkeberg.
204311: In Steenhuffel lived a woman who was said to be a sorceress. That sorceress grabbed children roughly, after which they cried for as long as three weeks.
204317: A man out with his horse saw a woman with a bad name standing in the doorway of her house. Because of this, the man's horse would not go any further. Only when the witch came closer and said: "Come, little fellow, come," did the horse move again.
204338: At the Blauwberghoeve the farmer one night saw a bowler hat floating around in his house. When the man said: "If you are of God, speak. If you are of the devil, be gone," the hat exploded with a bang and disappeared. The farmer's son, who lived a little way off, fell out of his bed. The priest came to read prayers over the place until he was drenched in sweat. He bound the sorcery on that farm for ninety-nine years.
204359: A farmer's wife had bought a pregnant goat from a woman in the neighbourhood. The goat grew fatter and fatter and her udder swelled right up. The animal never had young, but she gave as much milk as a goat that had just given birth. The woman from whom the farmer's wife had bought the goat was suspected of being a sorceress.
204363: In the past children were told they must not accept anything from an old woman. People were afraid the children would be bewitched.
204383: A man from Londerzeel had to go to Steenhuffel for a betrothal. When the man came to a haunted castle, his horse suddenly refused to go on. By the horse's legs lay an arm. In the castle the man heard laughter. The man was taken across the moat on a farm cart and could then continue.
204417:
A house in the Kerselarenstraat was haunted. The woman who lived there was flung out of her bed. The sheets flew around and rats walked through the hallway. The pillows on the beds swelled up. The buckets were sometimes suddenly full of dung and the windows flew open. Sometimes a violent thunderstorm would also suddenly break out. The friars came to read prayers over the house and predicted that the culprit would come by on Sunday at a certain time. 
In the end the people moved to another street.
204430: A man who had been to the market in Brussels with a woman found on the way back that his horse stood still at the house of a woman who was a sorceress. The man had to go and fetch another horse to pull the cart.
204432: In the past, when people had bad luck, they believed they were bewitched. On a farm where two cows had died, people went to the Dominicans in Leuven. One of the friars said: "The person who comes to fetch buttermilk every week is the guilty one." Indeed a neighbour came to those people every morning to fetch buttermilk.
204436: When an animal fell ill on a farm, the misfortune was blamed on a person who had visited. In one house butter could not be churned as long as a certain woman was sitting there. As soon as she had left, they had butter at once.
204446: Two bewitched children were advised by the friars to burn their pillows. In one child's pillow there was a crown, and in the other pillow a palm. The crown was not yet closed, but later both children died nonetheless.
204447: A man could turn a half cent into a Napoleon. He went to eat with his friends at a hotel, where he paid with that Napoleon. The change was for the waiter. Once the wizard had left the hotel, the gold Napoleon turned back into a half cent. That man could also walk over water with his friends.
204459: A cattle dealer drove his horse cart along the Diestersteenweg to go and sell a calf. In the old days those dealers often treated the farmers, because that way they could get more money for their animals. When the cattle dealer came home in the evening with a kilo of salt he had to bring back for his wife, he suddenly saw a goat standing in the middle of the road. The goat leapt up at the man, and he struck the animal on the head with the bag of salt because he believed it was a witch. That is how the man lost his salt.
204493: A man who saw a witch emerge from behind a little chapel fell to the ground in fright and broke his leg.
204515: Some people who had to go milking the cows early in the morning saw, to their great fright, a headless horse pass by.
204532: A white cat always came into a certain house. One Sunday, when the cat was sitting on the oven again, someone threw a dung fork at the animal. The cat ran off, however, and the dung fork stuck in a beam. Afterwards they had the greatest trouble pulling the dung fork out of the beam.
204538: People who had been ridden by the mare lay stiff as a board in their beds.
204540: A man was married to a girl from Halle who lived with her brother because her parents had died. Shortly after the wedding the girl's brother died. At night the man heard his brother-in-law walking on the stairs. One day a gentleman came by and asked to use the toilet. When the gentleman came back, he said: "Listen, strange things happen here. But from today nothing strange will happen any more". And so it was.
204563: By R.'s farm stood chestnut trees that were a good three hundred years old. At All Saints' all the children were allowed to gather chestnuts there. It was said that the old lord came to haunt that chestnut tree.
204569:
In Overwinden lived an old woman everyone was afraid of. A farmer who saw the woman coming quickly said to his wife: "Shut the gate, she's there!" But the farmer's wife did not dare shut the gate in the woman's face and let her in anyway. The next day the farmer had a fever of over forty degrees. The man believed he had been bewitched by the woman.
If that woman had touched the animals in a stable, the animals were ill the next day.
At the end of her life the woman lived in a stable with a stove in it. She sat there among her own excrement and slept on four planks. At her funeral her body was pulled into the grave with a hook. That woman was a witch.
204583: A wizard always sat drinking in an inn in Hoegaarden. One day the wizard was taken home by a man from Diest. That man should then normally have been home in five minutes, but the wizard made him wander about all night. At dawn the man lay unconscious in a ditch in front of his house.
204597: A twelve-year-old girl went to catechism class in Sint-Marte (1). One day the priest noticed that the children were having great fun because one of the girls could make mice by throwing earth on the floor. The priest took the girl aside and read out a text, which the girl had to repeat. After that, to her great regret, the girl could no longer make mice. Children who had special powers had not been baptised properly.
204616: In Sterrebeek people had spoken ill of the priest. It had even gone so far that the priest, with his maid and his sister, had had to leave the village. That day the priest's sister cursed Sterrebeek. Shortly afterwards a certain farm in Sterrebeek had much misfortune. Many children and cows died and the farmer became a real drunkard.
204633: If you wanted to know whether an old woman is a witch, you had to walk in her footsteps. A witch would then look back.
204643: People who had bad luck believed they had been ridden by the mare.
204664: A woman claimed to have seen a ghost one evening. She did not know exactly what the ghost looked like.
204669: A man had got lost at the Duivelsborre after a black cat had walked around him. The man believed the cat had bewitched him.
204682: The béguinage was haunted. Shadows of rats were always seen on the walls there, although no light fell in. There were also two slats (?) of black metal. Furthermore, strange cats and birds without feathers appeared. One of the béguines suggested praying, but a certain woman did not want to. The béguine who did pray sprinkled everything with holy water. One day she saw a banana tree standing behind the woman who refused to pray. That woman did not see it herself. Swallows had built a nest behind the metal slats.
204720: At the Mot in Orsmaal-Gussenhoven stood a house that was haunted. The woman who lived there sought advice from the Heilig Paterke (Holy Little Father). The priest told her: "You needn't be afraid. The haunting can do you no harm". After that the woman was no longer afraid. A man who had been playing cards heard, on his way home near the haunted house, a deafening noise that seemed to pursue him as far as the water. Then a splash was heard. The next morning there was a black cat in the hay loft, although there had never been a black cat there before.
204728:
Witches could cause foals or chickens to lie dead in their pens one morning for no apparent reason. When people had put chickens in a wicker basket to sell them, they often tied a crucifix to the basket to protect the animals from witchcraft. Unfortunately this often did not help.
Because stables were poorly ventilated, cows often fell ill from ammonia fumes. If an unknown woman in a black skirt and neckerchief happened to have visited, people believed she was a witch who had bewitched the cows.
In the twentieth century many people could read and write. As people became more sensible, they believed much less in witches.
204729: At night a little candle could sometimes be seen burning in a tree stump. That was the hand of a child that had been wrongly baptised, so people said.
204736: A man had bought a calf on the Zavelberg in Oetingen. He took the animal home in a wheelbarrow. At the Hellenbos he met a woman who rubbed the animal's back and said: "Ah, you have a lovely calf in your wheelbarrow!" When the man got home with the calf, the animal was ill. The man went to the friars of Affligem, where a clergyman told him: "Just go home, your calf will get better." And so it did.
204746: A miserly woman hid all her money in kettles and buckets. The woman died in poverty and there was no money to pay for the funeral. After her death the villagers saw an apparition in the field every night. It was the dead woman, digging under a cherry tree. The dead woman dug up the kettle with the money and set it on the grass without saying a word. When the woman's widower woke the next morning, he found silver coins in the kettle and a note saying that his wife had returned to give the money needed for her funeral.
204757: In a house people saw the paintings on the wall begin to dance.
204760: When people could not make butter, they believed they were bewitched. Also when they had black wheat, people blamed it on witchcraft.
204769: If you met a werewolf, you had to throw a handkerchief at the animal's mouth. The werewolf then had to unravel that handkerchief completely.
204786: A man returning at night from Loksbergen, where he had gone to sit up with the sick B., met three nuns in 't Kaubos. The next day it turned out that not a single nun had left the convent of Loksbergen that night.
204816: In the past, people whose livestock had died through witchcraft often went to pray with the brown friars of Dendermonde. When those friars came to read prayers over the farm, a rustling was often heard in the chimney. An unknown woman came into an inn and said to the innkeeper's wife: "I know where your son is! He's gone to the friars of Dendermonde!"
204849: A farmer from Bertem had made a pact with the devil, who would build him a new barn if he sold his soul. The barn would be built during the night and had to be finished before the rooster first crowed in the morning. In the middle of the night the farmer's wife got up to wake the hens, so that the rooster began to crow early and the devils, furious, had to abandon their unfinished work. There was still a hole in the barn that could never be closed afterwards.
204865: A man who had gone somewhere in winter to slaughter a pig was pestered on his way home by a meowing cat that kept getting under his feet. When the man struck at the cat with his knife, he heard a bang as if a cannonball had been fired and saw fire coming out of the cobblestones. The next moment the cat had vanished.
204890: A three-year-old girl who sometimes still lay in her cradle began crying at a certain point. Because the child would not stop crying, several doctors were consulted, but in vain. Finally the girl had prayers read over her by the brown friars in Sint-Truiden. The friar predicted: "The guilty one will come to ask for something, but you must not refuse her. After that she will not come by again." Shortly afterwards a woman came asking for a bucket of water. They gave her the water and never saw her again. The child recovered.
204914: When animals died in a stable, people believed the stable had been struck by the evil hand.
204928: Two boys who had made a bet had to spend the night at the castle of the Warande. Suddenly the boys saw a lit coach with two or three horses approaching. The coachman gave the two boys a lash with his whip.
204935: A woman who slept in a little attic room was always ridden by the maar (nightmare). Her son had misunderstood and thought his mother was being ridden by the 'maan' (moon). When one evening the moon shone on the boy's bed, he moved his bed. When his mother asked why he did that, the boy answered: "If I don't, I'll surely be ridden by the moon!"
204954: A Christian family had taken on a poor woman as a maid. Once when the family was not at home, the maid bewitched the cow so that the animal could no longer be caught. The priest came and read prayers over the maid for hours until she fell ill and had to lie down. Then they made her promise she would do nothing more. After that she was dismissed.
204960: A woman went to the church in Oetingen. Some people had placed a blessed candle by the door, so that the woman could not leave the church. Only when the candle was taken away did the witch get out of the church.
204966: A farmer had much misfortune in his stable after a neighbour had visited. After the friars of Affligem had read prayers over the stable, the trouble came to an end.
204984: In a bewitched house there was constant misfortune. The children's heads had even been turned back to front. The brown friars banished the witchcraft there for ninety-nine years, after which everything became normal again.
205036: A farmer's wife going to fetch her cows from the meadow met a woman. The farmer's wife suddenly fell and remained disabled for the rest of her life.
205042: On some farms the animals in the stable were always untied in a strange way, even though they had been tied up securely.
205107: In a haunted house in Molenstede fireballs flew around and the lid of the stove flew off.
205124: A man had been given a bag of sweets for his children by a woman. Because he did not trust her, he threw the sweets over the churchyard wall. He wanted to prevent his children from being bewitched.
205137: A man from Groenenberg (Vlezenbeek) had many problems. The newborn calves died. Some cows gave no milk, and the milk of the other animals stank when it was only a day old. Nor could they manage to churn butter. The farmer went to the friars of Affligem, who said: "You will have more problems, but here is a blessed candle that you must put under the threshold. The guilty one will then be unable to come in." The farmer must not borrow anything from a certain woman, or else she would have power over him. At night the man heard his potatoes rolling back and forth in the attic. He took his double-barrelled gun and went upstairs, but there was nothing to be seen. The next day the farmer could churn butter. An hour later, however, the butter had spoiled. When the sorceress came to return a borrowed oven peel, she cursed at the farmer. After that the farmer never had problems again.
205145: In Grimbergen lived an old woman who was said to be a sorceress. In the past, old women who went looking for four-leaf clovers were often suspected of witchcraft. A man who had piglets saw a sorceress pass by. The sorceress looked at the animals with a strange gaze. A few days later the piglets got a skin disease. The piglets then had prayers read over them by a friar.
205147: A woman making a pilgrimage to Wange on behalf of her sister met a little old woman on the way, who said: "Look what a lovely bunch of flowers I have. Come and smell!" After the woman had smelled the flowers, her nose swelled up. Bad books were also said to have been found in the old woman's house. That old woman's daughter was ill for a long time. People therefore said the old woman had had to bewitch her own child for lack of another victim.
205182: In the old days, when people saw a black cat, they believed it was a witch or a sorcerer.
205209: Somewhere the devils built a barn in a single night. Because there was still a hole in the barn that could not be closed, a small chapel was placed in it.
205238: A black cat brought bad luck, people believed. When people saw a toad or a black cat crossing the street, they said it was a witch.
205261: A man had an epileptic fit whenever he came onto the Alderweg. Suddenly the man remembered that his mother had promised to go on pilgrimage to Saint Quintinus in Tienen. For that, a collection first had to be held in the village. After the man had made the pilgrimage, he experienced nothing strange any more.
205271: A man got lost because of a woman who was suspected of being a witch.
205278: A child who went to catechism class made a little ball in her hand and threw it away. The next moment a mouse was running there. When the priest asked the girl to do the same again, she could no longer do it.
205323: A pregnant girl was given plums by a woman who was said to be a witch. "Do you dare eat those plums?" people asked the girl, to which she replied: "Yes, why not!" The girl did not believe that the woman was a witch. For the girl had placed a holy object under her threshold, yet the so-called witch crossed the threshold without any trouble.
205349: In Beigem one day someone struck at a black cat. The next day it was found that a woman from the village had a broken leg.
205387: A big dog with a long tail often sat by the Lintersepoort and frightened everyone. That was the werewolf. One day two factory workers on their way home gave the werewolf a sound thrashing. They recognised the werewolf as a man from the village. If you could make a werewolf bleed, you could recognise him.
205388: Some men who were playing cards saw a fifth man sitting at the table, who had no feet but paws, like an animal. When they saw that, the men cursed and ran away. That fifth man was kleudde (a shape-shifting bogeyman).
205389: A werewolf was regularly seen walking around a house in Landen. If you could make a werewolf bleed, he took on his human form and you could unmask him.
205397: On a farm in Herfelingen the cows were found untied every morning and the piglets behaved wildly. The cows also stopped giving milk. The people went to the fathers of Affligem, who gave them medals to hang above the door of every stable. This did not improve the situation, however. A father from Affligem came, who sweated heavily and could not get inside. The priest began to pray. When he was tired, a screaming and cursing woman came running out. After that the father was able to go in. That woman was a sorceress who brought some food every day and also came near the animals.
205401: People who could not sleep at night were said to have been ridden by the 'moen' (mare).
205402: A man from Attenhoven came to Halle to visit his girlfriend. When he went home in the evening, he saw a big cat sitting on a turnstile between Halle and Velm. The man had to go through that turnstile, but the cat would not budge. So he had to turn back or crawl through the hedge or the barbed wire. One day the young man told his girlfriend about the cat. He said: "If the cat is still there tonight, I'll knock it off the turnstile!" The girl replied: "No, you mustn't do that. You'll regret it!" The man went home and, despite his girlfriend's warnings, knocked the cat to the ground as he had planned. The next moment his girlfriend was standing right in front of him.
205410: A hunter who wanted to shoot hares suddenly saw so many hares that he no longer dared to shoot. Those hares were witches.
205435: If you saw a suspicious person walking, you had to put your feet in their footprints. Before five more steps, that person would look back and say: "I didn't know who was following me so quickly!"
