205442: A woman standing at the cooking pot by the open hearth saw a toad fall out of the chimney. The woman knew that such toads were witches and burned the animal. Afterwards the woman could also tell which witch had died.
205444: At Whitsun a procession was held in Werchter. The day before the procession a farmhand said: "I ought to go and get a new cap in Mechelen, because mine is so dirty." Another man said to the farmhand: "Well, we'll go and buy a new cap. Sit on the back of my horse, but don't look back." The farmhand bumped his feet against the tower of the Sint-Romboutskerk in Mechelen. At that the farmhand did look back for a moment. The next moment he was sitting on a molehill.
205479: A witch from Hoxem always tried to get into people's houses. At one family's home she once bewitched a small child, who as a result could no longer go to the toilet. The parish priest said that only the witch could solve the problem. The child's father sent for the witch and said: "You must undo the harm you have done to my child, or I will beat you to death." The witch fiddled with the child for a moment and after that it was cured.
205490: A joker had put a rat with nutshells tied to its tail in the attic of people in whose house a young man had just died. The occupants were terrified because they believed the dead man had come back.
205495: In R.'s house in Babelon someone had hanged himself. From then on all kinds of strange things happened in the house. The friars claimed they could do nothing about it and said: "That had to come back. You'll just have to wait, because we can't do anything about it".
205515: Farmer S. met a ghostly priest holding a candle in his hand.
205516: A girl who had been struck by the evil hand was prayed over in Affligem. The fathers advised the people not to show the child to anyone. They also gave the people a piece of an Easter candle. The first person to come and visit the child would be the guilty one. So the woman who came to see the child was not let in. In the end the girl was cured.
205542: Six people coming back from the fair in Engsbergen heard someone talking about them on the way, but could not catch up with that person. Along the way a cat had walked beside them by a hedge. The people walked and walked and always ended up back in Engsbergen. Towards morning they found themselves at the Zwart Water.
205544: A poacher saw a dog run out of the cornfield. When the poacher sat down by the wood, he saw a small hare running. A little later a slightly bigger hare appeared. Then an even fatter hare came along. On the fourth day the poacher saw a very fat hare that was limping.
205549: The miller had a chapel built by the smithy because one of his dead relatives always came and sat at that spot at night.
205560:
Near Leuven stood the 'Grauwschuur' or 'Duivelsschuur' (Devil's Barn).
A farmer who did not have enough room in his barn to store his harvest saw a black gentleman approaching in the field, who said: "Farmer grauw, farmer grauw, your barn is too narrow." When the farmer explained that he had no money for a new barn, the gentleman went on: "If you give me one pledge, I will see to a new barn." Assuming the gentleman meant a piece of land, the farmer agreed to the proposal. The condition was that the barn had to be finished before the cock first crowed in the morning. The farmer's wife, however, was uneasy and sat praying all night. When she saw towards morning that the devils were still at work, she clapped her hands, which made the cocks start crowing too early. A moment later all the devils had vanished. The barn still stands near Leuven. In the barn there is a hole that the devils had not yet bricked up.
205573: Witches could change themselves into an animal. Some people had seen a witch in Dworp who was spotted in Kasteelbrakel at the very same moment.
205585: If a blessed candle was placed under the threshold, witches could no longer come in.
205596: A man who was baking cakes saw someone come down the chimney. That apparition had hidden money somewhere. The apparition said to the cake baker: "We will split everything in half". In the end, however, the apparition itself made off with all the money.
205603:
A man had been given sausages by a sorceress who always went about with a black basket. The man fell ill from that food. He was bewitched.
Three children had even died through that woman's witchcraft.
205611: At the Kabeek in Oetingen people heard wonderful music. The people dancing there wore beautiful clothes. A man who was watching the scene clasped his hands together and spoke holy names. Because of this the spectacle vanished at once. If the man had kept quiet, he would have been taken into the circle of dancers.
205620: A sorceress used to live in Pepingen. A man always got stuck with his cart when he drove past her house. When the woman then came outside, the man could go on with the cart without any trouble.
205621: A girl who went to catechism class in preparation for her Solemn Communion saw a child make a mouse by rolling up a piece of paper and throwing it on the floor. The children told the priest, who ordered the girl to show the same trick again. After the priest had read over the girl, she could no longer make mice.
205624: A man could conjure mice out of a little heap of earth. Such sorcerers were probably hypnotists who could make people see things that were not there.
205626: A man driving from Landen to Waasmont passed a little café on the way. The man wanted to go in for a drink, but when he saw a woman going in, he drove on because he did not want to buy her a drink. A little further on a wheel flew off the man's cart. The man went to fetch the wheel. When he was standing at the café, the woman said to him: "You didn't want to come in, but now you have to come back and buy me a drink!" The man did so and afterwards was able to drive home safely.
205632: A woman suspected of being a sorceress had two daughters. One of the daughters died. The other daughter, who worked as a maid in Gent, married and had a healthy child. One day, however, the child fell ill, so a pilgrimage was made to Ninove. Two women who were keeping watch over the child at night went outside because there was so much noise and rattling in the washhouse. At midnight the child died.
205639: A girl caught smallpox after accepting a sweet from a sorceress the day before.
205651: A man who normally walked to work had to go by train because he had an injured leg. At four o'clock the man had to take the train to Namen in Tienen. A colleague had advised the man to be careful by the cemetery in Tienen. The man had laughed at that advice, but when he reached the iron gate of the cemetery, he heard a rushing noise there. The man started to run as fast as he could. When he reached Tienen station, there was blood in his shoe.
205662: People who were out with the horse and cart in the evening often drove into the ditch when they met a sorceress from the village. But often those people had already had a fair amount to drink.
205670: A farmer from Brabant had a bigger harvest every year and no longer had enough room in his barns to store it. One Sunday the farmer was walking in his field, cursing. The farmer said: "May the devil help me if there is no other way." A moment later a strange gentleman dressed in black stood beside the farmer. This gentleman offered to build the farmer a barn in a single night. The barn would be finished before the first cockcrow the next morning. The farmer did have to sell his soul, for it was the devil who stood before him. At first the farmer was afraid, but in the end he agreed to the proposal and signed a contract in his own blood. That night the farmer could not sleep. He saw thousands of devils leaping back and forth. They dragged trees, crowns and all, to the spot where the barn was to stand. When the farmer's wife learned from her husband what it all meant, she went downstairs, lit the lantern and went to the henhouse. The cock suddenly woke at the sight of the lantern and began to crow, although it was only just past midnight. The barn was not yet finished at that moment, but the devils had to leave, so the farmer kept his soul. There was still a hole in the barn that no one has ever been able to close. When a statue of a saint was bricked into the hole, the statue fell to pieces. The priests came to sprinkle the barn with holy water, but that did not help either. That barn was called the devil's barn.
205692: On a Sunday evening a girl was walking home with her boyfriend. The two had only just left the boy's house when he said: "I have to go back home right away. You go on ahead. If a dog comes near you, throw a handkerchief at its mouth and then it won't harm you." When the girl did indeed meet a dog, she did as her boyfriend had advised. The next day the girl saw her boyfriend again. She saw that he had the fibres of her handkerchief between his teeth. That boy was lodder (a shapeshifting spook) with his chain.
205704: In Attenhoven there lived a father whose child cried every night. One day the man found pins in the child's pillow. The man was convinced that the trouble had been caused by his aunt, who came to fetch milk from him every day. The man immediately went to his aunt, dragged her out of bed and said: "If you don't come and undo the harm to my child, I will kill you." The woman got dressed and meekly went along with the man. In the man's house the pins were taken out of the pillow, after which the child no longer cried. The man then said: "If you ever dare to do anything to the child again, I will kill you!" After that the man had no more trouble with his child.
205708: A woman who had to bring food to the field ran away in fright when she saw the little woman of the 'Ouen Vijver' (Old Pond) standing in the wheat field. That little woman sometimes suddenly disappeared.
205728: Because the French under Napoleon stole church bells to cast cannons from them, the farmers of Mazenzele hid their church bell in the Kravaalbos between Terheide and Meldert. There the bell was laid in a spring. Years later the bell could be heard ringing at twelve o'clock on Christmas night. The spring was called 't Klokkeputteke (the little bell pit).
205759: People who claimed they had been ridden by the mare had got lost on their way home because they were drunk.
205764: In a house where there was a little daughter, a neighbour regularly came to visit and would pick up the child. A few weeks later the child was dead. Two years later another little daughter in the same family died because of that neighbour. The parents sought advice from the fathers, who showed them the face of their neighbour in a bucket of water. The people then put a holy object under their threshold, so that the neighbour could no longer come in. In the end the people moved, and in their new house they had no more problems with the children.
205780: If a black cat was seen sitting by a small chapel, people believed it was a witch.
205797: One must accept nothing from a sorceress. Some children had been given biscuits by a woman at whose house they had gone to sing for New Year. The children who had eaten the biscuits fell ill afterwards. The children who had thrown the treats away had no problems.
205819: A woman came to a farm in Wulmersum to buy a cow. Before buying the cow, the woman walked around, touched a bush and said: "What a beautiful berry bush!" The next day that bush had completely withered. When the woman had been to the same farm once more, a grapevine withered. The woman had to destroy something. If she could not direct it at plants or animals, she brought harm on people.
205853: A house in Sint-Pieters-Kapelle suffered a great deal of misfortune. A white cat always came and sat there under a bush and under the stove. The people were advised to beat the cat to death, because the animal was a witch.
205868: In a house in the Pelokenstraat in Beert, rattling was heard at midnight. One day the rural policeman was asked by a gentleman to guard the house for a night. That night, however, the policeman heard no strange noises.
205870: A man coming back from the fair at Zelem tumbled into a ditch and could not get out. He got lost and did not find the way to his house until five o'clock in the morning. In the inn where he had been sitting, someone had said to him: "You won't be home today", to which the man had replied: "I'd like to see that, me not getting home today!"
205883: A man was talking with his girlfriend in Sittert when he suddenly saw an exceptionally large dog approaching. The animal was almost as big as a calf. The man went home quickly but was followed by the animal. He was scared to death and told no one what he had seen.
205887: People who were ridden by the mare could not move and felt as if a witch was sitting on them.
205897: When someone had dressed up as a ghost in a sheet, people believed that a dead person had returned because he had forgotten to keep a promise or because he had to atone for a sin.
205915: A twenty-year-old girl was coming back from the fair in Wezemaal with her boyfriend. When the girl suddenly felt a cat jump on her back, she ran away so fast that her boyfriend could not keep up with her. In the end the girl even died of fright. People claimed that the boy's mother had special powers.
205916: Some men were playing cards with someone who had special powers. When one of the players bent down to pick up a dropped card, he saw that the man had two horse's legs. A little later a big tomcat came in, and the wizard said: "Look who we have here!" Then one of the players said: "Listen, you'd better keep calm here. Mind your cards instead!" The next moment the wizard and the cat turned into fire.
205929: A young man had heard that his girlfriend and her mother were witches. When the boy was visiting his girlfriend, he pretended to have fallen asleep. At midnight the boy heard the girl's mother whisper: "Over hedges and over hedgerows to Cologne into the wine cellar." The girl whispered the same, and a moment later the two had vanished. The boy wanted to repeat these words, but he made a mistake and said: "Through hedges and through hedgerows to Cologne into the wine cellar." The boy arrived badly injured in the wine cellar among the witches.
205931:
If one wanted to talk about someone, one first had to name the day. That way the person in question would not know he was being talked about.
A woman made all her children die because she was forced to. Yet those children were as strong as bears. If she did not do it, she would have to put herself to death. When the last child was dying, the woman had to stand on someone else's land, otherwise she would be next. Sorcerers and sorceresses passed their magic power on to their children. So that sorceress too had had to take over magic power from someone. A relative of that sorceress had already married for the fourth time. That woman made all her husbands die.
205946: Stallichten (will-o'-the-wisps) were lost little souls that wandered about at night because they were seeking rest.
205948: If you hit a werewolf on the nose so that he began to bleed, he suddenly took on his human form. A carter in Wommersom had experienced this.
205966: Witches often harmed people out of jealousy because they had a nicer cart or because they boasted about something.
205967: In a laundry where ironing was done there was a small child lying in a cradle. One day an ugly old woman with a beard came in. The child was crying because it was hungry, and the woman took it in her arms. When the mother saw this, she said: "Will you leave that child alone! It's hungry!" The woman went outside. Someone then saw her go to the little chapel of Lenneke Mare, where she smashed a statue of Mary. That evening the child had convulsions and could no longer move its legs. The doctor did not know what to do. The child could not walk for many years and one of its legs stopped growing. People believed that the old woman had bewitched the child.
205975: A man walking home in the evening saw a black cat by the house of a witch and kicked at the animal. The next day the witch wore a bandage around her head.
205980: When a farmer in Melkwezer was harvesting, no one was allowed on the field before the harvest was in. A woman said to the farmer, who stood ready to leave with a full cart: "You're not going home." The farmer was not yet off the field when his cart fell over.
205981: The mayor could make white mice by throwing sand on the ground. After the mayor had been to the sacristy with the priest, he could no longer make mice.
205983: When a child had been born somewhere, no visitors were allowed in before the child was baptised. In a house in Krokegem a toad always came in through the drain hole whenever the baby was being washed. One day the mother poured a bucket of boiling water over the toad. The next day a woman was walking around the neighbourhood whose face was completely burned.
205999: At the Mollershof on the Frankrijkstraat in Oetingen, all sorts of noises were heard, although nobody could be seen. People believed they were the spirits of the dead, who came to point out the money.
206001: In a house lived three women who sold nuts. If you bought such nuts, you were sure to be bewitched. After the women died, a fortune was said to have been taken out of their chimney. People then said: "That money can't have been earned by selling nuts. It's witchcraft."
206004: If you shot dead a witch in the form of a cat, the witch would lie dead in her bed the next day. That happened to someone from the church council.
206014: If you had been touched by a sorceress, you became a victim of witchcraft. On a farm a sorceress had touched one of the animals. The next day that animal lay dead.
206016: People who were ridden by the mare lay stiff as a board in bed and could not call out. They felt as if someone was squeezing their throat shut. A man who was ridden by the mare had been advised to urinate into a bottle and seal it. The mare was a witch who sat on people.
206031: In Bekkevoort lived a woman with a bad name. One day that woman came and asked some people if she could have a ladder to get across the brook. The woman of the house answered: "Go and knock next door, you go there often enough!" The witch went on, threw her basket to the other side of the brook and then tried a jump herself. The witch landed in the middle of the brook, but when she got up she was bone dry.
206053: In a house where an old woman lived, there was always misfortune in the stable. One day a soldier came to stay in that house. That soldier was really a priest in disguise. He read prayers over the place. However, he had forgotten one spot. He shot at a crow on the roof, but missed. The priest asked the daughter of the house for a wedding ring. With the ring he shot at the crow again, and this time he hit it; he had struck the bird in the wing. When the old woman who lived there came home, her arm was bleeding. She had bewitched the stable.
206063: A woman was visited by a neighbour, who said that her mother was not doing well. The woman took her own mother along to pay a visit to the sick woman. The sick woman sat there with tangled hair and had not been washed for a long time. The sick woman, however, did not want her daughter to touch her. The visiting woman washed the sick woman and combed her hair. A little later another woman from the neighbourhood came to visit, who was suspected of being a witch. When the witch stood by the sick woman's bed, the sick woman began to moan as if she were being tormented. The witch tried several times to harm the helpless sick woman, but usually she could not get into the house.
206086: People who were ridden by the mare were in reality having a bad dream.
206094:
A man who had been playing cards and was walking home at night saw a bright light in the sky. In a house the man saw very beautiful things. When the man passed that house again the next morning, he saw a woman walking there, carrying a basket to fetch greens for her rabbits. The woman said to the man: "Well, what did you think of last night? Wasn't it beautiful?" The man replied: "It certainly was!"
What the man had seen had to do with evil. That woman dared to talk about it just like that. Near the woman's house a crucifix hung on a wall. The woman said: "If I pass by here when I die, I'll jump out of my coffin!" The woman did not do so, however. That woman did evil.
206135: A house in Beigem was haunted. At night all the doors could be heard opening and slamming shut there, but in the morning there was nothing strange to be seen. Something similar happened in a house in Kapelle-op-den-Bos.
206151: One Saturday a shepherd went to the barber with some dogs to get a shave. The shepherd claimed he was afraid of nothing. On the way, however, he experienced something strange in a lane. A violent wind suddenly rose and the dogs crept between their master's legs in fear.
206180: People who behaved strangely were said to have been ridden by the 'moel' (mare).
206183:
In Alsemberg lived a beggar woman who was said to be a sorceress. She was always at the church of Sint-Genesius-Rode when high mass ended at around a quarter to eleven. People were afraid of her.
When some people with a three-horse wagon reached the hill of Zevenborren, they could not go on. The horses were drenched in sweat from the effort. When they said to the sorceress: "If you don't let those horses go, we'll put you under them!", they could go on.
206221: A man going to Neerpoeten (1) saw a devil's head appear behind a woman's back. A moment later the devil's head had vanished. When the man walked home on Sundays at around eleven or twelve o'clock, he saw a witch appear in the shape of a cat. One day that cat was sitting at the crossroads of the Neerpotenstraat and the Veilinglaan. A growling sound was heard there.
206225: In a house where a suspicious woman often came by, the mother fell ill. Afterwards the people heard that the visitor had said to someone: "Now they say I'm a sorceress and now I won't be allowed in there anymore. You'll see!" So even before anyone had told her that a holy object had been put under the threshold of that house, the witch already knew she would not be able to enter it anymore.
206242: A mother and father had a child who had suffered from an unknown illness for a long time. One day the parents went to the white fathers of Affligem, who said: "You must stay up at night and you must not let anyone in. I will give you something to put under the threshold. Someone will come to visit who will not get over the threshold until you have called her in, but you must not do that. That woman will come and ask for something you don't have in the house." That night at twelve o'clock a woman did indeed come asking for dried pitch. The father answered: "If you must be here, come in!" and stood ready with the bread knife to cut the woman's throat. Two weeks later the child was dead.
206265: A man walking home one evening met a black cat on the way and said: "Come along, my little beastie." The cat followed the man. When the man got home, he saw a strange dog standing behind the cat.
206275: In Sint-Pieters-Kapelle lived a woman whose child would not grow. Because the woman believed the child was bewitched, she sought advice from the fathers of Edingen, who said: "A woman comes to the child every day. You must keep that woman out." When that woman was no longer let in, the witchcraft came to an end.
206285: A woman who slept alone in a small room was ridden by the mare every night. One day her sister said: "Now I really want to know who comes to bewitch you." The sister kept watch in the room until she heard a tapping on the window. Then she laid a knife on the woman's chest. The witch came in by way of the stove. When the mare felt the knife in her heart, she screamed horribly. After that the woman was no longer ridden by the mare.
206290: A vet returning from a farm where a cow had calved was harassed on the way by two vagabonds. The vet fixed the two to the spot by magic.
206307: A man who lived on the Gelrode hill had been visiting his wife's parents. On his way home the man met a werewolf. When he got home the man nearly dropped dead from fear. People then went to look at the place the man pointed out, but found nothing unusual there. The werewolf often made passers-by carry it.
206318: On the Velmse Baan lived a good farmer's wife who gave free milk to everyone. On that farm, however, the cows were found untied every morning, even though they had been properly tied up the evening before. The people believed they were bewitched and had the farm prayed over by the fathers, who advised them not to give away free milk any more. Everyone who came for milk had to pay a cent. After that the people had no more misfortune.
206350: One evening a man went to the buckwheat field hoping the watchman would have fallen asleep. But the watchman was not asleep at all, for the wailing of a thousand cats could be heard. Those were witches.
206352: People who had been 'led by the alf' (led astray by an elf) got lost and could no longer find their bearings. A man who had got lost on his way home only found the way after asking someone for help. The man had been ridden by the 'maan' (mare).
206356: A child was bewitched. They managed to transfer the magic power onto a goat, but the goat must not be slaughtered, or else the child would fall ill again. The people sought advice from a father, who asked whether anyone came to visit them. The people told of a neighbour who often came to fetch water from them. One morning the man had stayed at home and had forbidden the neighbour to come in any more. If a scapular was put under the threshold or something hung above the door, that neighbour could no longer come in.
206372:
A man noticed that hares and rabbits were eating the tops of his carrots. One night the man kept watch in his field to shoot one of the animals. When the man had been sitting there for a while, he saw a cat walking in the field. A little later the man heard a voice singing in the trees above him: "X called out to me: Pussycat, where are you. And had X not spoken so nicely, I would have broken his neck. Now I will break the foal's neck."
That cat was a witch. The foal that was in the meadow had broken loose and broke its neck when it crashed into the fence.
206389: In Duras a dead man appeared in the form of a ghost sitting on a wooden barrier.
206391: In the past it was said of spiders' webs: "In the morning, worry; in the afternoon, luck; in the evening, little; then the spider's head stays in."
206392: In the Hoogstraat in Sterrebeek there was always a black animal about that could not be caught. One day people had struck the animal. The next day a witch from the neighbourhood had a wound on her face.
206395: If children were bewitched by their mother, they died. Sorceresses sometimes also made sure that their children could not have children themselves.
206396: A man whose wife had died when his son was twelve often had himself prayed over by the parish priest. Some time later the man had a relationship with another woman. Whenever that woman visited the man, there was quarrelling in the neighbours' house. One day there was even a break-in there. In the end the man had that woman prayed over as well.
206402: The sorceresses held gatherings at a crossroads.
206404: In Lot lived a woman who was said to be a sorceress. A farmer's wife went to clean for that woman and her husband to earn a little extra. Although the farmer's wife did not believe the old woman could work magic, she did have a lot of bad luck: her cows regularly died, her house burned down twice and she was married three times. People believed that the farmer's wife had been bewitched by the old woman she cleaned for.
206420: On his way home a man saw a large bird flying above his head. When the man passed the house of a witch, he saw the bird drop into the garden of that house.
206422: In Glabbeek there lived a witch. When she went to a neighbour to borrow a darning needle, she covered the neighbour's husband in lice.
206437: A family in Wezembeek had noticed several times that gingerbread had disappeared from the cupboard. One day an old woman came to visit who claimed she could tell everything that had happened in the past by means of her mirror. When the people asked who had stolen their gingerbread, the old woman began to pray. Not three minutes later a neighbour could be seen in the mirror walking past, laughing and eating gingerbread.
206443:
During the fair a farmhand had been stabbed to death at the Kleuddemansbeek. Since that incident people said that the devil lingered on that bridge.
A man tried to cross the Kleuddemansbeek in the snow. However, he could not get across Kludde's plank. The man knelt down and prayed a Hail Mary. After that he crossed the brook without any trouble.
206475: A woman who had promised to pray for the Mission Cross had not kept her promise. When the woman came into the church, she saw a white friar disappear into the confessional. A while later the woman saw the friar a second time. The ghost grabbed her by the arm and said: "You have not done your duty". Where the friar had touched the woman, her arm was completely burnt.
206490: A girl fell down the stairs but was not hurt. After the family had moved, the girl one day fell out of the armchair. This knocked the girl unconscious. She was being tormented by a witch.
206511: In the past the children of Hoegaarden were very afraid of being bewitched by a witch. When the witch had beckoned to them, they often imagined that they could no longer lift their arm because they were bewitched.
206515: In an attic a basket of beans fell. When people went to look, however, there was no one to be seen. Those were sorceresses.
206522: When people met a black cat in the evening, they believed it was a witch. Witches were also called 'zwarte madam' (black madam) or 'klerre'.
206527:
Some people coming back from the fair were attacked by a black cat that would not be chased away. The next day those people's daughter was ill. The father went to the girl and found that her condition was very serious. The mother believed her daughter was bewitched, but the father did not believe it.
A man who was hammering at his cart at New Year was visited by a father, who said: "If you hammer on the first day of the year, you will have to hammer all year." But the man answered: "I can't do without my cart, because I have to take the milk to the people early tomorrow."
206574: A woman who had been ill for a year and could not be helped by the doctor was often visited by a woman from the neighbourhood. One day the sick woman's husband went on a pilgrimage to Dendermonde. That day the neighbour came at about eleven o'clock to ask for a wheelbarrow. The people gave her the wheelbarrow because they did not yet know that it was this visitor who was causing the harm. When the man came back from his pilgrimage in the evening, he said that he had arrived in Dendermonde at eleven o'clock. Because the people had given away the wheelbarrow, the pilgrimage had been in vain.
206579: A black cat was a witch that appeared at night with eyes like balls of fire. People were very frightened when they saw such cats.
206610: A woman who was sitting in church around Easter could not leave the church, because a piece of the Easter candle had been placed in the porch. The priest then led the woman out through the back door.
206617: People who had made a pact with the devil had unlimited power.
206623: On a farm in Nieuwenrode the cows fell ill. The people believed that a sorceress from the neighbourhood had bewitched the animals and went to the fathers of Dendermonde. The priests said to the farmer: "When you get home, one cow will be dead, but the other will stay alive."
206645: In the old days people believed that witches could change themselves into a black cat.
206659:
In a house on the Toren in Zichem, eight cats came in through the water drain. People believed these cats were witches. The occupant of the house laughed and said: "Well, pussycats, where have you all come from?"
The cats danced in a ring holding each other's paws, with the words: "J. asked me, pussycat, where do you come from?" When the man put water on the stove, the cats ran away for fear of getting burnt.
206667: Some men returning together from the fair in Beert saw a woman lying with crossed arms on the gate of their house. One of the men boxed the woman's ears. The next moment everything was lit up. The men took out their knives, but not one of them managed to get his knife open. The woman who lay there had a bad name.
206670: On Sundays the men often went to the café opposite the church, where they played cards until mass was over. One Sunday a gentleman came into the café and looked at the players' cards. The people let him be, until they noticed that the gentleman had horse's legs. At that, all the customers left the café. After that incident those men always went to mass on Sundays.
206686: M.S. from Langdorp had a quarrel with T., a little woman who had recently come to live near him. After T. had died, something strange happened. When M.'s mother went to fetch water, she saw T.'s black ghost hovering above the well. The mother screamed and went to fetch the men of the village. "Listen", said M.'s mother, "if we forgive T. and settle the quarrel, the ghost will surely disappear". And so it happened.
206691: In a small village northwest of Brussels (1) lived a farmer who had no barn to store his enormous harvest in. The farmer was visited by a gentleman who said to him: "That doesn't matter. If you sell me your soul, I will see that there is a barn, finished by the time the cock crows three times at twelve o'clock tonight." That evening a crowd of black men appeared and began pulling trees out of the forest. At eleven o'clock the cock crowed once. At half past eleven the bird crowed again. At five to twelve the farmer's wife clapped her hands, so that the cock crowed once more. The black men all had to run away. At the top of the barn there was still a hole that no one has ever been able to close. That is the little bird of the devil's barn.
206695: The widow of V.D.V. saw the corpse of her dead husband appear under a pear tree in Budingen. The dead man took his wife by the hand. The woman then decided to go on pilgrimage for her dead husband. After that her husband did not appear again.
206705: Many people from Sint-Pauwels (a hamlet of Galmaarden) went to the market in Geraardsbergen every Monday. They had to come home through the woods. One day they saw a cat there and kicked at it. The cat ran after them. When they got home and slammed the door, the cat had turned into a calf.
206712: A witch from Meldert often gave the children a pear. She also made the cows lie dead in the stable and the rats run over the carcasses.
206723: One day a woman from Elsleuken (Wolfsdonk) went to Bombosch to cut grass for her cows. She carried a brand-new sack. On the way she met her neighbour. The neighbour stood right in front of her and would not let her pass. After the women had stood talking for a while, the neighbour said: "When you get to those trees over there, your sack will tear." The woman did not believe it, but when she reached the trees, the sack with the grass tore as if it had been cut with a knife. Terrified, the woman ran home. Her husband was not superstitious, but because of this incident he did believe that the neighbour was a witch.
206740:
A mother who had already lost two or three children told some soldiers who were staying with her about her misfortune. When the woman was about to give birth again, the soldiers saw a toad in the house. They struck the animal dead with their sabres. The child was born healthy. A neighbour woman lay dead.
In the past people were afraid of toads. They believed those animals could spit fire.
206747: In a village lived an ugly old woman whom everyone feared. People believed she was a witch and had already made several children ill. One day her son was appointed mayor. Many villagers regularly visited the mayor to chat or to ask him something. A woman who wanted to knock at the mayor's door sank into the ground up to her knees in front of the house, as if she were standing in mud. The same happened to other people who passed by. The neighbours noticed that the strange phenomenon only occurred when the mayor's mother was in the house. The mayor had cobblestones laid in front of his house, but that could not stop people from sometimes sinking into the ground. One day someone had the courage to tell the mayor that the strange events only happened when his mother was visiting him. The mayor was completely bewildered, but when he thought it over, he realised it was true. When one day the mayor confronted his mother with the suspicion that she might have something to do with it, it suddenly grew very dark and began to thunder and lightning. The next moment the woman had vanished without a trace. The mayor went to his mother's house, where he saw a large hole in the middle of the kitchen. People believed the witch had sunk into that hole. She was never seen again, and no more strange things happened at the mayor's house.
206754: If the call of an owl was heard at a certain farm, it was believed that someone at that farm would soon die.
206758: A man saw the hand of a sorceress in the doorway, although no person could be seen. When the man struck at the hand with the poker, it was gone.
206769:
A woman who was ridden by the mare saw black cats at night and heard chains rattling. The dean came to read prayers over her.
In reality the woman probably had a nightmare.
206775: A woman who had promised to make a novena died before she had fulfilled her promise. In the evening, when going to bed, the widower saw his dead wife appear. The priest advised the man to make the novena himself. When the man had done so, his wife did not appear again.
206778: Near the Molenberg an old woman with a stick had been seen walking beside a field. When some time later the harvest failed, people believed that woman was responsible for the misfortune. She was said to have touched something in the field with her stick.
206821: Kludde (a shapeshifting spook) with his keet appeared at midnight with a chain that made a lot of noise. A girl was in a relationship with a boy from Essenbeek, who always had to be home by half past ten. One day, however, the pair came back from a dance through the Hallerbos around twelve o'clock. The boy said to the girl: "You go on ahead, I need to pee. If you meet anything, throw this red handkerchief at the apparition." A little later the girl saw Kludde with his keet come running up. Kludde was a tormenting spirit who often had himself carried by passers-by, who got drenched in sweat from the heavy weight. The girl quickly threw the red handkerchief at Kludde, who tore the cloth to shreds. Meanwhile the girl ran home. When she saw her boyfriend the following Monday, she noticed that he had the red fibres of the handkerchief between his teeth.
